“That Depends: Were you TRYING to keep the dust above the cupboards: Or is it okay that I cleaned it up? Because either way it’s gone
now I’m afraid.”
“You haven't found any skeletons in my closet then.” His face lit up a little as he joked, his concern and disappointment fading as I
cracked jokes.


“Oh, the one in the hallway?” Tapping my index finger to my chin I mocked ‘thinking’. “I haven't even tried to tackle your closet yet.
Not with the way you’re always knocking things over in there. I felt like if I opened it stuff would come toppling out. It seemed like it
would be a shame if I ended up getting crushed to death under junk. It seemed as though that’s just your hoarding place.”
“Hoarding place?”

“Mmhum. Where you put things quickly when you clean the rest of the place. Anyway, it’s not my place to go snooping. Though if you
really do have a skeleton please keep it out of Bjorn’s reach. I’d rather that my dog doesn't gnaw on human bones. If possible. ”

“Noted.” He took a deep breath and then finally pushed away his work to to back of his desk and stood up. Stretching his arms up and
popping his back with a low groan before nodding at the door. “Ai-chan...can you flip the sign? I’m closing up now.”

I turned, made a quick glance at the clock before shrugging my shoulders on my way to do as he asked. “Sure, but isn’t it early?”

“Eh...” He rubbed the back of his neck, accidentally smudging charcoal along his skin. “...it’s not by very much. If people haven't come by
now I doubt they will. Anyway - I’m hungry . And I need to make sure your arm is doing alright so we can finish it. It’s not itchy is it?”

I peeked out the door, and flipped the sign to ‘closed’ before popping back in to lock the shop up. “Hum? My arm is fine. The plastic is a
bit uncomfortable - but since the first night it’s not been too bad. I’ve been catching myself about to scratch: but I haven't! I promise.”
I headed for the stairs, then straight to the kitchen. I was beside him as he started digging through his fridge for a container of ‘food’ that
struck his fancy. At the sink I wet a paper towel and stepped closer - making a small noise in the back of my throat so I didn’t startle the
ghoul. He glanced straight up, his eyes wide and curious as his iries darted from my face to my hands. “Hum?”

“You’ve got charcoal smudged all across your neck and a bit on your chin. Hold still.”
“Ah. Yeah...I was sketching earlier.” I let out a huff of air and tried dabbing the wet cloth across the marks on his chin--- ”Got it?”

“Not if you keep talking, shush before this cloth makes it into your mouth. Hold still!”

Despite my words, or perhaps because of them the ghoul playfully ‘bit’ at the air in front of his mouth. Completely harmless, yet I
stepped back and put my hands on my hips as I stared down at him. “Come on. Uta. Here then. You can clean it off yourself.” I dropped
the cloth over onto his upturned face and laughed softly as he pulled it off; pouting.

“I was only playing...”

“You’re not the only one who is hungry around here, Uta! I don’t have the patience to play around.” With that said I stuck out my
tongue and turned away; headed for the cupboard where he had taken to putting all the food he had for me. It wasn’t very well organized,
or well stocked yet but I could probably manage to scrape something together if I got creative. A trip to the grocery store was probably
due soon. While I was at it I could find some things to give the place a ‘human’ touch.

“Are your canned foods stumping you...?”

I jumped, blinking as I got startled out of my thoughts. “Huh!? Oh. No. Well---maybe a little. I was thinking about getting some things
for your---er. Our house. A toaster would be nice...”

Uta hummed through a mouthful of meat that he slurped up like a bunch of ramen noodles. The strips of meat were once again
mercifully unrecognizable. “Or a blender. You could have a meat smoothie if you wanted.” I chuckled to myself, not thinking much of it.
The idea of meat in a smoothie was absolutely repulsive if I did say so myself. Perhaps that was simply because fruits were sweeter and

meat as a liquid seemed----

“I’ll try it.” I blinked, turning to give the ghoul a look that must have confused him. His head canted to the side, eyes wide. “---?”

“Sorry. That was more of a joke. Because...Well, Typically a blender is used with fruits and sweet things. But I guess for a ghoul that
would be ‘normal’.” I glanced at the meat he was currently slurping up. It was cold anyway, so I suppose other than texture it would be
the same to him. “I guess that could work pretty well. Especially if you got a covered cup that’s opaque with a straw. Nobody would
know what you had with you. Although I’d recommend using mostly blood with that...it’s supposed to be mostly liquified.”

I plucked a can of soup out of the cupboard and turned to get pots out to warm it up. I was getting used to the way that the ghoul hung
around, watching me do my ‘human’ things. Cooking and ‘food’ seemed to be a topic of particular curiosity. This time though, the mask
maker wandered away after finishing his own meal.

When I emerged from the kitchen with my bowl of soup I found him on the couch, fiddling with some supplies from his tattooing kit.
He glanced up and flipped his art book closed as I came closer so I wouldn’t see the sketch he’d finished for the tattoo. I plopped down
beside him and watched with the same very same curiosity that he always held for my cooking.

“Are you planning on working on the rest tonight?”

“Soon as you’re done eating and I’ve made sure it’s already starting to heal alright. If you’re up for it.”

“Yeah, just let me finish my din----” I paused, mid sentence as my phone rang. Shifting so I could get my cell out of my back pocket I tried
to keep my soup steady. Gently, the ghoul reached and held the bowl for me as I peered closely at the unknown number.

“Unknown...hum. Hello?” I hit the button to receive the call before it finished ringing and waited, listening for the reply on the other
end.

“Ms. Kaneshiro this is---” I hit the big red end button and let out a long, shaky sigh as soon as I heard the stern male voice on the other
end. Nobody I knew used that name. Nobody on friendlyterms at least. It made it pretty easy to hang up on them. Calmly I added the
unknown number to a list of blocked numbers.

“It’s not Tsukiyama, is it?” I shook my head immediately, the brief dark look in Uta’s eyes was unnerving as his eyes fixated on the little
device in my hands.
“No. No. Just some suits from my family trying to get in contact again. They’ve been really aggressive about it lately. I’m a little curious
and wonder what’s up. But I also don’t want anything to do with my ‘family’ if I try and find out it’ll just encourage them. I’ll just get
dragged back into some fucking cage again.”

When the phone rang again, I declined immediately, sending the caller to limbo. “Seems like I might need a new phone number if they’ll
be using extra numbers to call...” I grimaced and sat there; ready to decline another call if one came through. “They probably looked it up
with my name through the cell service companies. Do you think your service would mind if I got a new number under your name?”

“Sure. I’ll get you a sim tomorrow.”

I blinked, starting over at the ghoul. “Uta- You...” That was a very quick answer; and totally serious. “I didn’t mean---it was kinda a joke.
But would you, really?”

“Sure. They’re not trying to track me. Right?” I opened my mouth, intending to say ‘no’ right off the bat: But then again. They had
resources and there was no telling what they might be up to now. This number of phone calls was unusual.

“Probably not? Even if they were, I think that the CCG is sneakier about tracking people, so you’d notice far sooner if someone were
snooping around. They’ve never tried to contact anybody around here anyway. You know: because it’s the shitty side of town filled with
scary dangerous people?” I chuckled and shook my head. “Otherwise I’m sure my old boss would have handed me over on a silver platter
for a bribe.”

“I’ll drop it off at Anteiku while you're working.” He held out the bowl of soup for me and picked up his inking tools to fiddle with while
I started to down the soup before it got too cold.  I muffled my thanks through a mouthful and gulped down the rest by tipping the bowl
up into my mouth.

After I finished my meal and ran both of our bowls to the kitchen sink. I returned to the couch and smiled at the small ‘come here’ gesture
he made before holding up the blindfold. Scooting over next to him and closing my eyes, I waited for the blindfold to be wrapped around
my head.

Once again blinded I relied on my other senses to ‘see’ around myself. He shifted closer, touching my arm and pulling it across his knees
to unwrap the plastic and take a good look at his work. As his fingers worked across the untouched artwork I shivered. “It’s still a little
itchy, but not nearly as bad.”

“It’s healing nicely I think. It’s much faster for us...but this looks good.” His thumb lingered over the back of my hand rubbing in little
circles before he stopped and reached for the tools. “You’re okay with continuing with the rest of the tattoo tonight?”

“Of course. Excited for me to see it?”

“I hope that you don’t regret letting me put something on you without looking at it first...”

I smiled, trying to dismiss any worry he had about that. “Well it’s more fun if it’s a surprise. Anyway; you know me well enough by now.
## Yeah?”

“I suppose...” I heard the tattoo gun start to buzz and stayed still so I wouldn’t make him mess up. Once in a while he’d let up and give me
a moment to move when I asked, but besides those moments he worked steadily sinking ink into flesh. After quite some time the ghoul
spoke up again.

“Although...Not everything.”
Lost: I scrunched up my brows under the blindfold. “What’s that?” The needle was taken away from my skin and a free hand was
brought to my face, turning it around towards himself. “I don’t know everything about you. You are a strange anomaly. For a Human. I
don’t understand how someone like you could stick around...”

Oh. This recurring conversation . Was this an insecurity? Or merely curiosity which always brought this subject up in one way or another?
“You’re not so bad...Maybe I’m just worse than you think.” I laughed it off, but perhaps what I said about that was partly true. Steadily I
was getting used to the idea of murder, ‘cannabalisum’ (so long as it wasn’t me) and I was guilty of my own assault charge and possibly
accesory to murder somewhere along the line. I wasn’t innocent when I was able to sit by with the knowledge that people were killed.
Nor from the fact that I cooked the meat for Uta.

“...you’re going to keep trying to ‘scare’ me off; aren't you?”

“...hum. No.” Uta slid closer, pulling me gently towards him at the same time. “I didn’t mean to. Was I scaring you?”

“No. Do I look scared?” I raised my eyebrows, pursing together my lips to stare in blind defiance in the direction I could hear his
breathing and his voice. He seemed to take a minute to study me before letting out a breathy laugh.

“ Blind. On my couch and very much at my mercy. All willingly. Foolishly; no. You don’t.”

“That was unnecessarily mean, Uta-kun! Anyway; should I have turned and run away the second I thought you were a Ghouls ?”

“ Yes . I’d have thought that the CCG would have drilled that into the public by now.” A bitter note tinged the edges of his words and I
frowned; getting angry. Not with him. No, with the way things were. How unfair it all was. This was likely how all my friends felt...

“That’s dumb.” The ghoul snorted, real laughter bubbling up from his chest. “I’m happy.” I added, cutting off his laughter and putting
as much conviction as I could into the words. I meant them. “I’m really, really happy...” I reached out with the arm not being worked;
first touching his chest and working my way up to his shoulders and neck and finally to his cheek.

“I get it. I’m a senseless, foolish, stupid human with apparently zero survival instincts . But I trust you. I am very fond of you...and if you
ever do scare me then I’ll just tell you honestly. You shouldn’t have to worry over every little moment that something you do will scare
me.”

Wordlessly the ghoul reached up and cupped his hand over my own, pulling it away he held it for a moment. His fingers cupped over
mine briefly, squeezed and then let go. The sound of the tattoo gun fired up again and he guided me back in position as he worked.

## ♥

“There we are...” He was wiping a cool cloth over my arm. He began moving my arm this way and that to get a better look at the image
now printed there. “Ready to see?”

“Yeah of course I am, but---” I reached out again and found his shoulder again. Able to navigate from there I moved my hands up to cup
his face and lean in closer to ALMOST kiss him. A moment before I’d met lips he turned his face just a little. “Huh...?” I made a small,
confused noise; my eyebrows furrowed.

I thought this would be a sweet moment - had I done something wrong!? I pulled away and sat back, feeling the first tingle of
disappointed rejection.

“Ai-chan...As much as I’d love to...I did eat before starting to work on your arm. But if you insist...?” I could hear the playful smile on his
face as he spoke.

“O--oh! I completely forgot.” I flushed bright red under the blindfold. Humorously the ghoul chuckled at the forgetfulness and pulled
me closer, pressing his lips gently against my cheek, down my neck and then finally back up to my forehead where he lingered.
“It’s alright Ai-chan.”

I leaned back, settling back to sit on my legs tucked up under me. I felt the couch move and the bindings of the blindfold were pulled
apart, letting the first bit of light in again in over an hour. “There you are...Alright. Well. Take a look.”

The first thing I looked at was the ghouls face. Smiling, I leaned forward and pressed a kiss into his cheek, just left of his mouth and
giggled. “Not nervous are you?”

“You might not like it.”

“I doubt that very much. Every mask you make for your customers is perfect.” Still, I was putting it off for just a few more seconds as I
stalled. Finally I looked down at my arm. It was strange seeing my arm which had been completely bare up until now sported a real
tattoo. While Uta’s tattoos were all black and utterly devoid of color in the symbols and complex lines; the one he’d put on me
immediately surprised me with colors that ranged from black and bloody red, pale pink and bright whites that popped vibrantly off my
pale skin below.


“It’ll fade in color a little bit...tattoos always do...”

“It’s beautiful. ” I turned my arm around, looking at the cyclical forms of two antlered deer-wolves chasing after one another in an
ouroboros-esk manner.  He had figured out something from the little story I’d told him while also sneaking in the design similar to my
mask.

I looked up from the design and beamed happily. I saw his eyes still searching for my reaction, as though I might be hiding
disappointment somewhere in my eyes. “I really don’t see why you would have been worried! You know me best; perhaps only second to
Bjorn.” I teased and grinned before my eyes wandered back to the tattoo - it was hard not to gawk at it!

“You really like it---” I was surprised when Uta leaned back in his seat and let out a long sigh.
He looked so relieved!

“Eh?! You weren’t that worried about it- were you!? How could you be unsure about this?” I gestured with my marked arm. “It’s
fantastic.”

“...my other work is removable, Ai-chan. This is much more permanent. It would have been much harder for you to get rid of it if you
hated it.”

I reached up and cupped his cheeks; leaning near his ear just as he had with me earlier while downstairs. “Good. You seem to like putting
marks on me. But with this one I’ll gladly show it off and tell everybody who put it there!~”

I squeaked when an arm wrapped around my waist to keep me from moving away again, instead he was moments away from pulling me
fully into his lap--

Downstairs, the door to the shop opened and closed and there were feet lightly but quickly tapped up the apartment steps. I jolted and
turned my head sharply towards the doorway; caught by surprise. So close---just a few more moments without interruption and I might
have actually forgotten again that he’d eaten recently. Bjorn who had been very peacefully laying down and taking a nap on his bed bolted
up and stared at the doorway to the apartment intently; growling low in his throat. “I locked it like you asked me to, who---?”

“U-kun! There’s----eh! Oh dear.” The woman with flying fiery red hair stopped short and looked coyly from Uta and myself; a smug
smirk already on her face as she noticed how close we were. “Well I’m sorry for interrupting!”

Unperturbed, Uta replied with his arm remaining wrapped around me and preventing a retreat even under Itori’s scrutiny. “...what’s
wrong Itori?”

“Ah well---” Itori’s eyes briefly wandered before snapping back to the goth ghouls face. “Some intel on some--- merchandise came in.
They wanted some help moving it. I offered up our services. Roma was pretty excited about it. After being cooped up for so long she’s
wanting some fun.”

I felt out of the loop and rather awkward listening in on this conversation between them. Merchandise. Maybe...it was bloodwine? But
why would that involve Uta unless he just helped Itori once in a while with her business. It wouldn’t be that strange for two business
owning ghouls to help each other out. But...

There was the way that Itori’s eyes flicked to look at me and then Uta. I could probably chalk it up to it simply being because of the way
Uta’s arm was looped around my waist keeping me hovering over him while she intruded on the moment. But...she was being evasive in a
way I hadn’t known her to be before. Ever since I’d met her through Uta hadn’t they been pretty forthcoming with what they were?



The way merchandise had been said so hesitantly made it known that wasn’t the word she was originally going to use. And if it was blood
wine she would have just said so...

“Uta-kun. I’m going to take Bjorn for a walk. Okay?” I offered him a small smile; one that I hoped would let him know what I meant. I’d
let them have their conversation privately. This- whatever it was- was ‘ghoul’ stuff and still out of my reach. He seemed to carefully
consider me with his eyes before speaking.
“You could stay if you want.” Regardless, his arm retreated back to allow me to pull away.

“U-kun I’m not sure---” Itori started to speak but I shook my head, cutting her off.

“It’s alright. I’ll be back in about fifteen minutes. Sound good?”  I hoped that was enough time for them to figure out their business;
whatever it was. It was still cold outside! “Come on Bjorn, walk time!”

As expected, the large dog's attention was grabbed from Itori and back to me. He was instantly excited to get to go out and play in the
snow.

“Be careful Ai-chan.” I turned, pulled the quinque steel knife from a pocket and wiggled it in the air.
“I will! I won’t be longer than fifteen minutes.”

As I passed Itori I couldn’t help but to glance up curiously at her face. In her eyes I found an unease that unsettled a gut feeling inside me.
I was right to leave and I knew it: But sooner or later this was going to be important. I would not always be able to simply walk out the
door and make myself scarce. Nor would I want to.

## ♥


True to my word I timed my outing to fifteen minutes and was back at the entrance to the shop in perfect time. Which was good - any
longer and I might have started to freeze.  I opened the door with my own key and let Bjorn run through the shop and up the stairs to
greet Uta.
I slowly walked up the stairs and poked my head in the door, making sure they weren’t still talking about their unknown ghoulish business
dealings.

“And she’s back is safe and sound! See ?” Itori smiled and nudged the goth ghoul who was seated beside her. “Told you U-kun, she can
take care of herself! Scare away any villains?”

“No. That’s not my job. That’s his. ” I nodded at the large dog who happily took a treat from my hand.

“Eh. Him? He’s not scary. He just looks really fluffy!”

“Well he’s also not trying to bite you!” I laughed at the expression on her face. I’d seen so many people shrink away from the large beast to
know that he did scare a lot of people. “Most people are scared away by his size and if that’s not enough he can get pretty scary if he feels
like it.” I shrugged. In the back of my head I remembered when he had fought off my ex-boss in the tiny apartment. Had I been on the
receiving end of that - it would have been terrifying.

Briefly I leaned down and rubbed the dogs face; smooshing his cheeks while his tail wagged vigorously. “...but I’d rather it not come to
that. I’d be heartbroken if something happened to him. After all, he's not my guard dog. He’s my friend.” Back at my apartment I’d been
terrified that he’d been badly injured when he was attacked. It didn’t matter if he was a ‘big scary dog’ he was my responsibility. “I’m
supposed to take care of him, not the other way round’.”

“...anyway---” I glanced from Uta to Itroi. “You guys want coffee?”



## ♥



“I won’t be around for a few nights.” Uta stated as I began washing the coffee mugs from the impromptu ‘coffee time’ with Itori. I
turned my head around to give the ghoul who leaned at the kitchen entryway a curious, one raised eyebrow look.

“Something to do with your private chat earlier?”

He nodded once and watched as I went back to rinsing out the blood from a tupperware with the spraying hose. “Ai-chan--I’ll get that.
Don’t worry about my bowls.” I hesitated for a moment before shrugging my shoulders. Honestly I was relieved the man was willing to
clean his own bloody dishes.
“Suit yourself. Less house work for me!~”

“Are you not curious, what we spoke about?”

“Of course I am--- human nature ?” I shot him a half smile as I joked. “But at this very moment it doesn't seem to be ‘need to know’. Even
if you are willing to tell me....Itori didn’t seem to be.” I dried my hands on a towel and leaned against the counter. “Letting you tell me
would push her out of her comfort zone. Which is saying something, because from what I’ve seen and heard that woman will gossip
about anything ! And I can’t imagine Roma being any more pleased than Itori. She already doesn't like me very much...”

The ghoul shifted his gaze away and shook his head. “Roma would tell you just to upset you...”

I pursed my lips together firmly and studied my ghoul boyfriend. He avoided my gaze, glancing away now so I couldn’t see his eyes
clearly.
"So why is it you want to tell me?" I asked softly, moving past him, out of the kitchen and to seat myself down the couch. He followed me
out, I could hear his bare feet barely pad across the kitchen floor until it hit the carpet of the living room. "---You think it would upset me;
but you're still offering the information. Why?"

He was quiet for a few moments before his shoulders rose and fell in a defeated sort of shrug. "You will likely find out at some point
anyway. Better sooner than later. And because you deserve to know..."

I made a small humming noise of affirmation. "True I suppose. Rip the band-aid off right away, nice and quick. I’m sure there’s some
people that could tell me some really terrible stuff you’ve done - or do. But If I don't immediately need to know then I'm fine not
knowing." I hesitated and added: "For now at least. And...you might be right. Whatever it is might really upset me."

I pat the couch next to me, waiting for him to come sit back down. " But Figuring that out is my job, not yours. No matter how upsetting
it is, I think the worst thing I would ask of you is to simply keep me in the dark. Just like you already do. Not telling me who you’ve
hunted down. Or...warning me not to be around when you're chopping them up and putting them into itty bitty plastic containers. Like
that. Alright?”


The ghoulish man finally looked at me, unblinking for a lengthy few seconds before breaking the contact again. He moved, towards the
couch where he collapsed with a small bounce and let out a sigh; head leaned back and eyes closed. I watched him for a few more
moments before he said simply:

“Thank you.”

“Anything!~” Frighteningly enough; I felt I likely meant it.

## ♥


The rest of the night seemed to pass by quickly. Bjorn was happy with his walk around town and settled down snuggly in his bed by the
heater. Meanwhile I got a little snack together for myself; offering to cook for Uta at the same time. He seemed...

Distracted. Uncharacteristically he refused the cooked meal in lieu of simply eating it raw while he worked on something on his phone;
furiously typing out messages. While I remained perplexed, I simply let him be until it was time to sleep.

Leaning over the arm of the couch I inclined myself into his space between his face and his phone. “Uta-kun!~” I chirped pleasantly,
catching his wide red eyes. “I’m going to bed, alright? You should too if you’re running out for business, yeah?” The ghoul’s blank stare
remained for but a moment before he blinked and seemed to snap out of a sort of daze.
“Hum? Yeah. I’ll be in shortly.” Satisfied I stood up straight, and headed for the bathroom. Teeth brushed. Hair brushed. I dressed in
Uta’s over big shirt I used for PJ's and crawled into bed; settled with Bjorn laying beside the bed on my side.

I fell asleep before Uta came into the room - only half waking briefly when he shuffled into bed, pressed his lips into my cheek and settled
down quietly without a spoken word.
## Notes:
Edited: Some art of the non-spoiler variety!



## Chapter 40: Old Dangers
## Notes:
## OMG! WHAT IS THAT?! WHAT IIISSSSS THAT?
(it's another chapter so soon!) ♥

Trigger Warning: Very brief mentions of a Suicidal Character?
(See the end of the chapter for  more notes.)
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 40: Old Dangers

The room was quiet when I woke up in the morning. No sign of the ghoul except a note in his handwriting that he had left for me to find
on his pillow. I plucked up the note and squinted down at the scrawl.

Don’t forget your mask, knife and keys.
I’ll check in to see how you're doing when I can. Renji will watch out for you. Call him for anything you need.

“Renji huh?” I muttered to myself looking at the underline under the word. Bjorn stood and laid his head on the edge of the bed and
groaned.
“Hey bud. Uta’s gone for a little while.” Guess that meant I’ll be bringing Bjorn with me to work then as well. I didn’t want to leave him
here in the apartment on his own - even though I was sure he’d be fine. It was a hell of a lot more space than my old place had had.
However Yoshimura had said at one point it was okay as long as he stayed in the back and was out of the way. If Hinami was around then
she’d be delighted anyway.

I forced myself out of bed and around for work with Bjorn in tow behind me. On the way out I made sure to lock up behind me. On the
crowded train ride Bjorn stayed diligently by my side, a pleasant buffer between myself and others. Touka did a double take as we both
entered the café early in the morning. I smiled apologetically and shrugged. “Uta’s out, so I brought him along with me. Is Himani
around? I know she loves him.”

“Yeah, she’s upstairs.” The ghoul smiled faintly as she went to grab a cleaning rag for the counters. “As long as he’s not in the way, I don’t
care.”

I ushered the dog upstairs, left him in the adoring care of the youngest ghoul and went about my job. Several hours into the morning
Renji came to the cafe and sat down at the bar. I waved briefly and started to walk by to attend to another customer when he turned and
stopped me.

“Aika. One moment.” Renji said, forcing me to pause and look back at him.
“Hum? What’s up?”

“Uta gave me this. Told me it was for you.” Renji held out his hand, a small item sat in his palm. Perplexed, I leaned forward and took the
item from him. A small computer chip--- “ Oh ! My new sim card! He remembered!” I grinned triumphantly. “Thanks Renji!~”

“Yeah. Well with him away he asked me to watch out for you.” He waved a dismissive hand over his shoulder and then turned to two
behind the coffee bar to order.
“Don’t worry about it.” For a moment longer I watched the back of his head. I hoped dearly that Uta hadn’t somehow forced his friend
into being my watcher. “Don’t worry Renji-kun! Not getting into trouble on purpose.”


## ♥

Entering the shop after a busy day of work was normally the best part of the day. But unlocking the door and entering the empty shop
and equally empty apartment was dreary. Which was why after redressing in non-work clothing and cleaning up a bit I headed out with
Bjorn at my side. As we walked I looked down at his shiny, freshly brushed fur and grinned.
“Hinami really did a number on you, didn't she? Tormented you all day with a good brushing!” I giggled as the dog chuffed a breath and
stared ahead of us. A good walk would get him to forget all about that though! I pulled out my phone as I walked and changed out the
sim card, putting the old away into my wallet so it was safe and sound.

When my phone restarted I could see a few messages already received.

Uta: New phone # works?
I had no idea how long ago he’d written the message; only that he had  intended for me to get it as soon as I turned on my phone with the
new sim. I typed out a reply so he’d know I’d gotten the sim from Renji and was safe.
Aika: Aye-Aye!
I bit my lip and only paused a moment before adding:
Aika: Hope you're safe!~

I stared at the screen as I walked, hoping that something might pop up on the screen; a reply. Or the little indicator that showed he read it.
However, after a block of walking with my nose to the screen nothing had changed. Stifling my disappointment I put away my phone
and tried to focus. Despite the oppressive emptiness of the house, I knew exactly what I could do while Uta was away - and he could come
back to a nice surprise!!!

Bjorn plodded by my side as we got back to the train headed for the 20th ward. There was a used bookstore not too far from the café that
I’d been eyeing. Not to mention plenty of other little shops. It also was a much friendlier neighborhood than the 4th. I smiled to myself as
I remembered my conversation with Uta about books; in particular cooking books.

Also on the list; A toaster that wouldn’t let Uta burn bread when he tried to make it! A rice cooker so it was easier to make rice without
having to boil the water and watch it so carefully. And a blender for smoothies! Even meat ones if Uta really wanted. I smiled as I added
the things to a mental catalog of the apartment in my mind. Those items with the books would really start to make the place look..
## .normal.

Whatever normal looks like for a ghoul and human living together.

I checked my phone as I exited the subway; saw no new messages. I bit my lip; biting down disappointment and continued walking.
Unlike my usual pace, I walked more slowly through the ward looking at the shops that littered the area. It was nice around here. Really
nice. Had I not moved in with Uta, then the old mans suggestion that I live here wouldn’t have been a terrible one. The people walked
freely on the streets and there wasn’t the obnoxious bumping beat of music or the screaming of nearby neighbors. It was---peaceful.

“---Aika...?” “Bear-Bear!!!”

I turned quickly as I heard my own name (and that of my dog) being called. I spotted the woman with a head of plum purple hair and the
small child ghoul beside her. “T-touka. You surprised me!”

“You walk around all the time with your head in the clouds?! I thought you went home?”

“I..did.” I murmured, shrinking under the almost accusing tone of voice. “---but then I came back.” I added; nodding towards the
bookstore that lay just down the street. “I planned on going there actually.”


“Us too!” I glanced down at the child with a smile. “Right Hinami. You like books. Don’t you?” The ghoul child smiled and nodded her
head. I watched as her ‘hair’ swung around her shoulders. The wig of long hair hadn’t helped when it came to recognising her initially.
Which was of course the point! No doubt the investigation was still out looking for her after.... that.
Especially with a few dead investigators. Plenty of that had been on the news or overheard at work. However, now that I saw her face up
close (and with her hugging my dog) I knew exactly who she was!

Kaneki had read with her when he was still around. I supposed that now she wasn’t able to do that anymore. “Well---I've got some other
stops to make as well but how about we look around for books together!”

I glanced briefly towards Touka and smiled. My thoughts? Worse case: we ran into investigator Amon or his coworkers and I could be a
little buffer between them and my ghoul friends. The innocent human act; clueless and unsuspecting.

"What books do you like to read?" My attention was dragged back to the small girl.
"Well...I'm not actually looking for ones to read that much. I was looking for some old cook books actually. It's...to make Uta’s place look
a bit more....eh---" Out here it was too public with too many people around to overhear.  "---less like a single dude's house?" I chuckled
softly. "It's a little bland." Which ---yeah. That was actually kind of accurate. I suppose ghoul or not, guys were guys. His shop was well
decorated with masks but his actual home was rather undecorated. Not that my own place had been much better in that regard; but at
least I had an excuse.

Thankfully Touka caught on and smiled faintly. With Hinami clinging to Bjorn's side with her fingers weaved through his fur we walked
to the bookstore. Bjorn stayed outside and I followed them both around before spitting off when I spotted what I wanted. Staying at the
back I found some beat up cookbooks. Some older, some newer - almost all of them stained or slightly yellowing pages from kitchen oil,
heat or water damage from spilled ingredients. I opened a few of them and flipped through the old scrawls in the margins of the pages.
Many of them were barely legible but that would be fine.

'Perfect.' I thought smiling to myself and pulling a few more out of the case. Some were about cooking meat, or deserts. If I grabbed a
good assortment it would be more believable. Each one I flipped through to make sure they had notes or other ‘normal’ wear and tear.
After a little while of searching and with an armful of books I went to look for my two ghoul companions.

Hinami and Touka were by the books labeled for ‘young adults’ and the little girl already had her nose in one. “Looks like she found a
book.” Then, I spotted a small stack next to her. “Or a few!”

“Hinami. We can’t get all the books. You’ve got to pick just one for now.” Touka pursed her lips, obviously this had been a conversation
before but the little girl had forgotten or tried to wiggle around it by picking multiple.
“Hey Touka. I don’t mind getting her the extra ones.” I turned to the child and smiled when I saw her brown eyes peek up over the top
of her current book. “Alright? But just the ones you’ve already got here!”

“Really?!!”

“Yep!~” I was delighted to see the little girl grab up all her books and hold them to her chest as she struggled towards the check out desk.

“You don’t have to do that you know...” Touka muttered.


“I know. But---” I paused, looking from Touka to the child who struggled to put the books up on the counter for the poor cashier. “Look
at her! She’s so happy! I really don’t mind. Did you need anything? I could get it too. One order is easier for the cashier.” Touka tucked a
book she’d been holding behind her back and shook her head quickly. I opened my mouth to argue but stopped, smiling with a shrug.

I placed my books next to Hinami’s books and smiled at the cashier. “I’ll be getting all these. Thank you.”

The cashier nodded, thanked us for the patronage and began checking each book for a price and typing it into the system. Once I’d paid I
stepped aside for Touka. While we waited, Hinami smiled gleefully down into the bag that held her book haul. “Thank you Aika-san!”

“Of course. Gotta make sure you have something new to read. You go through them so fast!!!”

I felt my phone ring in my pocket and almost dropped my books in an attempt to answer it post-haste. Without looking at the number I
pushed it to my ear. “Moshi Moshi?” I said, with a small chuckle as I remembered how Uta answered.

“Where are you?” I blinked and pulled the phone away from my head to look at the caller ID finally.
“Renji?”

“Are you okay?”

“...Y-yeah? I’m fine. I’m out shopping with Touka and Hinami right now. I ran into them on my way to the bookstore.”

There was a sigh on the other end and I frowned.  “What’s wrong Renji? Is Uta okay?”

There was a pause on the other end and I could hear the noise of some rather familiar backstreets. The beat and thump of music gave
away his location. “He’s fine. I came to check on you and saw you weren’t back. I thought---You didn’t answer your old number so I had
to call him for this one...”

“....Oh.” I muttered softly, the frown fell off my face quickly as I realized that Renji, and now likely Uta thought I’d up and gone missing
between work and home. “I’m fine. Honestly. I am. I was just out to get some things. I know he left me a note saying to call you if I
needed anything but you really don’t need to check up on me. Unless you wanna beat me up some extra and have an extra training
session!” I tried to lift the mood with a small chuckle. Glancing down I saw Hinami looking up inquisitively as I talked on my phone.

“Is that Yomo-sama!?” I nodded and smiled meekly.
“Here, Renji. Hinami wants to say hi!”

I handed the phone down the the girl and almost choked when the young girl started speaking to the raven ghoul:
“You can’t beat up Aika-san!!! She bought me books!!!” I quickly took the phone from her protesting hands and laughed.
“S-sorry Renji-kun!” I tried to stifle giggles to speak clearly. “D-don’t worry! I’ll message Uta so he’s not worried. I’m absolutely one
hundred percent safe.”

“I’ll come pick you up.”

“What? No. That’s not---” I paused and stopped myself. “Actually! Fine. But if you do that you’re helping me shop! I’m not stopping my
life just because someone wants to be overprotective.” I was actually going to have to talk to Uta about this when he got back. “I’m in the

20th, right down the street from the Café. So I’ll be fine. Message me when you’re close by, okay?”

“---okay. That’s fine.  I’ll be there shortly, Aika.” I heard the other end click and I let out a long sigh. Touka had finished paying and was
giving me an odd stare. So I resigned to explain with an exhausted sigh.
“Apparently Uta asked Renji to check in on me. The men panicked when they didn’t know I was out shopping.”

“Oh I see...Uta’s out of town? I can walk you back to the---”

“Oooh no!” I held up my a hand and shook my head from side to side vigorously. “Stop right there! I told them I don’t need a protection
duty. And honestly. I’m here .” I pushed open the books store’s door and Bjron re-joined the ground with a wagging tail. “With Bjorn and
you too. The Café is right down the street if I needed help. Plus I live in the 4th ward. This place is safe as it gets around here.” I pulled
out my phone and shrugged my shoulders.

“Anyway, this was fun. We should go shopping more often. You two mind a picture?”

## ♥

Uta’s phone vibrated in the inner suit coat pocket and he pulled the device out and looked at the message displayed across the screen.
Behind his mask he smiled where nobody could see.

“No-Face. Come on! It’s showtime! It’s time for fun, it’s time for fun!”

“Right.” As the man passed the red haired woman in a large grinning mask he held up his phone between two fingers for her to see. On
screen a smiling human woman had a child ghoul perched up on her shoulders and by her side another plum-haired ghoul stood
throwing up a peace sign and a small friendly smile.

“I told you she was fine. Sending Renji-kun after her might have been a bit much you know.” The woman cautioned, arms crossed over
her chest. Behind her mask, she raised an eyebrow.

“...Yeah. I know. Come on. Roma’s right. Show time.”


## ♥

My foot tapped gently on the ground as I looked over the silver haired ghoul with an unamused stare. He pulled up in that ‘borrowed’ car
of his and stepped out onto the sidewalk. When he had arrived Touka and Hinami had both said their goodbyes and disappeared down
the street. Touka had to study - and Hinami went with her. The older ghoul keeping the younger safe.

“I sent him a message. But we really are going to have a talk on this whole---” I waved a finger in his direction. “Guard dog thing he has
you doing. Really. I. am. F ine. ” The ghoul didn’t meet my eyes as he spoke up.
“I was also worried. With the way things are right now I’m not certain that someone wouldn’t take the chance with him away. He’s told
us how investigators have been snooping around...”


“Amon...? I can handle him.” I laughed softly; shaking my head. “Seriously, worrying over that? You should really see the man's face
when I tell him not to use such formal family names. He almost blushes. He’s no problem to me. Annoying...but not dangerous!”

“I’ll bring you home now if---”

“Oh no. I told you I was out shopping.” I pointed to the bag in my hand and stepped around him. “If you’ve come out all this way then
you’ve volunteered to help. So I’m going to put this stuff in your car---” I popped open the door to the backseat of the car and placed
down the small pile.

“---And then we are going to go looking for some more home appliances that Uta doesn't have yet. Maybe a house plant or two. I’m really
really bored and the house is too empty.” I turned and started walking down the street again with Bjorn at my heel. Only briefly did I turn
back and raise an eyebrow at him when he hadn’t moved.

“Coming, or no?”
The man sighed and finally started to follow me down the sidewalks. “What exactly are you looking for?”

“Toaster, Blender. Um...some other stuff. But generally that sort of thing. I was buying cook books at the bookstore when you called.” I
smiled faintly as Renji’s eyebrow raised a little bit. Clearly the idea of putting cooking books in the home seemed odd.“Not that I think he
should cook. He managed to burn toast . I can see why he went for arts and crafts and not a restaurant. He’d be absolutely terrible...”

Finally, he cracked a small smile!!! I grinned at the achievement and shrugged. “Anyway. Figured I’d go ahead and make it more...homey.
You know?”

“Yeah. He’s never been one to try to fit in...”

I waved a hand dismissively. “Ah, that’s fine I suppose. But since I was invited to live there too I guess I’ll have to make sure he’s not living
like a lonely has-been frat dude.” I shot Renji a grin and added;  “You’re not living like a lonely has-been frat dude are you?”

“Not exactly.”

“Real convincing Renji. Don’t mind me as I don’t believe you.” Regardless I  grinned as I walked on. As the crowd grew less and less
congested I turned back to my ghoul companion and spoke again. “I mentioned ‘meat smoothie’ as a joke to Uta and he stared at me dead
ass in the face and said he’d try it.”

“---If he does that, he had better clean it out really well because I swear if I get a bone chip in my fruit smoothies---” I shook a fist in the
air; an unspoken and comical threat. “So---What exactly did Uta say to you before he left?”

Renji was mostly quiet, which was the norm for him. Yet it left me leading the conversation. He glanced down at me briefly before
answering. “He stopped by and gave me the computer chip, and asked that I watch out for you. Since he’ll be away.”

I hummed softly. “That's all?”

“He’ll be back by Monday.”

“That’s not really what I meant---Really? That’s not so long. So basically just the rest of the weekend. I suppose I can’t ask you to help
decorate!” The look on Renji’s face made me throw my head back and laugh. “I’m kidding ! Anyway, don’t you have someone you
should be watching out for?”

“More and more each day it seems.”


I faltered a step and fell silent for a minute as we walked. Finally I stopped and turned around. “Look Renji, I really don’t need an escort if
you need to be somewhere. I was mostly just messing with you when I dumped my stuff in your car. The last thing I want is to be a
burden.”

“No, she’ s safe and busy at the moment. The weekend however...”

“---Say no more! I will be fine on the weekend by myself. I can find something to preoccupy myself with.” Like painting my old
apartment before I moved completely out. Note to self: Add paint to the list of things to buy.

“I’ll even stay home. Alright? No wandering. Promise.”

“That’s not necessary, Aika.” The male shook his head, sending silver hair swaying. “...and he’s not the only one who worries. You should
know that all your friends do. Even if it doesn't seem like it; Touka does as well.”

“Alright...okay.” My shoulders slumped a little bit as I let out a long sigh. “Guess there’s no way to get out of making everybody worry
simply by existing, huh?”

“More training, but...likely no. Without a Quinque.”

“I don’t want one.” This time I felt the expression twist on my face as the revolution fell into my stomach like a lead weight.

“I suppose Uta told you what they were.” I couldn’t reply, instead I simply nodded my head while schooling my facial expression back to
neutral. From that moment onward we walked in silence to the store. My head was so full of thoughts, bouncing from topic to topic that
when we reached the store Renji had to call out to me to stop me from passing by.

“Wasn’t this the place?” He asked as his hand closed over one of my shoulders, pulling me to a stop. Startled, I jumped a bit like I was
shocked by a bit of electricity.
“Y-yeah. Sorry. I was just a bit distracted.”

“Bjorn, stay.” I pet his head and pointed at a spot outside the shop before stepping inside. The door jiggled and the woman at the front
desk greeted us kindly. “So, Renji-kun. Who’s the ‘Kitten’ we hear almost nothing about? None of the others are around.”


“Itori definitely puts you up to this.”
“You said that before, and no. Not exactly. I won’t tell her. I’m just curious. Girlfriend?”

“No...just a friend.”

“Uh, huh. And...the cats? The actual cats?”

“Strays. She found them the same night I found her. We’re taking care of them together.”

“How’d you meet?” I smiled deviously as Renji shot me a quick glance, as though I’d let it drop now that he was talking!!! “Come on. I
promise . I won’t say a word to Itori or Uta. Or any of them! ”


“It’s not that...”

I waited a few moments and I really thought he wasn’t going to tell me. By the electric blenders I bent down and looked between them to
find the best one. If Uta was going to put meat and possibly bone into it it would have to be pretty strong. Money from the café was
much better than I’d ever gotten before - I could spare the expense of a more expensive machine. Especially if getting a better one might
keep it from wearing out too quickly. Then Renji started speaking again, quietly so his voice didn’t carry far from us. “I was out looking
for some food. Instead I found her one night about to---” Craning my head upwards I was able to look at his face.

Something in his eyes made me pause and regret my pestering questions. My smile fell a little and I thought about what he said. “She was
about to---” I repeated. “...oh.” I muttered listlessly, as it struck me. The woman was suicidal. And poor Renji had caught her about to do
the deed. Poor Renji - who ate the Humans who threw away their lives.

I turned my attention back to the shelves full of blenders, picking between a black, white or red one. ‘Imagine if he was just a couple
minutes later. He and the Anteiku Ghouls would have had fresh dinner.’ An intrusive thought snaked through my head and hissed in one
ear.


“So you stopped her?” I asked quietly as I picked up a red blender and ignored my inner voice. Some color might be nice. Maybe all the
appliances should match? I turned to start looking to see if they had a toaster in the same color.

“No...I didn’t.”

Surprised, I looked up at Renji inquisitively but he was avoiding my gaze this time. Okay. So he didn’t stop her. But she also didn’t jump.
Clearly. “Soooo...You’re both taking care of some kittens then? Do you like cats? Did you guys name them? Are you keeping them?” He
instantly seemed relieved at the subject change; I watched his shoulders relax as he looked back down at me.
“Yeah...most animals actually. We haven't decided on names.”

“No disagreements from me!~” I chirped happily, getting up to look around more. “You’ve met Bjorn. I fully think that animals are
better than most people.” Stopping in front of the toasters I peered from one box to another before muttering with frustration.  “A
toaster is a toaster is a toaster, right? They look the same, don’t they? It’s only got one job...”

“That one matches the blender.” My companion noted by my side, pointing out a toaster that did in fact match.
“Perfect. That’ll do. Just so long as Uta doesn't mess with the dials I think we can avoid burning down the house.” For half a moment I
tried to do a juggling act with the two items before the blender was plucked out of my hands. “I’ve got it. What else do you need?”

“Last item from here was going to be a rice cooker, but I’ve got to pick up some paint. There are some stains in my old apartment that
need covering before I move completely out. Or there’s gonna be a murder investigation way to close to home...”

Had...Uta not told the group of bar ghouls about my boss attacking my dog in my home. Or what followed? “Long story. And for
another time.” I replied quietly when Renji’s eyebrows twitched upwards. There were not many code words I could use for: ‘My boss
broke into my house and I cracked his skull with a piece of rebar piping.’


Picking out a rice cooker was pretty fast; they did not have many choices of colors so I simply picked up a stainless steel machine. With all
three, two of which Renji carried under each arm; I went to the counter and paid. “Thank you Renji-kun. I actually don’t think I could
have gotten everything back myself. I...didn’t plan very far ahead.”

“---Just the one last stop. I’ll be really fast!”

## ♥

I got out of Renji’s car and grabbed all the bags that I could manage to hold at once before the silver haired man could get to many of
them. “I got it!” I said defiantly biting my lip and I tried to hercules all the bags at one time. At the door to Uta’s shop I put things down
and pulled out my keys to open it up.

Renji hesitated at the door until I waved him in. “If you wanna come in for a minute that’s fine. Thank you for helping. I swear I won’t
go anywhere for the weekend.”

“Why are you repainting your apartment....red?” He asked, lifting up the can to look at the bloody color. Now that we were alone I
suppose there was no reason not to answer.

“Uh...About that. I’m surprised that Uta hasn’t said anything.” I climbed the stairs into the apartment and put all the new machines in
their boxes on the counter. The old cook books I tucked up on a shelf above the sink and smiled as I positioned them in a way that looked
haphazard yet...just right..

“....shoot. I forgot a plant.” I muttered to myself. “This place really could use some green...”

I turned back around so I faced my guest and leaned back on the counter. He was still waiting for a reply so I took in a deep breath and let
it spill out as quickly as possible. Maybe if I said it quickly the memory would sting less?
“The night before my old boss went missing he showed up at my apartment, broke in and attacked my dog. I hit him with a bit of rebar.
In the head...and...well. There’s blood stains on the walls and I couldn’t get them out. Uta suggested the red.  I figured it would cover up
the stains well enough. I suppose black would have worked too.”

“You killed your boss?”

“I mean....” I sucked in air through my teeth and hissed softly. Avoiding steel blue eyes looking at me I tried to focus on the grain in the
wood of the cabinet. “I can’t imagine running around this ward covered in blood helped him survive. The investigators said that Ghouls
got to him before they found him---” I squirmed and felt shame turn my cheeks warm. “That’s...unfair of me. I’m sorry. I’m selfishly
hoping that it had been the Ghouls...”

“---I really would rather think it wasn't my fault. But I don’t think someone’s skull is supposed to crunch like that so if I’m honest about it
to myself I am fairly sure he was probably dead when the Ghouls found him and the fault rests solely on my shoulders....”

I bit my lip to keep it from trembling. Had I ever actually admitted that aloud before? Or had I always just shoved it onto ‘the Ghouls ate
him so..’. Now I was realizing that mistake - had I seemed insensitive before? Perhaps I’d never know.


“It’s okay Aika. It sounds like you did what you had too. Protecting your home and your friend.” Renji leaned down and gently patted
the top of Bjron’s head. The dog looked up but didn’t move away while his head was touched. “I’m the last person you have to make
excuses to. If I’d found someone dead or dying from a wound then even now I’d be the type to take advantage. I’m a scavenger. And back
when I was young I hunted just like Uta and the rest...”

I finally looked up, meeting cool steel briefly before looking away. Tears that I wouldn’t let spill pooled in my eyes until I blinked them
away. I had done what I needed to do. But other Humans wouldn’t see it like that. I’d always look back and think of something that could
have changed the outcome.

But perhaps I should let it go...
The ghouls got to eat an almost guilt free dinner in the 4th ward that night. And my old boss was a piece of shit who took advantage of the
poor and destitute. He got the end he deserved!!!

“Thanks Renji...” I muttered gently, pulling a knife from a drawer, I started to cut open the boxes for the new house warming items.

“Next time someone bothers you just let us know...”

I laughed, more sharply than I meant to. I cringed and shook my head. “Uta said something like that. Except I think he meant that if
someone bothers me he’d eat them.”

Renji cleared his throat with a cough and glanced away. “Yeah. That’s...likely exactly what he meant.”

“I told him he can’t do that or he’s going to run out of annoying people. Also it’ll bring too many investigators. With my boss
disappearing and then that one guy who was on the news...” I sighed softly as I lifted out the rice cooker and dusted off little bits of
styrofoam. I’d need to clean it up but setting it in place made me smile. “You know; even though I had my suspicions I went to him after
my boss ‘incident’. He didn’t even flinch...just ushered us both inside and helped clean me up when I was still in shock.”

There’s a lot about Uta that I’ve chalked up to being ‘ghoul things’. The sniffing for instance. Or offering to eat people who annoyed me!
In their own ways they were endearing. I continued getting the blender and the toaster out; gently peeling the plastic wrap from them.
Grinning with satisfaction at the soft hiss of plastic peeling.

“There...I think it looks a bit more...more---”

“Human.” I turned to Renji and smiled faintly. Placing my hands on my hips I took another look around and nodded.
“I can only hope so at least. If he’s ever put in a position where he has to let an investigator into his house then this will be better than
nothing as camouflage. Now that I’m actually living here I really doubt they’ll suspect him as much---” I explained, waving a hand over
the new additions before placing the hand on my chest. “Biased as they are; I doubt they’d suspect a Human living with a Ghoul.”

I closed my eyes and took a deep breath. “Alright. Thanks Renji-kun...Seriously. I don’t need another guard dog---but I’ll always take a
friend to accompany me. Now go ahead and go make sure your ‘kitten’ is safe. I won’t say a word about her to Uta or anybody. For now--
## -”

Splaying my fingers in front of me I cracked them. With a devilish grin I said:. “As for me: it’s time to clean!~ If I start now it won’t smell
like bleach anymore when he gets home!”

## ♥


The weekend went by pretty quickly all things considered. I kept myself busy and didn’t allow the loneliness to get to me much. Instead I
used the time to clean the floor, scrub the tiles and bleach out soap scum stains in the bathtub. By the end of the day on Sunday evening
even my nose was bothered by the scent so I took Bjorn outside and took a walk around the block before heading back to my apartment
for a while. While I was there I covered the place with plastic and pulled everything from the walls so I wouldn’t get paint on it.

I wasn’t getting my deposit back anyway, so I could just leave the frame of the futon here for the next poor sob who rented the place.
Looking around I saw that nearly half my clothing had already migrated to my new home. Food was sparse in the mini fridge and a thin
layer of dust was building up on surfaces that I normally dusted off regularly.

With a light heart and a cheery smile I picked up the rest of my skulls, a bag with the remainder of my clothing, and left the building
emptier than it had been since I moved in. As I left the building I flipped the light switch and closed the door behind me.

Skulls and bags in hand I passed Ms. Kirin. She did a double-take and glanced between my items and my face. She was still skittish but her
eyes seemed to glint dangerously when she spoke up this time. “Moving away dear?”

“...hum? No. Not really. Moving in actually.” I took a few steps closer to Uta’s shop door and pulled out a key to unlock it. I didn't take
my eyes off the old ghoul and I pulled open the door so I saw how her eyes widened as she realized what I meant. I hoped that I made it
clear that I was still important to the shop owner. “Oh...I see. Can I speak to the young man for a moment?”

My mouth went dry. Uta wasn’t here . I shook my head and forced a smile as I lied through my teeth. “Sorry. He took the weekend off. I
insisted he took some time off for himself once in a while. Especially with my moving in. When the shops open again I’m sure he’d be
happy to help if you have an issue with your mask. Goodnight.”

I shut the door, practically threw down the skulls and bag on a nearby shelf and turned the locks. Staying put, I held my breath as I
listened. My heart stopped when the knob of the door wiggled a little and then the woman’s footsteps walked away. After a minute I
sucked in a breath and felt my eyes tear up as I sank to my knees in front of the door.

Whining Bjorn came close to my side and pressed his head into my shoulder. “It’s okay, big guy. It’s okay. Everything is fine...” Still
shaken, I picked myself up and brought my things upstairs. Once there I went to the windows and made sure they were all locked and
closed up after airing the place out.

“He'll be back tomorrow. Nothing to worry about.” I murmured softly, convincing myself as I looked around the apartment. It was
clean. That at least brought a genuine smile to my face but it couldn't get rid of the worry. Finally I plucked up my phone and typed out a
message to someone I didn’t think I’d be asking help from.

Aika: Hey, I know this is an odd request. Can I stay with you tonight?
## Notes:
A/Notes: I imagine that Ghouls would have some overprotective traits that would be a bit overbearing or come out
as being kinda controlling in some circumstances. Either needing to be curbed or gotten used to. (Or a combo of
the two) While it can be a little endearing in a fictional story; These I know can be some rather toxic traits in real life
relationships. And I apologize if this makes anybody uncomfy!






## Chapter 41: Chapter 41: Helplessness
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 41:

I stood by the door waiting with a small bag for an overnight stay. Tucked away was my work clothing as well as my set of workout
clothing for training with Renji. I nervously played at the end of the strap of my bag until it began to fray under my fingertips. Right after
I messaged for help I’d also made sure to message Uta and Renji. While I refused to ring the alarm bells that would pull Renji from his
own plans or worry Uta: The least I could do was let them know I was spending the night over at a friend's house tonight and I was safe.

My body jerked when there was a knock on the door of the shop. Frozen in place, I waited.
“ Hey . Are you there? Aika?” I let my held breath go and leaned against the doorframe; heart in my throat as I spoke up.

“Touka...Hi.” I said quietly as I let the door click open and peeked out. My eyes darted behind her, up and down the alleyway. Spotting
nothing I let the door swing open a bit further and looked back at my coworker with a weak smile. The young woman on the doorstep
had a bored expression on her face, arms crossed over her chest until she spotted my expression. She followed my gaze up and down the
street with concern.

“You said somebody was bothering you...?”

“My neighbor was being weird again...with Uta out---” I trailed off before adding: “---and I know Renji is busy with something tonight
so...I’m so sorry to bother you. I know you’ve got school to study for...”

“Hey, it’s no problem. Come on. If we hurry, my friend from school is coming by with some home cooked food. Hinami heard you were
coming and was excited. It’ll be fun I guess.”

I smiled weakly as she waved me on. I followed her out with Bjorn in tow only turning back to lock up the door. Staying close on the
heels of the purple haired woman I couldn’t help but to keep looking over my shoulder. We walked in silence for a while until it started to
bother me, grating on my already fried nerves.

“---I’m probably being dramatic or something. I really am sorry...”

“Nah. You're probably right.” Touka shoved her hands into her pockets of her jeans and pursed her lips together firmly. “Don’t worry
about it. Anyway, if you get eaten then I’ve got to do even more work. Nobody else will chase around Roma cleaning up all her messes. I
sure as hell don’t want to. If Kaneki were around I’d make him.”

I chuckled softly and shrugged my shoulders. True enough. Touka stepped onto the subway and took a car that didn’t have any other
passengers and sat down.
“I was kinda waiting for something to rattle you...” The young woman shot me a deceptively bored expression and added casually. “You
know you could just report her to the CCG and---”

I leaned forward and cut her off with a whispered hiss. “No! Absolutely not . I don’t even want to tell Uta . I just want her to leave me be.
Nothing else!” And Uta would be just as likely to hurt her as the CCG at this point. After the numerous warnings she’d gotten. Of
course, let us not forget there was the ‘example’ of why not to go after me still lingering in parts and pieces in our fridge! I rubbed my
hands over my face and pinched the bridge of my nose.

“I’m probably going to have to talk to Uta about it though. There’s no way I can just not mention it to him...”


The ghoul beside me watched me for a moment before turning to look out the window as the 4th ward sped by us and we headed
towards the 20th ward. The sun was going down, but beside Touka I was at least in better hands than my own. Even trained I’d be
nothing next to a Ghoul...
I sunk further in my seat and found myself staring at the palms of my hands helplessly.




“Hey-Hey! We’re here. Are you okay?” I blinked. Emerging out of my daze and looked up, wide eyed at Touka as she tugged on my arm
to follow her out of the subway car. Bjorn kept up to follow us and looked up at me curiously as I allowed myself to be dragged along.
“Come on, before we end up in Itabashi!” She finally released me when my feet caught up with hers and I steadied myself without
tripping.

“Yoriko is going to be there any minute, so hurry up! And even if the food is bad you're going to say you love it.” I raised my eyebrows,
growing further and further from my dower mood I started to smile.
“Oh? Does her cooking suck---?” I stopped myself. I really could have slapped my own face at this point. ”Sorry, no. Of course you don’t
know. Sure. Sure. Yeah. I’ll tell her it’s amazing.”

“And eat it.” She insisted, not bothered by my small fuck up.

“Course.” I cracked a bigger smile. It seemed that perhaps Touka didn’t hate all Humans. Perhaps it was simply just about them knowing
about her nature as a Ghoul? She led me to a small apartment where she waved me through a couple hallways and up a set of stairs until
she got to her door. Keys out, door open and she waved us in. “Tadaima!!! Hinami. It’s us. Did Yoriko get here yet?”

Around the corner of the small apartment Hinami appeared and lit up like a light bulb when seeing me and more specifically Bjorn.
“Aika-san! Bear-bear!~” Bjorn, much to his own credit, went straight to the young ghoul. His tail was very slightly wagging. I grinned
because sooner or later he was going to have to admit that he liked the attention despite his protests! Stubborn dog. Stubborn, but sweet.

Slipping off my shoes near the doorway I stepped further inside to take a look around. I was struck by how ordinary it seemed. It was a
student's home. Books and papers, small but cozy. She even had some kitchen items that weren’t strictly necessary for her ghoul diet.
Perhaps it was simply a case of how well integrated into school and society she was.

“She’s not here yet!” Hinami answered Touka’s question as she led Bjorn back to where she had been sitting and patted a spot for him.
The small ghoul leaned against the dog and pulled out one of the books to resume reading. Touka sighed and waved her hand around the
room.
“Well...It’s small so you’ll have to find a place to sleep on the floor, but I’ve got extra pillows and blankets. The bathroom is at the end of
the hallway there.” Touka pointed around the small apartment before watching as I looked around. My mouth automatically curled into
a grin as I continued to notice common items found in a ‘human’ house hold. A rice cooker. A stack of clean dishes next to the sink. A
dirty mug from instant coffee. When I laughed softly Touka raised an eyebrow and crossed her arms across her chest indignantly.

“What?”

“Nothing! Nothing bad! It’s just I’m so glad that it seems to just be Uta who can’t decorate a house to look normal!” I giggled a bit harder
when a blush came to Touka’s face.
“What do you mean? This place is a mess...” Touka looked around her humble little home with flushed cheeks.

I shook my head and smiled. “It’s not a mess! It’s a bit cluttered but it's normal clutter. Nobody's home looks like a magazine and
it’s....cozy.” I took a seat next to Hinami and looked over her shoulder to see what she was reading. To my surprise the girl turned and

smiled; holding the book at a better angle for me to read along with her.

And so---Thirty minutes later Hinami was explaining the plot of the book to me with gusto as I listened in rapt interest. The reading she
had done with Kaneki had really helped her learn quite fast and she’d taken quickly to learning more and more even when he was missing.
I glanced up once in a while, looking for our host. Touka had gotten her studies out and sat at her desk, bent over, her eyebrows
scrunched as she wrote on pages and pages of homework.



There was a soft knock on the door and Touka was up in seconds, running across the room to answer it as fast as possible. I turned from
Hinami’s books and watched the hallway to see who it was that appeared. After just a few moments a young woman with reddish brown
hair entered the room. She had bangs across her forehead and the rest of her bob only went to her chin. Her green eyes surveyed the room;
quickly spotting the large dog next to the small girl!

“Wow! That’s such a big dog!” Bjorn’s head raised up and he sniffed the air; and sneezed. I raised my hand to wave with a small sheepish
smile..
“That big goof would be mine. Hi. I’m Aika. It’s nice to meet you.”

The girl beamed happily stepped inside, kicking off her shoes quickly near the door.
“Touka didn’t say she was having anybody else over! But you’ll have to test this new recipe I’m trying!!!” She held up a big pot which was
placed upon the counter on her way in. Touka followed her friend back into the room with one of the most peacefully happy expressions
I’d ever witnessed on her face.

“Well I’d be happy to try some. I hope it’s as good as Touka says because honestly I am starving. I spent the whole day cleaning my
boyfriend's house and I totally forgot to eat.” I must have said the right thing because Touka’s friend grinned cheerfully and looked really
pleased. And Touka blushed. Again!

“So how do you know Touka!?”

“Work.” I said with a reserved smile. “At the café. I started not too long ago. I normally only work in the mornings though. Touka can be
grumpy but she’s probably one of the more responsible people there!” I grinned, seeing Touka’s face further redden.

“And your boyfriend!!!!? Does he work at the café?” She glanced between Touka and I quickly and ‘whispered’: “It’s not that older
college student that hangs out there all the time right?”

“Nishiki? Heck nah!” I sputtered and laughed; shaking my head fervently from side to side. “For one: Ew. He’s a nice enough guy and all
but---soooo not my type. Plus, He’s got a girlfriend. My boyfriend doesn't work there. He only visits once in a while.”

“Oh I see. So what’s your type?” The girl grinned and leaned forward on her elbows on the small kotatsu. Now it was my turn to blush.
“Uh well...”

I hesitated for a minute, stumbling over words until I started; mumbling. “Um...I guess. Tall, dark and handsome?” I chuckled and
winced at my own cliche description. He was all three of those things I suppose. “Goth? Tattoos and piercings. He’s...kind of calming to
be around but also fun. Never boring! And he’s an artist. He’s really creative...” I smiled, describing him more to myself now as I leaned
my chin on my hand. “---And really sweet. He brought me brownies to work just because I said I liked them one time....”

I stopped and flushed darker red when I saw the young lady across from me staring with wide, gleefully shining eyes. She saw that I
stopped and squealed softly. “You obviously love him! It’s so cute! I keep telling Touka she’s gonna find someone like that some time.

But she’s never been interested in anybody at school and she hates gossiping about guys!” Still flushed pink I sat back and ducked my
head down.
“Ah, yeah...I suppose that...I do...”

From beside me I heard Hinami giggle and sit down beside me with a huge grin on her face. A second later I had arms around me,
hugging tightly. Before I could ask what it was for, or why she’d done it the child stood up and announced she’d be right back before
running off to the bathroom. Touka stared off, away from myself or her Human friend. While her eyes were towards her balcony
window, I saw her glance my way from the corner of her eye. As soon as she saw I spotted the look she quickly looked away again.

“Soooo how long have you and him been together? Have I seen him at the cafe?” The second question was aimed towards Touka.
“He doesn't visit the cafe all that often. I don’t think you’ve met him.” Touka answered, shrugging her shoulders.

“Together-together---is uh....” I shuffled awkwardly. “Not too long. He just invited me to live with him just the other day. And before
that we’d been going to places for fun. I suppose they were dates but neither of us really explicitly said so.”

“Okaaaaay. Well how did you meet?”

“He makes masks. His shop is actually only down the road from my apartment. Where I used to live. I just went in one day and ordered a
mask because they were so interesting. I suppose from then on I just stopped by to see his art and brought him a coffee. After that---” I
tapped my chin to think. “He brought me to Anteiku for a coffee since I’d been bringing him a bunch. I suppose not too long after that I
got a job at Anteiku. Even after my mask was done I kept visiting and bringing coffee. I guess I just liked him from the start...”

That was skipping quite a bit, but Touka’s Human friend didn’t need to know what she didn’t already know. But Yoriko didn’t seem to
mind if I was leaving out big details. She was way too busy looking completely ecstatic that she was able to gossip.

My stomach growled unexpectedly and I flushed darker red and bowed my head. “S-sorry.”
“OH! I almost completely forgot. I brought food! It should still be warm in the pot and there’s plenty for everybody!”

Touka stood up and walked to a cupboard where she brought out plates.
“Hinami. Dinner!” Touka yelled out for the child ghoul. I glanced briefly towards Touka and schooled my expression to be as neutral as
possible. Was...Touka and Hinami going to eat the food as well?

I smiled and thanked Touka when she gave me a bowl and utensils. As Yoriko scooped out some of the stew like food into my bowl. I
took a deep breath in and smelled the food. Surprisingly---despite some initial fears I was pretty sure it would be edible. Good even.

“Itadakimasu!!!~” I happily cheered before taking a bite of the food. I held back a cough and swallowed it down. Alright. So edible was
debatable. Swallowing it I managed to put a smile on my face and praise the food as Touka had asked me to. “Wow, that's really good! It’s
funny I just bought a bunch of cooking books so I could learn. Maybe you’ll tell me what you used in this!”

Despite my words I would need a drink after this food. Water preferably to dilute just how much salt this woman had put into it! Apart
from that, it really wouldn’t have been bad. Yoriko absolutely loved the praise though and I saw Touka take a bite of the food and smile
before swallowing it down.

I’d seen how Human food affected Ghouls before and I was in no hurry to see it again, yet when Hinami came back she picked up her
own ‘food’ and ate it down quickly as though she couldn’t get enough of it. It was odd after seeing Uta’s reaction to eating things. He had
seemed to struggle keeping a straight face.


“You said you didn’t eat anything all day, so do you want some more?” I glanced at the large dish that now was nearly empty - the last bit
being offered to me.

“I...suppose. I’d feel bad though.”

“Nonsense! I can make Touka more anytime! Please have the rest!”

With only a few moments more of hesitation I decided to ‘graciously’ accept - thus sparing Touka and Hinami from eating any more.
“Thank you so much. Cleaning all day really exhausted me. I was really happy when Touka invited me over.” While not exactly true, it
worked out fine enough.

My phone chimed softly and I pulled it from my pocket to see who it was.
Uta: Is everything alright?
I hesitated in answering; fingers hovering over ‘y’ to type yes. In the end I decided to answer truthfully.

Aika: Not exactly. I’ll have to talk to you later about it. Safe at Touka’s right now. Sorry if the house smells like bleach when you get
home. I did some cleaning! ♥

“Was that him!? Is he coming here?” I tucked away my phone and shyly smiled.
“I just let him know a little while ago I’d be here. But no. At least I’m pretty sure he isn’t coming here. I think he just wanted to make
sure I was safe.”

“He’s back then...?” Touka raised her head from her bowl of food, her fork poked at a bit still left in her bowl.

“Renji said that he would be back by tomorrow.” I then quickly added, for Yoriko’s benefit. “He’s been out of town for a few days with
some friends of his. So that’s why I took the opportunity to clean. I thought I’d surprise him. But being pretty much alone was kinda
boring, you know?”

The young woman nodded emphatically with flying red-brown hair! “You get used to being around people pretty quickly. Especially if
you were hanging out every day! But I just noticed---!!!” She pointed at my arm and I followed her gaze. I’d forgotten almost completely
about it but under a short sleeve my new colorful tattoo poked out a little.

“Oh that's a tattoo.” I said, rolling up my sleeve to show it off.

Touka leaned forward now, taking a good look at the design. “Did Uta-san do that? It looks like his work.”

“Yup!” I grinned and pointed out the earrings in my ears. “After he poked holes in my ears he seemed interested in tattoos. So I asked him
to make a design. I’ve always wanted a tattoo but never really pulled the trigger on it.” I gently swiped my finger over the design following
the circular trail of linework. After having to wrap it daily; today was the first day I hadn’t had to keep it wrapped at all. “I’m kinda
relieved it stopped itching so badly. It was really difficult to ignore for a while there...”

Shortly after Touka stood up and announced she’d be right back before going straight to the bathroom. My phone chimed again and I
took a peek at the message.

Uta: I won’t be back until later tomorrow night.
Aika: Okay. I’ll be okay. Staying with Touka tonight, girls night thing? And I already have my work clothes here. And after work I have
training with Renji-kun. I’ll see if he can bring me home after that.
Uta: Okay, don’t let him beat you up too badly. How is the tattoo doing?
Aika: First day unwrapped, not itchy at all. Seems okay. Haven't had much ink or blood leaking. It’s not red at all. I’ll send a picture.

## Aika : Image58930.png Sent
Aika: How is your thing going? Everybody safe?
Uta: Looks like it's healing well. Everybody is fine.
Uta: Itori says hello.
Uta: Nico also says hello.

Moments later I got a second message from someone else.

: Hey! How’s it going!? Uta says you're having a girl thing without me!!!
Aika: Kind of? More complicated than that. At Touka’s now.
