I flinched when I thought I overheard Touka retch from the bathroom so to quickly turn Yoriko’s attention away I opened up my
playlist of music and started to go through it; asking what kind of music she liked until Touka came back.

## ♥

It was pretty early when Touka and Yoriko both wanted to sleep, and Hinami had already dozed off while half laying on Bjorn. I stayed
on the ground, head propped up with pillows as I stared at the ceiling barely illuminated by the outside lights. The curtains didn’t keep all
of it out; casting shadows and shapes.

Odd... It’s so hard to sleep here.

The noise of the 4th ward was missing. The peace that had been nice during the day plagued me during the night. It really was laughable
that I found my own peace in being able to sleep to the sounds of chaos. Without it it was much harder to close my eyes and drift off.
Either that - or it was sleeping on the floor.


## ♥



Monday’s suck.

A universal truth by Aika Kaneshiro. I could write a book about that if I wanted. I squeezed my eyes shut for a moment, trying to block
out the entire day with only my eyelids.

Yet when it came time it was Touka who woke me up. Which I must admit did not make the day suck any less. That was to say; I much
prefer Uta’s method of waking me. I groaned as I sat up, hearing multiple cracks and pops of my misaligned spine shift back into their
proper places. If work wasn’t going to be bad enough I knew that punishing training from Renji was going to straight up kill me !

Sluggishly I manage to get up; all the while being scolded the whole time by Touka who scowled at me. While also telling me that she’d

already let me sleep in. I yelped softly when a pillow flew and smacked me in the head when my body sank back down to laying down at
one point. I found myself thinking that if Uta were here he’d be trying to get me to stay at home - sleeping in his bed or watching him
work on art and masks.

After being smacked by a pillow I was up on my feet for good. I took a few minutes in the bathroom to change into my work clothing,
brush my teeth and straighten up my appearance. At the very least I had to try to make it look like I hadn’t slept with my face accidentally
pressed to the hardwood floor.

I exited the bathroom and let the little ghoul girl run past me. Bjorn stood up and walked over to me, shoving his nose into my stomach
before walking to the door where he sat his butt down and waited.
“Touka, I’m going to head out now. Bjorn should walk before work!” From her desk the ghoul raised a hand and waved.
“Yeah, Okay. See you at work.”

Touka’s friend was hanging over her shoulder as I closed the door to the apartment. As I made my way down the stairway to the ground
floor and street level I gently pat Bjorn’s head and whispered thanks for his good behavior.

I took the long way around the area with Bjorn at my side, making sure that we walked for as long as we could before heading to the cafe.
Ten minutes til open I entered and smiled as I saw Touka had arrived before me. “Hey. You get lost on the way here or something?”

“Bjorn needed to walk out some energy before work. Did Hinami---”

“ Here! ” I turned around and smiled, half interrupted by the very person I meant to ask about.
“Hey, do you think you can watch Bjorn again today?” My face split into a grin as the small girl nodded her head fervently. “Alright.
Then I’ll leave him in your very good care!” Bumping him lightly, I nudged the mountainous dog towards the small girl and whispered.
“Go on, big guy! Make sure she doesn't get into trouble.” Wagging, the dog padded over towards the girl and let her entwine her fingers
into his fur once more before following her - or leading her up the stairs of the cafe. From my angle it was hard to tell who was really in
charge.

“Alright!” I put on a big smile and tried to pump myself up for a long day ahead of us. “Opening time, isn’t it?”

## ♥

When the manager came in I asked for a coffee made for myself, drinking it down for the burst of energy from the caffeine. Like my
cleaning at Uta’s shop, I threw myself into the work while bearing a happy grin. It was easy to get lost in the menial tasks of physical labor.
Cleaning or running coffee back and forth made it easy to go on autopilot. While cleaning the shop and apartment it kept me from
thinking about Ms. Kirin. Here it kept me from thinking about telling Uta about Ms. Kirin. I only knew it was the end of my day when a
head of silver hair came in the door and leaned against the counter.

I did a double take and glanced at the clock on the wall only to find that I’d actually been working almost an half hour past normal. “I was
caught up in something, so I am a little later than expected.”

“No problem. I totally didn’t notice. It got late really fast...” I glanced around quickly and then sighed softly. Of course. Without Roma
coming in and breaking everything I totally lost track of time. Looking around the cafe now I was glad for her absence. The place was

more cheerful and clean . At least for this short time I didn’t have to worry about stepping over ceramic shards or accidentally cutting
myself!

“Give me a few minutes and I’ll get changed and be ready to go in no time. Is it okay if I drop Bjorn off at home?”

Renji nodded and sat himself down at the counter while he waited for me to run up the stairs to the sitting room and grab my bag of
things. I waved to Hinami and Bjorn who lay together,  the younger ghoul once again reading while using him as a pillow. On her head
her small bird perched happily singing some whistle it had learned.

In a side room I changed out of the uniform and into a tank top, baggy pair of pants and sneakers that I liked because they were easy to
move in. Just because of the weather I topped the outfit with my winter coat.  I made sure my mask and knife lay in an easily accessible
part of my bag just in case and slung it over my shoulder as I emerged. With a short whistle I called Bjorn. He sat up, wiggled out from
under the ghoul child and tread after me as I passed through the upstairs sitting room.  “I’ll see you tomorrow, Hinami!”

I smiled as I heard the small voice of the girl call out a goodbye behind me. By Renji’s side I smiled faintly and rolled my shoulders. “Not
sure how I feel about getting beat up today, but I suppose I’ll make do. I’m ready when you are!”

Walking out of the café doors I waved back to my coworkers briefly before turning towards Renji.
“Heard anything new from Uta?” The small shake of the head was what I figured but I still felt disheartened. “He told me last night he
wouldn’t be back until late tonight. So I suppose I can train as late as you’d like to continue. But after I have a favor to ask?” Steel grey-
blue eyes turned towards. “Can you bring me home after?” Renji’s eyebrows lifted up slightly but he nodded.

“I intended on bringing you back. Is something wrong? Never thought you’d ask.”

“Um...kinda. The neighbor is acting a little strange again. So last night I asked Touka to come get me and I spent the night with her.” The
raven ghoul stopped walking and I stumbled a few steps ahead, turning back to give him a confused look.
“If you were in trouble why didn’t you say anything?”

“I mean...you said you were going to be busy. It wasn’t that big a deal I just---” I bit my lip. Something hadn’t felt right last night and I
hadn’t felt completely safe. Perhaps it was just how persistently creepy she’s been. “---But I didn’t want to bother you. You’ve got your
own people to worry about. I didn’t want to waste your time.”

Renji sighed, shaking his head slowly. The man faced forward again and started walking again; a faster pace now so he kept just ahead of
me. I caught back up and tried to match speed with him. “I’m serious, Renji. If it had been an emergency, I’d have called you right away.
Asking to stay with Touka was just a sort of extra precaution.” He shook his head from side to side again and let out a rumbling grumble.

The rest of the way to his car, and then for the ride towards the fourth ward I had to deal with the disquieted silence. Infact, Renji stayed
quiet while I dropped Bjorn off in the apartment, while I got the dog food and even as I quickly checked that I hadn’t gotten anything
new from Uta regarding when he would be getting home. From the apartment Renji led us to yet another entrance to the 24th ward.
Only once he threw off his coat and held up his fists did he speak again.

I shivered when I saw his face, scowling and serious. “Aika, for your own good. You need to understand that you can’t deal with a Ghoul
on your own...” I felt my heart freeze up briefly from the sharp reprimand. Of course I knew that! Did he think I didn’t ---?

I wasn’t given the time to rebut his statement, or explain that I was aware. I barely even had time to get my arms up to block a punch that
rattled the bones from my arms to my teeth and instantly made both arms feel weak like jello.

The second punch came from below and hit home over one side of my ribs and toppled me off my feet and to the ground.

As I coughed and sputtered for air I stared at the ground with a new and sudden helplessness clouding my thoughts.
Useless. Weak. How was any Human expected to fight a Ghoul? The punch to the ribs felt like being struck by a car! I looked up from the
ground, still gasping and squinted my eyes to see Renji standing over me. Fighting a Ghoul for real; I’d be dead in moments. No amount
of training would fix that. Not the training I’d had years ago with a sword. Not the training with a knife. Not running miles, or living
weights or vigorous stretching.

He’d never even need his Kagune.

Why even try...

I slumped further to the ground and hung my head. Wincing and chewing back a cry of pain I dragged in deeper breaths.
“Shit. Aika. Are you alright?” I cringed from the worried tone and felt the first sparks of helpless fury well up in my chest. Moments ago
he seemed happy to ‘teach me a lesson’! Now he was worried after doing the damage?!

“m’Fine.” I murmured quietly. It was a struggle but I fought to stand back up and stepped away from him. Disheartened, I slowly made
my way to my stuff, leaned down carefully for my jacket and then bag. As I started to climb back out of the underground tunnels he
called out again.

“Aika...? Where are you going?”

“ Home, Renji. I’m going home. That’s enough . I get it...You don’t have to bother with this anymore. You’ve proved your point. Its’s
been a waste of fucking time for the both of us, hasn’t it?”

"Aika...that's not what I meant."

"But it's true." I hissed out between clenched teeth. "Because I'm just Human. That's all. I'll always be weaker and always need to have
someone bringing me place to place like a fucking escort. So it's just another cage just like at my family’s and I'll never be free from
someone hanging over my shoulders and----"

As I twisted around to look down at the ghoul below my fingers slipped from the thin metal bars slicked with sweat from my palms.. "---
fuck !!!" A moment before falling I grasped uselessly at air. Before hitting the ground I saw the ghoul dive forward. Too slow.

## Pop.

A yelp escaped my lips as one leg caught my weight and the other twisted under me. My body didn't hit the ground, saved by a pair of
arms around my waist. Renji pulled me back up before I could take the concrete ground to the face.


"Are you okay?"


"Stupid Ghoul architecture!!!! Stupid slippery ladders. I'm fi-ahhh! !" I cursed, trailing off to hissing as I tried to put weight on my leg and
it buckled under me again only to send me back into the arms trying to support me.
“Aika...I did not mean that you could never defend yourself. Only that now you can’t. Until you can, you need to rely on us.”  Still filled
with bitter fury, I death gripped onto him and glared. Gradually though, upon surveying his tired and worried expression --- I relented
and relaxed.

Soft spoken, Renji began to explain. “...I do have people I have to look after. I’m stronger than them. So I have to make sure they stay safe.
Family and friends. They mean everything to me. I can not bear to lose anymore people, Aika...” Gently, as though I were made of glass he
stood me up on both feet while allowing me the choice to continue to lean on him. “Aika. You’re one of those people.” He rubbed his
face with a free hand and sighed. “It’s been a long while since I’ve seen Uta care about anything as much as he does about you. I really
don’t want to imagine what would happen if you died. Especially on my watch...” My anger evaporated and I slumped more of my
weight into his side. He supported me effortlessly.

“I’m going to pick you up.” I nodded weakly; my only reply apart from a small pained hiss through clenched teeth. As he picked up my
things off the ground and placed the strap around his shoulder I muttered faintly.
“I’m sorry Renji-kun....I didn’t mean to get angry at you. I like the training. I really do. Even though Uta complains about the bruises.”
My lips twitched faintly into a weak smile. “...I just...hate feeling helpless.”

“...I get it. How is your side?”

“Hurts. But I don't think anything is broken.” I muttered, taking in a deep breath right after and wincing. It was going to hurt for a few
days. My leg on the other hand might actually be a bigger issue. While obviously not broken, it had twisted and most likely sprained. That
had been entirely my own fault. Despite my complaints about the unsafe nature of ghoul architecture; had I been paying attention I
wouldn’t have fallen. Plus; I should have been extra careful since I’d already almost fallen from them in the past.

“...Renji...can you stay until Uta gets back?”

“Sure. Are there any supplies at Uta’s to take care of your injuries?”

“I’ve got some in the bag with me. But it can wait till we get someplace with better lighting and a comfy couch...”


Renji climbed up the ladder with me propped carefully in his arms with infinitely more grace than I could have ever hoped to possess. At
the top he quickly peeked to make sure the way was clear, placed me on the street level and then climbed out after.

“What happened last night ? How did your neighbor scare you?” He asked as he dragged the manhole cover back to its position.
“Something must have spooked you...”

Once I was back up in his arms and on our way I answered his question.“Well...She asked to see Uta. And I didn’t tell her he was away of
course. I just said that I’d insisted he took the weekend off and wouldn’t be disturbed. But I think she could tell I was lying. When I
closed the door she tried to open it to get in anyway. I had it locked so...she didn’t get in but...”


The arms holding me stiffened up quickly and I looked away from the street long enough to spot Renji’s tense expression. “How long has
this woman been an issue?”

“...Well. She used to yell at me before I knew Uta. Throw bottles. Just generally surly old woman behavior. But after she saw me hanging
around him she began to act a bit creepier. Followed me. I suppose it came to a head when she realized I knew about Uta. After that she
basically chased me back to Uta’s shop one time. She’s said some...really unnerving things. Uta already warned her off at least once. She
left me be and practically fled from me when I walked nearby up until yesterday but I guess it didn’t work very well in the long run.
Especially when he’s not around...”

“She’ll need a more significant warning then...”

I bit my lip and glanced down the street. “I think if Uta has to ‘speak’ to her again he’s just going to kill her.”

“...As Ghouls we are conditioned from a young age to protect ourselves...and those who mean the most to us. Against Humans, but also
other Ghouls...”

“...a real dog-eat dog-world. Huh?” I murmured.

We rounded the corner and were within sight of the shop. The closed sign remained in place and the street was empty save but for the
regular sounds of the city rumble and murmur. “He’s not back yet.” The silver haired ghoul said quietly; glancing up and down the
backstreet.
“You’ll stay though, right?” I asked again. There was very little chance he’d change his mind, especially after all he’d said down in the
underground. But I couldn’t help but worry a little that I’d be alone again.

“Yeah. I’ll stay until Uta finally shows back up...”

I squirmed in Renji’s arms, almost upsetting myself onto the ground while trying to grab my keys from a pocket. “Here. These keys to the
door. I can probably walk on my own for a little bit. Or at least limp.” He took the keys from my hands and fought with the door until it
finally opened up.

Inside the doorway Renji set me down on my feet. Immediately I felt my way to the light switch and flicked on the dim, moody shop
lights along with the brighter lamps that illuminated masks on the wall. “I’m sorry it probably just smells like bleach still. I was cleaning
up for a while. I had hoped I could surprise Uta a little bit. But I also planned on trying to air it out a bit more with fans.”

“I don’t think I’ve ever seen it this clean...” Renji glanced over the displayed, swiping a finger over a shelf to see it was clean.

“You should see the apartment! I put all the things I’d got while shopping in their place and I think it’s really coming together!” Limping,
I made it to the stairway and started to climb up by leaning on the handrail. Above us I could hear Bjorn scrambling and then winced as
he barked like mad behind the door.
“Okay, Okay! Bjorn. Calm. Caaaaaalm !~”  Renji stayed close behind me, likely making sure I didn’t fall backwards down and hurt
myself further.

I opened the door and smiled when I saw Bjorn bouncing to greet me. He sniffed the air and gently prodded at my side until I swatted his
nose gently.
“ Oof . Bear-bear. Little hurt here. Don’t poke.” Calming, the giant canine backed up and circled to watch from further away as both I
and Renji entered the apartment. I limped towards the kitchen and grabbed the coffee pot out of the clean dishes rack.


“Take a seat, I'll make some coffee. Uta says it’s almost as good as Anteiku’s so---”

“...Aika. Take a look at your leg before you do anything. I can make coffee.”

“But---” I blinked as the coffee pot was gently taken from my hands and I was herded carefully to the side. My view of the counter was
blocked. Instead, now I was staring at the back of his white button up.
“Unlike Uta---I make pretty good coffee. I used to work at Yoshimura’s as well when I was younger. Go take care of yourself...”

I took a deep breath and let it out slowly, smiling as Renji glanced over his shoulder. I could have sworn that I’d seen a small smile before
he turned back to the coffee brewer. “Yeah. Okay, okay. I suppose if you're not using that old coffee machine Uta has, it can’t be that
bad...I’ll take care of my injuries first.”

On the couch I sat myself down and looked for my bag. Renji had placed it down on the little coffee table.  I dragged it close enough to
pull out my little first aid kit with a little ‘Ah ha.’ . Rolling up my pant leg I held back a small gasp at the swelling that had already made
my ankle sensitive and red. A little bit of prodding and some painful, yet manageable movement tests at least confirmed that it really likely
wasn’t broken. If it had been I had little doubt I’d have fallen right over when trying to limp about.

All the while I tried to forget how much trouble I’d have been in if I’d gone and gotten it broken...

“Renji-kun, I’m going to get cleaned up before I wrap it. It looks okay all things considered. With a wrap and a little bit of rest I should be
good in no time. Maybe skip a couple training sessions if you're gonna start hitting me that hard from now on though...” Renji grunted in
an affirmative from the other room so I stood up, carefully minding both ribs and ankle, and walked to the bedroom. Gathering up clean
clothing I shuffled into the bathroom to quickly douse myself in warm water, soap, more water and then finally dressed in a new set of
fresh clothing.



Hair still damp, but dressed and presentable I went back to the couch and sat my butt down beside the silver haired ghoul. Renji sat
quietly sipping his steaming drink with eyes fixed upon the television across the room. “There’s a cup there for you. Five tablespoons of
sugar right?”

I snorted softly, shaking my head. “I used to put in five tablespoons---” I plucked the mug up quickly before he could reply. He’d already
put it in and there was no taking it back out. I took a sip and sighed. “---I’ve been cutting back since that much sugar is not exactly
healthy. I’ve been making an effort lately to---” Give a shit? “---take care of myself. But I suppose one cup of sugar coffee wouldn’t hurt!~”

“Since when?”

“I don’t know, maybe...a few weeks?” I flushed under the inquisitive gaze of the silver haired ghoul and was forced to look away. “---Since
you agreed to train me. And partly because Uta seemed so curious about my diet. It’s...a bit funny how he likes to watch me cook. Can’t
imagine it’s interesting watching someone boil water for shitty ramen packs every night. So I decided to learn to cook other things...that
just happen to be healthier.”

Scoffing, and muttering into my mug I added: “And I suppose I decided I might as well put in some effort into sticking around, right?
Dying of heart disease sounds terrible...” In quiet companionship we sat, watching the news scroll across the TV’s LED screen. Missing
people. Ghouls killed. Gruesome murder here or there. Ghoul’s captured. Some buildings on the other side of Tokyo had caught fire.


The usual things - the usual suspects.

“Aika, you should get that foot wrapped and take some medicine. Then sleep.”

“I wanted to wait to see when Uta got home...” A yawn sneaked it’s way out and I leaned back onto the couch. “I didn’t expect him to be
so late...” While seated I’d completely forgotten about my ankle yet now it was stiff. Renji’s reminder brought it back into focus. He was
right though.

I was stalling for time, and because I didn’t wish to go to bed I sluggishly wrapped my foot and ankle in an ace bandage. It took some
adjustments to make it comfortable and not cut off my circulation but I finally settled and popped a few Tylenol into my mouth and
swallowed.

“How’s your side?”

“Not broken I think. Not much to do about them except avoid getting smacked there any time soon. Also trying not to lean over too
much, and like all things: some rest will go a long way. Medicine doesn't hurt.” I pursed my lips together and rolled my eyes. “Can’t
imagine you’ve had to take much medicine at all huh?”

“We can get sick. A cold once in a while. But it’s a little less common.”

“Uta mentioned that. But wound care is just about getting food.” I noted with a pout. I recalled Uta’s wounds distinctly. He had healed a
rather large stomach wound that looked like it would have had his guts spilling out onto the floor of the apartment. With just a quick and
rather messy meal he recovered. Honestly an unpleasant memory, yet I could not deny the appeal of healing that fast might have.
Certainly my ribs and ankle would be history by now if I could have simply healed as quickly as them.


With a rather dramatic sigh I leaned back and went limp on the couch. “But I shall endure with only Tylenol. The most advanced of
medicines for daily aches, pains and small injuries.” A bit heavy on the sarcasm. I sat up and grinned goofily to show I was kidding.
Snapping my fingers, my face lit up with a ‘new’ idea.

“...I know! You’re worried Uta will be mad about me getting hurt!”

“That had crossed my mind...”

“Don’t worry Renji. I’ll tell him it was just normal training...” I didn’t want to explain how I’d snapped at Renji either. At least not right
away. Now because of tonight I thought I had a better understanding. They wanted --- needed--- to feel like they could protect me. The
feeling likely wasn’t dissimilar to the protective feeling I felt when I put myself between Uta and Amon on the occasions when we ran
into each other. Though, in their case they had the experience of losing one person after another after another...

“I’m going to bed, Renji-kun...make yourself comfy on the couch and I’ll try to relax a little about being escorted all over. At least until I
am stronger.”

“Goodnight Aika-chan.”

“Goodnight Renji-kun!~”  I said back, then whistled for Bjorn who came trotting after me to the bedroom. “Thank you...”

I laid down in bed, pulled Uta’s pillow to me and snuggled up into the blankets and closed my eyes. It was easy to fall asleep now. With
the knowledge that in the other room someone strong was willing to stay and protect me, and that someone else strong would be coming
back to sleep next to me soon.






Chapter 42: A ghoul returns home
## Notes:
This chapter is a bit on the short side - but it felt like a good place to stop the chapter before the next one.
But Uta is back!!!!!!
(See the end of the chapter for  more notes.)
Chapt er   Text

## Chapter: 42


I groaned as the bed bent under someone else’s weight. The pillow in my arms was gently pulled from my grasp and another person lay
their body down beside me. Blinking in the dark I searched for a familiar face. “Ai-chan...go back to sleep.” The familiar voice set me at
ease, but I still tried to murmur nonsense words in response.

## Uta ...
Just this side of consciousness I managed to mutter what I thought were intelligible words. “Welcome...home...”

## ♥

Warm. It was warm and I was.....

Stiff actually. I tried to wiggle but found firm resistance and no relief when attempting to move. A little more wiggling and a grunt
answered my struggles. I opened my eyes and took a peek at the window that lay just in front of me. The morning light was only barely
filtering in lighting up dust motes in the air. Early . It was still very early in the morning.

I twisted my head a bit and saw that a familiar face resting close by. Eyes closed and face lax; the ghoul breathed through his mouth which
lay slightly ajar. When I wiggled his expression scrunched up and his eyebrows furrowed together a bit. Closing his mouth he leaned his

head further forward until his nose brushed the junction between my shoulder and neck; murmuring something I couldn’t quite make
out. What’s more, I could feel that what was keeping me still was an arm casually thrown over my waist. More cautiously I tried to wiggle
my ankle and winced. That in particular was still painful and very stiff . Another mutter came from the sleeping ghoul and the arm
tightened to pull closer. A series of unfortunate events led to me hissing and then yelping in pain as a well muscled arm clamped down
around my waist, pulling me close and pressing into my injured ribs.

“Hum...?!” The body behind me seized up, frozen and then quickly released my waist. Sitting up quickly, Uta leaned over my body and
hovered there. “Ai-chan...?”

“I’m sorry I woke you up...you just squished me a little too hard is all.” I smiled, apologetically though I still winced from the twinges of
ache. “My side is a little banged up...You must be tired....”

“Mmm, sorry...” He sat back and yawned, covering his mouth with the palm of his hand before wiping his eyes with his knuckles.
“...Renji mentioned you were injured from training...”

“...and I also slipped from the ladder.” I added with a slight smile. Sitting up in bed I bit down on a yelp from the ache in my ribs.

“Clumsy...?”

“Something like that. I’ll be okay.” Following my words I let myself fall back into bed where the pillow caught me gently. “I really don’t
want to go to work though.”

“Then stay here.” I stifled a laugh knowing it would hurt and shook my head slowly. Of course he’s got such a simple answer to my
complaint. Just like I knew he would; he would offer to let me stay in his bed all day if I wanted.

“Can’t. I really hate the idea of flaking out on work because I got a little bruised. At any rate; people have to do things they don’t want to
do every single hour of every day. What time is it?”
Movement on the bed told me that Uta had rolled to the other side of the bed and grabbed his cellphone off the bedside table. “...nearly
six am. If you are going to work then you’ll have to get up soon.”

“...yeah. Sounds about r------ight. ” I paused mid sentence to yawn. Rolling slowly I laid on my stomach and stuffed my face into the
pillow. Only once I was out of bed and limping my way to the door could Uta see the extent of my injuries. Limping. Favoring one side.
Not to mention there were a set of bruises on each of my forearms where the first blow from Renji’s fists had landed.

Close behind me I heard the soft footfalls of a pursuing goth close in on me.
“Let me see.” His voice was gentle per the usual, yet it was a firm demand.

“Uta...I told you I’m really---” Renji’s conversation came back to me and I stopped dead in the middle of the hallway. “---fine. Fine . But
I’m sure it looks worse than it is.” I turned and held out my arms so he could see the bruising. I gazed down at my own arms and winced a
bit at the purples and blues that had taken up a good portion of my forearms. It really did look worse than it felt. The ghoul took hold of
my arms by the wrists and gently turned my arms around and pouted. Briefly I saw him check on the tattoo on my upper arm before
moving onwards.

Releasing my arms he pushed up the edge of my shirt so he could peek at my ribs. His face fell and I saw the ever so light clench of his
teeth. “It’s not so---” I was cut off with a hiss of air sucked through my clenched teeth when Uta dragged his fingers across the flesh of my
abdomen.

“...Stay home for today. I’ll call Yoshimura.”

“Uta...please.” I reached and caught his arm before he could wander back to get his phone. “ Please. I know you want to look out for me.
But it really does just look worse than it is. It hurts but I’m not dying and it’s not broken. If I start skipping work because I’m training

with Renji, Mr. Yoshimura might try and talk him out of doing it. Or Renji might decide on his own he doesn't want to help me
anymore. I like training. I really really do. I don’t mind the little bumps and bruises. I expected to get hurt from this sort of thing...”

I curled my fingers around his wrist gently, swiping my thumb over the tattoos penned into his skin. “I’ll take a rest when my injuries
ache at work. But if I brace my ankle and take it easy then I’ll be absolutely fine. A coffee shop really doesn't get that rambunctious.” I
could see the hard look in the black and red eyes. The red irises flicked down to my ankle before going to my eyes once more. “---I don’t
know if you have the time, but if you’d like to I wouldn’t mind someone walking me to the station today. To make sure I can get there
alright?”

His eyes opened up wider in surprise; staring with a new glitter as light caught the red of his eyes.
“...Okay.” A simple reply. But final enough for me to smile sweetly at the ghoul and release his wrist to let him retreat into the room. At
least now he would go get dressed now rather than call me out of work. I turned and limped my way into the kitchen and started a pot of
coffee for the both of us to drink before work. A fond smile remained on my face as I worked on the coffee, carefully straining it into two
cups. One black for Uta. Creme and a little sugar for myself.

I was thankful now that Renji had spoken to me the night before. Albeit I could have used the talk sans the injuries. It had been an honest
conversation that I’d needed to have. There were yet more things I’d have to confront. But for now I supposed that letting Uta, Renji and
my other friends watch my back was...acceptable. It grated on my nerves and it would be difficult to relax. Relying on other people
wasn’t exactly a forte of mine.

“Uta-kun...” I greeted him again, coffee in hand when he came from his room dressed in dark ripped jeans and a darkly patterned
geometric t-shirt. He stood nearby; holding out his hands to take the coffee. Instead of handing it to him (much to his clearly visible
confusion) I placed it on the coffee table with my own beside it.

Still confused and empty handed the ghoul tipped his head to one side.“Ai--”
“--chan?” Uta's words only hitched for a moment as I stepped close, closed my arms around his waist and rested the palms of my hands on
his upper back to bury my face against his chest.

Annnnnd deep breath in...
...and out.

## Ahhh...

It was really silly how much I’d missed the ghoul when he was away. Yet the short little weekend had felt so long. Familiar warmth,
familiar smell ---I relaxed to fully, leaning more of my weight into him off my bad leg. Arms wrapped around my waist and pulled me
flush against him. Bending his head down, he pressed his nose into the crown of my head and inhaled.


I flinched and glanced up when Bjorn barked. Loudly interrupting the moment. The huge canine then proceeded to waltz by the both of
us into the kitchen and sat next to his food bowl. Chuckling softly I relaxed my arms to pull from the hug. Uta’s arms fell away and stared
at the dog who continued to stare back - standing over his food dish.

“I suppose that is a very clear message if I’ve ever seen one...” I murmured, stepping away from my ghoul to go feed Bjorn. The dog sat

and watched as I dug out his food from the fridge. Double and triple checking that I had the right stuff I poured the meat into his bowl
and patted his head. “There you go, bear-bear.”

When I turned back the ghoul’s eyes were still fixed upon me and I smiled, placing my palms on my hips and imitating his head tilt.
“What? Hurry with your coffee, Uta-kun. It’ll get cold...”

“---and breakfast. Did you want me to cook something?” I glanced at the clock on the TV and pursed my lips in concentration. “I might
have enough time if I hurry...”

“...No. Maybe later.” Uta leaned down and picked up his coffee from the table, softly blowing on it before taking a sip. On my way out of
the room I paused for a moment; watching the way the ghoul smiled and closed his eyes after another sip. From the looks of it he had
missed good coffee while out with his friends.

“I’ll be out in just a minute!” I grabbed my uniform for work and leaned out of the bedroom, raising my voice to shout out to Uta. “Also,
if you haven't already; take a look at the kitchen. I bought some things.”

There came no reply, but upon exiting the bedroom and moving back to the kitchen I found the ghoul with a cookbook in his hands and
bent over to read it. I moved to stand beside him while I futzed with my little bow on the cafe uniform. Glancing between the book and
ghoul I spoke up. “I know that you wouldn’t have had any real reason to have these but if you’re ever questioned it’s probably best you
say these were from a family member of yours.”

Red and black eyes turned away from the handwritten notations and lists of ingredients to study me. “Not yours...?”

I shook my head sharply in response. “Unfortunately my family is too well known.” I grimaced at the idea of trying to convince someone
I had Kaneshiro cookbooks - or that these were them. The likelihood that family cookbooks existed were slim to begin with. If anything
the ones the cooks had used had been from their own family’s.  “At any rate it’s a better cover if you say they belong to you. Between the
two of us I’d rather they question me about being a Ghoul. At least I can get away from the conversation with a free and totally harmless
RC test.”

On the counters where I’d left them was the new blender, rice cooker and toaster. I pointed them out with a small smile. “Renji helped
me pick these up. He volunteered to help with shopping when he decided to check on my health and wellness. I may have used him to
carry a few things. I felt a little bad about it though...”

“I asked him to make sure you were okay when I was away.”

“Yeah.” I said quietly, eyes cast downwards as I avoided looking at his face. From the corner of my eyes I spotted an inquisitive expression
but I shook my head gently. Later. We could talk about it later. For now I had to get to work in one piece. “I’m still in one piece, aren't I?
Right now it’s your job to make sure I get to work. Hopefully on-time, and also in one piece. Alright?”

Leaning up on my toes I quickly pressed a peck onto his cheek. I took a single step around him to go get my new wrap and shoes on to
leave. Abruptly I felt myself pulled back around, lips to lips and a hand supporting my waist on my good side so I didn’t trip. A small
noise of surprise was swallowed in the sudden embrace.

As suddenly as he initiated; he pulled away. Wordlessly he released me and retreated in favor of getting his own shoes and coat while I
stood with a flushed face. It seemed as though he had missed me while he was away. He just didn't say it in so many words.


## ♥


“I’m really sorry I’m late.” I stood with my head bowed as I needlessly begged for forgiveness. The manager had already expressed several
times that he was just glad that I was alright. Uta already sat at the bar and was ordering a coffee.

“I tried to get her to stay home.” Uta said quietly over his coffee once it was brought out to him. Even now as I worked to make sure the
floors were kept clean I caught his eyes trailing me; as though he were just waiting for me to relent and admit my injuries were too much.
“She’s hurt.”

“Uta... please. ” I remarked, rolling my eyes as I leaned on a mop.
“Sir. I am fine.” I said towards the older gentleman. “If I felt like I couldn’t work I’d have called ahead and said so.”

The older man simply smiled kindly and chuckled. “Uta, I believe you’ll find that Humans are a lot hardier than we Ghouls generally give
them credit for.” I paused, watching the old mans’ face as his wrinkles crinkled in joy as he spoke to the younger ghoul. I wondered a lot if
perhaps some of the things he said came from his own experience with his wife. Had she been ‘hardier’ than what he’d expected?

In truth, my ankle did hurt. Though I was loath to admit it. It began to hurt enough that I started hiding grimaces behind a smile where I
could grit my teeth without showing my discomfort to customers. When I thought nobody was around to see I leaned off of the bad leg
and took a few deep breaths before going back to work.

An hour or so later I heard the manager speaking again and peeked around the corner of the shop to see that the goth ghoul was still
sitting at the counter; nursing a second cup of coffee.
“Uta. I would never object to you staying and having coffee with us. Your visits were always quite rare. But should your own shop not be
open now?” The old man was saying. Red and black eyes turned to meet my own peeking around the corner.  I smiled and raised my
brows.

“---You're still here? Aren't you kinda backed up on orders?”

I walked a few dishes back to the counter and placed them down for them to be taken away and cleaned. “Honestly, I’m alright. I know
you're busy too. If it’s not too much trouble...could you pick me up from work later?”

The moment of hesitancy almost made me rethink my request. Perhaps that wasn’t what he wanted and I was being too needy now?
Renji was wrong?  A moment later however; Uta took the last sip of his coffee. Where once he sat nursing it slowly, now he downed it in
a few gulps and slid money over the counter.

“Alright Ai-chan. I’ll be back later to get you.”

“Thanks Uta-kun. I’ll wait for you here!” I waved as the man quickly left the coffee shop to head back to his own shop. And then finally I
let out a long sigh.

“Ms. Aika. Perhaps now you’ll take a moment to sit down and rest your leg. Please. ”
I turned quickly around and pressed my lips into a thin pout, but did as the boss said. Oh it was so much better. “Sorry for the trouble,
## Sir.”

“Your training with Yomo has gotten quite difficult I see.”


“No. Not exactly. I actually fell off one of those tall ladders. Landed wrong and---well.” I grimaced as I indicated at my leg.

“Ah. I’m sure that does hurt. However in this case I was referring to your side, Ms. Aika.”

My mouth opened and closed a few times like a fish out of water. I’d been trying to disguise my sore side. Plus, my limb hurt worse than
my other injuries. I had figured that the covered up bruising would be enough to hide away that particular injury as long as nothing
decided to touch my ribs. “Ah...yeah. That also is a bit sore.”

A coffee slid across the counter and the manager nodded at it. “Drink and take a break. The cafe isn’t going to fall apart if you take a few
moments to yourself.” He looked around and smiled calmly.
“It’s a quiet day.” Following his gaze I looked around the cafe, and at the area outside the windows as people passed by in the sunlight.

“It’s nice...” I muttered softly.

“Indeed. Take a moment to enjoy it and then I have something for you to do.”


## ♥

I sneezed as a bit of dust flew up and groaned. The manager had brought me upstairs and set me in front of a bunch of books. The old
man had then asked me to go through and organize them for him. It was a task that was easily done while sitting and required very little
lifting so I supposed I could see why the old man thought it appropriate.

The old man had an odd choice of books though. I glanced at the titles and the author of the book in my hands. I never would have
figured that he would be a Sen Takatsuki fan. I gave the book in my hand titled: Kuro Yagi no Tamago ( The Black Goat's Egg ) with a
doubtful gaze. When I’d read it myself it hadn’t been the easiest thing to get through. The book contained some rather graphic
descriptions. While the old man was a Ghoul - I couldn’t imagine him sitting down and reading it.

However, I couldn’t deny he did have every book by her so far. The hardest part was putting them in order. While the boss hadn’t been
specific on what sort of order apart from the author's names, I was putting the books on the shelf in the order of publication rather than
title. That at least worked well since he had so many from the one single author. Apart from the books written by Sen he had some less
puzzling books. Books on coffee. Another on tea. Some about the historic parts of Japan and Tokyo. Basic cook books and even two that
had information on plant care and the use of herbs.

After placing “Salt and Opium” on the shelf I stood up and stretched out my back, careful to mind my side as I did. The muscles still
pulled and I still winced. “Well...all done here.”

“And just in time. Uta is waiting down stairs for you.”

I jolted from the voice near to me only to turn and see the boss smiling. Nodding I indicated at the books. “Right...Um. I hope it’s okay
that I put these ones in order of publication. And I made sure to dust off the shelf before placing them. I didn’t know you were a fan of
## Sen.”

The old man simply smiled faintly and nodded. “Yes. I suppose you could say that. Having those books means a great deal to me. Perhaps
another day I’ll discuss them. But please. The young man downstairs seems like he’s been worried about you.”


“Oh. Yeah. Alright. Is Roma back? ...I haven't heard any crashing.”

“Ah, about that. It seems as though she has not come back yet. It is still a slow quiet day so I am not concerned.”

“You don’t want me to stay do you? I’d be happy to.” Even as I asked I knew the answer, only to have it confirmed almost before the
words were all the way out of my mouth.

“No dear, not at all. Koma and Irimi have things handled here. And you need rest.”


I simply nodded to that. I’d likely be hearing it over and over again from everybody until I was back to being at one hundred percent. Did
they not realize that everybody was walking around with injuries every day? Sure they might not be severe but every human got bruises
and bumps and small cuts from day to day.  Hell I’d woken up with bruises I didn’t even know how I’d gotten them in the night. “I will
make sure to rest tonight. But I’ll be back bright and early tomorrow. Unless you’ve got even more books to organize again. Because then
I might have to arrange sleeping in all day instead.” Kidding, of course and I was pleased to see the constant smile on his face grow and the
wrinkles crinkled into tighter lines.

“No, I’m afraid that is all of my books I have here. Though I encourage you to take the day off if your leg hasn't gotten any better.
Standing on it will not help you recover. It would not do any good to do any permanent damage. Especially at your young age.”

“...I---yes sir.” I murmured at the ground; disappointed. I had the distinct feeling it would be hurting quite a lot after I pushed myself
today. It wasn’t that I regretted going to work.

“Thank you. I probably should...” I added , still looking at my feet.

“Very good.  I shall see you Wednesday.” He chuckled and added: “I suppose that Yomo will also be postponing any training for you
until you're better?”

Nodding, I let out a tired sigh. “Of course...” With a lifted hand I waved and turned around to head down the stairs, favoring my injured
limb and keeping weight off the bad leg. At the bottom of the stairs I peek to see who was at the counter. Exactly where I thought he’d be,
Uta was sitting with a coffee mug in his hands. Uta’s eyes were looking over his dark sunglasses to stare at a couple. I followed his gaze and
found the objects of his attention. His permanently ghoulish eyes were fixed upon Nishiki and Kimi who were seated at a table by the
windows drinking coffee and smiling at each other. Their conversation sounded indistinct and distant but they looked happy and Kimi
laughed at something her boyfriend had said.

I found myself looking at them curiously as well, curious. Kimi did show up with Nishiki often. Most of the occasions that I’d seen her----
my eyes shifted towards Nishiki ---he’d been with her. Her constant companion and her faithful guardian.

I’d heard what had happened to them. About Shuu...
Nishki had gotten nearly beaten to death and Kimi almost died when my old ‘friend’ tried to eat her. I suppose it made sense that she
clung so close to her ghoul .

I glanced at my own ghoul boyfriend once more. Dark eyes remained fixed on the other couple with a quiet concentration even as he
took a sip. My lips twitched into a smile when Kimi glanced in his direction before quickly looking away again; she looked uncomfortable
. I approached and gently tapped Uta on the shoulder making his head turn about to look with wide eyes.

“Did I surprise you?” I giggled softly when he blinked and pushed his glasses up to cover his eyes better. “You seemed to be scaring the
daylights out of Kimi with your staring. Figured I’d have to stop you.”

## “...was I?”


I hummed a soft affirmation before jerking my shoulders in a little shrug. “When you're thinking of something your stare can be kind of
intense. You certainly are taking the opportunity to get coffee today though. Aren't you? Is that three cups already?”

“Four.” The ghoul smiled, his expression borderline sheepish. “The coffee here really is the best around. And it’s peaceful here...”

That it was. I glanced around, caught Kimi’s gaze on us both. When she saw I’d seen her looking she smiled faintly and waved. “Hey
Aika-chan. How are you?”

“Good.... Good. ” I hesitated saying it a second time but as I said it it sounded more sure. I was good. When I came to work I was happy.
When I went home - my new place with Uta - I was happy . I was more than glad to simply watch him work on his art or help when the
opportunity came up. Seeing my gifted painting on his wall lighting up his---our---home up with some color made my stomach fill with
butterflies each and every time.

I couldn’t see past this week, or next...but moment to moment I was happy. I suppose that’s really what matters. Tomorrow isn’t a
promise, it’s a hope. But despite everything I suppose I have a whole lot of hope.
