## Chapter Text
## Chapter 43: ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
## 




Uta closed the door behind us once we got back to the studio. The sign in front was flipped back to open and the ghoul sat
himself back down at his desk where a half finished mask lay abandoned since he left to pick me up from work.

“Thank you for coming to get me.” I said softly, seating myself to straddle a chair backwards so I could rest my chin on the
backrest and watch him work. “I’m sorry to drag you away from your own work though...”

“It’s alright. The coffee there is good. Renji-kun has been saying for ages I should visit more often...”

Quiet filled the room, only interrupted by the quiet sounds of sculpting as Uta carved out a shape for a horn of the mask he
was crafting. This was not awkward silence; only a peaceful sort of quiet. It was a shame that I’d have to break it eventually
with some bad news. Sooner or later I’d have to speak to him about our unfortunate neighbor. Much as I would have liked to
simply forget about her - it wasn’t an option. One did not survive ghouls who threatened you by ignoring them.


“Uta...I’ve got something to tell you...But I don’t want you to get too upset about it.”

Skillful hands paused, knife held over wood waiting to chip and curl away a shape stood motionless. “Hum?”
“I told you in one of the messages I sent you that everything wasn’t great here. The reason I went to Touka’s when you were
gone. Well... Ms. Kirin...” I said the woman's name slowly, watching his body language for change. Oh boy did it. I pursed my
lips into a nervous line when the ghoul’s jaw clenched and unclenched. He sat up straighter, no longer hunched over his
work. In fact he seemed to have no interest in it any longer. Setting the knife and the project aside, those intense red eyes
caught me like a moth in a spider web.

“Did she bother you again?”


Cautiously I continued to explain, knitting together my fingers. “She asked to talk to you. I said we were taking time off from
work because I insisted you take a vacation. A lie because it didn’t seem like a good idea to tell her you were away. But I think
she knew I wasn’t being truthful because after I closed and locked the door... she tried to open the door anyway...”

“Uta!” I said more sharply as the man stood up, moving swiftly towards the door to the backstreet.
“Stay here.”
“No! Uta, please. Stop a moment.” I stood up and launched myself after him - springing up on my injured ankle and wincing
as I struggled to catch up. Snagging a sleeve, I tugged. “Please. Stop.” My words almost a desperate plea, I called out to Uta
hoping he’d at least stop and look at me. Thankfully, as worked up as he’d gotten in a few moments he wasn’t beyond reason
and I was able to hold his intense gaze.

“...I don’t like her. She creeps me out. Obviously she’s been a bit---er...threatening. She’s always been an ‘angry old lady
neighbor.’ Unpleasant and everything that entails but---” I hesitated and bit my bottom lip. “Uta...the last time somebody
even remotely threatened me you---” Killed them. And then ate them.

Actually, scratch that. The last two people who had threatened me were both now dead.
---and eaten.

“...Think for a moment. If my neighbor goes missing they’ll be even more investigators on this block. I’ve already had Amon
question me more than once in the last month. What do you think will happen if the lady across the street from me goes
missing as well? Disappearances around me. Around you...? The next person they’ll be hounding for a test will be you. Can
we talk to her? Calmly? I’ll make some coffee and we can bring her some...”

I let go of his sleeve and gently moved to gently smooth my hands over his shoulders. “--And maybe she’s had the wrong idea.
She saw me moving some items out of my old apartment and asked if I was moving away.” I added hopefully, I gently
squeezed his shoulders as I waited for a reply. Any kind of answer. For too long we stood still, his iris flicked around,
searching my face and eyes. The simmer of impending violence in his expression had calmed; though not disappeared
entirely.

“...First you asked me to leave Tsukiyama alone. And now an old woman you don’t even know. If we go over and I tell you
to leave, will you...?”

“It just seems like needless violence if we could try to solve this civilly. Without causing ourselves more problems. And don't
get me started on Tsukiyama. He’s...kind of a special case. He wasnice to me when I was younger. It’s hard to explain. Things
change though, but I’d still prefer if he doesn't die. It doesn't hurt that I’m not a naive little girl running away from home
anymore.” Finally, reluctant and knowing what it would mean if he asked me to leave ---I nodded, slowly. “If you tell me to
leave. I will. I promise. No questions, no arguments. Please just try it my way.”


He nodded once and I let go of him now satisfied that he wouldn’t be running off to murder an old woman, right away at
the very least. “Anyway...After I called her, Touka came and picked me up from here. I spent the night at her house. Her
human friend from school and Hinami also were there so it was a nice girls night thing. Did you know that Touka eats food
her friend brings her?” I pulled a face quickly before adding: “I let Renji know I was out of the house with Touka too, so he
wouldn’t worry too much.”

“Why didn’t you call Renji...?”

“Because he would have come running. I’m sure he’d have dropped everything too. But he said...” I bit my inner cheek as I
avoided Uta’s gaze. I wasn’t about to give away everything Renji had said about his human friend. “---That he’d be busy that

night. I didn’t want to interrupt. He’s got a life too you know.”

## “...”

“Uta...I promised I’d stay at home so he didn’t have to watch out for me. He had other plans. I didn't want to ruin them. I
figured one night at Touka’s would be fine and then you'd be back. Then we could sort things out. Calmly. And please don’t
be angry with Renji-kun either. He’s already made it rather clear that I'm pretty helpless right now. It’ll be a while before I’m
even remotely ready to try to actually defend myself.”

I indicated the bruised ribs and flaunted my arms. “This was probably an ass whooping wake-up call I needed.” The ghoul
hummed softly. This news seemingly upset him a bit less than the neighborhood ghoul issue. Not that I could blame him.
While he didn’t like me getting hurt ---
He trusted Renji.
Hell. I trusted Renji. The smack down had hurt sure; but at no point had I felt in true mortal danger.

“Renji mentioned last night that he spoke to you...and today you asked for me to come with you today. Because of your leg.”


“Well, yes and no. If you’d rather not, that's fine. I just thought that maybe---if you wanted it I’d give you the opportunity to
watch over me a bit more. So you wouldn’t have to worry.”

“It’s easier than following you to the station.” The ghoul turned and returned to his desk, pulling open a cabinet door and
pulled out a small shallow dish of human eyes. I stared at him with a loose jaw as he popped one into his mouth. What he
said took a minute to click into my brain correctly and process a result.


“Wait, wait, wait. Everyday?” I gasped; eyes going wide.


“Umhum...”

“This entire time?”

“...hummmm...” The ghoul muffled through a full mouth before swallowing and replying to my question. “No. Mostly just
since the holidays.”


Since the holidays basically meant ‘Ever since we’d been a couple .’ He’d been shadowing after me to make sure that I was
safe.


“No wonder my neighbor was practically falling over herself to flee from me when I saw her in the street. She wasn’t worried
about me telling you something, she was just afraid of you lurking nearby!”


Mid-bite the ghoul paused to asked a question: “...Are you upset?”




## “I...”

“...I’m not.” I said slowly as I considered it. If I took an introspective glance at how I felt learning this, ghouls and Uta in
general. Perhaps a few days ago I might have reacted differently, yet now---

No. I didn’t blame him. I didn’t even resent his actions a little bit. He’s done everything he could to not impose himself upon my
sense of independence. Respecting my desire to feel like I was able to take care of myself. All while making sure I don’t get killed
off when he’s not looking.


“---Well. If you’re shadowing me anyway you might as well just walk with me to the station.”
A chocolate brown eye disappeared into his mouth; he chewed quickly and swallowed. The ghoul tipped his head to one side
and looked intrigued by my words. Curious, he asked: “...What did Renji say to you?”


“He...I....” I paused, considering how to explain it. The start was a good idea. “I said before that I probably needed to be
taught the lesson. He started the ‘training’ by knocking me to my feet and giving me this.” I rubbed my side and grimaced,
still not fond of the memory of being beaten so easily. The ‘fight’ had been split seconds and nothing more. It had made me
doubt myself, caused misery and hopelessness to swell like a noxious cloud. Even if only momentarily it left something bitter
lingering.

“...He mentioned that I should rely more on the people who offer to help. Because by not letting people do so I’m just
making them worry. It would be easy for me to get hurt or killed...especially when I’m so involved with you.”


I glanced up and met the red eyes peering back at me, the dish of eyes forgotten as he listened to what I had to say. “He said:
‘I can’t bear to lose any more people’ . It reminded me of when you said every ghoul knows another who has disappeared into
that prison.” I ran my fingers through my hair, fisting them to tug gently before relaxing with a tired sigh. “I know having
everybody hovering should be more motivating. It should make me want to work harder. With enough work and training,
I’ll improve and you won’t have to protect me as much. And I really like training. I always have. So it’s not a lack of
motivation. Right now it’s just frustrating...and a bit discouraging if I’m honest. I really hate making you---and the others at
work worry about me.”


“...” The ghoul’s eyes were wide as I explained it to him But I waved a hand idly. “Don’t worry about it, Uta. I’ll figure it out.
I’ve just got to sort some things out in my head. Let me go make coffee. We have an old woman to go talk to. Talk only. So
unless she tries anything funny...” I motioned at him with a ‘i’ve got my eyes on you’ hand gesture before run-limping up the
stairs of the apartment.


## ♥




Coming back down the stairs I had Bjorn on my heels; wagging his tail happily because he thought he was going on a walk.
Carefully with a fresh pot of brewed coffee in one hand I patted the top of his head and apologized to the canine.

“Sorry bud. Stay. We’ll be back shortly.”

I smiled sadly as I was forced to shut the door gently in the dog's face; closing him away to stay safe and sound inside the
shop. I heard a few barks and whines from behind the door before he fell quiet. With the door closed and then locked I
turned my attention to the man next to me. In the past I might have mistaken his posture as casual, or lackadaisical. But now
knowing him, being up close and personal so often with a first class seat to see his small body languages----
He was alert and tense.

Carefully I reached out and touched his arm with my free hand. “Come on. Before the coffee gets cold.” It was I that stepped
forward and rapped my knuckles on the door before taking a step back to stand beside Uta. He shuffled his body to be
slightly ahead, and in front of me when the door cracked open.

A little old woman, just as she always was, answered the door. She had a square-ish face with a head of greying hair. Her grey
hair was pulled back into a ponytail and her wrinkled face hid her eyes much like Yoshimura who kept his closed. Surprise
was obvious on her expression the moment the door opened and she saw who had come knocking.

“....Uta-sama...” Despite the large gap in age, the woman still referred to him respectfully.
Her eyes turned to me, standing by the goth's side with a small nervous smile. “...”

“Hi Ms. Kirin. I brought some coffee I brewd. I was taught by the best, so it’s pretty good! Fresh too. Can we talk to you for
a moment? Not out in the street though if we can help it.”

The woman’s eyes opened and she looked at me with the same red and black eyes of any ghoul. They had stopped startling
me quite so much even on strangers. I suppose when someone woke up with a pair lying next to you they lost their terror
fairly quickly. “...Yes, I suppose...that would be fine.” Her eyes shifted from Uta to myself quickly a few times before settling
on him as she backed up to allow us both in.  Uta took the first few steps in and stopped as he looked around. The woman
shuffled into her home, quickly she was covering something on her table and shoving a bottle under the table.

“Ms. Kirin, it’s really fine. No need to clean up or anything.” I waved my free hand and put on a smile. It’s not as though I
didn’t know she was a ghoul.  “Coffee?”

“I...t-thank you dear.” I watched as the woman pulled out a few mugs from a small cupboard and placed them on the table.
Carefully I poured out three drinks and stepped back, taking one with me. Cautiously the woman leaned down and took her
own cup and brought it to her mouth with a slight quiver. “What do I owe the visit for?”

“...I’ve warned you before to leave Aika alone.” I glanced between Uta and the old woman, biting the inside of my cheek as
he got right to the point. Despite the fact that Uta’s eyes were wandering the small apartment I could tell he was still tense. “I-
--” The woman’s eyes darted from me to the ghoul looming next to me. Uta’s cup of coffee, the only one that remained, was
untouched and sat lonely on the coffee table.

I glanced around the old ghoul’s home quickly. It wasn’t much better than my old apartment. Slightly bigger. But it also had
a lot more things . Things being a nice word for junk. Shelves full of little tchotchkes suggested that she’d traveled, or had
family at one point who had. In the corner there were small piles of boxes and by the doorway her trash was set, ready to be
brought away. Her couch had a blanket thrown over it, a colorful unidentifiable pattern was artfully knitted into it. Beside
the couch a box overflowing with yarn sat with needles sticking out of it. A half completed project lay abandoned on the
couch arm rest.


“...” Silently I looked back to Uta with a quiet plea. I hoped that he’d try the nice, calm, and civil way to do this. He moved,
picking up the end of a knitted scarf and looked at the little loops that made it up close.

“I don’t...I-I'm not sure what you're talking about...I-I-I...I know. She is y-yours .”

“You attempted to enter my shop after being told it was closed.”
I watched the woman's eyes go wide, red iris giving away her terror. “Please. I’m sorry. Please.” I shuffled my feet nervously as
I watched Uta place the woman’s project back where it had been and look around some more --- in contrast to Uta’s
seemingly calm demeanor the woman was beside herself. I supposed that it made sense now, why Uta could use his old
position of ‘leader’ of the ward to keep me safe.

Even now after he stopped being officially the leader; They were terrified of him.


“Please, I’ll do anything. Please...just leave me alone. I’ll move! I’ll go far away. I’ll go to the 24th ward!!!”

I blinked, head tilting curiously as the other ward came up. The entrances to the 24th were where Renji trained me, but we
never went far in. That was because Renji had said it was easy to get lost. However when I’d asked about the ward’s living
areas he had explained to me that it was a hell hole due to the high ghoul population. Cannibalism was more rampant and
death was an everyday occurrence. Only the strong survived there and some of the ghouls that came from the 24th ward were
monstrous.


“Aika?”

“Hum?” I snapped out of my thoughts to see that Uta’s eyes were on me, looking for input. “You wanted to talk to her...”

“Ah...Well.” Shuffling around on the spot I looked from ghoul to ghoul. “Wellllll...Yes. I did ask that we come to talk.
Rather than you just storming over here angry..." I muttered, adding: "I'd prefer if we could get through the night without
killing anybody..."


My ghoul boyfriend turned to look at the old woman with an intense stare. Left in awkward silence between Uta and the
shaking woman I sighed.

"...look. Ms. Kirin. Could you please just leave me alone? I really hate saying this but: Honestly is it even worth the trouble at
this point to bother me? There's plenty of other people around here." ---To eat. Or to harass if that was her game. Who was I
to judge how she got her kicks?

“She can go to the 24th ward.” Uta said, taking up the woman's own suggestion. I on the other hand winced at the idea.
“Uta...come on. I’ve only heard a little but what I have makes it sound like hell.” I frowned, eyebrows furrowing together as I
shook my head. It was likely a misplaced concern but if she was sent to the 24th ward she’d likely die.  “She’s just an old
lady...”

## ♥



The woman known as Ms. Kirin looked from the Humam to the Ghoul and back. Her red eyes affixed to the young
woman’s eyes; light brown with a hint of pink blush where the light from the lamps struck the iris. The ex-leader of the 4th
ward looked back at her with a deceptively calm expression. One might think he looked almost bored.

Yet; in years past she’d seen him kill with that very same look on his face. As though it bored him to steal life from another.
The woman at Uta’s side was looking at him - endearing and worried - but no fear. Ms. Kirin listened to their conversation
and watched how Uta’s eyes fixed upon the woman.

And the young lady, not only was asking Uta to spare her life, but to let her stay. Asked simply to be left alone in exchange.
‘There’s other people around here to eat’ she’d practically said.


It was surprising to find this Human standing so fearlessly next to a Ghoul that could be so capable of violence and
monstrous actions. But perhaps more so to have that Ghoul stand by her - waiting on the young lady's decision.

“Ms. Kirin?”


## ♥

I sat myself down in my seat again as Uta started working on his project again. “She’s not just an old woman...” The ghoul
said quietly.

“She is.” I said confidently with a small smile on my face, helplessly happy that we’d left the home without any bloodshed.
The woman had relented and with shaking words promised never to bother me again. I laughed softly when Uta continued
to stare at me. “Ghoul or not Uta, she’s just an old lady. I’d feel bad kicking her from her home. Or killing her...”

“It wouldn’t be you killing her.”

I chewed my lip and shook my head. Taking the opportunity to stare at one of Uta’s newer art pieces I could get away from
looking into his eyes. He didn’t need more food yet so it would be a frivolous, stupid act of violence for violence sake. There
were other ways most of the time.

“It’s the same to me. Anyway, I wasn’t kidding. I am really afraid if there’s too much more surrounding me or right here in
this area Amon might just come back again to have a more detailed chat. He already crawls out of the woodwork enough as it
is.”

Uta turned his eyes down to his work again and I pursed my lips, spotting a small smirk on his face. “Perhaps him then...” He
was joking, but I still groaned and shook my head.

“Right, well I’m starving. I don’t think I stopped to eat anything today because I just got buried in books. I’m going to make
dinner. Do you want something cooked?”

“Yeah.”

“Anything in particular?” I asked softly, leaning down to try to be eye level with the hunched over craftsman; his gaze now

sternly fixed upon his work.

“No. Anything is fine. Can you put the jar of eyes on the counter for me? They’re better at room temperature.”

“Sure, sure. Come on Bjorn. Dinner time for you too!” Excited; the dog bounced to his feet and bounded up the stairway
past me like a gust. Leaving me to limp my way up the stairway and fix us all dinner. Bjorn got his first in his dog bowl - at
least this way he could be kept out of the way of cooking. Next - Uta’s eye jar was taken from the fridge and put on the
counter. The eyes were my undesirable but otherwise captive audience as I cooked.

As I made my own meal, followed closely by a slab of meat for Uta I found myself staring at the floating ocular organs in
their jar once in a while. Once I curiously tapped my fingernail against the glass and found myself staring into a pair of
emerald green eyes. Grimacing and shuttering, I pushed the jar further away and hid it on the other side of an appliance so
they couldn’t stare.

With a pair of tongs I grabbed Uta’s meal, plopped it on a plate and brought it to the living room with my own bowl of rice
with chicken. “ Uta! Food. ” I called out loud - hoping that it might bring him up the stairs to eat. When it didn’t I peeked
down the stairs and waited until I saw a head of onyx hair pop up near the doorway. "Can you bring it down?"


"Sure. As long as it's okay for me to eat in the shop too."

"Yeah."

Picking up both meals I carefully made my way down the stairs and set his dish in front of him before taking my place back
on ‘my’ chair.

I shoved a mouthful of rice into my mouth just as the door to the shop opened with a chiming bell. I swallowed quickly,
gulping down the mouthful of rice and turned to look at who had come in.

A young man around our own age, lean with sandy blonde hair. I did not recognise him but he walked in holding a bag and a
friendly smile.

“ Yo! Uta. You’re still open this late. I got a delivery if you want them?”
I froze as I heard the man's voice. While his face hadn’t brought up any immediate connections his voice was one I
remembered. From a time not terribly long ago; hiding under a white sheet in this very room...

“Ummm. Yeah. Thanks.”

The delivery guy looked from Uta and saw me seated, a bowl of rice in my hands and sniffed the air subtly. He leaned
towards Uta and did a terrible job at cupping his hand to whisper: “Uh...Hey. Uta, man isn’t that the adorable snack you had
before?”

“Ai-chan. This is Umi. He brings me some of my favorite snacks once in a while.” Uta pulled out some money and held it
out for Umi to take. Uta peeked into the brown paper bag the man had set on his desk and pulled out an eye, licking it before
popping it into his mouth.

Snapping out of my daze I smiled faintly. From the looks of it - Umi was just as surprised to see Uta eating in front of me as I
was to see Uta’s ‘delivery’ guy in person.

“Nice to meet you.”

“Umi, this is Aika. My girlfriend.” The sentence screamed off limits. The man's eyebrows raised up his forehead and his
hands raised up in front of his chest defensively as he took the message loud and clear.   “Oh... Oh !!! Cool man. That’s cool.
Uh---mind if I ask what are you eating?” Umi stared past Uta now, looking at the plate of cooked meat with curiosity.

“Ai-chan cooked me dinner. It’s good.”

“Cooked...?” The delivery ghoul glanced my way and I smiled, waving idly before sticking a bite of rice into my mouth.
“...guess it didn’t occur to me that you could do that. Maybe I’ll try it sometime. She cooked it for you?”

Uta took a bite of his dinner and nodded his head.

“Huh...”
I shifted nervously, only managing a sheepish smile under the inquisitive stare from the new ghoul. Finally he spoke up, light
hearted and grinning.  “Must be a real special gal. Glad he didn’t eat ya. Well Uta, I’ll be back next month around the same
time if that’s good for you.”

“Yeah. See you.” The mask maker's attention was already back on his craft, only once in a while picking a chunk of cooked
meat to bring it to his lips. The head of sandy hair disappeared out the door and I breathed again without realizing I’d
stopped. “Well...he seems nice.”

“Umhm. He’ll leave you be.”

“Yeah, it seemed like it.” I took a bite of rice and grabbed the egg I’d covered over it and dropped it into my mouth, eating it
before speaking again. “I worry a little bit...what other ghouls might think. There’s probably always going to be people like
Touka or Ms. Kirin who are more resistant to think of a Human knowing your identities, or dating as a good thing.”

Poking at my food I sighed softly. Touka at least had gotten over her hesitation and I think Ms. Kirin was just now getting
settled with the idea of leaving me be, if only for her own safety. Yet with Touka it had taken a while of slowly getting her
trust. Even now, I wasn’t sure how easily that trust could be broken. I couldn’t imagine it wouldn't take much.

The Clowns all seemed fairly okay with us. At least the ones I’d met thus far. Which was a huge relief. For the most part they
simply seemed to want Uta to be happy. Then there were people like Roma. I was dead certain the small woman was very
displeased to see that Uta had a Human girlfriend and had half a mind to make sure I didn’t stick around.

But I couldn't even hold some Ghoul’s dislike for humankind against them.
The animosity between Ghouls and Humans wasn’t entirely unfounded.

“...not regretting it, are you Ai-chan? Would you rather I were Human?”
I rolled my eyes and grinned. “You gonna eat me if I say yes?”
“Maybe.”
“Uta! Rude !” I stuffed the last couple bites into my mouth quickly and picked myself up out of the chair. As I limped by
him I leaned over and pecked him on the cheek lightly. “I wouldn’t like a Human better - because a Human wouldn’t be you
. Just like I’d be a totally different person if I grew up as a Ghoul. Right?”


“Hum...” He looked at me, head tilted curiously as he studied me.
“Are you trying to imagine if I were a Ghoul?” I asked.
“Hmm. That would be a sight....”

“Sorry to disappoint. Still Human.”
“I like my human.” He replied, lips twitching into a thin smile. “Have you checked your RC level since that investigator told
you it was high?”

Standing up straight again I pursed my lips and shook my head. “It’s only been a few weeks. Anyway those tests are expensive
when they aren't CCG mandated. I’m trying not to worry too much about it. Not much I could do at any rate. The
medications for that sort of thing are even more expensive than the tests...”


“...you could get sick.”

“I could also turn into a Ghoul.” I replied dryly. “I don’t think that’s likely though. It’s not exactly a very common
occurrence. Otherwise there’d be a lot more hysteria about it. I couldn’t even begin to tell you how I’d have gotten a high
count while being Human.”

“Cannibal?”
“ No . I told you before Uta. I really am not.” I giggled when he held out a bite of his cooked meat to me and raised his
eyebrows. “Thank you. But no! Eat your dinner.”

“Your loss. Willing to share if you change your mind. It’s good.” He flicked the piece into his mouth and went back to his
work again.

“I know Humans are willing to eat just about anything, but other people is kind of where most Humans draw the line. Are
you going to be long? We could watch a movie. I already told the manager I wouldn’t be in tomorrow. Resting off my leg so--
## -”

“Hm...I’ll be up shortly. Pick something out.”

“Pick something? Alright!~”



I got to the top of the stairs and took a deep breath; silently wincing as my ankle ached. “Right...first Tylenol.” I murmured
to myself. Bjorn had finished his dinner and came to my side; sniffing and grumbling as I limped to the bathroom to grab
some medicine out of the cupboard. “Not for you bud.” I threw back my head and swallowed the pill dry with a grimace as
the after taste clung to my tongue.


“You think he’ll like Suicide Squad?” Bjorn looked up at me with his ears perked and his head turned to the side. “Yeah. I
think so.”


I’d already seen it - and preferred most of the MCU to DC but it wasn’t a bad movie to watch again.

Back to the living room I let myself collapse onto the couch and relax with an arm thrown over my face to block out the
light.  My moment of rest was interrupted by a wet cold nose pressed into my cheek and a tongue slipping over my nose.
Turning away I giggled, tongue licking at my ear as I wiggled. “S-stop! Bud, come on. That’s enough. That’s so gross!
Chicken breath!”

With the remote I turned on the television and flipped through until I could find a service streaming the movie and clicked
play. Pausing it a few moments into the film it stayed on the logo screen to wait for when my ghoul joined me upstairs.


I stuck my tongue out at Bjorn as I got up to go back to the bathroom. While there to wash my face I picked up the
toothpaste and turned it over to look at the ingredients. Would another type be better? Surely there was tasteless, flavorless
toothpaste. After all, even some humans hated mint. I picked up my own brush and set to cleaning my teeth and tongue
before spitting and rinsing away the minty taste.


From the other room I heard the door to the studio open and close and footsteps pad across the floor to the door. “Ai-chan?”

“In here.”

The door, already cracked partyway open, creaked and a pair of ghoul eyes peeked in. “Mind if I---?”
“You can come in, just finished cleaning up. The movie is all ready to go.”

His hand outstretched, palm up and tattooed fingers flexing. “The toothpaste...?”

“Ah, here.” I muttered, flushed as I passed it over to him. I watched as he put a little inch worm bit of paste on his own brush
and shoved it into his mouth, scrubbing at his teeth and tongue thoroughly. Alone - away from prying eyes that might
persecute him for being what he was; he made a face at the taste and spat it out as though it were something vile.

I suppose for him, it wasn’t simply an unpleasant mint taste. It was something terrible like rotting trash.

“Hey...you know. I’m not sure if they do have coffee flavored toothpaste. But I think they make flavorless stuff. I can take a
look at the store sometime. See if I can find any.” He washed his mouth out and then spat out the water before looking up at
me with a serious expression. “Don’t...”

“Huh? Why not? That stuff is clearly disgusting to you. I know it’s not ‘eating’ it but still...”

“They monitor who’s buying that sort of thing...”
My mouth opened in protest but nothing but a small gasp escaped.

Of course, the largest demographic that might want such a thing would be Ghouls.
Of course they’d go so low as to track common staple products. While coffee was common; I wouldn’t be surprised if buying
a huge influx of it was also seen as suspicious.

The only reason why Yoshimura could get away with it was because he ran a coffee shop.

“I see...okay...” Just another thing I hadn’t -- could not have - realized without being told. Another hidden hardship. Another
kick in the stomach.

“What movie did you pick?” Uta leaned over and cupped water and sipped it into his mouth before swishing and spitting
once more.

“Suicide Squad. Have you seen it?”
“No. I haven't. Harlequin is in it, right?”

“Yeah?” I replied. Then a smile cracked across my lips and raised an eyebrow. “You like her cause she’s kinda like a clown,
right? I think the Joker is also in it. At least a little bit.”


“Is the Joker your favorite?”
To this I had to shake my head. Unfortunately out of the whole cast the crazy clown man hadn’t been my favorite.
“From the Suicide Squad my favorite is El Diablo. I suppose I just liked his character more. Although the lore behind his
character is kind of tragic. But his power is so cool!! It’s---” I cut myself off and grinned. ”...well, you’ll see. Come on.”



I carefully laid myself down on one end of the couch and picked up the remote to push play. Uta sat himself at the other end.
I glanced his way a few times as the beginning logo’s popped up and the DC intro start began to play. It was hard to
concentrate on the movie when I was looking away from it so often. Finally, dismayed by the distance between us I scooted
myself closer, ever mindful to keep my ribs from bumping uncomfortably.

The ghoul shifted to accommodate me almost as though it were second nature and snaked an arm around me to keep me
put. All while never even looking away from the movie. His hand lay idly on my hip making small circles with the pads of his
fingers as they ghosted over my flesh.


About midway through the movie, and after the ghoul had weaseled his whole hand under my shirt to continue to draw
patterns across my bare skin I whispered softly. My head remained leaned against his chest and I didn’t move to try to correct
his hands placement.
“I’ve got an idea. It’s a ways off, but next Halloween. You can be Joker. I’ll be your Harlequin. Unless of course you’d rather
it be the other way around.”

The fingers tracing invisible patterns paused. “Normally in the past we’ve got events on Halloween. Caused some hell
around town...”

“Oh. Alright....We? The Clowns.” I looked up from his chest and frowned. I was thinking I knew the answer well enough
already.

He nodded his head and looked away from the screen for the first time in over an hour to meet my gaze. “I could bring you.”

“To...the Ghoul event you’re talking about. Causing trouble? Is that safe?”


“...you’d be with me.” So, no. It wouldn’t be safe but it would be with him which would mean he’d be there to protect me. It
would be letting me further into their world. No doubt it would bring me closer to something altogether unpleasant; and yet
he was willing to share it.

“I’ll consider it. It depends if the others feel comfortable with me going as well. Bringing a Human might be a bit of a buzz
kill...right? But that’s almost a year from now. We don’t have to worry about that any time soon. Right now ---” I leaned
forward and pressed my lips gently into his, stealing a kiss. “---there’s plenty of other things to think of.”


## 
## ♥
## 


The ghoul leaned and stole a second chance to capture my lips, this embrace was harsher and hungrier than the last sweet
innocent peck. The fingers at my waist resumed moving and slid up my side as the ghoul swallowed a short gasp I made
because of the caress.

I whined softly and pulled back when his hand brushed along my injured ribs and he immediately pulled back as though I’d
bitten him.

“Sorry---”


No. None of that! No apologizing!

I cut him off by cupping his jaw and pressing myself back up against him and stealing the words from his lips. The man
groaned softly as he eagerly replied in kind. Apology forgotten, the ghoul’s teeth grazed my lips. I felt pressure as he ‘bit’
down on delicate flesh so I pulled away to licked my lips to feel for the damage. Yet, apart from being a bit sore I tasted no
coppery blood.

“Come here. Closer.” Palms reached to hold both sides of my hips. With a smirk he raised me up and pulled me closer so that
my weight was set down on his lap as he adjusted.

“Right there. Perfect.” He nearly purred as he fixed us so I straddled his hips. Leaning forward he moved to place a set of
toothy kisses up and down the column of my throat. I closed my eyes, leaned my throat back further and sighed softly when
he stopped biting to simply lean close and press his nose into the hollow of my throat and inhale.

Jumping would be a fast drop with a sudden stop.

## ♥

It was taking a while for her to let go and the figure in the dark shifted and began to watch the sky instead. Standing in the rain in the
middle of November was becoming a more likely cause of death than a fall from the bridge.

The stranger's eyes were brought back down to see the young woman leaning further out; staring intently down at something.
Somewhere in her eyes there was a spark of curiosity that made her slowly climb back over the railing and walk towards the stairs that

would bring her down below the bridge the long way. From a distance the stranger followed, careful to not alert the Human to his
presence nearby.
After a minute he was leaning around the corner to get a peek at what the woman was doing if not throwing herself off the bridge.

Close up he could see more details about the woman. She was youthful, probably a few years younger than himself. Her eyes were the
color of seafoam in the sun, marred only by the dark makeup that ran down her cheeks in smeared streaks. Her skin was pale and freckled
across her cheeks and nose. Hair short, to her jaw and dark. Clothing wise she was dressed light; not appropriate for the weather or the
temperatures. Not to mention she was soaked to the bone and the cloth now stuck to her skin.

She was currently leaning over a drenched cardboard box, new tears springing to her eyes as she looked down at the scene before her. Her
hands, shaky at best, reached into Renji’s blindspot and came back with a mewling kitten. The kitten - angry and defensive - flashed his
teeth and they sank into flesh but the girl only flinched and continued to hold the weakened thing regardless of how deeply it sank its
fangs. “Poor baby...I’ve got you. It’s okay.”

“It’s okay...I’m sorry they did this to you. It’ll be okay now baby...”

She glanced up and spotted the stranger before he had a chance to step back out of sight. Her eyes went wide and she hugged the cat
closer to herself even though it dug its teeth in deeper.

“...I saw you on the bridge. You’re soaked.” The man in shadow said, knowing that he’d been caught and would be unable to slink away.

“I...yeah. Ugh...you know. I found a cat...” The Human said weakly with a sad and tired rasp to her voice as she spoke up loudly enough
for him to hear her. “...do you want a cat?” She suddenly added, holding up the creature as if she could hand off the only thing that had
kept her from jumping.

“...it’s biting you.”

“Yeah. It’s okay. It’s only because he’s scared and lonely...he doesn't understand I’m not trying to hurt him.” Her eyes turned to the box
and new tears sprung up from the well of sorrow behind the seafoam. Shifting his position Renji peeked over the edge of the box to see
what was upsetting the woman. There had been other kittens. One other yet still breathed but the weather and rain had managed to end
most of their suffering sooner than the one in her arms. “...so do you want a cat?”

“Aren't you going to keep him?”

For a moment her eyes crinkled and she was making a heartbroken smile. The woman even managed to laugh harshly. She didn’t expect
to be around to take care of a cat yet here she was, completely distracted from the attempt on her life by the soft mewling of another
dying creature.
. “...I don’t have anything for him at home.” She peered up from her crouched position; her knees soaked in frozen rain and river
water.  “...You seem like you’d be an animal person.”

“Let me bring you home. Where do you live?”

The woman didn’t reply for a while, holding the cat until little by little its teeth pulled out of her hand followed closely by a small flow of
blood that she paid little to no mind for.

“How old are you?”
“Do you live in this ward?”
“How about your name?”
“Do you have any friends to call...”

When each question was replied with only silence the man began to think she might try and go back to the top of the bridge. Normally

this was how he got food for himself and for the Cafe of Ghouls in this ward. Normally he wouldn’t interfere if a Human wanted to take
their own lives. Yet, now that he had been spotted and spoken to her-- watching her jump felt wrong.

Should he get her to talk---?
“...what are you naming the cat?”
She raised her head up and blinked owlishly at that final question, finally giving him her attention. What was the cat's name...?
“What’s your name?” She asked instead; still not answering anything.

“...Renji.”

“Oh. ...I’m Keiko. Kei for short. I live a few blocks down from here.” She picked up the second kitten - weaker than the first and
stumbled up. She was trying not to jostle the cat in her arms too much. He yowled and clawed at her forearms to try to jump down and
run to the box again. She hugged the creature and whimpered softly, whispering to the cat. “I’m sorry buddy. I know...I know...”

Renji took a few steps forward, raising an umbrella up over the head of the woman and gesturing for her to head up the stairs .
“I’ll walk you home. You need to get warm. You and them.” She looked too tired to argue, simply falling into step as she made her way up
the stairs. For a moment she shot the umbrella with a tired but appreciative smile.

## ♥

Renji watched the woman climb a set of metal stairs that lead to an apartment door. He could smell the blood that ran down her arm
from where the cat had clawed and bitten her. Sweet and warm - but easy enough to resist despite a small hunger starting to bare its teeth.
Still, she continued to simply coo soft words at the creature until it began to have an effect. The creature, once attached with its teeth and
claws was cradled in her arms calmly shivering along with her.

Awkwardly Renji stood back from the doorway after she cracked open the door and stepped into the dark apartment. “Ms...will you be
alright?”

She turned and her eyes skimmed him and the street behind him. Slowly, she nodded her head. “Tomorrow I’ll bring these two to the
vet...maybe they can find a home...”

“...keep them.” The man named Renji said. She shot him an odd look. Something confused mixed with pain. Did he not understand they
were keeping her from—

Oh. He did.

Keiko broke eye contact again and pouted indignantly. “...If you care so much then help me get them dried off.” The woman kicked her
door open further and left it part way open as she marched into the dark. The man meanwhile stared at her retreating back in open
surprise.

“Ms...?” He took a few steps forward, pausing at the doorway until a cat yowled in fear and anger further inside.
“Ms. Keiko?” He followed her then and closed the door gently behind him. Stepping into a Human house was an assault of scent and
pangs of hunger. Her scent was strong here; mingled with a weaker smell of another man.

Following the sounds he found that the woman had gone to her bathroom and was filling the bathtub up with warm water. The stronger

of the cats now fought with her once more as she tried to warm the cats and wash away grime and dirt. She seemed not to pay attention to
the cuts and bites along her arms.

“...There’s towels in the closet in the hallway.” Kei said, wincing for the first time as the cat flailed and tried to grip its way away from the
water. At a loss of what else to do he turned and went to the closet she spoke of. He opened it, finding the towels there. Unfolded and
simply tossed inside but clean.

He looked down the hallway and slowly began to see the mess that her home held. He supposed that she had had a recent heartbreak.
There were empty ordered food containers near a chair. The chair itself was piled high with blankets and a few too many pillows that
suggested that she’d been napping there.

Renji turned away from the apartment’s mess to bring her back the towel. She took it and swaddled the cat so it couldn’t fight or move.
The second cat didn’t fight nearly as much, its body went from still to shivering and then wiggling to try to flee the water. It’s condition
slowly improved until it was weakly mewling as well.

“There we go.” She took a second towel from Renji’s hands and swaddled the second cat to bring them both out to the living room. They
were placed gently in the chair with blankets. She kneaded the blankets down into a nest of sorts for the creatures.

“There...hopefully they’ll be good until morning.”

Her eyes traveled across own home lifelessly. “Sorry it’s a mess in here. Thank you.”

“It’s no problem. I’m glad you got home safely. Please take care, Ms. Keiko.” The silver haired male bowed his head and took his leave
back through the front door and out into the rain.
Once he was free of the home he took in a deep breath of fresh air not scented with blood from the Human woman. He could still smell
it clinging to the inside of his lungs and nose. Hungry as he was it made his mouth water - but he was no longer a child. He’d grown up
and had more control than that.

Ms. Keiko would live another night.

## ♥

He wasn’t sure why he showed back up the next day but he found himself in front of the apartment building when she exited.
Her sea-foam eyes caught on him standing there and she hesitated at the top of her stairs. “Oh...h-hello again. Ren...er. Um....Renji, right?
You’re not like...stalking me now or something, are you?”

“No. I...Came back to see how the cats were doing.” He inwardly winced at how lame that sounded coming from him. Yet her face
relaxed as she believed his off the cuff reason.
“You really could have them if you want. The shelter didn’t want them. Too many people are bringing in cats. Overcrowding they said. I
guess they’ve stopped taking every stray that’s brought to them...”

She paused and the silence between them grew oppressive before she added: “Uh...do you want to see them? They got up a while ago and
have even started playing. I need to get some things for them at the store though.” The male smiled faintly when she pulled out a long
paper list and scanned over it quickly.

---until she sneezed and sniffled.



He had thought this was likely to happen. The Human had been out in the cold and soaked in the winter temperatures. When she’d
gotten home she’d been so focussed on treating the cats so they’d survive that she’d neglected herself. And why wouldn’t she when she
had up until that point deemed last night to be her last.

“You’ve gotten sick.”

“I...it’s nothing. I’ve always gotten sick pretty easily. It was just cold last night. I’ll be fine. Just some sniffles. Did you want to see them
before I head out?”

“I’ll come with you.” Why did I say that? The ghoul asked himself instantly a moment after the words left his mouth.

“Um...okay. I guess....if you want. Are you sure you’re not a stalker?”
“Positive.”

“Right. Okay.” She climbed slowly down the stairway and tucked away the list in a back pocket. “Alright then. I guess if you're serious
then. There’s a pet store a few blocks down, I was just going to walk..” Renji watched how her eyes would turn towards him once in a
while as they walked. She seemed nervous and he wondered not for the first time why he’d shown up on her doorstep once again.

He stayed quiet as she picked through cat beds and food. Toys and treats. With it piled up high in her arms she watched him again while
he looked towards the other cats being sold at the store. “You know I was absolutely serious when I said you could have them. I’ll even
buy this stuff for you so you don’t have to worry about it.”

“No...I don’t have a place they can stay. My home isn’t cat friendly unfortunately.”

“Oh. I suppose that makes sense...do you know anybody who does want a cat?”

“I don’t...”
Uta maybe. No. That woman that’s been hanging around him has a big dog. Renji glanced again at the cats and frowned. There’s no telling
how well a cat and dog would get along. Although a Uta getting that close with a Human is just as surprising as cats and dogs...

His thoughts went to Aika Kaneshiro. Uta had brought her to Helter Skelter to meet them soon after she’d learned he was a Ghoul. She’d
been friendly with a slight edge of nervous and almost eager energy. It was odd for Uta to make more friends - even more so for him to
make a new friend who was Human. Apart from an old woman who made masks - Renji had believed that would have been a once in a
lifetime kind of deal.

Yet, when he watched how Aika had relaxed gradually even after only an hour or two of knowing Uta’s friends Renji was sure she’d be
sticking around. Even after he tried and failed to warn her that Uta could be dangerous.

He scratched at his chin while his mind was in the clouds. Was that supposed to be a warning, or a test? Whatever it’s purpose, I suppose
she’s staying. Uta’s already rather attached to her, bringing her to a favorite perch. Not to mention he’d even been asking Itori for some advice
once in a while.

“Renji-san?”

He turned, glancing around to find that he’d followed Keiko without really paying any mind right to the checkout counter. “Are you
okay? Can you hold these for a moment? I need to get my wallet.”


The woman was trying to fish her wallet out of her back pants pocket and balance everything at once. “I’ve got it.” What am I doing?
Renji pulled out his own money and placed it down on the counter in time for the cashier to check Keiko out.
“Wait? What? Why? ”

“I...” Renji struggled, unsure what to do or say. “You should keep the cats and watch out for them. I’ll come by and see them once in a
while.” Then hesitating he added: “If that’s okay.”

“You...want to share the cats?” Her voice was dubious and unsure; as though she couldn’t believe what she was hearing. Maybe she’d just
heard him wrong; Right?

“Um...yeah. I suppose...” He wasn’t sure anymore how he’d gotten here, let alone if this was a good idea. This could go very badly . He
was likely creeping the woman out by simply showing back up a night after almost witnessing her commit suicide. Surely she knew he’d
seen her linger on the bridge.
Linger---but not to stop her.

The cashier took the money Renji laid down and bagged the items before saying a ‘ thank you’ and wishing them a good day. Quiet, Keiko
walked back towards her home. Her eyes still shifted to look up at him curiously. She wasn’t quite sure what to make of him yet.

At her doorway, she once again left it swinging open and told the ghoul he could enter. He did so, quickly closing the door to keep the
cats from running out.
“Do you live with someone else?” He asked without thinking much about it. The smell of the other person was older and faded- possibly
more than a week or two. Maybe if that person came back she’d be less likely to try again with or without the cats. Yet, moments after he
asked it was obviously a mistake.

“...not anymore.”
“Friend?”
Keiko’s lips trembled as she laid down the bags full of items for the cats
“...my brother. He’s dead.”

“...” Renji stood by silently; frozen in place. He knew more than most that feeling. Taking a second look around the woman’s apartment
he understood the reason for the mess and carelessness of it. He even understood why she’d been out in the rain at that bridge. While he
thought and observed her home once more he missed how she shook in place, fists curling to claw into her palms as fresh tears crept up in
her eyes.
“...what happened?”

“H-he was my younger brother. It was my job to keep him s-safe...He w-went m-m-m-missing. At first I didn’t think it was anything odd.
He always hung out with his friends. Sometimes for days on end without coming back. I tried to find him or his friends. But the last time
anybody saw him they said he was taken away by some guys in suits to the CCG building in the first ward. N-nobody will listen to m-m-
me. The CCG denied they’d e-e-ver s-seen him but someone put his obituary in the p-paper.”

She grabbed a newspaper up and showed it towards him. He took it gently and turned it around; looking down at the area which had
been circled in bright yellow highlighter. Ayuki Kamiyama; Died of natural causes on the first of November leaving behind a sister, Keiko
## Kamiyama.


“I hired someone. They found out the person who paid for the obituary. N-natural causes m-my ass. They work at the CCG and they’re
lying about something. But his friends are gone in the wind and everybody thinks I’m crazy...I am going crazy.” She muttered, clenching
her fists and her teeth as more tears threatened to spill from her eyes.

The ghoul turned the paper around; before re-reading the obituary of the woman’s brother. ‘Human taken by the CCG?’He eyed the
woman and breathed in deeply again. She was very Human.  Not only that, the other male scent in the house was absolutely Human as
well.

Kieko took his silence as something negative. She saw his deep intake of breath, saw the frowning face and thought him worried or
agitated.

“He---He wasn’t a Ghoul. I’m not a Ghoul.” She said suddenly as though desperate for him to believe her. He couldn't immediately tell if
he wanted to laugh or to frown even further at the lady for her desperate plea for him to believe her. If only she knew. She had a Ghoul
standing in her home now. “If they thought he was, they were wrong !  He got into trouble sometimes. But it wasn’t ever serious!”

“I apologize, Ms. Keiko. I wasn’t thinking that you were. It’s concerning that they’re taking random citizens...”

“You believe me! ?” He looked up again to stare into those sea-foam green eyes looking up at him; hopeful and shining.

“I..suppose. Yes.”

“I really have been going nuts.” She wiped her eyes and sniffled again. “I’m sorry...I shouldn’t have just spilled that all on you. Ever since
this happened everybody else thinks I’m a Ghoul. It’s been awful.”

“Did the CCG come to talk to you?”

“...No.” Her cheeks turned slightly pink as she continued to speak. "They won’t let me near the building anymore either. I kind of...made
a scene the last time. They uh...don’t like it when people go there and...I might have punched a secretary...”

That would have gotten Itori and Uta to laugh, but Renji was too serious as he began to understand the situation. “No test to tell if
you’re a Ghoul? It would have been just a small prick and a small bit of blood.” She still shook her head and he frowned. So they already
know she’s Human without even bothering to test her. So they must know the brother is also only Human.

Perhaps his friends were Ghouls and he was found out. It’s a death sentence to be caught harboring Ghouls.

“How well did you know his friends?”

“Almost not at all...They weren’t bad people though! They didn’t do anything to him. They wouldn’t. I...just can’t find them. It’s like
they’ve also disappeared. I don’t even know where to start looking for them.” Suddenly her brows scrunched and she was staring at him
distrustfully again. “...are you from the CCG? Is this some sort of trick or game?”

Renji blinked as surprise settled in. “No? I...definitely not. I’m...” He took a short breath and sighed. Quickly spinning a lie Renji
explained: “My sister was taken from me by them many years ago. I’m wondering if it may be a similar situation all over again. I’m sorry If
I’m asking too much of you, Ms. Keiko...”

Still, there was doubt in her expression. He pulled out his wallet and pulled out an old and worn picture of a smiling woman with dark
hair. “Hikari...my sister. It’s been a long time. I still miss her every day though.”  The womans seafoam eyes scanned over the picture and
her body relaxed.


“Oh...I’m sorry.”

“...normally when civilians die from the CCG’s hands it’s because they either got in the way by accident. Or they harbored Ghouls. It is
illegal to keep information about existing ghouls from them.”

“You think his friends were ghouls.” Keiko said, piecing together what Renji was saying slowly. “I...don’t know anything about that.” She
said, suddenly defiant. The ghoul looked at her curiously as he attitude shifted. “I barely knew his friends. But...they were really nice.
Other than that. I don’t know a thing about them.”

Is...she protecting them? While she might truly know nothing, her words seemed to carry the same tone someone might say: “...And even if
I did, I wouldn’t tell you.” Ghouls she didn’t even know.

“I’d be careful. If they come looking for information. It’s best to give them everything you do know so you can stay safe.” He placed
down the newspaper and looked down at a cat who had begun to attack his pant legs.

“I...right. Of course I wouldn’t keep anything from them. Especially not some monsters I don’t even know.” It stung. But another part of
him felt light - the woman was speaking defensively. Her words were harsh but also a lie.

“Okay Ms. Keiko. I’ll come back again sometime.”

“To see the cats.” She said, nodding at the kittens.
“To see the cats.” He agreed.

## ♥

## Chapter 44: The Morning After
## Notes:
It has been ages since I've posted. And honestly a lot has happened. I'm okay---just I think I got burnt out and lost
muse. I did (and do have a few more chapters saved up. And I will be TRYING to continue this. Because I still have
plans! So if any readers are still out there----I am very sorry it took so long. But I am really, really, really sorry! I will
try my best to continue! Albiet my writing might have changed, for better or worse!
We are also getting to the point, where the story is progressing a little less day by day- and will start skipping ahead
little by little!
I dearly hope my writing is not for the worst.
Chapt er   Text

## Chapter 44:
The morning after hurt all together more than I had expected it might. I had expected aches and pains from my side, but I hadn’t
expected I’d be woken from deep and restful sleep by them. Once again captured in a tangle of strong arms I had to try to struggle to
wiggle out of the grasp. In the end I woke the sleeping ghoul in the process of ‘sneaking’ out of bed.

He leaned up on his elbow and yawned as I limped out of the room; eyes following me as I held my side. I made my way first to the
bathroom to grab some Tylenol. Taking two pills this time I cupped water to my mouth and swallowed them. Cautiously I checked the
total damage. The area where Renji had struck was still bruised but the colors were turning sort of greenish yellow. Those were signs of
healing at least so it was good to see. The freshed bruises were the ones that very vaguely matched where Uta’s fingers had pressed into my
hips. Not to mention the ones on my neck and shoulders which all were toothy in nature.

I gently rubbed the hickies on my neck and sighed softly when they ached. His love bites were a bit deeper dug into the skin and muscle
than his usual nips and they left darker marks than before. Safe to say; they’d be imprinted on my body for nearly as long as my actual
injuries from fighting.

Stepping out of the bathroom I looked for the time on the television cable box and pursed my lips. Six am. No matter if I was skipping
work or not - I still woke up around the same time. I wandered back, poking my head into the room to spot the ghoul, now hogging all
the blankets.

“Hey! You’re supposed to share those!”

“Mmmm...” The ghoul curled, pulling them closer to his body while I tried to pry some of the blankets away from the ghoul without any
success. With force out of option I limped to my side of the bed and crawled back into bed; curling so my back was to the ghoul and
‘pouted’. Sure enough, blankets were thrown back over my body and a warm body encompassed my back. “Mmmm....”

I smiled faintly and hummed a similar noise back at him - sleepy and very willing to stay just where I was for as long as we both wanted. I
needed rest right? “Opening late, Uta?” I felt an affirmative nod brush my shoulder. I relaxed - perfectly comfortable allowing the ghoul
to nuzzle his nose up along my neck and breath in my scent.

## Familiarity. Comfort. Trust.
Those things were building blocks of love of all shapes and sizes.

“I’ll help you around the shop later. Once the medicine kicks in...!!!” I squeaked softly when a hand slowly groped for my waist, sliding
under my shirt to gently touch my ribs. Behind me the ghoul murmured softly.
“Still hurts?”

“A bit.”

“Did I make it worse?”

“Not really.” I murmured, absolutely unwilling to admit if he did. Truthfully I couldn’t be completely sure that our activities had had
any great effect on my ribs. “You did leave some new marks on my hips though.” Coyly I grinned and glanced from the corner of my eye
to spot the ghoul’s opening eyes. “---Don’t worry though. I liked the activity that put them there. I’m very willing to do that again
sometime.”

The hand at my ribs slowly retreated downwards, massaging circles into my hips. Still smiling I relaxed and closed my eyes while the
fingers continued to explore. Soon I felt my oversized t-shirt being pulled gently to the side for Uta to take a look. A soft hum followed
the examination of my neck and shoulders and fingers gently brushed these bruises as well.

“Please don’t bite any today, Uta...” I murmured gently. “The marks aren't going anywhere any time soon.”


Regardless, the ghoul gently pressed his lips to the bite bruises and held still for a moment. He didn’t bite. Instead his lips brushed
sensitive skin before moving to another spot and doing the same again. I squirmed a bit, rolling over to face him which forced a stop to
the strange behavior. "... please Uta. Another hour to sleep..."

His chin rested on the crown of my head as I tucked my head down to nuzzle closer. The warmth of another body was welcome in the
winter - heat shared kept both parties comfortable. I peeked open an eye and turned my head to try to get a look at where his shoulder
met his neck. My fingers lingered over smooth healed flesh.

No matter how I tried to think or reason my way around it; I couldn't understand exactly why it bothered me that the ghouls' skin had
healed back so quickly. His quick regeneration hid my own bite mark. Perhaps his ghoulish behavior was rubbing off on me? Or the idea
that ghouls did this was appealing in some way to a recessive part of my ‘lizard-brain’.

Perhaps, Ghouls and Humans were not so different in that regard.
To show off. To claim something or someone as their own. Their other half was their prize and treasure: special and to be protected. To
love. Being able to have someone and for them to bear a mark or symbol of that connection for the world to see was...fulfilling.


I sighed softly and closed my eyes again. Inwardly I tried to push away the playful butterflies in my stomach while under my
fingers;resting where the bite had been Uta’s pulse beat. Steady and slow. Peaceful.

Although sleep did not return to me, relaxation was the second best. My fingers moved to softly kneed into muscle on the ghoul’s neck
and back. And after a while Uta noticed. “Can’t sleep?”
I hummed softly in reply.  “I think my body is just too used to getting up at this time. You?”

“...Mmm. I’ll get up and make some coffee.”

“ No. ” I said quickly, giggling soon after. “Uta. I’ll make it.” Reluctant to uncurl from his side I moved slowly ; whining softly at the lost
heat more than pain from my aching body. “Get around for work. I’ll bring you something to eat down too if you want.

Uta rolled so that he lay on his back, arms out to starfish across the whole of the bed after I was up. “Just coffee is fine, Ai-chan. I’ll get
something later.”

“Are you sure? Alright.”

Bjorn hopped up to his feet and wagged his way after me as I left the room. I got his food around first before starting the water to boil on
the stove. A few minutes later the door to the bedroom opened and closed and the ghoul emerged - still only half dressed in a baggy pair
of sleep pants. He joined me in the kitchen and loomed quietly nearby as the water came to a boil. As I slowly poured water in circles over
the coffee grounds where it dripped into the pot the ghoul stayed close by; waiting for the finished product.

When it was done the ghoul leaned up to the cupboard and picked out two mugs. One of which had a funny message on it. While his
mugs had been for the most part all matching, plain and cream colored; mine are definitely not. When I’d moved we now collectively had
a full cabinet of many funny and novelty mugs.


He turned it around and read the message; lips twitching into a subtle smile. “Blood of my enemies?”

“You like it? I think I have another one that’s the ‘tears of my enemies’” I watched as he leaned up and picked out a few more mugs to
read them. I laughed out loud again when he picked up another mug that read: “ Mess with the honk, get the bonk .” The mug featured a
goose holding a baseball bat in its beak.

“Here. Pick one so I can pour your coffee.” The ‘ blood of my enemies ’ mug was placed on the counter along with the goose mug while he
put away the rest he had been reading. As I poured, the ghoul finally seemed to look around. First at the devices now located in the
kitchen then around at the picture as a while.  From the counter tops to the floor and even the top of the  cabinets it was dust free and
clean.

“You cleaned a lot...”

“Yeah. I tried to. Sorry if you can still smell the bleach. It was pretty strong for a few days. I was pretty bored honestly. Since I promised
not to go anywhere like shopping or out for fun I didn’t have much to do except lounge around here.” I poured my own drink after his
and added cream and sugar to it. “--I was going to paint my old apartment; I have the paint for it now. Even covered everything in plastic.
But after Ms. Kirin gave me that scare, I didn’t really have time. I guess I’m going to have to do that soon. Not to mention letting the
landlord know that I won’t be renewing.”

The ghoul lifted up his mug to his lips, inhaled and then exhaled a content noise. He sipped the drink and smiled faintly. “Good as
always.”

“Good enough to keep me around? I bet that’s why you asked me to move in!!!” I joked with a coy grin. “I better not teach you how to do
it yourself. I’ll become disposable.”

The expression on Uta’s face made me pause, else I’d have coffee up my nose. He had stopped from taking another sip and stared with
wide eyes. Laughing and choking up because of his surprised expression I held up a hand in placation.
“Uta-kun! It’s a joke! A joke! Please--”

Then, grinning like the Cheshire cat I added: “--Of course I was joking. You can never get rid of me. After all; there’s no way you can
make good coffee. I think you’d have figured it out by now if you could.” Nudging him playfully as I passed him I limped back out of the
kitchen and took a seat on the couch to watch the morning news.

The ghoul emerged; leaning on the door frame between the rooms. A slow smile crept onto his face as he got the ‘joke’ and the teasing
were just that. Taking a slow sip he pretended to mull it over. “Humm...I could learn. But it wouldn’t be as good.”

“Yeah. It would get really expensive to go to Anteiku every day for coffee. Not to mention having to ride the train over. What a pain! I
think you’re better off just keeping me around honestly.”

“I don’t think they’d let me back for coffee. They like you.”

I scoffed humorously and winked. “That’s just 'cause’ I’m so amazing you know.” I smiled, still joking until the ghoul walked past
me,leaned over the couch to press a surprise kiss onto my forehead. It was a soft whispered ‘you are’ that plucked softly on my
heartstrings and made me silent. No more jokes as he left the room to get dressed for the day.

## ♥

After Uta left the apartment to work on things in the shop and I’d finished my drink I finally decided to put on some proper clothing and
rewrap my foot tightly so it would keep down swelling. As I suspected the work the day before had aggravated it significantly and any

amount of wiggling or walking was quite painful.

Uta can heal from disembowelment but I sprained my ankle and it’s all over for a week or more.

Regardless there were things that had to be done. Walking down the stairs I grabbed my coat and Bjorn’s leash. “Uta-kun. I need to bring
Bjorn out for a walk. I won’t be going very far. Glad I took the day off work though...” I winced, hating that I had to admit that defeat.
“My ankle is annoying.”


“I’ll bring him.” The ghoul stood up, reaching to take the dog leash from my hands.

“But the shop, you just opened and---”

“You can watch it. If anybody comes; I’ll be right back.” When he stood up he patted the back of his seat and wheeled it closer to me.
“There’s some straps that need to be attached if you want to help.”

I flustered at the amount of trust he had in me to watch his shop. Especially since his shop was something that was precious to him.
Taking a seat; I squeaked softly when he pushed the chair back towards the desk and pointed out the masks that needed straps.

“Don’t take too long...” I murmured softly.

I watched with a wobbly smile as Uta hooked Bjorn’s leash to the dog. Then, as though he wasn’t quite sure if it’s what he should do - the
ghoul hesitantly laid the leash over the dog's back just like I did.  The canine, equally unsure, looked from me to the ghoul. “Go on, Bjorn.
I’ll be right here.” Finally, he walked to Uta’s side and waited patiently for the door to open.

“...I’ll be back Ai-chan.”
“Yeah, okay.” I murmured as I picked up a needle, thread and a set of straps meant to keep a mask on somebody. More confidently I
smiled and waved. “I’ll be here, stay safe you too.”

I couldn’t help that I looked up every couple minutes and listened to see if I could hear them coming back.
After ten minutes I started to worry.
Twenty was a tipping point when I anxiously touched my phone and looked at the contacts to see if Uta had sent anything at all. Or
anybody else for that matter.

Thirty minutes and the work on the masks was set aside entirely and despite my injured leg I paced back and forth across the shop. A t
forty-five minutes the door opened and I turned on a dime, hoping to see my boyfriend return. Instead I was faced with a familiar
investigator.

“Amon, What are---” Behind him stood Uta with Bjorn in tow. The dog bounded up to me and wiggled around while I leaned over to pat
his head. Quickly though he wandered off to a spot he preferred in the shop and laid down.

“I found him hanging outside your old apartment knocking on the door. Sorry I took so long.”

“Oh...What can I help you with, Amon-san? It hasn’t been that long since the last time you showed up. Nothing else happened, has it?
I’m going to start to think I attract bad luck.” I cursed inwardly; had I jinxed myself by mentioning the man the day before?

“No!” The man held up his hands and gave me a friendly smile. ”I’m sorry! But this time it’s nothing like that. I thought I’d drop off

some things for you.” The man rubbed the back of his neck nervously. Amon took a few steps over to the seat where Uta normally
measured people’s heads for a mask and sat down a silver suitcase. He clicked the button and I could see Uta tense from across the room. I
tried to peek around the investigator to see why. After the button clicked down, a few switches flipped and the case popped open
revealing the handle of a reddish hammer? The body of the weapon seemed to be kept contained by the case.

Was that...A Quinque?!

I didn’t have long to school my expression from horrified sickness to neutral before Amon turned and held out a small cardboard box he
pulled from a side pouch of the same suitcase. “Thankfully, I don’t have any bad news this time. But last time I saw you, you seemed a
little worried about your RC count. But if you had access to testing...it might make you feel better.”

He opened the box to show off three separate vials.
“I...seriously? Those tests are so expensive. I can’t accept those, Amon. I don’t have the money to pay for those--”

The investigator looked flustered once more, and sheepishly avoided looking at me or Uta. “Well. What the board doesn't know won’t
hurt them. The instructions are all in there. Normally they give these to us investigators to make sure none of us were exposed to
something. But my count has been steady for years...”

Amon moved to place them on the desk next to me, closing the lid and patting it. “A change in count isn’t alarming if it goes up or down
each month from ten or twenty points. But if it goes up and doesn't return to normal or if it continues to go up then you could have a
real problem...”

The investigator sighed, putting on a serious expression. “I didn’t want to scare you Ms. Ka---Aika. I simply feel it’s important to tell you
because your baseline readings were already so high. It puts you at greater risk. Regardless of what the office may think: You need those
tests far more than me.” I felt awkward as I glanced at the test kit and then back at the investigator.

He really really liked his job. Liked protecting people.
He even seemed so very earnest about this.


”There’s...just one thing with these. Normally if you did have a higher number it says to send it in and contact the office. If you need help
please call me before you send in the results.” The man awkwardly shifted his weight foot to foot for a moment before adding quieter:
“Those test id numbers are labeled for my use. And strictly speaking I am not supposed to give them out.”

My mouth made a little ‘o’ as I stared up at the investigator. He was taking a bit of a risk just to go ahead and get me some tests. It
was...sweet. Awkward - considering present company. I really had to wonder how well they could do their job if they could be standing
feet from a ghoul and not realize it. Uta really didn’t hide it well.


“So if I sent them in, they’d think your RC level’s had spiked.” I suddenly giggled. “Geez. That could really get you into hot water pretty
fast... I won’t . I promise.” More seriously I continued speaking: “Amon-san. Honestly I really appreciate how you’ve checked up on me a
few times after that whole mess with my boss a few months back. But now I’m fine. Better than fine. I’ve got a lot of friends watching my
back and I moved in with this guy...” I tipped my head towards the goth quickly. “He invited me to move in recently. So, I think I'm
doing a lot better than when you first met me. You really don’t need to keep checking in. I’m sure there’s a lot of people you should be
looking after. Family? Kids? Something like that?”


Flushed, the man's face got very red very quickly and he held up his hands in front of his chest. “N-no. Nothing like that. I...” Slowly his
shoulders slumped and his face held a sad smile. “I apologize. I just like seeing people involved in this sort of thing. Checking up on them
and making sure they’re still okay. It’s good to see the people who are still alive...”


Oh. Yeah. I supposed I understood that. In his profession he ran into situations with dead and dying humans. Brutalized, half eaten. I was
well aware that some ghouls did not simply eat humans but play with their food as well which would leave some gruesome scenes for
them to find. Seeing some living people he helped probably gave him some peace at night and let him sleep.

“I am fine Amon. I promise.” I took a second glance at the test kit and sighed a little dramatically . “If you insist on this, I’ll do it. Okay?
But...I’ve been trying not to worry about it too much.”

“Of course. I---” The man stopped speaking when a cell phone rang. He dug into his pocket and pulled out the device and pressed it to his
ear. “Amon speaking...?” A grim look overtook his friendly expression and he pulled the phone from his ear and covered the mouth piece
with his palm. “I’m sorry to cut this short...but work calls. Please. Use those to make sure you’re not getting worse. Once a month should
be okay. If nothing happens in three months - then that should be a good indication.”

He nodded towards us again, picked up his suitcase and let himself out of the shop with nothing but a small chime to announce his
departure. I stood still for a moment, staring at the door where he left.

“Huh....well that was.. .Interesting .”
When I looked back at the ghoul by my side I found that Uta had picked up the box and turned it over in his hands. Flipping open the
cardboard flap he opened the box revealing the three vials and a list of instructions. As promised. Carefully he picked one up and put it
close to his eye to peer through it before placing it back.
“You should use these.”

“I suppose so...” I muttered, as I gently took them from his hands and pulled out the instructions. “Seems fairly simple. Stab,
bleed...drops of this solution and...a testing meter? I really figured this would be more complex.” Deadpan I put things back into the box,
closed it and sighed. “---instead finding out if the number is rising is as simple as a PH test. It’s a little ridiculous. I guess I’ll test it again
some time.”

“...try now.”

“What? But he just tested it a few weeks ago? Remember?”

“...That was before you decided to bite me.” Though the mark was long gone the ghoul touched the spot where the bite had been. “...that
could have been bad for you. I’m not sure what happens to a human if they eat a Ghoul.”

“Are you concerned about that now? And anyway, biting is certainly not eating you.” The ghoul blinked and then avoided eye contact by
burying himself in work once more. Scooting me away he took his seat back at his desk and slid over to where I had been working before
growing worried for his safety. “You are worried!” I murmured and frowned at the box.

“Okay! Alright! But you're helping! I don’t think I can stab myself.”
Uta glanced up from the work desk and reached, palms up for the testing kit.
“Alright...”

“First prick the finger. Drop five to ten drops of blood into the vial. Add three drops of solution. Screw on the cap and shake well. Wait for
three minutes and then return to the solution.  Insert electronic scanner into the combined contents and hold the power button.”

Digging around in the box I found the little scanner and turned it around to look at the dark display. “...it looks like a thermometer. I
guess there’s probably something sharp around that you could use.”

The ghoul rolled and spun his chair around to face the drawer where he kept his piercing items and then rolled back with a sanitized
needle in hand. I watched as Uta pulled out a vial and held the needle waiting. I closed my eyes, bit my bottom lip and stuck my hand out,
index finger presented for easy stabbing.


A few heartbeats passed and then a sharp prick in my finger made me flinch back. Hissing through my teeth I tried to pull my hand back
only to be caught firmly around the wrist. “Hold on.” I looked at him through squinted eyes as I tried not to look as he gently squeezed
my finger and drop by drop the vial turned red.

After he was done, Uta released my hand and I brought it to my chest. Uta did the rest of the steps, following the instructions as I had
read them. Finally putting aside the solution he looked at the clock. “Three minutes. Then we check.”

His eyes flicked to my bleeding finger and reached out towards the wrist. Gently he pulled the limb towards him to take a look at it. Eyes
that matched the small well of blood on the fingertip looked over the small wound before searching my own eyes. “You should get a
bandaid, Ai-chan...”

When I made no move to pull away the ghoul bent forward and slipped the index into his mouth. My pulse fluttered under the fingers at
my wrist and my breath stalled with a small hiccup. I could feel his tongue slick over a small flow of blood, teeth pressing ever so gently on
the second knuckle and the slight suction as he pulled a little more blood from the punctured skin. All the while keeping eye contact.


When he pulled back there was a soft pop as his lips left the finger and he licked his lips. “Breath Ai-chan...” I hadn’t fully realized I’d
stopped, but I felt the relief of intaking oxygen and flushed red to the face.
“S-sorry.”

“...“ He tilted his head, expression blank.
“You didn’t frighten me.” I murmured quietly to reassure him. “You just surprised me. That didn’t bother you, did it?”

“No. I’m not hungry...” He seemed to think something over and then added: “After last night I wanted to double check to make sure the
taste wouldn't make me hungry.” A small smile tugged at his lips as he turned his head towards the desk. His eyes landed on where I’d
placed down the two straps I’d gotten done while he was out. “...”

“Oh. I didn’t get much done. I got worried after you were gone for over half an hour. I wasn’t able to concentrate on finishing up any
