others.” I smiled sheepishly. “I didn’t want to work on it while distracted and screw them up.”

“I’d have just fixed it. You were worried?”

“Of course I was! You were gone longer than I thought you’d be. Maybe don’t come home with investigators in tow next time too. That
almost gave me a heart attack. What on earth were you thinking?”

“I thought it would be funny.” My eye twitched as irritation reared its ugly head. Taking a calming breath I kneaded my fingers into my
temples.
“Seriously Uta? An investigator ? You brought a Dove to your home, because it would be funny? ”
The ghoul grinned to himself, amused by his ghoulish joke and close encounter with the ‘other side’ of society. “Watching you fluster
him is quite funny as well. I thought I’d bring him here where he’d embarrass himself.” Then the ghoul looked at the small test tube
sitting on the desk, waiting for it’s readings to be discovered. “It was good I did...he brought you those. Maybe I won’t eat that one..”

Ignoring his later comment, I rolled my eyes. “...I still can’t believe he just gave them away. These things are expensive. Even one can cost
over 500,000 Yen to the general public. Insurance companies won’t even cover part of it if the CCG doesn't send in an order for it!
Completely ridiculous. Tests like this only cost a couple yen to put together; yet companies overcharge to earn thousands of times the
worth of it.” Worst of all, I knew the Kaneshiro company was no better with their tests and medicines.


“Times up.” Uta noted as he picked up the small vial full of my blood and the solution. Unballing my fists I grabbed the small testing
device and waited as Uta popped off the top and held it steady for me while I dipped the end in and clicked the button.
“Here goes nothing.”

Uta leaned close, leaning to look at the testing screen as it blinked a polite message: “Please wait, Please wait, please wait.”

“Results: 675. Recommended action: Report information to Main Office.”
“Results: 675. Recommended action: Report information to Main Office.”
“Results: 675. Recommended action: Report information to Main Office.”
“Results: 675. Recommended action: Report information to Main Office.”
“Results: 675. Recommended action: Report information to Main Office.”

“...That’s...about five higher than the first test.” I murmured before I bit my bottom lip. Anxiety gnawed at my insides as I stared at a
blinking six hundred and seventy five. “It’s probably the normal fluctuation that he was talking about, Right?”

The ghoul beside me made a small noise in the back of his throat. It sounded like he agreed. Yet I couldn’t help but to look at the blinking
number with apprehension. I still wanted to know why it was high to begin with. “What level are Ghouls at again?”

“That depends. From what I’ve heard; if someone reaches one thousand they’ll develop ROS. Either gaining ghoulish traits or getting sick
with failed Kagune tumors.” He tipped his head and considered something. “I knew of a cannibal that hasn’t turned ghoulish even
though he’s been killing for ages..”

“A human cannibal?” I hesitated and scrunched my eyebrows. “That’s vaguely comforting in one way. At least that suggests it’s difficult
to raise the number enough to go over the limit. But also very deeply disturbing.”

“I haven't heard anything about him recently. I believe he was hospitalized due to poor health a little while back.”

“Oh. Wait. Hold on; so did anybody catch him? Do they know what he was doing?”

The ghoul tilted his head again. “You want him caught?”

“Yeah. I mean; He’s killing people.”

“I kill people.” Uta said, stating the obvious once more.

“Yes, I know that Uta. But it’s different. You need to. A human has other options. He’s just sick.”


“...I could get food from Anteiku. Or find it myself like Renji...”

“I wouldn’t ask that of you.”

“...Nishiki-san and Ki---”


“I’m not Kimi. And you’re not Nishiki.” I said; interrupting him and placing down the testing device on his desk. Reaching to cup gently
under his chin I made him look at me; staring into those bloody iris. “You’re fine the way you are. I love you; just as you are. Murder and
all...you don’t need to change anything.”

“---Maybe that makes me a horrible person...” But since I’d met him, I’ve seen ghouls conform around humans. Adjusting and suffering
to make the people around them feel comfortable. I couldn’t ask Uta to do that for me.

“...I love you too.” My heart seemed to swell at the soft words; no louder than a breath. I might be horrible; but it was worth it. Just to hear
those words! I leaned forward and pressed my forehead against his for just a moment before pulling back; releasing his chin. Noticing my
finger was still bleeding I pouted.
“You were right. I really do need a bandage...” This time it was of my own will that I held out the finger for him. Obediently the ghoul
leaned forward and swept the blood up off my skin with his tongue.

“Now that you’re back I’ll go upstairs to take care of this. Also I’ll have to hide these tests. I’ll be back to help you again...so you’d better
make me a long list of what I can do.” I collected up the test and all the kit's components before limping my way up the stairs to hide the
kit someplace. In the end I ended up putting it high up - on top of the kitchen cupboards where there was just enough space to slide it
where it couldn’t be seen from the ground.
Afterwards, I got a bandaid from the bathroom and wrapped it carefully around my finger. Returning back to the shop I picked up the
straps he’d shown me before he left and I sat on ‘my’chair to work. While I’m sure that this wasn’t exactly what Yoshimura had meant
when he said I should rest. I imagine that looked more like saying in bed in his head; however sitting again meant that my ankle was able
to rest regardless.




## Chapter 45: Raw Meat
## Notes:
As a Treat because I'd been so long. I am posting a few chapters at a time. I've gotta motivate myself into writing
more. And I hope that people who are/were reading it are still out there! I know how it can be after not having a
story update for two years (or more!) ♥
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 45: Raw Meat

A little over a week later and after many days of healing and ‘taking it easy’ I was able to leave the shop and take a deep breath of fresh,
crisp winter air. Without limping and without a wrap. Feeling invigorated I raised my hands up over my head and stretched out and
upwards with a throaty groan.
Uta exited out the shop after me, locking the door behind him. Despite it being my day off I was insisting that we headed over to get a
cup of coffee. I’d even neglected to make either of us coffee as of yet in favor of convincing him to go to the cafe. The ghoul had dressed
in a warm sweater and a beanie that covered most of his hair. Only his bangs hung by the side of his head.
Meanwhile I’d neglected a hat and instead had curled a scarf around my neck, shoulders and burrowed my jaw into the plush covering.
Body tucked away in the jacket I’d bought so long ago with Itori I felt plenty warm. Bjorn meanwhile was getting the zoomies out,
running down the backroad one way and then zipping back the other way past us.
With his fingers shoved into his pockets the ghoul followed as I walked us towards the subway station. “Hey Uta?”

“Mmm?”
“Can we go visit Itori tonight? I haven't seen her in a while. Actually---” I continued, with a raised eyebrow. “Neither have you. You’ve
been so busy catching up after the holidays and after your trip that you’ve hardly been out and about at all. You should probably drop by
so she knows you’re not dead at this point.”
The ghoul turned his eyes around to look at me from the side of his glasses. “The bar? Sure. I’ll let her know you’ll be there too. But we’ve
caught up on masks now. The only ones I have left to finish now are ones I make for fun...”
We were caught on mask orders. The plural pronoun was almost enough to make me giddy. Sure I wasn’t working for Uta in any official
way, and the tasks I had adopted were minimal and simple. Yet he’d insisted that I was helping and a couple customers were starting to
recognise me. At the very least I looked at it like I was taking away the menial, repetitive tasks and freeing him up to do the creative artsy
tasks such as carving, shaping and painting.
“Yeah...I suppose after that one guy and his friends bought a couple off the wall you’d have to replace those with more. Do you know
which ones---” I blinked as the ghoul moved to wrap an arm around my shoulders and pull me firmly closer as we walked down the road.
Bjorn on the other hand strode along my other side and let out a low warning growl. Looking up at his face first I followed where his iris
and his ire was currently aimed. Upon finding him looking at the shorter, square-faced old woman I pursed my lips and whispered softly.
“Come on Uta. I think she’ll be fine...remember. I said try to be `friendly’.”
I heard Uta intake a breath of air a little sharply as I pulled from his arm and raised a hand up to wave towards the old lady. “Hello Ms.
Kirin. How are you doing this morning!?”

The woman startled, dropping a bag of recycles with a clatter, scattering some of the bottles. Turning around the narrowed eyes fell upon
myself and the mask maker. Upon seeing us she seemed to shrink in place. “Good Morning, Ms. Aika. It’s nice to see you...where are you
two out to this early? Work again, dear?”
“Kind of!” I took a few steps forward, ignoring the warning grumbles from either the ghoul or Bjorn and bent down to pick up some of
the scattered bottles.
“But I'm not working today! We’re just going for a cup of coffee ourselves and to visit Yoshimura-sama. Also- I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to
startle you and make you drop your--- ” Curiously I peered at the labels on the recycling the woman was doing. There were bottles of
water, but also Ramune and Matcha bottles. Something Ghouls wouldn’t be able to drink.
“---cans. Do you collect these off the streets to turn in?”


“I---yes. I do...”

“That’s really nice! I wish more people did that. Do you want to come to have coffee with us? We can drop these off on the way.” I
smiled, ignoring the sideways glance from Uta.

The woman’s head turned to look nervously between myself and the man beside me. “I-I suppose that would be nice. But dear...Is that
really alright?”
“Yeah. It’s fine. Anteiku has really good coffee! If you haven't had it you should!” I glanced at Uta for myself. I knew it could be an issue.
I had my own issues with the woman after she’d already seemed interested in ending my life. It would be far better to be friendly and keep
her in our sights. Afterall, we’d tried the ‘threaten-and-forget’ method. Clearly that hadn’t worked. Was it difficult to act this way
towards her? Definitely. Was I being overly friendly? Perhaps.
It could be that I was overcompensating for the silent brooding boyfriend. “Why wouldn’t it be?”
“...It’s fine.”
Uta hadn’t been ecstatic about the idea of being friendly with her. But after our little visit I had managed to get him to at least say he
wouldn’t KOS her. He had in this case put on a stony expressionless expression once more.
“See---” I leaned down and picked up another bottle. “---It’s fine! Plus I owe you for startling you and making you drop all these. Lemmi
help!”
Bjorn stepped forward and picked up a bottle and brought it to me after watching me pick up a couple. Slowly the woman bent to pick
up a few that had fallen for herself. After a minute they were all deposited back into the bags she carried and she nodded her thanks.

“Come on. There’s a deposit for these near the station! Do you want me to carry some?”

The woman shook her head no, yet a few blocked on she stopped to take a breather. I reached out and smiled. “Please, let me help. Young
folk gotta be useful for something, right?”
Reluctantly the woman gave me one of the bags and I carried it onwards with a happy grin. Our odd little group paused again at the
recycling bins and we slowly emptied the bags into their proper spots. The train ride was nearly as quiet as I hummed softly as I watched
the subway and occasional city sights zip by. Once we were in the twentieth ward and getting off the train I picked up our conversation
once again. “Hey, if you know Uta then you must know Renji too maybe?”
“...” The woman seemed to think and then her eyes went wide. “Silver haired kid with the raven mask?”
“That’s the one! Figured you would. You’ve been in the fourth ward for a while haven't you?”
“Ages dear...Since I was young and I’m nearly eighty-five.” She nodded her head slowly and smiled; her anxiety seemed to be leaving her
so very slowly; but I was making some headway!

“Nah! Couldn’t be! Sixty. At most! Not a day older!”
The woman chuckled softly and smiled as the old women had a habit of doing while complimented by the young. Separated as I was
from most of society, I was still taught socialite habits and small talk by tutors. There had been the odd event or two that my parents had
wanted to show me off. Now, years later they came in handy! “Thank you dear. That’s nice of you to say.”

I happily entered Anteiku with a bounce in my step and took a seat at the counter where Koma was the first to see me. “Aika! You don’t
work today. Did you forget?”

I shook my head and with a quick nod at Uta and the old woman indicated I was with them. “Just came by to make sure the place wasn’t
falling to pieces, and get some coffee!”
Yoshimura entered the room through the door behind the counter and smiled; peering over our group with a friendly smile. “Ah. Aika
and Uta. Welcome back.” His eyes landed on the older woman and paused. “Hummm. I don’t believe I’ve seen you here before.
## Welcome!”
“Oh, sir. This is our neighbor down the street. She lived across from me before I moved in with Uta-kun.”
From my point of view I saw Koma’s face change suddenly as he eyed the older woman. He had heard through the grapevine about what
had happened. As had everybody at Anteiku. His gaze was now a little more intense. The manager on the other hand stayed neutral as he
nodded. “Oh I see.”
“I invited her to come along for a coffee.” I explained. “And helped her with her recycling while we were at it!” Koma and the manager
both started working on coffee orders while I leaned over and bumped Uta’s arm lightly.
“Hum?”

“You’re not mad at me are you?”

“Geez. You’re too friendly, Aika.” It wasn’t Uta who answered, instead it was Nishiki who leaned across the counter and ‘whispered’. It
wasn’t too subtle and I was sure that Ms. Kirin overheard. Though a quick glance around the cafe informed me that all the current
patrons were known ghouls. “Isn’t that the old hag who tried to kill you?”
The ‘hag’ in question bent her head towards the counter and pursed her lips into a thin line. Surely by now she’d come to the conclusion
that was most obvious by now. I was surrounded by a whole lot of ghouls who cared about my safety. It was perhaps cruel of me - but
even this I’d thought of ahead of time.
Afterall, If Uta alone wasn’t enough then perhaps knowing that I had others close to me would be enough to convince her to leave me be.
Not only that. But it should prove that I was friends with these people. Not simply getting information to hand them in. I was genuine
and truly not a threat.
“Umhum. But she’s fine. We made up - right?” I smiled faintly towards the old woman and waited. Slowly she raised her head and
managed a small smile.
“Yes dear.”

Ms. Kirin called for her bill far sooner than either Uta or myself. When the bill came for the old woman I leaned forward and plucked it
up faster than she could take it. “I’ll get your coffee since I invited you! If you like it here and you come in while I work I’ll make a cup for
you myself! Okay?”
Seemingly speechless, the elderly woman opened and closed her mouth a few times before nodding. “That’s very kind of you, dear...”

“Get home safe!” I waved as the short little woman shuffled out of the building with half a dozen pairs of eyes on her. “...hum...” I turned
my eyes towards the old man across the counter from me. On his face was a small, knowing smile. He nodded slightly and slid a second
sweetened coffee to me. It seemed at least Yoshimura had caught on and at the least seemed to approve.
“Geez. How careless are you? You invited her to your work? Look. I know you're friendly with us because you work with us but...Why
even try with that one?”
“Nishiki, despite popular opinion I genuinely think you’re pretty cool!” I laughed as his face turned three different colors before
returning to normal upon realizing I was joking around with him.
“Ever heard the saying: You catch more flies with honey than vinegar? You can win people to your side more easily by gentle persuasion
and flattery than by hostile confrontation.” I took a sip of my drink and let out a long sigh and finally let some of my own tension ease
away.
“And I’d much prefer to be friendly with someone who lives that close than to keep being at odds.” I glanced to my side and placed my
hand on Bjorn’s head and rubbed his ears. At the very least, this small bit of manipulation and friendly conversation (and the price of a
single coffee) might be just enough to get her to stop being aggressive.

## ♥

After some nice small talk and some very good coffee, Uta and I left the cafe with Bjorn happily loping after us. His nose was against the
ground smelling all around whenever he could afford to stop and sniff.
Uta on the other hand was quiet again. While it wasn’t unusual for Uta I remained worried after unexpectedly inviting Ms. Kirin with us.
I bumped his arm lightly and tilted my head at him. He peered down at me: “Hum? Are you hungry?”
I blinked, surprised by the question. With pursed lips I gently reached and raised his glasses out of his eyes to peer at him closely. He
slowed and stopped while I peered up into his wide eyes. The random examination clearly perplexed him but he stayed quiet.
“...hum. I thought you were mad or something. You were so quiet at the cafe.” Then, belatedly I answered: “No. I’m not really hungry...”
My stomach growled, as though to disprove my statement a moment after it left my lips. I sniffed the air and sighed while saliva pooling
in my mouth. I had to admit that the bakery really knew how to market their goods. Just let the smell waft out the doors and down the
street! “But those brownies smell amazing!~”
The ghoul sniffed and I saw his lips twitch down into a grimace before returning to neutral. “Does it? We can stop.”
Mouth watering I could hardly resist the offer to stop and grab a treat. I smiled sheepishly and nodded. “You don’t mind? You can wait
outside with Bjorn if you want.” That at least gave him an excuse not to walk inside. It was an out he was more than happy to accept. I
grinned as I left the ghoul by the doorway with the big white dog who watched me enter the bakery and sweet store. Standing in front of
the main counter I leaned over and peered in at the colorful treats.
“Can I help you dear?” I stood up straight again and smiled at the friendly face behind the counter.
“Yes please! My boyfriend picked me up some brownies from here before and I swear they were the best I’ve ever had! I had to come
back!” I laughed softly and added: “And the smell brought me back of course!”
The middle aged woman with curls spun in her hair laughed softly. “I’ve been hearing that all day. I suppose the scent gets away from this
place through the vents while we bake a fresh batch. But you came at a good time. There’s some brownies fresh from the oven ready.
Would you like one of those?”

“Two!” I said cheerfully, glancing back towards Uta who could be seen waiting for me through the glass storefront. Sure, he couldn’t eat
it. But I could at least act like he could and order an extra. It really didn’t hurt that they were delicious! It certainly wasn’t going to go to
waste.

The woman peered past me and then smiled. “Oh! Of course. One for your boyfriend! I think I remember seeing him here a month or so
back! Not one of our usual customers...”
“I normally come here for work. But we live in different ward so we don’t get over here much for casual shopping.”
“Ah. That explains it! ★” I watched as the woman brought out a steaming hot pan of brownies and cut them into slices before placing
two of them in wrapping. I handed over the money for them in exchange and took my treats with a smile. The woman across the counter
bowed her head and her usual goodbyes and thank you’s were spoken.
With my fresh baked goodies bagged up in one hand I exited the shop to return to Uta’s side. The ghoul had been quietly watching the
people come and go down the street. Bjorn was the first to notice I’d exited the building; wagging his tail and standing up upon my
return. The ghoul turned next, cocking his head curiously when he looked at the small brown baggie in my hands. “Found what you
wanted?”
“Mmmhm! Those brownies you brought to work for me before were amazing! Had to get more!” Aware we were in public I held up the
bag and grinned. “I bought you one too!”
I laughed softly when his mouth briefly made a little ‘o’ of surprise on his face before settling back to his neutral expression. Of course I
didn’t want him to eat it and get sick as he had before with a muffin, but for public appearances---- I winked. “Thanks Ai-chan. They
smell warm.”
“Yeah! They were fresh from the oven. She just took them out. Is there anyplace you want to go since we’re in the area?” With his hands
dug into his pockets he started to walk. Keeping up with him I watched his face as he thought it over.
“Hum. Yeah actually. There is an art supply store around here I should visit. They might have some extra supplies I can’t get at our local
shop...”
“Okay!” I happily agreed. The ghoul watched forward as we walked the streets, but he seemed to be thinking.
“Ai-chan. Why don’t you wait over there?” He spoke up as he pointed out a table across from the craft store. I glanced to where he was
pointing and pouted.
“What---why?”
“A surprise.” Of course it was. The ghoul continued on his way towards the shop with a short wave over his shoulder. “Wait here and eat
your brownie Ai-chan!~ I won’t be long.”
Disgruntled yet obedient, I sat myself down with a huff of air and pursed my lips as I pulled out one of the still warm brownies. Bjorn
settled down to sit next to me and watch the storefront where Uta last was seen.
“Stay here he says.” I murmured, taking a bite out of the brownie. ‘Ohhhh that’s good!’ I thought my souring mood fled in favor of
enjoying the flavor of warm baked fudge brownies. I happily hummed and swayed with a mouthful of sweet brownie and very slowly
tried to nibble at it to enjoy it thoroughly.
When I took the last bite and glanced again to the store front I realized that the ghoul was taking quite a while. I wondered if perhaps I
should go to see if he needed help carrying something - but then again it might ruin whatever surprise he had meant. And how much
trouble could he possibly get into in an art store? Idle with little to do I pulled out my phone and flipped through emails and social
media. Although I wasn’t one big on posting too much on such sites as it would attract attention to myself, I had in recent months found

Itori and admired her photos she took. I flipped through news articles, flicking past the deaths and disappearances as I pretended I didn’t
see them.
As I flipped past dead faces I was appreciative that Uta didn’t seem to keep the heads of his victims. Or at least, he did not keep them in
the fridge. If he was eating them beforehand....well. I wasn’t going to ask or question him. Though; ss of yet no further beheadings had
been reported so I supposed that gave me my answer regardless.
I jumped when a pair of black shoes came into my view standing over me. Looking up I saw Uta looking down at me, eyes curiously fixed
down at my phone. On the screen was another report - unread as I had been mulling along in dark thoughts. “Uta, you startled me. What
are---”
I looked at what was in his hands and paused. The huge 24 by 36 inch canvases threw me off because they were not mask supplies as I
expected. “Planning on making some big paintings?”
“They’re for you.”

“...me?” I blinked, looking at the couple things in his hands. Fresh paint, brushes, canvas. “Did you get oil or acrylic?” I asked softly,
reaching for a bag to see what he’d picked up.
“Acrylic. Is that okay?”
“Mhum. I can use either really. You picked these all up for me?”

“How was the brownie?”

“Good.---wait. Don’t distract me! Did you get what you needed? I thought you said ....” He wiggled the bag as though it answered the
question, a tiny ghost of a smile on his lips.
“The shop near us doesn't have a large canvas. Just small sketch pads.” So he had come here specifically to pick up these for me.
“I suppose I could...try to paint again. After making that one for you I haven't touched paint again. But it was pretty nice to get back at it.
And I’ve drawn a couple things in that sketchbook you got me...there’s a couple that might be nice to put onto actual canvas...”
I wondered if Yoshimura might like something colorful that matched the coffee shop. Maybe something for the upper room. There was a
blank wall near the bookshelf and a beautiful purple wisteria painting might be just what it needed---
I found myself grinning as I looked over the supplies and then ghoul. “Thank you, Uta! I think I’ve got a few ideas already!”

## ♥

On the way home we didn’t speak much. Not for lack of interest, but Uta let me think. Thinking of my future projects I gazed at the
blank canvas in front of me and imagined the purple with the light golds and whites illuminating the background. Perhaps against red?
Another painting might be spider lilies. A purple sunset in the background? With each painting bursting with color in my mind I silently
sat fixated on the blank white canvases. A matching set that could go on walls facing each other, or beside one another---
“Ai-chan?” I looked up, pulled from a daze. The ghoul next to me seemed happy. Or perhaps simply pleased with himself was a better
descriptor.

“Hum?” I hummed a soft question after he called my name. The images that had danced in my mind faded slightly but by no means
escaped me.
“Did you still want to go to the bar tonight?” He asked, and nodded at the canvases. “Or...no?”
“Yeah! Of course I do. I can work on those later.”
“Are you sure?”
“Of course I am! I’ve gotta set up a girls night with Itori anyway, as promised!” The ghoul pouted childishly.
“...without me?” At this, I couldn’t help but to snicker at him. Nudging him with my elbow I grinned.
“Sorry Uta-kun! Gals only!~ I think I’ve got verifiable proof you don’t apply.”
“You said Nico could attend.”
“Yeah, wellllll...It’s not so strange gossipping about guys in front of him. Plus, I told Itori that he needs to pick out some clothing for me
some time. I’m sure he’d pick out something with more color. Which I probably could use more of to be perfectly honest.” He still
pursed his lips together into a little pout, but didn’t argue anymore. I giggled softly and nudged him again, whispering. “I’ll make sure to
spend the entire day with you after. Hum-kay? Whatever you want to do?”
His red iris turned towards me and slowly he grinned, flashing a row of teeth. Maybe ‘anything you want’ might have been too much to
say; but he couldn’t pick anything too bad. Right. Right?
“I warned you before about making promises like that. What If I want you in my bed all day?” I tried to hide my flushed cheeks and avoid
prying glances from strangers. Softly, so nobody could overhear I whispered back.
“I guess that’s where I’ll stay then, isn’t it? So long as you don’t pout about not being one of the ‘gals’.”
As though hitting a switch, the ghoul sat up straighter and his small pout turned into a tiny smile. “Yes.”
I rolled my eyes and laughed into one of my palms to stifle the sound. This ghoul. One moment he sat there with a petulant, sulking
expression - the next he looked so pleased with himself. Sometimes I really had to wonder if he was truly a grown-up!
“Right then. Our stop is here.” I picked up a bag of paints while Uta held the large canvases under an arm. “I’m getting something to eat
before we go to visit. Although....” I muttered, more to myself than to my companion as we walked. “I should probably go to the grocery
store again soon. I’m almost out of things to make...Maybe some miso soup? Or soba noodles?”
“We can stop on the way someplace if you want.”
“Um. Yeah that sounds good.” I smiled for half a moment. I liked the idea. However, remembering who I was with made my grin fade.
With Uta being a ghoul I decided against it and shook my head. “---But...nevermind. It’s fine. We don’t need to.”

## “...”

“...?” I glanced towards the silent ghoul when I felt his gaze on me. Again, behind his sunglasses I couldn’t see his eyes.
“Hum? What is it?” He seemed to be mulling something over before speaking softly.
“You don’t eat out at restaurants much. Do you not like them?”

“Ah. Well...It’s not that I don’t like restaurants. I used to but---” I stopped and shrugged my shoulders. “I don’t want to drag you into
that situation. It kind of looks odd if you’re with me and not eating. It’s just easier to eat at home or make my own food. Anyway,
restaurant food isn’t always the most healthy thing around. I suppose it depends where I went but---”
“Because of me?”
“Um. Well...” Yes. Technically. But I didn’t feel any sort of resentment for that. Would it have been nice to be able to have a proper
dinner date type thing with my boyfriend; certainly. That sort of thing - sitting at a restaurant and chatting over a meal wasn’t possible for
us. “Last time we went somewhere to eat you A) Actually ate a muffin. And then B) Tried to eat my cake.” I held up my fingers as I
spoke.
“Yes. To seem ‘normal’....and to tease you.” I deadpanned at the small grin on his face.
“You’d get sick, Uta.”
“I’d be fine.”
“I remember the muffin? You hurled in an alleyway.”
“And I survived.”
“Isn’t it gross?”
“Very.”

“...you’re not going to let this go, are you?”
“No. So where do you want to go?”
I pursed my lips together and frowned in frustration. He really was insisting so stubbornly! All at his own detriment. “...Fine. You win.
Though I can’t imagine how this is winning for you... If you want me to pick a place then...Sushi.”
The ghoul’s head tilted curiously and I saw the red iris of his eye turn to watch me as we walked. “...Sushi. Raw fish? Humans eat some
strange things.”

“Yes. Sushi. Raw fish. Rice. That sort of thing.”

“Okay.”

“...” I watched him as he faced forward as we walked. “Just...okay?”
“...you do know I’m not---” I stalled out, not knowing how to speak what's on my mind. Uta waited patiently as I stumbled for words.
We even got all the way back to the shop and inside before I thought I had it just right. “Uta. You know that I’m not pushing you to do
Human things? Right? We don’t need to go out for food like other couples...it’s not that important. It’s like...I can’t do Ghoul things. I---
## ”
I waved a hand idly in the air and sighed. “---I have no idea what a Ghoul ‘dinner-date’ equivalent would be but---you get the idea. I don’t
expect you to do the whole Human act if we could just avoid something trivial like a restaurant.”
Uta took the bag of paint tubes from my hand and moved across his shop. Gently he leaned the large canvas against the side of his desk.
Seating himself in his rolling chair Uta moved to a drawer and started to empty it of his supplies, moving them over and sorting them
neatly away to leave room for the new paints. “...I want to, Ai-chan. It’s not trivial. It’s important to me.”
At a complete loss now I could only watch as he placed the colors of paint tubes in order in the drawer. My drawer if I was understanding
what he was doing; piercing out space in his space ---for me. I truly didn’t understand. Coming from a Ghoul who did much less to blend
in with humans than others. From his constant Kakugan to the carefree way he existed day to day. He hadn’t bothered to make his home

look Human. Or hide his mask shop that should scream to the world ghouls come here often. It didn’t make sense that this would matter
so much to him.
“I...don’t understand. At all. Am I maybe missing something?”
“You asked about a Ghoul ‘dinner-date’?” The man paused, looking up from the desk to think. He pulled off his sunglasses and perched
them atop his head. The red of his iris darted over to where I stood and surveyed my expression as he spoke up. “...Bringing you hunting
with me. Maybe bringing home food and eating together would be the closest thing to a ‘dinner date’.”
It took a massive amount of willpower not to make a horrified face at the suggestion. In a small voice I managed to reply. “I’d...rather not
do that...”

The ghoul wasn’t surprised, in a light and playful voice he replied softly. “Hmmm. I know. So...sushi. Instead of people.”

## ♥

So sushi it was. An hour later we were in a restaurant, seated at a table and ordering sushi for two which was...odd. While I’d picked
Sashimi, Uta had ordered Maki-zushi. It seemed like a good choice all things considered. The shape and size of them made them fairly easy
to swallow whole so this at the very least wouldn’t force him to chew or taste them too much.
I dipped my food into a bit of soy sauce and dropped it into my mouth, chewing it slowly as I observed Uta pick up a roll, place it in his
mouth and chew. I froze up for a moment as I watched him. I realized only belataly that he wasn’t actually chewing; only pretending to
before swallowing it down. He hummed softly as though it did taste good and picked up another piece to place it in his mouth.
This very normal situation felt...foreign somehow. There was something wrong about it.
I’d grown so accustomed to Uta eating bloody human meat that seeing him eat anything else was kind of disturbing for a reason I
couldn’t quite put my finger on. As I chewed on my own food I was perplexed with this peculiar puzzle.
“Ai-chan, how’s your food?”
“Oh...it’s fine.” The words felt lame and flat as they fell from my mouth. The small smile I did manage was about as pleasant as chewing
sandpaper. Only midway through the meal, and when I heard from across the table Uta’s stomach start to protest did it really click why it
was so upsetting. This sort of thing was kind of masochistic and self-destructive for him.
And for what?
While I understood why Touka ate her friends home cooked meals, Uta didn’t have to keep up the same appearances. Nor was he the
type of Ghoul to do things to fit in. There had to be a reason behind it - I just couldn’t see it.
I popped another bite of my meal into my mouth and chewed it. Though the enjoying part of the meal had fled as I watched him pop
another into his mouth, forgo pretending to chew and simply swallow it. The next time he lifted a roll towards his mouth I’d had enough
of watching him toil away at eating. I reached across with a pair of chopsticks and grabbed it from between his utensils; yanking it away
from him before it made it to his mouth. “Ai-chan! Hey!”
Stuffing it into my mouth, I chewed and swallowed it. I stuck my tongue out and clicked the chopsticks together while narrowing my
eyes at him as a silent ‘threat’. When I tried again, he yanked it out of reach and dropped it into his mouth to swallow it quickly.
Slowly a grin spread across his face as he picked up another roll. “If you wanted it you should have asked! You can’t just take food from
someone you know.” I laughed softly as we transformed the grueling task of eating human food to a childish game of ‘keep away’. The
remainder of his sushi rolls were ‘fought’ over while the rest of the patrons shot us annoyed and irritated looks as our antics got louder
and more rambunctious.
“Excuse me. Could you two please...calm down? I’ll have to ask you both to leave otherwise.”

I froze standing halfway up and reaching over the table to grab another roll from Uta. Stalled in place I glanced up at the hostess with
wide eyes. My face flushed with heat as embarrassment settled in.
“Ah! Y-yeah! I am so sorry!” Sitting back down quickly I watched the ghoul flick the last piece of his ‘meal’ into his mouth and swallow.
The hostess frowned more severely when the ghoul reached across the table to snag my food and I reactionarily stabbed the chopsticks
into the table where his hand had been a moment before he tugged it back.
“Please....” The hostess hissed, now thoroughly done with our behavior and mere moments from booting us out of the establishment.
“...yes! Sorry! Uta. Stop!!! Shhh!” I hissed across the table, but it turned into a snicker as I shoved the last of my food into my mouth
before he could get it and swallowed.
“I will go get your check. Have a good night...” I lowered my head as the woman still sounded annoyed.
After exiting the building I started to giggle aloud. “She...was so angry...we probably shouldn’t go back there again.” Yet...I couldn’t bring
myself to be annoyed at it. The ghoul next to me shared a similar grin, though it turned slightly when his face went a little green. A hand
went to his stomach and his smile turned to a grimace.
“Hey...you feeling alright? Do you want to go home instead?”
“No. I’m fine. But I should have let you win more.”
“Pfft. Let me win? I totally got those from you fair and square!”
He grinned again, and wrapped an arm around my shoulders. Leaning close he whispered softly: “You really think you could take food
from a ghoul if they didn’t want you to have it?”
“...Almost got you with the chopsticks.” I retorted, raising an eyebrow.
“...I didn’t expect you to try to stab me with them.”

“Well you were going after my food, Uta. I ordered that because I like it.”
We both laughed as we walked down the street in a moment of blissful normality. On the train people were pushed in close together for
their end of day commute and so I stood in front of Uta with my back pressed into him while he kept us steady on our feet. The ghoul
doubled as protection from unwanted strangers from trying to get too close or gods forbid touch. We made it all the way to Helter Skelter
before the ghoul once again held his stomach and stopped walking to take a breath. “Uta! Hey...come on. There’s a bathroom inside.
You’re gonna have to throw that shit up. Please...you’re going to get sick if you keep it down much longer...”

No longer arguing, the ghoul, green in the face and looking exhausted walked into the bar and headed straight for the bathroom. I winced
as I spotted who was also at the bar. Renji, Itori and Nico were all welcome sights. But seeing Roma hadn’t been expected or welcome.
“Ah, Hey guys.”
“Heya----!!! What’s wrong with U-kun?” Itori leaned over the counter to watch as Uta’s back disappeared as he closed the door to the
bathroom behind himself. Sighing softly, I muttered.
“He insisted we went to a restaurant and he ate some human food.”

“You made him eat human food?” Roma’s accusation struck a nerve and I turned to glare at her. Did she really think I was stupid? Of
course I wouldn’t have forced him to eat human food!


“No. That’s not what---”
“Geez. You really are stupid. If we could eat human food don’t you think we would?” I clamped my mouth shut and ground my teeth
together as she cut me off to geer at me. Reluctantly I silently took the only open seat. Unfortunately, it lay directly next to her. I, along
with the others in the bar winced at the sound of the ghoul retching in the bathroom. Turning my head I watched the door to the
restroom anxiously. I debated getting up and going to...help? Hold his hair maybe. Would that be strange? It didn’t last long and the
ghoul emerged looking a little better.
“Feeling better?” I hopped off the chair, letting him sit. Unable to get far he circled my waist with an arm and pulled me back to sit on his
lap with his chin resting on my shoulder.
“Mmm. Much better.”
“You should probably get something to eat.” I murmured, frowning. “Actual food this time.” I wanted to call his actions before a stupid
stunt. But he had said it was important to him so I didn’t want to mock him for it. In the end It had been fun - at least after I’d pushed
him to play a game rather than sit there suffering and gulping it fast enough he wouldn’t be able to taste it.
Roma continued to glare regardless. In front of her there was a dish of bloody strips of meat. In fact I only now noticed that there was
also a plate in front of Nico and Itori as well. Dinner presumably. However, while Itori and Nico had paused their meal to forgo eating in
front of me - Roma gleefully stuffed a piece into her mouth and chewed loudly as though this would finally be the thing to upset me.
“U-kun. I’ve got some more in the back. I’ll fetch you a plate if you’d like.”
“Mmm. Thanks Itori.”
The red head stood and left us to fetch Uta his own meal. When Roma saw that her loud, chewing and sloppy noises didn’t seem to phase
me and I’d failed to give the reaction she wanted; she held out a strip of bleeding meat towards me and wiggled it
“Want some?” This again, was something Uta did. Regularly. So I simply shook my head and leaned back into Uta a bit more.
“No thanks I---” Her face contorted; a scowl that was trying to be a feral sort of smile.
“Come on. Uta can eat your food! Get sick of your food! We blend into human places! But now you’re here with us ghouls! And you’re
not even willing to take a single bite? What sort of hypocrisy is that? How pathetic are you?” The small ghoul shoved the bit of human
meat into her mouth and ground her teeth down on it angrily as she sneered.
“Come now Roma, dear. You know it’s not the same thing.” Nico came to my rescue. “Leave the poor dear alone, alright? I’m surprised
enough that she’s sitting here with us...give her some credit.”
I winced, leaning further back into Uta’s embrace with a heavy heart. While Nico had meant well by it, even the comment meant to
defend me was like a backhanded blow. He was surprised I was willing to sit here with them. It was surprising I could stomach being near
them.
All my efforts I’d made to relax, accept and love my friends and Uta ---and it was still surprising?
The arm around my waist tensed briefly and I turned my head around to see Uta looking at me. The expression seemed to read as
inquisitive, questioning silently: ‘Are you okay?’
I managed a weak smile and nodded and the ghoul relaxed, going back to eat his meal at the counter.
A loud pop made me jump before realizing it was just the sound of a cork being pulled from a bottle.
“Okay! Okay! That’s enough of that! How about a round of drinks for everybody!” Itori stood up, holding a bottle of blood wine in her
hands. She began pouring everybody, excluding myself, a glass. The conversations including me, meat and my humanity stopped there.

For me, she moved to make up a colorful, sweet drink and slid it over with a smile.
“Tell me how that one tastes! I’ve been trying to mix up something new! Maybe it’ll be yummy enough for you to spill some gossip!” The
woman winked and grinned coyly causing a flush to cross my face.
“Course I will try it.” I eyed the drink, and then the ghoul before picking up the drink and took a sip. Instantly my face screwed up and I
swallowed painfully before coughing. “Ah? I...take that as a no?”
“To---much---lemon. So sour!” I coughed to try to clear the feeling of every part of my mouth shriveling up in protest.
“Here here! Sorry! Sorry!” Regardless of her apologies the red-headed ghoul was laughing. She poured out a cup of water for me which I
downed quickly.
“Sour huh? What should I add?”
“Maybe...Do you have any strawberry liqueur?” The ghoul turned and ran her fingers over her bottles, clicking her nails over the glasses
until she found one. Pulling a pink bottle off the shelf she uncapped it and poured in a bit of the liquid until the yellow drink turned into
a swirling mix of pastel pinks and yellows.
“There. Any better?”
I took another sip of it, and although it certainly was still sour it was a big improvement. More importantly, it was drinkable without
scrunching up my face.
“It’s much better now. As long as you have more strawberry flavoring and less lemon for the next person you should be fine.” I cupped
the glass between my hands and brought it back up to my mouth again; sipping down alcohol and hoping that it might ease some stress
off my back for a little while.
Albeit Itori’s offering of alcohol to all parties had calmed the group, I still felt tension in the air. The small ghoul woman still stared at me
with hostility in her eyes and turned up her nose when I tried to look at her. As a result, I stayed quiet and didn’t speak much at all unless
Itori or Nico drew me into a conversation - which more often than not included telling stories about ‘old days’ in the fourth ward and
some ghoul history that I didn't know much of.
Roma left first. Her nose still upturned and her attitude still like a petulant child she called back as she left: “Tell that stupid old man that
I quit! It’s boring there without Kaneki. I thought it would be more fun!”
“Oh...okay...” I murmured, the small woman already long gone. As bad as I did feel for hating Uta’s friend; that was a relief.
Soon after Itori leaned across the bar with a grin and whispered. “Sooo? How are you and Uta doing, hum? Getting closer?!~” I blinked,
my face already flush from alcohol went even redder for the implication.
“I---well---that is...uh...!!!!”
The woman simply laughed, tipping her head back and covering her mouth as mirth bubbled forth. When she stopped her eyes were on
the goth who’s hold around my waist was tightening and loosening almost anxiously: “Well that’s a relief. U-kun can finally stop asking
for advice---”
I turned my head around and was able to see that the ghoul was avoiding his friends' gazes and either staring very hard at a piece of art on
the wall or sticking his nose down into his glass of blood-wine. “---you should probably know though that the smell is all over you,
dear!~”
“...it’s a good thing you don’t want kids....” Itori said wistfully, her eyes looked sad and far away for a moment before returning. “I’m
happy though. Uta could use somebody to settle him down and ground him a bit.” This part she said, quietly and the ghoul holding me
seemed to pretend he hadn’t heard a word or really wasn’t paying attention as Renji stood up and came nearer.

“Speaking of Humans and Ghouls!!!! Ren-kun! You need to spill and tell us about this Human woman we’ve smelled all over you for a
while! You know we could just track her down and take a look----”
“Don’t...do that.”
I blinked, surprised as the silver haired ghoul snapped at his friends. Itori’s own eyes went wide quickly before she settled on staring at
him with cautious curiosity. “Okay Ren...but you know she might be safer if you introduced us, or at least told us about her a bit. At least
then we could avoid her.”
The silver haired ghoul grunted and looked away from the group; still unwilling to share his Human friend with them all. I think I could
understand why he might want to keep her secret:
“Renji-kun...she doesn't know that you’re a Ghoul. Does she?”

The ghoul’s guilty expression and the way his eyes turned away and his fist clenched tight on the counter top from me seemed to prove
my statement correct. The others seemed to take that information all fairly well. Nico sighed softly and shook his head, and Itori glanced
down to her own wine glass - swishing it around. “...well its rather risky to tell her. If she runs off to the CCG then he’s doomed. So if she
reacts badly she’d have to die...”
The conversation stalled out there and the room went ominously quiet until Itori spoke up again a while later:
“U-kun! I know I’m not one to normally cut you off, but you have to get Ai-chan back home safe and sound, don’t you? And she’s pretty
drunk now too!”
“I’ll get them home...” Renji stood up and I turned my head around to look up at him with an open mouth. Now even after his outburst
about his ‘kitten’ he stood by, coat thrown over his shoulder and ready to escort us both home. Carefully the goth ghoul nudged me off
his lap and I swayed on my feet. Now of course it hit me again how much I’d drunk - it never did when I stayed sitting.
“Itori...how much do I owe you?”
“Don’t worry about it hun, I’ll make you up a tab you can pay the next time you visit! So come back soon!” The female ghoul leaned
across the counter and whispered. “Bring him back more often for me okay?”
“Yeah. I will!”
## ♥

Girls night was set up for the following night. Soon after leaving the bar with Renji and Uta I got a message from Itori asking if I was free
to go out that soon. From the back seat of Renji’s commandeered vehicle I hastily replied; eager for the distraction. Girls night would at
the very least not include Roma - That I made sure of with Itori. The red head assured me it was only going to be myself, herself and
## Nico.
“Girls night tomorrow. Itori and Nico will pick me up from home. Alright Uta-kun?”
“Hum? Yeah.”
I peered at him, narrowing my eyes slightly and scrutinizing him. I did wonder if he was going to try to stalk around hidden as he had
when following me to the station in the mornings to go to work. But then again with both Itori and Nico watching my back I was
confident that I’d be safe and that he trusted them. “I know you seemed bummed we’re not including you, are you okay with me going
with them?”

The ghoul, drunk off fermented blood sighed softly and slouched down in his seat. His eyes, tired and half-lidded as though he might fall
asleep in the back seat stared through me.
“Um-hmmm...they’ll keep you safe and bring you back.” Then, as though it was an afterthought or something that just slipped out, he
added: “They’re a lot of fun...just be careful.”
I was about to ask what he meant, but the ghoul’s eyes slipped closed and a moment later a soft snore sounded the start to his sleep. Renji
peered into the rear-view mirror and raised an eyebrow. “He’s asleep?”
“Hum. Seems like it.”
“Need help getting him inside?”
“I might need help. He’s a lot heavier than he looks.” I smiled faintly remembering how the ghoul would once in a while walk into a room
and lean his weight on me and hold on briefly before moving on to do his regular routine. The driver cleared his throat and avoided my
gaze in the mirror and my face went red once more. “What---I hadn’t meant---not like that!”
“Whatever.”
“Anyway...what you said back at the bar. You’re Kitten doesn't know?”
He glanced over his shoulder at Uta and frowned. Shaking his head he decided to reply with silence. “...the others are right. If she doesn't
react well then----” The car stopped around the corner to Hysy ArtMask Studio. He glanced again into the mirror and held my gaze for a
moment. “...if you hadn’t reacted well to Uta...if you’d been too afraid or he thought you might run to the CCG then...”
“He’d have killed me back then. I know.” I spoke softly hoping the sleeping ghoul wouldn’t hear it; be he awake or truely asleep. “And
life would have gone on. But the longer you keep it from her the worse it’s going to be...anyway. I’d say you have a little bit of an
advantage.”
“How so?”
“Scavenger lifestyle? I know it’s not much. And it’s a bit morbid but, to me at least it seems like it’s a bit more of an innocent way to live. I
think that’s an easier pill to swallow.”
“...how are you handling his lifestyle? It’s far from innocent.”
“When he hunts...I make myself scarce. I don’t watch the news for missing people or murders. It is getting easier and easier to just
disregard what he’s eating.” Who those people might have been. “Easier to turn a blind eye to that aspect of our lives.”
I peered down at the sleeping ghoul, his mouth had dropped open a bit and if left for long he’d no doubt start to drool. My mouth curled
into a smile as I watched him; reminded of the sketches the man had made of me while I’d been unconscious on his studio floor trying to
rest. Gently, I reached out and brushed hair away from his face and watched his expression twitch and relax as I grazed my thumb along
his jawline.
“...I’m relieved...”
The silver haired ghoul didn’t elaborate before he got out of the car. A few moments later he had pulled Uta from the car and supported a
half-sleeping ghoul on his shoulder as they stumbled to the doorway. I got out and rushed (half-stumbling myself) to the door and
unlocked it.
Renji managed to move Uta up the stairs and looked around, first moving to put the unconscious goth on the couch. I caught up and
slung an arm around Uta and smiled.

“I can get him to bed from here.” Hefting more of the weight onto my shoulders I half dragged half carried him to the room with Uta’s
feet barely cooperating. Next to the bed I finally let his weight go, pushing him onto the bed fully clothed (sans his shoes, which had been
left at the door).
I smiled as the ghoul turned to lay on his side, snuggling into the covers and nuzzling into the familiar shared scent of the bedding. I
quietly exited the room and saw that Renji was on his way back out. “Thank you Renji, again.”
“It seems like you’ll be good with him. Goodnight Ai-chan.”
“Well, unless you’re going to offer to brush his teeth while he’s unconscious...no. I’m good. I think he’ll survive with a blood-breath in
the morning. Which, now that I say it sounds nasty.” With a fond smile I added: “I really don’t want to wake him though. Get home safe
Renji...maybe check up on your friend, hum?”
The ghoul nodded his head once in acknowledgment and left. After he was gone I double checked the shop front door to lock it and then
made my way back up the stairway. My eyes went to Bjorn who stood by the fridge, wide eyes begging for dinner.

When I climbed into bed nearly thirty minutes later the ghoul was still sound asleep in exactly the same place as when I’d left him. His
back faced my place on the bed and I took the chance to snuggle close and throw an arm and leg over him. At least this way in the
morning the blood-breath wouldn’t be my problem.





46: Girls Night Out/ The Trouble with Being Human
## Notes:
Two chapters kinda put into one. The girls night out part was cut short, and the next part was just really really
long. So you get a very long chapter today!
Parts of this I already had written.

Might do some editing on spelling and grammar later if I screwed up. Only read over it once or twice, didn't do
much proof reading!
Chapt er   Text
Chapter 46:  Girls Night, and the trouble with being human.


“Are you ready to go!?”

I grinned and gave Itori a thumbs up as I walked down the steps from our shared apartment; careful not to trip on the heels she had
insisted I got dressed up in. I stopped just a moment to lean close and gently kiss the goth ghoul on the cheek. Giggling at the wide-eyed
look he gave, I darted off without giving him any chance to ‘retaliate’.

“I’ll be back, Uta-kun!” I watched over my shoulder for a moment before breezing past Itori and Nico. They would keep me safe. Uta
knew that, but he had been tense most of the morning. “I don’t know how long you two plan to keep me, but I should probably warn
you not to keep me out too late. Otherwise he’s gonna start stalking.”

Itori smiled coyly and lifted a hand to her mouth as she giggled. “Oh, don’t worry! We’ll have you back by dark. Do you ha—” I
interrupted her, patting the bag at my side.
“Mask. Knife.” Along with my phone, wallet and a really loud whistle. Just in case. Everything was just in case.

“Right, and how is your leg?”

“Getting better everyday!” I reassured her as she glanced downwards; noting the slight limp. “Don’t worry about it. I barely notice it.”

“I didn’t realize you’d still be hurt, maybe the heels weren’t the best idea...” I laughed softly, already knowing that. She probably wasn’t
used to friends being ‘hurt’ for so long. Not when ghouls healed so quickly.
“Itori, seriously! I. Am. Fine.” I said kindly but firmly. “Stop fretting, you’re gonna be a buzzkill!”

I watched her face as she took in what I meant and laughed. “Right, girls night!”

“---and Nico!~” I added, glancing at the man with a smile. “I hope you remembered you were going to pick out something for me to
wear! I could use some more color in my wardrobe.”

“Of course my dear! Your palette is rather dull.”

“Well I am sorrrrrrrrry that my attire hasn’t been my primary concern! I can dress myself though!” The man in turn scoffed a bit.
“Well, I’d argue that you clearly can’t. Needless to say. I can’t let you keep going out in things as drab as this.” His fingers gently plucked
at my shirt while he remained grinning. All in good fun.

“What’s wrong with this?” I mocked a defensive tone, looking down at my outfit. I was wearing nice clothing. Heels. I’d put on a skirt for
this too! Sure it might be black, but it was a skirt! And the shirt was an off white cream color. I hummed softly and pouted; In retrospect,
perhaps it was still a bit ‘black and white’ themed. “Fine, fine. So maybe I’m a bit colorblind. I’m just not as confident as you are; what
can I say!”

“You can say ‘yes’ and ‘thank you’ when I pick out some cloths for you, darling!~”


I laughed, happily as he winked. “Alright, alright. Yes. And Thank you Nico!”

So it was that I was being dragged around to every clothing shop the two Ghouls could find. Itori was finding some dramatic dresses that
I couldn’t even think of a place to wear; while to my surprise Nico was taking things a bit easier on me. He was holding a small number of
bags, filled with things they insisted I get. He had taken it upon himself to ease me into some brighter colors with just splashes here or
there rather than going for a full palette change.

“What about this, dear? You can wear it with all that dark clothing you’ve got.” He was holding a red crop top blazer-like top. The edging
was black but it was colorful. At least compared to the rest of my clothing.
“We could find you some pants to match...” He hummed softly and searched the racks, leaving me holding the jacket. “Here...”

To my surprise he found some jeans. Electric yellow, lined with black with ripped knees and patches. Something entirely within my style.
“I....actually love it, Nico!”

“Here—try it with this shirt!” Itori butt in suddenly; holding up a skin tight looking shirt with a deep cut v-neck.
“Alright, alright! How about I try on the whole outfit, and you can tell me if it’s a yes or no!”

I took the jeans, the jacket and the shirt with me to a fitting room; dressed quickly and looked in the mirror. Although the amount the
shirt dove between my breasts showing off my sternum was a bit much; It looked good. That much I couldn’t deny. It still fit my aesthetic
without being quite so bland.

“Okay, fair enough. The colors actually go together. I never would have guessed—” I took a step outside of the fitting room and glanced
up with a smile, only to step backwards just as quickly into the room.

“Aika?! Hey—wait, it looks good!” Itori spoke, mistaking my dodging back for reluctance.

“Shhh...” I hissed between my teeth. I stripped out of the clothing quickly and re-dressed before exiting; the items held close to my chest
as I ducked behind clothing racks. My eyes followed someone in that store; a gentleman wearing a suit with a small golden castle emblem
on his lapels. I ducked as his eyes surveyed the store again. As I ducked down, I watched and followed the man's shoes as he walked closer.
Slipping in between the racks like a child hiding from their parent, I was hidden in clothing while he walked around and questioned some
patrols.

“Pardon me, did you see this woman come into the store?”

I felt my pulse up in my throat as Nico and Itori had to answer; lying for me as they were questioned. Odd. Normally it would be the
other way around, wouldn’t it? A suited man going after one of them while I lied through my teeth about their whereabouts.

A few minutes later I saw Nico’s face peek over the clothing racks at me. I could see the concern in his eyes as he spoke up. “He’s gone
dear, I must say that was nerve wracking~”

“...Not everyday you’re not the one they’re after. Right?” I muttered as I crawled my way out of the rack of clothing.
“Uta mentioned something about some big corporate types pestering you. I hadn’t realized it was that big.” Itori said, the fun gone from
her voice. She seemed serious as she watched where the man had disappeared out the front of the store.

“Sorry—I suppose I ended up being the buzzkill. Thank you for helping me find things.” I moved so I could look out the window of the
store front; eyeing the clean swept streets of the first ward. “I should have known going shopping in this area would be a bad idea...they’re
life fucking flies.”

“So, how exactly are you related to those guys...? They had a picture of you that seemed a little—dated?”


“...Kogane no Shiro Company.” I muttered, grimacing with a sigh. I motioned at myself and rolled my eyes. Uta really hadn’t told her?
“Aika Kaneshiro...disowned heir. Black sheep daughter. I ran away over four years ago now. But lately they’ve been annoying. More than
usual.” I grit my teeth, tense as I watched out for more suited goons.

“Seriously? That Kaneshiro!” I turned and shushed her, putting a finger to my lips when she raised her voice a bit too loudly.
“...uuugh.” I groaned in disgust.
“Yes. That one. Maybe I should change my last name legally somehow—we can go to another ward. If you want to keep shopping. I
think I’ve got plenty of color.” I tried to change the subject, glancing up at Nico with a faint smile. “For now at least! We can find another
time to go out again! Promise!”

“---You two should probably head home without me though.” I could see Itori’s mouth open before I cut her off; my tone turned
serious.
“The last thing you want is a multi-billion dollar corporation looking into you. The less of my friends they’ve got eyes on, the better. I’ll
go to the station and go right back to the fourth ward....They wouldn’t follow me there.” I smirked a bit, amused. “Posh, hoity-toity
bodyguards are afraid of that place.”

“U-kun won’t like that, Aika-chan...”

“...I’ll message him. I’m sure he won’t mind meeting me at the station. And I’ll have to tell him about them stalking me around again—
which means I’ll have to convince him not to eat some corporate jerks...” I pulled out my phone and already was shooting him a brief
message debriefing him on what was happening. And requesting an ‘escort’.

“Please...I don’t want them harassing anybody else. Trust me...they’re persistent. If you think a government agency is bad... A
cooperation with that much sway would be so much worse.”

My phone chimed and I looked down at the message:

Uta: On my way.

“There...see. Uta’s on his way to the station.” I smiled and turned my phone around for her to see, her own phone chiming a few times.
The redhead frowned as she read over the message but nodded.
“Alright Ai-chan...stay safe. I won’t hear the end of it if you don’t get back in one piece."

“‘Course! Don’t let them see you either if you can help it.” I turned and went to the front of the store, checked out the items and put
them in a bag I already had. I glanced behind me but saw that my friends had already made themselves scarce.

## ♥


Approximately One Month Later. Early February, evening after work at the ghoul cafe; Anteiku.

I took a step out of the subway and looked around. Spotting the usual head of charcoal hair I made a beeline for the ghoul who sat on a
bench waiting. Uta had in the last month taken up the offer to make sure I got home safe every day. Or, at the very least he picked me up
from the station in the fourth ward to walk me home. Although at the start I had apologized for the need of extra precautions Uta had
over that time not complained once - not accepted any apology.



I suppose to his mind there wasn’t anything to apologize for.
I leaned over the bench and looked down his notebook before he had a chance to notice I was there. “Boo!~” I gently clapped my hands
over his shoulders and laughed. He didn’t jump - but he did turn and smile faintly.
“Late today?”

“Ah, yeah. Sorry. I sent a text but the service was a bit spotty today. Kimi wanted to show me the bangles she bought so I stayed a few
minutes to see them. So... I missed the first train. She bought a matching pair of these leather bracelets for her and Nishiki.” I giggled and
shook my head. “I really can’t imagine him wearing it though. I hope he doesn't say anything stupid about them. She seemed so happy.
Sorry I’m late. Can I make up for it somehow?”

“...Will you go out for a date with me tonight?”

“...?” I blinked, surprised by the proposition. Honestly, ever since we’d been ‘official boyfriend x girlfriend’ everybody knew we hadn’t
gone on another date-date . Unless of course I could count that disaster with the sushi.
“Sure!!!” Then quickly I added: “Wait! Wait! Wait! Not a restaurant though! You’ve got to pick something fun!”

“No food...” Uta closed his sketchbook and stood up. “...how about some more sightseeing? It’s been a little warmer...”

“The snow did all melt away this week...”

“Do you like dancing, Ai-chan?”

I opened and closed my mouth as a blush crossed my face. “Well...I generally have two left feet. Or at least that’s what my tutors told
me...What kind of dancing?”

“Nothing formal. Just a club. Itori and Nico recommended it once.”

“Yeah. Sure. A club sounds fine and then some sightseeing?”

He hummed softly, agreeing. “There’s also some shops in the area I was thinking of. So we can stop in if it is too cold for you.”

“Okay! Sounds perfect!” I beamed happily as I hopped around the bench and joined him at his side as we made our way back towards
home. Once we got through the front door I dashed up the stairway and met Bjorn who jumped and wiggled until I grasped his huge
head and rubbed behind his ears.
“Good boy! Will you be alright alone - Uta and I are going to have a bit of fun? Mkay?” Of course there wasn’t any reply from the canine
but I still smiled and rubbed his face until he was satisfied.

“Alright! I should pick out something nice to wear...What do you think?” I glanced to see that Uta hadn’t followed me up and Bjorn
didn’t have any input. “No input from the boys, huh?” That left me to pick something by myself. With a shrug I went to the bedroom
and pulled open a drawer with my clothing folded neatly. “Alright...let's try some things.”

## ♥


I walked down the stairs carefully. It wasn’t everyday that I picked out a nice outfit - but I also had to keep in mind warmth and comfort.
I walked down the stairway, careful not to twist my ankle in the shoes I’d picked out. That deep cut v-neck shirt Itori had picked out. A

pair of black jeans that were comfortable and warm, yet when paired with the nice shirt and a pair of high heeled boots looked nice
enough for a casual date. If I wore the red coat Nico had picked out before it would be perfect.

“Uta-kun...how’s this?”

The ghoul tipped his head back to look at me as I stood behind him. His eyes opened a bit wider in surprise and then he turned his seat
around to get a better look. “...cute.”

“You think this is alright then? I wondered about the boots...you said sight seeing so I wasn’t totally sure.”

“I’ll be carrying you for that.” The ghoul tipped his head to one side and studied me more closely. Under the scrutiny I looked away and
flushed light pink.
“What? Is something wrong?”

“No. Nothing’s wrong.”

The ghoul stood and stepped closer. As he did so he pulled the necklace from around his throat off and encircled it around my neck-
clasping it in place. He stepped back to take a look at it and finally commented. “There. It looked like you needed something. You can
borrow that for the night. But I’ll want it back later. It was a gift from a friend.”

Then, his hand reached for my earrings to touch the second set of Quinque steel studs. He had put them in just a few days after the ‘girls
night out.’

“These are all healed now.” I nodded and laughed softly.
“Well yeah. They have been for almost a week now. You can put in another set, maybe somewhere else if you’re up to it...”

Idly I pressed my hand over the arm where my tattoo still colorfully displayed on my skin. I was looking forward to summer when I could
really show it off! For now it stayed under a layer of warm clothing for the most part. As it happens I had plans to start running when it
really started to warm up at the end of spring. “So how about it? Want to put another hole in me?”

The ghoul’s face turned mischievous before he turned to his drawer full of piercing items. “Sure Ai-chan!~ But normally it’s at the end of
a date that I’d stick something in you.”

When my face turned tomato red and my mouth opened in shocked silence the ghoul burst with laughter, bending over to hold himself
up and wiping at his eyes with the back of his hand. “AH! HAHAHA! Ai-chan. You should see your face!”

“Idiot! D-don’t say things like that!”

“Why not, dear?” The ghoul laughed more softly and leaned forward to press his lips into my forehead. “It’s fun! ---Now. Which earring
do you like?” In his hands he held out a few choices. More round dot earrings, and a crescent moon, another set was a simple loop.

“Surprise me!~” I closed my eyes and waited with a smile on my lips.


I heard the ghoul suck in a breath and then chuckle. “Alright. A surprise then."

I listened as the ghoul moved around me, clicking metal, and the smell of alcohol and sanitizer. Hands clasp over my shoulders and pulled
me along until he urged me to sit. "Right there. Perfect!~"


"A little pinch and---" I tried not to whimper when he placed the needle through the flesh without a countdown. Biting my lip I whined.
"No fair Uta! A little warning next time?"

"Next time. You already want more?" I opened my eyes and stuck my tongue out at the ghoul. Unperturbed he leaned down so he was
level with me and softly said: “Eyes closed, Ai-chan. Other side now.” Obediently I shut my eyes and waited.

“Alright. Three. Two. One .” On one the ghoul pressed the needle through the other ear.
“ Ahhh! I take it back! No warning is better!”

“You can open your eyes now.” His voice trembled with laughter and I peeked open my eyes and wiped away a bit of moisture from my
eyes before it could form tears and slip out down my cheeks.
“Don’t laugh!” I said indignantly, prodding a finger into his chest. Carefully the ghoul touched the new earrings and took a sanitizer to
clean them one last time.
“But your reaction is funny. Take a look in the mirror. If you don’t like those ones, they can be changed out after they heal.”

Sliding off the seat I moved to see which ones he had put in. I turned my head so I could peer at one side closely. Above my first piercings
a pair of small cuffed hoops hung; pierced through the cartilage.
“Ooo! I like these!” I turned and turned my head first left and then right to show them off.
“What do you think?” It was a silly question; clearly he liked piercings. But it made me feel all the better to see his smile grow and have
him comment that they looked cool.

“Are you ready to go out then?"

"Yeah. Dressed and now accessorized, I think I’m ready!” Uta stood up, checked the front door and then waved as he hopped up each
stair to disappear into the apartment.
“I’ll be just a minute.”

“Right. Can you grab my coat on the way down? It’s the red one by the door.”

I smiled as the ghoul yelled back a ‘yeah’. I took a seat in his chair and looked down. I touched the necklace choker and took a moment to
study it up close. It looked like some beat up coin latched to a leather necklace/choker by a small ring. Further up along the necklace there
was a small shiny rhinestone of some kind.

The necklace was well worn, well loved and soft against my neck; comfortable. It seemed like something he had had for many many years.
Maybe even from back when he was a kid in charge of a ward of ghouls. All the things it must have been through with him; my fingers
smoothed over the face of the beat up coin and idly looked across the dim store.


I dropped my hand from the necklace and smiled when I heard the ghoul return down the stairs. He was wearing nice dress pants with a
thin chain leading from his belt loops to a wallet in his back pocket. Hard heeled dress shoes and a slim cut black button down that he left
partway unbuttoned completed the look.
“Fancy!” I commented, smiling genuinely over his outfit. “Only thing you left out was a fancy hat! Got some glasses?”

“Hm. Yeah.” He patted one of his shirt pockets before pulling them out and placing them on the bridge of his nose.

When I stepped out the front door I leaned back in and called out: “Bjorn, we’ll be back! Be good!”

## ♥


## Thirteenth Ward Rooftops: Approx 8:30pm

My voice screamed shrilly through the air as the ghoul leapt forward, bouncing me on his back as we launched through the air. His feet
landed safely back on the ground and my scream turned to laughter as I leaned closer and continued to hold on with a death grip.
Though he had started off with a slow paced; a gentle series of jumps across the building tops he had since picked up the pace and begun
to bounce us across the tops of Tokyo at a breakneck pace while I kept myself pressed tight to his back; hands buried into his clothing and
gripping his limbs to hold on.

He was chuckling when he finally came to a stop. At the pause I took the moment to pull gently at his cheeks!!!
“You think that’s funny? Are you trying to give me a heart attack!?” I could feel the ghoul smiling even as I gently pulled at his cheeks and
I let go to lean closer again. I buried my face into the back of his neck causing him to shiver when my nose pressed against his spine.
“Yeah! Cold, isn’t it!?” I murmured into his back, smirking into the flesh of his neck. “My nose and ears are frozen thanks to that lil’
shortcut of yours!!!”

Though, I wasn’t annoyed. Not truly. Sure - it was cold and was bordering on pain now. But I was only teasing, and based on the fact
that Uta still was chuckling as I poked at him it seemed he understood that perfectly fine. In truth I enjoyed all the running and jumping;
my heart was beating like a jackrabbit in my chest.  Excitement - rather than fear - set my pulse on edge.

“We’re here Ai-chan. The club is just over there.” Uta nodded his head forward, towards a brightly lit neon set of lights and groups of
people filing into the building. “We can warm up inside. Hold tight. We’re going down.”

I hugged tightly again, wrapping my arms and legs around him as tightly as I could as he stepped off the edge of the building to land
down on the back alleyway street. He leaned down and let me slide from his back and looked up and down the alleyway just to double
check nobody had seen either of us. When his mask came off and his sunglasses replaced them, so too did my own mask get pulled from
my face. I carefully put it away into my bag strapped over my shoulders; safe and accessible if need be.


I met his gaze and then followed his lead as he walked us out of the alleyway and across the street. I was surprised when the ghoul walked
us past the line waiting to get in - right up to the bouncer who gave the ghoul a scrutinizing look. Uta tipped his glasses down and stared
at the larger man for a moment. The larger man raised his eyebrows and then moved his judgment down upon my head. “She’s with me.”


“Ah so she’s for--”  Whatever he was going to say was sharply cut off by Uta’s slightly raised voice.
“ No.” An arm curled around my shoulders and pulled me closer.

“Alright. Go on in.” The man unhitched the velvet gate. As we passed he leaned forward and spoke to Uta once more.
“Friendly warning. Keep her close. There’s some clients looking at a lot of prospects tonight...” Uta nodded his head but didn't reply as we
walked into the club and the base and bright lights drowned out any thoughts I might have had on asking what on earth that had been
about.

I personally didn’t know where to look first. The bar? The stage? The dance floor?! It seemed like ages since the last time I was able to get
out to someplace as lit up as this! Not since before leaving home for good. I’d been so naive back then. Naive and very very lucky that I’d
never been swept up into anything that could have killed me. I grinned ear to ear before looking back up at Uta. However, when I tried to
meet his gaze I found that it was elsewhere searching the club. “Uta?”

He didn’t hear me.
I reached out and tugged gently on his sleeve and flashed a concerned, questioning smile. I tried to say in my expression. ‘Is everything
okay?’   The ghoul turned to look at my face and the serious expression there relaxed a small amount. He leaned close and spoke into my
ear so I could hear over the music. “Make sure to stay close to me.”

I wanted to ask what was on his mind but with the amount of noise it seemed useless. I rolled my eyes and for good measure ‘tugged’ him
closer with a grin. I’m not going anywhere. Tipping my head I indicated towards the dance floor. Coming?

## ♥
Honestly I didn’t expect to last very long in the churning crowd without falling over my own feet or perhaps worse; someone else's. So I
was happy when a new group of people got onto the big stage and started playing live music. While still loud it allowed me to take a
moment to pause and at this point I was able to gently pull and maneuver us both away from the crowd to sit at an open spot of the bar.
The ghoul was smiling as he sat at the bar, and he ordered a drink for the both of us.

What came back a minute later was two small glasses of peach colored alcohol. He raised the glass to his lips, took a very convincing sip
and then put the glass back down. It looked like there would be no forcing down human drinks and food tonight for him, which was a
relief. When the bartender wasn’t looking I picked up Uta’s glass and drank down a sip of it myself before sliding it back in front of the
ghoul.

By the time I finished both drinks, Uta had gotten a glass of plain water and  I felt warm and a bit fuzzier as the buzz lifted my spirits and
made me giggle helplessly.
“Don’t order any more alcohol.” I said, leaning towards Uta’s ear to make sure he heard me. “I don’t want to get drunk...” Or puke when
Uta inevitably carried me on his back to see the sights or run back homewards.

The ghoul nodded, then whispered back.
“Stay right here Ai-chan. Don’t move.” Uta stood up, looked around the crowd and then stepped away. The groups of people swallowed
up his body before I could ask where he was going. I let out a long breath and shook my head. Oh well. I raised my hand and asked the
bartender for a glass of iced water while I waited. That at least might dilute the alcohol a bit more.


A few minutes passed and a woman took a seat next to me. I didn’t pay much mind until she leaned into my space. The scent of lavender
was almost overwhelming on her. A hand grabbed my own and the woman loudly exclaimed. “Hey! You’re kind of pretty!”

“...thank...you?” I murmured, leaning away and taking my hand back. I glanced once over her and noticed she herself was extremely
beautiful. Pale clean skin, dark hair; choppy but long in the back. She wore a coat not dissimilar to my own but instead of black and red it
was purple and white. Her face was half covered by a small fabric mask. Both Uta’s and the bouncer's warnings sprung to mind and I
instantly felt myself go on guard. There was something wrong about this situation.

“OH! I’m sorry. That sounded rude, didn’t it? I’ve been all over this place tonight looking for some beautiful women for an upcoming
