photoshoot and party. You wouldn’t happen to be a model are you?”

“No. Sorry.”

“Well you know you could make a lot of money at this party coming up---”

“No thanks.” The woman’s half hidden expression faltered a little and she leaned back. She took a moment to collect herself before
exuberantly adding: “There’s a lot of VIP’s. I’ve had people I invited make well over 20,000 yen in a night!”

“She said no.” I felt my heart skip and beat and my muscles relax all at once. Relieved, I turned to see that Uta had returned just in time.
He stood behind the woman, staring blankly forward at her over his dark sunglasses. “Go. She’s off limits.”

The woman hopped off the chair and scurried away, disappearing into the crowd without a single sound. No arguments, complaints or
continued bribery. She was simply gone . I had no doubt she would be off to go lure someone else into her trap. “What did she say?”

“She was trying to get me to go with her to a party or something. Seemed fishy though...” I pursed my lips together into a thin frown. “I
assume it was fishy since you shooed her off so quickly.”

“...yeah. Don’t go with anybody...or let them get too close.” The ghoul reached out and took my hand, turning it over to show that there
was a small red ink blot on my wrist. I blinked, surprise and a cold horror spreading across my limb in his grasp.
“What---?”
The ghoul dipped his finger into my glass of water and then wiped it; smudged the dot and then wiped it on a napkin so it wasn’t clearly a
mark.
## “...”

Now I was uncomfortable as I looked at the residual red ink smudge where he’d tried to clean it away.

“Do you still want to dance?”
“No. Not really...Can we go? Maybe to the shops in the area before they close for the night?”
He readily agreed, staying by my side as we left the building with its booming music and weird strangers trying to lure people away to
some ‘party’ or ‘photo shoot’.

I sighed, relieved as I was once again able to hear myself think as well as actually speak. “Ahh! You know when I was younger I really was
so drawn to those places. But they’re so loud...”
I saw the small smirk on Uta’s face and lifted an eyebrow at him. “What?”

“Getting old already, Ai-chan?”


“Hey! I’m not old . I’m only two years older than you kiddo! ” The man threw his head back and laughed while I stuck my tongue out
playfully. “You should respect. Your. Elders!!!” I punctuated each word with a poke of my finger into one of his biceps.

“Okay Ai- senpai !~” I flushed pink and then red as blood flooded to my cheeks and ears. I shoved  him lightly and shook my head
fervently from side to side.
“ No ! Absolutely not! Don’t do that! I was kidding ! We’re basically the same age...anyway, you’ve got more life experience than me.”

The ghoul’s smirk straightened out though the glee still gleaned in his eyes. “Hum. I suppose that’s true...” I turned my own gaze down to
my palm where the red mark had been rubbed away and slowly my own smile slipped from my face.

“Uta...what was that mark for?”

## “...”

I glanced upwards to look at him, but he kept his eyes straight ahead and tilted so the sunglasses blocked his eyes. Chewing the inside of
my cheek I looked away when the quiet continued. We passed a few shops that had closed early - but many ahead of us were still open.
Food. Books. Jewelry. Anything you could want in a shopping center...

“...you’re going to make me guess then?” I took a breath and sighed. Staring forward I watched as a few shops passed us by, none of them
really what interested me so I didn’t mind that our conversation made us pass them up. “If I have to guess I’d say it was probably
trafficking...right? And that woman was a ghoul...” More silence.

“---I assume the mark was to label me later when I left the bar there would be somebody to swoop in. Because I was alone and didn’t seem
to be hanging out with any friends. I suppose that would make me an easy target. And the bouncer...he knows about it. Probably a Ghoul
as well. So that’s what his warning was about. Do I have that all right?”

## “...yeah.”

Pursing my lips I stopped us in front of a storefront and peeked through the window. “Alright then. Maybe next time a little warning to
watch out for that sort of thing? Okay? I mean, I doubt they’d have dragged me out kicking and screaming but still---”

The ghoul tipped his head to the side and pulled his sunglasses down his nose to look at me clearly. “You’re not bothered...?”

“That’s a bit of a loaded question. Saying I’m not bothered might be going too far. I’m not... not bothered. It’s just that a lot has
happened in the last couple months. And quite frankly...that really isn’t all that shocking...” I mean looking back, there were plenty of
things that did bother me. But along with that there were plenty of things that I’d grown to accept. I pursed my lips together and waved
an idle hand. “It’s not like I didn’t know people got kidnapped and trafficked before. That sort of thing seems... normal.  I was naive
Uta...not stupid. Humans do that to each other too. Ghoul’s don’t have a copyright on being horrible to each other...”

He slid his glasses back up his nose and covered his eyes. He raised his head and looked through the glass pane of the storefront and
nodded. “Did you want to go in here?”

A jewelry store. My eyes trailed over the golds, silvers, and gems to the stainless steel and metal knick-knacks to hang from ears, fingers,
necks and even toes. I was happy this time that he wanted to drop the subject now that I had my answer. Human trafficking is a little bit
of a buzzkill for a date, isn’t it?


“Yeah actually. Since you’re just letting me borrow this--” I gently ran my fingers along the necklace around my throat. “--It reminded me
I don’t have much in the way of anything to accessorize with. And it looks like they have things that aren't just gold and silver---” I pushed
the front door open and went straight to the case full of what looked like stainless steel and bits of leather.

“Welcome! ✰” A young woman stood behind the counter; all smiles as she greeted her late night customers. “Please, let me know if you
see anything you like!”

I paused, eyes going wide as I saw a pair of bracelets that seemed to be made of a black porous rock. I glanced up to see that Uta had gone
to a counter with a bunch of different types of piercings, gauges and other small facial or body jewelry. The store clerk seemed to see my
interest and leaned over the counter.

“Found something you like?”

I pointed out the bracelet set and nodded. “What kind of stones are these?”

“Oh. That rough black stone there is lava stone. The red stone accents are red jasper. The matching one is the opposite. Red Jasper with
the accented black lava stone. They are sold as a set. Are you interested in them?”

I nodded my head once more and watched as she picked up the two bracelets out of the case. Standing up I was able to reach out and pick
them up to study them closer. Another glance over my shoulder, I checked to make sure Uta was still busy.

Perhaps...I wasn’t Kimi and he wasn’t Nishiki. But the idea of getting jewelry wasn’t far off the mark. Bites were like jewelry that marked
me as his. So it should work the other way around as well; shouldn’t it?

I took out my wallet from my bag and slid my card across the counter. “Can you wrap these up for me, please?” I leaned and cupped my
hand to whisper really low. “Without him seeing, please?”

The woman nodded to agree without saying a word. She put both bracelets into wrapping paper and dropped them into a small paper
bag with the store’s emblem on it before ringing up the purchase.


With my loot secured in my bag next to my mask I returned to Uta’s side. “Hey...you see anything?”

“No. Not really...” He touched his piercings and wiggled one. I remembered of course that he preferred the quinque steel because it
didn’t try to close up the wounds as quickly.
“Maybe another place will have something you like. Where’d you normally get these?” I said, making idle chatter.

“A friend. I’ll have to check to see if he is able to make any more like the last set.”

“Mkay. I’m ready to go. You?”

## ♥

## ♥


The ghoul peered curiously at the bag in my hand a few times. Clearly wanting to know what I’d picked up. After watching him steal
glances several times I laughed softly and waved us to a bench.
“Alright! Alright! I was going to wait until later but I will show you!” I sat down and patted the seat next to me lightly before opening the
bag and drawing out the wrapped bracelets.

“Here...um...this one is for you...” I flushed pink, sudden anxiety churning in my stomach as it filled with a crawling feeling.
“You don’t have to wear it if you don’t like it...” I said, already making up excuses if he didn’t like it. I held out the little black paper
wrapped gift and waited. The ghoul picked it up and carefully unwrapped the gift, slowly and gently so as to not tear the paper wrapping.
The black lava stone bracelet with the red jade accent lay out in his open palm and he seemed to grow still to stare at it. I unwrapped my
own, showing off the red jade with the black accent as I slipped it on my own wrist.

Opposite, yet matching as a pair. Wasn’t that...like us?

“Is...it too corny? When I saw them I thought they were kind of perfect...”
The ghoul didn’t spare words; instead he simply shattered my worries by slipping the bracelet onto his left arm and tightened the band
with his teeth. He turned his arm around and studied it before looking up, leaning forward and stealing a quick peck on the lips.  “Thank
you Ai-chan...I like it.”

I blinked, flushing pink and raising my hand to cover my lips as my eyes darted around us along the fairly busy streets. While Uta hadn’t
been shy about the small moments of PDA in Itori’s bar - it had for the most part been kept to a minimum outside of the privacy of the
home.  The ghoul smiled and stood up, putting his hands into his pockets while he waited, his head turned up and down the street as
though looking for something.

“R-right...good then. I’m glad you like it.” I said, hopping up to stand next to him.
“Well Ai-chan where to n---” The ghoul froze and looked around once more, eyes turning around to survey the area once more.

I paused and didn’t speak as I turned my head and struggled to listen to see if I could hear what he was sensing. There was...a harsh high
pitch clank. Followed by a short pause. Followed by another clank and a crash. It was faint and muffled behind the usual bustling of the
city.

“What is that sound?” I whispered and leaned automatically towards the ghoul, trying to locate the direction even if I didn’t know the
source. Another clashing clang was followed by a car alarm going off one street over. The ghoul stepped around me, throwing an arm
around my shoulders and herding me away from the noises.
“Hurry...”

“Hurry...” The ghoul said again, picking up our pace. I struggled to keep up standing in high heel boots. I bit my lip as my ankles
wobbled - the old injury flaring up with residual pain.
He pulled us off to the side through one alleyway and down a backstreet to emerge on an even busier street. He had his phone out in his
other hand, sending a message before speaking to me once more.

”Ai-chan. Go down this street, go to the subway station and ride back home.”

“Uta? What the hell is going on?”


“The Doves are having a little party in this ward tonight...You’re not safe here.”

“Neither are you . Aren't you coming with me?”

“...” The ghoul glanced away, eyes turned towards the sound of fighting. “...You’re going to go fight them off?” I murmured realizing
why he was torn.

“Roma already is here someplace...and Itori is on her way.”

Another crash and sounds of destruction echoed down the streets, growing closer as now undoubtedly a few civilians were involved.
While I didn’t care much for Roma, the idea that Itori was on her way to help fight and might end up in trouble was distressing.
“Alright...go watch her back and---”

“Hey...you there? What are you doing? Please present your ID’s. Wait---your eyes! You’re a g---”


The ghoul in front of me swiftly wrapped his arms around me, pulled me close and shielded my face. Unfortunately it did nothing to
shield the sound of a scream cut off half-way, flesh ripping or the dead weight of a body hitting the ground with a wet squelch.
“U...ta?” I glanced up over his shoulder and could see the red of his Kagune flowing from his lower back and over his shoulder. I wasn’t
stupid; I pierced together what he’d done.

I took a breath, trying to calm my hummingbird heartbeat down. The investigator had seen his face - likely mine as well before calling out
to us. There was no way he was going to be convinced that Uta wasn’t a Ghoul in this situation when we were so close to an active fight.
Had he survived the night he would be able to point us both out. His death was horrible.
It was necessary.

The alleyway seemed narrow and the space between Uta’s arms even smaller. It was hard to breathe but I still managed--- slowly. I pushed
away from Uta, pressing my hands into his chest to separate us. I took another deep breath, quelling the anxiety and the fear that was
starting to try to push to the forefront of my mind.
“Ai-chan...?”

“Put your mask on...so that doesn't have to happen again.” I murmured, reaching into my bag for my own face covering. The ghoul
didn’t argue, and had pulled on his mark just in time for someone behind me to shout in alarm. Frozen, my eyes went fearfully wide.

“...Hey! Ryoichi!? Ryo---Shit. Reporting SS-ranked ghoul sighting. No-face found with unknown-----”

The ghoul took my mask from my hands and pressed it over my face, latching the straps in place with practiced hands.
“Hold on tight.” Uta’s Kagune disappeared and arms wrapped around my waist and pulled me off my feet, hauling me onto his back. I
wrapped my legs around his middle and death gripped onto his shoulders while the investigator yelled behind us.

“Deer-masked unknown individual with no-face! Officer Ryoichi down.---”

“Shit. Shit. Shit...U---” I had to stop myself from using his name even if I were only hissing it into his ear. “On your left.” The ghoul had
sprinted back out of the narrow alleyway with me clutching to him only to be flanked on the side by another two investigators.. The
static and calling from investigator to investigator was unnerving as they reported our locations and directions even as Uta sped away,

dodging while I winced and dug my nails in deeper from fear that one of those swings may land true.

I turned my head to look behind us as Uta leapt up, first onto a high fence before clearing the distance to a lower roof that they wouldn’t
be able to easily follow after. The men were left behind on the ground.

The ghoul paused, let me down to stand on my own and pulled out his phone to make a call. A familiar red-headed face popped up on
the screen from his contacts. Itori’s voice came through clearly, though the sounds of fighting in the background were muffled.

“WA-HOO! I haven't seen them this worked up in a while. When are you going to be here? You're missing all the fun!~ Did I hear over
their radio’s that you were close?”

“I’ve got her with me. They found us.”

There was quiet on the other end of the phone; no voices, just the muffled battle as it raged on. “Aika is with you? That's---shit. Alright.
I’ll try to get Gypsy to make a bigger distraction so they’ll have a reason to leave you...you’re going to have to run her back home though. The
subway station is crawling with Doves. I doubt they’d let you two out of the area...”

“Why didn’t we know about this ahead of time?” Uta asked, eerily calm.

“Sorry. Contacts told me about this last minute. I sent you the message as soon as I got the info.”

I heard the shouting from the street below and peeked over the ridge of the building before ducking back as a spray of hard shards
smashed into the wall siding. “We should move. Sooner or later one of them is going to get up here.”

“Sorry Hun! Didn’t realize you were with him tonight!”

I smiled faintly at the sound of Itori’s voice and shrugged even though she couldn’t see it.
“Yeah. Really put a damper on date night.” Then, smiling at Uta I added: “I’ll just have to have him make it up to me later. We’ll have to
find a nice peaceful place. Maybe I’ll drag him from the city and I’ll force him to go stargazing...something lazy and calm.”

The laughter on the other end of the phone cheered me up and she hung up the call.

“Stargazing?”

“What? Is that a no? Have you been out of the city much? It’s really nice to leave once in a while. Where there’s less light pollution you
can see the sky clear...You don’t want to?”

“No...I do.”

“Maybe while we’re out there you can meet some of my family. I won’t introduce you to my parents. That would just be awful, trust me
you don’t wanna see them. But my uncle on the other hand...you could meet him.”

The ghoul tilted his head and glanced down towards me. The featureless mask seemed to stare ominously yet he sounded curious behind
it. “The one who brought you out of the city and went hunting when you were younger?”

“The same!” I winced as I heard the door to the roof being kicked as the investigator tried to bust through it. “Time to go. I really picked
the wrong shoes for this!” The ghoul laughed softly as he knelt down this time, letting me wrap my arms and legs around him before he
took off, jumping from roof to roof while putting distance between us and the investigators.


## ♥


Uta dropped down from the roof and set me down on my feet. I leaned down to pull up the grating to an entrance to the 24th ward.
“They really aren't giving up, are they? I know where we are. I saw the street sign. We’re ten minutes from home. If we hide down here
he’ll pass right by.”

The ghoul cocked his head, looking at the entrance before lifting his head and looking around. Albeit, I still didn’t understand how well
he could see behind the leather mask.
“Go. Hide down there. We’re too close to home...I’ll lead them away.” He turned his head, pulled up the bottom half of his mask  and
sniffed the air. “Hurry...and don’t fall.”

I opened my mouth to protest, already an uneasy feeling began to settle in my stomach but I closed my mouth tight and clenched my jaw.
“I won’t fall .” I managed to grind out as I started to lower my body down into the hole. “Just be careful.”

I paused when the ghoul leaned down to place the solid metal grate over the hole and his footsteps echoed away. I slid down the ladder
and huddled below ground, breathing quietly and listening hard for any sounds from above.

Soon after I heard shouting, radios and one, two....three sets of footsteps as they pounded across the pavement above me. One of the
investigators stopped directly above and radioed somebody. I closed my eyes tight and held a hand over my mouth to muffle any noises at
all.

“No-Face and the Unknown Deer-Masked Ghoul entered the Fourth Ward, we lost them for a little while and they split up.
They seem to be leading us on a wild goose chase.”

“They can’t run forever, track them both down. You have authorization to use any means necessary. That bastard is worth
a lot of heads.”

“Dead or alive, Sir?”

“Bring them both in: Alive. We might be able to use No-Faces new friend against him. That Ghoul owes us a lot of men...”

“Yes sir.”

The officer above took off, running after his fellow investigators. I opened my eyes and peered around before letting out a long slow sigh;
still wary that someone might be listening. There wasn’t much to do but to keep hiding until it was safe. If I gave them plenty of time for
Uta to lead them away - then it would be safe to crawl out and sneak my way home.

With a soft thump I leaned my head back, hitting the wall and sighing. This...wasn’t my favorite date. First with the Human trafficking at
the club - and then getting chased by a raid of investigators? Though I had been mostly teasing about star-gazing; maybe getting out of
the city would be nice for a night.

The minutes passed by; first five then ten and then when twenty had come around I stood up and moved towards the ladder. I paused at
the bottom and listened. When all seemed clear I climbed up and out. At the street level I looked up and down the alleyway and scurried
towards home, peeking around corners and ducking behind trash bins when I heard voices.


I debated taking the mask off my face - if I was found now without Uta then I’d be just a normal human. Or---had they taken my
description including what I was wearing. And then they’d know my face for sure.

The mask stayed on, just in case.

Only a few blocks from home I felt the hair on my neck raise and turned just in time to see a red flash. My body reacted faster than my
mind; ducking and dodging out of the way of a Kagune.

Scratch that. I thought; glaring down the side street. It was a Quinque; holding it on the other end was an investigator who stepped out
around the corner and made a disappointed ‘ tsk ’ing sound.

“They said you looked pretty harmless. But you’re fast, aren't you lil’ deer?” I didn’t reply as I took quick stock of the man. About Uta’s
height, slimmer than him but still able bodied. Far more practiced than me. Renji’s warning that I wasn’t ready didn’t only apply to
## Ghouls.

I couldn’t fight the CCG either.

I turned and ran, spinning around the corner as another flash of red flicked out in my direction.
‘Fuck! Fuck! Fuck! FUCK!” I panted, breathing through ragged desperate gasps as I ran; tripping over my shoes with their too high heels. I
could still hear the man behind me - running after me while swinging the weapon and creating chaos behind me.

“Ah! Come on, Bambi! Fight back!!! It’s boring if you just run!”

I didn’t dare look behind me as I skid around corners. I was only a couple blocks from home! I could have been safe by now. Instead I had
the terrible luck to run into this douche!!! I turned another corner and nearly tripped over cans and bottles; sending a stack of them flying
with a huge racket.

The old woman who had placed them there turned and glared with red and black kakugan eyes. “Watch where you---Aika?” The woman
stared at my mask with wide eyes as my mouth worked to try to find the words.
“R-run! Get inside. Doves!” I hissed quietly, desperately.

“ There you are, Bambi! ” I turned and ducked, throwing up an arm to block the Quinque from hitting me square in the face. The
tentacle was rough and stung when it struck; cutting into flesh like a cheese grinder; peeling away skin as it knocked me back against a wall
and to the ground.

I flashed back to the fight with Renji.

Me on the ground. Gasping.
## Helpless.
This time I was in trouble. In real mortal danger because my ‘enemy’ wasn’t Renji, my friend.

“DEAR RUN! GET UP AND GO. NOW!” I turned to the voice calling out to me and stared from behind my mask, my eyes wide in
panic and confusion. The person calling out to me was my neighbor. From her shoulders a thick blade seemed to protrude and block the

‘blade’ of a Bikaku Quinque as it went to strike me for a second time. Harshly the woman shouted, nearly growling as she held back my
attackers.

## “GO!”

As I struggled to stand up, my mind sluggishly recognized only one very important thing. The old woman wasn’t wearing her mask. She
was exposed. This was my fault! My body cooperated to stand up, numb and weak but functional. I stared until another voice called out,
joining the other investigator making the number of people after me double to two.

“That Deer Mask one was seen previously with ‘No Face’. Capture her if possible!” The investigator who now was in combat
with the old woman called out to his co-worker.

I took a step backwards; trembling as I forced myself to turn and sprint away. Away from the shop. Away from the old woman. Away
from anything familiar so I could put as much space between home and myself as possible. Uta was right. She wasn’t just an old woman -
she was a Ghou. She could fend for herself and she was trying to help me. Best not waste it. I ran until I was out of breath and the sounds
of fighting grew more distant. Still shaking I pulled out my phone and tried to dial.

“Ah, ha! There you are!”

The phone nearly dropped out of my hands when I heard the voice nearby. “Ryo was my partner you bitch!!!” I yelped and ducked out of
the way, fleeing once more in the opposite direction. My legs and lungs already burned with effort to keep just out of range - getting out
of sight was becoming harder and harder to do and more than ever I was regretting the choice of shoes.

I turned my head, left and right to look for an out. I couldn’t run into any buildings, most were closed at this late hour and it might get
someone into deadly trouble. A light bulb went off in my head as I thought of what might save me. I turned down a side street and
zigzagged my way towards the nearest river.

I glanced behind me to make sure I was out of view and then leapt over the ledge of the fencing that normally stopped people from falling
down the bank into the river. The steep rocks gave way under my weight and I landed on my butt; sliding down the scree until I fell into
the water. Gasping and neck deep in half frozen water I glanced up at the bank. The man searching for me leaned over the fence and
scanned the top of the water.

I ducked my head under the water and disappeared; staring up through freezing water at the faded lights that were still up from the
holidays. The silhouette of the man stayed for twenty seconds...

## Thirty...

I struggled as I counted to a full minute - my lungs feeling like they were going to bust and colorful dots started to take up most of my
view. When the man's shape moved away I pushed my head up above the water and forced myself to take a slow deep breath so I didn’t re-
alert him.
To my horror he returned to the ledge and looked down just in time to meet my gaze. I froze momentarily.


“Found you Bitch! You’ll pay!” My whole body both felt numb and burned with the cold as I tried to pull myself up the opposite bank
under the bridge. Something warm shot through my shoulder and dripped down my back while a voice behind me laughed.
“ Crawl away like a bug!!! Vermin! Monster!!!!”

Ducking under the Bridge I clawed my way up  the other side, kicking off my high heeled boots to run faster. Another shot of warmth
shot into one of my thighs and I lost my balance and fell on the roadway on the opposite side of the river. With footsteps closing in
behind me I tried to push my body up off the ground one more time.

A boot slammed down in the middle of my back, grinding into flesh to hurt me more. I craned my neck and sneered at the man who
pinned me down under his foot. Barely above a whisper the man seemed to sneer. “I was right... Those are not ghoul eyes! You're just a
Human bitch! Tell me --- why turn on your own species? Is ghoul cock that good?”

I coughed when I tried to respond, wincing and glaring through gathering tears.

“Oh no, no, no! Don’t cry now!” He kicked his leg into my ribs, ripping an animal-like cry of pain from me.
“It’s far too late to get out of this by---” The investigator's leg suddenly wasn’t on my back crushing me to the ground anymore. The man
had cried out and been thrown back by something, landing on his feet halfway down the bridge.

“You’ve made a mistake Mr. Investigator...” My heart skipped and I turned my head about to search for the owner of the voice. Spotting
a dark shape through streaming tears I blinked to focus the image.
Uta. A few dozen feet away.
I sighed, relaxing my body slowly.

Everything would be alright...

Glancing back at the investigator I watched him for a moment as the man gathered himself after being struck. “Well, well! Looks like a
knight in---oh shit...”

Shivering, defeated. I lay still on the ground with no more energy to fight or run away. With just enough life in me to look up I turned my
head from Ghoul to investigator and back around to see what he was looking at. Uta stood in the same place and a tall lithe figure stood
behind him leaning against a building. Their colorful outfit and grinning clown mask were a dead give away. Nico.

Uta’s mask was off, dropped to the ground nearby. In its place there was a fleshy mask that draped down his back towards his normal
Kakuhou and connected with his Kagune. His Kagune sprouted from his back; six extra limbs that looked much more like arms than the
long flexible limbs with hooks at the ends; just like I'd seen before.

“Investigator Hayashi reporting No-Face Kakuj---AHHHH!” The man was cut off as the flesh that surrounded Uta’s upper face
and head seemed to be a trisected set of jaws that opened wide enough to fit a whole Human and lunged.

“You’ve touched something that is mine and mine alone!” The voice was both foreign and familiar to me. It was unmistakably Uta;
but it almost seemed to echo back on himself or as if he were speaking through more than one mouth. I stared, struggling to keep my
head up to watch as Uta chased the man, struck him to the ground and hunched over him. The sight and gore was hidden from me but I
knew what was happening. I could hear the undeniably happy munching noises from the ghoul as he enjoyed his impromptu meal.

“Gnarly!~ I really do forget sometimes how messy that can be! Dear, I am afraid that you are quite the mess.” I coughed and turned my
eyes about to see Nico. He hadn’t gotten closer - and my vision was hazy but he sounded worried.

“My dear. I would get closer to try to help...but----” Nico eyed the Kakuja Ghoul on the bridge and grimaced. “I don’t really fancy getting
eaten tonight...”


I turned my head back around towards Uta. Uta, who had just turned into a huge hulking form. Even now as he ate, four of the six arms
held down his prey which could no longer fight back while two held clear across to either side of the bridge for support.

“...Uta...” The voice that came out was weak - rough and raspy. The ghoul didn’t stop eating. “Uuuu...ta!” I tried harder. Still, the sloppy
noises of flesh, blood and bone continued without pause. I could barely push myself up on shaking arms.

“Uta-kun please...help me...” I whispered as I slumped forward, reaching. The red jasper of my new bracelet shimmered in the street light
and I felt my lips tremble. “...I want to go home. Uta...”

The ghoul’s head raised up. Where his eyes should be were just fleshy Kagune but he seemed to see me regardless. Just like with his
ordinary leather mask. He could see me; Calling out to him. Half a body dropped from the jaws of his strange jaw like Kagune and landed
with a wet thunk. “Ai-chan...you’re hurt...”

Uta turned and abandoned his food to cross the distance between us. Once he got to my side I felt something warm scoop up my body as
hands that were large enough to hold my torso wrapped around me and pulled me close. A deep growl came from the man as he quickly
inspected the wound on my arm.

“Uta...please. Let's go home and we can see what’s wrong with me there...I’m freezing...and dizzy...” As it was, the world was swimming
before my eyes. The warmth from the limbs on me helped, but slowly and surely the edges were going dark so I closed my eyes and heard
no more.

## ♥
Special short:

Uta gently set the manhole lid down and bolted away, the faster he moved away from this location the safer Aika would be. He turned his
head, scanning with all his senses to see if he could find the investigators and lure them away.

He could hear the radio chatter of CCG as he moved further away from Aika’s hiding place; the only thing on his mind getting them
away from her as his friends messaged his phone with updates. He grit his teeth, finding he was aggravated with his friends. Roma for one
was causing more trouble than helping.

Aika had called her a ‘walking disaster’ and she hadn’t been far off. She had no idea what sort of monster that small woman really was.


Uta stopped and turned, looking behind him as the investigators broke off; fanning out further so they weren’t all chasing him.

“Where is your girl? I thought she was with you.”

Uta turned his head, looking over the Ghoul who had joined him on the rooftop. The bright colors of the man's attire, not to mention
the smiley pin on his scarf were a dead giveaway.

“Big Sister...you joined in too?”

“Stay home for this? I could never!~”

## ♥

Another body dropped to the ground as the ghoul ended their life. He was trying to track down every officer in the area. They were
threatening his territory, his home and...his Aika.

“...Oh Lover boy!~ Isn’t that her there...?” Nico sniffed and then dropped his voice into a more even tone: “She’s bleeding quite badly. I
can smell it from here...”

Uta leapt forward, racing across the rooftops as the figures in the distance made it to the river.
Closing in on the distance he watched as Ai-chan ran, fled, and failed; falling to the ground when another shot struck her leg; splattering
blood across the paving and sending her to the ground.

Closing in, he could hear them now.
“--- why turn on your own species? Is ghoul cock that good?” He knew she was Human, he would have to die.


“Oh no, no, no! Don’t cry now!”

Up until the moment that the man swung his leg into Aika’s ribs and made her cry out in pain, Uta had planned to kill him away from
her. Make sure she didn’t need to see him as a monster any more that night. She wouldn’t have to see yet another death. Not when he had
seen in her eyes that the first one had rattled her quite badly. Seeing her face full of fear and shock made his heart race; until it pounded in
his head and all he could see was red.

“It’s far too late to get out of this by---”

“You’ve made a mistake Mr. Investigator...You’ve touched something that is mine and mine alone!”



## ♥


## Chapter 47:  Aftermath

When I first woke up I was warm. Too warm. Delirious as someone touched me and placed cool items on my head or had to hold my
arms down to keep me from hitting them.
“Uta!”   My voice was hoarse when I called for him; not sure where I was or who had me. For all I knew...maybe the CCG had gotten me
after all. Maybe Uta turning into that thing on the bridge had been a delirium as I hoped for something to come save me.


The confusion got better though, as time passed I realized I must not be in the CCG, or a hospital. It was too cozy for that; and gradually
I realized there was someone talking to me in a soothing voice. A cool cloth was placed over my eyes and forehead and there were soft
hands wrapping something around my forearm.

“Ms. Aika? Are you awake?”

“...Yoshimura?” I murmured, finally recognizing the owner of the voice. “Where am I?”

The cloth was lifted from my eyes and I blinked, wincing away from the bright light over my head. “You are at Anteiku. Do you
remember what happened?”

“Uta and I. We were on a date...Investigators attacked us...” I winced as the man's hands continued to wind a bandage around my arm as
gently as he possibly could.
“Yes. I’m afraid they did. Do you remember after that...?”

Uta killing a man, and the sound of his partner screaming. They must have been close.

Uta’s head splitting open like a trisected set of jaws. Those jaws enveloped the investigator while Uta bent over him, chewing,
moaning and enjoying the revenge meal.

“Yeah...” I said, feeling strangely hollow.

“Can you tell me about it?” He asked kindly.

“No.” My answer was soft, but came immediately without having to think about it. Uta hadn’t wanted me to tell anyone he had a
Rinkaku. This seemed like something that should be kept secret as well.

“Alright then. If you are sure. Do you remember how badly you’ve been hurt?”

“My arm was cut up...”

He waited, seeing if I remembered anymore. When I didn’t continue he sighed softly and helped my memory along.
“Yes. They must have had an Ukaku Quinque, you were shot in the thigh and shoulder. You’ve also got a few broken ribs and cuts and
bruises. It seems as though the shots went straight through without doing any lethal damage. It’s quite lucky. We managed to get you to
drink some water and take some medicine while you slept, but you will need to try to eat and drink on your own as soon as possible.
Everybody has been quite restless...We were worried we might have another Anteiku member lost as Kaneki was. ”

I struggled to sit up, or at least lift my head wanting to look around the room. Meeting the bosses closed eyes I grimace. Under his eyes
there were darker circles from lack of sleep. “...Sir. How long was I out for?”

“Almost three days. I was beginning to think we might have to risk bringing you to a proper hospital.” That would have been quite the
risk for them. “I’m glad you finally woke up, my dear.”

“Where is Uta!? I need to talk to hi...mmmm...” I had begun to move; trying to spring from bed. My body failed instantly and a wave of
weakness hit me like a tidal wave and forced me back down. “ Hush my dear. He’s in the next room. Sleeping...he’s been watching over
you this whole time. I only got him to go rest once your fever went down early this morning.”

I closed my eyes and let my body incline back down to rest as I was told. Truly there wasn’t enough strength in my limbs to do much else
without shaking. “Bjorn?”


The elderly ghoul smiled and turned his head towards the doorway. “Your dog is downstairs with Hinami and Touka. Hinami has been
very happy to watch out for him.”

“...Is everybody else okay? Did anybody get hurt? How is Uta? Was he hurt?”

“Nobody was seriously injured. Save for yourself, of course. Please . Do not try to get up again. Stay there and rest. Otherwise I fear your
wounds will reopen.” I sighed softly when the cool towel was placed back onto my forehead.

“...When Uta wakes up, make sure to wake me up...please?”

“I think it’s best that you concentrate on getting rest.” The old man smiled calmly and added: “---however. I will suggest it to the young
man when he awakens.”

“....thank you sir...I’m sorry.”

“Hum?”

“For getting hurt again...”

The manager’s expression softened and he gently placed his hand on my forehead, over the cloth. “That isn’t your fault. However, now is
not the time to worry about that. I will bring you something to eat and drink.”

## ♥




I took a bite from the bread and cheese that the manager brought me and grimaced. Hungry as I was, my stomach churned unhappily as
the bland food hit my pallet. Soup would have been better--- Although the fever Yoshimura said that I’d had had broken; I was still sick.

I sneezed. I coughed. I croaked when I spoke. And everytime I moved I winced as my ribs ached.


After I got a satisfactory amount of food into my body the older gentleman let me lay in the room, lights turned off. Nothing to keep me
company but the hum of chatter in the next couple rooms. Undoubtedly, he would be telling the others that I’d woken up - but to leave
me be.

A buzz nearby alerted me to the location of my phone. I squirmed to the edge of the bed to pick it up and  was dismayed to find a large
crack down the screen that splintered out from one of the corners. On screen I saw messages from Itori, Nico, Renji. I flipped through
them - a few were questioning if I was okay. Asking where I was. If I was safe. Where Uta was.

Then following those were more recent messages apologizing for not being able to help or wishing me well.


Nico in particular seemed especially remorseful. In the singular text he sent he once again apologized for not coming to my aid.

Aika: Don’t worry about it. I don’t blame you.

Not with Uta being as he had been. I closed out my phone and stuffed it under my pillow as I laid back and closed my eyes. Behind my
eyelids I relived those moments once more. Lying helpless on the ground. Freezing and afraid - but so relieved.

So it had been real; not some fever dream. Hadn’t it?

Even when Uta turned into... that thing. That form I couldn’t understand ...I could not help but to be relieved even as it had shoved a
whole man in it’s—his ‘mouth’.

I’d been saved. I’d been rescued and I was safe . Who cared what he had looked like while he did it. Who cared that I could still recall the
sound of crunching bone and ripping flesh. The way he moaned and enjoyed it all. He had saved me. I was desensitized more and more
each day to horrors of all kinds. With how things were going, maybe there would be a day when Roma teased me with a piece of meat and
I finally snapped and ate it.

Maybe I was the monster because even with that sound still replaying in my head; I could get some sleep and it was peaceful.

## ♥


When I opened my eyes again I saw a head of charcoal hair, messy and unkempt laying out on the edge of my bed. Unthinking, I reached
out and ran my fingers through the locks. The head jerked up and wide Kakugan’s stared at my face; searching for something there.
“Ai-chan...” Uta breathed out softly.

“Hey...” I murmured lamely. I frowned when I noticed how he jerked back from my hand as I reached for him. “...Uta?”

He seemed almost skittish and like a kid with his hand in the cookie jar, waiting for the moment when he was yelled at.
“Uta...It’s okay. ” I said more softly, patting the bed. “...It’s okay. Come here. You can lay down here, you don’t need to sit there like that.
It doesn't look comfortable. Don’t snuggle too close. I still feel too warm...”

Those black and red eyes watched me carefully as he pulled himself up onto the bed, sitting close. His eyes stayed on me, as though I
might vanish if he blinked or looked away.
“Ai-chan...” He reached a hand over me slowly, placing it on my forehead to feel the fever. “...Still so warm.”

“Mmmm...probably taking a dip in the river in the middle of January wasn’t the smartest idea.” I admitted with a smile on my lips.
“...Getting flung around by that tentacle sword—” His lips twitched as I once again used the wrong name for it. “—Wasn’t very good for
me either. If it wasn’t for—” I paused, eyes wide and I tried to sit up again only to fall back with a sharp cry.

“Ai, don’t do that. Yoshimura said you were really hurt...”

I heard a commotion outside and the door creaked open as a few faces peaked in.

“Aika-san? Are you okay?” Touka; behind her I heard a few other mutters. Meaning there were even more Ghouls standing out there,
worried.

“...Ms. Kirin. Is she...okay?”

“Your neighbor?”

“You mean that old hag—”

I cut off Nishiki’s comment sharply; managing to raise my voice even though my voice ripped at my throat.

“She saved me— While I was running away from them. If...if it wasn’t for her they’d have killed me. She fought them.” I gave Uta a
heart broken expression as his eyes searched my face. “She fought them without a mask on...If...if both the investigators that saw her
aren’t both dead— if she got hurt. It’s my fault!” I felt tears form and fall from my eyes. “ It’s my fault—” I sobbed softly.

If she was dead; it was MY fault!

“...Koma, Irimi. Check the area. See if you can find out anything about Ms. Kirin. Uta, is that alright with you?”

“...hum...Yeah.” The goth answered softly, eyes not moving off myself as he gave permission for the others to intrude on his territory
while he attended his girlfriend. He wiped away my tears with his thumb as they kept falling down my cheeks. The rest of the Ghouls
present were quiet, watching as I cried softly and leaned into Uta’s hands which cradled my head. Gradually, as if he were testing if it were
okay he laid his body down closer to me, rubbing along my side slowly to soothe me.

Quietly Yoshimura ushered the others out and away again; leaving me with Uta while I cried myself out until sleep overtook me.

## ♥


I stayed at the coffee shop for several days after.

The Quinque had done a number on my arm and it needed a lot of attention; bandaged what felt like nearly hourly. Treated with
antibacterial creams and cooled off with ice. Yoshimura was kind enough to do the honors under the careful observation of one particular
goth ghoul who refused to leave my side for more than a few minutes.

Uta hadn’t spoken a word about what happened. Hadn’t even asked if I’d remembered. That would come later; but I was pushing it
back. As far back as possible. While I knew I couldn’t ignore it forever; I could ignore it long enough that I could think properly and get
accustomed to the memory. Once everything had sunk in, then I could bring it up.

Ms. Kirin was missing officially. While Uta’s shop and apartment had been unmolested. Her apartment was raided and torn appart. My
old apartment’s door had been knocked in; left half hanging on its hinges. I was glad that I no longer lived there and had painted over the
walls before I left because according to Koma and Irimi the CCG were all over the area. No doubt Amonwas going to show up at some
point to question me all over again. I only hoped that I wasn’t injured when that happened. Otherwise the man was going to have even
more questions.

“Hey Uta-kun...if the CCG ask why you weren’t home. You should lie. Tell them we went out for a date—maybe out of town. Visiting
family. My uncle I told you about. That’s why we haven't been home.” If it came down to it, I was sure he’d cover for me.

“Stargazing?” He asked gently, staying by my side as my arm felt as if it were on fire once more.

“...Yeah.” I whimpered softly.

“...Is it your arm again? More ice?”

“Yeah... I’m glad it didn't hit my tattooed arm. I think it would have been ruined by that.” There was a quiet pause from the man beside
me and then he started to chuckle.
“My strange, strange human. To be concerned with that...”

“Don’t tease me! I don’t want anything to happen to it! You made it for me!” I peeked out one eye and watched him; his face barely
smiling as he watched me.
“I’ll get you some ice...don’t move.”

Don’t move. As if I’d been able to for most of the time here. Apart from getting up to use the restroom I’d been kept bedridden. None of
the Ghouls seemed willing to let me get up on my own or lift a finger. Enough was enough!

“I can move, Uta...” I spoke, defiant of the order he’d given me. Sitting up, reaching out and grasping a fist full of his shirt; I pulled him
close enough to press my lips to his. Something he had been avoiding since that night.

“—And I’ll move if I want to.” I spoke after breaking the impromptu kiss, staring into his wide eyes. “I can go down and get it myself. My
leg doesn't hurt so bad anymore and it’s certainly still attached.”

“Ai-chan...” I could hear the argument in his voice, an almost growl-like warning at the back of his throat. But instead of backing down I
scoffed.
“If I don’t move soon I’m going to get a blood clot from being in bed so long and I hardly think you’d want that either. Then I really
would have to go to the hospital. And they’ll wanna know what took the skin off my arm then; won’t they?”

Wobbly after not using my legs for most of the week I managed to get up and limp across the room. Catching myself on the doorframe I
kept limping forwards. Uta followed shortly behind, warm hands landing on my good hip and shoulder; helping hold me upright.

“I’m alright, Uta. This is from not walking about on my own for so long. People aren’t meant to be so immobile for this long you know.
It’s bad for us fragile humans...” I turned my head, sticking my tongue out at him to tease— to show him it really was okay. After
everything...

My help cracked a small smile finally; chuckling.  He continued to hover protectively near me while I managed to climb my way down the
stairs, peeking into the cafe. I wasn’t too surprised to see that the place was closed. With them taking care of me it was a full time job.
They closed early and were only open a few hours of the day. Other businesses in the area had done the same after the fighting played
across the national news; nobody wanted to be open past dark.

“ Aika! You’re up!” Hinami was the first to speak, loudly announcing my presence and throwing up her hands with a cheer. Bjorn bound
towards me, skidding to a stop so he wouldn’t jump up but pressed his head to my stomach until I pet him and scratched behind his ears.
“Yeah...A bit sore. But I’m up. I can’t stand another minute in bed. I swear to god if anybody tries making me—”

“It’s good to see you up.” Touka smiled.
Renji glanced up from his coffee and nodded. “...How’s your arm, Aika?”
To my trainer I held up the hand and made a fist, clenching it tight. I winced from the pain but put on a brave grin.
“Good...it hurts. But I think it’s just surface level; like a bad road rash. I might be human, but I’m not that easily broken!” I turned my fist
into a thumbs up and grinned; pleased that the room seemed to collectively exhale.


I moved to sit, taking a stool at the counter and resting my leg. “...Are there any updates on Ms. Kirin...?” I asked, ruining the mood right
away.

“It seems like she might have been taken alive.” The busty redhead leaned out from behind Renji with a sad smile on her face. “It’s not the
good news you were hoping for. But it’s the best I could find...” If that was the best Itori could do, that’s probably all there was.

“...Okay...” I sighed and bit my bottom lip to keep it from trembling. That meant she might be interrogated. She might still give up Uta
and myself. But beyond that, she could be sent off to the ghoul containment center. “Well...if you hear anything else.”

“I’ll let you know.”

## ♥


Later when I returned to the stairs to the makeshift room Yoshimura had made up for my recovery Uta followed, seating himself in a
chair near the head of the bed.

I watched him for a while, turning it into a sort of staring contest; until I blinked and groaned. I rubbed my dry eyes. “I’m never going to
win a staring contest with you, am I?”

“...Ai...Do you remember what happened?”

“Umhum...” Silence.

“...Don’t worry Uta. I didn’t say anything about it to the manager when he asked what I remembered. You want that as a secret too, don’t
you?”

I turned my head, smiling softly. I moved to pat my hand on the bed. “... It’s okay.”
We don’t need to talk about it. It could just be Okay .

## Chapter 48: Inheritance

Another two weeks passed. Uta and I went home; returned to ‘normal’ . Despite the boss's concerns I went back to work. After I’d
insisted I needed it to get my mind off everything that happened he finally relented.

The others worried; I could see it in their expressions as I refused to talk about what happened that night. Even for Renji I went mute
when he asked what happened. The most I told him was that an investigator found out I was human, attacked me, was about to kill me
and Uta swooped in to save me. At the end of the day the investigator was dead and I was alive.

That was all there was to it.

Uta hung around the cafe a lot more. He started showing up early and staying late when he dropped me off and picked me up. I
practically felt his eyes on me while they asked about that night and as I pushed off their questions with casual shrugs.

## ♥


“Ai-chan...?”

He’d asked twice since it happened; speaking soft and starting and stopping the conversation by calling my name gently.  I knew what
that tone of voice meant; the silent question:

Are you okay? I think I was alright for now. I wasn’t afraid of Uta. That clearly had been his concern at first. Now I wasn’t sure what he
thought as I continued to put off talking about that.

“Yeah?” This is how it went . I would answer and then we would sit quietly for a minute where nobody spoke. He was waiting for me to
ask—wanted me to be the one to ask rather than telling me .

His pencil would start moving again and I would know the conversation was over. I took a breath and glanced up from my book,
watching the ghoul as he sat hunched over his notebook sketching out ideas for masks. “Uta...”

His head raised immediately, ghoulish eyes focused on me. I had his full attention. “...You want to talk about what happened on the
bridge?”

“...You’ve avoided everyone’s questions. It makes me wonder...you normally would have asked me about it by now.” Maybe that was
true; I’d asked him about a lot of other things. And Uta was normally generous and gave me plenty of time to get accustomed to things
without needing to force the conversation.

“Alright; that thing you did on the bridge...that wasn’t your normal kagune. The one you showed me before.”

“You do remember.”

“I remember. I’m not...sure exactly what I saw. But I didn’t tell anybody about it; because it seemed like something you might want to

keep to yourself. Are you...upset that I saw? Or something?” Being clingier and more standoffish than normal was a combination which
was giving me a sort of emotional whiplash.

“No. I’m not upset, Ai. I was worried after I lost my cool that you’d run from me.”

If losing his cool meant he turned into a giant... monster? Well I could see why he normally stayed composed. But he’d done it for me;
hadn’t he?

You’ve touched something that is mine and mine alone!

Those were his words before he had ripped into the man; punishing him for touching me . For harming a hair on my head and threatening
my life.

“I was relieved Uta...Maybe I don’t remember everything that well after all. Because all I can remember thinking was that ‘ everything will
be okay now ’. Even though I should be horrified, I felt safe instead. I’m not saying anything to my friends at Anteiku, because I don’t
know how to tell them that...”

I let out a long, tired sigh before smiling weakly: “Can our next date-night have no human trafficking. Or a raid? Or murder in the streets?
Or Amon showing up out of nowhere as if by magic. Just...normal stuff? Maybe a picnic by a pond in a park with a bunch of stupid
ducks...”

“Ducks?”

“Yeah...some ducks. Maybe the worst thing to happen is they steal my sandwich and you chase them off. That would be a nice date.”

“You want ducks to steal your sandwich?”

I laughed; I laughed until there were tears in my eyes and Uta was smiling again. “Yeah! I think that sounds great!”

## ♥




“Boss. Briefcase---”

I froze along with the others in the cafe; glancing out the front window at a man in a suit, holding a suitcase and looking around. The
ghouls immediately noticed the suitcase by his side. It was an understandable reaction but for me he stood out for a completely different
reason. “Everybody calm down. I’ll handle it.”

I stared at the man as he reached for the front door of the shop, turning my head to stare at the bar counter top before I could be spotted
staring. Uta settled back into his seat, outwardly he seemed relaxed as he continued to sip his coffee like nothing at all was happening.

“Hello. Would you like a cup of coffee?” I listened intently to the conversation as Yoshimura stepped out from behind the counter and
began to speak to the man in a suit. Medium height, light colored locks. His hair was short,choppy and though he tried to comb it it still
stuck out a bit.

“No. I’m sorry. I’m here on business actually. I’ve heard some rumors...”


“---have you by any chance hired a young woman by the name of Aika Kaneshiro? I’ve been trying my best to contact her. But she’s hard
to get a hold of.” I bit my lip, staring so hard into the wood counter that I thought it might combust. Internally I curse; the moment he
walked in I had a feeling that suit wasn’t one of the Doves! It was fine tailored and far more expensive than a corporate worker would
wear. Far more expensive than anything the CCG grunts could afford.

The suitcase was simply a suitcase this time.

Unlike the suit in the store that ruined our girls day out, this one wasn’t wearing my family's crest. However the more I listened the more
I was beginning to recognize his voice. Eyes turned on me, looking at how stiffly I was standing; bowed head.

“May I ask your reason for searching for her?”

“I’m afraid that it is a personal business matter with her family. It’s imperative that I reach Ms. Kaneshiro at the earliest time available.”

I stood up, stiffened my back and turned to face the man with the best glare I could muster. “Yeah. That’s me. Kazu. Long time no see.
They upgrade you from butler to corporate lawyer, or is it a bounty hunter now? Warden?”

The finely tailored man startled and turned to stare at me. He did once over; glancing over my work outfit and seemed to size me up and
down. He seemed unconvinced and pulled a paper from a pocket in the lining of his jacket. He would look at it, and then back up at my
scowling face a few times before he finally put it away.

“Must be. It’s been a few years since this picture was taken. Even longer since I’ve actually seen you. I suppose you do still look similar. I’d
remember you glaring at me like anywhere... Please come with me to----”

“ Fuck off. Was something unclear when I ran away ? Or maybe hanging up the phone half a dozen times hadn’t been a good enough
indicator that I don’t want anything to do with my ‘family’” I hissed the last word, angry. Pissed. They’d come to my work and scared my
coworkers, friends and the customers.

“I’ve had enough! I don’t want anything to do with my family, or their stupid business. So if you can quit with the goon-squad routine—
## ”

“Ms. Kane----”

“ Don’t . Call me that! It’s Aika. Just Aika! ” I snarled, unable to stop myself from raising my voice.


“I am not here on behalf of your parents .” The man spoke firmly, raising his voice enough to be heard over me. He took a calming breath
while I gawked at him, continuing:  “Please allow me to explain. Perhaps in private. This is...a rather sensitive matter. I’d rather not speak
in a cafe full of customers. Or make more of a scene than we already have.”

The man inclined his head towards Yoshimura politely. “Please. I beg your forgiveness, sir. There seemed to be no other way to contact
her. She has been extremely evasive.”


The old man nodded back, but turned towards me. “Ms. Aika. If you do wish to speak to this gentleman, you may use the back sitting
room.”


My face twisted into several emotions, first anger and confusion then a twisted misery and finally frustration. “Fine. Let's get this over
with.”

“If you would follow me.” Yoshimura led the suit up the stairway and disappeared.
“I’ll be right back after I deal with this asshole—.” I muttered quietly to Uta as I left his side, storming up the stairway after the old man
and unwanted guest.

In the sitting room I found the man already seated. Yoshimura started to leave when I reached out and gently touched his arm.
“Stay? Please Sir...” I was liable to leap across the coffee table to beat him to a pulp if I was left alone with him. And Yoshimura seemed
like a good mediator if push came to shove.

Without a word he turned around and stood like a silent guardian by my side. While the suit glanced a few times from myself to my silent
sentinel he did finally begin speaking.

“Your uncle hired me several years ago to make sure that in the event of your parents death the board of directors at the company could
not stop you from collecting inheritance in light of your departure from your family home. I am your lawyer to represent you . Not your
parents. Nor is it in my contract to bring you back to your family home. As I am sure you are concerned with, considering your
considerable attempts to evade myself and those who work for the company.”

I could only stare now with my jaw going slack. Dumbstruck as this man explained his purpose.
“If something were to...happen....?” I muttered slowly and quietly, mouthing the words but not quite believing them.

## Processing.

He bowed his head in a solemn gesture. “It wasn’t publicly announced but your parents; the sole owners of the Company Kogane no
Shiro perished in an accident a number of months ago. Litigation of the ownership of the company began then - but without the valid
heir to the company it has stalled for the last couple months. The board is attempting to take complete control. If they succeed there is a
possibility that it and all the research could be sold to the highest bidder while they collect the money from such a deal.”

I swayed on my feet, each breath didn’t feel like enough air. A moment later I felt hands holding firmly to my shoulders, steadying me and
making sure I didn’t fall.

“I am very sorry again to have come here like this. However after months of trying to contact you though less...abrasive means. This was
the last route I could think of. You have my apologies again. sir.”

I shouldn’t be sad. I shouldn’t . Yet...I’d just been told that my family was dead; and it still felt like I’d lost something despite how much I
loathed them . I blinked rapidly and took a deep breath. “Okay...why...why would my uncle hire you for this anyway. He’s just as much
an outcast as me.”

“Not so. Unlike him, you were never taken out of your parents' will or the estate. Despite your run-away and continued denial, you are
still a Kaneshiro. The last Kaneshiro who is eligible to inherit anything for that matter. You never once filed to rid yourself of that name -
nor did your family strip you of your inheritance. Unlike your uncle who has been stripped of his name and disowned. They also never
had any more children. Which leaves you; and only you.”

“...filing that kind of paperwork takes money. I didn’t have the funds to get rid of the name!” I spat venomously. I watched the suited
man study me and then sigh.

“If you do not wish to contest the sale of the company then I suppose my job here will be concluded. The most I can do in this event is
make sure that funds are deposited into your account. You should be able to live comfortably from now on. Live wherever you please,
however you please. Nobody else will bother you regarding the company or estate. If you get the chance. You should speak to your uncle
at some point...his message said you’d know where to find him.”

As he stood and started to walk out of the room I glared at the ground in front of me.

“ Wait.” I said sharply, clearly and loudly. Kazu stopped in his tracks and looked back impassively. “Who are they trying to sell the
company to...?”

“Hum? I can think of a few people who might want it. It is one of the top three stem cell and genetic research labs in the country.
Arguably the world. With their particularly extensive research....if it were going for bid then I suppose the CCG would be a strong
contender. If not them, possibly the nation of Japan itself might have some stake in it.”

“No.” I said harshly, fingers curling into fists.

“...no? I don’t know what you expect me to do Ms. Kaneshiro. If you do nothing they will sell it for a profit. The only thing I can do in
that event is make sure you get some of the money. Any other action requires----”

“Fine. Then you work for me .”  I watched the man's face twitch slightly as I cut him off before he could finish his sentence.
“I suppose you would change your mind...”

“I'm not going back to live in some gilded cage. Once it’s no longer being put up for sale I’ll decide for myself what to do with it and what
happens.”

“As you say, Ms. Kaneshiro.” He bent his head into a small bow. “I shall get together everything I need to organize. Perhaps this time you
might be willing to answer your phone calls?”


“...don’t be a smart ass...” I sneered quietly as he left the room and walked down the stairs. I heard the bell to the front door chime before
either myself or the manager said a word.





“I can see that this has troubled you, my dear. I am sorry about your family. Even though you have mentioned you were not close to
them, it can still sting. Perhaps you might relax with a cup of coffee...?”

“T-thank you sir. I’m sorry--- “ I turned and bowed my head. “---for the disturbance I caused. I shouldn’t have yelled.”

“Nonsense...however, forgive me for asking. I wonder what caused you to change your mind. Clearly I can see dealing with family
matters is quite upsetting to you.”

I took a step back and allowed myself to fall backwards in an armchair.

“My parents' company is a gene research and stem cell company like he said. But they have so many branching research projects...they’ve
created some horrific biological and chemical weapons before and if it was sold off to the CCG I’m positive that they’d just...make more

weapons against Ghouls...” My eyes filled with tears that I couldn’t blink back and they dripped down my face silently. Rubbing at my
face I growled softly; gritting my teeth angrily.

My fists flexed and curled into balls until my nails bit into the palms of my hands.

“Damn it. Damn it all.” I slammed my fist into the chair and then sagged again. “...I’ll just. I’ll just try and stall until I can think of
something.” I wiped my eyes with my forearm and sniffled.

I nearly jumped when the old man’s hand landed lightly on my shoulder, a gentle support as he spoke.
“Ms. Aika. Please don’t feel responsible for something like this, it is too great a weight for any one person. Each person can only do so
much.” He smiled kindly and added: “I told you before, you are a lot like someone else I know who needs to focus on things they can do,
and let their friends help with the rest. I have found peace in making sure that this ward stays peaceful. Everything beyond that I am
afraid is beyond me. We each do what we can...”

He gently patted my shoulder and then left the room.


Maybe he was right, but how could I ever face any of them again if I could have stopped them---but chose not to. This is what I can do; the only
thing I can do. The only choice I can make is to keep my friends safe. To make sure the CCG doesn't get a single extra bit of help. So they get no
more weapons. They get no more research. They get nothing from me or mine.

After a few minutes of breathing deeply I felt a new fury filled determination.

## ♥


I stood up, wiped my face and walked calmly back down the stairs to the main floor. Upon my arrival the cafe’s hum died down. Looking
around I saw that only the employees, Renji and Uta remained.

“Ai-chan...what happened?” Uta turned his chair around so he now faced me but I shook my head from side to side.
“I’ll explain at home. Okay?”

“...alright. You okay?” I gave him a small nod and a strangled smile as I took my seat next to him again. A hot coffee with cinnamon sticks
was placed in front of me. It was well past the holidays, but the manager had noticed that I’d taken a liking to it. It seemed like the cafe
had more cinnamon sticks around than usual now; Personally I’d like to think he kept them around for me now. I took a sip fresh off the
top and exhaled a satisfied: Ahhhh!~

“I’m okay. It’s just going to be a pain in my butt to deal with.”

“Thought you were going to tell him to take a hike.”

“Seems like I can’t do that. I’ve got no choice...” I nudged him gently with an elbow. “Like I said. At home.”

The ghoul continued to look at me curiously and once opened his mouth before Yoshimura interjected. “Uta, I would suggest you speak
in the privacy of your home when speaking about this particular subject.”

The old man’s gaze turned to myself. “I shall be keeping everything I’ve heard to myself. So long as she would bid me too.” I relaxed and
nodded thankfully. I reached over and gently touched Uta’s arm, squeezed and then went back to sipping my coffee.


At home . Even among other Ghouls, it was best if this wasn’t known by too many.

## ♥


The trip home was quiet, but I could see that Uta was itching to ask questions. The moment we returned he placed the closed sign up and
turned expectantly towards me.

“I’m okay...” I forced a small smile; it felt flimsy and fell from my face quickly after. “No...maybe I’m not. I suppose I have to explain
now.” Here we go. “M y uncle hired that guy to make sure the company my family owned didn’t fuck up the inheritence....”

“Inheritance...?”

“It’s something you get when your family dies? I figured since I’d kinda—” I waved a hand in a few circular motions. “—fled? Ran away?
Abandoned them? I figured that I’d have been completely cut off. Like my uncle. Not really part of the will or family tree you know?”

“But as it happens that’s not quite how it went...and now they’re dead. Kazu said they have been for a little while now. So this guy who’s
been calling me—” I chuckled at the dismayed and annoyed memory of the lawyer’s face. “---has been struggling for a while to get me
cornered to tell me. But I kept hanging up on him.”

I snorted softly, the laughter felt inappropriate but oh so sweet. I remembered Kazu from when I was younger. He had been one of the
butlers; and in charge of keeping me inside. I had called him Warden back then when I was in my teens. He had been really good at his
job; right up until he hadn’t been. Never knew what happened to him after that; maybe they fired him?

“So I’ve got two choices:  Let it be sold off to the highest bidder and receive a portion of the money deposited into an account. He said it
would be enough to do anything I might please for as long as I live. I could go anywhere or do anything I wanted basically....which makes
sense. It’s a huge company...”

“—I’d be fine with them sticking money in an account and being done with it. I’m doing fine now without any of that after all. But if I
let it be sold off he mentioned it’s very likely the CCG will be the ones to buy it. My family has spent so long simply taking money from
the highest bidder, they didn’t care who it hurt. Even the medical side of the company was profiting off of people’s misfortune for so
long. I can’t let that happen anymore. If it’s sold off to the CCG, I don’t want to imagine the havoc it would ravage against Ghouls. Or
anybody else for that matter...so there’s no other choice I can make but to stop them...”

“So...I take control of it as head of the company. Which would mean I decide what it does and doesn’t do. What is and isn’t researched.
Maybe I can force the whole thing to grind to a stop. Kazu is getting things around for me now...which means don’t eat him .” I pursed
my lips together and pouted at Uta when the man grinned.

“So...you're the sole inheritor of a multi-billion yen company?”

“Yeah, I suppose so. I promise not to get too snobby.”

“I don’t think that’s possible for you, Ai-chan.”

“Uta...please. Can you keep this from the others? Please? At least for now. No telling the Clowns.” I took the spare office chair, sitting on
it backwards and leaning my chin on the back of the seat.


“Before I left home I knew there was some research happening involving Ghouls...but I’m not sure what it is. It didn’t really matter to me
back then. Or even after I met you guys; I figured my connections to them were all cut. But now I need to find out what they were doing
before I ran away. What fucked up shit they’ve done since then. And what they’ve been working on more recently. I can probably find
out what they’ve already given the CCG...and from there I can make sure that whatever the CCG wants, they don’t get. ”

I gently tapped my fingers against my chin as I continued to think..

I could weed out the people in the company who won’t want to work towards my goals. Maybe I can hire someone to help. A Ghoul? I glanced
at Uta and pondered quietly. If I’m cautious about it I might even be able to weed out those who have strong anti-ghoul stances. And of course
people who are also in the CCG, or have family in the CCG will need to go.

I will have to frame it carefully or I’ll get scrutinized and they'll sniff out that something is wrong.
Perhaps simply a ‘shift in direction’. No more weapons.
With the stem cell research I could lean into the production of human organs for transplant. With that in mind, if we can produce them fast
enough it might eventually be an alternative food source for Ghouls!!! With an alternative food source then---

I blinked, brought back to the current moment by two large black and red eyes staring curiously at me, inches from my face. “Ai-chan...?”

“I think...this might be a good thing. It’s...just going to take a lot of work. And Uta? I’m serious about not eating Kazu...”
