## Chapter 49: Time Flies
5 Months Later (Mid June)

I flexed my fingers, looking at the callous that had built up on my palm where my knife rubbed when training with Renji. The time
passed in a flash. With June already almost halfway over I suppose school would soon be out and Touka would be back for more work
soon.

“Aika, hello? Can you handle them—” I blinked from my daze when Koma leaned into my line of sight and waved a hand.
“Right, sorry!” I jumped back into work with a smile as I served a tray full of coffee to a table full of investigators. I glanced between the
two of them and smiled.

“It’s kinda rare you guys get time out of the office just for some coffee isn’t it. I almost never see any investigators around here.” That was,
until recently.

“Ah well...you’ve got to make time at some point. Especially for coffee as good as this.” The older man said. The friendly tone was pretty
deceptive, I’d give him that. The younger one sitting across from him was more hyperactive. The boy's head wouldn’t stop turning to look
around the shop and at one point he had stood up on his tippy toes and surveyed the cafe.

“Ah. I see. If you know Mr. Amon, please say hello for me.”

“You know Amon?”

“Well. A little bit. There was an issue with my old workplace. Really nasty case some months back before I worked here. He still checks in
on me once in a while to make sure I’m doing alright!” Unfortunately. It seemed to have become a monthly thing. Though it wasn’t
scheduled since he could pop up at any time of the month rather than a specific date. Just this past month he’d come with another set of
RC tests out of the kindness of his heart.

The results of that showed that my numbers were not climbing at a rate that he was concerned with. This at least gave me hope that he’d
leave me sooner than later. The difference had only been about 20 points and he’d said at this rate it would quite some time before it was

an issue. He had added that the numbers might fluctuate slightly and the ten points difference really wasn't much. I had no desire to
bring up the question of whether biting a ghoul might result in it raising, and staying raised.

“He’s been really kind to me since then. So please, give him a little hello. If you’ve got time of course.”

“I will. Thank you Ms....?”

“Aika. I’m Aika. It’s very nice to meet you. But I must go back to work. Please enjoy your coffee.” I bowed my head and turned around to
go back to the counter to grab another tray of coffee for another table. I glanced quickly at Koma and Irimi behind the counter and
smiled in the most reassuring manner I could.

Much of the time when Investigators came in Yoshimura handled them himself, however ever since I’d stepped up one day when the boss
was absent it seemed that I was trusted enough to handle them. I supposed that it helped that I wasn’t a Ghoul. All the better to send the
human to get them off the ghoul’s tails.

The first time an investigator had come in, they had waved a hand at the seat across from them and handed over a biscuit; insisting I eat it.
I had argued that I was on shift for the moment - but relented since I knew why they were trying to get me to eat it. Slowly I ate it and had
been dragged into a long conversation.  In the middle of it I had asked Yoshimura to make me a sandwich off the menu because I was ‘still
hungry’. I’d told the investigator:

“Well if you’re going to force me to take my break now I’ll be having my lunch too. I hope you don’t mind.”

The man had relented and left when I asked if I could keep sitting with them and started taking big bites out of my sandwich.

“Got it handled.” I said quietly as I passed the counter. “Just call me over if they need anything else.”

I went back to serving others with a reassuring smile. For the other ghoul patrons I could see they were worried to see investigators
around. To a regular I asked: “Would you like Sugar?”
I smiled as they went with our now commonly deployed alibi.

“Yes please. Thank you dear.”

I got them a little package of sugar out of my apron and handed it to them. They took it, opened it and pretended to pour it into the
coffee while they actually poured it into their hand and dumped it on the floor under the table. They knew I’d clean it up later when the
coast was clear. It was our little agreement that let them have a little bit more plausible deniability. The little empty sugar pack on the
table beside them was ‘proof’ they could eat/drink human food and were overlooked.

An hour before the end of my shift I spotted a head of silver hair enter through the door and turn around to look around. Blue-grey eyes
fixated on the investigators for a moment before roaming.

“Renji-kun! Hey!” I smiled in lue of waving with my arms full. “Koma, Renji’s here. Can you get his regular for me?”

From the corner of my eye I could see that the two men got up, picking up their suitcases as they went on their way. They were out of the
door and out of earshot but I still whispered as I passed the raven ghoul. “Hey Renji, have you seen all the Doves?”

“They’ve gotten more numerous lately.”

“Yeah. We’ve been a bit concerned; they’re all over the 20th like flies. Normally we have to worry about this sort of thing in other wards.
Uta’s also been saying he wants to see how I’ve improved.”

“Hey! We’ve been curious too! It’s been a while and you’ve been training with Yomo here for nearly half a year. Sooooo how’s it going?”
Koma budded into our conversation with a toothy grin. He leaned over the counter while he cleaned a mug with a little white towel;
shining it to spotlessness. Meanwhile Irimi looked up, listening in as well with a small smile on her face.


“Well I suppose it’s been helpful. I’m not really sure if it’s been---”

“She’s been doing well.” I pursed my lips together into a firm line when Renji interrupted.

“He’s being generous. I’m doing as well as one can expect.” I added doubtfully.

“I want to see for myself! Maybe you’ll be a match for the Devil Ape one day! Huh, you never know?”

“Oh I really doubt that---” I stopped speaking, turning when the door to the cafe opened and closed. Upon turning I spotted a familiar
set of sunglasses entering the cafe. Dropping the tray of glasses on the counter I raised a hand to wave. “Uta! Did you forget it’s training
day? You didn’t have to come pick me up.”

He took a seat by Renji and smiled faintly towards me when I greeted him enthusiastically. “I remembered.”

“So...when's the show starting?” Koma spoke up with a huge grin on his face.

“What show would you be referring to?” The elderly manager showed his face now; stepping from the kitchen behind the counter. His
smile was ever present as he looked between Renji and Uta. “It is good to see you boys.”

Groaning, I rubbed the bridge of my nose and temples. “There’s no show. It’s just training. And nobody is coming.” I rolled my eyes and
muttered.
“---Koma wants to see me train with Renji because he’s under the impression I’m ‘super strong’ now. Mr. Yoshimura, please talk some
sense into them.”

“You’ve improved significantly.” Renji took the mug of coffee slid to him by Irimi, looking at it pensively. “If you walked into the CCG
main office right now, I’m sure they’d have no trouble giving you a job with only a little more training.” I opened my mouth to speak,
but found no words.

Seriously? Considering the audience; What a morbid thing to say!
“Oh come on. I’ve come nowhere near to actually beating you. You can’t say that!”

“I’ve seen less competent investigators.” He spoke again, sipping his drink.


“No shit?!”

“I....Renji, that really feels like a backhanded compliment.” I murmured, trying to keep from flushing pink. Between Renji
complimenting my progress and Koma's shocked reaction I couldn’t help but feel just a little flustered. “Thank you, I suppose. But still...”

“Raven’s pretty strong. Ai-chan.” Uta said casually, his lips twitching into a smile not allowing the subject to die. I knew if anybody was
going to want to see, it would be him. “If he’s saying you’re strong - then I’d believe him. Before long you’ll have people wanting to fight
you.”

“Right...I really hope you’re not on the list.”


“At the top.” Just as I thought.

“I can see how strange it might be for you. However, it might be good for your friends here to see that you can take care of yourself.
Right?” I turned my head around to look over the counter. Meeting Irimi's dark brown eyes I pursed my lips doubtfully. “I can speak for
myself when I say that it would make me worry about you less.”

I grimaced and then pouted. “That....” I waved a finger at her accusingly. “ That ...is a dirty trick! Of course I’m going to say fine to that .
That’s not fair at all!”

I'd already expressed that I didn't want any of them to worry too much. I’d been letting Renji or Uta pick me up; or sometimes Touka,
Koma or Irimi would walk with me to get home.

“ Fine! Ask Renji.” I nodded towards him, my last hope to stop people from observing.
And yet; His head nodded deeming it acceptable.

“So! When’s the show?” Koma repeated, grinning because of the vindication he got from getting what he wanted. The manager stepped
around the counter and started towards the front door.
“I’ll be closing in an hour. That should give you both time to warm up.”

“Manager?! Seriously, you too ?” I groaned and rolled my eyes. The wrinkles around his eyes crinkled as his smile spread. There’s no getting
out of this, is there?

“Right. Of course. Of course. Fine! Pick on the human. I see how it is. I guess the show starts in an hour, Koma.”

“Closest entry.” Renji stood up, picking up his coat as he turned to leave; half cup of coffee left behind him. “Come on Aika.”

“The rest of my shift though—!”

“We’ve got things handled here.”

I turned from Renji who was already halfway out the door to the manager who waved me along. “I—but...uuuugh! Wait! Wait up
Renji!!! I’ve got to get changed!”

“Then catch up. You know where it is by now.”
Renji, you ass!!!

I raced up the stairs, skipping steps as I went. I grabbed my duffle bag out of the sitting area and closed myself into the bathroom to
quickly change. My work clothes got shoved unceremoniously into a bag. They’d wrinkle and I’d have to drag out the iron from Uta’s
closet but I was in a hurry. Hurrying from the bathroom I slipped my sneakers on as I went. I skipped four or five steps at a time and leapt
down the final distance. Sliding to a stop in front of the front door, sneakers squeaking on the floor as I spun and bolted out the door.
Flying from the establishment like it was burning down I shouted over my shoulder:

“I’ll see you guys in a bit!”

## ♥


I caught up with the Silver haired ghoul quickly and slowed down to walk once I was side by side with him. “Geez. You really had to rush
out of there didn’t you?”

“...Uta may start to pick fights again.” I glanced at him, raising an eyebrow. After training with Renji this long I realized that he would do
this sometimes. When he wanted to speak about something he’d bring it up out of the blue without any warning.

“Why? Because of our training? He has always stated that if I got strong I could fight him one day. I don’t really want to though...”
Actually the idea of fighting him scared me. Not because I thought he’d hurt me. But learning to not hold back and stabbing into Renji
had been hard enough during training.

Hurting Uta however; no matter how benignly, that would be too much.

“I don’t doubt he will want to...” Renji sighed and shook his head. “No. I meant investigators. Or with me. He seemed more restless
lately. All of his group does...” Renji smiled faintly and added: “I doubt very much that you’d have to worry about Uta harming you,
even in a fight.”

“Good to know. I remember when you called him dangerous and tried to warn me away. As for the Clowns. I haven't seen Roma in
months. After she didn’t show back up at the Cafe for work I figured I’d have at least seen her at the bar. But---” I shrugged my shoulders.
“Haven’t seen or heard about her since then. And that was nearly...six months ago? Shortly after Uta’s event.”

“...He still hasn’t told you about those, has he?”

“I haven't asked, but he invited me to one. So I suppose I’ll know sooner than later.”

“And you agreed?” I winced as Renji’s voice took on a more severe tone.

“Of course. With some terms of course. Itori and the rest of them have to be okay with my attendance. I realize of course that I will
probably not like whatever these events are. Not to mention it's probably dangerous for a human. But...I don’t think Uta will let me get
hurt.” He had proven that time and time again as he did terrible things to keep me from getting hurt. He was willing to kill for my safety.
“ And I’ve had this training for some time. Since you say I’m so strong now, I’m sure I’ll be okay. Right Renji-kun!?”


I leaned down first, grabbing the cover to the manhole and pulling it up. He gave me a scolding look but dropped down first. A moment
later I followed, leaping from a quarter of the way from the bottom and landing with a soft springy thump. As the months had gone by
I’d seen my own improvement. After all it was hard not notice that I was able to jump, dodge and lift things that had been otherwise
impossible before. Not to mention that I could keep up with him while running for much longer periods of time.

“Give me a minute. You ran out of there so fast I didn’t get a chance to wrap my arms.”

“Anyway...” I continued from where I’d left off as I wrapped a strip of cloth around my forearms, the scarring on the one arm a constant
reminder of how bad things could go for me. “I don’t think there’s much of anything I can’t get used to at this point. Whatever Uta
does...it’s just...part of who he is.”

I’ve already decided I like who he is enough to stay; haven't I? If there was a time to run away; it had passed. Tugging on the wrapping for
my arms; I tightened them and tucked the end under so it wouldn’t come undone.

“Alright. Might as well start and get warmed up. I don’t want to completely embarrass myself when they all get here.”

## ♥


I slid back across the floor of the tunnel with my shoes struggling to catch and get a grip on the concrete. Bending the knee, tensing and
then bursting forward like a spring I swung a fist at his face. Blocked by the ghoul’s crossed arms; my other hand swung and aimed at his
ribs - knife in hand.


I saw the realization in his eyes a moment before the knife would have made contact. A moment later an electric shock ran through my
body; stopping me and making my body shutter in pain. I jumped back and caught my breath as the electric surging through my body
dissipated slowly; traces still danced over my skin.

He wasn’t attacking anymore; but I kept my guard up. Knife in front held in a defensive stance. I eyed the ghoul across the tunnel from
me. Although I’d tried to forget the others were there I’d heard the gasps from the sidelined.  My own eyes surveyed my mentor;
particularly the huge claw-like talons that wrapped around his arms and hovered as a set of extra-large predatory talons. Not unlike
gauntlets I thought. His eyes red on black; staring at me with fixed concentration.

Both of us - breathing hard.
Both of us - eyeing the other.
Both of us - bleeding.

Months of going home bruised after every training. Eating a balanced diet and exercising even on the ‘off’ days had turned into muscle,
endurance and speed. Bjorn had loved the opportunity to run at odd hours of the day; it had been hard work. All that work resulted in
this. Standing here capable of holding my own with naught but a knife? The fact that he decided to pull out his Kagune?! A cherry on top.

I counted this as a win.
Evidence I’d conquered another stepping stone.

“That hurt Renji-kun!” I huffed out a lungful of air. “You haven’t—used those—before. I guess—that’s your Kagune?” I spoke between
breaths. Slowly I smiled, grinning through bared teeth. Out of all the months I’d been fighting he had never once brought out his
Kagune, not a single time.

A high pitch whistle from the sidelines startled me and made me turn to look.
“Geez. You really weren’t kidding, Yomo!” A moment after my eyes were taken off Renji I felt my side take a blow that knocked me off
my feet onto the ground where I rolled to a stop.

“Oops...” I heard from the sidelines.

Groaning, I pushed face up off the ground and glared at the ghoul. I narrowed my eyes while I collected myself, pulling my body up off
the ground and dusting off my clothing.
“Don’t take your eyes off your opponent. Focus !”

Hissing through my teeth I spat out a bit of blood from my cut lip. My right hand grabbed up my dropped knife and held it out at him.
“I know that, Renji! But the peanut gallery kind of distracted me!”

“Then ignore them.”

“Seems counterproductive for ‘ be aware of your surroundings’.” I ground out between my teeth as I circled him, watching his Kagun and
waiting for an opening.

Watching his Kagune wrapped around his arms as they were, my initial guess might have been Koukaku. But judging by where they
connected; He’s got an Ukaku. Just like Touka. Made sense if they were related. Uta had told me that Kagune types were at least partially
genetic. I tried to remember what Uta had told me about Kagune types. Ukaku were best for face paced fights because using them
depleted stamina quickly. But Renji seemed to have found a way to make better use of them.



If I just dodged and weaved around him for long enough; maybe he would tire out while using it.
I know what he would say if I didn't attack now. ‘You can’t back off just because your opponent has a weapon.’ Or something like that...

I drove forward again, swapping hands that my knife was in. His Kagune went up defensively and I ducked around him, dodging from
foot to foot like it was a dance as he struck; swiping at empty air as I moved around him looking to wear him out as I looked for any
opening I could.

I jumped upwards, trying to leap over him so I’d have a chance at his back. A moment later a crackle of electricity struck me making my
nerves jolt alive. I landed on the other side and slid down to a kneel; weapon at the ready but fingers twitching as my body was still
discharging the extra static.


A throat cleared from the peanut gallery and this time I kept my guard up, refusing to look away.
“Perhaps, Yomo, that would be enough for tonight. You both look quite tired. Ms. Aika has some injuries I believe should be looked at
before you continue.”

Renji’s shoulders relaxed and his kagune dissipated into thin air. “Enough Aika. You did well.”
My heart still beat in my chest like a drum and slowly I let up on my stance and relaxed. Breathing and finally taking in all my injuries for
the day.

The worst of which seemed to be a cut on my forehead that was bleeding down between my face and mask. Carefully I lifted it away and
sighed softly when I saw the inside of the mask. It would need to be cleaned up later once I got home; and a bit of extra padding so it
wouldn’t do that again. With the back of my wrapped hand I wiped away at my forehead and eye to get rid of some blood.

“Damn it... “ I muttered under my breath as I licked my lips and tasted copper.
“Uta, I found a sharp spot in the mask.”

“Oh man. Aika, you alright? You’re bleeding. Yomo went a little hard on you...”

“What...oh. Yeah. I’m fine. Looks worse than it is. All head wounds bleed a lot.” I responded to Koma’s concerns by shrugging it off. The
group of ghouls approached wearing worried expressions; save for Uta whose blank countenance gave away very little about what he
thought most of the time.

Renji retrieved my bag and returned with it in hand. “Here. Clean up. Otherwise we’ll have investigators showing up because you’re
wandering the streets covered in blood...”

“And who’s fault is that? What about you? Got blood on you too.”

The ghoul grinned good naturally as he spun my own words against me. “...and who’s fault is that, Aika?”

“Oh please. Most of it’s probably mine!”

“No...I think most of it’s mine actually.” Renji noted aloud, looking down his arms which had trace amounts of blood from when I’d
sliced into the limbs which he used to guard. His shirt was stained red across it and a few smudges and a cut across the chest. “Apart from
that little scrape you’re not bleeding Aika. But you got me with that blade quite a few times.”


“Here. I guess you need this more than me, right Renji-kun! .” I held out a moist towelette and grinned. “You bring an extra shirt?”


“I’ll cover it with my jacket.” The man bent to retrieve the dusty item and brushed it off before tugging it on and buttoning down the
front of it.

“You’re gonna look weird wearing a jacket in July.”

“They’ll be too concerned about your face if you don’t clean that up soon.” I dragged my arm back over my face again, soaking up more
blood in the wrappings. Damn it. He was right. Sooner than later I’d have to treat it or the blood loss would start to stack up.

“Right. Well this is why I wear a red shirt!” I joked and grabbed my bag from Renji. I took a seat and plopped myself down; finally
releasing the knife in my hands to the ground beside me. Digging through my bag I passed my wrinkling work clothes to grab the small
med kit I kept for exactly this reason.

“Lil’ help?”

This was the usual. A ritual that happened whenever we trained and I got hurt. Renji helped clean me up after beating me down. It was
kind of nice. For some reason in my mind it helped cement the fact that he wasn’t hurting me to hurt me. It was all for my benefit. I asked
for this - every time I came back for more.

Normally this is where I asked about the human woman whom to this very day he kept from Uta and Itori; but with an audience I silently
let the ghoul press a clean towel to my forehead and then bandage it tightly so it would stop bleeding. At first he’d fumbled, failing at
times to know what to do. Over the last few months he’d gotten pretty good at treating human wounds.

“Can you imagine if she got a Quinque! She might even be able to beat one of us!”

I frowned, a sick feeling stirring in my gut. I know his words were supposed to be encouragement . Some form of ‘ good job, you’ve come
far’. Maybe he was even right to a point. I might have a better fighting chance with one of those, but using it would be unacceptable. I
shivered and shook my head as I fought back revulsion. Each time I was forced to think of those things I imagined my friends, caught,
tortured and taken apart for scraps.

“I’m good with my knife. But thank you.” I eyed Koma and the woman next to him. “Irimi, are you guys all less worried about me now?”
They nodded, but the older gentleman shook his head.

“I’m afraid, I shall always worry about you.” The old man said gently; his smile while still present ---seemed sad . Why? Hadn’t I shown I
was gettin stronger? I could defend myself -- maybe at some point I could defend someone else? “--- But I must admit that was an impressive
display, Ms. Aika.”

I smiled, chuckling softly. Rubbing the back of my neck I looked away, anywhere but my friends as my cheeks flushed pink. “Right.
Well...that was the first time Renji used his Kagune. So I suppose that’s something.”

I took a moment to look at my boyfriend, smiling and tilting my head curiously. He hadn’t said a word since arriving to watch the
training, nor after we had finished. In fact he seemed to be deliberately hiding his expression behind that poker-face mask. “Uta-
kun...what do you think?”

The ghoul’s mask fell away when I called out to him specifically. A small twitch of his lips signaled a smile and he eyed the mask that lay
beside where I sat. He stepped closer, leaned to pick up the mask and study it. “...you're right about that spot, I’ll fix it when we get
home...”


“I meant about the fight.”

“...I think you’re going to need someone else to train with soon.”

“Huh? But Renji’s a good trainer!”

“But If you keep fighting the same person you’re not going to get any better after a certain point, right?”

“Says the guy who kept picking fights with him.” I pointed out and giggled at the flash of surprise that flashed over Uta’s expression,
followed quickly by a small pout.
“That’s different.”

“Was it? I think you just want me to fight you.”

“...it would be good practice.”

“No it wouldn't be.” I argued, shaking my head. “I wouldn’t be able to hit you.”

“I’d go easy on you. I could let you hit me.” He completely missed the point. Or he was ignoring it. I rolled my eyes and decided that if he
wanted to hear it so bad - I’d tell him. Again.
“I love you too much to try to hurt you. Even in training. Which I’ve already told you. I’m beginning to think you just like hearing me say
so. ”

The goth ghoul leaned to sit on his haunches so we were on equal level and looked over my face. He eyed the traces of blood and leaned
forward. He brought his hand to my forehead where I was bleeding and swiped fingers across the streams before bringing it to his mouth
without hesitation. I didn’t even flinch as he tasted it. Behind him though I spotted the different looks he was getting from the Anteiku
Ghouls. Shock and horror, concern. Of course, they didn’t typically see how he would act like this sometimes.

Finally he spoke up again; his gentle voice calm as ever.  “I hadn’t realized how strong you were getting...”

Unperturbed, I laughed. “Well, no. I suppose you’ve never come to training. I was a little worried you might get antsy about Renji
beating the pulp out of me.” Or not worried so much as possessive or defensive. After what happened with the CCG a few months back,
there had been some time where he hadn’t allowed any other ghoul or human get too close to me.

When Amon had shown up shortly after and I was still on the mend Uta had glowered at the man until he got nervous and left. “You can
be scary when you glower at people like that—”

“...scary?” The words were soft and his lips were downturn; unhappy or thoughtful.

“---if you start training me, you’ll have to go easy. You know? Anyway, it’s not like Renji has ever gotten serious. If I fought a Ghoul, I’d
still be dead-meat. You’ll always need to protect me...”

“You’re still bleeding, Aika. You should clean that up...you’ve got a meeting with the board tomorrow. Don’t you?” I turned to the
Raven ghoul and smiled sheepishly.
“Yeah...the lawyer finally got it all sorted out. Tomorrow that’s happening. I’m sure they’ll survive if I have a bandaid on my forehead.” I
exhaled a shaking breath and moved to stand up, stretching out my limbs and whining as the muscles stretched.


“Uta-kuuuun!~” I turned my attention back to the goth and smiled. “Wanna head home? Renji beat me up again!”

I heard Renji choke as I jokingly complained.
“Yeah.” I grinned as Uta stood up too, gave Renji a thousand yard stare before turning and walking towards the access point.
“Come on Ai-chan, I’m hungry. Cook me dinner.” I chuckled and jogged after him, sweeping up my bag of stuff on the way.
“Ok,ok!~ See you all later!”

Waving at the group of ghouls left underground; I briefly saw each of their faces. Some, like Koma, seemed to beam; excited to have seen
my progress. While the manager still seemed sad and I couldn’t place why.

“Uta-kun...you know I was joking about being beaten up by Renji. Yeah?”

“Umhum.” He confirmed with a soft hum and continued to walk towards the station.

“Are you bothering Renji again and starting fights?”

I saw how his eyes glanced towards me and settled on my face as I watched him.
“He said something about it. Is everything okay? You seem restless lately...I’ve seen how many masks you’ve been making.” He had been
throwing himself into his work more than usual and the walls were completely lined with ‘extra’ masks that he’d made completely on a
whim.

“A little bored.” He admitted softly. “How about you? When Renji-kun brought up that meeting you seemed nervous. You don’t have
to do it, if you don’t want to Ai-chan.” I laughed softly; filled with anxiety all over again.
“...Yoshimura said the same. But I do—anyway. I asked for help before. If Itori can find some people that I can put in the right places—”
I swallowed dryly as I looked around the train station. All was quiet.

When the train pulled up and the doors opened a few people stepped out and we filed in. I looked up and down the car and reached to
grab Uta’s hand, pulling him along to an empty car and sat. When we started moving again I spoke softly again; eyes fixed on my lap.

“—I could actually help? You know how I said that nobody was working on alternate foods? Or something to help ? What if... this could
help? Maybe something like that could happen in our lifetime? And even if it can’t...then I can take away just one thing from them . And
that’s worth being a little uncomfortable. It’s just a business suit after all. I won’t die. ” I looked up and grinned as I cracked a joke.

“Ai...you told me all this before.”

“I know...” I exhaled softly; knowing he was right. He was critical of my efforts, though he still supported me. Telling me I should do as I
pleased even if it didn’t end up helping. Hope and gusto faded from my eyes as I leaned towards him, letting my thigh touch his. My head
tilted til it lay on his shoulder. Sighing I muttered: “I know. But maybe if I say it enough. I’ll believe it and it will be true...”

## ♥

I closed my eyes for most of the ride home, relaxing against my boyfriend and trying to forget that tomorrow I’d have to stand in front of
a board that wanted nothing more than to sell my company and give it over to people who wanted to use it to harm my friends. There
was a chance that there would be CCG representatives there as well; they would have questions about why I wouldn’t want to sell.

“Ai-chan...Relax...” I exhaled and peeked open my eye; looking upwards at his face. From this angle I could see under his sunglasses.
Those onyx and blood red eyes were focused down at me.

“Sorry...until the meeting is over, I doubt much of anything will be on my mind.”

“I’m sure I could distract you, if you’d like.” I felt blood flood to my cheeks and ears, the tone of his voice was light, playful and
suggestive.
“You could certainly try!” I felt butterflies in my stomach as his arm curled around my waist, pulling me close as the train came to a stop.

His hand remained around me as we walked home; the soft curve of his lips grabbing my attention as we made our way. After he closed
the door to the studio I leaned up, held both sides of his face and pressed my lips against his. In an instant he reciprocated; hands on my
hips and pressing my ass into the nearest counter with a groan before pulling back and growling. “Ai-chan...I warned you about doing
that while I was hungry.”

“I know, I know. Are you hungry because I was bleeding earlier?” I remembered how he’d licked blood from his fingers after he’d swiped
it from my bleeding forehead.

“Partly.” He admitted and leaned in to nip at my neck, despite his own warnings about being hungry. “Watching you fight made me
hungry...”

“Hungry? Not horny ? That’s a shame!~” I smirked as he pulled back enough that I could see his expression again.
“Maybe it’s both.” He spoke with eyes wide and held cocked as if the idea was a new one to him.

“I’ll cook dinner. And then if you're still feeling that way, you can have me! Deal?”

I didn’t need to hear an answer when I could see his face; eyes lighting up as I proposed my so-called ‘deal’. Slipping around him I ran up
the stairs into the apartment, glancing over a shoulder I could see him slowly following.

Bjorn barked and bounced around the room, happy that we had returned. First he greeted me.
“Good boy, did you keep the house safe!? Who’s the best house protector...? You are! Good boy!” I leaned down and laughed as the huge
canine licked at my face and continued to wiggle his whole body instead of just his tail.

When Bjorn was done with me he moved onto Uta who he had grown fond of over the past few months. While Uta petted the dog, I
stood and made my way to the kitchen. First washing my face off over the sink and then slowly getting pans out to cook Uta’s dinner.
“...Organ meat or muscle? Or do you want a little of both...?”

“Both.”

“Okay. Do you want the organs raw then? And the muscle cooked like normal?”

A soft affirmative hum was all I got in reply and I smiled. Like normal . Bjorn getting used to Uta wasn’t the only thing that had changed.
I plucked out the Tupperware from the fridge, checked that it wasn’t chicken for the dog, and then looked through it. Finding a good
chunk of muscle, I lightly plucked it up between two fingers and dropped it into the pan. Fat and blood soon followed, dumped over the
meat while I reached with my soiled fingers to rinse them under the sinks hot water.

I used a set of tongs to move the meat around, flipping it so it wouldn’t burn. When it was done I went back to the fridge, grabbing organ
meat from its box and cutting it up in little bite-sized bites which were deposited over the plate. The last of the blood in the now empty
Tupperware served as a drizzle over everything before I tossed the plastic in the sink, letting the hot water flow over it while I delivered his
plate. “Here you are.”

As he ate I did the dishes, soaking my hands in the water that was almost too hot; turning my skin a heated red color and burning away
the guilt. Five months. He had hunted six....or maybe seven times during that time. Each time I hid in the bedroom or stayed at work
until he was done with the mess .


Each and every time I’d pretend it didn’t bother me. Ignore that it happened at all. But I’d see the fresh meat in the fridge. See the blood
in the containers still running fresh red before it had a chance to turn brown. Seven times; I think it was seven. I was forgetting already
how many people he’d killed. Then again—should I be counting the ones he killed between meals? The random threats to his territory? Or the
investigators that just ‘disappeared’?

I glanced over my shoulder, leaning out the kitchen with a smile. “Good?”
The ghoul had his mouth full but he glanced up, eyes wide looking almost innocent as he stuffed his face with human meat . “Good!
Almost finished with the dishes. Do you want coffee with dinner?”

I waited a few moments, frowning when I didn’t hear a reply.  “Nah, later.”
My body jerked, flinching when the answer came just a few inches from my right ear.
“Jeezus Uta! Come on...you know that scares me! You’re so quiet.” I laughed regardless, leaning into him as he wrapped his arms around
from behind, placing the dish into the sink.

“I just finished those!”

Chapter 50: Semi-HostileTakeover

The next morning I awoke in a bed that still smelled of sex, sweat and blood. My ghoul was wrapped around me, naked as we had fallen
asleep the night before. He had kept licking the wound on my shoulder any time it bled until it had finally stopped.

And I had fallen asleep soon after with plans on my mind to take a shower the next morning. Just as soon as my alarm went off. So when
it finally did go off I awoke, reaching for my phone. Behind me the man groaned; growling slightly as I slipped further from his arms. I
grunted as he flexed, pulling me away from my phone and back to him.


“Uta...I need to get up. Kazu is going to be picking me up in an hour. I need to get a shower and get dressed. And maybe; maybe if I’m
lucky I’ll have time to eat something.” I felt Uta’s warm tongue slide over my shoulder again, and winced more out of the expectation of
pain than actual pain. I reached with my fingers; brushing the edges of where I thought the bite was only to find that it wasn’t nearly as
bad as I thought it would have been. It only stung a little.

“Uta-kun, I’m taking a shower...” I finally did manage to slip from his arms, escaping from bed. I turned off the alarm and dragged the
sheets with me as I walked across the room in the nude. From my drawer I picked out a new bra and a pair of underwear.

“You can join me if you get up sleepyhead. Or you can stay in bed!~”

Leaving him behind I went for a shower straight away. Turning the water to its hottest setting, I waited for it to steam up the room before
dipping under the water.  I hissed as the water stung my skin, burning as much as it relaxed my muscles and felt good. A few minutes into
my shower; with bubbles already in my hair the ghoul entered the room. He was still in the nude, having walked straight from the
bedroom. He stepped up behind me and sighed as the water hit and rolled over his shoulders and back.

“What are you doing today when I’m away? Masks?”

“...I haven't got any orders I’m behind on. I’m not sure.”

It was a longshot, but I did wonder if perhaps he was more worried about me going than he let on. “....If I could, I'd bring you. I
wouldn’t be so nervous. But I don’t think that would be a good idea.” Not with his eyes. There were some settings that sunglasses just
would look suspicious.

“I could wait outside.”

“Maybe. I could also ‘hire’ you as a bodyguard!~ But...I think...it would be better if you kept as far from this as possible.” I nibbled on my
bottom lip, sighing as he moved my hair and his lips traced the side of my throat.
“Keeping me away?”

Yes. Yes I wanted to keep him away. To keep him far away from that sort of world. It was harsh, unforgiving. Not to mention the
backstabbing and throat ripping; But not in the ways that the 4th ward were those things. I turned my body around and reached up to
hold his face in my hands. “...you always protect me. Let me protect you from that sort of world...it’s a different kind of vicious Uta...just
as bloodthirsty but with a completely different set of rules. You don’t need to have to balance on two different tightropes at the same
time...okay? I’ve got this.”

I closed my eyes as he leaned forward and rested his forehead against mine. “Keeping me safe...? And what about you.”

I grinned and peaked my eyes open; seeing his eyes still focusing in such close quarters.
“I’ve got a plan to keep me safe. I won’t have to be around the company all that much, just to check in once in a while. Wanna hear about
it?” I don’t need an answer to know he would; at least I could try and reassure him. This was the farthest and the most ‘danger’ I’d have
been in since that night. As protective as he could be; he can’t be there today.

“I might be the head of the company. But I won’t be the face that most people know outside of it; I’ll have my own mask for the public.
Kazu will have that role. He’s about to get a promotion—so don’t eat him. I need him, alive!”

“As long as he behaves, Ai-chan...”

I smiled faintly and added: “He’ll be the one to deal with any public outrage. He’s a lawyer and a politician at heart. Good at
manipulating people with honey’d words and good at wooing a crowd with his voice. He’s also conventionally attractive, older than
me—but not too old that he’ll sound out of touch. He’s perfect. Plus—I kind of want to give him trouble for when I was a kid.”

The ghoul hummed softly, smiling faintly as he looked down at me. “So you won’t be moving away for this?”


“Were you worried I’d be leaving?” I watched how his eyes slid away from my face for a moment and scoffed. “Uta—I’m notleaving! I’m
doing everything I can so I barely have to deal with any of that myself. But—As soon as this is over we are going on a trip. I’m going to
steal you away. I think you should meet some of my family. Well...the only family I’ve got left.”

“Your uncle. Where did he live?”

“About two hours away, outside the city. He’s got a nice little cabin tucked away in the hills...it’s nice and calm there. Kazu mentioned he
wanted to see me anyway. So ...we could visit for the weekend? We’ll bring some of your food in a small freezer box.” That would work,
although it might take a little convincing uncle not to make him eat something he hunted.

“Please? Maybe you could ask Renji to drive? Those two might like each other. Since my uncle used to train me with the sword; for
fencing?”

“Yeah...they might.” I could feel hands, rubbing up and down my sides now. Soap slicked up my skin as he moved to touch more and
more; cupping around my hip and up my ribs.
“...He’ll be happy to meet you too.”

“This weekend? You want to go stargazing.” I smiled, happy that he remembered.
“Something relaxing....far away from the city. Neither of us will have to worry about a thing...”

I slid my hands down his shoulders and over his chest, tracing a few tattoos before I went back to cleaning myself, getting ready. “We’d
better hurry...or Kazu will kick down our door while we’re still in the shower. I’ve got to get there early...”

“It’s three in the morning, Ai-chan...”

I smiled faintly and kissed his cheek: “All part of the plan!~It’s going to be a very long day though.”


## ♥

I stood in front of the shop fiddling with the sleeve of the black blazer that I wore; a matching outfit as I took on the look of a ‘suit’. In
the mirror I had a grimace; noting that I looked just like a CCG officer. At least it’s not a pencil skirt though. Moths still flickered around
the street lights and the sky was still dark; it would be for several more hours.

I heard the soles of his shoes before I saw the man appear around the corner, straightening his jacket. “There you are. There’s a car around
the corner. Come along, I’d rather not be in this ward any longer than I have to be. Especially at this hour.”

I glanced back at the closed door of Hysy and then forward, nodding. “Let’s go get this over with.”

In the car I watched out the darkly tinted windows as the city transformed; slums to the high rises. Kazu was explaining as we traveled. “---
They won’t be happy with this. But they won’t have a choice. I have all the paperwork. There shouldn’t be a thing out of place.”

“Will there be representatives from companies that want to buy the company there?”

“It is very likely.”

“...They are going to be disappointed; I won’t be selling.”

“Yes, Madam.”


“Hummm...Did you do what I asked?” I said, pouting at my own reflection in the mirror-like windows. The woman stared back; red
lipstick and eyeshadow. Gems hanging from her ears and necks. I didn’t recognise her at all.

“The CCG contract? Yes. I have the paperwork worked out. It will require giving back quite a bit of funding to break the contract; but
the company can afford it. Your parents always kept a good reputation with them, so there’s nothing too crippling in their contract. The
other contracts you mentioned disliking expire this fall. It would be in the company's best interest to keep them until they’re expiry date
and simply refuse to renew. It is of course at your discretion.”

Just a few more months? It would be better to save some of the company's reputation if they weren’t dealing with weapons or Ghouls. “ That’s
fine. But I want you to make sure we’re not giving away too much information. Downsize anything that’s a weapon and move people
around. Also Kazu, after today I have a new job for you.”

I glanced up, looked in the rearview mirror and met the driver's eyes. “Yes Madam?”

“I want you to handle the public. Be the face of the company while I handle how it runs. You can name your price.”

The man was quiet for sometime before speaking. “...You want me to run things?”

“No. I want to pay you to oversee. I don’t want my face on anything . But I want you to issue my orders. Be a mouthpiece and help me
move the company how I want. What I’m going to do with it might not be popular and I want you to handle the public on top of the
stuff you already have been doing. I can hire extra help so it’s not all on you; but with the sort of money the company has, I can make sure
you get to live anywhere you want. You and your family will be safe and protected. I want to buy your loyalty and your silence. Not a
word will ever be mentioned about my boyfriend. Not about where I live. Not a word about my real life. I don’t want you to utter
anything about the 4th Ward. This Aika and the one living there are two completely different people. And I don’t want either
mentioned; Understand?”

“Very well. I understand.”

“Good...Understand that if you fail, there will be consequences.” I hated how easy it was to fall back on my training; the way my family
had raised me. How easy it was to threaten someone like that.

“Of course, madam. I would expect nothing less from a Kaneshiro.”

I could never let him know how much those words stung.



## ♥



“It's time.”

I waited in the car as Kazu got out. He moved to open my door, pausing to give me a moment to compose. I took a breath and steeled my
expression, thinking of the cold expression my mother had always given looking down at people from under eyelashes.

“Showtime.” I murmured before the door clicked open. Aika Kaneshiro stepped out; back straight and head held high; ice in her
expression. A woman who wasn’t me walked tall and proud; steady on high heels with swaying hips. Already I could picture the news
headline.

‘ Kogane no Shiro Owner and Wife Dead in Tragic Accident; Heir of Company Returns.’


Kazu held the door from the private underground parking lot, struggling to hold the heavy steel security door as he ushered me inside. It
had been ages since I’d been in this building; glancing around it looked just the same. It smelled just as antiseptic as I remembered.

“Kazu, did you make sure most of the staff were out today?”

“Already taken care of, Madam. Everyone non-essential are home today.”

We stepped into the elevator with a small portly man who was pressing buttons to go upwards. He did a double take when he saw me,
sputtering and sticking out a foot to catch the door.

“M-M-Ms. K-kaneshiro! W-what a surprise! What good luck—I was hoping to speak to you before the meeting!”

I glanced down at him, watching him closely with that icey expression on my face. I didn’t recognise him.
“This is the board's president. Mr. Watanabe.” Kazu supplied the name for me. I raised an eyebrow and kept staring down at the little
man until he shifted uncomfortably. Breaking eye contact I looked up to watch the numbers of the floor we were on rise.

“Very well.” I said simply, not giving him the time of day.

“I–W-well. Ms...I have a proposition you would be interested in hearing, young Miss!”

“I’m afraid you shall have to wait to hear my announcement while we are at the table with everybody else, Mr. Watanabe.”


DING . The elevator leveled off and I took the first step off, walking down the long hallway to the left, following my memory to the
board room. Behind me Kazu walked, staying to my right as my right hand man. I barely gave him a glance; happy when he very subtly
nodded his head.

Good. So far so good—

“Madam.” Kazu stepped forward, opening the double doors to the board room for me. I felt my breath hitch as I stared out across the
board of over 30 members. I glanced behind me, hearing the heavy breathing of the board director as he hurried to catch up with us. He
moved past and hurried to take his seat at the head of the table.

I raised a brow and moved, following the man to the plush chair. I stopped next to him and touched the back of the seat; staring down at
him. “You are in my seat, sir.”

“M-M–madam?”

Deep breath Aika. Opening my mouth I spoke loudly and clearly for all to hear; voice echoing off the marbled walls, floor and table.

“As of this moment. You are all relieved of your duties.”

The room was silent for only a moment before the yelling started. Complaints roared out as the men and women stood up in their chairs,
smacked the table with their fists and voiced their displeasure.
“You can’t do that! The shareholders need to hold a vote to—”

“You will find that as of this morning, I am the one in control of the company. I am the sole owner of the company and I’ve returned. In
the absence of a Kaneshiro, you lot have made attempts to sell off something that does not belong to you for a profit. — Kazu, if you
would. ”


The man stepped up close to my side, holding paperwork aloft. “Gentleman, ladies. You shall find the paperwork here and the details of
your severance. A vote of non-confidence was taken and all of you are expelled from this day forth.”

Mr. Watanabe choked and sputtered, his face turning red as he turned towards me  “You—you will regret this !!!” Without glancing at
him I sighed.
“Everyone, please leave. Save for the representatives for the contracts that we currently hold, or...those who were hoping to buy. I will
speak with them.”

I turned my head, looking at the small gathering of people on our left standing by the wall. Among them there were CCG representatives.
I glanced at their silver suitcases and frowned. “Kazu, were weapons not collected at the door?”

“I gave the order for them to be, however—” He trailed off and I understood. They hadn’t listened, or the CCG had insisted they kept them
on them.

I waited til the last of the board members had filed out before snapping my fingers: “Make sure security sees them out. I don’t want any
of them lingering where they don’t belong.”

“Yes Madam.”

“Now—” I waved a hand over the table. “You all may take a seat if you would like, however I will tell you that this will not take long. First
and foremost, I would like to express that there will be no weapons in this building. ”

“That being said, I shall keep this short. I will not be selling the company. In fact as we speak we are buying back shares and consolidating.
The Kogane no Shiro company will be shifting priorities. Kazu has the paperwork for you—”

He moved, calmly handing the paperwork to the CCG representatives. “As of this moment, our contract with the CCG is null and void.
The funding for this year shall be returned in full, but at this time your access to our research and development is revoked. The details of
which have all been taken care of and are in the paperwork being provided. A lawyer will be in contact shortly if there are any issues. You
may stay until the ending of the meeting if you’d like—”

Unlike the board of directors, the ones who had come from other companies—or in some cases the government did not scream or yell.
Some of them calmly filed out of the building while others stayed to see what was happening.

“---As for everyone else, a few of your companies have contracts that continue for a short time with us. We will continue to honor our
agreements, however...and at the end of the term and our obligations are complete they will not be renewed under their current
conditions.” I swallowed and took a breath.

“My parents created weapons. But that isn’t the sort of person I want to be. I want to create solutions and cures rather than poisons and
armaments. Organs for those who need them. Medicine that ordinary people can afford. Research to help those who have ROS. That is
now Kogane no Shiro ’s, my goal!”

I looked down at the table and frowned, closing my eyes. “I could have just taken the easy way out. Sold the company. But then I’d have
to watch as my name continued to be used on drugs that nobody can afford. Munitions that end up in the streets and kill children and
tear apart families. Poisons that end up in the water supply. And that’s not something I can accept.” Looking up I relaxed my face a little,
glancing over the ones who were left. “You may return to your company heads; inform them of what I plan to do. And I extend this
offer: I want to work with you; I want your help with the future. Make it something different. Because I don’t think we’ve gotten safer in
the last 20 years the way we have been doing things. For now, you are all dismissed. Kazu—Please. Give these ladies and gentlemen our
contact information. I think I've said all I need to.”

“Of course Madam.”

I heard a small clapping sound and looked up; as a few of the people who had gathered clapped their hands; smiles on their faces. A small
crowd approached the table and began speaking all at once; my head buzzed as they congratulated me and spoke rapidly in excited voices.


“I am excited to bring this news back to our head—”

“I like the direction—I’m sure Mr. Minoto will agree. He’s been wanting to work on stem cell organ transplants for years!”

“A brighter future—Maybe my baby sister can finally afford her medicine!”


“Right, right. Everyone please...Kazu here will be taking on the communications for the company. I’m sure we are about to get a lot of
them. I am excited that so many of you are excited for the new direction. And I hope that we might be able to work together on the new
future!”

I waited quietly as Kazu dealt with the rest of the crowd of investors, representatives and even a few CEO’s of different companies.
Behind the people who had been happy with the announcement had been a larger group that had stood quietly.

I never realized exactly how much sway my parents really had . I nibbled my lip and looked back out the large windows that gave me a
birds eye view of the city. I could even see the CCG building in the distance.




“Ms. Kaneshiro...?”

I jumped as someone near me spoke. Kazu was still busy with the dwindling crowd and hadn’t noticed them approaching either. I turned
and faced the CCG reps. I  did a quick look towards Kazu; nerves crawling in my stomach. But he was busy with the others.

“Your aid there seemed busy, I hoped you might be able to speak to us.”


I would be forced to face the CCG alone for the moment. Two of them, each holding their silver cases. I took a breath, reminding myself
that this wasn’t a fight .

“Of course; I apologize for all this being so sudden. I’m afraid I felt it necessary to make these changes as fast as possible...I’ve never saw
eye to eye with my parents' position of putting profit over people.”

The man representing the CCG was tall and thin, graying hair. His mouth was set in a thin frown. While beside him a shorter woman,
brown hair and unremarkable features; save for a friendly smile that never left her face. “I see, it comes as a surprise. The CCG has always
worked very closely with your parents. We will be in contact, perhaps we might even convince you that we want the same future. We
would be interested as well, in a cure . I think.”

“For the moment sir, I think I need to focus on getting my company back in shape; make it something that my parents never would have.
I appreciate you coming—” I held out my hand and smiled. “Perhaps in the future.”

Never. Never with them. Still, I smiled as I lied through my teeth and cursed them silently. Of course; that wouldn’t have been very
diplomatic to say out loud; would it?



## ♥


The sun had sunk under the horizon by the time I was done with everything. Greeted everyone. Answered questions. Given declarations
to so many people. In the end; more of the investors and would-be bidders were unhappy with me than those who liked my ideas. That
was to be expected since they had come here in hopes of buying out the company.

I sent Uta a text message, letting him know I would still be a little while since everything had taken much longer than I had expected. It
would still be hours before I managed to get home. And we had to make sure nobody followed me.

“You did well today, Madam. Much better than I expected.”

“Kazu, No need for the backhanded compliment. Say what you mean. Do you think you can handle it; head of communications? You’ll
be on the front lines. You saw how upset some of them were. I expect you to handle all that so it doesn't interfere with my real life.”

“Some of them were quite angry. But the news is breaking and I believe that the people will be on your side.“

I sure hope so.
I smiled at the memory of the woman’s face, one of the inventor's aids; she spoke about her little sister being able to get her medicine.
That would be nice, wouldn’t it?


“Kazu...what do you think about what I’m doing? Your honest opinion.”

The man paused, looking up from the paperwork strewn over the board table. He glanced around and then back up at me; sitting with
my legs draped over two chairs and sunk down into the squishy chair that the director had before me.

“....It is interesting Madam. Working for you is very different from working for your parents. I remember chasing you around the gardens
trying to get you back in the house; and how troublesome you made my job. But you’ve grown up. Still I’m not sure you realize how some
of your decisions may play out—” He glanced over the paperwork for the CCG and frowned.

“But...they are not without merit. You didn’t rush anything. It’s certainly more than I expected when Hiroshi contacted me. ”

He glanced up again, a thoughtful frown on his face. “...Forgive me the question Madam. But why do you dislike the CCG? From the
moment I mentioned them buying the company you seem staunchly opposed.”

“Like I said...I don’t like knowing my family's name is attached to weapons. Just the other month, you must have seen the fights in the
streets. The battles between Ghouls and Investigators are getting out of hand. They completely destroyed a whole street in Chiyoda...and
that’s just in the first ward. They fixed it in a week. The other wards are worse off because they don’t ever fix what they’ve broken. It’s left
to the people in the area to piece things back together. They don’t care if they break something in a ward like the 4th, because they don’t
even like looking at the 4th...and they don’t care about the citizens.”

“I see; I suppose your time out there has helped you see a point of view that not many of these people have. It may be difficult to convince
them. But I promise you, I shall try my best. It is what you are paying me for afterall.”

## ♥

The meeting and acting like that had taken everything out of me for the day. When I finally returned home well after sunset I was
dragging my feet across Uta’s shop floor. He greeted me casually. His ghoulish eyes peered at me from the couch when I finally pushed
open the apartment door.


“Ai-chan...It’s late.”

“Hum...” I murmured softly. I managed to only take off the shoes which left red blisters on my feet and stumble my way to him. I
reached for my earrings; pulling out the red gems and dropping them on the coffee table. Next came off the necklace; large and gaudy.
Worth thousands I was told. I dropped it haphazardly. I collapsed on the couch next to him, moving until I could curl with my head in his
lap. I closed my eyes and finally let my body relax completely.

“...You’re still in your suit.” That I was. But now I was finally safe to completely relax; and I didn’t want to get up again. My body ached
worse than after even the most harsh lessons with Renji. I’d been tense as if I were about to fight all day long.

“...I’m so tired...”

“Bad?”

“...No. More to do later. But not bad . Kazu will handle everything else for a little while. He accepted the job I gave him...So we are free
for at least the weekend.”

The ghoul’s hand gently laid on my head, pulling my hair out of it’s bun and then stroking his fingers through the locks. “I spoke to
Renji-kun. He’ll come with us...Itori too.”

“Itori...?” I questioned groggily; the feeling of fingers through my hair was almost enough to send me to sleep right there and then. “Why
does she want to come...?

“Bored.” He answered softly, eyes on the Tv. The news was playing. I blinked a few times, realizing what he was watching. What he must
have been watching all day. Unlike most nights where the biggest news was the CCG or ghouls; today had been my company. Me.  “We
wouldn’t want that. You’ve probably seen this all day. It must be weird...right?”

“That’s not you...”

I watched a few seconds of ‘my’ appearance on tv. A woman walking from a darkly tinted the car to the building past reporters in the
midday sun. I didn’t recognise the woman who was on the Tv screen. Kazu had picked her out for the job. She had darker reddish plum
hair than me. But she was about the same height and weight. I had to admit that my right hand man had done a good job making sure the
press didn’t get very good angles for their cameras; they never saw the woman's face. Most people won’t realize I arrived long before the
decoy.

“She looks similar, but not too much like me. That’s kind of the point...” The news continued, panning back to the reporters who
continued to ramble on before they flashed to the recording of Kazu making an announcement.

“No longer will this company be working towards weapons and yearly skyrocketing profit. After years of profit, it’s time that Kogane no Shiro
gives back. To help move us forward together, we will be focusing on medical research and development; some real treatments for the things
that ail us. Medicines are expensive; so much so that ordinary people such as those sitting at home watching from a screen right now can’t
afford them! Organs grown in a lab are effective, but they aren’t being developed at the speed that is necessary for anybody who needs them to
get. The things that keep us healthy shouldn’t be a privilege for only the wealthy; they are for everyone no matter who they are. That is now our
goal moving forward.”

I smiled gently as I listened to the speech. As it drew to a close I spoke along with it.

“Years of making weapons hasn’t made the world safer; it’s time we try something else...”
“Years of making weapons hasn’t made the world safer; it’s time we try something else...He’s a good puppet. Don’t you think so?”


I glanced up, meeting red eyes as they stared down at me; blinking as he realized that the speech had been mine. I rolled so I laid on my

back, facing upwards. “...Maybe in the end it’ll just be hope-filled propaganda. But...at least I did what I planned to. It took five months
of planning, but as of today the CCG don’t have Kogane no Shiro in their pocket anymore...and my face isn’t known to most everyone.
To everyone else on the outside; Ms. Kaneshiro is that girl.”

## ♥


I managed to get up and get something to eat. Fruit; something easy and I didn’t need to cook it. I shuffled off to bed shortly after,
stripping off clothing and crawling into the cocoon of scent in my underwear. Uta hadn’t come to bed yet when I finally drifted off. But I
could still hear that re-recording of the news playing in the other room.

works out without blowing up in her face!

## Chapter 51: Weekend Away
## Notes:
Excited for this one :3
