Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 51: Weekend Away

Two days Later: Saturday Morning

In the morning I awoke cocooned in strong arms; held to Uta’s chest as he breathed slow and deep. I moved my head, wiggling until I
could press my ear to his chest and listen to the sound of his heartbeat. He lay with his chin nested on the crown of my head.
“...mmm...Ai...you awake?”

I smiled as I listened to him speak. It sounded strange with one ear pressed to his chest; listening to the deeper timber as it hummed past
his ribcage. “Mmmm...”

“Renji’s going to pick us up later...”

Right. The weekend. Stargazing and relaxing in the wild. Meeting with my uncle.

“Did you tell him to pack up some food? Same with Itori if she’s coming...I know you don’t especially need to eat every single day, but if
you don’t eat something he’ll probably insist you eat something you can’t eat.”

“Yeah. They’ll bring their own. I promise I won’t eat your uncle...”

I held tight to my ghoul and giggled as he joked. “Good...at least I didn’t have to tell you not to this time.”

The bed was hard to get out of. Normally he was happy to let me stay in bed; teased me about it. But thankfully Uta seemed determined
to get me out of it today. He nudged me along as I struggled to stay awake in the early morning. I showered, washed my face with cold
water and when I came out of the bathroom there was a pot of coffee already brewing and a bowl of fruit ready for me. The very top fruit
was a small piece of apple; carved like a flower.

I popped a grape into my mouth and mumbled: “You know, if I’m not mistaken I think you are excited..”

“...I am.”

That was a surprise; I had known he was happy enough to come along. It was something new. Something interesting. Something to cure
his boredom for a while. It’s not like he left the city often. It’s not where his food was. Or his business. Or his group of friends. So that was
understandable if he’d never left.

“You’re excited for stargazing?”

“I want to meet your uncle...Renji and Itori too.”

“Yeah? He’s a cool guy for sure. The best of my family. I wouldn't have expected you’d be that excited though.”

“I’m curious what he’s like....since he’s related to you.”

Oh. My lips parted as I could only open my mouth; words caught in my throat. I’d forgotten. Trying to think of a single Ghoul that I
knew that could have introduced me to their family; and the only one that came to mind was Touka. And that was only because Renji
was her uncle. But besides that? Uta couldn’t show me off to a pair of parents and tell them about me or how we met. There were no
relatives for me to compare who he looked most like. There was nobody but his friends who could tell me happy or embarrassing
childhood memories.

None of them could; could they?

“...yeah. He’s...he’s my fathers brother. You’ll like him I think. He’s like—A more outgoing Renji? If Renji liked to talk to people and
joke around more.”


That definitely got his attention; Uta stared at me with those wide eyes of his. “Really?”
“Yeah. Like I told you before; you’ll like him. Maybe he’ll get Renji talking and they’ll be two of them, right?”

I went to the fridge, picking out things to pre-make some PB&J Sandwiches. I made a couple and then packed them into the cooler with
Uta’s food, putting the ziplocked sandwiches on top of his tupperware of unidentifiable meat. Honestly it looked like we were heading
out for a picnic.

Bjorn would be staying behind. I’d arranged it with the manager and Hinami. The little girl would be watching over the dog; and the
manager would be watching over the little girl for the weekend. It would work out well—and while the trip didn’t turn out to be just Uta
and I it was still a trip away from most everything.

I heard a set of quick honks from outside and jumped up; shoveling the rest of my fruit into my mouth quickly. “Renji’s here—Bjorn!
Come on pup! We gotta get you to Hinami! Grab your leash!”
I rinsed the bowl and did a quick scrub over it before putting it in the drying rack to be put away after we got back. Hurrying, I picked up
Bjorn’s bag which held everything he might need for a stay with the little ghoul girl. Food, a brush. His leash. Plenty of treats and a bone
for him to chew on.

“Uta, can you get—” I glanced over my shoulder to see that he’d already lugged the cooler over one shoulder with our bags hanging from
his other hand. Strong. “—our bags. I guess you beat me to it. Got everything you need?”

“Yeah.”
“Right, time to go then!” I walked Bjorn out the door and waited for Uta to lock the shop behind us.

I walked around the corner of the small alley road with a small bounce in my step. Renji’s most recent beat up abandoned car sat by the
curb with what looked like a few minor dents in the front. “Hey, Renji-kun! We just need to stop at Anteiku for a minute to drop off this
fluff-ball.”

“Right, get in— Uta. There’s room in the trunk. ” I smiled and gave a little salute before hopping into the back seat and Bjorn followed
after. A few moments later Uta pushed in after the dog, squeezing into the back of the car.

“You alright back there?” I heard Itori giggle as I was being squished up with Bjorn; I got the dog's breath while Uta got flacked in the
head by his tail. I loved on the pup the whole trip to the cafe though. It wasn’t often we separated; so Bjorn wouldn’t be altogether happy.
But I knew that at the very least Hinami would take great care of him. At the cafe I piled out of the car, leading Bjorn with me inside.
Renji got out as well to head inside, walk behind the counter and into the back where he could get to the freezers.

“Bjorn!” I turned and grinned as Hinami came out of the back room, arms wide to hug onto the chest of the huge dog.
“Alright, Hinami! Big job for you; you sure you can take care of him for the weekend for me? I brought everything he could possibly
need with me. Right here—” Handing off the bag to the kid, she beamed up at me.
“I can! He’ll keep me and Hetare company!”

Alright. With that settled. “Thank you again boss, I don’t think we’d all survive squished into that car with him too.”

“It is not a problem Ms. Aika. Please, give my regards to your Uncle.”

“Of course, Sir! I’ll be back for my Monday shift! You have my number, if anything goes wrong. Give me a call right away!”

Renji emerged from the door behind the counter holding a cooler. Presumably, he had gotten some food for himself. “Got everything
you need?”

“Yeah.”


When I jumped back into the car I glanced at Uta who had his elbow on the door frame, chin in hand. His eyes watched as Humans
walked by; clueless to what the cafe really was.

The car shook as Renji closed the back trunk and then got into the front. He put on his seat belt, restarted the car and started driving.
“So...Where exactly is this place?”

“You can take Route 20 for most of the way. He lives kinda near Aokigahara! Once we get closer I can tell you turn by turn, but you’ll be
able to see Mt Fuji really really well! We should get a picture of all of us with it in the background!”

Renji glanced up at the rearview mirror, met my eye for a moment and then looked back at the road. “Near Aokigahara huh...?”

“Yeah...Hey guys. Before we go...”

“Something wrong, Aika-chan?” Itori turned in her seat to look at me, her eyebrows furrowed.

“I think you’ll all like him...I hope. Please, please, please don’t be mad at me for not mentioning this before—!” I tried to smile, but it was
awkward and strained. I really should have said something earlier. We couldn’t go without them knowing; it would be cruel to drag them
out to the woods without saying anything.

“—but there’s just one itty-bitty little thing about my uncle I didn’t mention? He...Well he used to be in the CCG—Ages, and ages ago.” I
squeaked out as all three Ghouls stared at me.

“Aika! That’s kind of a big deal!” Itori said, aghast. Of course they’d be uncomfortable with this.

“That is why I’m mentioning it now. Before we left. We could go home if you want. Forget about the trip...But I don’t think it will be a
problem. He left them over years ago. He never talked about it. I only knew 'cause’ the staff liked to talk about rumors. They said he quit
out of the blue and moved out to the wilderness all of a sudden. He never ever talks about it...or Ghouls at all for that matter. I can almost
guarantee it won’t come up.”

“He quit?”

“Yeah...I think I remember a little. He used to live in the city back then. When I was really small he came and lived with us at my parents
estate. But not too long after that he disappeared. Moved away from Tokyo and I didn’t see him again until I was almost ten...

The silence in the car was loud as I fiddled my fingers in my lap. “I’ll still go.” Uta said softly, making me glance up. The car started up
and Renji pulled away from the curb.
“...We better get going. It’s over two hours to get there...”

## ♥

I watched the city get further and further behind us and as we got closer and closer to the large mountain I swayed side to side; humming
along with the music that Renji had turned on about an hour into the ride. The tape wasn’t his of course. It had belonged to the human
that the car belonged to before Renji found it. But it was nice to have regardless — whoever they had been, they had been listening to the
perfect road trip music.

“Right here is the turn—” I finally pointed off onto a dirt road, leading through some thick trees on either side. Renji shot me a look
before he took the turn, driving slowly as the road became bumpy and rugged. I continued to direct him as it took a winding way until we
came to a small parking spot with some picnic tables.

“Right, and here’s where we park. The rest of the way is on foot.”


“Aika-chan...how far is your uncle's house? This looks a bit abandoned. Are you sure anybody has been here recently.” Itori looked
around, staring at the old picnic tables with what looked like an inch of moss and lichen growing on them.

“Yeah, he said likes it like this. Less people bother him out here. It’s a little bit of a hike though. Got your walking shoes on Itori?” I
laughed at her expression and added: “At least it’s not boring, right?”

Hopping out of the car I stretched my arms up over my head and groaned; breathing in fresh air. I walked to the back of the car as Renji
hit the button to open the back. He reached for his and Itori’s cooler first. I grabbed my duffle bag with our change of clothing and the
rolled up hammock.  I’d brought along one for the night's stay because out here I had always preferred to sleep up off the ground. I
wasn’t sure what shape my old hammock was in since it had been a few years. Plus, that one had barely held me. This was big enough that
Uta could sleep next to me in it!

With everything unloaded from the car I turned and happily started the march into the woods, following a very lightly traveled path. A
path that was only occasionally marked by symbols carved into trees or hanging baubles from the limbs. I hopped over fallen trees with
gitty haste, occasionally glancing behind me to make sure the three Ghouls hadn’t gotten lost. “Don’t worry...it’s only about a thirty
minute hike!~”

True to my word, as thirty minutes was closing in I could smell smoke and wood; cooking meat over a fire.
“Told you it wasn’t far!” I sped up, hurrying forward as I ducked under a branch. On the other side I finally spotted my Uncle’s cabin.
Small. Humble. One room cabin with moss growing thick on the roof. The wood on the outside matched the surrounding woods and
blended in, but I couldn't miss the man sitting on a half log in front of a fire pit. He was a big man; muscled and above average height. He
wore a tank top in the July heat. When he spotted me he stood up, brushed off his pants and walked a few paces closer, arms open.

“ Uncle! ” I shouted and the man grinned back. I picked up my pace.

“Aika... wait —”

Ignoring Uta I ran forward, dropped my dufflebag and jumped to the hug as he swung me around in a tight circle.
“I missed you! I haven't seen you in years —!!!” I looked up at him when my feet were back on the ground and scoffed. “You look exactly
the same! Maybe just a couple extra grays.”

“...and you Glowbug—you look happier. And your hair got long.” I watched how he looked upwards, eyes flicking between the three
others who had come with me. For a moment I thought I saw him tense; but then it was gone like a trick of light.  “...And...who would
your friends be Glowbug?” I smiled at the nickname, one he used since I was very little.

“These are my friends. Renji and Itori—and that’s Uta.” I pointed to each one so he didn’t get mixed up. Then with a warm smile I
added: “Uta is my boyfriend. I wanted to bring him out to meet you. I thought he should meet my family.”

“ Boyfriend... ? Are you old enough for one of those?” I lightly punched my uncle's arm, pouting at the teasing he was immediately
starting. “ Staup!!! Uncle please — Guys! This joker is my Uncle. The one and only Hiroshi Kaneshiro. ”

“And the world is glad for it! Imagine if there were more than one?” Hiroshi chuckled. “Imagine how much trouble two of me could get
into?”

“Still only half as much as me!” I countered with a smirk. I turned to look back at Uta again. It was just then that I realized that the three
Ghouls were kind of far away. Not to mention I could see Renji and Itori’s eyes fixed upon Hiroshi like he had two heads. Uta’s
expression was as inscrutable as ever. Maybe it was because of the whole CCG thing? Or maybe it was just hard to adjust not being around
the forth ward; he was feeling out of place? That might make him put up his walls again; his social mask.

“Aika...this is your uncle? Is he related to you...?” Renji asked, his shoulders looking tense.


“By blood.” Hiroshi answered calmly, picking up a stick to poke at the fire as he took his seat back by the fire.
“What Renji-kun? Can’t see the resemblance?” Leaning closer to my uncle I flashed a grin, flexing my arm to try and match the man's
musculature. “We look practically like twins!”

“Your mother always did say you looked more like me than your father. Your father was not amused.” He chuckled and looked back at my
friends again. Nodding at the seats around the fire.

“Come on, settle in. If I know my niece any she’ll wanna stay the night at least. There’s plenty of room around the fire.”

I went to grab my dropped bags. Maybe if I just ignored how awkward it was, everyone would settle down and relax if they just had time?
Hauling the bags closer to the fire I dropped them down and sat on a log near my uncle. Patting the log I was on I called out: “Uta.
Seriously. Come sit—We can set up the hammock later if you’re tired?”

Finally the others came closer, uneasily sitting around the fire. Renji and Itori sat further away while Uta dropped the cooler and took a
spot right next to me, shoving himself between me and my uncle. The ghoul watched Hiroshi as he poked at the fire and adjusted the
wood.

“So—How long have you had a boyfriend, Glowbug?”

“Um...Six or seven-ish months?” I answered sheepishly as he actually pouted. He kept poking at the fire.
“Six or seven months? And you didn’t think to tell your uncle.”

I laughed. “Well, it’s not like you ever come to the city and it’s not the easiest thing to come see you. You used to only come out here
during the weekends and you stayed with us—I saw you more often back then!”

“Right...Back then.”

“Yeah...but that was a really long time ago. You could come back, you know...?”

“I’m surprised you even remember that; You were five when I moved out here permanently.” Hiroshi said, avoiding my question and
setting down the stick he’d been turning coals with and reached to turn over the meat cooking over the fire.

“I definitely remember when you taught me to hunt and fence. You know, I was surprised that you hired Kazu to help me with
everything—But if you wanted to come back to the city; I could get you a place again? You’d be closer and I could visit more often.”


“I can’t Glowbug...” I frowned and my shoulders sagged. Can’t? I’d hoped I could convince him to at least have a temporary place in the
city; then he could meet the rest of my friends. Yoshimura. I could make him coffee!
“You could at least come visit...you’d really love my coworkers!”

“Glow, you know I’m not welcome in Tokyo...”

“But—I mean. I thought since ...”
I glanced down at the ground, furrowing my brows in confusion. I thought since my parents were dead it would be okay; it’s not like they
could keep him away or forbid him from seeing me anymore.

“—Where are you living now Glowbug, and where'd you meet your friends?” He changed the topic and quickly glanced at Uta. “I’m
curious where you found your boyfriend...I’m not surprised you like him. He’s exactly the type that would have annoyed your mother
and my brother.” Which was to say, exactly my type.



“It’s the tattoos. Definitely the tattoos!” I joked, leaning my weight into Uta and bumping his arm. It still didn’t make him break his gaze
at my uncle and I was beginning to wonder if he’d even blinked since we got here. “I met Uta first, he’s got a mask shop right down the
way from where I used to live. I’m still in the Fourth though. So...um. I also live with him now. Renji and Itori are his friends and he
introduced us. But they’re great—all my friends are. And now I work at a coffee shop in the 20th ward. Right now someone’s watching
Bjorn there for me. He’s too big for all of us in the car.”


“That lil’ must have gotten massive, right? A coffee shop huh. In that 20th ward...I can’t imagine that—Did you say you live with him...?
Together?” He sounded doubtful. Incredulous, as though the idea was completely ridiculous.

“Yeah Uncle. I’m not a kid anymore—And Renji’s been helping train me—” I flexed, showing off the work I'd put in.
“I noticed...I also noticed you’ve got some new scars too. Everything okay kid?”

Shiiiiiiiit. I jerked my arms down, hiding the scars by tugging my shirt sleeve back down over the forearm where I’d been hit some
months back. “That—oh...those are...an accident?”

“...An accident. What sort of accident? Wouldn’t have anything to do with your boyfriend here would it, or your training?” Watching his
eyes fall on Uta and then to Renji. I winced and held up my hands to defend them both.
“Nonono! Nothing to do with them! It’s no big deal. I promise...They’d never—”

This was not going as I thought it would. Uta, Renji and Itori were being too quiet and standoffish and Uncle was watching them closely too.
Despite his attempts to seem relaxed and ask about my life; there was something clearly wrong here. Just what the hell is going on? Was it all
because of the CCG? That explained Uta and the others - but why was uncle acting like this?

“Um...you know. After that car ride I’m going to get something to eat. We brought our own food Uncle, so you don’t have to worry
about it. I’m not sure when you last hunted so I didn’t want to put that on you since I didn’t give you any warning we were coming.”

“Sure Glowbug. I’d offer you some food, but this is the last of the deer...”

“It’s no problem! I prepared!”  I leaned forward and picked out a sandwich from the cooler that Uta had set near our feet. I opened the
ziplock and took a bite out of the sandwich; glancing from person to person as an uncomfortable quiet settled over the small camp.

I ate my food in silence, trying not to get sick as the atmosphere got worse and worse by the moment. I only got through half my
sandwich before putting it back in the bag and back in the cooler.

“So...I’m...I’m going to set up the hammock now before it gets too late, Okay?” I stood, leaning down to kiss Uta on the cheek. His
expression strangely didn't change even a little bit; not a hint of a smile. Normally it didn’t matter if he was in a mood, he’d still at least
twitch.

“Everybody play nice...” I mumbled; grabbing the folded up hammock and walked by my uncle, shoving his shoulder playfully as I passed
him. “That means you too. They’re important to me.”

Picking a tree by the side of the cabin I tried to listen to see if any of them started a conversation or tried to speak to each other; and
yet...no. Quiet. Crackling fire. The familiar smell of meat cooking. The buzz of insects in the forest around us. I had hammered in one
side of the hammock into the tree when Hiroshi finally sighed loudly; rubbing the back of his neck.

“Well...This isn’t going well, is it? Not exactly what I expected when she brought a boy...”

I held the other side of the  hammock in my hands, turning halfway to see what he was talking about. “—I certainly didn’t expect
Glowbug to bring three Ghouls with her to visit.”


“Hmm?” I swallowed hard and glanced quickly between everybody. No, no, no.

“Uh...H-hey, what makes you say that? They’re definitely not—” I was cut off as everyone started moving all of a sudden.

In a blink of an eye Uta stood and had begun moving towards me. My uncle was on his feet. Stepping between Uta and me with an arm
held out; pushing me back and protectively caging me behind him, stopping me from moving towards my boyfriend. Renji grabbed Uta’s
arm to hold him back and Itori had gotten up and backed up a few yards away, watching from a distance with a frown on her face.

“Get Ai-chan back to the car—” Uta growled.
“Uta wait—” Renji said; calmly.

“Stop! Stop...wait—Uta please. It’s just...a misunderstanding. Uncle. Stop.” I said, grasping onto the sleeve of his shirt and trying to pull
him back a bit. Away from Uta.

“Glowbug...Go inside—Your friends aren’t Human.”

His statement knocked the breath out of me and my heartbeat jumped to my throat. Physically I felt sick. He knew. He knew and he
wasn’t reacting well. I know how it ends up if people don’t react well—

“I—I know!” Finally I admitted it. “I know Uncle. But they’re fine—I’m not in any danger! I promise! I promise! So please....we can sit
down and talk about this!” I had to try and work out damage control. How to make sure my friends didn’t kill my uncle, and how to
make sure my uncle didn’t call the CCG.

“You know?” The arm that Hiroshi Kaneshiro had thrown up protectively in front of me fell a few inches. I pushed past his arm and
darted towards Uta, using the shock as an opening. Grasping onto his shirt I held tight; as if holding onto the ghoul would stop him from
doing anything too rash.

“I know. I’m sorry.  I thought...just for a weekend—”  We could have a nice normal family outing where my friends and boyfriend could
meet my family. “—We could just...be normal? I know you used to be in the CCG— But—”

“Aika, that’s not how he knew about us.” Renji said softly from my side. He wasn’t holding Uta back anymore as the goth wound his
arms around my waist. His chin leaned on my shoulder as he watched Hiroshi carefully.




“You didn’t know that your uncle was a Ghoul. Did you?”

## Notes:
Okay, so I really wanna know if anybody expected that---and at what point did you start to suspect?

## Chapter Text

## Chapter 52: Family Secrets/ Secret Families


“...what? No...he’s—I...I would have known...?” I turned in Uta’s arms, trying to look at my uncle. He met my eyes for a few
moments and then glanced away without denying it. “Yeah. Well, We Kaneshiro’s have got some pretty nasty family secrets.”

“W-how...?” I choked out. How was he a Ghoul? How long? How could I have not noticed? I’d visited so much! I’d known him
my whole life!

“Alright, alright. Can we all sit down? Uta, was it?—I’m not going to eat her. She’s my niece for heaven's sake. You can trust
me not to harm her. You on the other hand, I don’t trust. So get your mouth away from her neck boy...”

I tensed and frowned; opening my mouth. “Uncle...stop—”
Uta held onto me still; tight around the waist. As my uncle complained about it, he slid his mouth to my neck and licked up
the side of my throat in a very Uta like fashion.

I watched my uncle’s face, as his eyebrows scrunched up and his expression turned angry. He took half a step forward; his
eyes going ghoulish red on black. The change confirmed with finality that he was in fact a Ghoul.

“U-uta...N-not now. Please. This is not really the moment to be joking around like that.”
He made a soft growling noise in the back of his throat before going back to resting his head on my shoulder.


Hiroshi closed his eyes, took a breath and once he opened them again they were their normal hue. He moved to sit down first
- staring at the fire. “ ...I’ll explain. If we all just. Sit down. This isn’t how I’d have liked to have this discussion Aika...but it
seems there’s not much of a choice.”


Renji and Itori moved to sit back down first, looking to Uta to do the same. Slowly the goth ghoul unwound his arms and sat
back down. He pulled me with him to sit in his lap; not giving me a choice in the matter.



“Uncle?” My voice cracked a bit and he smiled sadly.

“Right. Glowbug, I am truly sorry for keeping it from you...Your mother insisted. That woman didn’t want you to know
about Ghouls at all if she could have helped it. I practically had to blackmail her to make it so you could visit once in a
while—would have been a shame if anybody found out about me, right?”

“So you are related to her by blood?” Renji asked again.

“Yes. She is my family. By blood. Her father was my brother. Which means....there’s Ghoul in the family. You’re looking at
the Kaneshiro family's biggest family secret. And they tried their damndest to bury it. It would have been terrible for the
business to have a brother that turned ghoul. It would have caused a panic internally, not to mention for the public. Nobody
would have trusted the company if it got out that its owners could suddenly turn Ghoul.”

“Are—does that mean...he’s a one-eyed Ghoul like Kaneki...?” I muttered; thinking of the boy and his singular ghoul strange
eye that he kept hidden.

“Nothing as fancy as that—I know what you're talking about though. It’s hard to get news out here, but there was that kid
that was in some accident a while ago, right? I’m not like that—You might call me a ‘late bloomer’. I turned Ghoul more than
20 years ago. When you were still just a lil’ baby Glowbug. I worked for the CCG for years, but when my RC numbers
started to climb...well you can imagine how happy they were about that.”

That explained why he couldn’t come back to the city. If he went back they’d hunt him down.

The ghoul near my shoulder leaned his face into my neck and whispered. “...He’s been a Ghoul most of your life.”

“It took a while to dig up the dirt on our family. But in some records they forgot to destroy I found a woman on your fathers
side was a Ghoul. And as it turns out, those genes are aggressive. Almost self-cannibalistically so. Never did figure out how,
but something triggered them and the rate that my numbers rose was too fast to stop it. Your father started taking RC
suppressants as a precaution as soon as my numbers were getting dangerously high. He avoided ‘going Ghoul’, but I wasn’t
so lucky. I quit—er fled my job and for a while I stayed with them; kept away from the public hidden while your father had
those people in the lab working on all sorts of things. Trying to stall it as long as possible and trying to reverse what happened
to me. Your mother was worried about you. So when you were a young child, they used to test your level almost every day.
When you were real small—”

Hiroshi motioned with his hand, nearly just above his knee. “You’d come to me crying to me that your fingertips hurt
because of all the needles they kept taking blood with. Have you had your RC levels tested recently by Glowbug?”

“I...remember that.” I remembered crying my heart out as I was held tight by the wrist as my body wiggled trying to get away.
I would scream at the top of my lungs. There would be a sharp pain and then I was released with a bleeding finger.

“T-they weren’t too high. Just—” I swallowed as my voice cracked. “Just a little over normal.”

“Just over normal? So low 600’s then?”


“690.” Uta replied when my mouth wouldn’t work.

“690. It’s a little high...Have you been testing it regularly?”

“Every...every once in a while. It’s only gone up around 20 points in the last five months. Back in January it was 675.”

My uncle considered and then exhaled what sounded like a relieved sigh. “20 points in a few months isn’t bad. As long as it
doesn't accelerate you should be alright kid. I wish I remembered what they were when you were a kid. I want to say they
were high back then too. But I can’t be sure. Your mother kept me away as much as possible—As if I’d hurt you. Or I was
infectious.” He sighed, eyes sad as he watched the flames lick across the meat over the fire.

I jolted as my uncle suddenly clapped his hands together and looked over the group. “Well. Since that’s out of the way—
How about dinner?” He reached and picked it up, biting the meat off the poker and swallowed.


## ♥

The Ghouls ate quietly.  Renji and Itori ate their food raw as always, while Uta pulled out his meals which I had pre-cooked
for him. From across the fire Hiroshi raised his head and seemed curious.

“Hey kid—what are you eating?”

Uta had taken off his sunglasses; propping them up on his head. He stared at my uncle blankly. “....kid?”

“Yeah, that’s my kid niece you’re dating. That makes you a kid too.---Anyway, did you cook that?”

Flawed as his approach was, my uncle was actually trying to be friendly with Uta. “...Ai-chan cooked it for me.”

“You cooked him food?”

“Yeah. Um...one day I asked if it were possible. And he was curious so he tried it. Once in a while I cook for him—but he’s
really terrible at cooking. So he’d burn it if he tried for himself.” I was still processing so my laugh felt stiff.

“Huh, I didn't think anybody else would like it that way...”

Hiroshi took another bite out of the meat he had cooked over the fire. It couldn’t be deer like he had said before - and he
stayed out in the woods by himself. So—who was it? He noticed my staring and looked away.

“It makes sense now why you chose to live here. Next to the forest.” Renji mentioned, looking out into the forest.

“Does it? Suppose’ it depends on who you ask. But...people—Humans come here to die quite often. It’s not hard to find
food.” Hiroshi took another bite of the meat, finishing it off. “It’s the only way I could stand myself. Keep some kind of
humanity...”

“....Of course. Aokigahara—the sea of trees.” It made sense now, he lived so close to what some people called the ‘Suicide
Forest’. That meant that he ate like the Ghouls at Anteiku!

“Uh...so when I was a kid—We ate together and—” I must have looked green in the face because my uncle’s eyes went wide.


“Oh no Glowbug—You never ate anybody! I promise!!! I never would have let you–” He lowered his hands and chuckled.
“I admit I did have to throw up a lot of deer though. I always ate after you went to bed...”

I relaxed a bit, leaning into Uta for the support. My sandwiches went untouched. There was no way I could have kept them
down.

“I planned on telling you when you came out. I just didn’t expect—” He glanced at the others. “Company...I wanted to tell
you that it would be okay. About watching your RC levels. All you have to do is tell Kazu you need tests and suppressants.
He’ll know what you need and be able to get it for you. You’ll never have to worry about turning out like me.”

Suppressants. To keep from turning into a Ghoul? Family secrets? Secret parts of my family that they tried to bury? It was
bad enough to have such a shady company to deal with; now there was this?!

“He knows...about all this? —I...I’m...sorry. My head kind of hurts. I think I’m going to lay down...”

“Sure Bug—go on. I’ll just....get to know your friends. We can talk about it later. — Hey bug?”

I wiggled from Uta’s arms pausing only to look up at my uncle again. “Yeah?”
“...I’m really happy to see you kiddo...”

I smiled and went to him, leaning down to hug him. He reached up and wrapped a single arm around me, patting my back.
“Go take a nap kiddo. There’s some Tylenol in the cabin. Go grab some if you need it.”

“Thanks...I missed you too.” I stepped around him, pausing between going back to the hammock or grabbing the Tylenol. In
the end I went for the cabin, pushing open the door and heading in. It was a sparse building. He had lived simply since
coming out here. The room had furniture that he’d built himself. A bed, a desk, a couple simple chairs and a dresser. He had
some paperwork stacked up, and a laptop sitting on the desk. It hadn’t been there last time and I doubted that he had any
internet out here since there wasn’t even electricity. It looked like he had a solar powered charger for it.

I opened the bottom drawer to the desk where he used to keep the medicine and pulled out the bottle of Tylenol, popping it
in my mouth and swallowing it dry.

I put the bottle back and took another quick look around. I hesitated for only a moment before I began to snoop.

Pulling open drawer after drawer—looking around to see if I found anything new or different. I wish I hadn’t when I came
across a stack of Id cards. I dropped them back into the drawer and closed it.

I looked up at my uncle's map of the area. It was nailed to the wall. Covered in colorful tacks.
When I was a kid I thought it was when we went hunting, so he’d know where he had trapped things but now seeing where
the hundreds of tacks were located on the map I realized they must have been the places where he got his food.

Each one saved on the board—Ids kept in his drawer. Maybe...So he wouldn’t forget?

I turned and left the cabin, quietly closing the door behind me. Outside the Ghouls were talking now, pausing only when
they noticed I had returned: “Hey there Glowbug, you found the Tylenol alright?”

“Yeah–thanks.”


“They were telling me about your training. You’ll have to show me your progress later! After your head feels better—go rest.
I’ll keep em’ entertained while you sleep.”

After knocking the other anchor into a tree I crawled in, wrapping the fabric around me as I hung from the tree; watching
the firelight through the sheets.

“SO! Anybody like to sing? I got some songs I know!” I smiled faintly to myself, curling up so my back was to the fire as he
began to strum and play: ‘Cat’s in the Cradle’.

Right, I hadn’t warned them about that either, did I? He really loved those old American oldies.
They could suffer for a little while, just until I could clear my head.

At some point I did manage to fall asleep to some softly strung song. The singing rocking me off to sleep like years past when
he’d sing me to sleep near the fire.

## ♥

“Hey Glowbug? You should get something to eat lil’ bug.” I blinked and yawned.

For a moment I forgot when or where I was. Staring up at my uncle as he peeked into my hammock with a gentle smile. It
could have all been a dream...

“It’s getting dark and I’m running out of music...if you sleep all day you’ll be up all night.” Then softer he whispered in a
hushed tone: “Your boyfriend is getting anxious...I think. It’s really hard to tell. Does his face ever change?”

I scoffed and then started giggling, laughing until tears started to well up in my eyes. Same old uncle. “Yeah, yeah...I’ll be up
in a second.”

“Alright, you know I just remembered. I got something—hold on.” My uncle disappeared from my view and I rolled til I
could get out of the hammock, landing on my feet and stretching.

I glanced towards the fire and slowly made my way over to sit by Uta once more.

“Did he bother you guys too much with the music?”

“No. It’s nice...he talked a lot about you...” I felt my face heat up; suddenly worried about what he could have said while I
was out of it.

“Oh...ha...did he?”

“He calls you Glowbug because you liked to light things on fire. And play with sparklers?” I smiled sheepishly and opened
my mouth to defend myself.

“Alright here they are—they’re still in date. I checked.” My uncle came back out of his cabin with white and blue box with
bold red text written on the front. I stared at him incredulously, my eyes wide as I recognised the box he was holding.

“...You got Twinkies? Seriously! How long have you had these? I haven't been here in years!” And he clearly couldn't eat
them himself. They also weren’t easy to get in Japan. Not unless you found a specialty store.


“...Well.” He smiled sheepishly and glanced off; rubbing the back of his neck. “...I always keep them around for you. When
one box goes bad I make sure to get another. You know...Just in case you came and visited? They’re the banana creme...” My
favorite flavor of them.

He had always been waiting for me to visit? All this time. “Sorry uncle, I just—”

“You're busy. I know kid—don’t sweat it.” He set his hand on my head and ruffled my hair as I squirmed and complained
about it. “Oh—also these!” He pulled some little sticks from his pocket and held them out. My face lit up as I saw what they
were!

“OH these!”

Going to Uta I set down the twinkie box on the cooler and held the sticks with a grin on my face. “What are those, Ai-
chan...?”

“Sparklers!” I pushed one into Uta’s hands and tossed another two to Itori and Renji. I leaned forwards, let the tip get licked
by the flame and pulled back — watching the end light up and begin to send harmless sparks through the air. I watched,
transfixed on the shining spark as it burnt down to the end.

“And that’s why I call her Glowbug!~” My uncle laughed aloud, pointing out my face. “We should all count ourselves lucky
she’s not a lil’ pyro. Although there was that one time—”

“That was an accident! And I was 10!” I sputtered, glancing away from the sparkler and flushing pink. “You don’t need to
bring up embarrassing stories!”

“You were 11 actually. You were running around with a stick almost fully engulfed in fire and you almost burnt down half
the forest with that accident. And I’m your uncle. Of course I do! It’s practically the job description!~”

A small chuckle to my right caught my attention and I saw that Uta was finally smiling just a tiny bit. “AH-HA! There—his
face does change. Here I was beginning to think he got it stuck like that somehow.”

“Uncle—!!!!” I started to complain until I saw that Renji and Itori were laughing at the joke as well.

Shutting my mouth I decided to simply lean into Uta’s side.
They were getting along;
that’s all I wanted right now.

Chapter 53: A Parting Gift (To Keep You Safe)
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)

## Chapter Text

Chapter 53: A Parting Gift (To Keep You Safe)



“Uta—Come on.” I stood and tugged gently on his sleeve. The ghoul glanced up and stared at me with wide eyes.
“It’s dark enough now. There’s a clearing a little ways away...we can go and watch the stars for a bit? I can grab a
blanket.”

He stood up and started to follow as I held onto him, pulling him gently towards a small ‘path’ to where I knew
there was a clearing.

“Hey goth kid—” My uncle glanced up and narrowed his eyes. “...The clearing isn’t that far away . Got it?"

"Uncle — seriously!!! Stop! "

"I was your age at one point too!—Hey! Don't you walk away when I'm talking to you!" I was tugging on Uta's
arm, away from my uncle and towards the clearing. As I passed my hammock I pulled a blanket from it and threw
it over my shoulder.

"Either one of you wanna go with them? Keep an eye on her...or him? No? The stars are nice this time of year—"

I smiled faintly as I kept walking forwards and ignoring my uncle. He was joking , mostly. But he was also showing
he cared about me. He was worried. That much was clear to see. But he also wasn’t stopping Uta and I from
walking off into the forest. That probably meant that to some degree he trusted Uta not to try anything, or to hurt
me.  “Please don’t mind him too much...he likes to joke. I’m sure he’d tease you about those old sunglasses of
yours too.”

“What is wrong with my face?” Uta asked, making me giggle as I stepped out into the clearing. A few deer startled
and jumped up; bolting off into the forest.  The clearing was close enough to the cabin that I could still vaguely
hear voices and see the firelight.

I turned and reached up to cup his face in my hands, pulling close to press my lips against his for a quick peck.
“There’s nothing wrong with your face, you just don’t express very much most of the time. You were hiding
behind your mask again—It’s okay. I like your face the way it is.”

I pulled away and pulled the blanket off my shoulder, throwing it over the ground and spreading it out for two

people to lay down on. “Alright, now we just lay down...and look up!” I laid down first, staring upwards at the sky.
I’d seen it before of course. But even now, It took my breath away. So far from society with little to no light to
block out the stars it was spectacular . Thousands upon thousands of lights in a sky that was colored such deep
blues and purples until it all faded away in the east to the black of void.

Uta knelt down and then laid down beside me, close enough that his side touched mine. I moved my hand,
looking until I found his.

“Isn’t it pretty? Sometimes I’d fall asleep out here...especially when there’s a meteor shower. If you see one,
remember to make a wish!”

If only this moment right here could last forever. Or at least — a month. I could take about a full month of this. The
song of insects. The sky and stars. Relaxing. Absolutely no doves in the ward.


“Ai-chan...?”

“Hum?”

“Are you worried?”

“...I’m...a little overwhelmed right now. I’m not sure what to think. Or what to worry about first. It seems like
there’s always too much happening.” My hand gently gripped his as I continued staring up into the sky; looking
for a star to wish on. In the distance I could hear my uncle start strumming his guitar again and faintly smiled. “It’s
good to see him again—it’s just shocking. It shouldn’t be I guess. I just thought I would have known. I guess not.
To think my parents kept it from me...I wonder if they ever planned on telling me...or what else they might not
have mentioned.”

Maybe if I hadn’t run away they would have eventually told me and I’d be sworn to silence just as they wanted it.
I’d have been fed suppressants as soon as my RC level’s got too high for their comfort and I never would have left
my gilded cage. I would have been too frightened to turn into a ‘monster’ to ever leave.

“My Ai-chan, my Human...could turn into a Ghoul...” I heard him say softly; as though thinking aloud.  I turned
my head to look at him. Instead of looking upwards at the sky his head was turned to look at me.
“Hard to imagine; isn’t it?” I asked quietly; not able to picture it. I had tried to think of it before. What would
happen if I turned into a Ghoul? How different would I be?

How much of me was me because I was Human? All of it? 50%? Would who I was change and be more like him?
—I remembered the ease in which Uta could take a life. He could do it without blinking or caring. With no regrets or
guilt. Would it be like that? I think I’m afraid of that. But at the same time; anybody could be that way if they had
a cause.

If someone threatened Uta? If someone tried to hurt my friends?

If I had to choose helping them at any cost over my humanity; what would happen?

“Not at all...not for me. I can imagine it—” He turned his head back to stare at the sky. “Oh—a star...I wish—”

I let go of his hand, rolled myself up so I straddled his waist and pressed my hands to his mouth to keep him from
talking. “No—Don’t say it out loud! I–it won’t come true if you do. Shhhh. You make the wish quiet. In your head -
or your heart. Okay? And you never tell anybody what it was.”


I raised my hands slowly off his mouth and blushed. “So, go ahead and make your wish Uta—”
He stared up at me; eyes wandering my face for a moment before settling on my eyes. “Did your wishes ever come
true Ai-chan?...”

“...When I was a kid, I used to go into some secret passageways in the house. I got up to the attic. It was one of the
only places I could hide...keep everything my parents didn’t want me to have. I used to watch the sky from up
there through a little window and wish on every single star. If I could just escape...I’m not there anymore, am I?”

Smiling weakly I went to move; only to have his hands hold onto my hips firmly. I squirmed a bit but he didn’t let
me budge an inch. “Okay—I guess we’ll keep talking like this; do you like me on top, Uta-kun!~”

In the starlight and moonlight his face was cast in shadows but I could see the ghost of a smirk. “I'm still imagining
my Ai-chan as a Ghoul. Strong enough to fight me...maybe even beat me.” He sighed almost blissfully .

“...What if I took the suppressants and never—” If there was a choice. If it was black and white like that; and I
purposefully avoided becoming a Ghoul. What would that decision say to him? Would he think I didn’t love him?
That I thought I was above being a Ghoul?

I didn’t want to have to eat people ; human life was nice . It was easy . It was— mostly —peaceful. “...Since we’re
talking about it...what if I wanted to stay Human?”

His little smirk faded and those eyes searched my face again.
“Then I keep my human...My fragile Ai-chan. Close to me, so nobody but me can ever touch her.” His voice
dropped lower; growling possessively. His hands gripped tighter, pulling me impossibly closer making me squeak
softly. A moment later we flipped with him on top of me, hips pressed between my thighs. He leaned down—a
hair's breadth away from stealing a kiss.

“Hey you kids, what are you doing out there? You know we can see you from here!”

I jumped as my uncle's voice carried through the forest and turned my head towards the fire. I swore I could hear
the ghoul above me hiss in disappointment as the moment was interrupted.
I leaned up and softly kissed him, not heeding my uncle's voice in the distance. He leaned into it while nipping and
tasting me.


When he pulled back to breath reached up with my hands; holding his head so he couldn’t dive back into another
kiss–yet. “Uta—Human or Ghoul. I want to stay with you. I love you and I’d carry a thousand scars for you—if it
meant I could stay with you.”

Perhaps the scariest part was that I knew that if he asked it of me; I’d choose to be a Ghoul...
If it was that or loose him—


“Seriously you kids! Get back over there before I come out there myself and drag you apart myself! I’ve
got something for Aika... ”


“I think he’s serious...” I whispered softly, faintly smiling up at the ghoul who stared down at me; eyes wide.

“I love you.”
It wasn’t too often that he said the words aloud. More often than not Uta was a more ‘show not tell’ type of
Ghoul. But my heart soared every time he did say it, as though it were the first time I’d heard it from him.

“Let’s head back...I don’t really want you fighting my Uncle. Please?”
The ghoul smirked and chuckled, leaning back off me. “What if I really want to, Ai-chan?”

“No—Don’t you dare. Anyway—if we ever got married he’d be your uncle too! So you can’t go killing your
family, okay?” I rolled to my feet, tugging at the blanket until I got it from under Uta.
Running ahead I headed for the fire and left Uta standing in the field.

“Come on, let's go see what he wants to give me.”

## ♥

“There you are. I was just about to go march out there and pry him off you.” My uncle's eyes looked behind me,
following the ghoul as he stepped over a branch and made his way back to his seat by the fire.
“You could try old man.”

I shot Uta a silent look. He just can’t resist himself, can he? As long as he wasn’t actually starting fights I supposed
it was probably fine. “Uncle, you said you had something for me? The Twinkies and sparklers are enough. I don’t
need anything else. You’re going to make me feel bad for not visiting...”

“Yeah—if you wait right here. It’s inside. It’s been a while so I gotta dust it off...Wait here.”


I watched him leave the firelight, going to his cabin and disappearing into the dark. The inside lit with candle light
which I could only barely make him out moving past the windows as he retrieved whatever it was.
I glanced at Itori and Renji and raised a brow. “Did he mention what it was to you two?”

They shook their heads; Itori leaned in her seat to see if she could peek in the doorway to get the first look. I was
still looking at her and Renji when I saw their eyes widen. “No way—He’s still got one of those?”

I turned, trying to see what she was talking about. Upon turning around I spotted my uncle lugging out a metal
briefcase.
It was dented on one side and had rust on the hinges but it was undoubtedly a CCG quinque case.
Unperturbed by the other Ghouls by the fire Hiroshi approached, placing down the case beside me and
unclipping the latches.

“This...I give you this.” The case clicked open and he reached in, pulling a wakizashi with a red blade from the
case. The Ito-wrap was made of black leather while the Fuchi of the weapon seemed to be the same metal as my
knife. Just below the Fuchi there were crystal-like formations that flowed into the metal of the blade flawlessly. My
uncle moved to press it into my hand.

“No—” The word left my mouth before I’d even thought about it. Bile rose threatened to rise at the back of my
throat and I had to swallow it down with a grimace. I tried to pull my hand away and back myself across the log. I
didn’t want to touch it, let alone own such a thing!

“No, I–I don’t want that.”

“Glowbug—” He reached, grasping my arm by the wrist and pulling me back so I wasn’t escaping. His fingers
wrapped around mine, forcing me to grip the weapon’s hilt. I could feel the impossibly warm leather wrappings
around the hilt even as I tried futilely to let go of it.

“Please. You may not like it; but if it’s to keep you safe I need you to keep it. I can not be there to protect you...So
please. Please use the only tool I have to do so. The only thing I can do from out here is give you my weapon.”

“N-No. You’re not going to convince me to take that thing—” It had been a Ghoul at one point. A living
breathing person. How could he not understand? They might do the same thing to him if they ever found out
where he was! What if one day I would be holding some sword named after my uncle? Or Uta. Or Renji or any
one of my friends!?

He turned his gaze on Uta: “Maybe not. But he could...Please—I just want her safe. At any cost.”


“How do you still have that?” Itori spoke up and stared at the weapon with wide eyes. A look that was equally
disgusted as interested. “And why does it have such a short blade...?”


“...I fled the CCG. And I took this with me. I disabled the tracking in the suitcase—which is why it’s a little worse
for wear.”

Hiroshi let go of my hands and the weapon almost immediately fell.
Uta reached past me and grabbed it by the hilt before it hit the ground. He raised it and turned it over in his hands,
studying it nonchalantly. “It’s not much bigger than what she’s already got...”

Hiroshi held his hand out for the weapon. Uta turned it over a few more times and then returned it. My uncle
stepped back and held the weapon out in front of him.
“It was a Bikaku...The Ghoul who had it had a remarkably malleable kagune...” He clenched his hand around the
weapon and the weapon flared to life: crystals humming and RC cells bursting from them much like they did
from Uta’s back. The comparison made me want to puke or cry even more. The cells surrounded the blade as an
almost formless blood-like flow of cells. When he moved the blade the cells followed like a curling tail.

He turned away from fire, walked a few paces away and then swung at a tree. My uncle was far too far away to hit
the tree with such a short blade, but I watched in horror as the malleable liquid around it followed the swing and
slashed across the bark leaving a deep groove. A quick flick of the wrist and the tail followed again; putting an X on
the bark.

Hiroshi spoke calmly, glancing over his shoulder. “Despite its size, its range is about 4 meters and the response time
is faster than most. It’ll take some time to get used to, and she’ll need to train with it. But she knows how to handle
a sword. If she won’t take it now, hold onto it for her. Convince her. Keep it until she needs it.”

He lowered the sword and the cells disrupted returning to an inactive state. Hiroshi stared at the weapon before
returning it to the beat up case. I stared as my uncle approached me again. For a moment I thought he’d try and
hand it to me again, but he turned to Uta. Holding out the case for him to take. “...Watch over her...And know
that if anything happens to her on your watch —I’m coming to kill you. There isn’t a soul on this planet that
could stop me. Even if it kills me...”

I shivered, shrinking back as the man I knew as my uncle stared down Uta with ghoulish eyes and a threat that I
felt he fully meant regardless of if he could carry it out; he would try. He would die trying.

Uta reached out and took the case, held it for a moment. He kept his eyes on Hiroshi and then set the case down
by our cooler without replying to the threat.

“...Goodnight everyone. If you need any blankets or pillows I have a couple extra...” I watched my uncle turn away
and walk to his cabin. He disappeared through the door and appeared again a few seconds later, setting a pile of
blankets down outside the cabin. He returned, shutting his door with a quiet snap. I waited until the candle inside
was blown out and it was dark again.

“...I—I’m going to go to bed now...”

Or I was going to try.

I got up and went to the hammock, pausing to look back and mutter: “Uta...it’s big enough for you to sleep with
me. If you want.” I crawled in and curled up, trying to push stop thinking about how the warmth of the hilt
reminded me of the warmth of Uta’s kagune wrapped around me. Sitting on a rooftop in winter. Fingers gently
tracing over the ghoul’s most dangerous weapon while he used it for such a mundane thing as to warm me.

It was only a few minutes later that the hammock swayed as Uta peeked in. He took off his shoes, slipping in
beside me. He wrapped his arms around me and tangled our limbs. The hammock naturally pushed us close
together; nestling our bodies flush together.

He didn’t say anything, simply placed his chin on the top of my head like always and held onto me. I breathed in
and shivered; he smelled like himself —with just a hint of campfire. A magical mix of familiar and nostalgic that
knocked me right out.

## ♥

I woke up at first light and the sound of someone splitting wood. I opened my eyes, nuzzling close to Uta and
breathing in that magical scent again.
“Good morning.” Uta said, his voice sounding like he’d probably already been awake for some time before me.

I shifted and yawned; pressing my face up against his throat and nuzzling.
“Mmmm...we could sleep a little more and make it a good afternoon...” I felt the ghoul inhale and exhaled, hands
moving over my back. At some point he had slipped his hands under the hem of my shirt and was touching the
skin under; gently kneading it.

“...That sounds nice. But...Your uncle might not approve. He’s already come by a few times.”

“You’re not afraid of my uncle, are you Uta-kun?~” I whispered in a teasing tone, pressing a kiss to his throat.

“...You didn’t want me fighting him. I can if you want.”

## No.
“I guess we’ll have to get up then...” I shifted, struggling to move out of the hammock without it flipping us both
out onto the ground.
When I finally got my feet on the ground I slipped my shoes back on and looked around the little camp. Renji was
already seated by the firepit; the coals were low but still burning. I hadn’t known my uncle to ever let it die
completely.

Itori on the other hand still seemed to be sleeping. She had taken all the pillows and a few of the blankets and made

a place by the fire.

“Ah, there you are. Finally up Glowbug?” Uncle was standing near the corner of the cabin, an axe slung over his
shoulders and a grin on his face. Apparently all his seriousness the night before was forgotten. “I got up a little
while ago, caught you some food. You didn’t eat much last night—Figured you could use some protein.”

“I—I wasn’t really hungry...” My stomach was growling now though.
“Hope rabbit is alright. It’s hung up on the rack.” I glanced at the rack that we had always used to skin the animals
I hunted. Deer. Bear. Rabbits. Plenty of rabbits.

“Coals should still be hot enough for you, but I’ll add some wood just to be sure—”

I slipped out of the hammock and stretched; eyeing the rabbit. My stomach growled a little louder and I rolled my
eyes. “Uncle, you got a knife?”

“Huh? Oh right. Here kiddo...” He pulled a knife from his pocket and handed it to me, handle first. He reached
for my head right after; ruffling my hair. “The pans are where they’ve always been...and I clean them after I use
them.”

“Stop, you’re messing up my hair!”

“You’ve got bed head, Glowbug. Trust me, I’m not making it any worse!”

I pouted, trying to fix my hair the best I could by running my hands through it. I pulled a few leaves from it and
then tied it up into a messy bun.
Stepping up to the rack I looked over the rabbit. It was dead. It had been bled out and its neck cleanly snapped.
He’d already strung it up for me by each foot.
Rolling my sleeves up I took the knife and began cutting around the ankles of the creature.

Rabbits were always the easiest. He’d taught me when I was still just a young child. I had been squeamish about
the animals at first, but during the time when I visited him I learned that if I wanted meat he was going to make me
work for it.
If I hunted an animal it would be my job to finish the job.

At some point I heard music behind me and started to sway and hum softly. I discard organs I wouldn’t eat and
clean out the meat. Just like old times. “Uncle, you know I can’t eat this whole thing—Can I bring the extra meat
home since you won’t eat it?”

“Of course, Glowbug. Just put the stuff you don’t want in the bucket there and I’ll get rid of it.”

“Do you still make soap from the fat? If you still hunt—” Animals. But I had to ask out of curiosity.

“I still hunt. And fish. I can normally sell or trade the pelts and meat in some of the smaller towns. There’s this
older lady nearby who will fix up any of my clothing with holes as long as I bring her rabbit meat and some of their
fur.”

“That’s great! I forgot to ask, but do you need anything out here? I could probably have some stuff sent out if you
needed.”

“No Glowbug, I’m alright. You don’t have to worry about your ol’ uncle!”

I cut what was left of the rabbit down when it was only cleaned meat left. “Okay. If you say so. There we go—all
done.” I turned and froze; wide eyed like a deer caught in the headlights. I stood there holding the rabbit, blood on
my hands.
“Uh—?” Uta and Renji were staring.

I’d completely forgotten I’d had a peanut gallery when I was doing that.
“Hey, that looks good kiddo! You didn’t nick the organs either! Not even a little rusty!” My uncle patted my back
roughly as he passed by, inspecting the meat and the unwanted organs.
“Well it’s not that hard...you taught me as a kid so—”

“So what you're saying is I taught you well!” He laughed at my expression and pointed at the fire which had logs
set up to hold a pan over the coals. “Now cook it up. We can all hear your stomach growling!”

“R-right...”

I put the knife between my teeth while I moved awkwardly to grab a pan from the chest of cookware and put it
over the fire. With the knife I cut off smaller chunks of raw meat and tossed them in; immediately making them
sizzle and filling the air with the smell of meat.

I put the leftovers in the cooler, settling the meat on the bottom under Uta’s empty Tupperware and the ice that
was left over. If for some reason we were stopped on our way back into the city I could at the very least show that
the cooler was full of perfectly ordinary meat .

Using a small well  by the side of the cabin I washed the blood off my hands and the knife.

Uta was still staring though.

I sat back down, trying to ignore the way his eyes were following me. I turned the meat over by poking it with the
knife and flipping it. Finally when I couldn’t take it anymore I spoke up: “Is...something wrong, Uta-kun?”

“No.”

“You’re staring.”


“You’ve got something on your face.” He reached over and swiped his thumb over my cheek, wiping away a red
smear.
“Oh—from the rabbit.” I glanced down at my shirt and tried to see if there was any more. “Was that all of it?”

“Yeah.”

## ♥

As the three Ghouls and Aika piled back into Renji’s beat up vehicle Uta’s mind was still on the way Aika cut into
the rabbit.
The blood stained her hands and splattered on her face without her realizing.
She was both so focused on her work and yet so relaxed; her hands working organs from meat and meat from bone
as if she’d done it a thousand times before.
She hummed a soothing song and swayed her hips as she tossed the animal's guts from its carcass without a
thought.

Then she turned to him with such a surprised and innocent look on her face.
And still she couldn’t understand why it was so easy to imagine her as a Ghoul?
Perhaps it was simply easier to think that she would make a good Ghoul than believe that a Human really loved
him. It was in her genetics...wasn’t it? Perhaps that’s why she could love him.

There was a moment the night before he had almost gotten too excited about the idea; Imagining his Ai-chan
having such fun with him forever.
Getting his sweet human accustomed to him and his world was fun.
But he would never be bored again if she were like him.

She had said she’d carry a thousand scars for him. Now that idea refused to leave his head. Not when the bite mark
he had left on her a few days earlier was still visible, pressed into her shoulder.

But then again, his Ai-chan might want to stay Human. Fragile. Innocent.
Uta glanced at the silver case that sat on the seat between him and Aika.
It might never get old having her crawl into his arms so willingly and this was looking like it could be fun too. Renji
was going to have his hands full with her wielding something like that.

## ♥

“Aika...You should use the weapon.”

I stared dumb struck as Renji spoke up. He had eyed the case with distaste, but was still trying to convince me to
use it regardless?
“Renji...Uta told me what those are—I can’t. I can’t —”

“...You can.” I winced at the blunt tone Renji spoke with. “And you should. It’s getting dangerous. You know
Aika, that things have been escalating. You’ve seen the Doves in the 20th ward. But all the wards are crawling with
Doves and there are Ghouls who are getting displaced. They are hungry and desperate. You need to be able to
protect yourself—We aren’t always going to be able to watch after you.”

“I don’t need to use one of those to—”

“ We’ve lost enough friends and family, Aika. Please...use it to protect yourself.”

All my arguments fell away; killed instantly by that single sentence. I tried to think of anything to say to combat it.
But no words could ever combat that.

“...I don’t like it.”

“Aika—”

“I didn’t say no. I said I don’t like it. ”


## Notes:

You guys get a tiny thing kinda with some of Uta's thoughts? (Technically 3rd person)

## Chapter 54: 
## Notes:
Warning: This one is mostly 
(I think some commenters are right. He definitely has a blood kink. Among...others.)
(See the end of the chapter for  more notes.)

## Chapter Text

## Chapter 54:
## 



I hurried from Renji’s car to Uta’s shop door, opening the door with my key quickly and heading in.
Uta was lagging behind while lugging the bag and cooler. I held the metal briefcase and the last thing I wanted to
do was get caught with this thing. Simply having it in my possession was extremely illegal.

We hadn't even stopped at the cafe to pick up Bjorn yet because I wanted to hide it someplace before going within
a hundred yards of my job.
How did they expect me to carry this around with me all the time?

Japan has some strict laws about weapons and anything bigger than 6cms was absolutely not allowed. Unless of
course you were a CCG member.


And a Quinque being welded by a random civilian? There was no way people wouldn't notice a sword strapped to
my hip and I’d be picked up by the cops at the very least . From there I’d be in a holding cell at the CCG and
questioned. From what I know from Ghouls - they weren’t above torture.

I’d have to think of some way to have it with me and keep it hidden on my person. Something innocuous and
common that nobody would really question. I could think about it later and with the things Uta had just laying
around for crafts there was likely an answer someplace.

I ran up the stairs of the shop and opened the apartment door, looking around for a good spot.
Somewhere where someone wouldn’t look. Under the bed or the couch was too obvious. So was his closet in the
hallway.

By the time I’d found a good spot Uta was already in the apartment, putting the tupperware in the sink and
looking at the skinned rabbit meat that was in the cooler. “...Where do you want this?”

“Huh? Oh it can go in a tupperware—I can get it in a minute.”

## Chapter 55:

I took a nap; waking up in the early evening to an empty bed. I shifted my body and winced as muscles and bones
cried out in protest. Forget Yoshimura, how was I going to lie to Renji? I was supposed to continue training with
him like normal and now I felt like my legs were probably going to be out of commission for anything that made
me move faster than a walk for a few days — not to mention the marks Uta had definitely left on my body.

I know that I should at least try and get out of bed, find out where Uta was and get myself something to eat. My
stomach was growling to emphasize that point. I pushed the covers away from me and shivered. Uta had put me
into bed naked and I’d passed out so soon after; I couldn’t even remember if I’d asked for anything to eat.

I rolled over, staring at the glass of water standing on my small bedside table. That was thoughtful . I gulped it
down so fast that I was gasping for breath after I finished; delighting in the relief it brought.

My phone wasn’t on the bedside so it must still be in the living room on the TV stand where I’d left it after hiding
the quinque. Right before Uta had demanded my attention. I rolled out of bed and felt my legs wobble like jello.
Looking down my body I could see I was covered in fresh bruises. My hips in general had hand sized prints and
small scabbed over cuts where Uta’s nails had dug in and broken the skin. Although I hadn’t seen it yet, I could
already guess that my neck and shoulders were a sunset of purples, reds and blues. Not to mention at least one bite
that broke the skin.

First I grabbed underwear, slipping on the panties and then a bra. Then I considered pants but jeans didn’t appeal
to me. Too rough on my sore hips. Instead I flicked through some of his clothing and picked up one of his baggier
pants. Among his clothing I eyed some of his suits; a zebra print pair of pants and jacket were especially
outlandish. I had to remember to ask at some point where the hell he would even wear something like that.

I pulled his baggy pants on, followed by a long sleeve shirt with a turtleneck that could hide most of the bruised
marks and broken skin.

Uta was as absent in the living room as the bedroom. The same with the kitchen. And the rest of the apartment for
that matter. Which meant he had probably gone down to his shop at some point after dropping me into bed.
Before heading down I took my phone from the TV stand and quickly text Hinami:

Aika: Would you mind watching Bjorn for another night? Feeling sick after staying in the woods.


I was definitely going to lie to the kid. And to the old man. A few moments later I got a text back.

Now that that was taken care of, I had to get some food. Cooking was out of the question simply because standing
so long in front of the stove was going to start hurting me sooner rather than later. I’d have to order something. I
began to consider different foods while cracking the door that led from the apartment down into his shop. As
soon as the door cracked I could smell something that was good but I forgot about it the moment I spotted the
ghoul leaning back in his chair, his sketchbook in hand and scribbling away in it. Careful not to fall (more bruises
or worse broken bones was the last thing I needed) I climbed down the stairway and went to him; leaning close so I
might be able to get a peek at what he was drawing.

The moment I got close he closed the book and looked over his shoulder.

“Oh? Is it a secret drawing? Is it something lewd?” I spoke softly; grinning as I teased him. Leaning closer to the

“Nothing bad.”

“...I ordered you pizza. You should eat.”

“You ordered me pizza!?!!—Wait! You can’t distract me with food!!!” He leaned over his desk and picked up the

to my nose and I could feel my mouth water and my stomach growl again. Or I could be; my resolve crumbled to
dust in the wind. “...You—This is...completely cheating...I’m asking later. After I eat...”

I took my seat and picked out a piece and took a huge bite out of it and closed my eyes while I chewed it. Why did
it always taste like the best food of your life when you were really hungry? Warm. Cheesy. The perfect amount of
grease. The bread wasn’t burnt but was still a little crisp and crunchy!

“How are you feeling, Ai-chan?”

I glanced up at Uta with my mouth full. Chewing fast I swallowed the mouthful quickly and coughed.
“Good...um.” I blushed and added: “ Really good . Just a little sore. And my voice...from... yeah. How about you?”

“For now.”
I choked . For now he says .
I swallowed the bite and coughed once more. “Uta!!!”

“You don’t want more?”

“No that— Yes . I would. But—y-your gonna let me heal first! I don’t even know what to say to Renji. I’m
supposed to go to work and I have training with him after! I can barely move!” I had yet to give Yoshimura my
excuse. At least he would take it without questioning but Renji knew that I had been fine when he dropped us off.

“Wait–Hold on...I got food on my hands. I don’t wanna get oil on it...” I set the box of the rest of the pizza aside
and jumped up; wincing as I completely forgot my injuries .

Uta had a sink tucked away in his storage room for the shop. It was used mostly for washing off paint from
brushes but for now I quickly washed my hands free of oil and limped back out. He was still waiting for me,
holding the book for me to take. I glanced over his placid face and squinted. “You know...if you really don’t want
me to look it’s okay for you to say so...”

“Some of them aren’t finished. But I want you to see.”

I took the book and opened it. Turning through the first few pages I saw that a decent number of the sketches

about Ghouls. “I forgot you drew these of me...drooling all over my sleeve. There’s no way to convince you to get

“None.”

As I continued flipping I saw he had added quite a few doodles and sketches. Some of me, some of his other
friends at the bar. But in the recent pictures I saw a picture of my fight with Renji captured in lead. There’s no way

am...”


Another couple pages and I was staring at a portrait image of myself. My long hair down, tucked behind an ear and
a slight smile on my lips. I was holding up my mask to cover half my face —
My breath caught as I stared at the image.

Although it was in black and white; a ghoulish eye with blackened sclera stared back at me
“...You said you couldn’t imagine it. So I thought I’d show you.”

“You know Uta...if anybody else saw this they might get the wrong idea.”

“...you don’t like it.”

“What—no! Uta it’s really good...I guess it’s a bit...I’m not sure how to describe it. Jarring? I’m so used to your
eyes being that way, but...not seeing me with them. And it looks realistic.”
I moved to flip to the next page but a hand stopped me. Uta’s tattooed fingers gently took the book from my
hands and set it aside. “The rest aren't done.”

“Okay. Another time.” It was likely just an excuse not to show them to me; and I wasn’t going to pressure him into
it. “Thanks for the food, Uta. I really do appreciate it.”

“—Actually, I was wondering if you could help me with something. Or two things.”

“Yeah.” I smiled as he readily agreed. I hadn’t even told him what I’d wanted yet.
“Well, first. Can you call Mr. Yoshimura for me? Tell him I’m not feeling well and am sleeping. That I won’t be

Uta’s smirk popped up again; eyes widening just a little as I asked this of him. “ D-don’t —absolutely don’t tell
him the truth.” I said, accidentally raising my voice high enough that the words cracked.

“Okay...what’s the second thing, Ai-chan?”

“I’ve got some questions about that...sword. And maybe you can help me figure out a good way to carry it with me
without getting caught.”

“Sure.”

Sure? Just like that. Uta picked up his phone, scrolled through his contacts and held it to his ear after tapping one.
“Ah...Yoshimura-san...Uta. Ai-chan’s not feeling well. She’s going to be staying home.” I cocked my head to the

answered questions from the other side. “She can’t talk. No. No...Ok-ok~”

He lowered the phone from his ear, eyes peering down on it. “He seemed worried about you...”
“Yeah...maybe but I don’t know what else to tell him...”
