Pulling it out I set it aside and stacked the movies haphazardly for now. There wasn’t a point in putting them away
while the sword was out for now.

Uta took a seat on the couch and lounge with his arms along the back and his legs spread wide. He took up most of
the couch while Renji stood, looking around the apartment. It had been a little while since he’d been here and
some things had changed.

My painting was mounted on a wall, the colorful flowers brought color into the room. As did a few fake plants.
Moved to look  in the kitchen, stocked with all the human ‘necessities’. Even if I didn’t use half of them - I still
kept the place stocked like a human home.

From the spices in the cabinet that I had immediately poured out half of to make them look used, the liquor lined
up along the back counter, to the cookbooks that lined a shelf above the sink. A vacuum sat in the corner of the
room, used often to pick up dog hair to make sure it didn’t get all over the place or out of control.

Renji finishes looking around and sets the crock-pot on the counter. Returning to the doorway between the
kitchen and the living room he’s looking down at the case and my expression at it. The case isn’t even open, but I
know what’s in it and it makes my stomach turn.


“...What were you wanting to ask?”

“...Does...do you know if it needs to stay in this case? Or is it safe to keep outside it?” Did the case have a function
other than uniformity? Perhaps the sword weapons would decay? Since they were made with body parts. “No.”

“So...it could be stored in a different way? Like a normal sheath?”

“Yeah. It would be better if you did and we got rid of that box...sooner than later. Your Uncle said he disabled the
tracker. But I’d rather not chance it.” That much we could both agree upon, if for some reason the tracker clicked
on they’d have a beacon to Uta’s home.

“Since you insist that I keep it with me I’ll need to think of a way to carry it...” I nibbled my bottom lip and
glanced between the Ghouls. “I think I have an idea...I’d need Uta’s help making it...”

“Ai-chan...” I trailed off, looking up to Uta when he called my nickname. “I know you’re not frightened of my
Kagune. So why do you make that face?”

“I—I’m not frightened. I...it...they...”

Uta blinked, glancing at the metal case and then back at me. They. I was speaking as if the sword, the thing it was
made of, was a person still. “It’s okay to use it to keep yourself safe.” Renji spoke aloud, perhaps understanding my
issue with it a little better than Uta for the moment. The goth ghoul didn’t understand the guilt I felt. Guilt wasn’t
something that he expressed. Honestly; who was I to say he should feel it? He ate; he lived.

But Renji. Renji should know better! Shouldn’t he?

“—And would you think that if it were you? Or Uta? Or Itori! Nico. Yoshimura. Koma. Irimi. Nishiki. Or lil’
Hinami! Touka!What if one day one of you gets caught. Torn apart for bits and pieces to be turned against your
friends and your family! What if one day someone I know hands me a weapon and instead of a stranger, it’s yours.
Every time I think of that...I—” I felt tears spring to my eyes and my stomach turn. What if all that was left of my
friends and my lover was a bit of warm steel and a Quinque that would forever remind me of what I’d lost?


Perhaps my empathy was misplaced for a human. But I cared about them. I hadn’t had people I cared about
before now. Only Bjorn who had mended my heart in ways that still were a miracle to this day. Now that I did
have people I was terrified to lose a single one of them. Losing them wouldn't be gentle or kind when the time
came. The world was cruel and violent and they would be ripped from me. Though I hated her, even this wasn’t a
fate I wished upon Roma.


I was scared to lose them. It’s why I had gone over every little corner of our home and tried to make it look human.
To make sure that Uta would pass scrutiny if there ever was some Doves that showed up. It’s why I would
cheerfully talk to Amon and stand between Uta and the investigator; grabbing the investigator's attention by being
all smiles. It’s why I was the first person to jump up and serve the investigators at the cafe now-a-days. Anything I
could do.


I stared at the ground, eyeing the box as a few tears slipped from my face. “...I don’t know who this was. But they
had family and friends who cared about them...And my uncle killed them. He had this weapon made and turned it
upon other Ghouls while he worked...”

Renji’s black boots showed up in my peripheral and then he knelt down, a hand on my shoulder. “...That won’t
happen. I promise.” I raised my head, searching Renji’s eyes and glancing at Uta. His face was calm as ever; but he
leaned forward with his elbows on his knees. His head tilted just slightly to one side as he watched me weep over a
Ghoul I didn’t even know. Who had died decades ago.

“I won’t allow it...You don’t have to worry Aika.” He glanced at the weapon case. Leaning over he flipped the
latches and lifted the weapon from the case. “ This is your weapon now. Use it so that you stay with us and we
don’t have to worry so much about what will happen to you. I told you before...we’ve all lost so many people
already—”

He glanced over at the goth ghoul in question. “Uta convinced me to train you to fight. And I have. But one day
you will have to kill to keep yourself alive...don’t allow your empathy for strangers and the dead take you away
from those who care about you Aika.”

The way he said I will have to kill someone left no room to argue. It was simply the world we lived in. At some
point, that day would come. Being among Ghouls, and being with Uta assured it.

He held out the weapon in front of him and I reached to take it, wrapping my fingers around the hilt and pulling
it towards me. Its red crystals glittered like blood.

It was beautiful and terrible .

“Okay...If I’m carrying it around. Then I need to have the sheath made.” I nibbled at my lip and looked at Uta.
“...I was thinking it could be fitted to an umbrella. Folded up nobody could tell, and everybody carries umbrella’s
all the time. It wouldn’t be seen as strange.”

## ♥

I leaned over Uta’s shoulder watching him as he worked on the sheath that would double as the pole of the
umbrella. His tools were spread over the living room table so he wouldn’t be working on it out in the open. It had
only taken him a couple days to figure out how it would work and now he was almost done. All that was really left
to do was attach it by soldering it to the top part of the umbrella I’d picked out. It white with crimson spider lilies
on the outside with a dark red underside.
“Have you thought of a name for it, Ai-chan?”

I sighed and made a noncommittal sound. He had asked me before as he had begun to work on it but I felt
awkward about naming the sword. It already had a name at one point or another - but I didn’t know it. That
being said; since it was now mine I wanted to give it a name that was fitting.


“...Crystal Lily?” It matched the crystal like formations, and the spider lilies and it felt...like a decent name.
Beautiful. It deserved a beautiful name. But I still felt awkward as the ghoul didn’t say anything. He turned on the
soldering gun and started to attach the umbrella to the sheath. “You think it’s lame, don’t you...? I could always
just ask my uncle...he might remember the actual name...””

“...No. It’s a pretty name. It suits you. Here—” He held out the Umbrella-sheath to me and I turned it over in my
hands. It was sturdy. Now all there was left to do was check to see if it worked. Hopping up I picked up the sword
from the table and slid it into the sheath. Admittedly it made a very satisfying singing hiss as it left or sank into its
casing.  Folded up and sheathed it looked just like an ordinary umbrella.

When the sword was sheathed fully there was a small click. An addition that Uta had added to make the umbrella
more functional and so the sword would never fall out on accident. All that I had to do to pull the sword was to
press on a button trigger and it would release. Testing, I clicked the button and drew the sword.

"It's perfect...I don't want to open the Umbrella inside if I can help it though. Bad luck..."

"I finished it in time."

"In time?"

"Training. Renji’s on his way. You’re going to try it out.”

Of course he’d call Renji over on the weekend, getting me to try out the sword that I’d tried my best to avoid using
at all. “Uta...I’m sure I could still benefit from training without it.”

Uta set his tools down and stood up from the couch. “There’s no point fighting unarmed, Ai-chan. Plus...You’ll
be fighting me. You’ll need it.”

## Notes:

She had to get some things off her chest, and she did. We'll see if it enough to let her use the
sword.

Do I steal some ideas from commenters? Yes.
Do sometimes commenters already guess what I was planning. Also yes. Idk how you do it. You
magical people. Witches.

I feel like taking a vote on how many people think she'll turn ghoul vs those who think she'll
stay human. I'm not telling you. I'm just a curious author. Plz tell me.
Also I already know. But you don't. So that's fun. >:P
New Job is making me write a little slower. But I'm still writing!


Chapter 56: Isn’t this fun?!
## Notes:
(If this chapter is a bit awkwardly written it's cause I was having a HELL of a time trying to write it. I'm not sure
I'm happy with it still...but I've rewritten it like 5 times. Not even kidding. But I need to move on or I'mma fall
back into a rut of not writing! And we dont want that.)
## Chapter Text

Chapter 56: Isn’t this fun?!


“You?” I knew he had wanted to join in on the training; especially after he and the others watched the fight the
last time.
But I hadn’t expected him to be joining this soon; and not the first time I even tried the weapon. “I can’t fight you
## Uta...”

“Why not Ai-chan, It'll be fun.” He was looking at me as he popped an eye into his mouth.

Fun? I suppose training could be considered fun . It was a work out. It definitely got my heart racing. I could
clearly see how far I’d come and the progress I've made.
But it hadn’t been fun learning to be okay with stabbing Renji; causing real harm didn’t excite me.

Even if I knew he would heal within seconds it had taken ages just to learn it was okay to put small cuts and minor
slashes on the silver haired ghoul.
He still told me to cut harder and deeper from time to time.

Cut harder. That’s not going to do anything to a ghoul that attacks you.

In truth I was more worried about fighting the Doves than Ghouls.

Now Uta expected me to attack him with this weapon that was made to kill his kind? Even if it was likely I’d never
actually be able to do any real harm to him, I didn’t like the idea at all.
Nor quite frankly did I particularly fancy getting my ass handed to me.

“Uta...I don’t really want to fight you...”


His expression was unreadable, blank as he picked up another eyeball and licked it.
Uta could be stubborn. I knew there was a pretty high chance he was hoping to just ignore what I’d said and do
what he wanted regardless.
“I just healed up too. I don’t want to have to call out of work again.” Then I added: “You're only allowed to make
me black and blue once a week Uta, and your quota is met...Plus I prefer the other way .”

I saw his lips curl into that subtle smile of his, but a second later it fell. “...Nobody will go easy on you Ai-
chan...it’s best if you learn not to hold back either.”

“And fighting you will help with that...how?”

He cocked his head to one side and seemed to consider his words for a moment before speaking again: “Because, I
won’t go as easy on you as Renji-kun has...” He meant well , didn’t he? Still, it made me nervous .
“...So am I going to end up more or less bruised than a few days ago?”

“Depends.”

“On?”

“How much you learned from Renji...” The ghoul sat down in his work chair, spinning to face the table casually.
He picked up a pencil and began sketching something in a notebook. “...and what you want to do after the fight.”
His words had some clear implications. How he could say such things with such a straight face I would never
understand .


“I doubt I’ll be in any shape moving, let alone anything else if you end up beating me to a pulp Uta!”

The bell rang to the shop and I turned to see Renji had arrived. His stern expression is as ever present as Uta’s
poker face.

“Hey Renji-kun...give me a moment. I’m closing shop. I’m coming with you.” Uta stood from the desk, closing
his sketchbook and heading for the front door. “...Don’t forget your Quinque, Ai-chan.”

There went my hopes they might just forget about it.

I stepped away from them and  jogged up the stairway to grab the umbrella that leaned against the wall near the
front door of the apartment.
It was innocuous. Completely Innocent. Something nobody would ever think to question. Investigators would
walk right past it and never realize; just like the ghouls themselves.

I picked it up, along with my gym bag full of medical supplies for when I got hurt. Lastly my mask was shoved
into the bag for safe keeping.
I could hear them talking; Uta was telling Renji he would be going with us today and I didn’t hear any push back.
Not a single argument that it was a bad idea—I paused at the top of the stairway with a frown on my lips.

## Fun?
He thought it would be fun to fight me? Why? I wasn’t strong enough, was I? I might never be.
Maybe it was fun to poke fun at me when he inevitably came to that conclusion? Surely he wasn’t mocking me,
was he?
A warm head leaned against me and I looked down at Bjorn with a small smile.
“...Hey there bear-bear. You’re not going to wanna fight me, are you? No. You wouldn’t hurt a soul! Would you?”
I rubbed his face and head quickly before pulling the door shut and heading down to meet Uta and Renji.

“...Right. I’m ready...”  I guess.



## ♥

The closest entrance wasn’t far, but the walk there was quiet. The two ghouls walked a short distance ahead of me
while I lagged behind.

I wanted to say something to Uta, but I wasn’t sure how I could even begin to try to convince him this wasn’t a
good idea. Plus he might be right about things. If Renji was going easy on me (and he undoubtedly must be) then
it would only hurt me in the long run.

But fighting Uta was scary. I couldn’t admit it aloud. Not to him.

I wasn’t even sure if he knew how many times he’d scared or startled me, and I’d packed it away and shrugged it
off as best as I could.

All those scary parts made me feel safe when he was protecting me, but if he turned it around and I had to face
him in a fight the dread might overwhelm me.

It might not be a good idea.

I know Uta was capable of holding back; the fact that he hadn’t broken me yet clearly showed that. He was careful
and gentle with me even at times that lesser people might have lost their composure.

Still, I could get seriously hurt if Uta didn't hold back enough.

Even if he didn’t accidentally do something fatal; break a bone and it could set me back months worth of training.

I wouldn’t be able to work at the cafe. People would worry about me and wonder what happened for that to
happen! What was I supposed to tell them, that Uta hurt me by accident?

Renji picked up the manhole cover and waited for me to drop down. The two ghouls followed suit.

By the time they got to the bottom with me I was already taking my mask out; strapped its leather fastenings tight
to my head and tossing the bag aside out of the way.

In the beginning of my training the mask had felt like a burden to have it on during a fight.

But now the way the plush leather pressed against my face and the weight of it had become comforting.
## Safe.



I couldn’t place exactly when I’d started to feel that way.

It could have been because of training, fighting Renji with it on.

I’d just gotten used to it.

But on the other hand perhaps it really had been when it protected me during my encounter with the Doves.
I was sure that if there was anybody left that had seen my face or his they would have already busted down our
door and came for us.

Plus; on most occasions the mask kept me from bloodying my face.

Uta placed his leather mask over his face and I was unable to see or read his expression; not even his eyes.

More than once before I lamented not seeing his hidden smiles; now I lamented the loss because I wanted to know
what he was thinking.

“I’ll be training with Aika first Renji—you’ll have to wait your turn.”

I swallowed thickly as my mouth went dry.

“Uta...” Renji spoke firmly. He stepped forward and gave his friend a disapproving stare. “She hasn’t even used
the weapon yet...”

“That’s fine. Ai-chan...play with me for a little bit, okay? You’ll figure it out.”

## Play?

I blinked and realized my mistake; it hadn’t been a question but a warning.

Unlike Renji, Uta wasn’t waiting for me to start the fight. The ghoul was already charging forward.

## Shiii—

I jumped back, ducking as Uta reached out for me.


For what was probably the first time since meeting him I was fleeing his tattooed fingers as they reached for me;
uncertain what might happen if he did manage to grasp onto me.

“Uta—” I yelped as he sprang forward again, so fast that I could barely keep up or even get a chance to draw the
sword.

I swung the sword, clicked the button and the umbrella part of it flew off to the sidelines.

If it was damaged, I’d have to take a look later.

For now all I could manage was to lift the sword in an attempt to defend myself as I back peddled away from the
goth ghoul.

“Come on Ai-chan. I saw you fight Renji-kun. You can do better than this.”

Attack. I know that’s what Renji would demand. And what Uta wanted—

4 meter range. It gave me approximately 13 Feet that I could keep between me and Uta as long as I kept the sword
moving; the tail turning and curling in front of me as I was forced to back up further and further.

“I’m not playing Uta! I don’t want to fight you...”

I leapt away as the ghoul closed in once more; his speed beating Renji out by a mile.

I swung blindly out of panic when Uta got too close; the coiling Quinque blade swiped past him as he side stepped
it with ease.

Caught in a cat and mouse dance across the concrete underground I realized quite quickly that Uta was quite agile
despite being somewhat sedentary.

Most days I would equate him to a lazy cat; lounging around or quietly working on art in one form or another.


But the way he sidestepped and ducked was almost comically casual. He only moved the bare minimum it took to
get out of the way before giving chase again.


“I’’ll catch you Ai-chan. If you don’t fight seriously like your life is on the line I might as well be the one to eat
you...before someone else gets you.”

Panic flooded my mind as he closed in. I didn’t want to believe a word he was saying, but suddenly he wasn’t my
kind Uta.

He wasn’t my boyfriend who pulled me towards him every night before falling asleep.

Not the man who couldn’t seem to fall asleep lately unless he had his head resting on my head or in the crook of
my neck.

He wasn’t the one who stood by me in the kitchen watching me cook my human food, commenting on how it
looked.

He wasn’t the one who protected me from the danger.

He was someone who knocked me off my feet. Thrown into a concrete pillar and then to the ground. He was
someone pinning me down while I struggled against his impossible strength. He was someone who ignored the
way I cried out in pain.

“You’re mine Ai-chan!~” He moved his mask away from his mouth and had his teeth clenched down on my
shoulder.

My Uta could bite harder, could break skin without me worrying; but not like this. It felt too real—

My sword had been knocked out of my hand, slid too far from reach.
But my other hand found my knife - it’s Quinque steel cool in my hand as I pulled it from my pocket.


I stuck with it, fear driving the knife into the ghoul above me. The ghoul over me grunted in pain, released his
teeth and pulled away.

“Uta! Enough—” I heard Renji say as I turned on my stomach and crawled as fast as I could to grab my fallen
weapon.

“Ai-chan—”

I turned, still sitting on the ground and saw the ghoul standing over me.
He was taking a step closer and I swung the sword in a swift motion.
The blade struck true; slashing across his torso. Hip to shoulder cutting deep into his flesh.
It was only after the blood began to pour from his wounds that I recognized he was holding his arms out in a
friendly gesture; reaching to help me up.

Uta took a few steps back, hands raised to his chest where the new wound split his skin and muscle. The small
Quinque steel weapon still was stuck from between his ribs.

He took another step back, lifting his hands up with his palms out as Renji approached; grabbing Uta’s shoulder
and roughly pushing him back further. “Enough...Enough Uta...”

“I...—” I heard my voice try to speak, eyes stuck on the knife plunged in Uta. “I’m sorry Uta—I didn’t mean to—
## ”

“Aika, we can stop for the day—” Renji was saying; pushing Uta further back from me. As though he was
dangerous.

“N–no. No, Renji. It’s fine. We should keep going.” I was calming down. I could understand why Uta did what
he did—at least in theory. He was right. Even if the method was flawed; might have scared me and added to the
already numerous bottled up nightmares. It didn’t change that he was right.

I pushed myself back up on my feet, clutching my sword tight in my hand. “Uta—are you okay?”

“I’m fine.” Uta pulled at the shredded bits of his shirt, pulling it the rest of the way off. He lifted his mask so it sat
on top of his head, so I could see his face again.

Tentatively I walked past Renji and took a closer look at him; his chest looked like it was piercing itself together.

“Your wound is already healing?”

“...Yeah. Remember when I was hurt?”


I did remember. It was a lot worse when I found him. Worse when he’d first gotten attacked and he had ended up
healing without a scratch.

The ghoul reached out towards my head and I flinched—Staring at how his hand hovered inches from my mask.

His eyes were huge, eyes locked on mine. He waited a moment and then slowly grasped the skull of the mask,
unclipped the buckles that kept it on and pulled it away from my face.

"Lets go home, Ai-chan..."





## ♥

Uta walked closer to me on the way home.

When the door to the shop closed behind us and I walked up the stairway I heard the ghoul following behind - his
clogs tapping lightly as he hurried to catch up.

At the top of the stairway I kicked off my shoes and placed the umbrella sword down.

Thankfully it hadn’t been damaged and would be okay for the next time I trained.

Which after talking to Renji would be tomorrow rather than every other day. Rather than letting the day scare me
out of training I had to ‘get back in the saddle’ as some might say.

I went to bed even though it was much too early.

Uta wasn’t saying a word to me as I left him in the living room.

I stripped out of my training clothes, put on some comfortable shorts and a tank top and curled up in our bed.


It smelled good; familiar.

## Safe.



Before I fell asleep I felt someone crawl into bed with me.

They wrapped their arms around me and pulled my body to them, entangling our limbs and nestling their chin on
the crown of my head.

“...your mine Ai-chan. I won’t let anybody else eat you.”

He’s terrible at apologizing.



## ♥

Uta held her close to him, feeling her pulse beat under her skin. Alive and fragile against him. His to keep. His to
protect. His.

But...he recalled the wet lines that had streaked from her eyes when he pulled off her mask.
He had made her cry.
There were wounds on her body now that were put there with his own hands and unlike the reminders of their
more intimate moments they didn't make him proud. It hadn't been fun like he thought.

Now every movement he made, he made with care. There was a new feeling in his chest...or his stomach. A
heaviness.
And now the idea that she might run from him and it would be his own fault made him want to clutch her closer
than ever.
Yet his sweet human would be blameless if she feared him now.

Seeing her flinch from him had made him realize the damage that had been done with his own hands.
What he said was a mistake.
Instead of encouraging her to fight harder it had scared her.

He wouldn't apologize; but he could try and fix what he had broken. Slowly.


## Chapter 57: Need Some Space
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for notes.)
## Chapter Text

Chapter 57: Need some space


Uta awoke before Aika.
His body tensed and on high alert; arms wrapped tight around his woman.
Some noise or smell had woken him.

Now he stared wide-eyed into the dark, his kagune restless and ready to erupt from his Kakuhou in case he needed
to protect his territory and his Aika.

Yet nothing seemed out of place.
He couldn’t hear or smell anybody in the apartment moving around.
His human was still beside him; nestled safely in his arms. Her body warm; her heart beating.

Then there was a small whimper in the dark.

The woman in his arms pulled herself closer to him; face nuzzling into his chest and hands gripping his shirt he
had crawled into bed still wearing.

Uta relaxed.

That must have been what it was; It had been her . Some beast in her dreams had made her call out and he had
woken to defend her from the monsters.

Aika whimpered in her sleep; tears gathering around her eyes wetting his chest when they fell.

“Uta—please—”


She was still asleep.

That strange heaviness in him turned and twisted in his gut. Were the monsters in her mind wearing his face?

Uta’s hand moved to hold her head, petting through the locks and attempting to soothe her back to more peaceful
dreams.



## ♥


When I woke I still felt tired.

I couldn’t remember what I had dreamed of, but my head and my eyes hurt. The beginnings of a migraine.

I stretched out, hand passing over the empty spot beside me.


Uta’s body was missing from my side when I woke and I wondered if he had left me before I woke up because of
what happened the night before.


Was it because I hadn’t had fun or played with him like he wanted?

I spent some time just laying still in bed and thinking through everything that happened the night before.

The thoughts of last night mixed in with the memories of months before when he saved me on the bridge from
the Doves.


I am stronger now than I was before. After all that training I knew I could fight that man who had been attacking
me. Perhaps I could have defended myself without needing Ms. Kirin’s help. Uta never would have had to do what
he did.


Grabbing Uta’s pillow I pulled it towards me, holding it close. With eyes closed tight I started to rifle through the
box of memories I’d set aside. There was so much that had happened after I met him but like a forgotten doom-box
I had shoved it under the bed and hoped to forget about it.
But it was all still here, festering.

My old boss coming to attack me kicked off everything; hadn’t it? The moment I cracked his skull with a pipe.
The sickening crack still rang in my head and had been a bell to start everything—

Running to Uta with bloody hands and having him welcome me in.
Learning he was a Ghoul. Feeding him food when he was hurt. Learning to be okay with it.

Then as soon as I began to relax and get used to how things were, Ghouls attacked the cafe.

I only survived out of luck while a friend was kidnapped, tortured and never returned home.

The way Uta would murder anybody who threatened me. The mugger, the ghoul in the street. Their bodies
ended up in Uta’s fridge; in Uta.

The Doves; when they chased us through the streets.

Of course some of his friends didn’t approve of us when we started dating for real. Dealing with Roma. She
had seemed to make it her job to torment me or drive me away any way she could.
## The Doves. Again.

All the blood on my hands when I cut Renji; each and every time I worried that I’d hit something bad and he’d
really be hurt.

Finding out my uncle was a Ghoul.
That I could end up turning into one myself.

I took a deep breath of our mixed scents and relaxed further into the bed, stretching out. Uta saying things like he
could eat me wasn’t what scared me. For just a split moment I hadn’t recognized him as my ghoul. My protector.


On the other hand; how could he expect me to fight like he could? Even if it was in my blood I wasn’t strong like
him or the rest of the Ghouls.
I’d just gotten the weapon.
I needed practice.
What I needed was a chance to just swing it around and get used to the feeling without the threat of physical-
bodily harm.

I carefully re-packed the mental box; neatly laying everything in it and closing the lid. Placing it under the bed for
later. I should talk to someone; but who?

## Renji? No.
Itori was a no as well. I loved her; but she wasn’t someone I could go with this.
Touka would listen, but she was too young and busy with school. I didn’t want to weigh her mind down with my
own troubles.

The muscles in my back ached when I finally moved.

When I changed my clothing I saw that I had black and blue marks across the skin once again. Though, funny
enough, the marks weren't nearly as bad as when he had made it his mission to have me pressed up against the
different surfaces of his apartment.

While I expected to train more today, I had to stay in decent condition for work the day after. Yoshimura liked me;
but even he likely had limits on the number of days his staff could call out. Especially due to injury.

I slipped into comfortable clothing in the bedroom and into my shoes at the front door.

I fed Bjorn and pet him but skipped my own breakfast. Grabbed my umbrella on the way, I walked down the
stairway.

Uta was exactly where I expected him to be; bent over his work.


I saw as I walked down the stairs the subtle way he would turn his head when I arrived in the room. An almost
unnoticeable acknowledgment of my presence.

He went back to his work just as soon as he noticed I was there, without a word of greeting.

“Uta...” I say to draw more of his attention and his head rises and turns so I can see his eyes. “Good morning.”

“Ah, good morning Aika...”

“You didn’t wake me up when you got up?”

“I got up early and your body needs rest...”

I pouted a bit and walked up beside him.

First I put the hot coffee on his desk and then planted my hands on the back of his chair.

“You know...I’m actually not that beat up. I was thinking that I should train a little every day. You are
right...training is fun sometimes...but—” Not the way he had made it last night. Never like that again.

The ghoul nodded at a box on the desk where I usually sat by the side and watched him. “...I brought you donuts
Ai-chan...” I frowned at the box, confused.

First he ordered me pizza after fucking me black and blue. Now he was going out early and grabbing me donuts
from the bakery? I knew for sure he must have gone and gotten them himself; and I also knew the bakery wasn’t
someplace he could normally stand the smell of.

I picked up the box and popped the lid, glancing in it to see what he had grabbed.

He had gotten ordinary glazed donuts.

Nothing special, but I felt my mouth water looking at the glistening glazing drizzled over the pastries.


I looked up at what he was working on, hovering over his shoulder and watching his hands sketch out mask
shapes all across the papers.


“Thanks Uta...” I placed the donuts back down on the desk. “I’m going to go out— alone . I’ll be alright. I’ll bring
my umbrella and I’ll be in the 20th anyway. Okay? I’ll send a message if I end up taking a while.”

Already I had decided where I was heading. There was at least one person who might give me advice when I asked
for it. A listening ear when I needed it.

Uta barely glanced at me when I went to the door. “....Okay.”

Once I was a distance from the shop I pulled out my phone and hit a contact on the screen. Lifting it I heard a
familiar voice answer on the other end.

“...Mr. Yoshimura...I was wondering if I could talk to you?”

## ♥


The old man was dressed in only slightly more casual clothing when I met him on the street near to Anteiku. A
brown coat and a matching hat; a patterned lightweight scarf around his neck. He smiled as I approached.

“Ah, good morning Ms. Aika...It’s good to see you.”

“I’m sorry if I’m interrupting your morning, Sir...I couldn't think of a single person better to talk to.”

“Not at all, I was just about to go pick up some things we need for the café. If you don’t mind helping, I would be
happy to listen over a cup of coffee?”

“Sure, I’d be happy to help.” I could use the time away from Uta.

I began to follow the manager as he turned and started walking down the street.

It was quiet, but peaceful walking through the 20th ward. I watched as birds flew from each of the little trees
planted to bring greenery and  life into the ward.
Once in a while Yoshimura stopped in stores; picked up napkins, soap or some other common item that was
needed.

“...Sir, forgive me for asking. But what do you do when you're not working at the cafe?”

“Don’t apologize my dear, It’s quite alright to ask. I enjoy reading.” I remembered his books he had asked me to
organize for him.

“I remember now; you're a Sen Takatsuki fan. Right? All those books you had me organize were from her...I think
you had every single one...” I pursed my lips as I thought. “---actually you know a new book is coming out soon?
Or maybe it already has—It’s...July? I think was supposed to be released in June. If you don’t have it already, we
can check the bookstore!”

“I would love that.” I smiled and relaxed more, walking with him to the bookstore.

Glancing across the street I spotted a music store and paused in the doorway of the bookstore. There were guitars
in the window and stacks upon stacks of records. Metal music notes hung on wires; glittering in the sun.

“Ms. Aika?”

“Huh? Oh sorry. I’m coming...” I followed into the store and breathed in deeply. The smell of ‘ bookstore’ was
always so nice. I gazed around the shelves while Yoshimura went for the second with new books.“I was just
distracted. I didn't realize there was a shop like that here.”

“I believe it opened recently. Do you play an instrument, Ms. Aika?” The old man had picked up a book and I saw
the name S. Takatsuki on the front of it. So it has come out!  I looked at his face, solemn despite holding his favorite
author's newest book.
Odd. I really thought he’d be happier.

“I...Well I did. When I was a kid—” I answered his question. “I thought about picking it back up a few times. I
also drew and painted and Uta’s been getting me supplies and trying to get me to do that again. I think he likes the
amount of color I use. It’s been good—away from my old home I’m able to do those things without it...being for
someone else? Actually my uncle plays too. Visiting him reminded me.”

“That’s good.”

“Did you find the book...?”

“I did. Thank you for reminding me. I must have missed it in my old age.” I smiled and giggled softly.

“Not a problem! Since I know you like her I’ll keep an eye out. Maybe she’ll do a signing in a shop nearby and you
could get them autographed!”

The old man smiled faintly and went back to the front of the store; paying for his book and heading out with me
in tow.
I nearly bumped into him when he stopped; my eyes were on the music shop. “Why don’t we stop Ms.
Aika...Perhaps you’ll find something new to pick up.”

I glanced from the music shop and then back to the old man who stood there with bags in hand, smiling at me.
“Sure...if you don’t mind, Sir.”

“Not at all.”
He followed me as I walked across the street, peering in the front window and then opened the front door. A bell
chimed and I held the door for Yoshimura before stepping in.
The air was cool and free of humidity. Better for instruments and records.

Yoshimura went for the records immediately, flipping through them and picking out some that must have been
familiar to him. Perhaps he listened to them when he was younger. Actually a record player in the cafe might be
nice.

“Hey—I mean welcome! Hold on—I’m just setting up some things.”

I heard a man speak from another room.
A man who couldn’t be older than me or Uta stuck his head out from the backroom and smiled. His hair was
messy and when he came out from the back wiping his hands on his pants I saw he was dressed in jeans and a
graphic tee layered over a long sleeve.
“Welcome—the shop’s kinda new and I’m still setting up some things set up.  I’m sorry for the mess. Is there
something I could help you with?”

“I just noticed the shop today. I used to play...I just wanted to have a look around.”

“Oh...what did you use to play?”

“Uh—” I laughed awkwardly and considered my answer: “A...lot of things actually? But I was thinking I could get
a guitar.” My eyes wandered the walls where the instruments were hung.
One caught my eye, behind and above the man's counter. A red guitar the color of wine.

The man followed my gaze and chuckled.

“Yeah...everyone looks at her first. That’s our Gibson...Orianthi SJ-200. Wine Red. She’s expensive though. So if
you’re looking for something else we definitely can find you something.”
“Right, of course...” My eyes still strayed to the guitar up on the wall a few times while he handed me other brands.
With my hands on an Epiphone I strummed a few measures of ‘Boulevard of Broken Dreams’ which got the man
to give me a thumbs up and wink.
“Hey, that’s good. When did you play last? You picked it right up like it was last week!”

“It’s...been over---god...ten years?” I handed the guitar back and smiled. “Thank you. I think I’ll have to think
about it—but I’m sure I’ll be back!” I glanced at the red guitar on the wall again. I was...going to ask Kazu for a
favor.

The young man smiled and waved. “Hey—actually! Would you mind giving me your number! I’m new to the
area and I don’t have any pretty women’s numbers in my phone yet!!! I’d love to hit you up for a date sometime!
We can talk about music if you’d like?”

I paused for a moment, dumbstruck before I realized that the man was flirting. I laughed and then covered my
mouth.
“Oh...I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to laugh! I’m so sorry—I just wasn’t expecting— But I’m already taken. I don’t
think my boyfriend would like that very much!”
In fact the thing that was making me laugh was imagining what Uta’s face would look like if he’d heard that. I’d
have to tell him not to eat the bold music shop owner for asking for a date.

“Oh...your boyfriend—Right of course you're taken already! Sorry—”

Yoshimura followed me from the store and I couldn’t help but giggle a bit more once we were out of ear shot.
“Poor boy...I didn't mean to laugh in his face. I hope he makes some friends though—”

“You did not get a guitar though, were you not planning to?”

“...Yeah. I’ve gotta make a call—but that can wait till after I talk with you. In private.” About Ghouls. About me
and Uta and about the last few months.
I had some things to try and get off my chest, and perhaps Mr. Yoshimura was the best man to help me.

## ♥

I sat down on the couch that the manager kept in the sitting room, soft and comfortable.

The same one I’d woke up on the day I’d passed out from hunger. And now, just like that day there was a tray full
of sandwiches and a cup of coffee for me.

“Sir, you didn’t need to make the sandwiches! But thank you.”

“I like making them. And your stomach was growling, my dear.”

“Oh—I hadn’t really noticed.” I hadn’t eaten for a while, had I? Not before training. And not when I got home.
Picking up one of the little triangles I took a bite from it. For a ghoul, he made really good food!

“What was on your mind, dear?” The older man sat across from me, a cup of coffee in hand. “Are you having
problems with Uta?”

“...a lot is on my mind. It’s not—No. Not like that.” I nibbled a bit more sandwich and thought. “It’s just...a lot
has happened. And it’s...starting to weigh me down. It’s not like I can’t talk to him. He listens to every word I
say...But I need advice that I think you’d be better at giving me. A different point of view? It’s been a lot.”

“Start at the beginning then, my dear.”

So I did. Starting with meeting Uta. Yoshimura was quiet as I recounted the tale. He only hummed softly when I
spoke about my old boss and his fate. He nodded when I told him about the mugger.

“...You know of course that Uta eats differently than we do here at Anteiku. I don’t feel like this was a surprise to
you. If it bothers you, you could try and change his mind. Though he is rather stuck in his ways.”

“Of course; I know. He always warns me before he goes and hunts. I’m either at work or staying in the bedroom
while he cleans up. I’m not—I wouldn't do that.” I sighed softly and slumped.

“...I must be crazy, right?” I continued, telling him about my recent trip to my uncles.
How everything had unfolded and then the bombshell: “My uncle is a Ghoul...apparently...so was my great-
grandmother. Which means I have Ghoul genetics...when he was younger his RC levels just jumped and he went
from ordinary Human to Ghoul. The family hid it...and he left the city. And the CCG.”

Yoshimura sat up and looked over me before finishing his coffee and setting the empty cup down. “...What did
Uta do on the bridge that scared you so badly, Ms. Aika?”

“I—I’m not going to tell you that part.” I said softly, looking at the old man's face. That part was Uta’s secret that
I wasn’t going to spill.

“—Sometimes the things that scare me aren’t what happened, it was how I reacted to it. At first I’m startled but I
got over it. I’m able to pack it away to think about later. It’s this guilt that I wasn’t reacting like a sane Human
should. Like a normal person. I should be screaming. Crying. I should be angry. I should feel scared and hurt. A
normal person would have run to the hills by now, right? But instead I felt welcome with Uta even with blood on
my hands. I felt grateful to Nico when he had helped keep me hidden. I felt safe with Uta because he tries his

hardest to keep everything dangerous away.” The only dangerous things near me were the things he invited to be
close to me; his friends. The Clowns.

I glanced out the window and frowned: “Instead of fear; I was happy and relieved that he had come for me on the
bridge.”

“...It scares me that the easy answer might be to let myself become Ghoul? If it was in my blood then was I ever
really Human? And what if I choose to stay human...I wonder what that sort of decision would make my friends
think. It’s not like any of you got a choice...”

I wrapped my arms around myself and stared down at the floor. My coffee had gotten cold in its cup while I spoke
at length. The old man across from me was patient and listened to it all. And now he was looking at me with those
ghoulish eyes of his—open.

“...I see. I suspect there must be a lot on your mind. But that is quite a lot for one person to hold. All of this has
been on your mind while you worked with us.” His tone was so sad.


Standing he took both our cups. “I’m going to make us another cup of coffee Aika. After...Let me tell you about
my Ukina.”

## ♥

“What are you working on?” I leaned on the back of his chair when I got home; looking over his shoulder.

He was still barely looking at me even after I came back from Anteiku.

The long talk with Yoshimura had made me sad . But it also grounded me. He shared his experience; as a Ghoul
with a Human lover.

The need to protect her. To keep her away from all the parts of his life that were bloody or might scare her away.

She had adjusted to his world despite everything. He had been surprised every time his Ukina had accepted him or
his world. In the end she had surprised Yoshimura with her determination and gone as far as to eat human meat to
keep their unborn baby.

“You love him...Human or Ghoul. Love has the greatest change on someone. That is the same. We bend further than
anybody could imagine for the ones we love...”


—And then he was forced to kill her. He was forced to miss her every day and the pain never went away. It had
become part of him.

He had asked me never to repeat a word that I’d heard from that tale to anybody; And I was going to keep that
promise.



“I was drawing some ideas for a new mask for you, Ai-chan...”

“But—I like my old one? There’s nothing wrong with it!”

“...I am glad that you do. But there’s an event in August. You should have a different mask for it.”
## Event .
One of those things that he left; disappeared with his friends and then returned a few days later. He hadn’t
mentioned it in a little while, but it seems he hadn’t forgotten he had invited me.

“It’s an event for Ghouls. So it’s a mask to protect me from other Ghouls...because Humans aren’t supposed to be
there. Right?”

“Yeah.”

“Is that really safe...Renji didn’t seem happy when I mentioned you had invited me to go along.”

Uta’s head turned slightly and his lips downturned a bit. “...Renji doesn't like them.”

“I probably won’t either...will I? And you know it. So—Why would you want me to go? If it’s not safe. If you
know it will upset me...?”

“You’ll be safe with me Ai-chan....I promise.”
“You won’t believe I love you until you’ve shown me all the worst parts of yourself, will you?” The words fell from
my lips before I could stop them. “...until you can prove to yourself that I’m not afraid of you. Or until you scare
me off.”

“You were afraid of me.” I glanced up at the front door. The shop was still open, so we had to be a little careful
about what we said. But as long as it was empty...

When I laid in bed for a long time, I had thought about what I needed to say to Uta. And more on the way home
after speaking to Yoshimura.


He had done something frightening again .
Yet once again, inexplicably I was able to put it aside because I loved him. I could bend for him. Somehow I needed
to say that to him and make sure he knew. That he understood that.

“I tried to think about this for a while. Since the bridge...with the...” I paused, unsure how to describe what Uta
had done. Instead I simply moved on. “...I wouldn’t say I was afraid of you Uta. You’ve said things like that before.
‘I could eat you’. ‘You smell delicious.’ ‘I could just take a little bite.’ ”

I smiled weakly as I quoted a few of his comments. He tilted his head back to watch me as I leaned on his chair.
“I know why you did what you did. Showing me that Renji was going easy on me and I need to work harder...I
understand. For a moment last night...you did scare me. For a few minutes I forgot that you were you. My ghoul . I
was thinking of all the things I’d miss if I died. And I stabbed you because I had to try to protect myself...”

“I just wish you’d listened to me when I told you I can’t fight you. It’s not just that I think I’ll lose Uta. I just love
you too much to even imagine hurting you. Whether it’s by making you bleed, or being the reason you're caught
by the CCG one day. That scares me.”

“—If what you said last night or anything else you do scared me that badly then I would never be so relaxed with
your mouth near my neck, or hold my finger out for you to lick paper cuts when I’m working on something. I
would flinch when you lick up my blood or look away when you eat. I think...that eating me just so that someone
else couldn’t, would be like giving me up. Giving up the way you like sleeping wrapped around me. Giving up the
coffee I make for you in the mornings before work. Giving up talking with me while you work on masks or your
other art. Laying around and being lazy in the evenings. I think you're happy with me here. You would miss me...”

I thought back on what Mr. Yoshimura had told me earlier in the day. The way he had lost his wife. It had been so
long, and yet the man was still grieving every single day.

“---So you might. You might hurt me. You might kill me. You might eat me someday. But...I feel like you’d fight
like hell before you ever gave in.”
Maybe that was all I could ever ask from Uta. As long as he could still keep me without eating me, he wouldn’t.

Uta opened his mouth as if to say something else and I shushed him by placing a finger over his lips.“—But I also
know. You want me to be stronger. Maybe you and I could train every other day; when Renji isn’t training me.
He’s got a life too, you know. You could just give me pointers while I try to figure out how to use that sword.
Or...if it’s not too unfair to ask; you are really fast. You could dodge while I try to hit you. At least for now. Once I
get better then we can try a fight again. I’ll try at least. Does that sound fair?”

I lifted my finger from the ghoul’s lips and waited. “...I would miss you. What if I do eat you, Ai-chan...? Would
you hate me?”

I hesitated, trying to imagine that scenario. Any scenario that I could truly hate Uta. “...I don’t think I could. If

you killed me because you were hungry on a Tuesday afternoon I wouldn’t be happy with you...But if I was killed
somehow. Or...if it was either you or me —you have to promise me one thing though, Uta!”

“I’m not going to eat you Ai-chan...I just wanted to know.”

“I know—But listen. Promise anyway for me! If I died and you do eat me. You have to take care of yourself. You
don’t do anything reckless and get yourself killed. Okay? And you don’t sulk in your shop for the rest of your life.”

He blinked; his face unreadable before he spoke softly: “...I don’t understand you Ai-chan...”

“...That’s okay, isn’t it? You still love me.”

He turned his face back down, looking towards his desk and the sketches he’d been working on all day. He
handed a sketchbook over his shoulder and I took it.
“I do...you can look through the designs and pick one you like; I’ll make it for you. Anything you like...”
“I messaged Renji on my way home—” I flipped through the sketchbook, looking through the designs. Many of
them reminded me of the Clowns. Of his friends' masks. It made sense that he would make me something
matching . But I wasn’t a Ghoul, or a Clown...so was that really okay?

“...I canceled our training today. I thought you and I could go running. Maybe stop in the 24th to swing that
sword around. Or we could stop over by the bar. You haven't been there in a couple weeks, Uta. Itori is going to
start feeling neglected.”

I glanced at the donuts he had gotten me earlier, laid forgotten on his desk. I opened the box and picked one out
and took a bite. Although older now, they were still good.
“Thank you Uta-kun...for the donuts.”

The donuts. The mask he was planning all day. The fact that he stayed quiet and at arm’s length all day. He gave
me space.

He’s terrible with apologies; but he loved me. Maybe he just didn't know how to react to me being afraid of him. It
was a reaction he was used to from other humans. But not me.

Even though sometimes it felt like it, I wasn’t the only one bending.

We were both twisting our lives around so that the other would fit in it.

“You know...a boy at a music store I stopped in today flirted with me! He tried getting my number and asking for

a date.”

I laughed at the way Uta’s head turned to stare at me. I would have to convince him not to kill the poor boy. He was
just new and lonely after-all.


## Notes:
I wouldn't say her fears are resolved. Far from it; But at least she was able to talk with someone about it! So it's
easier to put them back in the box for a little while.
Also I will have more on Yomo's 'kitten' at some point. It might be a side story I do sometime when I get muse for
it. :3

## Chapter 58: Side Effects May Include...
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for notes.)
## Chapter Text

## Chapter 58: Side Effects May Include...

I stared down at the sword in my hand and then glanced up towards Uta expectantly.

He had come with me to the 24th ward. No longer was he itching for a fight with me, instead he seemed relaxed .

Having agreed to take things slow and to help me learn to use the weapon. I wasn’t Renji, or another ghoul.
Throwing me into battle wasn’t going to toughen me up like it might a young ghoul. So a gentler approach would
be needed.


“...You know I have no idea how these things move generally...Except by watching yours...”

Then again, his Kagune was controlled by him . If only it was as easy as flexing a muscle for me .

“ I also saw Renji’s...But his is a lot different from yours...” Renji’s Kagune seemed to curl around his hands to
form his ‘gauntlets’. The other swords that the investigators used were also different. Most of them seemed to be
more solid than my own blade. Or kept a firmer shape more akin to a standard weapon.

“Every ghoul’s Kagune is different. Some shoot projectiles.” Uta answered, his eyes on the sword in my hand.

It was active as I moved it; its form flowed fluidly through the air as long as it moved slowly. Upon moving quickly
such as whipping my arm in a direction it would follow the motion and slice as surely as any blade.

“First you can try just getting it to strike at the column there. Later you can try attacking me with it.”

“Uta—”

“It’s just practice, Ai-chan. I’ll dodge.” Uta said softly.

“...Okay...but you'll dodge as if it were a real fight, right?”

“I will. Concentrate on accuracy first over speed. Learn how it moves.”

I giggled and the ghoul tilted his head. I could imagine his wide-eyes staring at me from behind his mask. “Sorry,
you sounded just like Renji there for a second! Next you’ll be telling me not to hit myself with it!”

“I’ve seen an investigator do that before...”

“Seriously! You have?!” My laughter echoed down the concrete underground and came back to us.

“He died.” Uta added offhandedly.

“Oh— oh . From...hitting himself with his own Quinque?”

“No...He just wasn’t a very good investigator.”

It shouldn’t be funny , but I couldn’t help the small snort of laughter that escaped me. His even tone somehow
made the delivery sound almost like a joke.

“Alright. I’m not trying to be a good ‘Investigator’. But I agree; no hitting myself with it...Got it!”


I turned towards the nearest column and exhaled to steady myself.

At least this thing wasn’t alive. Or one of my friends. Or boyfriend. It definitely wasn’t going to be fighting back
either.

I shifted my stance and swung the sword, sending the Quinque crashing against the concrete fixture.





## ♥

I spotted the man in front of Uta’s shop the moment we turned the corner.

Kazuha was standing outside the door, his eyes locked onto the sign on the door that told people that the owner
was out.

I double checked that neither me or Uta had our masks on and then sped up to reach the man before he turned
around.

“Boo!~”

Kazu jumped and turned around.

His eyes were wide and fearful; the blood fleeing his face left him ghostly white.

I bent at the waist holding my stomach and cackled loudly. Tears sprung to the corners of my eyes. I loved
tormenting him.

He composed himself rather quickly, though still seemed shaken. “....M-Madam...of course it’s you.”


“Hey Kazu—Did you get it already!?” I looked down at the large package in his hands and beamed. “You did,
didn't you! Aha!!! You’re great Kazu!—I might just keep you!”

The man glanced wordlessly at Uta as the ghoul caught up and joined at my side.

Kazu eyed Uta for a moment; taking in his appearance all over again. For a second his eyes settled on Uta’s and I
realized that the ghoul wasn’t wearing his stereotypical sunglasses. I was about to open my mouth and explain that
they were ‘tattoos’ when Kazu looked back at myself.

His expression didn’t give away any alarm so I closed my mouth. He knew about uncle anyway. Knew where he
lived and what he was. If he had a problem with Ghouls...he already would have done something.

He was paid well to not care.

“Of course Madam...You don’t request things often. I thought it prudent to bring it to you immediately.” He
said, not even bothering to mention Uta. “Though I admit I do not enjoy standing out on the street in this area...”

“We can go inside.” I plucked my own key from my pocket and unlocked the door to the shop, holding it open
for Uta and Kazu; the latter of which was hauling in a large box.

Closing the door behind them I giddily followed Kazuha to a table where he placed the delivery on and stepped
back.

“...Madam. I also brought these. After your visit to your uncle's...." He trailed off and allowed me to deduce what
he was speaking about.

He pulled a smaller box from his inner suit pocket and held them out for me to take. I recognized them
immediately as RC tests. "As well as these..."

Between his other hand he held a pill bottle filled with nondescript red pills.

"It is my understanding you were made aware of these. As well as why you would need to take them. If your RC
cells multiply too fast and too high you risk the chance of ending up like your uncle. However, your uncle might
have neglected to tell you their side effects..."

I reached out and took the pills and the tests from Kazu.
"Side effects...?" Uncle hadn’t mentioned side effects.

"I understand you may not recall your father's symptoms when he took them. But these pills can cause a number
of uncomfortable symptoms. Of course. You know the alternative.”


“The alternative is I change into a Ghoul...or develop ROC...” I grimaced, eyes on the pills as I turned the bottle
over trying to count them. “What are the side effects?”

“Because of your background, it is unlikely that you would need to be hospitalized for ROC...”

“You don’t know that for sure though, do you? My father never turned into a Ghoul with these. Maybe he would
have gotten ROC instead, right?”

I frowned at the pills and then glanced upwards at Kazu. He averted his gaze away from me for a moment; his eyes
strayed to the masks along the walls.

Uta moved to his desk, making himself comfortable and picking up his drawing pad. His eyes never left Kazu
though; the red irises followed the blonde man across the room.

I put the pills and tests aside safely and went to the large package on the table. As I trailed my fingers over it I had
to ask a question that occurred to me recently.


“I should have asked sooner but...Kazu. You never told me what exactly happened to them. You said it was an
accident...And the news wasn’t very specific about it either.”

“You never asked, Madam. It was my understanding that you did not care. It was also suggested heavily that I am
not at liberty to disclose information...unless specifically prompted for it.”

Unless specifically prompted. Hiroshi had probably told him not to say anything unless I asked. That means if I
order him to tell me, he would.

“I don’t really care. I wasn’t close with them. But tell me anyway if it relates to that in any way.” I nodded towards
the pills I’d set aside.

Kazu glanced at it then back at myself. He inclined his head in a subtle bow and began to speak.


“Very well. At your request madam. Your father took those pills for over twenty years without fail. Until late last
year when he missed a dose on a long flight back to Japan. Mid-flight he changed and proceeded to kill and eat
your mother, two other friends who had taken the trip with them and the staff serving them. The pilot and copilot
were locked in the front and thus landed the plane safely. Your father was found dead when they unsealed the
plane. It is presumed that after he realized what he’d done; he killed himself...”

Kazuha didn’t mince words. He didn’t pause or stumble over his words. He didn’t make it sound pretty or nicer.
He just told the truth; stark and awful as it was.

“...I—” I eyed the pills on the desk and swallowed thickly.

What could I possibly say to that?

I expected it was some car accident. Maybe they got attacked by Ghouls. Maybe they  were attacked by some other
company who wanted to get rid of competition. But I hadn't expected that.

“So...w-what were the side effects?”


“...headaches, fatigue, muscle weakness, stomach pain, vomiting, nausea, parosmia, parageusia, a loss of appetite, a
decreased immune response, and thinning of your blood...It's recommended that you simply keep an eye on your
RC cell levels unless they are at a critical level. That being said...those pills may slow them. Even stop them for a
very long time. But they don't reverse the damage once it's done...and stopping them suddenly could cause an
undesired effect ."

That was a lot of things that went with taking those pills. But then again imagining my father changing and
ripping into the woman he had loved was awful, even if I didn’t much care for them—

Father had really loved my mother, even if they hadn’t treated me well.
And he still did that to her...?

“Parageusia...parosmia?” I asked quietly, not recognizing the words in the list of symptoms.

“Changes in your senses of taste and smell. Your father described most foods as ‘bitter’ or ‘metallic’...Now. If you
don’t have any further need for me, I should be leaving. Madam, I will send you the documents you asked for
shortly. It’s taken some time to gather them all. As well as some I need you to sign and return.”

Yeah. The less he was seen around the real me the better. “Right...yeah. Thank you for bringing me this.”

“...It was my pleasure Madam. If you need anything else feel free to message me.”


I watched Kazu leave and stared at the door for a long time after. I shook my head, breaking the spell and grabbed
up the pills and the tests. “I’m going to put these with the other tests...”

“What’s in the box, Ai-chan?” Uta lifted his pencil from his sketchbook and I followed his gaze to the large box.
Slowly a small smile played across my lips.

“Ah– that. I told you I went to the music store before...I had Kazu pick something I wanted up. It...would have
been weird to pick it up myself... ” More quietly and quickly I muttered: “...itwasalittleexpensive...”

The ghoul blinked and cocked his head and I sighed.

“I don’t normally buy frivolous things but...”

I pocketed the tests and pills and went to the package, tearing off the outer paper and then opening the box.

Inside was a nice leather case with gold clips. Unhooking them I opened it to the smell of leather and well oiled
wood. I took a deep breath of the scent and picked up the wine red Gibson guitar. My fingers barely strumming
across the strings and I sighed wistfully at the sound.

“It was too pretty... I couldn’t resist . Anyway, it’s not like my parents ever got me anything I actually wanted.
So...it won’t hurt to buy something once in a while...”

“You couldn't pick it up yourself...How expensive was it?”

I drummed my fingers across the guitar's wood and avoided looking at Uta as I muttered the price. The ghoul
leaned in closer when he couldn’t hear me say it the first time.

“Well I could have. But it might have seemed a bit odd. Since it’s quite a lot of money...About...900,000 yen...” I
repeated, speaking just a bit louder. I watched his expression and saw his eyebrows lift just a tiny bit. “And if I
went myself that boy would have been there...I figured we should avoid the shop so he didn’t try flirting again.
## Right?”

I glanced up at the ghoul and smiled faintly as I continued to lightly strum my fingers over the strings.

“...I haven't really mentioned it but...if there's anything you need for your shop. I could always get you the money.
Or pay your rent? Get you some supplies for masks? Anything...?”


Honestly I didn’t need to work at the cafe anymore...but I wanted to. I generally didn’t touch the money from the
company—except for this one little thing.

“You don’t have to Ai-chan...can you play while I work? I’m finishing up the sketches of your new mask...you can
pick out one you like the most.”

I beamed, my heart swelling with happiness as I nodded excitedly. “Of course! Did you remember I still wanted
horns or antlers?”

The ghoul nodded his head, bent over his sketchbook.

I took a seat nearby, got comfortable and began to strum away at a song: Nandemonaiya.

Uta continued to work through each and every song I played and customers came and went.

## ♥



## Notes:
(A slightly shorter chapter for today--- the next parts probably going to be longer. And...oof. Yeah. Prepare for
some feelings on the next chapter I think.)
But, yeah. We finally learn what happened to her parents.
*sprinkles in ghoul trauma.*
Yup Ai-chan. Even people who love each other can hurt and kill each other. The world is terrible, isn't it? (☞ﾟヮﾟ
