## Chapter 59: A Reason To Fight
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text

## Chapter 59: A Reason To Fight

## Two Weeks Later...


I balked before the edge and the gap between the two buildings. There was easily a forty foot drop if I missed the
next rooftop. Uta leapt across the gaps, no sweat. Try as I might, I couldn’t keep up with him and he always ended
up looking back across the gap, waiting for me to follow or catch up.

“Trust me Ai-chan...”

Right. Trust him. When I had told Uta I wanted to go running with him on the days that I wasn’t training with
Renji I hadn’t expected him to have us running on the rooftops. But here I am, two weeks later and throwing
myself from one building to the next.

I backed up as far as I could and took a breath. Preparing to throw myself off it.
Charging forward I ran as fast as I could, planted my foot firmly on the edge and flung myself off as hard as I
could; sailing over the yawning gap. Its darkness spread out below me like a maw ready to swallow me.

I felt my stomach rise up into my throat as the edge of the next roof seemed higher than it should. I wasn’t going to
make it. My hands missed the edge of the roof by a couple feet and I started to fall into the dark alley below.

“Shiiii—!” The alarmed cry left my lips, cut off as something warm wrapped around me and hoisted me back up;
over the lip of the rooftop.
My hands tightly gripped the muscle as it flexed around me. For a moment I hung limply, suspended and wrapped
safely in Uta’s Kagune.

“Caught you Ai-chan.”

“...You did.~”  I smiled sheepishly as he swung me to the roof. I held onto the warm muscle-like extension of Uta
for a few more moments. It wrapped around my waist and held me sturdy as I felt my feet on the ground. Only
when I let up on my grip did it dissipate from under my fingers and I was standing on my own again.


“I could carry you the rest of the way if you want.”

“No...it’s okay. Just keep catching me if I fall, okay?”

The ghoul nodded and started running again, leaping to the next building and waited for me to catch up. I could
make most gaps; landing on my feet and continuing to run forward. It was easier when I didn’t hesitate or stop but
sometimes the distance made my body hesitate. Uta was going slow for me and would wait to make sure I didn’t
splatter myself on the streets below.

He’d teased once or twice that he’d eat me if I did; but he caught me every single time.

I followed him into the 14th ward and across another large gap. My feet landed safely behind him and I let out a
short ‘whoop’ of joy.

“...You made it that time. Last time we came you fell.”

I walked by him, bumping elbow into his arm and grinning.
“Yeah—! I did! It’s getting easier. And I don’t know about you, but I think it’s pretty fun!~”

His mask covered his expression the same as usual but I could see his hair blowing gently in the summer wind.
Running behind him did have some advantages!~

“Hey...Uta. I just noticed your hair is getting longer.”

“Yeah. I was thinking of cutting it again.”

I curled a finger in his ponytail, wrapping it and then letting it go. Stepping around him I spoke close to his ear.

“Really? You could leave it—gives me more to grab onto!~”

I heard the small intake of breath and ducked as his hands reached to grab at me and pull me close.
Giggling, I jumped over the edge of the building. I dropped down to a metal escape staircase and then to the street
level; right in front of Helter Skelter's flickering street sign.

“Hurry up No-face!~”

I pushed open the door and walked in and took my seat at the bar.
After glancing around I took off my mask and set it aside. It was only friends here.
At the bar Itori was waiting with a huge smile on her face. I could tell with a glance that she was already a little
tipsy, probably on the account of Nico sitting at the counter. From what I’d learned about Itori, she really liked to
drink. However lately she’d made a habit of not drinking alone.


“Aika-chan! So that was you and Uta on the roof! I thought I heard two sets of feet! How many times did U-kun
save you tonight?”

The goth ghoul caught up with me, hovered close for a split second with his hand placed on my hip before he sat
down in his usual chair. He pulled off his own mask and set it beside my own.

“Just twice today. I’m getting used to the rooftops. Normally the ground is fairly flat and I never had to worry
about splattering on the concrete. But Uta-kun’s been running me ragged on his nights!”

“Oh—and you’ve got an umbrella tonight? Even though it’s not raining?” Nico commented, looking at the
accessory at my side.

“Never know what the forecast is?~” I cheerfully said, then added: “I havn’t seen you in a few weeks at least...I
guess they didn’t tell you? It’s a sword. See?” I pointed out the familiar grip.

“I had to find a way to carry it since they insisted. Uta made a special sheath for it so it’s hidden.”

“—Oh!~ That’s the Quinque. Itori might have mentioned something...and you brought that here? What’s the
special occasion?”

I pointed at Uta and rolled my eyes. Since he was the cause, he was going to get the blame. “No special occasion.
He...and Renji insist I bring it everywhere now. Even when he’s with me. So you can blame the Quinque in the bar
on him.”

“She’ll be bringing it with her when she comes with us to our event too.” Uta announced.

Itori glanced up from the weapon and raised her eyebrow. “So...he convinced you to go with us to the next one?
It’s at the end of next week. He brought it up before but I’m really surprised you’d want to go, Aika-chan...”

“...’Convincing’ me would suggest I knew where I was going.” I noted, leaning my elbows on the bar and blew air
upwards across my face. Pushing a lock of hair out of my face. “Apparently he wants to surprise me. I did tell him
you all had to agree that it was okay...”

“You’re bringing her even though she doesn't know about the Au—!!?”
“—She’ll find out when we get there.” Uta interrupted Itori.

“Uta!!!” Itori put her hands on her hips and stared at Uta with a dumbfounded expression.

“I thought you told her by now...this is remarkably dumb. Even for you. She’s not going to like it...you need to tell
her! Before we get there.”

I pursed my lips and awkwardly shifted in my chair. “Yeah. Well good luck convincing him not to be stubborn—
Itori. I’ve asked a few times now. Could I get a drink? Maybe you can help him with the mask he wants to make

for me. He drew a few options. But I’m still not sure which one I like better...I really want it to have horns. Or
antlers—”

I picked up my mask and stroked my fingers over the bone of its face almost lovingly.

“I won’t say no to a new mask, but if I wore this one what harm would it be? It’s not like we’re going to be on a
stage, right?”

## “...” Silence.
Oh no. I looked up from the skull mask.

“...right? It’s not like you're in front of a crowd?”

## “...”

A pink-lemonade cocktail slid in front of me and Itori smiled faintly. “About that—The Clowns play a certain part
in the...’event’. You might say....” She glanced at Uta and then back to me, thinking of a good way to phrase what
she wanted to say. “...’Announcers’?”

“So it is front and center. In front of a crowd of Ghouls?”

“...Wellllll...yes...”

“Where I—a human—shouldn't be!” I spun towards Uta.” You didn’t say it was on a stage! In front of a crowd!
What if they find out about me!?”

“They won’t.”

“I smell human!”

“I’ll make sure you don’t. You’ll smell like me. And you’ll be next to me the whole time. Nobody would dare lay a
finger on you with us.”

I pursed my lips and stared at the goth ghoul. So stubborn.

“You know, Uta! If you’re really serious about bringing her. We can make her smell different if we borrow some
clothes from Itori or Roma. Some contacts to make her eyes look like ours!~ It might not be a bad thing if the
types of Ghouls at the...’event’ think she is with the Clowns. I know you like being the show-man, but you could
also sit back on this and keep her close to you while we handle the stage! Itori, Roma and I are all going. It’s plenty
of hands to keep things running smoothly.”

Nico spoke, his eyes looking me up and down.


“That is of course if she doesn't freak out about where we are going...I’m afraid I agree with Itori on this Uta. You
can’t drag her there without telling her what it is. It’s rather cruel...”


I picked up my drink and took a few sips. Maybe it could help with this conversation just a little bit.
With a click I set down the glass and exhaled.

“I told you Uta. I’d only go if they agreed. They don’t agree with bringing me without telling me. So can someone
just...tell me?”

Uta was seated next to me on one side hunched over the bar, peering me out from the corner of his eye. On the
other side Nico sat two seats away, sipping his own glass of wine. He and Itori were looking at Uta expectantly.

And yet nobody said a word.

“Uta...I’ll still go with you. No matter what it is. I’ll go because you want me to go.”

If he was reaching out and inviting me to walk in part of his life, then I would take his hand and walk with him.
Even if he led me somewhere terrible. Even if I hated some parts of his life; I couldn’t hate him. I’d prove that I
loved him every single day if that’s what it took.

Yoshimura said love was capable of changing people; but in my case I wondered if it all was really for the best.

“—Just don’t...spring some crazy shit on me and expect me to just deal with it on the spot. It would just be easier
to tell me ahead of time. Give me time to scrap together at least the semblance of some sanity...” Roma was already
going to be there. Likely set on torturing me. I doubt she would have agreed to me coming if she didn’t plan on it.

“...it’s an auction.” Uta said simply after a minute of quiet; one ghoulish red eye fixed on me as he lifted his drink
to his lips and took a sip of the fermented blood.

“An...auction?” I parroted blandly. I didn't quite understand right away what was so bad about that.

“...It’s a ghoul auction, Aika. From time to time we, the Clowns, act as comedy and auctioneers on the stage.” Itori
answered, almost sounding sympathetic as she refilled my glass with some more alcohol.

A ghoul auction?
Where they sold—
....people? Human trafficking?

That’s what he did when he ran out to have fun?
I reached out, gripped the glass of alcohol and tipped the rest of the drink into my mouth in one go.

“Uh... I’ll get you more—on the house...” Itori said softly; standing near my glass and pouring more from a
pitcher. Her eyes turned to Uta and her mouth curved down into a more severe frown.


“Ai-chan?”

I was staring at my drink which refilled in front of me; debating pouring it into my mouth as well. Maybe it would
numb the part of myself that was screaming inside my head.  I could feel the beginnings of a headache coming on
as I stared at the glass.

“Ai-chan...?” I looked up.

“Sorry—I...I’m not sure what I expected...but selling people wasn’t quite what I had in mind. I figured you were
killing people...”

That sounded completely terrible too, didn’t it? I was ‘okay’ with him murdering people for fun. I leaned forward and
pinched the bridge of my nose. It made sense why he had known what to look for when he wiped away the mark
on my wrist at the club. He would know the ins and outs of that underworld type function.

“So...you kidnap people and sell them?”

“Not exactly, Dear!~ We’re just the auctioneers. Going once, going twice....that sort of thing. Uta likes being the
showman up on the stage. But I think if you're going, he should stay with you and out of the spotlight...We can
handle the stage.”

Just the auctioneers.
Just the people who announced the price of people going to slaughter.
Just the people who were the ‘face’ of the operation.
## Just—

“...Aika?”

I could feel their eyes on me. They must be worrying how I’d react to this.
I dealt with so much already, didn't I?

I felt dizzy. Light headed.
I needed fresh air.

“I’m...I’m going to go for a walk. Just outside—Not far.” Uta started to stand up and I held out a hand.
“Don’t...I’ll be just outside Uta. I just need a minute.”

I barely registered as I calmly slipped from the bar stool or grabbed my mask from the counter. My hand gripped
my ‘umbrella’ at my side as I exited the bar. I wasn’t entirely sure if any of them followed.

I just needed to get a little bit away and drink in some of the evening air.

I didn’t stray too far from the lights near Helter Skelter. Just down the street, leaning against the wall of a dead end
alleyway. Close enough that any of them would hear me if I shouted for help. But far enough that I could calm

down. Leaning back against a wall I took in deep breaths to slow down my rapidly beating heart.

Itori and Nico had been right; It was a good thing Uta hadn’t ended up waiting until the day of to tell me about
what the ‘event’ was. It was good that I hadn’t walked into it and learned what it was among a crowd; or worse. Up
on stage.

I couldn't imagine dealing with that on the spot. Now at least I could think. At least right now I didn’t have
Roma grinning at me waiting for me to crack. To shatter.

I would have preferred knowing before now. With how much he had insisted upon not telling me I had started to
imagine even worse scenarios than this. I thought he was killing people. Been resigned to that. Maybe I thought he
was part of those random ghoul attacks in different wards; the ones they sometimes called binge eaters.

A tiny voice slithered in one ear and hissed:
‘At least he’s not doing anything to hurt your friends, right?’

‘As long as the people in your life were happy and safe, what did it matter?’

“He’s not kicking puppies...or punting orphans off skyscrapers...” I murmured to myself, rubbing my hands over
my face. Well, at least I hoped there wouldn’t be any kids at the auction. The thought made my stomach twist. I...I
hated it but I’d have to ask more about how the ghoul auction worked. Why he and the others ever got involved. I
would have to try and understand why he liked it.

I remembered Nico’s words. ‘Uta likes to be a showman.’.
Maybe that’s all there was to it...



“HELP! Please! Someone—”

I raised my head up and peeked out from around the corner of the alleyway. The voice had sounded small and far
away but I still slipped on my mask to be safe. When I got the clasps and buckles set in the back I stood still,
waiting to see if I heard the voice again.

I could hear footsteps running. Getting closer.
Ducking back into the dark of the alleyway I clenched my teeth tight. There was no time to dart back to the bar—
the voices were getting too close.

“Leave me alone! Please—”

It sounded like a little kid...?
Was someone going after a kid?
Would a ghoul attack a kid or—

A few moments later a little girl wearing a mask sprung from an alleyway up the road. Her footsteps were hurried

but she was stumbling as she fled in a panic.

A pair of investigators were tailing her closely behind. A middle aged man, his slicked back hair starting to gray
around his temples. Behind him another suit followed on his tail. Their weapons were at the ready as they gave
chase.

I was wrong.

Two investigators, not a ghoul. And they were hunting a child.

I stared at the girl as she ran towards where I was hiding. Any second she would be past and keep going; trying to
escape her pursuers. I could stay hidden and they likely would never see me.
But she was too slow; they were playing with her.
Even I could see that.

Studying her mask as she got closer I felt dread and fear hit my stomach like a tangle of lead snakes. It’s that girl. I
recognised her mask. I’d helped Uta make it! I remember making sure Uta didn’t give her the one with
glitter!


Her mother had been so afraid for her child. I could remember her mothers words and cautious expressions she
had looked at me back then. They’d been having some close calls, and the kid needed a mask to keep safe. And now
here the little girl was; alone and running from certain death.

“ Oh come back little girl! We just want to talk about where your mommy went! She wasn’t very nice leaving you
all alone with us!”

“Sir...she’s just a kid—” I heard the second man say. His tone was uncertain, clearly a rookie who wasn’t quite
comfortable with murdering a child; yet.

In a split second decision I reached out from my hiding place and grabbed the kid around the waist and pulled her
into the alleyway. She fought, flailing her little body until I let her go. In hushed and hurried tones I whispered to
the child:

“Run kid... go . Hide behind the dumpster. I’ve got it.”

I’ve got it? Did I? I had no idea what I was doing.

I don’t care if they’re Human.
I don’t care if she’s a Ghoul!
I couldn’t just stand here and watch them murder a kid in the street!

I turned my back to the young ghoul girl and readied myself for the two investigators. My hand clutched hard
around the sword hilt and readied to draw it. The men rounded the corner after having seen me pull the child

from the road.

“Oh look here Rookie! We found another vermin to exterminate! We might get you a Quinque tonight after all!”

The rookie behind him spoke into a radio.

“Officer Tsukumo reported a sighting of a Skull Deer Masked Ghoul in Nakano, 14th ward. Engaging.”

The older man was grinning as he raised his weapon and charged forward; bringing a Quinque that was shaped a
bit like an enlarged cleaver down at me. I pushed the button the the umbrella in my hand, the sheath slid off and I
raised it to block the blow. It collided with the metal of my blade and I bent my knees like Renji showed me to
absorb the impact.

“Confirm Officer Tsukumo! Skull Deer Mask? Is the target alone?” I could hear as the rookie answered the radio,
telling headquarters information about what was going on. I knew I’d have to put a stop to that as soon as
possible. The less they knew about me, the better. I couldn’t let them call backup!

“No...she’s with a child Ghoul.”

“Bring her in alive. Keep an eye out for other Ghouls. She has connections to No-Face.”

I grit my teeth as I pushed the older man back and gripped the weapon making it flare to life under my fingers. It's
a bloody red blade fountaining out from the crystals. I took a swipe at the investigator and the malleable blade
struck off the man's Quinque and pushed him back.

Behind me I heard a whimper. I barely turned my head and saw that the little girl was ducked behind the
dumpster; her little mask peeked out.

If they got past me, they’d get her.
I’d be dead.
She’d be dead.

Damn it.
Uta. Itori. Nico. Come on—you have to hear this. Right? But what if the investigators saw where they came from
and reported it over the radio!? They could connect the bar to the Ghouls?

“How interesting. A Ghoul using a Quinque—Where would you have gotten a thing like that young lady? Rookie.
## Tell—”

I charged forward, flicking the sword at the older gentleman but twisting my wrist in the last second to send the
end of it at the younger recruit. Training with Uta had helped with my accuracy.

The tip of the sword punched through the radio in the man's hands and their immediate connection to

headquarters sputtered, crackled static and then died.

A moment later I was ducking under the blow of the cleaver and backed up once more; losing a few more feet.
Now only a few feet from the girl’s ‘hiding place’. No place to go. Nowhere to run.

“SHIT—Sir. The radio! She destroyed the radio!” The rookie was panicking while the older man simply grinned
wider.

“I can see that rookie. Don’t worry. She might be tricky. But we’ll take both of their Kakuhous by the end of the
night.”

“Sir they said alive—and No-Face. Isn’t he on the most wanted list? He’s S rated.”

“Forget what headquarters said...you get the little girl while I deal with this pest.”

‘The day may come when you will need to kill.’

Renji had told me that. I had agreed to protect myself if the day came. I hadn’t thought it would only be weeks
before something like this happened. Maybe being around Uta, the Clowns and even the Ghouls at Anteiku
meant I was on borrowed time. My hands could only stay clean for so long—

I readied myself, feet spread into a wide stance and waited until the men attacked. The younger man made a move
to step forward and I glanced at him and narrowed my eyes.

## THEY WOULD NOT GET PAST ME. ABSOLUTELY NOT!

Dodging to the left of a strike from the older man I struck with the Wakizashi. He lifted his own cleaver blade and
metal clashed with metal. The malleable part of the blade followed through though, continuing to wrap around
towards the investigator's face. I watched with sick satisfaction as his eyes widened in shock just before it cut into
his cheek.

He stumbled back, clutching his face with one hand and cursing. “You’re dead! You fucking vermin! You
SUBHUMAN TRASH! I’ll kill every single last one of you!”

Charging forwards I lifted my sword and swung it towards him.

Once.  Renji telling me to protect myself. I had to know more about his kitten.
Twice. Uta’s small smile he made just for me when he looked up from his work.
Three. How happy Hinami was when she saw me and Bjorn.
Four.   The old man’s sad smile as he told me about his dead wife.
Five. Touka begrudgingly told me to watch my back. She wasn’t going to be at work during the school season.
Six. My uncle happy to see me again after years apart. He would kill Uta if I didn't survive.

—turning the blade around after each swing. Each reason to fight. Each reason to stay alive! Pushing them back

towards the mouth of the alleyway.

Seven. The girl in the alleyway behind me, whimpering in fear.
Eight. Her mother who must be out there worried sick about her child.
Nine. I wanted to kill this creep.

This ghoul hating fuck who would kill each and every one of my dear friends if he got the chance.

The Quinque in my hands was whipping and curling so quickly in the alley that its tip cut marks into the brick
walls on either side.

“Rookie—”

I glanced over the man's shoulder and saw the rookie's face. It looked like he saw a ghost before he turned tail and
ran.

My sword swung the moment I saw the opening. The moment the older man realized his backup abandoned him
Crystal Lily slipped between the older man’s shoulders and jawline.
Separating the two.

The world seemed almost to stand still as the man's head fell from his shoulders. The Quinque fell from his hand
with a clatter.

The spray of arterial blood had only lasted a few seconds but it coated the alleyway. Dripping down the walls.
Soaking into the ground. Wetting garbage left behind and the bottoms of my shoes. The headless corpse collapsed
to the ground seconds after the head.

“...Don’t hunt children. You monsters...” I managed to speak to nobody in particular, but the sound was foreign to
me. Cold. Distant. Emotionless. Empty.

We would have to leave soon. Otherwise Doves would be swarming the area when that young man got a phone
call through to the CCG headquarters. I needed to go back to the bar and make sure Itori closed down fast and
made herself scarce so they couldn’t question if she’d heard anything. If anybody asked the bar was closed for the
night—

Nobody drank on a Tuesday anyway, right?

I breathed out slowly and shivered as I felt blood cooling on my skin. It stuck and dried leaving my skin feeling
oddly tight. It smelled. Everything smelled so strongly of copper. Metal. The air was so thick with it all of a sudden
that breathing the air was like tasting it.

I felt...oddly calm.

It was only a handful of heartbeats before a masked face appeared at the end of the alleyway. I stepped between the
child and the person silhouetted against the street lights automatically, sword raised; ready to defend her once

more.

“Dear...oh you are quite the mess—” Nico spoke, noting the corpse on the ground and stepped carefully around
it.
Itori came next, her face bare. She looked at the corpse with distaste before her eyes met my mask. “Aika! Oh my
god—what happened?”

Then finally Uta’s masked face appeared and my body finally relaxed and lowered the sword in my hand.

“Uta...thank goodness...I didn’t know what to do...I—”

“Are you hurt?” Uta stepped over the corpse and reached for me, hands cupping my jaw and turning my masked
face to get a good look.

“No...No—” Shockingly no. Not that I could feel at least.

I wasn’t hurt at all. I hadn’t had a scratch laid on me during the fight. The investigator had been so much slower
than either Renji or Uta. A comparison might have been insulting actually. To top  it off, his short range weapon
had been a bad match against mine. And finally he had mistaken my initial defense and reluctance to strike as
weakness.

“...there was a rookie who ran away. Itori, you should close shop and everybody should leave before they show up
with more....”

“Did they see your face?”

“No...no they didn’t. They thought I was a Ghoul...”

I turned away from Uta and his inspection, pushing away his hands as they explored my skin for any injuries. I
bent and grabbed the umbrella sheath of my Quinque. I looked for a place to wipe the blade on my clothes but
found none. I turned to Uta and grabbed a corner of his cardigan quickly; wiping the blade off before putting it
away.

Finally I turned to the darkness of the alleyway and bent down, careful to avoid kneeling in the blood.

“Hey—Kiddo. It’s okay...come on. It’s safe. I promise...”

I lifted a hand and picked up the edge of my mask, showing the child my face. “Do you remember me?”

The child poked her head around the corner of the dumpster; her wide little eyes behind the mask looked terrified
. I heard Itori speak up behind me:

“Is that...a kid...?”


I ignored the ghoul behind me and stayed kneeling. The little girl studied my face for a moment before her eyes lit
up. She stood up on wobbly legs and walked a few steps closer towards me. “Ms. Mask Maker...?”

“Not quite.... It’s my boyfriend who makes them. I just helped a little bit. You remember me though!” I smiled,
ignoring the way blood cracked across my face as I did. I had to remain calm in front of the kid. Even if I wanted to
throw up. Nothing was more important right now then getting her to safety. Back to her parent - if that were still
possible.

If it wasn’t...
Then I’d speak to Yoshimura. He would know how to help the girl.

The girl ran to me, arms outstretched and collided with me. The force almost made me tip backwards into the
mess behind me but I caught her, wrapping an arm around her as she started to cry. I stood up, lifting her up and
balancing her on my hip as she wrapped her arms and legs around me. Her masked face buried in my collar bone as
she sobbed.


“Shhh...it’s okay. It’s okay. You’re safe now. Let's see if we can’t find your mother. You like that mask? Is it still
fitting alright?” I spoke softly to her, trying my best to exude comfort. Calmness.

The girl nodded her head and I smiled before pulling my mask back down over my face and turning around. I
walked back out of the alleyway, past the three ghouls and stepping over the corpse without even glancing at it.

“We’ve got to get you cleaned up a little kiddo. I don’t think your mother would like me getting blood all over
your clothing.” Since she was clinging to me she was pressed up against the gore that coated my clothing, soaking it
into her own little white dress. Too late to avoid it though.

I stopped outside Itori’s bar, unable to really think clearly. We couldn’t stay here. But I couldn’t just leave with
this child on my hip. Her mother would be freaked out if she couldn’t find her kid.

“Aika—You and Uta go home. We’ll look for the child’s mother.”

I turned and looked at Itori, then the child who clung even tighter to me. Her small hands gripping my clothes
with a death grip.

“We’ll send her parents to Uta’s shop. Go...before more of them show up.”

## ♥

How we got back to the shop was a blur. It had been on the ground. The weight of the child would have been too
much for me to clear the rooftops. But the child refused to let go of me. When Uta tried to pull her from me she
had gripped so tightly onto me that it had hurt.

Ghoul children were frighteningly powerful little beasts.


I was soaked through with drying blood. I walked through the shop with flakes of drying blood falling from my
body. Up the stairs where I heard Bjorn whining when he smelled us coming. I went straight to the apartment,
bringing the child with me as Uta trailed behind overseeing everything. He wasn’t letting me out of his sight.
Distantly I wondered what he thought...

Did he think I would hurt the kid?
That the kid would hurt me?
Was he still worried about my reaction to the auction? It seemed like such a distant thing to worry about now.

I grabbed a blanket and threw it haphazardly over the couch before sitting on it. At least I could avoid getting gore
all over the couch. The little ghoul shifted so that she lay on me, her face still tucked into my shoulder and neck.
“Hey, kiddo. You tell your mother cold water and lemon juice. Okay? It’ll get the stain right out...”

“Okay Ms. Pretty human...” The girl sniffled. “Are they going to find my mommy?”

“They’re looking—and I’m sure she’ll come as soon as she knows where you are. It’s just going to be an extra
couple minutes for her to get here. But you’re safe here and that’s what’s important....”

The arm that wasn’t wrapped around the girl's back still gripped the sword tightly. Bjorn settled down close by
with his giant head resting on the edge of the couch; his eyes were on the little ghoul girl. Uta on the other hand
stood quietly nearby; eyes on the human and young ghoul curled up on his couch. Soaked in blood and both
trying hard not to cry.


“...thank you Ms. Human...you saved me.”


I saved her .
She was saved. She was safe and it was because I helped.
Finally I began to relax, body finally relaxing. I had to hold back a sob and close my eyes to avoid upsetting the
child further.

I saved her .

That was good. I’d done the right thing. I know I had. The weight of the still living child in my lap told me that
without a doubt.

“Of course. I wouldn’t let them hurt you...”

I’d do it again. In a heartbeat and without a single doubt in my heart about it. The man I’d killed had been a
sadistic fuck; gleefully hunting a child like it was sport. For a new Quinque? To kill a child? To draw the mother
out and kill her too—

If she wasn’t already dead...


With the tension leaving my body I started to breathe steadily.

Out of all the people who had died because of me; I regretted this one least of all.

## ♥

Uta watched as Aika climbed the stairway to their apartment, bringing the ghoul child into their home. Both
human and ghoul’s grips were stuck to each other. As much as he wanted to check her over for wounds—
Attempts to separate them had been futile.

He was worried about Aika. This couldn’t have happened at a worse time—
They hadn’t heard the girl's small cries for help over the music in the bar. If Aika had called out it hadn’t been loud
enough. It was blood that drew them.

But it hadn’t been her blood that Nico had first smelled and drawn them out into the street.
At the first cut Nico had looked up and frowned at the door. Suggesting Uta check it out. But when more
followed he was up and running with the others close on his heels.

When Uta had first seen her in the alleyway she was soaked in red and smelling of sweet human blood.
So much so that he couldn’t smell her under it all.
He recognised her mask before he recognized the human under it. Her eyes looked dead . Like muted and blunted
glass with its shine taken away.

She hadn’t gone far just like she promised, but she still ran into trouble. And he hadn’t been there. Yet she still stood
on her two feet; completely unharmed. She fought and she’d won. She hadn’t needed him to do something terrible in
front of her again.

Her demeanor had changed the moment she faced the child in the alleyway.
Calm. Comforting. Caring. She was putting up a mask of her own to try to keep the kid from weeping about her
missing parent.

Itori and Nico were looking for the kids' parents, but he knew how this story often went. He expected he’d hear
from Itori soon with the bad news.

But for now— The child clinging to Aika was keeping her from crying or breaking down. At least temporarily.  Uta
was expecting some form of shock to kick in at some point. She would cry. She would be upset.

She would have nightmares that kept them both up whether she realized it or not.
And he would be there to comfort her the best he could.

Maybe she’d like her new mask...he had just gotten in the horns to start working on it.


## ♥

IMMEDIATELY after? Yeah. That's the kinda night she's having.

It's a slow decent.
Uta! Your slacking! You can't let your girlfriend wander out into the night. She might find a
