## Chapter Text


## Chapter 63: Auction


I was surprised to find that the Clowns actually rode to the auction in a rather nice car. Its windows were tinted
and reflective giving the members inside some privacy. There was limited space however, so to avoid being pressed
up next to Roma I crawled up into Uta’s lap. Roma for some reason had decided to put herself next to Uta — and
by extension; myself.


I stared at her from behind my mask and studied her closely. Yet, when she met my gaze she simply smiled and
waved. Adding in an almost cutesy voice: “Heeeey!”

What was her game? We didn’t get along. She seemed to hate me.
Yet since the moment we got in the car she had started to act friendly. A little too friendly.

Nothing about that could possibly be good.

No-Face wrapped his arm around my middle, pulling me back against him as his face was turned to watch out the
window. They hadn’t told me where in Tokyo we were going. Instead of going away from the busiest areas of the
city, we were in fact getting closer to a major metropolitan area.

“Zeum Hall...?” The type of pull the Ghouls would have to have to clear out this place for an auction with humans
would have to be massive. On par with what my company could do. Or perhaps Shu’s family? In fact both our family
names were likely carved somewhere for donating money to the project.

“I haven't been here since I was young...it looks the same though.”

Someone with a lot of money was pulling some strings. That being said; there weren’t many people here yet by the
looks of it.

“Yeah! It’s pretty fancy, isn’t it! I’m so excited!!! It’s been a while since we got to hold it here!” Roma bounced
excitedly in her seat. Already she had put her mask back on.

“We’re early. I suppose we’ll have to help set up. Uta...Just. Stay with her? We don’t need her getting snatched up
by someone who might get a real close up whiff of her.”

“And Aika—”

“Try not to get snatched? As far as I’m concerned I am literally attached to Uta-kun.” I clutched to the ghoul and
saw Itori smile fondly.
“Right...Just stay safe, Ai-chan. And...don’t think too much. Just try and have some fun.”

Don’t think too much.

“Don’t worry. Zero thinking happening over here...” I managed to smile weakly. I kind of wished Uta had made
this mask full face rather than just my upper face. Then at least I could hide my expression a little better.

Once everyone’s masks were on we stepped out of the car. I immediately wrapped my arm around Uta’s and
walked with him; side by side as I stared up at the building.

“You were here once before?”


I blinked, breaking out of a trance when Uta spoke to me. We had made it to the large auditorium with the stage
down below the stands. I glanced around, seeing that we were in fact all alone in the building; save for some people
dressed in work clothes moving boxes and props around.

Itori, Roma and Nico had walked ahead, bustling off to work on whatever they needed to. I wouldn’t think about
it too hard, just like Itori said.

“Oh...more than once. This was one of the places they would take me. There was plenty of Broadway that played
here. They liked seeing the performances. It was always a reward for being ‘good’. And I made sure to be on my
best behavior...otherwise they wouldn’t bring me out again...”

“...You know—I might not seem like it. But when I was a kid I thought I might want to be one of the actors, or the
singers up on stage! It always seemed so fun!”

Uta glanced down at me, head tilting. Apart from the motion I couldn’t see his expression at all behind that white
(bird?) mask. Still, I knew what he must be thinking.
“What? You don’t believe me?”

He turned his face to the stage and then looked around. Still empty.
“You could If you wanted. The stage is all yours...” Uta walked me up onto stage and took a step away, watching as
my face went red.

“You want to hear me sing, Uta? You’ve heard before....when you tattooed my arm.”

“Now you’ve got a stage. It’ll be fun...do you know some Broadway songs from when you saw something?”

It wouldn’t hurt to sing. Have some fun. Would it?
When in Rome.

I cleared my throat and thought of a song to sing. One of the first and happiest and uplifting songs I could
remember word for word.  Don’t Rain on My Parade. It had annoyed the staff for months when I was a child.

“Don't tell me not to live
Just sit and putter
Life's candy and the sun's
A ball of butter
Don't bring around a cloud
To rain on my parade!!!”


I closed my eyes and smiled; throwing my voice forward and hearing it echo back at me. Thankfully the song had
the same effect it had as a child, trapped in the house and waiting for the next time I got to go outside.

“Don't tell me not to fly
I've simply got to
If someone takes a spill
It's me and not you

Who told you you're allowed
To rain on my parade?!”


When I was done I took a deep breath in, and out. Pushing out a lot of nervous energy with the air. A few clapping
hands made me jolt. A few of the Clowns had come out on the stage to investigate the singing and were now
clapping. “Wendy can sing!”

“...I—Yeah? I guess I don’t often. It’s not the best...”

“You sing in the shower sometimes.” Uta revealed. My half mask couldn’t hide the way my face flushed pink.
“N-No-Face! C-Come on! Stop it!” I closed the distance between us and lightly smacked his arm.

One of the groups of people in work clothes moved a large box across the floor. They dropped one end of it and I
heard a soft cry come from within it. A moment later a cry for help . All my good cheer drained and I stood still;
the hair on my neck stood up on end. There was a living breathing Human being in the box. Likely all the boxes.

And they wouldn’t necessarily be living breathing people at the end of the day.

I knew my friends must all be waiting; collective breaths held as they waited on me for some response. Roma was
probably gleefully waiting for the time when my psyche snapped like a twig. The best thing I could do was ignore
it.

It would be like the act I put on for the company.

Cold. Calculating. I could do that. I’m Wendy right now. I’m playing a role. I’m with the Clowns.
With that in mind—


“Hey, Klutz. Don’t drop those.” I snapped at the workers. They didn’t deserve to be shaken in boxes before—before
whatever happened to them happened.

The workers turned and stared. The eyes behind their masks widened and one of them stammered as they spoke
up. “—S-Sorry Madam! It won’t happen again!”

Clearly they only saw me as one of the Clowns.
Oddly enough, their reaction wasn’t dissimilar to the people in my family's company. They way they listened,
apologies and promises to fix their ‘mistakes’ jumping from their mouths.

I turned my head away from the group. The human, whoever was inside, had gone quiet. It was for the best; I
don’t know how much begging I could withstand. There would be more later– of that I had no doubt.

Turning back to Uta I continued where I’d left off: “---You can’t go around telling people about me singing in the
shower! It's not even that good!”

“It is nice though.” Uta spoke softly, continuing the conversation as well as though nothing at all had occurred.
However he pulled me close and leaned his head down to my ear to whisper: “Are you okay?”

“...I’m fine. I’d be better if you weren’t wearing a full mask.”

“...Oh?”

“I could kiss you rather than butt heads!~” A pun, considering the ram horns on my new mask.
He chuckled softly, holding me close for a few more moments.
The ghoul chuckled faintly behind his mask and stepped away, leaving me on the edge of the stage.

“Keep singing Wendy...I’ll be right here.”

## ♥

Keeping the singing going was easier said than done. I was ignoring the workers now as they filed boxes past me. I
sang over the sounds of whimpering or pleading. I turned my back to the way one of the boxes had a suspicious red
stain on it and one of the workers mentioned the ‘item had been damaged in delivery’.

I was also ignoring the fact that standing at the edge of the stage looking out into the stands felt so familiar to a
certain dream I’d had recently.

I stopped singing when I noticed some people filling in the upper balconies of the auditorium. They’re eyes
seemed to zero in on me and stayed there like I was the show.

It was time to join Uta’s side now; and keep myself plastered there. I did just that. Stepping close to Uta and sliding
willingly into the tight grip around my waist. Stay close. Was an almost implicit command as I followed his lead off
the stage.


Uta pulled me hither and thither, greeting some Ghouls and brushing past others. Most stepped out of his way
and gave us a wide berth. We got looks; some of them lingering before Uta turned his head and stared until they
backed off.

Most of the Ghouls in the seats were well-to-do; while others were murmuring about hoping to see their ‘items’ for
a large amount of money.

“My company has been doing poorly. I could really use the money...” That kinda sucks.
“I hope I can buy a child!”  I hope she chokes.
“I need a new pet!”  I couldn’t help but wonder what sort of pet. How long would that last? And what happened to the
last one...?

Uta pulled me to a seat, high on a lonely balcony by ourselves. Across from me I could see—

I leaned forward, narrowing my eyes and squinting.
His preppy purple suit, and something about the way one of the Ghouls across from us sat—

“Shuu is here...” I murmured to Uta, nodding across the way.
Uta’s bird mask turned to face across the gap and I could feel him staring out at the ghoul across the way.
“...You recognised him?”

“...Hum? Yeah. Not by his mask. But he wears that ridiculous purple suit everywhere...”

Uta chuckled softly and looked over at other groups of Ghouls in the upper balconies. I followed his gaze and
noted each one. Presumably they were all Ghouls with more pull and influence. And money to boot.  It explained
why Shuu and his family were here.

Many of them were dressed nicely with attendants at their sides. One notable ghoul was a very large, broad
woman. She didn’t wear a mask; instead she had thick black glasses on a hat that obscured most of her face. On
each of her sides there was a suited man in a leopard print suit.

It was by far the most notable Ghouls I’d seen all day.
I nudged Uta’s arm and tilted my head slightly at the woman.

“Big Madam.”

“There’s quite a few people not wearing masks...is that usual?”

“Some of us still want to protect our identities. But we’re all Ghouls here. Ghouls like Big Madam are pretty
recognizable.” Between money and her looks; it made sense that she doesn't really bother.

My eyes snapped to the stage when the Clowns appeared on the stage. Roma and Nico walked on stage, bowing
and playing the clown. The entertainment. The fun of the party. Juggling, dancing about. Blowing kisses into the

crowd!

Roma especially seemed into the game, I could hear her giggles all the way from the stage.

And the crowd ate it up. Their laughter echoed in the vaulted room.
It was Itori’s voice that echoed a greeting loudly across the room, quieting the crowd.

“Ladies and Gentleman! We thank you for your patience! Today we begin the main event! THE AUCTION.”

I watched and listened; but I couldn’t find it in myself to cheer. Nor to laugh, or even smile. I couldn't see outside
my peripheral, so as the first item was brought up on stage I had tunnel vision; only focusing on them. My breath
caught as I stared at the person's face, screwed up in terror, hopelessness, fear...

Please. Don’t do this. Please just let me go! Please—I’ve got money! Do you want money—?

Their words and pleas didn’t go unheard. Everyone here heard them just fine. It was the laughing that got to me.
The way they not only didn’t care, they were enjoying this person's suffering.

And then the prices.

I felt like my gut curled up and tried to eject itself when they started the prices so low. 1 million yen? One started at
500 thousand when nobody immediately bidded, the final price was just under 750 thousand.

A Human life was worth less than a guitar!?


“And the final item on the menu tonight!~”

I blinked, surprised by the ending coming so fast. A quick glance at my phone's clock showed me it had actually
been hours. HOURS of Ghouls having bidding wars over Human beings.


“A special item today! It wasn’t on the docket! But it’s a perfect toy! Easily trained as a pet!”

My heart sank and I had to swallow down bile for another time. On the stage stood a skinny little child. He had
short black hair and pale skin; not more than 50 pounds soaking wet. He was trembling and without even the
energy left to even cry. He probably had been since he was taken—


“...how do I buy something?” I turned to look at Uta with my jaw clenched.
“Wendy...?” Uncertainty. I could hear that much in his voice.


“Tell me. How. do. I. buy. something...Tell me or I will never forgive you for this.” I felt the words hiss out from
behind my gritted teeth. “Never. I will hate you for this...”

I couldn’t see his expression, nor could I have guessed it at the moment. But he reached and picked up a little
plague with a number 7 on it.

“Big Madam is in the game for 1 million! Are there any competing bets!? It looks like—”

I heard Itori’s voice stop, hesitant as she spotted the number seven held up in the air from our balcony. The show
couldn’t stop though, could it?

“Well...it looks like Ladies and Gentleman that Wendy wants to add this Lost Boy to her collection.” My eye
twitched but I forced a smile onto my face since I was in the spotlight. Collection?

“Do I hear 1.5 million?”

“Two...?
“Three!!! Wendy isn’t backing down and Madam looks like she might have to back down soon!”

Big Madam seemed to be getting agitated, but I didn’t flinch or pull down the number. The number seven hung
in the air regardless of the rising price.

A Human life was worth more...this was pocket change for me.

“It seems like Wendy wins the bid for Five Million Yen! Congratulations!~”


Congratulations. I wanted to hurl. Vomit up everything I’d ever eaten. Tear at my own skin until any of this felt
real again. “Wendy...?”

I didn’t answer Uta. Instead I stood and turned, walking back out of the balcony and out to the auditorium. By
the time I made it down most of the Ghouls had filed off to pay for their ‘items’ or into the other halls. I could
hear them all mingling and recounting the events of the auction.

“HEY! What the hell are you thinking, Wendy! You know you have to pay for the items! You can’t just bid like—”

Roma’s voice grated on my last nerve. I wanted nothing more than to shove her off the stage and watch her fall
into the seats below. Maybe break her back on a seat; But it would be useless...it wouldn’t really hurt her like I’d
like to.

“I need to make some calls. I’ll have someone make a transfer. Just tell me where it needs to go.”

“Heh!? Do you have that sort of money? What are you going to do with the brat anyway!?”


“That’s none of your concern Gypsy. Is it? I can do anything I like with them. I bought them, didn't I?” I
snapped at her, eyes narrowing behind the mask. “So they’re mine to do with as I please. Isn’t that how it
works?”

The small ghoul frowned, lips turned down into a pout.

“...you can’t set them free, Wendy...” Itori’s voice was softer; but she was also quite right.

“Of course not...” I sighed and pulled out my phone. “I need to make that call. Tell me where the money needs to
go. I’ll make arrangements to have them picked up...”

I took a small card and looked at the directions on it. I lifted the phone to my ear and waited.

It only took Kazu two rings before picking up. “Madam?”

“...I apologize for the hour. But it needs to be done immediately and it needs to be done without any connection
to me. Understand?”

“Of course. Understood.”

“...Transfer 5 million yen to an address I’ll be sending you. Make sure it can’t be traced back. Use a throw away
account and then burn it. Then send a car to—” I pulled my phone away from my ear and looked at a map.
Telling him the address of the pick up location.

“There’s someone I need you to pick up. A little boy. Make sure you have security with you, anybody you trust
most. Make sure they won’t ask questions...Make sure they’re from my fathers inner circle. Bring the boy
somewhere safe. But he can’t leave.”

“....Understood Madam. The transfer will be complete in five minutes. Would you also like a car to come pick you up?
I will send Merlin.”

“...No.”

“Understood Madam.”

“...have him on standby in the area though. Use Security Grade: S799 with special clearance. Make sure it also isn’t
traceable...”

“Understood.” And the line went dead. I hung up and pocketed the phone.

The Clowns were silent, though Roma was staring . “What was all that! And you can’t do that!”

“Says who...? For all you know I bought the kid for No-Face to eat. How is my buying the child any different than

any of them doing the same. You should be happy, Roma!~”

I put on a fake smile and leaned down to the small woman’s height. “... I participated ! Isn’t that great!? Surely
that makes you happy! Right?”

“ You can’t just buy them to try and save them!”

Actually...with prices like that. I could . I could buy every single one of them, in perpetuity. I could ruin their little
game until it wasn’t fun anymore. I could crush this whole operation I could—

But I couldn’t actually do that. Not without ruffling the wrong feathers. As it was, Big Madam might not be my
biggest fan for the moment. Uta would be upset with me as well; and as angry as I was I didn’t want him to be
upset with me.

My phone beeped and I looked down at it.
Personal Bitch: “Transfer complete.”

“...They belong to me, don’t they? I’m not even sure if I really saved them anyway...what kind of life could I
possibly give them while they are trapped...it’s like a cage.” I would know a little about that.

“...what’s happening over there?” I changed the subject and nodded towards the other room, through a doorway
where people had filed through. Where the large crowd of talking Ghouls lingered.

“Oh...entertainment. Food!~ All kinds of things, Dear!~”

## ♥

Uta had leaned down to me and suggested that we go home. But I had simply shook my head and without
glancing his direction declined . “Aren’t you having fun, No-Face? I wouldn’t want to ruin it for you. Let's see what
kind of entertainment and food they have? Hum?”

The words had felt hollow but Roma had taken them and ran with it.


Uta wrapped a hand around my waist and guided me through the crowd. It was...a bit like a warped festival. There
were a couple vendors selling—all sorts of things. Uta stopped at one and bought some piercings, which meant
they must be made of that special steel.

Along with the vendors, other upper class Ghouls were looking to hire people for personal bodyguards, a bit like a
job fair.

But mostly I heard people talking .
Gossiping. About anything and everything.
Big Madam. The Doves activity. The Clowns. WENDY.


I tried not to look when I heard my name spoken. Not once or twice. But over and over. And the more we walked
around the more eyes seemed to follow us. I gripped tightly to my umbrella and tried to remain calm.


"Bonjour, Wendy ! It's been quite sometime... hasn't it Princesse?"

Of course, Shuu and his father were still here. I was tense as the man placed himself in our path. Would he be the
one to blow my cover? Reveal to all that I was human. That I was a sheep among wolves? He knew—of course he
would. Even if my scent was covered, Shuu would always know. That’s just how he was.

From what I’d heard about him: If Nico had a strong nose then ‘The Gourmet’ had an even more sensitive one.

"I must say, I saw you across the balconies and I was so surprised to see my childhood friend among a crowd like this.
Even more when you bid! Congrats by the way! What do you plan on doing with the lil’ tike? He’s not much of a
mouthful, is he?"

Uta tensed at my side, leaning to move me further from Shuu.

"Oh calm down, No-Face. I'm not going to start anything here. I am over our little disagreement. Can't we let
bygones be bygones? I think we can agree for once that we are worried about little Wendy’s safety. I never would
have brought her to a place like this...I much preferred my little Princesse cute and innocent.~"

“Wendy, Wendy, Wendy! Here, try this!” I turned just in time to have Roma shoving something into my
hands.

“It’s so delicious! I made sure to tell the chef over there that you were going  to try it, you know! After you won that
bid! You made quite the impression! He wants to know what you think!”

Roma was beside herself; giggling like mad with a devilish smirk on her lips as she shoved the plate with human
remains on it into my free hand. It was cut so it just looked like strips of meat, finely cut, diced and splayed out.

“Gypsy—” Nico stopped behind the small girl, having apparently tried to stop her antics unsuccessfully. He
couldn’t help now that Roma had already gotten this far. And I could see the man she called ‘chef’ looking our
way. Waiting. Waiting on my reaction.

Eyes were on me.
From every direction.
The longer I stalled the more I imagined staring and whispering.


## Think.
## Think!!!
## THINK GOD DAMN IT!

How could I possibly get out of this!?

Uta tried to help. He reached for some meat—prepared to take it off my hands. However Roma reached up and
slapped his hand away.
“Hey! Don’t take away her food, you bit meany! It’s for Wendy!”

The way she spoke was loud, carrying her voice across the room and only serving to draw more attention. Without
any more time I leaned my umbrella against my leg and picked up a small piece, lifting it towards my open mouth.

Once more I found myself wishing Uta had made the mask full face. I might have been able to wiggle out of this, or
hidden the meat. But now—

There was nobody to save me from this.

I dropped meat on my tongue—It was cool. The texture was a bit like Sushi. A realization that made me think
instantly I could never eat Sushi again after this. Roma had ruined one more thing for me without ever realizing it.

Closing my mouth around it was sickening. I didn’t want to taste it; the fact that I couldn’t tell the difference only
made everything so much worse. The only thing that made anything better was the memories of when Uta ate with
me. When he stomached human food and made himself sick for a short time; just to fit in.

I remembered how he had faked chewing and swallowed things down whole to avoid tasting the food.

I swallowed it without biting into it, letting gravity take over and slid it towards my stomach.
Such a small amount likely wouldn't make me sick like human food did to Uta, but I felt sick.

Perhaps though, the look on Roma’s face was worth it. Total shock. Her mouth was open; jaw slack as she
watched me eat a piece of Human flesh. The last time she’d done this...I’d been able to reject it.

This time, without any other choice, I was cornered into eating.

I picked up a second piece—watching her expression.
Only to have this one smacked from my hand.

“Princesse, don’t eat any more of that garbage. Honestly, the chef should be ashamed. Allowing a Clown to eat
something so mid-tier. Méprisable!!! I shall have to invite you personally to my estate. You can share a dinner
with me and taste true beauty!”

Shuu...He’s so dramatic.

A little late since I’d eaten one already; but I’d take it. If there was one person who could have done that so
smoothly - it was Shuu. Only he could get away with insulting the ‘chef’.

I hadn’t forgotten our last encounter, but for now—
“Of course, Gourmet. Thank you. I’d be honored...”

Shuu grasped the plate from my hand and thrust it into the hands of one of his servants.
“Dispose of this garbage before it turns my stomach.”

## ♥

My phone went off and I looked at the next message:

Personal Bitch: Package picked up. Instructions?
Aika: Make sure he gets something to eat. Drink. Make sure he’s cared for. Anything he likes...make sure he has it.
He can’t leave. Nobody can know we have him. Try and find out about his family.

## Personal Bitch: Understood.

I’m going to have to consider changing his name on my phone to something else. In serious circumstances it
wasn’t nearly as funny as it had been when I put it in.

When it was time to leave I followed along with Uta. My feet hurt from my shoes. My stomach was in knots and I
was mentally and physically exhausted. Above all, I still felt angry.

## Furious!

## Enraged.

It came in waves. Calming down only to come roaring back.

Apart from a word or two to Uta I hadn’t said a word to him, or anybody else for that matter. I couldn’t think of
what I could possibly say. I wasn’t happy with the Clowns. I wasn’t happy with Uta for thinking this was a good
idea - considering the idea at all.

I was pissed at how low the prices were on humans....
....and then angry at myself for thinking that was the problem.

“So! Wendy! Did you have FuN! You even bought a human!”

I didn’t flinch from Roma’s question. “You didn’t like that I did that...”

“Well at first maybe! But you ate some too! I guess that makes you just as bad as us! You can stop hating me for
being a Ghoul!”


I don’t hate her for being a ghoul. I hate her because she’s a hateful little cunt. I couldn't tell her that though. I had
tried being friendly with Roma, and she turned it down. I accepted that. It was fair that a Ghoul might not want
to be friends with me. But her behavior after...was unnecessarily uncivil.

“I don’t hate you because you're a Ghoul, Roma...”

I glanced up from the sidewalk. “Roma!—stop.”
I reached, grasping the back of her collar and tugged on her hard; pulling her back around the corner. I pointed
with the umbrella at a street mirror that showed around the corner.

The Clown’s car, parked just where we had left it.
Only now it had Doves patrolling around it.

“...Curses. They really are out and about lately. I wonder what they’re planning...”

“Who knows with them, but our ride back is a bust~ Roma Dear, you have any other options?”

“We can kill them!” She gleefully said.


“Wait—”

“We’re not soft on them like you are, Aika! We kill, we—”

“---You're going to get other Ghouls hurt if you attack them now! They’re too close to the Auction—” I blurted it
so fast the words spun together. Then, slowing down I added: “If you attack them here, they’ll bring more...it’ll
stir the hive. All the Ghouls from the Auction would be in danger as they all go back to their cars. I can get us a
ride. Just trust me...okay?”

Roma tugged herself out of my grip and pulled away. “I’m leaving...The only reason we even got a car to begin
with was because of you!”

I dropped my hand and watched her go, disappearing down an alleyway and vanishing into the night.  A few
moments passed and I kept staring at the spot where she had gone.

“...Wendy. What’s the plan?”
The three remaining ghouls were looking at me for an answer.

“I...if you trust me...then I have a driver who can pick us up. He should be close.”

I picked up my phone, dialed in our location and sent it to Kazu.
“You don’t have to worry about him either. Merlin’s been with my family for a very long time...”


We kept an eye on the Doves as they looked around the car and up and down the street. I held my breath as they
got close, but relaxed when I saw a vehicle pull up. It was ours, no doubt. Black on Black exterior. The darkest
mirrored back windows. Nearly silent engine that ran on electric. Best of all, it was armored and had security
clearances that some of the other models lacked.

I stepped forward and pulled open the door to the back, waving a hand into it for Itori, Nico and Uta to follow.
“Please, I’ll drop you anywhere you like...”

Once they were all in I followed, seating myself down inside and crossing my legs. I didn’t care if my shoes scuffed
the leather. It was my car.

“Ai-chan—”

“Uta...no. I...I don’t have anything to say right now. Just—” I clenched my teeth tightly, my hands in my lap
turned to white knuckled balls. “...I don’t want to hear anything you have to say right now. Please...”

And the ride home was in silence.

## ♥

Chapter 65: Chapter 64: Fury o’ Fury
## Chapter Text

Chapter 64: Fury o’ Fury


## ♥ ♥ ♥

Uta had kept his eyes on his Aika the whole night. From the time they first saw where it was being held, up until
they were in Aika’s armored company car. Driven by a man named Merlin.


From the moment Uta heard the announcement about an item not on the docket he knew that he’d fucked up.
All the way up until the night before there hadn’t been any children on the list of items being sold. Not one. They
were a rarer thing to appear. But not unheard of.

With her reaction to the ghoul child he wasn’t naive enough to think she wouldn’t respond the same to a human
one...

But far up on the balcony he couldn’t do anything when that moment came.
He wasn’t the auctioneer for the night.

If he had been he might have known at least a few minutes before anything had to be said. He could have stopped
it from being announced and simply had it quietly sold.

Maybe he could have bought the child himself and kept him safe for his mate as a gift?
As soon as he thought of the idea he binned it. She would have hated that too. It was a much too ghoulish thing to
do; she wouldn’t understand that he meant to do it out of care for her—


The moment she had turned to him he thought he’d figured out what the feeling in his stomach might have been.
He saw her clenched jaw. Heard her voice; dead of any emotion. Her eyes were dulled. In that moment that feeling
crawled up his throat and burned the guilt and regret into him.

He couldn’t feel guilt for the things he has done, or will continue to do to Humans. But for his Aika, he could feel
guilty for bringing her to someplace like this. Everyone had warned him. Renji-kun. Itori-chan. Nico. Even
Yoshimura had mentioned being careful with her. When Roma had been happy to have Aika come with them he
should have known it would go poorly.

He had no choice but to hand over the plague and watch as she bid up the cost of the child.


Aika’s face was set into a grimacing smile.
She was trying her best, but there were cracks. Her sanity itself might be splintering under the weight. She could
afford the price, but she hadn’t thought ahead. She couldn’t have known what she’d done by outbidding Big
Madam. Now she would be known even more in his world.

She would win; Uta knew that as soon as she took the plague from his hands. There wasn’t a price Aika could
place on a human life. To her, each person had value. She would pay anything to keep the child from getting hurt.

Uta watched Nico move the boy back off the stage. He would be put back into his cage and prepared to be picked
up. But unlike the other items he would be given a kinder fate.

What that was yet, Uta was fairly sure even Aika didn’t know. He wondered briefly if she planned on bringing him
home with them.

He offered to let her go home. They could all leave . All this could end .
And yet she had spoken coldly to him. She didn't want to ruin his fun .

It wasn’t fun . He wasn’t having fun, not when he had to worry now. The thought that she would hate him—abandon
him. Slip from his life because he couldn’t change.

He couldn't bear the thought that she’d be just like all the other Humans and the world that moved on without him.


He couldn’t react. He could only try and bury it under his neutral voice and his mask.

## ♥

When Roma shoved meat in her hands and cornered her into eating it Uta felt something like panic join the regret
and guilt. He wanted to snatch the meal from her hands and tell her it was a joke. But there were too many eyes on
them—There was no stopping her from eating it.

He watched with bated breath as she slipped it into her mouth. Her expression was tight, knowing she couldn’t
express her disgust without getting more negative attention.

He found himself thankful for the Gourmet, despite Tsukiyama’s scolding.

## ♥

‘ I don’t want to hear anything you have to say right now’


All he could do was stay quiet, and hope that he hadn’t broken everything. Apart from glancing upwards through the
tinted glass window that separated the back of the car from the driver, he kept his eyes on Aika.

At least he could see the shine back in her eyes.


## ♥ ♥ ♥

I still felt rage boiling when Merlin spoke up from the front seat. But hearing the familiar old voice could still draw
me into conversation as we got close to the 4th ward. He had an American accent, despite being with my family
for some time in Japan.

“Little Miss. Where exactly do you want dropped off? This is a dangerous part of Tokyo...” I smiled faintly at the
worry I heard in his voice.
“I’ll be alright, Merlin. Don’t worry. Kazu sent you to be my driver tonight? At this late hour?”

“I’m always your driver, Lil’ Miss. As of a month or so ago, it’s my job to make sure you’ve got a ride any time you
need it.”

“Kazu put you on that full time? On top of driving for the company?”

“No, you're my only responsibility. Don’t worry though, Kiddo. It’s been kind of relaxing. Kazuha mentioned you
don’t call much for anything. And I’m not getting any younger, you know?”

That was true.
“You could retire. You don’t have to work for me forever.”

I could see Merlin’s face as he looked up at the mirror. He wouldn’t be able to see into the back due to the
reflective bullet proof glass, but I could see him. He’d aged a dozen years since the last time I’d seen him. Years ago
he had been salt & pepper gray. But now he has grown all white hair. His pale blue eyes sparkled and the lines
around his eyes crinkled from a friendly smile.

“And leave you all alone, kiddo? I couldn’t do that. Kazuha is terrible company. You need me!”

“But—”

“Anyway, Ms...Nobody leaves the company. Not ever.”

“...Merlin what do you mean by that...?”

“We’re entering the Fourth Ward, Kiddo. Are you all getting out here?”


“No.” I answered. I briefly considered telling the old man to only drop off Uta, Nico and Itori; bringing me back
to my old home. Or to the company building; wherever Kazuha would keep the boy. But I needed to get a shower
and get out of these clothes. I didn’t fancy anything Kazu would have picked out for me.

“Uta and I are getting out here. If they want to go anywhere, please make sure they get there safely. As far as they
want. Nico. Itori. Please get home safe...Okay?”  I smiled faintly, my mood still rather dower as I nodded towards
the front of the car.

“Don’t worry about him...he works for me.” Merlin, like the others, wouldn't say anything about tonight. Or my
friends. They all knew about my father. “---And he can’t see you back here anyway...”

“If it’s privacy you are worried about, if it pleases the ladies and gentlemen I can close my eyes while I drive—”

“No!” I said quickly as the old man jerked the wheel by a little tiny bit making me yelp. “MERLIN! Stop!”

A second later the car came to a rather quick halt and I slipped from my seat onto the limo floor with a thud.
Laughing, but also yelling I shouted at the driver who was laughing as well.

“You said—”

“You are lucky there is bullet proof glass here or I’d strangle you! We’ll get out here! Don’t do that with them!”

“At your command!~”

## ♥

I stepped out of the car after Uta and closed the door after myself, turning to watch Merlin drive Itori and Nico
off to wherever they deemed safe. They were safe with Merlin, I was hoping the same was true with Merlin with
them.

I turned and started walking towards Uta’s shop fairly quickly, limping on my sore feet from the heels I wore. I
knew Uta must be following me silently. In fact,  ever since I told him I didn’t want to hear anything he had to say
he had been silent.

I unlocked the door. Threw the keys onto a counter and went straight up to the apartment. I shed the high heels at
the door. Tossing them haphazardly into the others near the door. Second, I pulled off my mask and tossed it and
the sword onto the couch.

The bedroom had some more casual clothing I could wear. I picked up a set and walked back out into the rest of
the apartment. Uta was carefully taking off his shoes, lining them up near the door. I watched him look at my heels
and then slowly do the same with them.

I went to the bathroom, pausing at the door and looking back to find Uta looking down at the mask I’d tossed
onto the couch. When he turned his head to face me I turned quickly and closed the bathroom door. In my haste

and my agitation it slammed behind me.

...And then I locked it.

I went to the sink, staring up into my ‘ghoul’ eyes and finally letting my mask slip off. Gripping the edge of the
sink I grit my teeth and shook. I was so furious I didn’t know what to do. There were so many petty angry ideas that
swelled up into my mind, along with more violent ideas.

Some portion of me wanted to punch Uta. The other wanted to just scream and break things. Maybe The mirror?
Grab the soap dispenser and throw it across the room. Maybe seeing the broken pieces strewn across the room
would help me put myself back together.

I saw the hot angry tears well up in my eyes and fell down my cheeks silently.
How dare he think this was okay. Any of it. How could he! How could anybody put prices, let alone prices so low
on a human life!? How could he sit by and not react to a child being sold for food...? As a toy?

It made me sick to my stomach. How could it not do the same to him?
I wiped at my eyes, smearing tears and make up across my face. I wanted these eyes out—

I wanted them out. And I never wanted to see them again. Not on my face. Not if it meant standing by and feeling
nothing.

I turned on the water, made sure my hands were clean and then picked the contacts out of my eyes. I tossed them,
not bothering to save them for another time. I’d never go back to something like that again...

I pulled the dress off, and tossed it to the floor. The rest of my clown outfit followed. I don’t care that it looked
nice. Or that Uta had worked on it for days to sew together the ensemble. Let it wrinkle. Let it be forgotten at the
back of the closet, never to be worn again...

I turned the water on in the shower and climbed in. From freezing to burning I stood under the stream of water
even as it burned my skin bright red. Crying under the spray of water, I couldn’t tell my tears apart from the water.

I could do nothing about the human meat that I’d eaten. It had been too long for me to throw it up. I had to live
with the nauseating fact that I’d eaten human meat for the rest of my life.

I scrubbed at my skin vigorously; filled the tub with burning water and sunk into it. I would strip all the scents
from my skin and soak myself in the most perfumed soaps I could find.

I thought I heard someone call for me as I lay in the tub, water covering my ears as I tilted my head back. I didn’t
reply, but I peeked up and stared at the door. They didn’t call for me again though I could see the shadow under
the doorway. It waited for some time before moving away.

I laid back down and let my head sink completely under the water.
Holding my breath.
## 15.

## 30.
## 45.
## ...58.
## ....59.
## 60!

I lifted my head from the water and breathed again; wiping away water from my eyes. Unsteadily I slowly pulled
myself up out of the tub, wrapped a towel around my body and another around my head of hair.
It had been well over an hour, perhaps even two by the time I emerged from the bathroom dressed in fresh
clothing and smelling nothing like the ghoul I loved.

I’d cried myself out for now.
Shed all the tears I could. No more remained for the moment.

I glanced around the apartment, finding him quickly. On the couch, still dressed in his clown suit. Still masked
actually...

He was seated as he usually did, legs spread and lounging, but he held my ramhorn mask in his hands and seemed
to be staring at it.

He knew I had come out. And I knew that he knew that I’d come out.
But he didn’t look up and he didn’t say anything.

“...the bathroom’s free. If you’d like a shower.” I managed, my voice sounded hoarse.

Finally the ghoul looked up.
## Silent.
I looked away and found my teeth clenched together again. Still angry.
“I’m...going to go for a little bit. I’ve got some things I’ve got to take care of.”

“I’ll come with you Aik—”

“Why? ” I snapped loudly. “ Why ...? So you can terrify the child even more? Make everything worse than it
already is? I need—I need you to stay here. While I go. I’ll go and I’ll figure out what the hell I’m going to do with
that kid. Because I don’t know...”

My hands clenched and relaxed at my sides until I crossed them over my chest and gripped into each opposing arm
to keep myself centered.

“I don’t know what I'm going to do with him...What am I supposed to do Uta? I can’t say: “Go be free!” He’s a
kid . I can try and see if he’s still got parents, but since he was at a ghoul auction I’m going to go ahead and assume
they are likely already dead . Hell, I’ll be lucky if I find out he didn’t witness them being eaten. Who knows what

kind of trauma that could do to someone! ”

I took a breath and continued: “All I can do right now is keep him locked up. How is that better than what the
CCG does to Ghouls? I can make sure he’s got toys and anything he wants, but he can’t leave . I could send him
far away...but that has so many pitfalls too.”

“---and DON’T... don’t come over here.” I said as he stood up, taking a step closer. He stopped short and froze.
“...I want to scream. And throw things to watch them break. I want to punch you ...I am so furious. And it’s a good
thing Roma didn’t come with us... because I might have pushed her from the moving vehicle ...I am angry at
you, Uta. But I HATE her. I hate her so much... ”

The ghoul took a couple more steps forward and I watched, hands clenching tightly to the point that they left
curved grooves in my skin where my nails were.

“Aika...I’m sorry...”

“You’re not...” I hissed under my breath.

“I am...”

“You’re not sorry in the ways I need you to be...”

“I shouldn’t have brought you—”

“ No. You shouldn’t have—! ”

“—But I should have told you sooner.” I couldn’t look at him, but I felt hands cup my face and saw his stupid
zebra pants instead in front of me. “I didn’t want you to hate me, Ai-chan. I can’t have you running away. I don’t
want you to leave...but I thought you needed to see...”

“I’ve seen enough Uta. I love you. I LOVE you...I love YOU ...it’s not in spite of you being a Ghoul! That’s part of
what you are. But it’s just a part!!!! But now I don’t know if you love me.I don’t know how you could! How can
you love me when you can put prices on Humans...when they’re lives mean less to you than some household
appliances or things bought for pleasure and fun?!”

I grabbed onto his wrists and squeezed as tight as I could muster. Much too tight if he were a normal human but
he didn’t pull away or complain about it. I felt like crying, my breathing came in short puffs and my torso was
wracked with sobs; but liquid didn’t fall from my eyes.

“ I’m not special, Uta ! I’m not different from them—”

“You are—”


“I’m not!”

“You are to me.” He paused and since I didn’t say anything right away he continued:
“...Shouldn’t have brought you. I knew you’d hate it...”

“Uta, they sell children —”

“...there wasn’t supposed to be any tonight. I checked. I knew you couldn’t handle that. It was added at the last
minute. None of us could have known.”

“But there are children other times! Why ...Why go after kids? They’re innocent! They haven't even learned to
hate yet! Ghoul or human! They don’t hate ! They’re just afraid ! They’re just afraid, Uta... ”

I let go of his wrists and shoved with all my might against his chest. To my surprise he stumbled back. His back hit
the wall of the hallway behind him and he stayed there.

I didn’t dwell on it and felt the rage and bile bubbling up again.
“...What if I started telling you how much your body was worth? Wouldn’t that upset you? How much money
would they put on your Kakugan? Your Kakuhou? How much is your Kagune worth to them? What is your life
worth to people who don’t care about who you are rather than what you are? You hate them, but you’re doing
the same damn thing! ”

The ghoul moved from the wall where I’d pushed him back and stood still for a moment before asking:

“How much am I worth, Aika...?”

“I couldn’t put a price on you, Uta.”

“Then you feel the same as me.”

“It’s not the same...I love you. I still love you. Despite the stupid thing you have done. But I couldn’t put a price
on ANY ghoul. Not even Roma and I hate her. That’s the difference between us ...”

The ghoul didn’t speak again for a minute and I rubbed my face, making sure there weren't any tears.
“Get...get cleaned up. I’m going to go find out where Kazuha is keeping the kid. And then I’m going to go see
them...I think. I might stay somewhere else for a couple nights. Okay?”

“...You're leaving?”

“I’ll be back...I just need...just a couple days to sort some things out. With the kid.” I bit my inner cheek and then
moved away from Uta, grabbing some notepad and pen from a kitchen drawer.

“I’ll write down the address...you can visit. If you want...”


I wrote down my parents' old address. Mine now .

I placed it down on the coffee table, and after another glance at Uta I grabbed a coat from the rack, slipped on
some sneakers and left. I’d tell Hinami she could keep Bjorn safe for a few days. Something had come up–I knew
she loved watching him.

Uta would survive a few days without me.
Maybe he would decide he didn’t want me to come back. It was all just a game. That he really didn’t love me.

I glanced at my keys on the counter in the shop and walked past them, leaving them behind me as I exited HySy
ArtMask Studio.

## ♥



## Chapter 65: The Boy
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text


## Chapter 65: The Boy
## ♥

Merlin picked me up. Nico and Itori hadn’t wanted to go far and he was still in the area when I called for him. I
jumped in and told him to drive towards my old home. A quick message to Kazuha told me where the boy would
be kept. As it happened, they were keeping him at my old address.

“In the toy room.” I shivered as I remembered that place. It was where they’d put me when I’d made an escape
attempt when I was smaller.

The staff was waiting for me outside the building when I arrived. Cooks and janitors and many other familiar
faces. At doorway Kazuha stood waiting.

“Welcome Home...Ms. Kaneshiro.”

“Hello Kazu...”


“Madam, it seems you’ve had a hard day. If you’d like I can have a hot bath drawn for you, and some food made?”

“I...I already took a bath. Some food would be nice...some Niku Udon?”

“Of course Madam, I’ll have the cooks make it at once. However, I am certain you did not come home for some
Niku Udon...you are going to insist upon seeing what you...bought?”

I winced, then nodded my head. “Where is the child...and what have you found out about him?”
Kazuha waved me inside through the arching double doors of the front lobby. “The gardens aren’t the proper
place to speak of such things. Come inside Madam. There’s a chill outside tonight...and your hair is still wet.”

I followed the man as he led me through the home I’d lived in for so long. It was exactly the same. Save perhaps for
a few portraits that had been hung since my absence. Long ago I’d thought I’d never set foot back in this
place...and now I walk back in willingly.

Though now I wasn’t trapped...

“You said in your message he was in the toy room...Why there?”

“For the moment I think it is best. It is furnished for a child.”

“There’s no windows. It’s underground. It’s...cold and it’s—”

“Safe. It is safe there. You did mention he can not leave. I also assume you don’t want anybody outside of the
household to know he is here. It is not so cold right now, Madam. I will make sure to change the temperature
controls to his liking.”

I sighed and nodded. Still, it was a cell. I felt bad for keeping a child in it when I’d hated it for myself.

“As for what he learned about him; His name is Yuto Kutsuki. He is 9 years old. His birth date is August 21st.
And his parents are dead...”

“He’ll be 10 soon. His birthday is next mo—” My eyes went wide when I heard the rest of what Kazuha had said.
“...please tell me he didn’t see them get—”

“Killed by Ghouls. Though, I am sure you were already aware of their fate.”

“I...had a feeling. I had hoped...”

Kazuha continued walking, down a stairway that dropped us into subterranean levels of the building. It was cold
in the hallways underground and we passed my doors. To the servants quarters mostly, or the kitchen and janitor
rooms. Below that, the stairway leads to the other rooms built into this building. Panic rooms. And cells. And the
toy room.


“Here we are, Madam.” Kazuha opened the door by scanning a security card next to the door. It clicked open and
he stepped aside for me. I walked into the room and looked through the thick panel of one way mirrored glass.
The room was sound proof and only we could see in.

It was a buffer between the room and outside, to make sure a child couldn’t run past someone and escape. It was
perfect for this. Kazuha closed the door behind himself and stepped up next to me.

“Madam...what are you going to do with the boy? I do not think you bought him to feed to your boyfriend I am
sure...” I glanced quickly at the man and then dropped my gaze. Of course he knew. It had been obvious the last time
they had met.

“...Do you plan on adopting him?”

Adopt him?

“...I...I-I don’t know...I had hoped his parents would be okay. Maybe a relative somewhere. Grandparents? We
could find them and send them far away...maybe to the States or to Canada? Somewhere far, far away...”

“I shall look into it for you madam. For now we shall look after him. As if he was a Kaneshiro.”

“Kinder...be. Kinder to him than my parents were to me. Give him anything he wants. The only rule is he can’t
leave. It’s for his safety that nobody knows he’s still alive. At least until you find any relatives. Does he know where
he is?”

“No Madam. He believes a Ghoul bought him to eat . Apart from that. We did not make him aware of our names.
Nor of your company.”

“Okay, Can you let me in...?”

“Of course. I shall be right here Madam.”

I stood by the door, heard it buzz and swing open. I stepped in and looked around. The toys were all still put away.
It was neat and clean. As Kazuha promised it was temperate in the room; comfortable.

The boy wasn’t playing. Or even sleeping on the bed.

He sat in the middle of the room just staring at the floor. I could tell he was shaking slightly as I approached him
and leaned down.

“Just do it fast.”

He thought he was going to die. He thought I was going to kill him and eat him.


“Yuto? My right hand man told me that your name is Yuto. Is that right?”

He nodded his head but didn’t look up. I studied his dark messy hair and his pale skin. “Are you hungry, Yuto?
Did they offer you any food?”

“I don’t want to eat human .”

“Hey...Yuto. I’m not a Ghoul, kiddo. We’re all Human here. I asked for some Udon earlier. I’m sure they’ll have
extra if you want some.”

“U-udon?” The child finally looked up and looked over my face. His bright blue eyes studied my face, looking for
something that would tell him if I was a Ghoul or not. I know it must be a trick of the eye, but his pale little face
and mop of black hair made him look a bit like a little Uta. The comparison brought tears to my eyes. Choking
them back I forced a smile.

“Yeah kiddo! Niku Udon! It’s really good...the chefs always make extra food here. So do you want some?”

Yuto nodded his head, though I could still see he doubted me .
“...You're not a Ghoul? Then why did someone buy me...?”

“...I...I bought you.” I said, deciding to speak only the truth to the child.
They were a kid, but they were old enough to understand what had happened to their parents. They were old
enough to know and remember the Auction.

“—Because I didn’t want anything bad to happen to you. I am sorry about your parents. This was all I could do...”

The child's lip trembled and he looked back at the floor. “I’m looking for someone to take care of you. But in the
meantime it’s for your safety that you stay here. So that nobody knows where you are. Do you know if you have
grandparents? Someone who could look after you?”

He shook his head from side to side.
“How about an aunt or uncle?”
Again, he shook his head.

“...How about an older sister or brother..?”
No. Not that either.

“...I could try and have you adopted by someone in another country. Far far away from the bad people who hurt
your family. They’d never find you again. I can promise it.”

The boy shook his head again and I sighed. “Okay...if there’s anything you want. You tell someone. A toy or a
book. A drum set!? You name it...you’ll get it. Okay Yuto?”

“...Okay Ms...”


“Good boy...” I reached and gently ruffled his hair. “We’ll get you some Niku Udon—”

I started to stand up only for the boy to reach up and hold onto my hand. “C-can you eat with me...? So...so I
know—”

He wanted proof I wasn’t a Ghoul.

“Okay Yuto. I’ll eat with you...” I sat myself down, crossing my legs and sitting across from him. “Kazu is the man
in a blue suit and blond hair. You yell for him anytime you need something. Okay?”

I looked over my shoulder and yelled. “Kazu...we’re both going to eat in here!”

## ♥

I ate my soup nice and slow, observing the child across from me as he picked and poked at his food.
He glanced up once in a while to make sure I was really eating mine. When he was satisfied that I was, and it
wasn’t poison—he began to eat it in earnest. He finished one bowl and I smirked a little. “Oh!~ Are you hungry
now? Do you want seconds?”

The boy glanced up and his lips twitched into a small smile before his eyes darted back down to the ground. “...yes
please...”

“Go on, shout at Kazu. It’s fun!” I nudged the boy and heard him giggle slightly.

“ K-KAZU ...I—I want more Udon!” I laughed as the boy nervously shouted for more food.
A few moments later a dejected looking Kazu entered the room, giving Yuto more food.

“Really Madam, must you teach him your bad manners...?”

“I must. You know I need to mess with you, Kazu...” After all the trouble he gave me as a kid.

Yuto took his food and downed it just as quickly once more. I looked at Kazu and nodded.

“Make sure he gets as much food as he wants...and that he can get a bath if he wants one. Some new clothing.
Nothing fancy and uncomfortable like I always had to wear. Get him jeans, T-shirts. Shorts and sweatpants. And a
TV so he can watch some cartoons. And...and...some video games so he can play! It’s not the middle ages anymore.
I don’t think a kid his age wants to play with wooden blocks!”

“Of course Madam. Shall I also make sure your wardrobe is updated to your liking. At least so long as you are to
remain inside the building?”

“...Yes. If you could.” I don’t know how long I was staying.


## ♥

I stayed with the boy for many more hours, watching as new items were brought down to the room for him. He
stared at it all in wonder as a huge TV was installed on the wall and video game consoles were set up for him to
play.

He picked through the clothing and picked out his favorites. He tossed away ones he didn’t like, and I sent them
back with the staff to find others more like the ones he enjoyed.

“Hey Yuto...I think you should go to sleep now. It’s been a very long day. You sleep tight. I’ll see you tomorrow,
okay? We can talk about anything you like. Fair?”

“Do you promise...?”

I held out my pinky and smiled. “Pinky promise!~”

## ♥

I climbed back up the stairs and let out a sigh as I came to my room . Pushing the door open I stepped in and
looked around. It was dust free. A few new wardrobe of clothing already lay folded on the bed for me. The types
of things I actually liked to wear .

A note beside them read - ‘These seemed like they might be what you’d be comfortable with.’

Of course. I picked up a band T-shirt and smiled faintly. Well he wasn’t wrong. I put them all away in drawers and
closed my closet. I pulled off my jacket, only to realize it wasn’t mine. It was Uta’s cardigan sweater that I’d
grabbed in a rush. I laid down, holding it to my chest and felt new tears in my eyes. Without much thought I
brought it up to my face and inhaled the scent on it...

Was he even missing me?
Would he want me to come back?
What was going to happen now...I told him I’d never leave.

## ♥

Two days later...

I got a message from Renji asking where I was. I told him.
Hell, I invited him over to visit. I gave Kazu the names of people who were welcome to come.
Uta. Renji. Itori, Nico...even the Ghouls from the café. Yoshimura. Touka. Nishiki. Kimi. Irimi. Koma.

I even mentioned that if Shuu showed up he wasn’t to be turned away. Though, with that one I made mention

that he should be made to wait for my approval. I did not want the Gourmet wandering my home freely. He still
thought of me as a pet no doubt; he was not going to wander my halls without knowing that it was my house. My
rules.

I looked over the messages that everyone had sent in the last few days. Touka was pissed that I was missing more
work. Yoshimura had tried to call, but I’d turned down the phone call. Instead I sent him a message to explain that
I needed time away for something that came up.

Most importantly; Uta didn’t show up.

I could only take it to mean he didn’t need me to go back. He was sleeping fine.
He didn’t love me like he said. Like he thought he did...

It hurt. It ached.


“Madam...there is someone here to visit you.”

I glanced up from my bookcase that I’d been going over, reorganizing and fitting in new books that I’d had
ordered. Another Gibson guitar already sat in the corner of my room.

“Who...?”

“A Mr. Renji is at the door, Madam. Should I let him in?”

“Yes. Let him in...I’ll be down in a few minutes.”

I splashed my face with water to make sure I didn’t look like I was crying and took a deep breath. Slowly walking
down the stairs I made sure not to sound like I was hurrying to see Renji...Even though I missed them.

I missed them all.
I missed Bjorn too. Hinami still had him. I couldn’t bear to explain to her why I wasn’t coming around. That me
and Uta were having a...problem? A break?

As I walked down the final set of stairs I looked towards the doorway, spotting Renji standing in the lobby. He
looked out of place and uncomfortable. He looked up as I descended down the final staircase.

“Renji-kun...It’s good to see you.”

“...Aika. All this...”

“...it’s..uh...my home? It’s a lot, isn’t it. I can ask the kitchen to make some coffee if you’d like?”

“...That’s not necessary, Aika. When are you going home?”


“Home...?” I paused and stared at him, eyebrows lifting. “I...I am...”
I glanced down at the floor and then turned away from Renji, walking down the hallway towards one of the
drawing rooms. “I’m sorry you came out here to ask that. Didn’t Uta tell you? I don’t think he wants me to go
back. We had a disagreement. He must have realized he doesn't actually love me...so it’s probably better if—”

“What are you talking about?”

“...Y-you can come sit in here and we can talk if you’d like Renji.” My voice cracked. “I’ll have some coffee made
for you before you go. It’s nothing like Anteiku but—”

“Aika.”

I stopped walking, pausing at the doorway to the drawing room. “Is something wrong Renji?”

“What are you doing in a place like this...?”

“...I own it? I used to hate it here. But it’s not so bad that I’m in control. I won’t say anything about anybody I
met. You’ll all be safe and—”

“Aika—”

“I’m sure you and I won’t have any more sparring lessons anymore...there’s security here so I won’t really have to
worry so much though. Plus I left the sword back at Uta’s place. He can keep it if he likes. The other stuff too.
Maybe he can sell the guitar for some—”

“Aika—”

“If you could, can you tell Yoshimura I really appreciated the job? It meant a lot that he trusted me—”

## “AIKA!”

I flinched and leaned against the door frame, unable to look up at the silver haired ghoul. I couldn't face him with
tears flowing down my face silently. “I’m sorry Renji, did I make you mad too...? I didn’t mean to.”

“...you need to go home, Aika.”

“He doesn't want me there Renji...he would have called. He would have messaged. He could have come to get me
himself. And he’s not here...so it’s probably for the best if I just stay here.”

I heard Renji’s footsteps as he closed in on me, turned me around roughly and leaned over me.


“I went to pick you up for training and he only mentioned that you were gone. When I saw his face I thought he
meant you died. The shop has been closed since you two got home from the auction. He’s not sleeping. I doubt
he’s eaten in a few days either.”

“He’ll get used to sleeping without me there. He doesn't...have to eat everyday either.” Still, I felt a pang of worry.
Why wouldn’t he eat? "Anyway, I...I can’t just leave Yuto alone here. I know there’s servants here but still...”

“Yuto...?”

“My...the kid?” Renji didn’t seem to understand, so Uta must not have told him.
I squirmed out from the wall and waved him to follow me down the stairs.
I looked back to make sure he was following and then continued:

“...At the Auction there was a child for sale. I...I bought him. I couldn't bear for—I couldn’t allow it. He’s
here...his name is Yuto. I’m taking care of him until we can find a better home for him.”

I opened the door to Yuto’s room and stepped into the room in between, letting Renji in behind me. The little kid
was seated on a huge bean bag chair with a ps5 controller in his hands. Currently he was smashing zombie brains in
some game called Dead Island 2. I wasn’t sure if it was really age appropriate, but seeing as he’d seen worse...well I
didn’t argue when he asked for it. I had instead watched him play for several hours the day before and he had gone
on and on about his favorite video games.

He was adjusting well.
He almost seemed happy.

“...that’s the child?”

“Yeah...a ghoul killed his family and took him. Put him in the auction. Uta said he didn’t know about it but—”

“...Did you ask the child who killed his family?”

I grimaced and stared at Renji. Was he serious?
“It hadn’t come up in conversation, Renji. I was trying to avoid bringing up bad memories...Even if I could find
out, then what? Even if I feel bad for the kid I’m not out for revenge.”

I pushed open the door to Yuto’s room and stepped inside. The kid paused his game and glanced over his shoulder
and faintly smiled. “Ms. Ai, did you bring me a snack?”

“Not right now kiddo. A friend of mine was visiting...He had a question about...something you might remember.”


“Oh...Okay...?” The boy's eyes glanced up at Renji, head craning back as he stepped closer. Yuto was wary as Renji
leaned down to speak to him.

“Do you remember the ghoul that attacked your parents?”

The boy immediately clammed up and I frowned at Renji; bristling slightly.
“Renji...” Wasn’t there a nicer way to say this?

“Yuto...I know it’s difficult." I would try in a gentler tone. "But can you tell me what their mask looked like? Were
they wearing one?”

The boy slowly nodded his head. “Yeah...she had a mask.” He held up his hands and motioned.
“...It had big black eyes. With a star. And a blue nose...”

## ♥

Before leaving I had patted the boy on the head and thanked him..but the moment I was out of his sight and his
hearing range I raged. I stormed out of the observation room and up the stairway. Renji was hurrying after me as I
picked a random picture off the wall and hurled it across the lobby. The frame shattered and scattered.

As did the vase I picked up next.
And a grandfather clock that I tipped over in my fury.

ROMA. Of course it was Roma. She had done this knowing that I’d be there. She must have planned it since
Uta had asked if it was okay for me to go. After all I had told Uta he had to check if it was. She knew that Uta had
been trying to avoid having children in the Auction. She had gone out, murdered this boy's family and put him in
the Auction at the last minute to upset me.

Staff had come running out the main lobby, finding it in disarray.
I waved them away. “Clean it later...I—”

I should go home. At least...to see Uta. To tell him what I’d found out. It... wasn’t his fault there was a child there. It
still hurt that he sold people but this wasn’t his fault.

I couldn’t stay away from the child for too long though. So I’d have to come back...
I had to start working more with the company too. It might be easier to do from the Kaneshiro Manor. I could
invite him to stay here with me...?

“Kazu—” I called loudly. A few moments later he appeared. His eyes judgmentally surveyed the mess before
landing on me, eyebrows raised.  “...have someone clean this up. I’m...going to be going home. Make sure Yuto is
taken care of in my absence. Tell him I’ll be back and we’re still looking for someone to take care of him.”
