## Chapter 66: Return Home
## Notes:
She's home. But it's not the same.
(See the end of the chapter for  more notes.)
## Chapter Text


## Chapter 66: Return Home



Standing in front of HYSY ArtMask Studio felt strange. The door had its closed sign on it and an attempt at the
doorknob was met with resistance. It was locked.
I didn’t have my keys either. They were left on the counter top when I left.

So I tried the next best thing. I knocked.
## Nothing.

“Uta...?” I said it too quietly. I still wasn’t sure I wanted to see him yet. I wasn’t sure he really would want to see
me.

I knocked again, louder this time.
“...Uta?” I spoke a bit louder.
Still nothing. Maybe he wasn’t home. Renji was wrong. He wasn’t at home lounging around waiting for me to
come back. He was out causing some chaos...

There was just one more thing to try. I  pulled up Uta’s contact information. With my finger hovering over his
contact image I hesitated. The picture was of us, back in December when I’d taken pictures during the Christmas
date. We looked happy. Even he did, with a tiny smile on his lips. One of those rare moments when I could see it in
his expression.

Back then I had asked him back then if he was alright with me being a Human. He had said he was okay dating a
Human. That was before either of us knew about my family history. He might have imagined me as a Ghoul
because of my higher than usual RC count...but up until my uncle revealed our family secret he couldn’t have
known that it was a distinct possibility.

He saw my humanity as an obstacle. But he had loved me anyway...right?


I pressed down on the call button and waited.
I heard the pick up on the other end, but I didn’t hear him say anything. Still he must know who was on the other
end of the phone.

“Uta...? I’m outside. The door is—”

The line went dead.
I stared at the disconnected call screen in disbelief.
The void in the center of my chest seemed to yawn wide, aching and tearing deeper.
Renji had been wrong.
Uta didn’t want me back here...

I turned my back to the door and took a few steps away in a daze. I’d told Merlin to wait just a few blocks away. I
could head back—pretend none of this happened. I’d have to tell Renji that going back wasn’t an option...

As I walked down the alleyway something wrapped around my waist, pulling me off my feet back backwards. For
a handful of seconds I thought this was it. I couldn’t even manage to scream.

I could only imagine that some ghoul had come down the street for a mask. The shop was closed but hey, there
was a nice little meal walking around.

How might Uta react if some ghoul killed me steps from his front door? I’d never know...
I was weaponless. No Quinque, no knife. I had made the mistake of leaving it all at Uta’s.

My eyes were shut tight as the person gripped onto me. I winced away from them and whimpered as they sniffed at
me. Any second they’d bite and it would be over...

“Aika...it’s me...”

“L-let go of me...” He did. I hastily stepped away from the male ghoul and turned to stare at him. “Uta...You
scared me...why did you hang up?”

“I came down to let you in.” He held out a set of keys, his face set on neutral. “You forgot these when you left.”

I had left them on purpose actually. But I reached out for them, taking them from Uta’s outstretched tattooed
fingers. “Did you take care of what you needed to? Are you coming back?”

“I...it’s more complicated than that. The kid doesn't have any surviving family...I—I found out who did it: Why
he was at the Auction...” I glanced up and down the alleyway.
This wasn’t a good place to talk about this, we couldn’t be caught talking about this sort of thing by the random
passerby.


“Can I come in...?”

Uta cocked his head. Though his expression didn’t even twitch. “...Why would you ask that?”

“Because...I was gone?” I wasn’t sure how to talk to him now. There had been such a rift ripped between the two
of us.

“You can...” He finally answered, turning from me and walking back to the shop.
He entered and I ran to catch up with him, catching the door before it closed behind him. I looked around the
shop and saw that he had been working in my absence.
Though it was a mess. There were scraps of fabric, leather and bits of other materials all over his desk and around
the floor.

Uta didn’t stop at the shop though, he continued to climb the steps up to the apartment above. Whereas I stopped
at the ground floor.

“Uta...”

He glanced down, seeing me down below. “Maybe...we can just talk down here....?”
Uta slowly turned and walked down the stairs, his eyes on me as he sunk down in his office chair.

“...you're not staying.”

“I...have to go back.”

“You don’t have to. I want you to stay here.” Did he really mean that?

“I can’t...Yuto is still settling in. I can’t leave him alone.”

“The human child?”

“The child. Yes.” I felt my tone get defensive as he specified that the child was human. “I’m taking care of him
while we look for someplace else safe for him. Since Roma killed his family...”

I watched his face closely for a reaction.

I was relieved to find shock in his expression. His eyes went wide. Mouth opened just a little. His hands clenched in
his lap before he returned to neutral. “You’re sure...?”

“A female ghoul. Big black eyes with a star. A big blue nose...can you think of another. Not to mention who else
would have slipped a child into the Auction at the last minute like that?”


He was quiet for a minute, actually trying to think if there was another similar. Then finally he answered: “No. I
can’t.”

“She must have planned that since she knew you were bringing me. There’s no other reason to do that...”

“I am sorry, Ai-chan...” My bottom lip trembled before I caught it and bit my inner cheek.

“I’m not staying, Uta. I have to go back. Anyway, you didn’t visit. I said you could. I gave you my address. They
knew to let you in at the gates. But you didn't, so I thought...”

I crossed my arms and took a shaky breath. “...Renji came by and told me you're not sleeping or eating. It doesn't
sound like you...so he must have just made it up. By the looks of things It seems like you’ve been busy...” I glanced
around the room again, looking at the scraps spread out around his work area.

Uta stared up at me from his seat and I avoided his eyes, looking away.
It’s wrong. Something about this feels all wrong. I was digging the rift even wider somehow. I was ruining things...it
was my fault...

But it’s not, is it? Why do I have to always be okay with everything he does? Why do I have to change!?

“You can always come visit me. I can have a room made up for you there. If you want to stay for a while. You’d
have to bring your own food...You can’t kill anybody and butcher them in my manor though. So it has to be cut
up and portioned out. Like you have here.”

My house, my rules. If he wanted to see me, then he was going to have to agree to them.
“—You could meet the kid...if you want. You have to be nice though. He’s...he’s afraid of Ghouls though.
So...you’ll have to hide your eyes. He looks a little bit like you...”

I don’t know why I said that out loud. It slipped out. “...not the eyes. Obviously...”

“...does he?” Uta asked; his tone of voice actually sounded vaguely interested. Uta must have seen him at the
Auction of course; but I hadn’t noticed the similarities until I was close up.

“Mmm...a little bit.”

Silence seemed to swallow the room for a minute. I could only try and decipher Uta’s expression while he studied
me.

“I...I need to focus on work. It might be easier to do that from my manor. Kazuha will be close to me to keep
everything running on track. I can make sure that everything in my company is running smoothly and make the
transition towards making more synthetic organs. Maybe...in a couple years it’ll be enough...”

I stared at the ground, twisting my hands together. “...If...If I can do that and it’s successful. Then it won’t matter

who’s Ghoul or Human anymore? Wouldn’t it be nice? There could be the first generation of Ghouls who never
had to shed blood to survive...? Never are hunted down. Grow up with their parents. And the first generation of
Humans that never have to fear...”

“You won’t stay with me then? You could work on it here.”

“I could...” I said softly. “I...kind of doubted you wanted me around still...”

Something had broken. I couldn’t count on myself to implicitly trust him anymore. I had trusted him too much. I had
thought he could do nothing to harm that;  and now I couldn’t trust myself.

“I love you Ai-chan...”

“I love you too...I could come back on the weekends? If you really do miss me you can always come stay a night or
two with me. Plus, I think I’ll be resigning at Anteiku...”

“Have you told the old man?”

“...No. Not yet. He’s not stupid though. I think he knows something’s up. I feel bad for leaving in the middle of
the summer. But at least Touka’s out of school and can help more again...”

“You could stay tonight.” Uta suggested. I glanced at the stairway that had once felt so familiar.

“I’ve only been away for two days. I haven't forgiven you yet.” I was still angry, even if I wasn’t crying and
screaming at him. The fury and disbelief was still there. “I’m not just going to forgive this...”

“How can you forgive me if you stay away from me? Stay the night. Please...Ai-chan...”

“...Uta...I—”

The ghoul slid his rolling work chair closer, captured my hands in his own and looked up at me:
“...” His expression seemed to actually be pleading? I recalled what Renji had said about him not eating. Or
sleeping.

“...Just one night. I’ll cook you something and then I’ll sleep on the couch.”

“I’ll sleep on the couch....” Uta argued.

“Okay...Alright. I’ll stay the night.” His lips twitched so slightly I might have thought it a mirage if I didn’t know
Uta well enough. He let go of my hands, pushed his chair back and stood. He didn’t reach for me again as he
walked up the stairs to the apartment.

I watched him climb for a few seconds before slowly following. Once inside I found myself glancing around the
apartment, as if it might have gone back to how it was before I’d left.

But everything was still in its place. Right where I’d left it. He had put both my masks out on the coffee table. The
knife and the sword as well.

I took my shoes off at the door, and continued my inspection. The sink was almost empty. Except for the
Tupperware I’d used the night we left for the Auction. He hadn’t cleaned it, or presumably any other dish.

Was he really not eating?
I leaned down and opened the fridge. Everything was...still here? There might have been an eyeball or two missing.
But he hadn’t eaten a larger meal in a couple days?

Or...he had gone out and hunted something fresh.
I grimaced at the thought and stood up. “...How much do you want to eat? You hungry?”

“I am...”

Okay then. If he was hungry, maybe he really hadn’t hunted. I knew that he didn’t need to eat everyday.
If he really felt like it he could eat a whole Human in a day and probably survive most the rest of the month on it.

I really shouldn’t be worrying about his diet.
Still, I did. I love him. I couldn’t help it...

I pulled out the meat and opened it.

Immediately I slammed the container and closed it again as I felt bile trying to come up my throat. Tears sprung to
my eyes and I gagged.

I couldn’t. I couldn’t. I couldn’t.

## I COULDN'T DO THIS.

## ♥

Uta sat down on the couch, watching his Human —he still thought like that. Even if she was putting distance
between them, two days did not mean she wasn’t his. He watched Aika as she went to the kitchen preparing to
make him some food. Just like always.

He had grown used to it and so had she—

## Yet...
He watched as she opened the container and then shut it. She put the container down and gagged over the sink
and her breathing was—erratic. Strange. Panicked.


Uta stood up and was by her side in only a few heartbeats. He automatically wrapped a hand around her hip and
pulled her close but she elbowed him.

“...I...I’m fine. Just...just eat it raw. I—I can’t...”

He watched as she ran to the bathroom. Uta picked up the container and looked down at it. The meat inside was
still okay to eat. It seemed like his Ai-chan couldn’t bear cooking it anymore...

Uta considered just eating it raw like she said. It’s not like he wasn’t used to it. But he could hear his Human
gagging and throwing up in the bathroom. After a momentary consideration he placed the container down and
went to the bathroom doorway.

It was open.

He moved into the room, flipping the switch to turn on the light and moving to her side.
“Uta—I’m sorry. I—”  Uta carefully gathered up her hair and held it, another hand soothing over her back.

“I like it cooked...but you don’t have to cook it anymore for me. It’s okay.”
He had pushed her too far for months on end. It was only now that he risked having her leave him that he realized
that.
It was only now that the high line cracks were spreading and Aika shattered.

She was his Human. His bright and happy sunshine Human. She brought warmth to a cold world that otherwise
hated him and his kind. He couldn’t expect her to be like him. He shouldn’t want that.

“...Can you talk me through how to cook it myself?”

She nodded her head—and then puked up more bile.

## ♥



I got up from the bathroom floor and grimaced. My stomach hurt and my mouth tasted horrible. Uta pulled out a
fresh toothbrush and handed it to me with toothpaste already on it. I briefly looked at him from the side of my eye
before wetting the brush and brushing vigorously over my teeth.

He was acting—
Clingy wasn’t exactly the word. He wasn’t touching me unless he had to. As soon as I stopped puking he let go of
my hair and stopped rubbing my back. But he was hovering...

I spat and rinsed and cleaned the brush off.


“You...wanted me to talk you through cooking?”

“It’s an art. I should be able to learn.”

I couldn’t help but to smile a bit at that. “Really? You think? Maybe...but I’ve seen you burn toast.”

“I’ll try harder, Ai-chan. I’ll try cooking for you too...” He was trying. It wasn’t exactly everything I needed, but it
was a good first step.

“That would be nice...”

I walked back out into the living room and sat myself on the couch, pulling my legs up with me to curl and tuck
myself next to the arm. Uta followed, glanced at me and then went to the kitchen.
He opened the container and started pulling out a pan to cook in.

“Tomorrow I’ll come back with you. I can meet the h–the child. Are we keeping him?”

My eyes widened at the suggestion. Are WE keeping him? WE? Keeping? A child?

“Everyone keeps asking me that! I–I hadn’t planned on it. No...I was looking for somewhere safe for him. As soon
as I found a family I was going to set up...maybe an adoption. A new identity. A new name....I wasn’t sure exactly
how this could work.”
I swallowed my saliva and stared at Uta’s back as he worked in the kitchen. Why bring that up!?


“...What do I do first, Ai-chan...?”

“...Pour some of the fat and blood into the bottom of the pan. It’ll help keep from burning the meat. Put the stove
on medium. If you put it on high it’s going to burn no matter what you do...”

He did as I told him and I watched him from a distance as he placed the meat on the pan. Uta was doing okay, he
was focused on the cooking.

“I thought about asking my uncle if he could watch the kid. He did really well hiding what he was as long as I was
with him around that age. And he likes kids even if he never had any of his own...He could learn to hunt and fight
like I did. Those were some of the happiest times for me...Uncle could keep him safe too. It’s out of the city...”

I could smell the meat cooking, but at this distance and since I wasn’t handling it...I could deal with this. “—It
wouldn’t have to be permanent either. He could just go out there for a little two or three week break?”

“You don’t want to keep him...”


“I want to keep him alive, Uta ...Even if I did want a kid. Even if I wanted to adopt a kid. They’d never be safe. Not
in this world...” I exhaled a breath and looked down at the two masks on the table. “...If you’ve changed your mind
about kids, Uta. You’re going to have to wait for the next world to come around...”

The ghoul peeked over his shoulder, eyes wide. I softly snorted at the expression and looked away again.


## ♥

A miracle happened. He didn’t burn his food. Not terribly at least. Not even with me distracting him with the talk
concerning the child, and children. At my instruction he even took everything off the burner and turned off the
stove after he was done, so as to not burn down the whole building.

Uta stayed in the kitchen while he ate. Only when he was finished did he come out and sit on the other end of the
couch.

“I accidentally took your cardigan the other day when I left. I forgot it at the house when I left...I can bring it back.
Or you can if you're visiting tomorrow...”

“...Okay.” The ghoul answered softly.
He seemed to be mulling something over in his mind for some time. “I can visit anytime?”

“Of course.... I’ll set up a room for you. You can paint or draw right on the walls if you’d like. Make it all your
own.” It lightened my heart just a little to see that bring a smile to the ghouls face.

## ♥


I slipped into the bedroom and looked around. Most everything was just as I expected, though on the bed I did
notice something odd . There were a few of my shirts and sweaters piled up in the middle, bundled up. I climbed
into bed and looked through the pile.

From the looks of it, he had gathered up a few things that I’d worn and made a little...pillow out of it. Gathering my
scent for him to sleep next to.

I put myself in ‘his’ spot and held a pillow to my body. I could hardly call him weird for that, not when I’d nuzzled
into his cardigan the last two nights in a row.

A part of me wanted to do nothing more than invite him back into my life so that I could fall asleep safe and
sound in his arms...

But another part still wanted him to earn that back.



## ♥

## Chapter 67: Cold Shoulder

## Chapter Text



## Chapter 67: Cold Shoulder




I awoke in the morning and sat up quickly; glancing around to find myself back in our bedroom. Surrounded by
familiar scents and comfortable sheets. Just missing the familiar ghoul that usually held me. “Uta-kun...?” Where
was he?

The past few days came back to me as I reached out and felt the bed, hand bumping into the little pile of scented
clothing Uta had dragged up onto the bed.

Right...The Auction. The boy. Me leaving. That all happened. And now I had a child prisoner in my basement and
me and Uta were—strained to a breaking point.
Sitting up in bed I looked around the room now that there was some sunlight pouring into the window. I could
see that Uta had hung up my clown dress. It was right next to his zebra stripe one.

I swallowed down the bitter bile that threatened to rise in my throat.

“Ai-chan...?”
Uta appeared at the doorway, looking in.

“Sorry...I just woke up. I didn’t mean to call for you...” I grimaced and rubbed my face. I was still angry, regardless
of how much I still loved him. Regardless of how much part of me wished I could have slept next to him and
woken up next to him.

Uta lingered at the door for a minute, fingers drumming silently across the molding around the door.

“Do you want me to order breakfast...? Waffles?”


“No, that’s okay I—” I was about to reject the offer, telling him that my cooks could make something for me when
I got home. But I stopped. It would be nice to have a familiar breakfast rather than one made by my cooks. I didn’t
want that to become the norm.

What I wanted most was everything to be like it had been before. With some...small changes.
I wanted so much to trust him again. I really really did.

“Yeah. Sorry. Yes. Some waffles would be nice...Are you still coming with me today? And are you eating before we
go? If you choose to stay overnight, I don’t have anything there for you...”

“I ate before you woke up.” He stepped into the room and started going through his clothing, picking out some
and tossing them onto the bottom of the bed. I watched as he pulled off his shirt and tossed it into the overflowing
bin.


I never did get those done.
Neither had he in the two days I was gone. So what exactly had he done here all alone if not the dishes or the
laundry? I watched as he pulled on a new shirt and then swapped out his relaxed baggy pants for a pair of black
skinny jeans. He glanced over his shoulder and met my eye which caused me to get flustered and look away; caught
staring.

“...Should I wear a suit instead?”

“A suit?” Instantly I thought of the zebra stripe one and grimaced. However, when I looked back towards him he
was holding a totally normal suit. Black with a red collared shirt.

“You don’t have to. I’m sure Kazu would be happier if you did. But honestly Kazu can suck it up. You don’t have
to wear anything special. I’m not going to be. If Kazuha wants me in a dress he’s going to have to fight me and put
me in it himself.”

I slid from bed, stood beside him for a moment. I barely brushed up against him accidentally as I reached to pull
out some of my own clothing. I ignored the touch, pulling away after I’d grabbed what I needed.

As I left the bedroom after I’d dressed. I passed the ghoul. I could feel the ghost of his hand as he reached for my
hips. I side stepped it, pulling away and continuing to walk out to the living room. He stayed close; following on
my heels and hovering close.

“Uta...” I said softly, turning my head to look at him over my shoulder.  I was about to tell him to stop.

—but this sort of behavior wasn’t really what bothered me . It wasn’t the way he hovered. Or even his
possessiveness. His protectiveness. In a strange way I liked that he was a Ghoul. I liked most of the otherwise ‘odd’
behaviors. But it was difficult to quantify that with the negatives; with the murder and the fear of us both getting
caught one day.

My trust wasn’t broken because he was a Ghoul. I didn’t want him to apologize for what he was.
So what did I want? What could he possibly do to apologize or make things ‘right’? I wish he’d just—

“Did you order my food yet? If not...I can give them a call myself.”

“I did before I asked.”

I turned and raised an eyebrow at him. “You ordered them before you even asked if I wanted them?”

“They’re on the coffee table already, Ai-chan.” I sniffed and yes . Now that he mentioned it the apartment did
smell of delicious waffles with maple syrup drizzled over them. The scent made my mouth water.


“And what if I didn’t want them?” I definitely wanted them.

“You like waffles like I like eyes. I didn’t think you’d turn them down.”

“Jellied donuts might be a better comparison.” I rebutted.

Just as Uta said, a Styrofoam container with warm waffles was set on the table for me. I sat down and pulled it into
my lap. I closed my eyes and took a bite. It was so good...

With a pleased hum I wiggled a little in my seat as the flavor settled on the tongue.
I only stopped short with food still in my mouth when I heard subtle laughing. I remembered my threat to never
eat in front of him again—
Because I was doing the ‘happy food dance’.

With food still in my mouth I spoke, but it came out muffled.
“Stop laughing!!!!”

The ghoul’s lips stretched into a small smile. I wished it wasn’t as restrained.

I swallowed my food and scowled at him.
“I should pick Bjorn up from Hinami soon. I miss him.”

With a fork in one hand and my phone in the other I ate and sent the small ghoul girl a message:

Aika: I’m going to come pick up Bjorn today. Thank you so much for watching him for so long. Are you still at
## Anteiku?

A handful of bites passed and then she responded.

Hinami: It’s no problem. I love him!
## ♥
Hinami: Are you okay? Everyone seems worried about you.

Aika: I’m okay. I’ll see you soon.


I placed down my phone and kept eating.

“When I pick up Bjorn I’ll talk to Mr. Yoshimura...” I was nervous to quit my job at Anteiku. Not that I thought
they would react poorly, but I knew they were worried after I was missing for this long. Now I would be back,
only to be leaving for good. Leaving the job at least.

I would miss them.
But I had things I needed to do.

Perhaps once I moved things along in my company I could go back.
When things were happier. And safer.
Once the food was finished I tossed the container. “Alright, we can go. Merlin should be ready in a few minutes to
pick us up. If you're ready?”

My masks were on the table, along with the sword and the knife. Pretty much where I’d left them before. I reached
and picked up my familiar deer skull mask. Wendigo .
Next I picked up my ‘umbrella’ sword and small knife. The knife I hid in a pocket while the umbrella I held at my
side.

Uta followed me as I left the apartment. He stopped at his desk for a moment and leaned over it. I watched as he
picked through a few notebooks before choosing one to take with him. With it tucked under his arm he turned off
the lights in the shop one by one.

Uta paused, looking at the things I had in my hands. Then he spoke gently: “You’re not going to forget them
again, are you Ai-chan?” Forget. Did he really think I’d forgotten them before...?

“No. I—” I patted my pocket only to find it empty. Oh...I had almost left it behind again. They must be in my
other pants pocket.
“Hold on. Let me go get them.” I set down the umbrella and mask and ran back up the stairs into the apartment
door.

I moved fast, grabbed my pants from the pile of laundry and searched through the pockets to pull out the set of
keys. I sighed in relief; feeling better with them back in my hand.

Despite everything, this was my home. I wanted it to feel like home again.
I turned and jogged back down the stairs. “Come on, Merlin will wonder what's keeping us...”

## ♥

I stared up at the Anteiku sign outside the coffee shop and took a deep breath.
Merlin pulled up around the corner and would wait there for my return. Uta followed me into the cafe despite
telling him he could wait in the car - this wouldn’t take long.

Uta stood by the counter, but didn’t sit down. Koma and Irimi both shot him confused looks but greeted me
cheerfully. Touka on the other hand scowled and marched up to me with a tray still balanced in her hand.

“Hey! Where the hell have you been!?”

“...Hi Touka. It’s nice to see you too.”

“You just disappeared for a week and you say: ‘Hi, nice to see you?’” I smiled sadly. Her eyes searched my

expression and I watched her hard exterior melt away a bit. “...What’s wrong? What happened?”

I wondered what she would feel when she knew I was leaving. It wasn’t like Ken all over again, but it couldn’t be a
good feeling getting used to someone—only for them to leave. To have it happen over and over with different
people.

“Nothing to worry about Touka...Can I talk to Yoshimura if he’s around?”

“Sure...he’s in the back. You can go ahead...” Her eyes burned a hole in my back as I nodded and walked away,
heading to the back.
The old man was making sandwiches at the counter. He looked up when I entered the room, but only for a
moment.

“Sir...”

“Ms. Aika...it’s good to see you are alright.” He paused and then added: “You are, aren’t you dear? You should
remember what I told you, to rely on your friends. You would be surprised what people will do to help you, if you
just ask.”

“Sir, I came to give you my resignation. I am sorry that it’s at short notice.” I bowed my head down respectfully,
staring at the ground. “I wanted to thank you. You hired me when I was struggling...and you’ve been a great
friend.”

Yoshimura didn’t look up from his work, but he smiled sadly. “I thought this might happen. Are you alright, dear?
## Is Uta?”

“I—My resignation doesn't really have anything to do with Uta. Except...I’ve decided to focus on the work I plan
for my company. I want—I need to expedite it. Maybe once everything is going smoothly—I’d like to come back
and work at Anteiku again. When things are more peaceful...”

The old man placed the finished sandwiches on a plate and covered them in wrap.
“I see. Are you certain everything is alright, dear?”

“No...” I pursed my lips to stop a tremble. “Things are not alright....”

I pause, uncertain how much to say. ”Did you ever upset your wife? Do something that might push her
away...anything that’s unforgivable?”

“I am sure that I did. However, Ukina was quite forgiving. As you are. More than most could have expected from
you. May I ask what has Uta done to upset you that you can’t forgive him.”

I debated telling him. Surely he hadn’t done anything quite as dumb as Uta had. Both Yoshimura and Nishiki
seemed like people who kept their loved ones as far from ‘ghoul stuff’ as possible. “...Do you know about ghoul
auctions...?”


Yoshimura hummed softly. “I am aware of them. I suppose I shouldn’t be surprised he told you of them.”

“Unfortunately, he didn't just tell me. He brought me to one.” I grimace. Yoshimura’s eyebrows raised and he
cracked his eyes. “---I know it’s partly my own fault in agreeing, but I only agreed because he wanted me there by
his side. He was dumb enough to take me even though he knew I’d hate it...now I am so...” I clenched my jaw and
grit my teeth. “ ---furious at him. It’s painful. Loving someone and being so angry at them at the same time...and I
can’t think of a way to forgive him without asking him to change.”


“That young man does run with some dangerous folks. It is still surprising that he would have brought you. Surely
Yomo would have told him it was a bad idea. Have you asked him to stop going to them?”

“...I haven't. I’m afraid that I might need him to change for my own sanity—and I don’t know if he can.”

I took a breath and added: “It’s okay Sir. I’ll figure it out. I haven't really talked to him about it. I think I must be
insane; since I still love him...And I’m not going to just up and disappear. I can promise that! I’ll still stop by for
coffee! If you need anything you can always give me a call! For right now, I’m going to work on making sure things
get better...for everyone .”

The old ghoul smiled faintly and nodded. “I hope I see the day when it does.  Please be careful. Uta’s life is more
dangerous than most. You have seen that first hand. Try not to be dragged too deep into it that you drown...”

I smiled faintly; feeling a bit somber. It might be too late for that already. It felt like I was either going to drown, or
learn to breathe underwater. In a manner of speaking.
“...Thank you again, Sir.” I bowed my head again. “Please take care of yourself!”

## ♥

I found Hinami in the upper floors of the cafe, Bjorn was with her.
He bounced and wiggled his butt all around the room when I entered. I dropped to my knees and hugged his huge
head. “Awwww...Bear-Bear. I missed you so, so much. Never again. You're gonna stay with me always...forever
and ever.” I nuzzled into the dog's fur. This was better than therapy...

Is there therapy for couples like me and Uta? Probably not.

“Thank you Hinami...you’ve been so helpful watching him. Here—” I stood and dug money from my pocket:
holding it out to her. For a second I could see her about to say no. I stopped her, pushing the money into her
hands.

“I know I didn’t tell you I’d pay you for the help, but you definitely earned it! It’s summer...so why don’t you go
buy some pretty dresses? Or some new books? School books are expensive, you know? I know you're trying to
learn on your own. And if you need anything you can let me know!”


I held my arms open to her for a hug. She ran into it, wrapping her arms around my middle and squeezing tight.

“Ms. Aika? Are you leaving?”

“I’m still gonna be around. I just won’t be here as often. Okay? But I’m always a phone call away. I mean it.
Anything you need. ”

## ♥

Each goodbye was hard in its own way. Touka had met me on the stairway, her back leaning against the wall.
“You're leaving then?”

“Yeah.”

“I told you...at some point one of us was going to make you—”

“It’s not like that. Touka...It’s not. Trust me when I say that me leaving has nothing to do with Ghouls. Not
specifically at least. There’s other things I need to focus on...like you in school. I’ll be back as soon as I can be.”

The young lady scowled at the wall, looking anywhere but my face. “Hey...Touka?”

“What?”

“If I can do what I plan to: we can live in a world where nobody has to die for others to live. In a world like that,
maybe they’ll have cake...for everyone.”

She scoffed but I could see the small smile on her lips. “Eyepatch told you about that?...Don’t promise things you
can’t do.”

“Don’t tell me what I can’t do!”

## ♥

The expensive armored car rolled away from the 20th ward and away from the quiet little cafe. Away from the
sweet people who changed everything.
I loved Uta, but without them I might never have seen that Ghouls might want peace .


Then again, wanting peace and having it were two different things. Peace was hardly ever achieved without
violence and bloodshed preceding it.

“Do you think Renji would visit for lessons? I don’t know any entrances to the 24th in the area around my manor.
I don’t want to start slacking on them though. It would set me back. Plus...I enjoy them...There’s a gym

somewhere in the manor...”

“If you want to continue he may. I will train with you, Ai-chan...”

I exhaled and scowled out the window.
“.. .Right now I just wanna fist fight you.”

“We could do that. Would it help?”
Of course Uta would be happy to oblige. Hadn’t he learned from last time?

“Because kicking my ass would definitely help.” I rolled my eyes. “...When we get there you’ll need a tour and I’ll
tell Kazu to make a room for you.”


The ghoul was quiet. Most of the time it didn't bother me. But now it seemed to weigh heavy in the room. When
we arrived I got out of the car, grabbed my things and walked straight up to Kazu who was waiting to met me on
the stairway. Bjorn bounded out the car and started playing in the grass. Since everything was behind a gated fence
I could let him run and be free for a while.

"Welcome home, Madam."

"Kazu, Uta is here with me. Can you make a room for him?"

"Of course, as you wish. Is there anything I should include in such a room? He is aware that we don't have... food
for him, I hope?"

"He knows. He won't hurt anyone here."

I glanced at Uta as he climbed out of the car.  His eyes were searching the gardens spread out in front of the manor,
the gates that rose up all around the property and then finally the large manor itself. The ghoul looked entirely out
of place.


"Can you make sure that his room has pencils, pens, paper...mmm ...." I tried to think of everything he might
want. "---a desk and a rolling chair? And maybe a few sets of clothing. Something similar to what he's already
wearing."



"Of course, madam. It would help to get his measurements. But I am sure that we can find— something for him to
wear."

"Just don't make it all suits...And no zebra print..."

Kazu lifted an eyebrow at the rather strange specification. “ Very well? ...Do you want me to do the honor of a
tour, or shall you handle it yourself?”

“I’ll show him around. How has Yuto been? Is he alright?”

“He asked for you Madam; last night before bed. The staff watching him at night also reported that he continues
to suffer from night terrors. However, when he is awake he appears to be doing well.”

That was to be expected, after what had happened to him. I was sure that Roma hadn’t made it anything less than
absolutely traumatizing for him. She had probably put on a show just to make it worse for the child.

“Okay. I’ll go see him after I show Uta around.”

“Madam, are you planning on introducing that ghoul to the boy? It may not be such a good idea. Not with his
eyes like that. Can he not fix them?”

Kazu was casually ignoring   that ghoul as he walked up to my side and stood there, staring at the human man
who was blatantly speaking about him.

“He should also be aware—” Kazuha’s eyes shifted from my face to Uta’s, holding his gaze steadily without
flinching. “—That due to your late fathers condition, as well as your parents' concerns about Ghouls: The house is
outfitted specifically to deal with any threat. Especially Ghouls. Violence or any threat towards the Madam or any
of the staff is strictly prohibited. Any threat will be disposed of swiftly and without mercy.”

I gave my right hand man a harsh scowl. “Kazuha—I appreciate the thought. But don’t threaten him. And he can
not ‘fix’ his eyes. That’s just how they are.”

“Of course not!” The blonde man’s expression shifted into a ‘warm’ smile. He lifted his hand over his heart and
bowed respectfully. “It was by no means a threat! I apologize if it seemed like one. It is simply our duty to make

sure you remain safe...He is of course welcome here. And of course, under the same protection as the Madam. Nor
was my concern about his eyes an insult. ”

Of course it wasn’t...
Kazuha sure had a lot of nerve, staring Uta down like that. He still hadn’t broken eye contact with the ghoul.
Anyway, if Kazuha did threaten Uta I was half afraid the ghoul might just take it as a challenge.

“Come on Uta. I’ll show you around while Kazuha fixes up a room for you.” I shoved the umbrella and mask into
Kazuha’s hands. “Have those brought to my room please.”

“At your command, Madam!”

## ♥

I walked Uta around the building, pointing out rooms as we went. He was quiet  the entire time and I felt a bit like
I was talking to myself the longer we walked. I left off quite a few rooms, rooms that served little to no purpose but
to hold company.

“That’s pretty much it...if you get lost you can ask anybody where to go. They’ll point you in the right direction.
Maybe I can have a map made. Any questions? It’s a lot to take in...”

“Where is your room?”
Oh. The one question I didn’t really want to answer. Of course. I had left it off the tour. Despite owning
everything I still was staying in the same childhood room they had for me.

I should have moved from it...since it held so many bad memories. Yet still I stayed in my cell. Moving to my
parents room seemed wrong .

“It’s...a bit of a climb. Top floor. But I’ll show you some other time. Let's go see Yuto now. I want to check if he's
doing alright.” Waving Uta to come with me, I started to climb down the stairwell that led down...deep
underground where the boy was being kept.

I stopped outside Yuto’s observation room and scanned the card that would let us in. I stepped in and closed the
door behind Uta before looking through the window.


As I had mentioned to Uta it was adorned with nearly anything a child might want to play with now. TV, video
games. A drum set. An electric guitar. There was now a new set of swings, a playground-like jungle gym, even
some rock climbing hand holds bolted into the concrete. He must have asked for those things just today—

I prepared to enter the room, but stopped. Kazuha’s warning about Uta’s eyes rang in my head. If he walked in

there with his ghoul eyes the kid was going to go ballistic.

“Uta...it might be better if you stay out here. Kazu said that he’s already got nightmares. I think he’d be too
frightened of your eyes...considering...”

Uta looked unsurprised by this request. However, he pulled sunglasses from his pocket.
“I’d like to meet him, Ai-chan.”

I was surprised by that. Why ? Why risk it if the child wasn’t anybody to Uta. It’s not like I expected him to care
about the kid. How could I, when he didn't seem to care about any Human but myself?

Could I trust him?

“ No. ” I said gently. “Stay out here...please.”

The ghoul seemed surprised by my denial. His expression shifted briefly before going neutral again.

“Alright.”

## ♥

Uta watched Aika as she entered the room.
The young boy dropped what he had been doing and ran to her across the large room.
He quickly realized that he couldn’t hear what was being said inside the room without pushing a button on the
wall that fed the sound from inside to the observation room.
He stood in the quiet and continued to observe the room he was in while he waited for his mate to return from
speaking with the child.

Both doors were some form of reinforced steel. The windows were more than three inches thick and layered.
Likely bullet proof or stronger. Despite all that, the room was filled with everything a child might want. This place
was no Cochlea but it was built like it .

The place was a fortress.
He had noticed the armed security that was roaming along the perimeter of the property. Nor did it escape his
notice that they were watching inwards as well as out.

Likely due to him...

It was likely not on Aika’s order, but that man’s. Kazuha. If he didn’t seem so loyal to Aika, eating him would be
rather tempting...

Uta went back to watching Aika as she ruffled the boy's thick black hair and smiled happily down at him. He
thought he could make out the words as her mouth moved: I’ll be back soon. I’ll have them send down some snacks
soon, alright?

Aika exited Yuto’s room and closed the door behind herself. Uta heard it locked automatically.

“Alright...Come on. Let's find out where Kazuha decided to put your room.”

## ♥

I looked around the room Kazuha had picked out for Uta. They had set it up quickly.
Most of the items left for the ghoul were still in their packaging. A desk with lots of shelf space sat in the corner
under lamplight while a full sized bed with black sheets lay in another. It was a fairly bare bones room. The only
luxury was that it had its own bathroom with a shower...but it could be added to. If Uta wanted to decorate.

“Okay...it seems he got some basic art supplies. I think I forgot to mention charcoal...but hopefully this is enough
for now.” I noticed a note written and picked it up and scowled; and binned it.

“I’m going to go see about sending down some snacks for Yuto. Settle in...and...you can make this space your own.
Whenever you visit...”

## ♥

I laid face down in bed; cursing the day.
I hated that everything felt so heavy. I had a chip on my shoulder and I could feel it biting at me.
I hated that Uta seemed so distant and that I kept pushing him away. I had hoped that by showing him more of
this place he might at least ask questions.

But I couldn’t get a read on his emotions.
I couldn’t even tell if they were there .

If he could just...
Express something.
## Anything!

Chapter 68: (Fighting) Like Lovers Do
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text

Chapter 68: (Fighting) Like Lovers Do

I lay in bed until it was very early in the morning. 3 am and yet no sleep seemed to be coming to collect me. Finally
giving up I crawled out of bed and turned on the lamp over my desk. Slumped over my desk I started going over
some paperwork that Kazuha had given me...


Yet like sleep, the focus required to review the forms escaped me. After reading a paragraph not once or twice but
five times and still not understanding what I needed to, I slammed my forehead onto the desk.

Dammmmmmn iiiiiit.

I laid slumped forward with my cheek pressed on the desktop. Only when a warm furry head pressed into my side
and slid into my lap did I look up again.

“...Hey Bear-Bear...you're a good boy...a real good boy.”

The huge dog whined softly and pressed his body against my leg. He could probably tell I was upset, he knew me
well enough. Pressing my forehead into his I held his great big head in my hands, rubbing at his cheeks and behind
his ears.

“...I don’t know what to do....”

## ♥

Kazuha met me outside the dining room a few minutes after 7am. He stood beside the door, back straight and
arms folded  behind his back. He looked like a dignified statue more than a man. At least until he spoke. He
glanced only for a moment down at the dog who followed me and wandered around; sniffing every corner of the
house as we went.

“Madam, I am glad I caught you. I wanted to ask if you went over the paperwork I left for you.”

“No...Sorry.” Kazuha didn’t seem disappointed. If anything he had as good a poker face than Uta. “---I didn’t sleep
well. I tried looking over them, but I couldn’t focus. I’ll try looking at them later today...”

“I see, it is no problem Madam. However, move forward with your plans as you hope I shall need you to work on
the things I give you in a timely manner so things don’t get delayed. You were the one that wanted to review
employee files for specific sectors and have them all interviewed and questioned.”

“...Yeah. I know Kazu. You really don’t have to remind me. I was the one who told you to do that...I quit working
at Anteiku yesterday. I’ll be able to focus more on this. Stop reminding me—”

I couldn’t help but grumble, lack of sleep making me even grumpier than usual. On top of everything else it was
making me snap a little at him.

“...I see. Of course Madam.”

“I’m sorry...I don’t mean to snap. Kazu—can you find a way to try and weed out people with strong Anti-Ghoul
stances? And anyone with CCG family members. Not all at once—” That could get me into trouble. “...Slowly.

Find legitimate reasons to move them to defunct projects or out of the company completely if possible.”

“Of course...I can see that you are quite tired Madam. I take no offense to your mood. Perhaps some food shall
help.”

I passed him and pushed the door to the dining room open. There was a woman waiting with a smile.

“Hello Ms. Aika!”

I cheered a little at the short and slightly plum woman. Ms. Sato. One of the head cooks. I hadn’t seen her since
arriving, but it was good to know she was still around. She had always let me stay in the kitchen while she cooked.

She was on the older side now, but she was as cheerful and as spirited as ever. “It is so good to see you again! It has
been some time. I remember when you were just this tall! I hope you don’t mind that I’ve made you a more
traditional breakfast this morning.”

“No. That’s fine.” I weakly smiled as she reminisced about years past. Funny how everyone else remembered them
so fondly.

“Miso Soup, Tsukemono, Natto, grilled fish...and of course. Some green tea.” The woman paused and then
looked nervous . “Ms....May I ask something?”

“Of course...” I sat down, picking up an intricately decorated pair of chopsticks.

“...Is it true that the man with you is a Ghoul ?” Ms. Sato leaned in close and whispered ‘Ghoul’ like it was a curse
word. I ate a few bites of food before answering her.
“Yeah. He is.”

The woman’s expression was slightly fearful . Filled with genuine concern, likely for herself as well as my own
safety. How good it was to see that normal people still made expressions with their faces now-a-days. Not like Kazu
and Uta. Get stuck around men like that and you could begin to doubt it.

“Please...Ms. Sato. Relax. There’s no need to be afraid. That man ’s name is Uta. He’s my boyfriend. I promise he’s
not going to hurt anybody here.”

She looked unconvinced, still leaning down to whisper to me as I ate.
“Some of the others said his eyes were red and black—your uncles got like that when he was hungry. I remember
those days. Scary days those were...and your father. He was impossible to cook for. He liked nothing . Save for
lemon cake...Suppose it was because it was already bitter.”

I continued to eat as I listened to her. “His eyes are always like that. He doesn't mean to be scary. Can you tell me
more about when my uncle was here...did you work for us when he—”

“When he turned Ghoul? Yes. I did...though I was much younger than I am now. I remember. Wasn’t too long

before you were born. Your father had him locked him up in that room down there where that young man is now.
You know he’s the reason it’s so secure, don’t you?”

I shook my head. It made sense though .

“Made specifically for him. You know your uncle used to work for the CCG. He actually helped them make it.
Made it ‘ghoul proof’. Your uncle was down there for some time before they made sure he wasn’t going to attack
anyone here...I’m surprised they ever let him out. If it were me I’d—”

I paused eating, staring at Ms. Sato with a hard look. She seemed to realize her mistake and stopped. Her
expression wavered and she tried to put on a smile. “...Well anyway. If you say that man with you is okay I shall
take your word for it Ms. Aika...just that the staff is nervous. Especially after the nasty affair with your parents...”

I resumed eating, keeping my eye on her. I wasn’t too hungry anymore. I stood up from the table, food half
finished. “...Ms. Sato. If you have opinions about Ghouls. I’d like you to discard them. Be mindful that you are
employed by a family with Ghoul blood in their veins. And be aware that I love my Uncle...and my boyfriend.”

“Of course...I apologize.”

## ♥

I nearly walked straight into Uta when I turned the corner on my way towards his room.
Although I was angry at him, I had no intention of ignoring that he had come to visit me at my own home. If we
had any hope of repairing what was broken it wouldn’t do to discourage him from returning or staying with me.

I yelped and stumbled, saved from hitting the floor when the ghoul wrapped his arm around my waist and hoisted
me back up onto my feet. “Careful Ai-chan...”

“You scared me—what...where were you off to?”

“I was looking around...” He turned to look back at some art on the walls. “There’s quite a lot of rare art here.
Your parents were collectors. They seemed fond of Katsushika Hokusai and Yokoyama Taikan.  I think I saw a
few by Utagawa Kuniyoshi as well...”

I looked up at the art and murmured. “...there’s some by Yoshida as well somewhere. Closer to my room I think...”

Silence . I shifted uncomfortably. Even looking at art he seemed so blank. Irritation gnawed at me like an
unwanted infestation.

“Uta—” I heard the tension in my voice, the way it snapped at him.

He glanced towards me, face setting in a familiar hardened mask .

I waited a few moments, trying to think of what to say. Finally I sighed:
“—How about that training? No weapons.” Bumps and bruises would feel better than this aching hurt or the
anger. Perhaps putting that fury into something would make it go away.

The ghoul blinked and tilted his head slightly. “That’s fine.”

“No biting either Uta. I like to give Kazu a hard time, but he might try shooting you if you actually hurt me too
badly.”

“Just our fists.”

There should be a first aid kit already in the gym, so I didn’t have to worry too much if I got a little banged up. I
nodded my head down the hall I’d come from: “The gyms this way. Same stairway to get to Yuto, it’s just a floor
above him.”

I walked, glancing out a window to see that Bjorn was once again running around the yard. Currently harassing a
gardener; the staff in question was smiling though.

“...Ms. Sato told me today that the room Yuto is in was made to contain my uncle...when he first turned Ghoul
that is.”

“I thought the design seemed familiar. It’s similar to the cells in Cochlea.”

“My uncle assisted in the design...he...might have taken the design from the prison.”

Once we reached the door to the gym I shoved it open and walked in. I swept my hand over the wall to the right
and found the lightswitch. Slowly each light flicked on, one row after another to slowly reveal a large room. There
was a boxing ring and weights. Punching bags and plenty of space for all sorts of mixed martial arts.

“Here we are...”

I walked to the mats meant for martial arts and kicked off my shoes before turning around, facing the ghoul.
“Here’s fine...It should be large enough if Renji wants to come train me some I think...”

Uta shrugged off his outer jacket, dropping it to the ground near the wall. He pulled off his shoes as well before
stepping on the mat. At least if I hit the ground it won’t hurt as badly here as on concrete.

“Remember...no biting. No Kagune. No weapons...”
“I remember, Ai-chan.”

I lifted my arms up into a defensive stance and took a breath. Uta kept his arms at his sides and waited. With a
grumble I leapt forward first.


I wasn’t surprised that he dodged it.
It had been a wide attack; easy to see through.

I fell back into the training that Renji and I had done in the very beginning, just without a knife. The range was
about the same as being completely bare handed.


## However—
When Uta closed in close I expected pain from a strike, tensed for it. What I didn’t expect was the sweep and
much gentler shove that landed my butt back on the mat. Blinking up  at the ceiling of the gym room I was
confused.

And pissed. Of all the times he went soft on me?! He decided NOW to fuck around and play gentle? Was he
teasing me?!

“Uta—What the hell!” I leapt back up on my feet with my teeth clenched in rage. The ghoul ducked and weaved
out of my way; and then I was once more put on the mat.

I bound back up.
I realized I was acting more rashly now. Swinging wider and more widely. Not thinking through any attack. It
wasn’t at all how any single one of my trainers had taught me. Both Renji and my uncle would be scolding me
right now.

“Uta!” I swung my fist and felt it connect. It took a second for me to register that I’d struck him across the face
with my closed fist. He caught my wrists in his hands and held firmly.

“Ai-chan...You’re angry.”

“No shit I’m angry! What was your first clue!?” I felt hot angry tears threatening to fall from my eyes. Uta’s
face was bruised, but it was quickly fading even as I watched his face. His stupid emotionless face! I struggled, trying
to pull my hands away from his grip but failing miserably.

“I am sorry Ai-chan...I can not help that I am a Ghoul—”

“Idiot! I’m not angry about that! It has nothing to do with that!”

The ghoul’s eyes searched my face as I stared up at him, face contorted in rage and sorrow.

“I’m pissed because you made a choice to bring me to that place even though you knew I’d hate it. You knew it
would upset me. I’m angry that you don’t seem to think I could really love you, despite everything I’ve done
and gone through to show you I do! I’m angry because you ignored every voice of reason from your friends like
Renji and took me somewhere dangerous like that!”

I fought to try to get my arms free from him and ended up kneeing him in the groin. The ghoul grunted and bent

forward, but did not release my hands. “Ai-chan—”

“NO! Shut up! Shut up and listen! I only went there because you wanted me to be there! I trusted you with my
heart and you broke it on purpose. Just because you could! What could you have possibly hoped to have gained
from that?”

Tears fell from my eyes now, dripping down my cheeks and falling from my jaw.
“Uta-kun. I can live with you killing people to survive. I can hide in the room next door while you turn someone
who was a person into boxes of meat. I could even cook that meat for you. I could lie to investigators. Help hide
you in any way I could think of! I could endure every accidental harm that comes to me because I’m around you.
Because after all that, I still have you! And I thought I knew you loved me.”

I sniffled and whimpered. “But now I can’t be sure! I know I wear my heart on my sleeve, but you don’t even react
when I leave!!! You don’t reach out for two days! When I come back, you just stare at me and are so quiet! I can’t
read your mind, Uta! I can’t tell how you're feeling and you won’t tell me!”

The ghoul pulled me close despite my protests. Letting go of my wrists, only to wrap his arms firmly around my
waist. I wiggled uselessly until he dropped to his knees and then sank down to sit on the mat bringing me with
him. Straddled seated over his lap.

I tried to push him away with my arms but he only held on firmly.
“Uta this isn’t—”

“Please don’t leave...”

I paused and listened. His face and nose were nuzzled up against my neck. His arms held me tight. He spoke just
above a whisper.

“Please...I know. I know that going put you in danger and I am sorry. But please—don’t leave.”

His voice, the soft begging and a single slightly jagged intake of breath was all I could tell that he was upset. “I need
you to stay...”

Slowly I relaxed my hands, moving from pushing him away to wrapping them around his back.
“I need some things to change Uta-kun...I can’t keep bending. I can’t anymore...”

The ghoul kept his face nuzzled against me, inhaling my scent from my neck and my hair.
“...those auctions. They’re unnecessarily cruel. It’s not about being Human or Ghoul. It really is no better than the
investigators, if you just reduce someone down to a handful of coins. I can support your survival...but not
something like that.”

“...The Clowns won’t stop...”

I sniffed softly and moved my own face to lean on his shoulder.

“Well it’s a good thing I’m only in love with Uta and not all the Clowns...” Gripping his shirt I breathed in a
ragged breath. “I won’t ask you to stop completely...can you...go less often?”

There was a painfully long pause where I thought he would reject it.
But he nodded.

“...Can you keep Roma away from me?”
The ghoul made a noise close to a growl as I spoke the name. It was heartening to know he was also unhappy with
her. “...Don’t worry about her, Ai-chan...”

“...Okay...” I leaned away from him, pushing gently but firmly so I could see his face. He resisted at first but then
sat back. I cupped my hands around his jaw and stared at him. He still looked—fairly masked. “Please...Uta....”

Slowly, his expression relaxed into a very tired expression. I could see the dark bags under his eyes and the
uncertainty in the red hues.

“Stay...?”

“I’m not going anywhere. I told you. I love you....but—”

Uncertainty. A twitch of his brow. The down-turned lips.
I smiled faintly; relieved.

“I was serious about working more with my company...trying to speed up production of organs. Hopefully it’ll
work...”

The ghoul’s hands gently moved across my back, kneading gently over my shirt. “Do you make them now...?”

“Yes...on a smaller scale. They’re used in human transplants. But it’s too slow to support all the ghouls. If you
consider you need about 100-200 pounds of meat every month. It’s...too much to keep up with. And far more
than I have a ‘valid’ excuse to greenlight at the moment. Not to mention, I don’t even know if it’ll work...”

“...Could I try one?”

I stared at Uta. “You...want to try...one?”

“You can prove it works. Right? I can help...for your peaceful world.”

“I—I’d need to prove not only if you can eat it, but that it will actually provide nutrients to you over...at least a
month's time. A-and you're not an experiment...I know you don’t believe in any of it working...for all I know it’ll
taste bad. Or poison you.”

“I’ll try it...” He leaned forward and pressed his lips to my forehead, lip ring making a cool impression on my brow
before he pulled back.



This...was good. Not perfect. It didn't make up for everything.
And certainly there were things that I'd still have to bend for --- accepting he killed to eat was one thing. Being
happy about it was another.
Still...at least it was a step in the right direction.

For now I could just relax in his arms again and maybe drift off for some much needed rest.

Both of us could use it...

## ♥
