## Chapter 69: The Doctor
## Chapter Text

## Chapter 69: The Doctor

I closed my eyes and relaxed as Uta held me tightly; face nestled against my throat and buried against my hair.
Uta had said he wanted to try one of the synthesized organs made by the company I owned; but then he had
pulled me close again and gone back to simply holding me .


I could fall asleep just like this...

“...Stay Human.”

I opened my eyes. After sitting quietly for some time with them closed, and so close to falling asleep they were
sensitive to light and bleary.
We were still in the gym, sitting on the ground and just holding onto each other.
Unsure that I’d actually heard him correctly, I made a quizzical humming noise.

“...Stay Human, Ai-chan...If you need to, take the medicine.”

“...Why would you want that? I figured...” I trailed off. I had thought he of all people would want me to be a
Ghoul, just like him. I had even considered it, just for him.

“I won’t deny I’ve imagined it. Perhaps it would be nice. For you to be as strong as us. Have your own Kagune—”
His hands pressed gently into my back, kneading his fingertips into muscle. “But...you're happy being Human,
and I love my sweet little human. So I’ll protect that so you don’t have to be like me...”

I hummed again softly, my own fingers curling to grip gently onto his shirt.

“...the medicine seemed bad though...some of the side effects sounded—” Worse than being a Ghoul? It sounded
rude; but it was true. “Like they’d make me kind of sick...”

“The alternative is to eat like me...or Renji, if you wanted.”

“If my RC count goes too high. Maybe...Maybe I’ll take the pills. I could always change my mind. After I succeed
and an alternative is available;  I can always stop taking the pills”

The ghoul holding me shifted, leaning back to look me in the eyes. I smiled faintly as he searched my expression:

“In a safer environment than an airplane...for obvious reasons. I wouldn’t want to try and eat you Uta...But in that
world, it wouldn’t matter; Ghoul or Human. And no more side effects.”

“You would miss waffles too much, Ai-chan.” His face mercifully cracked into a small grin.

I chuckled softly. “Yeah...that’s true. I’d have to start working on a waffle alternative. Or a way to make human
food edible.”

I smiled sadly and added: “...anyway, the medicine would already ruin waffles for me. Part of the symptoms
already make food taste bad. Ghoul downsides with no upsides, right?”

“Hmmm...that’s true...”

“...My legs are kind of going numb sitting like this though, Uta-kun...” The ghoul shifted slightly, hands lifting me
up off his lap. He shifted from sitting to kneeling and then slowly stood; pulling me up with him and making sure
I was steady on my feet.

“Do you still want to fist fight me...?”

I scoffed and pushed him without any real force to it. “Careful, you make me mad again and I just might.”
Looking up at his face, I could still see that he wore his ‘mask’...though when he met my eyes it cracked just a bit.
He looks so tired.

I cupped my hands around his jaw and leaned up, pressing my lips to his cheek. “...you look tired Uta-kun...Renji
told me you didn’t eat or sleep...”

“Mmm. I didn’t have much of an appetite. I’ve told you, I can’t sleep without you next to me.”

“Are you not being slightly hyperbolic...”

“Not at all.” The ghoul said, speaking completely seriously. My lips turned down into a worried frown. If he was
serious then it might cause some small troubles with me staying here . He obviously belonged at his shop.

Traveling back and forth from the 4th ward to the 21st was clearly a far commute. Further than my trip to get to
Anteiku each day.

I turned from Uta and went to collect my shoes, pulling them on and preparing to leave the gym.
Our fight was over, for now. I’d have to make sure that I kept a better hold on making sure that nothing like this
happened again. I couldn’t allow myself to bend to a point where I broke.


“---And now...? Are you hungry? I can see if Kazu can get something from the company brought...but...”

The ghoul followed me out of the gym after slipping his own shoes on.

“A little bit. What’s wrong?”

I glanced over my shoulder as I walked. Worrying on my bottom lip I tried to think of what I’d have to do to make
sure that I got proper data.
“Like I said, I’d hate to treat you like some sort of experiment, but to make sure that it’s healthy for you and it
really would work —we’d have to have a proper health check on you beforehand. Like a basic doctor's check up.”

“I’ve never been to the doctors...”

Oh. Right. He wouldn’t have—would he?

“Right...Well it would check very basic things to get a reading on how healthy you are to begin with. So it can be
compared to readings later on. Heart rate, blood pressure, hearing, eyesight. Height and weight...That sort of
thing.” I tried to think of all the things that a doctor might check on someone for a general physical. “ — But since
you're a Ghoul it also would include: A general panel blood test. Probably including a baseline measurement of
RC cells...to make sure nothing that you eat was having a negative effect on you. Is that okay? If you want, we can
both get a check done. I haven't been to the doctors in years. Since it would be done by my own people, you don’t
have to worry about getting ‘caught’.”

“It’s been some time since you checked your RC levels...” The ghoul mentioned.

“Okay, then I’ll tell Kazu that we’ll both get checked up. I’ll have my RC Cell levels checked again and I’ll tell him
to get some organs brought over—” I smiled and bounced a little in my step; cheerful for the first time in days.


Instead of simply yelling for Kazuha or calling his phone I headed to where I was sure that he would be; his office.

I noted that on the way staff lingering in the hallways would stare at Uta and myself. They gave us a wide berth or
scattered, making themselves busy in adjacent rooms.

I knocked on Kazuha’s office door and entered with Uta following on my heels. “Kazu. Could you get our doctor
in today...if he’s not on property already.”

Kazuha was bent over his desk, the blinds drawn so the room was mostly dark with only a lamp lighting over his
paperwork.
The desk was covered from side to side with it and the man looked up at me with a pair of half-moon spectacles
balanced upon his nose.


“A doctor? Are you feeling well Madam?”

“Mmm, fine. But Myself and Uta will have a check up done.” Actually, while he would be here. “It would also be a
good idea if Yuto also has a general check up as well.”

“I can arrange that—” He looked over his desk, shifting through paperwork until he found his cellphone.

“—Kazu. Also, could you arrange to have some organs brought over from the labs? The reason Uta is having a
check up is because he wanted to see if my idea about Ghouls being able to eat the ones we can make might be
viable. I thought it best we got baseline data, so I can make sure he’s not being hurt by it...”

Kazuha’s eyes glanced from me to Uta and back. “I suppose that makes finding a willing test subject easy...”

I scowled at the wording but Kazuha ignored the expression. “I suppose we shall see if it works...I’ll have the
doctor in in the next hour. You remember your way, don’t you?”

“I do— And Kazu? ” The man glanced up again from his phone. In the dim light I could see he also had dark bags
under his eyes. “I’ll take a look at the files you gave me in a little while. But maybe you should take a bit of a rest...”

He was quiet for a few moments then relaxed his shoulders. “Of course Madam. I shall after I get a bit more work
done.”

I reached out and took Uta’s hand, pulling him along with me to the ‘medical room’.  A room on the first floor
that was kept to deal with any injuries, as well as for the doctor to come for home visits. Be it for the family or any
of the staff. We stopped on the way a few times when Uta wanted to look at a painting or another piece of art that
was on display.

When he stopped again I chuckled softly. “You know...I think I might replace some of these.”

“Oh? With what?”

“I was thinking I could put some of your masks up on a wall—maybe a few of your drawings would look nice.” I’d
pay for them obviously. I smiled as the ghoul’s eyes went wide, a gleam in his eye as he faintly smiled. “---I like your
art better than most of the paintings that are here anyway. You can choose where to display it. I think they’re
beautiful. Maybe in the front lobby? Somewhere everyone could see. Would you like—”

I was caught off guard when the ghoul tugged me close and pressed his lips to mine. He backed me up against the
door to the med room; hungrily kissing me.

I think he rather likes that idea.

I ran my hands up his chest, over his shoulders and finally tangled them in his ponytail. Breaking the kiss for a
breath I leaned my head back. The ghoul in turn decided it was the perfect time to kiss and nip up my throat.


The sound of a throat clearing announced the arrival of someone else.

Uta paused and we both turned our heads from what we were doing to spot the family's staff doctor.

“Good morning, Gentleman and Lady...perhaps I might interrupt.”
For the first time since arriving, the staff member before us wasn’t someone familiar to me. He was younger than I
thought he would be. Medium height. Dark wavy hair with bangs; the back was tied into a short ponytail.

“Are you the doctor...? I remember Dr. Hamasaki...I guess he was pretty old when I left.”

“My predecessor. Yes. He unfortunately passed a few years after you left, if I recall. If what I’ve been told is correct,
that's close to five years ago? You are Aika Kaneshiro. And this...must be Uta. Your boyfriend. From what Kazuha
tells me—he is a Ghoul, correct?”

I glanced between the Doctor and Uta, who was staring at the doctor with his very clearly ghoulish eyes. “Yeeeees?
He is...obviously.”

The young doctor smiled; a wide grin that lit up his face as he looked Uta up and down. “Yes yes, obviously!
Pardon, I thought I’d make sure. This will certainly be fascinating! I do hope you don’t mind my enthusiasm,
Uta-san! It’s not very often I’d get a chance to examine a Ghoul so close up!!!”

In a split second he turned back to myself, almost giddy as he bounced on the balls of his feet. “---Not that you
aren’t fascinating yourself Ms. Kaneshiro! A Human with ghoul genetics and a predisposition for a mid-life
change! It really is quite amazing!”

I saw a staff member running down the hallway behind the young doctor. When she finally got to us she was out
of breath. I forgot her name; but at least she was familiar. “I—I’m sorry, madam. Kazuha-sama sent me as soon as
he heard the doctor arrived. T-this is...Mr. Chikafuji!”

“Ahhh! I totally forgot to introduce myself!” The doctor grinned and waved us towards the door of the office we
had been kissing by. “NOW!” He clapped his hands together loudly. “---No time like the present. Come on—
unless you’d prefer I look at you separately.”

“No...” I glanced at Uta and saw him quickly glance. It was Uta’s first time having a doctor look at him, so maybe it
also wouldn't be good to leave him alone with the clearly eccentric doctor.

“We can get checked at the same time. Uta’s never had a check up.”

“Oh? Hum...Well I shall be sure to be gentle with him!~ I am kidding of course—I do have to poke you with
some needles! But I can see you clearly won’t be afraid of needles, would you?”

Where on earth did Kazuha find this man?


I took Uta’s hand, cast him the most reassuring smile I could and led him into the office.

## ♥

I sat on a chair across from Uta as Mr. Chikafuji bounced from one of us to the other. First he checked our heights
and weights and took his blood pressure. Checked his breathing and used an otoscope to look in his ears.

“Your name is Uta. Any family name?”
“No.”
“No? No name or not one you’ll tell me? Is that a ghoul thing?If you married, would you take her name or would
you make something new?”
My jaw opened in shock at the question. Yet, the doctor didn’t wait or pause for an answer, nor did Uta react to it
from what I could tell.

“What’s your Birth Date?”
“December 2nd.”
“And how old are you?”
## “27.”
“Any allergies?”
“No.”
“Do you not count human food as an allergy? I suppose not. Have you had any health issues in the past, not due
to injury?”
“No.”
“Any injuries that haven't healed or have left lasting pain or stiffness?”
“No.”
“....to be expected, Ghouls heal quite nicely!~ Now your eyes...are they always like this?”
“Yes.”
“Since birth?”
“As long as I remember.”
“Very interesting...so it’s not something you are doing actively.”

He was jotting down each answer on a sheet as Uta answered them. “I’m going to have you do a very basic vision
test, is that alright? All I need you to do is stand on that end of the room, cover one eye and read out the smallest
line of text to me. Then we’ll swap and do the same for the other eye.”

I watched as Uta, doing the same tests right after him. Mr. Chikafuji was clearly more interested in Uta. But he still
was excited to get my information.

“Amazing! Uta-san! You’ve got really good vision! It’s above the average 20/20 for Humans! And Aika!~ Your
vision is 20/20! Not really remarkable...but you don’t need glasses! So that’s some good news, isn’t it?”


Next a hearing test.
Unsurprisingly, Uta aced everything. Meanwhile my own tests continued to come out as just about average.

Next he pulled out test tubes and held them in front of Uta and myself, asking us to each smell it and guess what it
was. Uta missed a few of those that were human food while I got them all right.

The doctor continued; going through different tests and taking measurements that I hadn’t ever considered.

## ♥



“Alright, last but not least! A blood test and RC test! It’s just a little poke!~” I winced as the doctor took my arm
and gently guided the needle into the crook of my arm to draw blood. He took some and placed it on an RC
testing strip where it would process while he worked on Uta.

He put aside the vials after they’d been labeled and then threw away the needle he had used. “Alright—and next
you, Uta-san!~ I’ve got a special needle for you!” He pulled out another set of needles that I couldn’t tell were any
different, but judging by the doctor's words...it must be quinque steel.

“If you could roll up your sleeve, I’d like to get the same vein as Ms. Kaneshiro’s. I shall try to miss your tattoos.”
The man seemed to giggle some as he poked the needle into Uta; though despite his enthusiasm he seemed to be
just as gentle with the ghoul as he had myself.

“There we go.” He held up the vial with Uta’s blood in it and grinned. “That should be plenty! I am excited to see
how the readings come out! And of course to check on you again at some point! If you get sick or don’t feel
well...you should visit a doctor! Me , of course! If you’d like you could say I’m your primary—might get you out
of trouble with the CCG one day, you never know!~”

Maybe a doctor would have to be a bit eccentric to work on an estate like my family's. Especially with patients like
my family. I watched him as he placed the two RC tests next to each other and stood by, leaned over them as he
waited.

Five minutes later I saw his smile widen. He whistled as he held up both tests in the air.

“Amazing...that’s quite the difference! But of course it would be. Uta-san, you're sitting about...3700! It’s quite
high. Though not the highest out there. Normal is—between 1000 to about 8000. For Ghouls. Aika on the other
hand...727. It’s quite high. For a Human .”

## Huh?
I suddenly felt my stomach drop, a wave of fatigue overcome me. I felt a pressure rising in my head as I felt my
pulse in my throat, ears and nose and my hearing began to ring.


“S-sorry. Can you...repeat that?...727?”

“Hum? Yes? That is correct. When was the last time you checked?”

“A month or so?”

“Annnnd?~”

“...690 back then.”

“ Oh . That is a concerning jump then. That’s...37 points higher a little over a month? At a rate like that, you’d be a
Ghoul within a year!” He sounded...cheerful. Though the expression fell from his face when he seemed to take
note that I wasn’t happy with that news.

“At least, if that trend continued. Before you get concerned though...Perhaps a recent activity might explain the
jump?”

The memory of cool slimy meat slid down my throat while a crowd of Ghouls stared at me from all sides.

“...maybe. Should I start taking the pills soon then?”

“...Hum...In my professional opinion: You can wait. If it’s really a trend the pills are available. Honestly, unless you
start having some undesired effects, sudden hunger for human flesh for example; you should be fine until...800’s. I
would be happy to check weekly for you. At that point I would start becoming concerned for you and suggest,
should you wish to remain human, that you take the medicine. You should just keep an eye on other side effects.
You might start getting more ghoulish traits if it continues.”

“Like...what exactly?”

“Oh nothing too terrible, so don’t look so concerned. Relax Ms. Kaneshiro. It’s certainly nothing anybody would
complain about. Increased strength. Stamina. You might see better; like your boyfriend here...although you might
also get a craving for steak before you actually wanted human meat .” The doctor shrugged cheerfully,
adding:  “Perhaps it’s just me but it’s not something I’d mind!”

“---Now! I believe I have a child to check up on—Don’t worry! No needles for the little guy!”


## ♥




“...” I was in a daze as we left the med office. My lip hurt, likely due to how much I was nibbling on it to the point
that I now tasted copper.

Uta reached for me, slipping his tattooed hand around my hands which nervously fidgeted in front of my chest.
He walked with me, holding my hand as he led me forward.
“We should maybe check on Yuto...”

“He’ll be alright.”

“The doctor was a little weird—Maybe—”

“---We both need sleep, Ai-chan.”


I worried about Yuto, but the draw of sleep was so tempting. Kazuha may have picked out an eccentric doctor, but
surely not one that would harm a kid.

“...Just...a short nap. I've got work to go over...Files. I'm trying to weed through some employees. See who can be
let go and sectors that can be eliminated..." I was murmuring, rambling as I followed along with the ghoul.

We were at his door soon enough. “Uta...You can sleep as long as you like. But if you go home please let me
know—Kazu should have some organs here in a bit, but I don't’ know exactly how long that’ll—” I was pulled
into his arms again, lifted off my feet and pulled into the room before I fully registered that he meant sleeping
together again in the same bed.

Uta carried me. Holding around my waist and hoisting me off my feet. He turned when he got to the bed and fell
back; laying us out on the bed in a bouncing jumble. My body laid out over his as he kept his arms wrapped
around my middle. I grunted softly at the less than comfortable landing and laughed.

“Is this how you plan on sleeping, it’s not very comfortable...”

Slowly he unwound his arms and allowed me to slide off of him to the side. He rolled onto his side and pulled me
back, nestling his head firmly against my chest with his arms wrapped around my middle again.

“....” My hands went to his hair, pulling out the ponytail and combing through the charcoal locks. “...when you
say you can’t sleep...it’s not an inflated truth or hyperbole, is it...? You really can’t. Is that a ghoul thing...? Not
being able to sleep if their—”
What had Nico said the CCG had called us? Mates? Kind of odd...

“---If your other half isn’t near you?”


The ghoul didn’t reply. After a minute of stretched silence I decided to take a peek down at his face. His eyes were
closed and his mouth slightly ajar; asleep. He must have fallen asleep almost immediately after cuddling close...

If only it were so easy for me.

## 727...

It was getting dangerously high. Something that had once seemed like a far off looming threat seemed to be lurking
closer...

## ♥



Perhaps there was something to Uta’s claim that he could only sleep next to me.
Or at the very least there was some truth that we slept better this way. Despite the worry worming its way around
my mind, I rested far better than the last two nights combined. With him holding me close like a precious doll I
was able to finally relax. It felt safe...

He still had his face pressed against my torso, arms grasping and holding me to him so it was unlikely I could
## 'escape'.
Likely , he was so relaxed because he inhaled my scent with every breath.

I had woken up because the sun was shining in the window. Which meant that it was now closing in on 'evening'
with the sun in the west.

While he slept his mouth was curled up into a soft smile. I couldn't bring myself to wake him.
Instead I stole glances down at his face until he groaned in his sleep and pulled me tight to himself again.

"Uta-kun...I know you want my scent, but you can't smother yourself in your sleep." I spoke as just a whisper,
fanning my fingers through his hair so gently to get it out of his face.

He was waking, slowly but surely. I just kept moving my hands through his hair until finally those eyes of his
opened up and he moved so he could peek up at me.

“...Ai-chan....you’re up.”

“Mmmm...Normally I’m the one waking up last. I got a rare chance to see your sleeping face...it’s cute!~” I smiled,
teasing him just a small bit. “It’s getting close to sunset though, Uta. We can see if Kazu managed to get the organs
here and then you’d better leave if you want to get home before it gets—”

“I’m staying.”

“But your shop ...it’s been closed for a week now, hasn’t it?”

The ghoul closed his eyes and stayed put despite being awake now. “I’ll go home in the morning. Are you going to
come back with me?.”


I frowned. Wrapping my arms around his head and hugging him to me. “...I can’t Uta. I told you. I’ll come back
during the weekends but—I’ve got work that I’ve got to get done. Especially right now. After I’ve finished sorting
through employee files and getting things set how I want them...”

“Bring them with you.”

“Uta...Kazuha is here . I doubt either you or he would be happy with staying on our couch. It’s convenient to have
him close to work on these things.” I sighed softly. If Uta really wasn’t sleeping well without me—if he really
wasn’t eating well, then me being away might actually hurt him.

“ I promise ...as soon as I lay out the groundwork I’ll come home and I’ll do whatever I can from there. It’s just
going to take a couple weeks...maybe a month. In the meantime, we can try feeding you the organs for that month.
If you stay here I can keep a close eye on your health! It would be better if you're getting good sleep to rule out that
as a variable... You...could take a vacation ?”

“...A vacation?”

“Yeah? A vacation. A break?...There’s a pool? There’s definitely some jacuzzi baths here. You could rest and relax?
Get a tan?” I was joking of course. If he wasn’t a Ghoul I’d assume he’d burn to a crisp. For all I knew he’d burn
and regenerate even paler than before. “There’s a bar—you could invite Itori and Nico? Renji too if you want?
Maybe I can convince Renji that it’s safe here and he’ll finally introduce us to his ‘Kitten’?... Couldn’t...we use
some relaxation? If the organs work, you won’t have to worry about food...? I...I know I can’t feed all the Ghouls
right now. But I might be able to feed just one . You can help me work out the kinks...make it better for Ghouls...
please? ”

I nibbled on my bottom lip as Uta lay still, probably mulling over what I offered.

“...I slept better with you close too...” I finally admitted it. “I need to be here . I need you here with me. Even if you
just want to stay in your room working anyway. Even if you only wanted me close to sleep next to—”


“Ai-chan.” He moved, hand covering my mouth and stopping me from rambling further. “A vacation sounds
nice...”


## ♥



## Chapter 70: Human Tofu
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text

## Chapter 70: Human Tofu


I sat nervously across the table from Uta.
Kazuha also stood by and although I knew he’d never admit it, I was sure that he was also curious about what was
about to happen.
Uta was looking curiously at the pile of ‘meat’ in front of him.

“...I didn’t realize he was just going to grab only liver for you.” I said softly, glancing at Kazu.

“I apologize. It is the furthest along in development. Liver has a lot of nutrients...at least in theory. I figured it was
the best choice.”

The ghoul lifted a piece and sniffed. I watched with bated breath as he licked it and then...
He opened his mouth wide and took a large bite. I couldn’t bear to breathe as I watched; fixated on his every tiny
micro expression.

From the moment he took a bite, I noticed the slight hesitation as he chewed.

He did though. Chew the liver...and swallow.

He didn’t grimace like he had over human food; which was a good start.

“So...?”

“It’s bland. Almost tasteless...” I frowned a bit, disappointed by the answer. So this wouldn’t work, would it?  Yet a
moment later, despite the complaint he took another large bite, chewed and swallowed.

He kept eating it even though it wasn’t good?

“Maybe...I could figure out a way to make it less bland...? Do you feel like you’ll puke it back up?”

The ghoul swallowed another bite and paused, placing a hand over his stomach as he seemed to try and feel how
his body was taking the ‘meal’.

“Not so far.”

“That is a good first step.” Kazuha stated stoically. “Better than I could have anticipated.”

“We’ll have to figure out how to make it not as bland. I know it’s probably not the best...but could you stomach
this for a little while, Uta-kun?”
Uta finished the first liver and moved onto the next with a small nod.

“Do you suggest Blood-Barbecue sauce, Madam?” I knew Kazuha meant it as a joke; one of the very few I would
likely ever hear him attempt to tell...but—

He saw the small mischievous smile that appeared on my face. “Madam, please tell me your not actually
considering—”

“ You're the one to suggest it!”

“It was a jest, Madam...”

“Maybe not a sauce..but...maybe they’re bland because they’ve never been in a human?”

“We can not put organs in people and then take them back out—”

“No, no! I wasn’t suggesting something barbaric like that! But we could have them used to filter blood before any
Ghoul eats them? Donated blood? They could be hooked to artificial systems where the liver filters the blood—”

“You're adding steps that made it rather complex, Madam. It would be difficult to do and also produce a high
volume of them. You are making what is essentially Tofu for Ghouls. I wouldn’t make it your life's goal for it to
taste good.”


“Well then, the alternative is ‘ Kazuha’s Blood-Barbeque sauce — I’ll make sure it’s on every store shelf with
your face on it.”

Kazuha’s face twitched. “I’ll see what I can do...”

My right-hand man walked from the room, leaving me with the ghoul who was eating from the small pile of
artificial human livers.
He glanced up at me, cheeks filled with meat before swallowing and giving me a quizzical look.

I smiled fondly, looking down at the counter and tracing some of the grout lines as I spoke: “I know you don’t feel
bad for killing to eat. You shouldn’t...I would never ask you to. And even if having a ‘guiltless’ meal where nobody
had to die for it means nothing to you. I am really happy you agreed to try this... thank you .”

“It’s not nothing to me.” I glanced up from the counter top. “It’s not ‘nothing’ if it means you are happy.”

I couldn't help but to beam at him, tears threatening to sting my eyes before I blinked them back.
“I don’t plan on feeding you bland Tofu-Human forever Uta...I’m hoping we can actually make it palatable
somehow.”

“He may be right.”

“...He’s not though, is he? We both know there are Ghouls out there that would take bland food over killing . But
we also know there’s Ghouls who would rather kill and have it taste good than eat something that only keeps them
alive ...”
Hell, there were Ghouls that would kill because they wanted to—Because they hated humans. Like Roma. I wanted
to make things better, but for Ghouls like that...where would they fit into the future I wanted to steer us towards?

I stood and moved around the table, leaning on Uta’s side as he slowly continued to munch on ‘human-tofu’.

“ — I have to make it taste good, so that there’s no excuse. Nobody can say I didn’t try my best to make things
better. I wouldn’t want my food to taste like cardboard...and I can’t expect people to change their ways just
because I—or anyone else says it’s ‘moral’. I won’t be mad if you go back to eating like usual after this little
vacation...But I hope that you want to be part of my future...? If— when I fix it so it tastes good?”

“...if it doesn't work? Would you be part of mine? Even if it’s not better...”

“...We should be careful...this almost sounds like a marriage proposal.” I giggled as his expression flipped from
concern to surprise in a manner of moments. “Of course, Uta. I’ll stay with you...Because it’s better with you .” I
leaned close and pressed my lips to his cheek.

“...You could marry me.” I felt my face flush and pulled back; searching his face for any hint that he was joking .

Instead he raised a hand to my shoulder, pushing aside the cloth and looking at the mark that he’d left in me for
life. Half of a whole, an incomplete set.

“...I told you it would scar Uta...and yet I can’t leave a mark on you at all.”

“You could try again. Any time you like.”

“I think I should probably avoid biting you for a while?” I leaned my face forward, meeting our foreheads in the
middle. “Does it bother you that I haven't left a mark?”

“...I can wait for you to make it official.” With his metaphorical mask cracked for me I could see a fond spark in his
eyes.

“So what does a ghoul wedding look like? Is there any celebration after the whole biting thing? I don’t fancy big
white dresses...”

The ghoul smiled and turned in his seat. An arm wrapped around my waist and pulled me up onto his lap.  “There
is. A party where you invite all your friends and family. Drinking. Food...No white dress. There’s some traditional
dresses. Jewelry. Things like that.”

“Really? That sounds like my kind of party!~”

I smiled fondly at the idea of a party with everyone invited; especially over something happy. There hadn’t been
anything like that since perhaps Christmas with the cafe.

“...so, Uta!~ Would you take my name or were you lying about a family name?”

“I didn’t lie. I must have had one, but I forgot it...” I furrowed my brows and shot him a concerned look that he
only shook his head too. “...I was eight when my parents were killed. I don’t remember the name they had. It
didn’t seem important to find out...”

“Oh...I’m sorry Uta.”

“It’s been a very long time since then. I do not even remember them. It doesn't bother me.”
I looked at his face, but despite the fact that he had cracked his mask open for me, I didn’t see any distress there.

“...I suppose it would be hard to miss something you don’t remember...or something you never had.” I thought of
my own parents, wishing that they had been parents that I could have missed. Kind Hearted. Loving. Involved in
my life, rather than puppeteering it from the sideline.

“So...Uta Kaneshiro? What do you think? Or we could make something up like the doc said...whatever name you
want.” Wrapping my arms around his shoulders I stayed put in his lap as he brought another bite of tofu liver to
his mouth.


Oddly enough this didn’t bother me .
Nobody died for him to eat this. I didn’t have to think about how they had a name or a face or people waiting for
them at home. Meat could be meat, and people could be people. Hopefully.

Uta had as a matter of fact almost completely finished the liver, and thus far it seemed that his stomach was
keeping it down. Even if it didn’t taste all that great - it was still a success!

“Do you want me to take your name?” I considered Uta’s question and then shook my head.

“If I had a choice...it would be my preference to never be called Kaneshiro again.” Instead of telling people to just
call me Aika, they could use a married name. Whatever Uta picked. It was a nice thought...

“You could pick anything...as long as you share it with me!~”

The ghoul seemed to start thinking right away and I giggled.
“You don’t have to think of something right now on the spot. Think about it for a while. I’m not going
anywhere...”



## ♥

I kept my eye on Uta for some time after ‘dinner’. He seemed fine. After an hour passed I started to relax and feel
the beginnings of giddiness.

“...How are you feeling?”

The ghoul glanced down at me, his lips slightly downturned as I asked the same question I’d asked half a dozen
times already. “I’m still fine, Ai-chan...”

“I know. I know . I’m just—what about your hunger? I haven't asked about that. Are you still hungry...?” If he
could eat it, but it didn’t help feed his hunger then it was all for not.

“Mmmm.” Uta’s lips curled into a smirk only a moment before I was pinned to a wall, right next to some
expensive work or art. My back was flat to the wall and Uta loomed over me with a mischievous look on his face.

“I could still eat...Maybe some dessert. Something that tastes sweet.”


For a split second I felt concerned that the liver hadn’t filled him at all before I flushed red.

Oh. Oh he is teasing! I laughed even though my face was still cherry red.

“I think you’re mixing up hungry and horny again, Uta. Not that I mind!~”

“Am I? I think—”
Uta took a step back quite suddenly, hands held up. His head turned and his ghoulish eyes were trained on
someone down the hallway. I followed his gaze and squinted into the sunset lit hallways cast in shadows.

First I took note of a figure in the hallway.  It appeared to only be security. Doing their rounds. “Uta...what’s
wrong—”
Then I spotted how they held themselves.
How they had their weapon out.
Pointing it at—

“Put that away.” I snapped, my voice echoing down the hallways as I hurried between Uta and the security staff
member.

“That thing was—” Thing. That thing!?

“Put that away and report to Kazuha this instant...”

The security officer took the sights of the weapon off of us and slowly put the weapon away. I heard the hurried
footsteps before I glanced backwards to see two more Humans join us.
A member of the cleaning staff and head of security.

“Madam, we heard yelling. What is the problem?”

“Bring that man to Kazuha...” I clenched my fists at my side. “Actually...have all the staff brought to a board
room. The one on the second floor will work.”

“Everybody, Madam?”

“All members of staff. Everybody. I don’t care if they’re sleeping, drag them out of bed...”

“Y-yes. Of course Madam, right away...”

I watched, bristling with anger as the members of staff walked away.
Uta lowered his hands, but stayed quiet as I pulled out my phone and dialed for Kazuha. On the other end I heard
Kazuha’s tired voice, groggy from sleep.

“Madam...?”

“I know I told you to go to bed. I apologize. We’re having a staff meeting. I think before I go through the company

staff—in-house staff needs to be looked at more closely.”

There was a pause and then a sigh. In the background of the call I could hear the shuffle of sheets and fabric as
Kazuha got up out of bed.

“What happened...?”

“Security pointed their weapons at Uta. I want to make it clear that that will never happen again...”
I heard an unfamiliar curse from over the phone line before he spoke again:
“Of course. Understood Madam.”

“Board room, second floor. Everybody. I don’t care if they’re a cook or the janitor or a member of  security...”
I hung up a moment later and clenched my fingers around the device.


“Ai-chan. I understand why they reacted like that. I’m not bothered by it.”

“I can understand too...I do understand.” I turned to Uta and pocketed my phone and then reached out to him.
Curling my fingers into his shirt I tugged on him to stand closer. “But...you protect me in your territory. When
anybody threatened me there you ate them. This is what you might call my territory. I promised you it was
safe...they’ve all been jumpy and skittish all day. But now they’re pointing weapons at you. So now I’m fixing it.
This will be fixed. It won’t happen again.”

“Your territory, humm?” The ghoul leaned forward, bending his head to make sure he could look me in the eye. I
didn't fail to notice the tiny smirk on his face. “Acting a little ghoulish Ai-chan...”

“...I only meant in a manner of speaking. I own everything in it. It is a place where I sleep. I eat. People here do as I
say. Things grind to a halt if I order it. That makes it mine. Doesn't it?”
I didn’t consider myself territorial like a Ghoul, but the idea that someone was threatening Uta under my nose like
this—it ground on my last nerve sparking rage.

I let go of his shirt, reaching to touch my scarred shoulder and smiling fondly up at him. I was resolute with my
choice.

“And you're mine too...So they won’t be threatening my fiance.”

“Fiance?”

“It seemed appropriate until I put my mark on you. Did I misinterpret something...? Perhaps you didn’t mean to
ask me to marry you?”

“No.” The ghoul’s eyes gleamed as he stared at me. “I did...”


“...and so you have my answer!~” I leaned forward up on my toes and pressed a gentle kiss against his lips. “Now
let me go make sure nobody dares to point a weapon at you again.”



## ♥

Looking at everyone gathered I found myself rather surprised.
The amount of people here was more than I had ever imagined.
Most of them worked in the background; away from prying eyes where I’d never even seen them. Now they stood
in groups representing what they did.

Security with security. Cleaning with cleaning. Cooks and kitchen all together. So on so forth.

The outliers were people like Kazuha. Or the Doctor who was standing by a window with a huge leering grin on
his face. Merlin stood aside from the rest of the drivers, closer to Kazu and the Doc—exchanging words with the
latter.

Uta had followed me into the room, standing behind me. I had watched several of the staff members from various
groups tense and the muttering that followed. This was why we were here. I took a deep breath and let it out nice
and slow.

I had to remain calm.
No yelling, no snapping.

Professional. Just like my meeting with the company.

“It has come to my attention that among my staff there are people uncomfortable with Uta being here. Perhaps, to
be more concise: uncomfortable with Ghouls.” My eyes landed on Ms. Sato and lingered there while the older
woman squirmed.
She didn’t get a pass just because she had been kind to me as a child.

If I couldn’t even put my foot down here, how was I going to convince the outside world?!

“You are all aware of the fate of my parents. Many of you have worked for them for years so I can understand that
you may still be shaken by what happened. Perhaps they tolerated it, perhaps it was even encouraged to have less
than positive views on Ghouls. My father spent his life avoiding becoming a Ghoul so I can’t imagine he expressed
any support for them despite his own brother being one. However, I will not. Not in the company, and especially
not in my own household.”


I took a breath and then spoke a little louder:

“I will especially not tolerate anybody pointing a weapon at my fiance while he simply is trying to kiss me in the
hallways...”

Kazuha’s eyes widened slightly at the announcement. I swore I could even spot a faint blush appear on his face
while the Doctor simply giggled and lifted his hand and held it palm out. Merlin’s head lifted and he was glancing
at Uta and then myself. At first he seemed annoyed...

Then I watched him pull out some money and slap it into the doctor's then outstretched hand... he caught my eye
and put on a sheepish smile.

Were they taking bets?

Kazuha cleared his throat and stepped forward. “I apologize, Madam. I will do a thorough review of our staff and
make sure that appropriate measures are taken. You can rest assured that nothing like this will happen again.”

“...Good. And Kazuha? If they have any issue with ghoul staff joining them they should resign.”

“Resign? You—” He only hesitated a moment before nodding: “Of course. If you have people in mind, please let
me know.”

I didn’t....currently . But considering everything I wanted , would it be such a terrible idea? If they agreed not to
hunt too close to the house and never hurt anybody here . Perhaps anybody I hired would like to be part of the
first group of Ghouls who would eat the tofu-human regularly by choice.



“ You can’t be serious! ”

I turned my head to see that the man who had aimed his weapon at Uta had stepped forward, raising his voice
above the soft muttering of others behind him.
“We already are being told to ignore them. Then to protect them—now you expect us to work with those things!?
We’re supposed to just listen to her cause she’s the daughter of some—”

“ Everybody here is the same in the eyes of the CCG, surely you all realize that? Ghoul or Human?” I grit my
teeth and stepped closer to the man. “Surely you’re not so stupid to think they wouldn’t throw you into prison
and torture you just the same as any Ghoul you call a ‘thing’?”

“And why would I get tortured, huh?! I’d just tell them where to find the vermin’s nest!”


I didn’t get a chance to react.

Not his words or even the fact that he reached for the weapon that was still strapped to his belt.

Kazuha’s fingers snapped and pointed at the officer. Two men behind him disarmed the young man and began
dragging him away out the board room doorway as he kicked and screamed about monsters .
I was fairly sure the word ghoul-fucker was thrown in there at least once.

I was staring at the spot where he had been for a minute; listening for a long time as he was dragged down the
hallway before all was quiet again.


Most of the staff remaining simply quietly muttered among themselves. I took another deep breath and looked
back up again.

“I realize that changes might be difficult. You are not accustomed to myself, or my friends. I am sure you are not
sure what to expect from me since I’ve been gone. The last time many of you saw me I was a very different person.
I know that my arrival may be unwelcomed by some who would prefer it to stay the same...and perhaps it wasn’t
widely announced when I arrived with Uta that he was a Ghoul. That he was my boyfriend. My fiance . However,
I am not the type of person who would bring someone to my home if I thought they were going to harm anybody.
I expect my staff to treat my guests, regardless of their status with the same respect you would give myself, or to
Kazuha...anything less is disgraceful.”

I glanced at Ms. Sato and frowned. “---Off handed comments about ghouls and what should be done with them are
not welcome. Nor are threats or violence. From either party.”



## ♥

Many of the people in the room filled out, heading back to bed or off to keep doing their work.
First to approach me was the head of security who apologized for the behavior of the young man. He would be
looking into the security to ensure that nothing like that behavior happened again.

“Captain? Is that what I should call you? I don’t care what Uta is doing. Or how threatening you think he is.
Nobody is to point a weapon at him again. Understood?”

The man had looked a little pale, but nodded his agreement and hurried off with a dozen security scurrying after
him like ducklings.


Merlin was the second person who came up to me. He was spinning an unlit cigar in between his fingers and
giving me a huge goofy grin as he walked over.
I smiled faintly as he approached and felt my shoulders fall as some tension left me.

“Hey there Lil’ Lady...Congrats.”

“Congrats...?”

“On the engagement of course. Didn’t think you’d be marrying the fellow...Not so soon at any rate. But I suppose
I was wrong.”

“From the looks of it, you lost a bet? ”

“Yeah...with that quack. Was a bad bet to take, wasn’t it?” Merlin grinned and stuck the unlit cigar between his
lips.



“What’s going to happen to him?”

“I told you, Lil’ Aika. ’ Nobody leaves '...” Merlin scratched at his beard, but seemed unbothered by the notion that
another staff member had been dragged away. “Alive that is...”

My eyes widened, recalling the conversation that night in the car. Merlin had been so shifty about that particular
comment.
“ That’s what you meant?! On top of everything else did my parents kill anybody who didn’t agree with them!?”

“Ehhhhh. I can’t tell you that they were good people. It would be a lie...but as for that. Yes and no . Your father
didn’t do any of the killing. Mother wasn’t fond of it either. But you can’t expect any of us to just stand by when
something like that happens. As you said: we all know the secret . We are all the same in the eyes of the CCG. You
could say that the Kaneshiro household is a bit like a hive of hornets protecting their nest .” Merlin clapped a hand
over Uta’s shoulder in a friendly manner.

“Anyway, I don’t see any difference...’cept maybe this one's eyes. You hungry kiddo? Fresh meat down the hall for
the taking if you wanted it...”

Uta glanced at Merlin blankly under the friendly touch and blinked. He only glanced at me briefly before
answering: “I’m on a special diet...”

“---and I didn’t mean for him to die! Kazuha !”

Kazu glanced my way, torn from his conversation with a few members of staff. When he saw my expression he
frowned and shook his head.

“ Ai-chan ...it’s too late for that.” Uta said.
“Why? Why is it too late?”

“They snapped his neck the moment he was down the end of the hallway.” Uta replied calmly; now glancing
around the room. His eyes lingered on a few faces and studied them. Clearly something had just occurred to him
that I didn’t understand quite yet.

“Look kiddo...Don’t feel too bad. He should have known better than to shake the hive .” Merlin pulled out a chair
from a table and sat down on it, finally lighting his cigar even though we were inside.
I couldn't even bring myself to yell at him for lighting it indoors; I was still trying to process that the officer from
before was dead .
Just like that .

“...You shouldn’t feel too bad about that man, he never would have lasted more than a week after threatening you
and your gentle-lad there. Trying to pull the gun was just reckless and suicidal. Didn’t like him much myself
anyways...”

“What’s that supposed to mean?” I could only mutter softly; staring hopelessly at the older gentleman.
I’d only known him as a slightly rough around the edges driver who cracked jokes from time to time.

“After a stunt like that?” He puffed out a circle of smoke and smiled solemnly.

“I know I’m not going to be ruining your view of your father, you never did like him much. But what sort of
people do you think work for a place like this ?”

To be completely honest, I hadn’t ever considered where the people had come from. Their origins. How they
came to work here of all places; a household of half ‘monsters’ and more money than anybody could possibly
spend.
My parents themselves weren’t exactly upstanding members of society.
So who were the staff?

The older man sighed and let out a puff of smoke. “You don’t find it strange that Kazuha was able to arrange
buying that kid so quickly? Or why I didn’t even ask why I had to pick you up a few blocks from a ghoul auction ?
Or why you were with the Clowns ?”

Merlin glanced at Uta with a raised eyebrow.
“How...do you know that?”


“...you don’t survive the sort of world your da’ was a part of without knowing a few ‘ faces’ . What Kazu does for
you now, was what I did for your father. A sorta fixer . Someone who got things done. You order it and it
happens. With some of the things your father wanted; it included Ghouls.”

I glanced away from Merlin for a moment to look around the room full of people who were casually chatting with
each other, seemingly having forgotten that someone had been dragged off to die—Kazuha was speaking calmly
with a nervous looking Ms. Sato. I made a note to make sure that nothing happened to her.
Not... death at least.

“Anyway, that man you're so worried about was an arsonist. Killed three people, including a child when he burnt
down an apartment building. Yappy fellow too. Like...one of those small dogs? Chihuahuas? Trust me, he’s
already stepped on some other peoples toes since he was hired...pretty sure some of the maid staff wanted to shove
him down a long set of stairs. Plenty of them around, you know?”

I didn’t want to laugh, even though Merlin was trying pretty hard to get me to laugh at the rather morbid jokes.
When he saw it wasn’t working he dropped his smile a bit.

“The gardeners? The drivers? The maids? Burglary. Embezzlement. Organized crime. That doc fellow—” Merlin
thumbed towards the doctor who was watching us from across the room; he grinned with just a few too many
teeth when he was mentioned.

“—was charged with smuggling some ‘interesting’ things before Kazuha found him. ‘Parently having bits of dead
n’ mummified Humans or Ghouls isn’t exactly legal. Then there’s Ms. Sato. Poisoned her first and second
husband. Funny, isn’t it? Not sure it’s a good idea to have the poisoner as head cook, but she’s good at it. And it's
not like anybody died here. From the food at least. Although that apple pie of hers might be worth dying for!~”
He chuckled and sighed wistfully, kicking back his legs.

“Are the entire staff criminals...?” Uta asked for me as I glanced from one friendly familiar face to the next.

“Nearly everyone.” Kazuha had crossed the room and joined the conversation; now standing with his arms behind
his back like a statue. “---I should note; that does not apply to the staff at the labs or corporate building. Only the
household staff. Nobody outside the staff in the manor has any knowledge of your family history. That is what
makes it rather difficult to move them as quickly as you wish Madam. You have my apologies for not informing
you sooner. I had not expected you to move in—and when you did. You seemed...”

He glanced at Uta briefly and frowned severely. “— distressed...However, your father employed these people.
Made their problems go away and in exchange had their loyalty. Seeing as many of them were around when you
were here before, your safety was never a concern. That particular man was one that I hired in the last few months.
You may put the blame squarely on my shoulders for his behavior. Future staff will be checked thoroughly and
approved by yourself.”

“‘ These people ’ he says. As if he’s innocent!” Merlin chuckled.

Kazuha sighed, exasperated as he continued to deal with Merlin. His predecessor, if I was following what I’d been

told. “I think it’s hardly important—”

“Plenty more you need to tell her still—Anyway; this lad was caught pick pocketing . Tried to pickpocket Sir
Kaneshiro himself while he was out one day. Luckiest day of lil’ Kazu’s life.” Merlin announced for him when
Kazuha hadn’t done it fast enough on his own.

“...I was young. A kid!” I stared at Kazuha as he snapped. I don’t think I’d ever seen him break composure like that
before. It was gone in a fleeting moment though; he cleared his throat and reasserted his composure.

“Young and starving on the street. Fourth ward , wasn’t it Lil’ Kazu? The ol’ Sir pulled you up by the scruff of
your neck, gave you a home and set you on your feet and made sure you got an education so you could do what
you do now for the young lady. The bottom line is most of us would never want to leave...We got it good here.
Better here than out there.”

Merlin blew out another ring of smoke and I watched Kazuha’s disdainful expression as he waved away the smell
of it. Merlin held up the cigar in his hand. “...You know how much each of these cost out there? I’ve been smoking
them for over twenty-five years now. I couldn’t afford to do that anywhere else...”

“...and you...? What did you do when my father hired you?”

“I was one of the first ‘misbegotten’ staff. I was in the US Navy ‘for your father picked me up. I got into a spot of
trouble not long after I got off the boat here about thirty years ago. Got drunk. When I woke up I was in cuffs in a
cell. They said I killed a guy. Beat him to death in a drunken rage. I was about to spend the rest of my life sitting
behind bars—your father happened to be around and made the problem disappear . Freedom. A second chance. A
good paying job. I’d be a fool not to do anything he wanted in exchange. There’s conditions of course. Keep the
secrets. Keep him safe. ‘Fix’ a few things for him once in a while. And of course keep out of the liquor cabinets. I
quit the same night. Haven't picked up a bottle since...”

It explained a lot. Why nobody ever said a word—
The odd assortment of people.
I’d never once questioned how any of them had gotten here.

“ Don’t get me wrong . They ain't bad people, Lil’ Lady...just put in unfortunate situations. Down on your luck,
bad-luck people. You don’t like ya’ father. Trust me I understand. Locking you up like that. The ways you’s was
raised weren’t right. But there’s a reason why he’s never been found out...Why all of us are all loyal. He did well by
us. For now, they’re uncertain that you’ll do the same.”

Merlin glanced at Uta quickly before looking back at myself. “None of us get to choose where we stand in life. So
it’s best to stay loyal to those who stand with you.”
Then, as if having a second thought he glanced over his shoulder at the doctor.

“Well...cept that Doc. Not too sure ‘bout him. There’s a few screws loose en’ him. But don’t tell him I said that...”
Merlin quietly muttered, taking another drag off the cigar. “He’s a decent enough fello’ I guess. Trust worth as the

rest o’ us. It’s just lil’ freaky how he gets when he’s examining you, isn’t it?”

“What will happen to—whatever his name was...”

“Oh. Probably be sent off for testing. Research—Lab, right Kazu?”

Kazuha grimaced but nodded. “Unless your fiance has any wish to eat him, he will be sent off to the lab after all
identifiable parts are stripped.”

“But...his family.”

“...none of us got any, Lil’ Lady. Suppose it’s also a job requirement . Or maybe part of that bad luck I told you
about.” Merlin smiled sadly again, leaning his chair back and closing his eyes peacefully.



## ♥


Uta watched Aika as they exited the board room.
It wasn’t how she thought the night would go. Another strike at her moral compass. Another blow to her overall
moral. He could see the way she walked and the way her brows furrowed together as she considered all that she’d
learned.

All of them were criminals.
The staff. Kazuha. The doctor. Merlin. She hadn't thought to consider it, so it took her by surprise and shook what she
previously believed about them .

Yet she didn’t think ill of him?
Everybody at Anteiku; All the customers and all the staff?
Even Aika herself was a criminal ; simply for the crime of knowing a Ghoul and staying silent.

It was a fact that Uta often thought she forgot about; right up until an investigator was near.

Even in those times rather than worry that she might be caught and taken away for such a crime, she seemed more
worried that her friends were in danger.
He had watched her thrust herself into conversations and distract the Humans away without a single care that she
was exposing herself to scrutiny as well.

“I feel stupid...” Uta’s eyes glanced from the hallway ahead down at the solemn faced woman; his mate. His fiance.

“Hmmm? You’re upset they are criminals..?”


“Not...” She seemed to struggle for a moment then sighed, shoulders falling. “Not about anything they’ve done. I
remember most of them. I know how they really are, at least how they were after working in the manor. I’m upset
with myself. I should have known sooner. It was obvious, wasn’t it? Even if it wasn’t—I should have thought to
ask more questions. Get the answers for myself. I say it’s my territory. And yet I have no idea how most of it
works...how stupid was that?”

His lips pressed together, frowning at the realization she’d come to. He couldn’t exactly disagree.  But she was
learning that she needed to figure things out fast . Otherwise her plans for their future might go up in smoke—and
they’d be in his future.

As long as she was with him, he didn’t really care. He could figure out a way to make her happy; one way or another.
But until it did go up in flames, he’d be supportive. Even help by eating bland and frankly bad food if Aika would
stay happy. If she kept being some warmth in the world for a Ghoul like him.

“They still listen to you regardless.”

“...they listen to Kazuha. So all of it hinges on one man .”

“And he listens to you.”

“And if he stops? What then?”

“...then I eat him.” Uta smiled faintly as Aika’s frown fell into a blank stare. Slowly she smiled and rolled her eyes at
his ‘joke’.

“ Maybe ...if he ever betrays me like that. Then you can eat him. But until then, he’s off limits. Everybody here is.”

## Chapter 71: Vacation



“We are relaxing. Immediately ...”

“Is relaxing normally done so rushed?”

“...After everything that’s happened? Yes. So we need to start relaxing as fast as possible."

I laughed, despite the worry deep down that it really was true; bad things kept happening. One after another.
When there wasn't much room between each new ‘bad’ thing you had to squeeze in time for relaxing or maybe go
mad from it all.

At least I could say there wasn’t a boring moment since meeting Uta...

After only a few minutes of preparation I had begun by guiding the very willing ghoul to come along with me.

He had seemed momentarily confused at first when we grabbed some clothes from his room and then left; only to
enter several different ones. One after another, when they didn’t have what I was looking for I went to the next
one.

After checking a few of the larger rooms I had found one that included an indoor jacuzzi large enough for both of
us to very comfortably lay out and have our own jets. I ignored the luxurious bedroom with the four poster bed,
draped in black and purple linens and went straight to the bathroom to fill the huge tub with hot water. I flipped
the lights onto ‘low’ and leaned over the edge to test the jets on each side.

“I think Kazu doesn't like you very much...” I muttered as I glanced around the bathroom. Maybe putting Uta in
his rather humble room was his passive aggressive way of telling Uta he didn’t like him. Or...it was because Uta’s
room was the room furthest from my own bedroom. “...he really should have put you in a nicer room like this. I
could have your stuff moved, if you’d like?”

“Perhaps, if we’re sharing a room. Both our things would fit better in here.”

I glanced over my shoulder and smiled faintly. Our things would fit better here wouldn’t they?

His desk could go in one corner with all his projects he wanted to work on, and mine could be in the other corner;
stacked with all my company paperwork I had to get through.

Working separately but together—it would be peaceful in quiet company.


It might be time I moved myself out of my old ‘prison’. I didn’t have to stay up there where I’d been kept as a kid.
“If we stayed together in the same room it would make staying here so much for the next month easier on you,
wouldn't it? Not that I’m keeping you here.”

I walked back across the room to him, standing next to him in the bedroom as he looked around. He touched the
bedding, running his hands over the silken sheets and plush duvet.
“I can have materials brought here...so you can still make masks? More art supplies? Canvases? So you’re not
bored. Anything you’d like—?”

Uta turned his eyes on me again, cocking his head to one side like a curious dog. “You don’t have to, Ai-chan.”

“But—”
