Uta had sent me a message saying that he was on his way back with our company over half an hour ago, and since
then I hadn’t been able to stay still.
I was already dressed in my swimming suit with a silky swaying skirt tied around my waist. The pool was already
set up with a net and many many floats and lounging chairs. I’d even managed to get the livers put in a cooler by
the pool...just in case Uta got hungry or if the others wanted to try.

Merlin was retrieving them now.
I’d even sent money with the request that Uta buy plenty of blood wine.

Still, I was nervous. To see Itori and Nico for the first time since...the Auction. I didn’t know if they thought I was
angry with them as well. I wasn’t. I had never been. As I told Uta, it’s not like I was in love with them. I didn’t need
them to be better.

I’d also tell them about me and Uta; our marriage. They’d be some of the first of our Ghoul friends to know.

I jumped when I heard the tires pull onto the driveway, the gate swinging open and bringing guests!!!

Nearly shaking with excitement I pushed open the main doors and hurried down the steps to meet Uta in the
middle, wrapping my arms around him.
Two days. He had gone home to work at his shop for two whole days.

“I missed you, Uta-kun!~” The ghoul leaned his head down and nuzzled against my neck, inhaling my scent and
nodding. He missed me too. But he had work to do, just as I did. I couldn’t deny that his work was important as well;
keeping his fellow Ghouls safe with their masks.

“Did they come too...?” I stood on my tippy toes, looking over his shoulder to see Itori and Nico looking around
the front of the manor.
The red head whistled as she craned her neck to look up at the building.

“...Man. I heard the Kaneshiro’s were loaded. I didn’t know you had it like this.” Itori’s eyes landed on me and her
eyes went wide. “Wow, you look great!”

“It’s...I—thank you? I suppose this place is...Okay? I guess? No Renji-kun with you?” I looked for the silver haired
ghoul but he seemed to be absent. Disappointing, but if he showed up later the staff was instructed to let him in at
any time.

I smiled sheepishly and stepped away from Uta to wave both her and Nico to the building. “You can visit anytime
you like. I’ll put you on the list of people who can. Come with me. I’ll show you around.”

They followed into the lobby. I smiled at the set of three masks surrounding a huge charcoal drawing that Uta had
done. “Those are new! I wanted to make sure that Uta’s work was where everybody can see it as soon as they walk
in!”

I gave them a very short tour, mostly to walk them back to the pool. I pointed at the bar that stood by the pool and
smiled. “There’s some fridges in there for the blood wine. Glasses in the cupboard. You’re welcome to use them!”

“I hope you brought some swimming suits; there’s a changing shack you can use there—” I pointed at another
building next to the pool. “Uta-kun—I got you something!”
I hurried over to a bench by the pool and picked up a box to hand to the ghoul.

He took it and opened it, showing the black and red checkered swim trunks I’d picked out for him.
“Do you like them?”

“They’re perfect. Thank you, Ai-chan.”

“Oh I have the perfect thing!~”

“And I wore mine under my clothing! U-kun mentioned you were throwing a party and there was a pool!” Itori
winked and giggled. “I can’t believe Renji is missing this!~”

“I’m hoping he shows up later...I wanted to tell you all together...but—”
I glanced at Uta, stepping close to his side and leaning into him before looking back to the two waiting Ghouls.

“Uta and I...aaaaaaaaaaaare...going to get married!~”

I drew out the announcement as long as possible, feeling my heartbeat in my throat.

A solid second passed before Itori squealed, running over to me and pulling me from Uta’s side to hug me tight
that made me feel like all the air in my lungs were being squeezed out.

“OH! That’s amazing! When!? When’s the wedding!? There’s so much to do! Are you doing it the Human way
or—”


“We’ll have a Ghoul wedding.” Uta spoke up, looking down at me with a fond smile. “No white dresses, right Ai-
chan?”

“Right—” I wheezed. “Plus...I think it would be better. With all my friends? Everyone I want there are
Ghouls...except. Kimi...she’s Human. I think that she’d be okay with everyone though! Since she’s dating Nishiki!
That being said—I have no idea what needs to be ‘set up’. Or when...or where to have it. I was hoping....that
maybe everyone wouldn’t mind leaving Tokyo for a bit. Going out near my Uncle? There’s that field by his home.
And...I could have him at my wedding? It would be important to me...since he’s my family. He’ll be yours too,
## Uta.”

Uta smiled faintly and ‘took’ me back from Itori and pulled me close “That would be fine.”

“Congrats! Of course we knew—” Nico smiled, winking as he motioned at his shoulder. “With a mark like that...”

“Well yes...but—” Itori glanced at Uta’s blank collarbone.

“Not from lack of trying...” I blushed faintly and looked away from any of them.
“She’s not able to bite hard enough to put a mark.” Uta supplied softly. “I can wait til she can.”
I grasped his arm, lifting it to show his wrist where we wore matching though opposite bracelets. The ones I had
gotten him on one of our dates; before it had gone south...and Uta ate half a man.

“Until then—These are okay!”

Itori was beaming, looking between me and Uta. “Our U-kun getting married! You’ll be a little family! I can not
wait to see Ren-kun’s face! Maybe he’ll actually drop that grumpy look on his face. He loved this sort of thing
when his sister got married...I don’t think any of us have been to a wedding in so long...”

I smiled and nodded: “I thought that was another reason to have a ‘Ghoul’ wedding. I want...something happy for
everyone to go to. Maybe if someone can get in contact with Kaneki he could come too...?”

“Tsukiyama too?” Uta questioned and I didn’t have an answer right away for him.
“I’m not sure. I know I must be crazy because I want to say yes.”

“Hmmm...He was your friend as a kid. Invite him.”
I glanced up at Uta and raised an eyebrow. Considering how he’d acted before I was surprised by Uta’s insistence.
The two of them didn’t really get along since their confrontation; or at least I thought not.

“You are friends with the Gourmet! I was surprised, Aika!~ Friends in high places, hum? He wouldn’t have done
what he did at the Auction if he wasn’t a friend. That’s for sure. He insulted that Ghoul chef for you—a rather
well known chef!~” Nico commented with a weary smile. “I am sorry I couldn’t do much else for you my dear...”

I wouldn’t comment on there being Ghoul chefs. But for someone called the ‘Gourmet’ perhaps it was a big deal

for him to do what he had done there. Bigger than I had initially considered. I should thank him? I’d been so upset
that I’d forgotten...

“It’s okay Nico...you did what you could. I don’t blame you. There’s nothing anybody else could have done at that
point. I am not angry with anybody but Roma right now...I promise.” I glanced at Uta and nudged him lightly. “I
was pissed at Uta...but we worked it out.”

Upon being nudged the ghoul wrapped his arms around me from back to front, holding me close; his head resting
on my shoulder. He made an affirmative noise and I smiled faintly.

“What about...the kid you...bought?” Itori seemed hesitant to ask.

“He’s in the basement—” I paused and I winced. “That sounds really horrible. Ahhh... containment room sounds
worse...you know...I really don't have a good way to say this. I could just show you later. But he’s got a very large
room with nearly every toy a child could think of, let alone want.”

“He seems happy, all things considered. He is rather fond of Ai-chan...” Uta supplied with a chuckle.

“He’s warming up to you too, Uta-kun! We did his hair cause it was getting long. He asked for it to be shaved up
like Uta’s!~ He looks like a little mini-Uta! It’s adorable!”

“I can’t believe this is happening!” Itori was laughing, holding her hand over her mouth and looking at Uta with
happiness. And also a very amused expression. “Oh man...I’m glad I didn’t put money down on this. I would have
bet Ren-kun would be the one with a family. But look at you U-kun! A wife and a kid! You’ve really settled down,
haven't you?~”

“I—W-we aren’t keeping the kid—” I lifted my hands up, waving away her assumption. “It’s just temporary until
we can find a safe place for him to stay. A new family. A new identity...maybe really far away so nobody could ever
recognise him. It’s just...setting up that sort of thing takes a bit of time.”

The ghoul by my shoulder hummed softly. “Your uncle is watching him soon, isn’t he?”

“Mmm... yeah. We’ll have to bring him out to the countryside before we go back to the shop. I was hoping that
Renji could take us all out there again. I hate to bother him...but I’d rather if he brought us rather than Merlin...I
don’t think the staff or even Kazuha know exactly where he lives.”

And I’d like to keep it that way. I may trust them a lot, but not with that.
Worse case scenario, that information could be tortured out of them.

I clapped my hands together and took a deep breath.
“But enough of that! We’re celebrating! And having fun!” I turned in Uta’s arms and pushed him gently
towards the shack where the changing room was. “Go, go, go! Change into your new shorts! I’m not going to win
a game of volleyball without you!”



## ♥




I pressed a button on a radio on the bar-top and swayed to the music. “There we go!~”

Shedding my skirt from my waist I ran and jumped into the deep end of the pool. When I reached the surface
again I threw my hair back, wrapping a band around it to keep it from getting in my face all over again.

“Come on Itori—it’s heated!”

Nico was already kicked back, relaxing in the sun. He had shed his shirt and was now leaned back, soaking up the
rays with a smile on his face.
Itori stripped off her outer clothing and folded them onto a lounge chair. She was wearing a two piece bikini; red
with hearts and diamonds all over it. Not unlike her clown mask actually.

I climbed out of the pool when I saw Uta come back out with his clothes hanging from his arm, dressed in the set
of trunks I’d gotten him. Perfect.

Hiding a smirk that would have given it away I walked around him as if inspecting.
“They look really good...”

No warning, I threw my weight into him, wrapped my arms around his middle and tackled him off the edge of the
pool into the deep end!

“Gottcha!~”

I heard a soft gasp from him as we tipped over  into the pool. I laughed right before he hit the water with a huge
splash! I came back up coughing water from my nose and still laughing.
The goth ghoul held on tight to my waist, legs kicking under the water to keep us both afloat as he shook water
from his hair and face and accessed the situation.

“You—”

“I got you off guard huh? I win!~”

The ghoul blinked, wiping away water from his eyes. Then slowly...he grinned.

“You get a point...you have not won anything.”


Oh boy!


## ♥



Renji appearing over two hours later was as much a surprise as it was a joyous moment. A member of staff guided
the ghoul to the pool where Uta, Nico, Itori and myself were playing Volleyball in the pool.

No matter how much I’d dive headlong for every ball I’d still end up missing.
Itori was being completely unfair about it—aiming for me each time!!!

The multicolored ball bounced off the back of my head when I heard Renji’s voice. I turned and grinned at him.
Bjorn bounced around the edge of the pool and rushed to greet the silver haired ghoul, meeting him before I
could. Pulling myself up and out of the pool rushed over to him, stopping short from giving him a wet hug.

“Renji-kun! You made it! I didn’t think you would when you were so late...”
The ghoul nodded, walking to a chair at the bar. I followed him, eager to tell him the good news.
However he seemed—off. Renji was serious a lot of the time, but this seemed different than most times.

“Hey...are you okay?”

“Yeah.”

“Renji ran off into a fight recently, didn’t you? After that doctor.” Renji shot Itori a harsh look and the woman
grinned, leaning on the edge of the pool.
“Oh, come on now, Ren-kun! You know me, I hear things...So how’d it go? What did you find down there?”

“You don’t already know?”

“Sadly no...” Itori pouted. “Someone destroyed my ear before I could get close. And reception isn’t good
underground. I didn’t catch what happened.”

“Doctors lab...?” I looked between all the Ghouls and pouted. I felt out of the loop. “Someone please explain.”

“You know Kaneki, of course, how he was originally human? He was turned into a one-eye by a doctor .” Itori
crossed her two pointer fingers over each other as she explained. “---Transplanted organs from a Ghoul named
Rize." Itori said it much too cheerfully for my liking.



"It seems Ken, Algori Tree and CCG were all looking into the doctor..." Renji spoke seriously, almost sounding
somber as he added: “Ken has a half-kakuja now...”

“Oh, he’s really going overboard...isn’t he? I remember when he was such a nervous little boy! They grow up so fast!
What a tragedy~ ”

“What’s a doctor doing making Humans into Ghouls?” I asked, frowning. “I don’t see why someone would do
that...”

Renji stared for a moment at Itori and then dropped his gaze down to the bar.
"Dr. Kanou is trying to create hybrids...there were... things there that weren't Human or Ghoul. It doesn't seem to
have a high success rate."

“Anything else, Ren-kun?”

“.. .No . Nothing. Ken and the others got out safely. Tsukiyama was there.” Renji turned to me, eyes searching my
face for a reaction.

He’s changing the subject.

He was friends with Uta and Itori, but he was separated from them in a way I’d always sort of noticed but never
commented on. He ate suicide victims. He was more like...Yoshimura. More humane in his own way.

Less like the Clowns. It seemed like...whatever he found he wasn’t sharing...

“Was he? I guess I’ll have to send him an actual invitation. A letter maybe...? He’d probably love some stupid letter
with one of those wax seals...I could make it all official.”

“Invitation?”

“Yeah. To our wedding!” I beamed, giggling at the openly surprised look on Renji’s face. He looked at Uta and
then back at myself quickly, mouth falling slightly ajar.

“ You're invited of course! There's not really a date set yet...” I nudged the ghoul and laughed as the expression
didn't fade from his face. "Geez, why do you look so surprised, Renji?"

"...it's just hard to believe that he's getting married."


"Before you, you mean? How's 'Kitten' doing? If you want to beat him to marriage you'd better hurry up and
introduce us all to her!"

"No." I laughed aloud when that one topic turned his expression serious once more.

"Right, well I don’t hear you denying you like her! Here, have some blood-wine!" I slid behind the counter and
pulled out a glass, pouring it to the brim and sliding it across to the silver haired (and usually sober) ghoul.

" Relax Renji-kun! No more talking about serious things! It’s absolutely not allowed! We're celebrating! Relaxing!
Having fun! Got it? "  I glanced at Itori and pouted a bit.
She smiled impishly but nodded and turned back to the pool game.

"Alright Aika-chan! But you can't get away from the game just because you and Uta are losing so bad!!!"

"Yeah! Well just you wait—I was just warming up!!! Anyway!” I cupped my hands around my mouth and shouted
as loud as I could: “ 50 Points to whoever pushes Renji into the pool!"

Beside me Renji choked on his drink.



## ♥



I sat on the steps of the pool in the shallow end, giggling as certain silver haired ghoul sat soaking, fully clothed
next to me. His silver hair dripped with the water and he wore a small pout.

“Uta really tackled you there, didn’t he?”

“You put him up to it.”

“Of course!”

“You still lost though!” Itori laughed from across the pool. She had returned to the bar, standing behind it and
trying to pour drinks for everybody. Rolling my eyes I shrugged.


“Yeah...Uta being amazing doesn't make up for my ineptitude at pool volleyball! But seeing Renji being shoved in
was so worth it. You should be more careful though Uta! You shouldn’t tackle people into the shallow end! He could
have hit his head and drowned! I’m fairly certain you’d still die from drowning...”

Imagine that, a Ghoul drowning in 4 feet of water in a swimming pool...

The goth ghoul was currently seated at the bar, though he didn’t drink with his friends. Instead he abstained
despite Itori’s questions. “Really U-kun! We’re celebrating ...don’t you want a drink?”

“...”  I turned and gazed at the two Ghouls near the bar. “Oh...Are you not drinking?”

“I thought I shouldn’t. It might affect your experiment.”

My experiment...

His diet! Right!

“Experiment? What are you talking about...?” Itori raised an eyebrow, looking between us. “Are you
experimenting on Uta?”

“We didn’t mention it before, but Uta’s been eating a sort of...special diet to see if I could come up with an
alternative...?” The smile on my face was sheepish and wary of their opinion.
It was one thing for Uta to approve of trying; but another to see the reaction of other Ghouls.

“We’re able to make organs for human transplant...I was hoping to find out if maybe Ghouls could...you
know...eat that instead?”

“ Uta eating meat substitute...?” She sounded dubious. I knew it was likely far from what they’d come to expect
from their Clown Uta.

“ ...annnnd?” Itori’s eyes were on the goth, looking him up and down. Nico on the other hand was looking at me
closely. “An alternative...so that’s what you're working on. I was curious what you’d be doing with all this...”

“Yes. It’s what I’m doing; apart from inviting my friends over to have a party...? This was what I was hoping to
work on. As for if it’s working, well it’s been over two weeks? The best person to ask would be Uta himself.”

Uta leaned back in his seat, leaning on the bar as Itori leaned across it. She hardly let him get a word in before she
was asking questions:  “Does it work? What is it made of if it’s not Human? How often have you been eating?
What does it taste like? ”

I smiled as Uta stared back at Itori as she bombarded him with questions. Listening in I heard him tell the other
Clowns that it didn’t taste good but it wasn’t that bad. Bland. Tasteless. Vaguely unpleasant. But he also told them

about how he didn’t throw it back up and how he hadn’t felt hungry the whole time. All good things in my book...

Meanwhile Renji said... nothing. I turned my head to see what he thought and I found his eyes focused on me.
“...I’m not sure what you did to convince him to do that. But it must have been pretty serious.”

“...we had a heart to heart. I was quite angry with him when I came back from the Auction...he’s been trying to
make it up to me. Even helping me with this. Even if he doesn't believe in it...I hope that one day things like that
don’t exist. There won’t have to be such...animosity...?” I clenched my fists and then slowly relaxed them, placing
them on my lap.

“...It’s not perfect, but one day it might be...” I said more softly. “I told Touka maybe one day I could figure out
how to make a cake she could eat...I have to live up to that, you know?”

Renji’s mouth twitched into a small smile before he bowed his head, nodding. “Yeah...Try not to disappoint her,
alright?”

“Trying my best.” I leaned closer and cupped a hand around my mouth to whisper: “...you want to try the meat?
The company can’t keep up with feeding more than just Uta for now. But I should really get a second opinion on
it. Make sure he’s not just sparing my feelings!”

Renji chuckled softly and nodded: “Sure Aika...”



## ♥





## Chapter 73:
## Chapter Text

## Chapter 73:


“So?”

I grinned at the silver haired ghoul as we walked down the hallway.
I had pulled him from the others with the promise of dry clothing. There was bound to be something here that he
could wear, the staff wore fairly plain clothing and they wouldn’t miss a shirt and pair of pants.

“Tell me about the lady friend.”

Renji sighed and turned his head to look away from me. He could pretend to be looking at the art all he liked; he
was only avoiding the topic.

“Come on, I’m not asking so I can tell Uta or Itori. I’m really curious. And...concerned about you? I’m allowed to
be concerned, right? You’re friends with her. Aren’t you? But does she know you're a Ghoul? I know it’s been a
while since she met you...so have you told her? Has she figured it out?”

“No. She doesn't know. I’d like to keep it that way.”

“You are being careful not to let her know.” Renji nodded and I ‘hummed’ softly.
I see. “Is it about your safety? Or do you just want her not to know because ‘she’s safer not knowing’?”

Renji glanced my way, looking at me from the side of his eye without saying a word. “I suppose I can see why you
wouldn’t tell her. Since getting involved with Uta everything has felt a bit non-stop. But I still don’t regret it. Plus
you kind of have an advantage Uta doesn't...”

“Advantage...?”

“Ah! So you are interested! Yeah, you’ve got an advantage. How you get food...I won’t lie. It would have been
easier to accept if he ate like you or the other Anteiku Ghouls do. Less...stressful I suppose?”

“...We still hunt if we need to Aika.”

“Maybe. It’s not a perfect solution...but when there’s a choice you make a kinder one. Uta may not make that
same choice; I won’t force him. But I respect that choice regardless. I only meant that it may be easier to accept for
someone else. Do you like her?”


“What sort of question is that...?”

“An honest one! Do you like her? As a person? As a friend? Maybe you like her a bit more than just a friend? Is she
a good person? Do you think she’d be okay with you being a Ghoul? What sort of things do you talk about? Since
I know it’s not your favorite restaurant.”

Renji exhaled and groaned. “You're just as bad as Itori...”

“I’m not...” I pouted and rolled my eyes. “If I were, I'd ask what else you were hiding from them about the raid on
that doctors lab they were talking about earlier. Instead I’m just asking about the girl you’ve been spending time
with.”

“I’m not dumb...” I added defensively when Renji turned from the paintings to stare at me. “But I’m also not
going to be too pushy about it. I won’t ask about whatever you want to hide. So...tell me about the lady friend?
You said before that you met her—” How to word this— “—In a bit of a low spot? How about we start there. Is she
doing better?”

Renji’s eyes searched mine for a moment then he let out a sigh; finally relaxing some tension from his shoulders.

“Mmmm... I think so. She’s more determined now. She thinks the CCG kidnapped and executed her brother.
She’s upset...acting reckless. She’s going to get herself into trouble...I have to be careful in case they are watching
her...”

So he’s worried about her! “Really? Why would they do that? She’s Human, right...?”

“She is. So was her brother. I’ve been trying to find out; ask around...but that’s Itori’s specialty. I don’t want to
involve her. I think he must have had friends who were Ghouls. He might have known or he might not have. But
they're gone in the wind...and investigators aren’t very talkative when I ask them.”

“I can’t imagine they would be...” Not that I felt too bad for investigators. Out of the ones I’d had the misfortune
to meet, most of them had it coming to them.

“Alright, here hold on a second...There should be some spare plain shirts here.” I opened a storage closet door,
walking in and spinning around to look through the supply of shirts and pants in various sizes. “---And some plain
dress pants. Is that okay with you? The staff normally wear them, but there’s plenty of extra and they’re dry at
least. We can hang up your coat to dry in the sun...and shoes. What size are you?”

“Large would be fine...25.5.” (US 8 Mens)

I shuffled around some and pulled together an outfit for him. Handing it to him with a smile I joked: “Don’t ask
for underwear...but at least there’s this. I’ll show you to the restroom if you’d like to get out of those wet clothes.”

“Thank you Aika...”

“No problem. After all, I did put Uta up to push you into the pool. I knew if anybody was going to do it, Uta

would! And then I could get you alone to talk to!”

“You planned on cornering me...?”

Snickering mischievously I winked. “Well, I certainly didn’t plan on winning volleyball against Itori and Nico. Uta
had to make every point...we were losing so bad that even pushing you in we lost.” I smiled coyly and shrugged; I
hoped he wouldn’t think too poorly of me for the trick. “I do want you to try the ‘tofu’ meat if you don’t mind
though...Uta said he can eat it and he says it’s not...as bad as human food at least. He hadn’t thrown any of it up
and he seems alright thus far. But...”

“You’d like a second opinion...”

“Right. Just—keep in mind that I know it probably doesn't taste good. He’s just eating it to make me feel better.
But he’s been really supportive considering he absolutely doesn't actually believe in any of it...”

“Uta is...”

“A pessimist. I can’t call it sulking or brooding; because it’s not. His world view is just nihilistic...? Not that I could
ever blame him for that...”

“And you are an optimist.”

“Me? An optimist...? No.”

Renji raised an eyebrow. “You want to change all of society and don’t think you're being optimistic?”

“I AM being optimistic...but I am not an optimist.” There was a difference. “I try to be. But of course I have my
own doubts. ‘Will this really work? What if people disagree? What if they don’t want change? What if they would
rather keep fighting? Even if I do change things? What happens to the few people who might lay outside that new
society...?’ I can’t help but think I’m being selfish; wanting it to change because it’s what I think would be better.
Some will disagree. There would still be people under a new boot, just like Ghouls are now but I can’t help but
think it would help most people. I think it would be better for the people I care about...so everything else doesn't
matter as much to me.”

No matter what direction society took, it would crush some people under its boot like ants.

“Just think...I doubt the thousands of people working at the CCG will be happy to suddenly lose their career.
Their whole livelihood. The jobs that care and feed their own families? And in a world where people suddenly
begin seeing ghouls as their equals, as people? The CCG will look like monsters and murderers instead of the
Ghouls. I won’t deny that it would be painful for them; but I can’t find it in me to care about that...”

Renji stood by for a moment and then shook his head. “You overthink things, Aika...”

“Maybe...Perhaps I should dive head first into things like Uta! It works pretty well for him! Like when he pushed
you into the pool!”


“Definitely not.” I threw my head back and laughed when the silver haired ghoul stared at me with a truly deadpan
expression.



## ♥



I sat at the dining room table next to Renji. Staring at him as he sat with a plate in front of him and—the three
other Ghouls watching on as well. “Well go on, Ren-kun...”

“Since you're curious, Itori. Do you just want a bite?”

“Ehhh... I don’t know if I’m up for ‘fake Human’ at the moment. I ate recently so...” Itori grimaced a bit and
pulled back. I felt a twinge of disappointment but held my face in a firm mask. It was to be expected. One person’s
denial at the start didn’t mean it would fail. Some people would take some convincing.

“Actually it’s ‘real’. ‘Tofu’ really isn’t the right word for it. It’s 100% Human. 100% Human DNA.  It just never
was a person? It’s grown from stem cells. Which is a type of cell, simply put, that can create many many other
types of cells present in the body. When in a human body stem cells are what’s used to repair different damaged
cells. But science has found a way to make them create—”

I pointed at the ‘food’. “—Things such as that. Tell the cell it needs to make Liver and it does based on the base
DNA that it has. Humanity really likes bending nature to suit itself...even its own nature and the nature of our
cells. Nifty, yeah?”

“Bending nature is...‘niffty’?” Itori chuckled softly and shrugged her shoulders. “Alright...Alright Aika-chan. I’ll
try it. Ren-kun. Cut off a piece for me.”

“And myself as well. Better to help with Aika’s ‘experiment’ right dear!?~ We don’t have to go through all the tests
like Uta did, do we?”

I glanced at the goth ghoul in question and smiled sheepishly. He must have told them about the doctor. It would
be best not to parade the group of Ghouls into his office. He’d probably be weirdly into that. I really didn’t need to see
him get all excited about having so many Ghouls in his office at a time...

“No! You guys taste testing it and confirming that other Ghouls can eat it is enough ‘data’. I appreciate even the
willingness to try it. Once I can confirm that it’s healthy enough for Uta, I have to figure out how to determine
how to make it taste better....”

Renji cut the meat into three pieces and the two other Ghouls picked them up.
“Well...here goes nothing.” They sniffed, albeit less obviously than Uta and opened their mouths; dropping the

‘food’ in.

I looked between them all quickly, Itori, Renji and Nico. Watching for their reaction. Waiting to see if they had
anything to say.

Itori made a face instantly; stopped chewing and swallowed it quickly.
Nico hesitated before eating it much more stoically than I had thought possible.
Renji ate it with an absolute calm mask over his features. He swallowed and stared at the plate in front of him
without making a single face.

Finally, when I almost couldn’t take it Renji spoke up: “This...is not good.”

“Really...you guys don’t need to spare my feelings. As I said, I suspected it might not taste good after Uta had his
first taste. I am asking for your honest reactions.”

“...U-kun! You’ve been eating that!? For how long? It’s—” Itori made a face again and shivered in disgust.

“Uuugh—it’s gross!” I turned my head to Uta, raising a brow. The ghoul looked away, avoiding my eye contact.
He’d been caught. Still, I couldn’t be angry. Despite being lied to it was incredibly sweet of him to try and spare
whatever feelings I might have had about him not liking it.

“...Well. Human food is worse. At least this seems to be alright to eat—” Nico cut off as Renji stood up from the
table and hurried away; getting to the rubbish bin by the door before curling over and retching. Vomiting the
‘fake’ meat back up.

“...at least it was for me. Perhaps not all can stomach it”

“Oh my god, Renji!” I bounced up onto my feet, grabbing a cloth napkin from the table as I went. “Here...I’m so
sorry. Uta didn’t have a problem. I really didn’t expect any with you or the others...”

What would cause a rejection? Was it the taste that bothered him enough to vomit it back up? Couldn’t be, or at least
Itori might have also thrown it up. Or perhaps was a sort of immune response that he was having that the others
didn't to the foo—

“How do you two feel...?” I asked, glancing over my shoulder at Itori and Nico.

“The taste is still in my mouth, bleh!” She was a little ‘green in the gills’ but she wasn’t vomiting. Neither was
Nico. Uta I knew could keep it down and it fed him to the point where he didn’t feel hungry—or at least he said
so.
Perhaps I should double check he actually meant that.
He’d gone two weeks without anything else, so I had to assume that he really wasn’t hungry. He could be reckless
and do some silly things, but I still don’t think he’d risk that.


“It would appear that both Itori and myself are alright. Only Renji had the reaction.”

It would require more testing. On Renji specifically. Perhaps blood samples to find out more about a Ghoul’s
immune system; whatever that looked like. Find out what exactly was causing his body to reject something that the
others allowed...Now isn’t the time for any of that though.

“I am really, really sorry Renji...There’s still blood-wine outside at the pool, right?” I glanced at Itori and smiled
when she nodded. “I’m sure that’ll help you feel better. All of you—cept you!” I pointed at Uta and narrowed my
eyes playfully. “You are going to have to keep dealing with the diet until the end of the month. But Uta...you don’t
have to pretend to like it.”

“I’ve had worse...”

“Liar!” I stuck my tongue out at him and pouted. “You and I are having a talk later about how important it is that
you tell the truth when I ask about these things...”

I stood up from Renji’s side and stepped closer to Uta, still pouting as I leaned into his space.
A couple inches from his face I dropped the pout—his eyes were wide as he glanced in my direction. I gave him a
few more seconds to think I was actually upset before I smiled, pressing my lips to his cheek.



Whispering soft; just for him to hear: “Lying about the taste was unnecessary, but also incredibly sweet of you...Love’
ya, but the truth from now on? I still need a few more weeks of data...Okay?”

“Okay Ai-chan...” The ghouls' semi-startled eyes settled at half-lidded as he smiled fondly.

“Alright, let's get you Ghouls and gals back to the pool. Get you guys something that tastes better?”



## ♥


Later that night I sat at my desk in our now shared room. The light was on, illuminating the corner while Uta lay
in bed with a book in his hand. Once in a while I could feel him looking at me.

I glanced over my shoulder and smiled sheepishly when I caught his eye. “What are you working on, Ai-chan...?”

“I’m trying to think of reasons why Renji couldn’t eat it...My best guess is that he had an immune reaction that
you and the others didn’t have? Are there any humans you come across that you don’t want to eat? Based on
smell...? Or any other sort of sense? Or any human meat ever disagree with you like what happened to Renji?”


The ghoul cocked his head to the side and I could see a small frown on his lips from across the room. “...yes.
## Sometimes. Rarely. Why?”

“One theory I had was that his body rejected it in the same way a human body might reject the wrong type of
donated blood.” I tapped my pencil on my lips as I glared down at the paperwork in front of me. “Perhaps that
rare Human you don’t feel inclined to eat has something that’s not compatible with your body? ...It complicates
things though...”

“How so?”

“If Ghouls have types like that, then it’ll require different sets of DNA ‘food’. Currently most of the stem cells are
of a very similar typing...it makes replicating them easier. More variation makes development harder...it wouldn’t
help if only some Ghouls could eat it, would it?”

More tapping. I furrowed my brows at the problem, glaring at it like it might suddenly back down and fix itself.

“...then there’s the matter of taste. I wonder if—” I trailed off, murmuring to myself quietly more than talking to
Uta. He patiently listened to the rambling without commenting.

“---even if Kazuha can’t get the livers to filter the blood through it, how much actual human blood do you think it
might take to taste good? Humans add things to tofu all the time to make it taste good—or better. So even if we
can’t make it 100% synthetically, taking a portion of donated blood and mixing it in with the synthetic might—”

“Ai-chan...Why don’t you stop for now?”

I rubbed my face. My eyes were tired and they hurt. My body was sore. I was exhausted.
I glanced at the clock and balked. 2 AM. “I’m sorry...is the light bothering you?”

“No. But you are tired. The world won’t end if you sleep...”

“Mmmm...can you guarantee that, what if I’m about to have a stroke of genius and figure it all out!? I might be
missing out...” I joked as I stood up from my office chair, back cracking when I moved. A soft groan escaped me
and I dragged my feet to bed. I allowed my body to fall into the plush bed and laid still.

Warm hands collected me, gathering me all the way up onto the bed. I was limp as he carefully pulled aside
clothing and held me close; nestling his head on the crown of my head.
Just like always...

“Goodnight...mmm. I forgot to ask before—”

“Mmmm?”


“...The Tofu Meat is really feeding you? You really don’t feel hungry...? It’s important...”

There was about thirty seconds of quiet and then the ghoul finally spoke up. “I don’t feel hungry, Ai-chan. Not at
all.”



With a satisfied smile I began to drift off to sleep: That’s good.
I wonder if there’s any side effects he hasn’t mentioned...
....I should ask...





Chapter 74: I bet on losing dogs.
## Notes:
A/N: Ya'll are gonna hate me.
(See the end of the chapter for  more notes.)
## Chapter Text


Chapter 74: I bet on losing dogs.



1 Month Post Auction: Last Days of August




“I’ll be away for at least a few days, Yuto. Kazu will be at your beck and call. So you make sure you bother him day
and night for me!” I grinned and ruffled the kids' hair.

“And if he gives you any trouble at all I got you a special phone. You can send me messages on it and I can send
you messages back. I’ll set up things with Hiroshi and you’ll be learning to hunt and playing in the woods soon!”

Yuto seemed sad that I was leaving for any amount of time.
However, he smiled brightly; overjoyed as I handed him the small smartphone. It was programmed not to call
anybody else, nor would it be able to connect to the internet. I couldn’t risk it.

“Be a good boy, okay?”

The child nodded his head. “...Say hi to Uta, okay?”

“Mmmm? I think you warmed up to him, hum?~”

“No! It’s not like that...”

“Oh it’s not, is it? Don’t worry. I’ll tell him you said hi.”

I waved to Yuto as I left the room, sighing as the door closed behind me. A whole month had come and gone and
now... I was heading home .

To Uta and to the cozy (albeit dark) shop in the middle of the noisy, dangerous, shit-show that was the fourth
ward.  HOME.

“Kazuha, I’m heading to the 20th ward first. I’m going to make sure to invite Yoshimura and the others to my
wedding. Merlin will drop me off there. I can ride the subway back from there...”

“Yes, Madam. Perhaps...you might reconsider letting Merlin take you all the way. Things have been more restless
in the area during the last few months. It would be safer for you if—”

I shook my head and Kazuha stopped short, sighing softly. “Very well. He will drop you off...please be careful,
Madam. Perhaps if your fiance isn’t too busy he can pick you up part way?”

“I’ll tell him to meet me somewhere in the middle...happy?”

The corner of his mouth twitched and he shook his head.
“Thrilled Madam...” I laughed softly as he joked. He was getting better. Maybe he was getting more comfortable
around me?


“Glad you’re so worried about me...now get back to work!~ Company doesn't run itself. Does it?” I turned and
waved with a huge grin on my face, walking from the house with a small bag slung over my shoulder and my
‘umbrella’ held in one hand. I whistled and Bjorn bound out from a bush, shaking off dirt as he trotted by my side.

“Come on, Bear-Bear! We’re going home! I hope you liked our lil’ vacation here!”

I leaned down and brushed off the dirt from his fur with a soft giggle. “I’m sure the gardeners loved you. You
menace!”

He barked and wagged his way to the car, jumping in as soon as I opened a door for him. “Good boy!”

“Thanks Madam! Now where are we heading?”

“Not you!”

“Am I not a good boy? My mother must have lied...” I scoffed and shook my head as Merlin glanced back towards
the passenger mirrored window; a huge grin peaked out from under his stash. “Alright. Tell me where we’re
headed. I shall get you there in at least one piece!”

“No more than one piece would be nice!”

“Right, that is what Kazuha said as well!~”



## ♥



Bjorn sat on the long seat with his head in my lap, my hand slowly stroked his head as I watched out the window.
I smiled fondly as I started seeing familiar landscapes of the 20th ward. The bookstore. The bakery. The music
store down the way from the cafe.
I couldn’t help but notice how quiet the ward seemed. At this time of day normally people were rushing around
after work...

Merlin stopped in front of the cafe. I hopped out and let Bjorn out with me. I looked up at the cafe sign with a
small smile before Merlin rolled down his window. “...Is it quiet today? You sure you don’t want me to give you a
ride to the 4th? I know you said you were okay...but I can’t help but be a bit worried about you kid.”

“I’m alright. I don’t know how long I’ll take here. I’ve gotta catch them up with how everything is going. I left in a
kind of a hurry before. So go home. I’m going to message Uta to come pick me up in a bit. You don’t have to
worry.”


“Alright, alright. I know I can’t compete with your tall, dark and gloomy boyfriend—er...Fiance!”

“He’s not gloomy!” I rolled my eyes and waved as the car pulled away. Looking down I reached and pet Bjorn’s
head. “Alright bud, we got some people to invite to a wedding! Maybe Touka’s in! And Hinami!” I paused at the
door, sending Uta a message that I was quickly inviting Yoshimura and the rest for the wedding, and grabbing a
cup of coffee before I went home.

Excited to see my friends that I’d left nearly a month back I pushed the door open, listening to the soft jingle of the
bell. I paused a step or two in and my smile fell...

“Yoshimura-sama!? Irimi? Kom—”


“Aika-san! What are you doing here?”

I jumped as Koma came out of the storage closet beside me. His face looked stern and worried.
“Oh my god, Koma. You scared the hell out of me! Why are you jumping out of closets...and where is everybody?
Why is it so—” Empty. Everything seemed to be in its place but there weren’t cups out. There weren't any
customers. The chairs were set up as if it were the end of the night even though Anteiku stayed open later than
this.

Hollowed out.

“You shouldn’t be here...” Ouch.

“But...I mean I know I quit kind of suddenly but...”

“No. That’s not what I meant—”

“Ms. Aika...What Koma means to say is that it’s dangerous right now. You need to leave as quickly as possible. Get
out of the 20th ward.” Mr. Yoshimura stepped out from the room behind the counter, he also had a rather stern
frown on his face. “As fast as you can.”

“I...What’s happening?”

“The Doves are coming...”

“The...Doves? Coming here? To the 20th ward? Why? To do what? Can’t we just send them away like always.”

“Here. As in Anteiku. They are not coming for coffee today, Ms. Aika...”

“We all need to leave then...” I knew the moment the words escaped my mouth that they weren’t leaving.

It was hopeless to try and convince them; still I couldn’t help but try. They were my friends! They were important to
me!

“Please...? Ol’ man...you can’t just...I—I was—I was here to invite you all to my wedding!” I felt the beginnings of
tears form behind my eyes; a heaviness in my gut.
They were going to die, weren’t they?

“We could all still leave...I want you at our wedding...”

“That—” Koma started and then smiled so happily it made my heart ache to see it. “Oh man! That’s great! You and
Uta are getting married?”

“Yes...we are. We’re going to have a Ghoul wedding. Whatever that means...I really want you all to be there...so
please?” I turned to face Yoshimura and felt my lip tremble. By my side Bjorn leaned into me and whined. “...you
wouldn’t reject a wedding invitation...would you? That seems really rude...”

“I am sorry. Ms. Aika. I am happy that you and Uta have made up. I wish there was more time for you to tell me
about it. But I must insist you leave immediately...Please.”

“Where is Renji? Where is Touka? Where’s—” I couldn’t lose them all! I just couldn’t.

“They left already...It is just us staying.” Behind the two male Ghouls, Irimi stood on the stairway and smiled
sadly. “You should run along too. Don’t worry we’ll take care of things here.”

I heard and felt my phone beeping. Its notifications were erratic; no doubt there was a worried ghoul at the other
end. Glancing down I saw that I had an incoming call from Renji and a half dozen and counting messages from
Uta. Furthest up and most recent was the message that said:

‘run, the doves are on the way.’

I picked up the phone call from Renji and sniffled. “I’m...” I choked back a soft sob before continuing. “I’m
leaving Anteiku now. I’ll be out of the 20th soon...” I didn’t wait for Renji to reply, in the background I could
hear the engine running from some beat up piece of junk as it skid down the roadway. Likely on its way to get
me...

I dropped my arm down by my side and stared up at Yoshimura through blurry tearfilled eyes.
“Go on. Get outta here! Tell Uta congrats. Never thought that man would get hitched!” Koma still smiled and I
whimpered, reaching for him and tugging him into a hug. “Hey...” I let go quickly from Koma. Irimi met me
halfway. “Take care of yourself...”

I walked to the old man and wrapped my arms around him, squeezing as hard as I could muster.

“...Thank you. For everything...”

I had to go. I had to leave quickly. Or else...

Turning I hurried towards the exit. I pause for just a second, considering not looking back.
I shouldn’t. But—

I turned and forced a smile with tears streaming down my face.

“Hey, you guys! I’m going to make the world better. Whatever it takes...it’ll be better...I promise...And Mr.
Yoshimura. You should know, I did it. The synthetic meat works. Uta ate it for a whole month. So, survive so you can
see for yourself, okay?”

With Bjorn on my heels I ran from the cafe, rushing from the store to cross the street and duck down alleyways
and crossing streets. I could see trucks. Vans. Soldiers gathering on the main streets and slowly marching their way
down to cage the whole area in a field of personnel.
It was to trap the Ghouls here; to kill them inside the net.

I wiped my face with my arm as I ran.
The subway would be down.
The normal roads were impassable.
There must have been an evacuation order given at the last minute. So the Ghouls couldn’t escape. I glanced up
along the alleyways and saw frightened human faces poking out as I ran by. It didn’t give the Humans much time to
prepare either. There were still some trapped inside the dangerous zone.

They wouldn’t show that on TV, would they? They really didn’t care about casualties.
The CCG had their own version of morality.

When I almost ran straight into a barricade of officers I pulled back quickly, panting and catching my breath.
Bjorn growled softly, hair standing on end as he stood protectively at my side.

“Shhh...shhh...come on. Quiet. Quiet...We have to be careful. Careful, Bear-Bear. Sneaky...”

I lifted my phone and messaged Uta:

Aika: ‘Trying to leave. Roads Blocked.’

Then the next message was the cross streets I was closest to.

Aika:   'Taking back streets to try to work my way towards the outside of their boundary...'

Uta: 'Coming to get you'


Aika: No it's to—(Message saved as draft, no signal)

I stared at the 'no signal ' symbol on the screen.
They must have done something to cut off communication.
I pocketed my phone once again and swallowed down my rising terror. I gripped Bjorn's collar and slowly walked
down streets and alleyways with my breath held every moment .

The CCG members seemed to flood the streets like ants. I was forced to turn back a few times to try to find a new
opening in the net. A new hole to wiggle through. Each time I got close, the hole seemed to close, threatening to
catch around my neck like a noose.

Once, as I peeked around the corner I saw what would happen if they found me—The fate for even a Human in
times such as this. Several CCG officers pulled a couple from the street and tossed them into the back of a van as
they cried at the point of weapons. They would no doubt be carted off to some detainment while the CCG
decided if they were guilty of the crime of being a Ghoul.
Knowing a Ghoul.
Or just in the wrong place and wrong time.

With a little other choice I pulled my Wendigo mask from my bag and placed it over my face.
It would be better to fight than be dragged away like that...



## ♥

“You there. Stop for a moment.”

I bolted without bothering to look back or hesitate. There was no world where this ended well.

I could only run as fast as I could and hope that it was enough.
The dog bounding by my side refused to run too far ahead. His huge head turned to look behind us at the man
who was chasing.

I could hear the man's voice call out, telling me to stop, to come back. As though I could trust that everything
would be okay; as though I thought they weren't going to kill me on site.
Or shove me into the back of a van to be questioned later.

Foolishly, I hoped that Uta hadn't made it into the ward. That he wasn't able to look for me. Because it would
mean that he was inside this mess. That he was in danger as well.

"Ghoul spotted. ID: Wendigo. B Rank. I've got her. She's with a dog. No other Ghouls in the area."

“Did you say a Dog?!”

I glanced over my shoulder to see how closely I was being followed. He was a man in a suit. Tall. Stoic face that
stared straight ahead with a dead-eyed stare. So serious...

"Home. Go home!" I shoved Bjorn down a right hand turn that would take him further away before climbing up a
ladder. I glanced down and saw the canine looking up at me, whining and then bolting away from the man who
was following me— He was safe.


He knew ‘home’. He knew where to run...could find it and Uta. If something happened, Uta would take care of him.
I was sure of it.

I kept moving. Up a ladder; leaping off the roof onto another building. Down a set of metal letters to the ground
level and back up again.
Yet no matter how hard I tried I couldn’t seem to shake the investigator off my tail.
As I began to tire, he began to catch up.
Get closer...almost within reach of his Quinque.

"This will be easier if you stop running..."

As if. He could bite my ass...

If only I wasn’t so Human. I wasn’t so weak—
If I hadn’t slacked off for a month I might be in better shape to fight back rather than just RUN!

My heavy legs tripped over one another and I fell; weapon falling from my hand and sliding a few feet from my
outstretched hand.
Fuck— I reached, scrambling for it but felt something curled around my ankle and then lift me.

In a blink of an eye I was thrown like a rag-doll into a solid brick wall and dropped to the ground.

There was a soft tsk sound behind me as the investigator approached. “B ranking is too high for you, isn’t it?
You’re a C at best. Helpless. Did you steal a Quinque because you can’t use your Kagune well? How could you
have ever killed an investigator...? It was your mate who killed them, wasn’t it? No-Face? He’s not here, is he...?”

I turned to face the man, groaning in pain as I flipped onto my back; propped up on my elbows. I winced while I
tried to scoot away from him.
“Go to hell...” I spat.

“...No. You wouldn’t have run so far if he was...or we would have run into him by now if that were the case. You
are alone.” He didn’t sound malicious . Unlike some of the others who made it personal, it was almost clinical how
calmly he was speaking.

I rolled to my feet, feeling my back scream in protest as I started to run again.
Something slammed into my back and threw me back to the ground. “Sorry. I would like to put you out of your
misery before putting you in that prison. But I can't let you go...you’re the perfect bait for him.”

Perfect bait for—Uta?!
## No. Never.
I couldn’t let him do that— Reaching out I tried to grab my sword again; only to feel the investigators Quinque
slap down upon my back again, crushing me to the ground before letting up and swiping me into another wall.
Laying on the alleyway ground I licked my lip and tasted blood and the warmth that dripped down my chin and
pooled in the dirt.

‘ Everything hurts.’

“It will be easier for both of us if you stop struggling...I thought that perhaps Investigator Kaito had been crazy
when he suggested that you were Human. But is that the case?” I heard footsteps come closer and the man loomed
over me, looking down at me as my lips bled from under my mask.


“...I think it is. Isn’t it? How odd ...Perhaps you’ve been brainwashed. I know Investigator Suzuya was quite
affected by his time with the Ghouls he was captured by.  Rehabilitation perhaps would help...I could help you—?
You never have to be hurt by a Ghoul again.” I reached again for my sword, finally grasped the hilt and swung the
umbrella at him. He ducked back and frowned sadly down at me; a pitying expression on his face.

“No? I suppose you are far too gone for help to reach you...the best for you is putting you out of your misery.
Headquarters would like you alive.” He hesitated and seemed to consider calmly as I tried to crawl away.

“However, I think we only need your body for bait. It would be kinder for you.” He swung and the strike hit my
hand, crushing my fingers and ripping a scream out of my lungs and sending my weapon flying.
I lay whimpering, clutching my broken hand to my chest and curling around it protectively.

If only I could heal like the rest of my friends...

I heard a growl first. Raised my head to see a flash of silvery white hair a second later.
## Renji?

The man screamed as something ripped into him. Digging its teeth in deep and yanking its head side to side.

I stared with wide-eyed wonder at Bjorn who held his teeth deep in the investigator's weapon arm; growling and
ripping into flesh.
My Bjorn. Gentle giant. Tall as a man standing on his back legs. A dog who had never actually bitten anybody, let
alone had to fight off someone.
He had only ever been huge.
He now latched onto the man and shook with all his might.

## NO!

“Bear-Bear...Run! Go HOME! Run—” I felt a new sob rip of my throat as Bjorn was struck across the head
with a closed fist.
I tried to stand, falling back to the ground as one of my legs gave out under me. Twisting around I could see it was
wrong—disfigured out of its usual working angle. I could only watch as the investigator's arm was ripped and
pulled apart by the canine's fangs.
The man continued punching, trying to pull his arm from Bjorn's grip.  I heard the whine of pain from Bjorn and
saw the way he jerked back; letting go only when the man struck one of his eyes.

Even hurt, he moved between me and the investigator; hunkering low to the ground and growling loudly with his

teeth bared—and all his hair on end.



“Wendigo!?”

Uta. That was Uta!!!

“HERE!” I yelled back, feeling hope return to me for a fleeting moment. I was here. Uta was coming to get me.
Renji was probably with him...
Or shortly on his heels. He would save me!
He could fight instead of Bjorn and we could all go home—!!!



“What a sad mutt. Its loyalty is wasted...like yours. Can you not see that you waste your loyalty on something that
can’t love you back?”

The investigator's weapon lashed out at Bjorn, cutting him.
Slicing deep. Staining his snow white fur red.
Throwing him back. Next to me. His body landed heavily next to me.
My canine companion lay on the ground next to me, whining in pain but not moving. Panting heavily but too
still. He tried to lift his head and couldn’t.

I swallowed blood, a pulsing sound drowned out almost everything else as I stared at the stained red mess of fur.
Not Bjorn! Not my Bear-Bear! This...wasn’t happening! This wasn’t happening! Please! PLEASE! No. I needed
him! I need him please! No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.

## No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.



“Wendy!!!”

Too late. Help was too late...


I couldn’t answer or reply. Couldn’t call out for my loved ones to find me.
Like loose threads being pulled, the world unraveled.
I felt the anguished scream rip out of me
## .
## ♥


Uta had run from the time they had jumped out of Renji’s car, out of breath and legs hurting.
He was tired .
Weaker than he should be.
He hadn’t wanted to admit it to Aika when she was doing his experiment but he’d noticed it about a week into the
new diet. That fake meat had fed him, filled his stomach but it lacked the nutrition that normally made him so
strong. He hadn’t had the chance to hunt again like he’d planned to, not with the CCG out in force.

He was lucky that Renji-kun had tagged along to help him...
The Raven ghoul was close on his tail as they traveled by foot after they’d passed the CCG barrier of officers.
Behind them the distant radio calls announced No-Face and Raven in the area. But the two Ghouls looked
forward approaching the last place that Aika had told them she was.

“Are you sure this is where she said...It’s so close...” Renji peeked out from around a corner, staring at a CCG post
set up in the center of the street.

“She was here...” Uta could smell her; so she couldn’t have gone far!

As they followed the trail it didn't take a genius to notice that her tracks were leading in a way that seemed to imply
she was fleeing.

“Bear...Run! Run—”
Uta’s head turned, facing the sound of her voice. That was her. He turned in the direction and started sprinting
faster, leaping over building rooftops and getting closer by the second.

“WENDIGO!” He bellowed it as loud as he could. If more officers came he’d kill them. Simple as that. He was
alright with it, and as long as Aika survived she could learn to be okay with it too.

He heard the growling and then the sharp whine of an animal close by and headed for it.

He had nearly reached her.

Just a few more seconds.

Then he could save her, scoop her up and bring her home...finally home. Perhaps he wouldn’t let her leave for at least
a week. Just a few hours out of her manor and away from him, and she was in trouble again...

“Wendy!!!”

A shrill cry made the hair on the back of his neck stand on end and his Kagune bristle under his flesh, ready to
burst from the organ.
He couldn’t control his Kakugan as they spiderwebbed veins out from the center of his irises.

That was the anguished cry of his mate.

He knew that sound.
That all too familiar sound that people made when someone close to them had just died.
Someone had made Aika scream like that; and now he was going to make sure that the one responsible for making her
make that noise was the next one to go.

He jumped from the top of the building and landed on the ground below, Renji by his side when he landed. “Uta,
be careful...”


"Get her somewhere safe... " Uta growled, voice growling lowly in his throat. “I’ve got him...”


His mate was kneeling, bent over her fallen pet. Her head was pressed into stained red fur, nuzzling into him. Her
fingers clutching at the fur in fists and whimpering as sobs shook her body.

She mourned her pet; a creature who had in his last moments protected her from danger that he himself was too
late for. Again.
She was hurt again .
Yet the beast had done the best he could.
Uta had felt neutral towards the dog from the start, but over time he had grown to like that huge canine. It was
difficult not to love a loyal beast.
Moreover, Aika thought of him like a best friend....or family. That made him his as well.

The investigator that had done this stood nearby, turning to look at them both as Uta and Renji approached.

“I see...I was right. She was perfect bait. It is very strange. Have you deluded yourself into thinking you love her? I
can’t see how you could. A Ghoul loving a Human? She is Human, isn’t she? How could something like you love
their food? I thought Investigator Kiyoshi had to be crazy when he mentioned he thought the deer mask was
Human...but then he turned up dead rather quickly after that. Didn’t he?”


The investigators one arm was shredded and bleeding thanks to Bjorn's teeth, but he stood unaffected.  He readied
his weapon and stared at the Ghouls in front of him.  “There are others on their way. It’s good you came, it means
I don’t have to put her in prison to rot. It wouldn’t have been pretty what they’d have done to her. I think this is
much better. Easier. Cleaner . After you're both dead I can put her out of her misery...”

He glanced over his shoulder and looked at Aika, broken and the fight gone out of her as she bent over her dog.

“Assuming that you do somehow ‘love’ her...have you ever considered that it would have been better to have
stayed out of her life? Knowing what sort of life it would mean for her to have a monster like you in it ...? She
could be happily living far from this right now. She’d be happier without you...”

One of Uta’s Kagune tails struck out at the investigator and he dodged and sliced his sword at it. Despite the attack
he kept talking.

“Did that touch a nerve? What sort of daily torment does she endure just to be around you I wonder?”

Dodged again.


“Does she have to swallow down bile each time you eat?”

Ducked and blocked another blow.

“Does she imagine the lives you trample over each time you kill her kind?”

“First Class Investigator’s are resorting to killing dogs, and injuring human women now? How the mighty have
fallen...”

## ♥

I heard talking. That man's cold and clinical voice echoing in a void left in my chest. Shaking, I raised my head
from stained fur and saw the human's back turned to me.  Beyond him, blurred by tears I could see Uta and Renji.
They had their Kagune out and at the ready. Fighting. The investigator wasn’t allowing them to get close...

Too late. They’d gotten here too late.

I pulled Bjorn’s heavy head into my lap and pet his fur, rubbing behind his ears and hoping against hope that he’d
open his eyes. Whine. Whimper...anything. A thousand scenarios played in my head.

What if I’d left him at the mansion? He could be playing in the gardens and bothering the staff.
What if I’d had Merlin bring him all the way to Uta’s? I could have walked back alone—
What if I’d left him with Hinami? He’d be loved and cared for by the small ghoul.
What if...
What if...
What if...

Yet, each time an alternate future played in my head. Each what if ended and I was left staring down at his face.
Eyes closed and jaw slack. Reality came knocking after each delirious wishful thought and crushed my heart under
its boot.

I couldn’t deny the truth in front of me.

If it were not for Bjorn—

I could imagine it. If I’d stayed with my family I’d have learned more about the company. How to control it. Move it.
Make it do as I wanted when I grew up. I’d be taught more. I would learn to fear Ghouls and what I might one day
become. I’d take medicine just like my father to keep it at bay–making my food taste disgusting.

I’d look for a cure with them.
I’d go with them on business trips. Meetings. Travel.
I’d have been in that plane.

I’d have been killed by my own father.
I’d be dead.
## Eaten.

Bjorn was my friend.
My family.
He had saved me. Gave me a reason to leave that old life. Loved unconditionally. Watched my back every single day
to make sure I stayed safe and... I couldn’t save him. Not once...
I’d failed him...

“U..Uta—” I murmured his name softly, voice raw and cracking.  My eyes stared forwards.

“Kill him. Please. Kill him...please...”

## ♥

Uta’s eyes fixed upon Aika as she sat up from her dead friend. Her dead-eyed glassy gaze fixed upon him as she
spoke.

Please kill him.

She was asking him to kill for her; because she couldn’t.
She couldn’t do it and she wanted this person dead. Not that he had planned for anything else. The investigator
had put one foot in the grave the moment Aika had screamed like she had.

## But—
Uta was so used to her begging him not to kill.
‘ Don’t kill him, Uta...’
‘You can’t eat him.’
‘You can’t just eat everyone you don’t like!’

To think, this person had hurt her so deeply that now she was begging him to kill for her.

“I will...I’ll kill him. You stay right there. I’ll come get you in a minute. We’ll go home...”

She nodded her head slowly, eyes on him as he let his Kakuhou push more and more RC cells out of him,
spreading along his back and from his face; taking over to create that ‘horrifying’ venus fly trap that he got his
name for. The RC cells flexed. He could feel the way they wavered; unsteady and unstable. Weaker.

He turned to ‘face’ the investigator regardless.

“Ah...I see why they call you No-Face. What a nasty Kakuja you have...They aren’t very imaginative in naming, are

they?”

Aika’s dead eyed stare was still on him as Uta leapt forward, jaws reaching for the man; arms flexing to grasp or
pound him into the ground. She watched for a minute as the two dueled and then looked back down at the dog
cradled in her lap.

“...rest. You protected me enough...you’re a g-good boy...”

Her voice trembled as she spoke, her hands digging into his fur to pull his collar and dog tags from around his
neck. Aika ignored the fight happening close to her, staying by Bjorn’s side even when the investigator aimed an
attack at her.

Uta stepped in the way, arms swiping away the attack and hunkering down in front of her as a means to protect
her.

“...How odd. The two of you should be studied.”



There were more coming, back up. He could hear them coming and in his current condition...
“No-Face. We need to go...” Renji joined his side but Uta kept facing the investigator. “I have to kill him.”

“No, we have to leave—” Renji turned his gaze on the human woman and hissed softly. The only way Uta would
budge is if she asked for it. “Wendigo. We have to leave...now. Now isn’t the time for this fight...”

The woman’s eyes were still on her pet. Slowly she reached for the dog again, her good hand digging into fur and
unclipping his collar from deep under his thick fur. She clipped it around her own neck and nodded her head
finally. “...we can kill him later...? Remember him?”

“Yeah...I’ll remember.” Uta agreed, taking a step back. His Kakuja’s arms slowly reach for her, giant hands
encompassing her waist, lifting and supporting her broken body.
“...can we take him with us...please?”

Uta eyed the dead dog. It would be dead weight. He wasn’t sure what they’d do with it...
But hearing Ai-chan’s pleas made him reach for the dog's body anyway, scooping him gently and tucking him
under an arm.

Renji covered their retreat with a flash of electricity and Aika laid limply against his back. Held there by his extra
arms.
“Aika...” He said, voice echoing and growling strangely from his Kakuja transformation.

Until they were in the clear he would use it to hold her steady.

“Aika?”

Hmmm. She wasn’t answering. But she was alive; her heart beat loudly enough that he could feel it through her skin.
That was enough for him for now.

## Chapter 75: Silence
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text



## Chapter 75: Silence.

I’d rather feel physical pain over the ache in my heart any day.
All I could do was focus on the way my leg was in agony as we set it at home.
The laceration down my back.
The broken bones in my hands.

The feeling of my busted lip and various cuts of lacerations, they all grounded me at first.
When the mental agony became too much I could escape the thoughts of my dying or dead friends by
purposefully wiggling some broken part of my body.

Uta hadn’t killed that investigator but now they’d know I was Human.
They’d update everyone that “Wendigo” was just an ordinary Human girl.

I was a weakness. A burden and a target on Uta’s back. Something I’d never wanted to be.

Would they come after HYSY next?
Would that be the next place they attacked?
If they could get away with destroying a much loved cafe in the 20th ward, what couldn’t they do?

I wanted to order Kazuha to use all our resources to destroy the CCG. I wanted him to find out that man's name
and crush him in any way I could.
I wanted him to hurt.
And then I wanted him dead...

It hurt to lay on the couch and turn my head to see Bjorn's bed, tucked over by the heating vent he’d loved so
much. But I couldn’t bring myself to ask Uta to move it, or the dog toys strewn over the floor.
I fell asleep several times; each time I woke I woke up in the same nightmare—

One day.

Two days.

Three days...Uta told me at some point that Kazuha had buried Bjorn in the garden at my manor.
Then suddenly it had been a week since the raid on Yoshimura’s cafe.


The ‘Owl Suppression Operation’ as the CCG called it. The owl was Yoshimura—or at least he was one of them.
There was apparently more than one? I wasn’t sure. I wasn’t following the news very closely with so many drugs in
my system.

Kazuha had visited; bringing the strange doctor who gave me some pain meds.



I don't want to be awake. I didn’t want to be conscious of anything.
The meds numbed everything for a while and I eagerly took them.


## Yoshimura.
## Koma.
## Irimi.
## Bjorn.

Somewhere in the fog of it all I remembered a name the TV said; ‘ Koutarou Amon ’. Missing in action.
For some reason even that hurt.

## ♥



Uta tried his best to soothe me. Staying close. Getting anything I might need. He moved me from the couch to the
bed nightly, letting me rest my broken body on the soft bedding. He didn’t complain when I cried late at night. Or
when I refused food that he tried his best to make. He brought his work up from the shop and did it in the living
room when I lay on the couch. He answered the text messages from Yuto, making sure the child wasn’t left alone
for too long.

He brought ice cream, brownies and waffles.
All my usual favorite foods.

Yet it was tasteless to me.
Even the sweetness of junk food was unappealing. Kazu had the doctor check my RC cells again to find them
about the same as before, only risen by a handful of points. It was good news–but not something I could really feel
like celebrating.

“Madam, if you don’t eat or drink more we are going to have to hook you up with an IV.”


I didn’t speak; but I ate. I drank to avoid the IV and needles; swallowing down food and water as only a means to
survive.

“With her in this condition we should move her back to—” I was staring at my food, slowly chewing the tasteless
crap when I heard Kazuha cut off, stepping back as Uta growled.

“ I’m taking care of her.”

“...of course...Sir . ” I barely raised my eyes, a spark of curiosity being one of the first positive emotions in a while.
That was the first time Kazuha had called him Sir . Perhaps it was because I’d announced my marriage to him.
That would make him Sir to the rest of the staff.

“I only meant that the doctor is present there all the time.”

“He can visit here...”

“Yes but— Look at her. She’s losing weight and she’s pale! ”  Kazuha dropped some of his formality to swing a
hand in my direction.  “ She needs more than this—You can’t just let her lay in bed all day! She needs to get out
and get some air. Has she spoken a word since then? She might even need medication more than morphine ...!!!”

“I’ll bring her out.” Uta stood firm, adding: “Seeing some friends will help. I wanted her leg to get better first...”

“Well. There’s good news for you then; her knee was snapped like a twig!!!”

“How is that good news!? ” Kazuha spun to glare at the doctor, but the doc just grinned.

“Let me finish! Kazu! Such a short fuse today, how unlike you!~ The good news is that she’s healing quickly ! Not so
quickly as a Ghoul; Her RC levels are still Human . But since they are so high the effect is significant . It’s been a
week but when I examined the breaks they looked like it’s about 3 weeks into healing. I’d say about a week or
maybe two, and she’ll be up on her feet. Her hand too is healing well. And that lash on her back, all but gone! It’s
truly remarkable ! Ah!~ I can’t help but wish she was at the manor so I could observe her more closely—”

The doctor held up his hands and chuckled. “Of course, she is safer here. With her fiance!~ Isn’t that right, Sir? As
I stated before though...there’s nothing wrong with her throat. She should be able to talk. It’s my professional
opinion that she’s just choosing not to .”


Him too? I couldn’t help but notice the doc was also calling Uta ‘Sir’. I stared blankly forward, lifting a bite of food
to my mouth and eating it. Going through the motions.



Time was hard to track. I couldn’t really judge if I was healing quickly when most of the time I was asleep or
drugged so I couldn’t feel the pain. These moments of lucidity felt like awakening from a waking nightmare...but
even now I still couldn’t figure out how I was feeling.

After reveling in numbness it was hard to be sure what I was feeling when the feelings came back.

“By the way, I got that report you wanted Sir...Normally I’d only do as the Madam requested. However—seeing as
I think she’d approve anything you asked for: Investigator Amon went missing during the last operation. His body
wasn’t recovered but the CCG are announcing him as among the deceased. The body of the ‘Owl’ was also not
recovered...”

Uta took some paperwork from Kazuha; the latter turned his gaze towards me. Meeting my eyes and blinking.
“Hey...Madam?” Kazuha frowned when I didn’t answer. He took a step closer, leaning down to my level on the
couch.

“Aika-san...? How are you feeling...? Merlin and the others are really worried about you. Yuto asks about you
daily...”

I lifted my eyes to stare at Kazu, chewing paused. It was strange hearing him drop the formalities. He almost
sounded like a normal human rather than a robot. I almost felt like teasing him about it.

“What about the name of that investigator?” Uta asked, looking through everything Kazuha had handed him.
Kazuha looked away from me before I could muster the strength to try and speak to him.

“Based on what you told me; Asahi Hayashi. First Class Investigator. No family from the records. He was taken in
by the CCG at a young age. Progressed up the ranks quickly as well. A natural they say according to all his records.
I can’t be requesting too many pieces of information like this without it being noticed . Please keep that in mind.
We are trying to do everything quietly .”

“Yeah. Okay. This was all I needed. Let me know if this guy shows up anywhere looking for her...”

“Of course. I can do that, Sir...”
“If he shows up I’ll kill him...”

“You may have to get in line, Sir...there are a lot of people who would want to have a word with someone who hurt
the Madam.”

Kazuha stood up and sighed, giving me a final glance before waving to the doctor to come along with him. “Let's
go...the less we show up here the safer she is.”

## ♥

Uta sat down at the end of the couch, moving my legs gently and placed them in his lap while he read the
paperwork that Kazuha had brought for him. Flipping sheet after sheet through reports.


It was true that I hadn’t said a word since that night. Not one . I couldn’t find my voice. What could I say? There
were a few times that I opened my mouth and tried to talk but...nothing came out. Everything felt wrong . If I
spoke it would make it all real .


I got many of my questions answered whether I asked or not. Renji was okay. He showed up in the early
morning hours of that first night. He told us he was watching out for Touka to make sure she didn’t run off and
do something reckless. So Touka was okay.

Apparently Nishiki had gone. Left Kimi behind in favor of keeping her safe.
It seemed stupid to me, leaving her behind wouldn’t make her safe, would it?

But then again...
Look at me. I stayed with Uta and I kept getting broken and hurt.

Anteiku was gone.
All that was left were smoldering remains. Wiped off the face of Tokyo, to be forgotten after a few months. Years
from now would anybody remember the sleepy little cafe or the sweet staff that used to serve coffee there?

“...Renji’s been bringing me some small food to hold me over. I’ve gotta eat something more...” Uta announced,
frowning down at a picture on a page I could see was labeled ‘CCG’ on it.

I opened my mouth, almost whispering something but stopping when only a small crackle came out. The ghoul
glanced upwards, eyes fixed upon my face and searching. Perhaps he thought it was a hallucination.

I had to talk at some point. Staying silent hadn’t made things go back to how they used to be. All I could muster
was a sad look and reaching out to grip his sleeve...

Uta’s head cocked, his mouth downturned into a frown. Still not speaking. I glanced at the TV playing the CCG
‘victory march’ all over it. They had a heavy presence everywhere at the moment. Even here in the 4th ward and I
was worried about him.

I can’t lose anymore people.

I could see the recognition in his face as he realized what I was silently saying. “...I’ll ask Renji to come along.
Touka probably needs food as well. We can make sure everybody has food. Then we can all lay low for a bit...I
should tell Itori and Nico as well...”

Relieved a little I loosened my grip on him and nodded.

All my Ghoul friends, the ones that ate peacefully at Anteiku, would now have to hunt. To search for their own
food. Funny how the CCG’s effort to make things peaceful made things worse. More people would die because
of this.


“Alright. I’ll be back.” Uta placed the papers on the table and stood back up, taking my legs off his lap carefully
again. He paused and leaned down; pressing his forehead to mine quickly before walking away...out the apartment
into the shop and beyond.

## ♥

Everything was quiet for a while and I fell asleep, only to be awoken by voices. Uta...Renji...Touka?

Touka sounded upset.
## Loud.

She was probably why I was woken up at all.
I opened my eyes and slowly moved my body, hobbling out of bed and across the room to the apartment door.
They were down stairs. I stared at the stairs going down with anxiety. I made it haphazardly down two before
someone came rushing to help. Without questioning why I was up, or making my way down the stairs while
clinging to the wall; Uta picked me up off my feet and gathered me up in his arms to carry.

“...Ai-chan...There’s ‘food’ down here.” He didn’t bring me down right away, not until I nodded.

Touka I mouthed, air not escaping my mouth as I ‘spoke’.

“Yeah...Touka is here.” He turned and carried me down. I could see Renji drop a white cloth over something in
the middle of the floor but ignored it. Touka turned and faced me, her expression softening slightly as she looked
over me. My leg dangled, wrapped in its tight cast to stop me from bending it.  My right hand was in a brace that
kept my fingers straight.

“Aika...you got hurt...”

“...” I nodded silently, staying in Uta’s arms. “She’s getting better.” Uta said for me.

“Ken’s gone...” She said softly, eyes down to the ground. Her shoulders were tense and shaking slightly.

“Nobody knows where he’s at right now...The CCG got him. They said he’s dead now.”

Her lips trembled and I felt bad for her. She loved that boy, whether either of them admitted it to each other or
not was another issue. But to be torn apart from one another over and over...

It must hurt. I couldn’t imagine...
