“Yoshimura and the others...Anteiku is gone.”

I knew all this. I’d had all week to think of it in my moments of lucidity between sleeping.
I leaned my head against Uta’s chest and glanced at the covered bodies in the shop center. Bodies. As in more than

one. It made sense if it was for more than one Ghoul...still...

“Is....is she okay? Uta? She’s not talking?”

“She hasn’t since last week, right Uta?” Renji looked over me quickly with a frown. I swallowed and tried again.
“...H—hi...T-ouka...”

The hands holding onto me tensed and he shifted me slightly to try and get a better look at my face. “Ai-chan. Do
you want some water...?”

I swallowed again and nodded. My voice felt raw after not using it for so long. Uta placed me down in his seat and
picked up a glass he had by his work station, handing it off to me and crouching down next to me while I sipped it.
“D-did the bo–” I cleared my throat as words cracked or popped in the middle of them. Some syllables I had to
force or they’d taper off to a whisper. “---boys help get you some fo–od? If I have to, I'll y—ell at them to make
sure they s—hare...”

Touka’s eyes were wide and she glanced at the covered bodies and I swore she blushed. “No—I mean yes. Yomo said
I could have some...since...” Since Anteiku was gone.

“—That’s go—od. You should con—cen—trate on s—chool, right? It should be starting again s-soon?”

Touka blinked, staring at me before slowly looking at the ground. “Yeah...it does.”

“M—ake sure you pass all your cl—asses! I’m going to bo—ther you about it!”

“Y-yeah. I’ll try!”

“Need any he—lp buying boo—ks?”

“No...I—” She hesitated and fumbled over some of her words and managed a faint smile. Glancing at Renji I saw
he was staring, a relieved look on his face. I felt better talking to someone...seeing the young lady still alive. Upset,
but alive. Not all of Anteiku was dead. Not everything the old man worked for was gone, was it?

It livened a part of me that wanted to keep going...

“L—et Renji-kun know if you do. I’ll make sure you have everything you need for school...” My voice would get
better slowly. I took another sip of water and coughed a little.

“W-why would you do that!?”

“You know. Kids are the future!” I smiled a bit wider.
It felt strange on my face; cracking my dry lips and making me taste blood.

“You’re not serious!?”


“Of course I am seri—ous Touka. I wouldn’t really jo—ke about buying you books. Anyway, I care about your
Uncle...and I care about you. Is that so hard to beli—eve...? Anyway, I’ll be upstairs while you all divvy up your
meals. Uta-kun...could you maybe...?”

The ghoul nodded, gathering me back up in his arms and turning to carry me up the stairs again.

“Aika...I...I’m glad you're okay...I’m sorry about...” I heard Touka say softly after us; trailing off to avoid
mentioning what really hurt me the most.

“You too, Touka. I’m sure Kaneki will show up somewhere. He’s really strong now, isn’t he?”

“Yeah...he is...”

Uta carried me slowly up the stairs, careful not to bump my leg as he turned us to fit through the doorway at the
top of the stairs. “Do you want to go to the bedroom?”

I nodded my head. Our little ritual when he got ‘food’.

“...Renji helped me find food this time.” Uta said softly as he placed me down on the bed. I hadn’t really asked.
Didn’t need to know. But now he was looking at me expectantly as though waiting to see my reaction to it.
Perhaps I’d say something to him. I smiled weakly and shrugged my way under the blanket to curl.

“Ai-chan...?” He frowned.

“...We—re you guys safe? Did you see any investigators lingering around?”

“We were safe...I’ve got to go help. I’ll put on some music.” He leaned forward, pressed his forehead to mine
quickly again and retreated out of the bedroom. A moment before the door closed I called out, voice cracking.
“Wait—”

The door paused just an inch from closed. “After, do you want to take a bath...it’s difficult with the casts...”

The door peeked open and the ghoul glanced back, a single red and black eye focusing on me through the space. “I
need to eat first...We’ll take a bath right after.”

“Okay...wake me up if I fall asleep...I’m sorry...I’ve been so quiet...”


## ♥

It’s okay. Uta thought as he closed the door to the bedroom.
It was okay that she went silent.


Some people screamed and raged. Some threw themselves recklessly into their work. Or into other passions. Others shut
down.  She wasn’t the first person he’d seen react to something tragic by clamming up and escaping into silence.

As long as she was alive he could wait for her to talk again. As long as she was alive he could keep calling to get her
help. Her people would come and help her to make sure she ate right. Drank water when he couldn’t get her too.

They could check up on his human.
His human, who was healing quite fast for a Human.

He had asked several times for the doctor to recheck her, asking if she should start suppressants. Yet the doctor had
smiled at him and shook his head.

‘You are worried about her! How sweet! No. She’s fine, just as I said before. Don’t be concerned. I told you...she’ll
have some benefits. Just be glad that at the moment it’s working in her favor. Trust me, when she’s better she’ll be
begging for steak!~’

Not an entirely comforting notion—

The fact that she’d been silent had worried him, but the dead-eyed stares had concerned him more. She was in
mourning. She retreated into her own world and mourned her loss. He would let her do what she needed, be there
for her, care for her. Then be there when she comes out of it.

The fact that he accepted her silence didn’t stop him from being relieved now that she was speaking again.

He looked up and saw Renji carrying the two bodies over his shoulder with Touka trailing behind, awkwardly
looking around the apartment and noticing all the human things that Ai-chan had decorated the place with. Uta
dragged out a plastic sheet and put it on the ground for Renji to put the bodies on. Getting blood out of the carpet
was a pain.

“She’s talking again...” Renji commented softly so the human in the other room wouldn’t hear. Renji looked at
him with raised eyebrows, clearly wondering when he was going to mention that.

“...That was the first...I thought she might become quiet like you, Renji-kun. Maybe I’ll contact Tsukiyama...” If
Touka being here got her talking, perhaps that pretentious— he might be able to squeeze some more words out of
her.

Uta moved to the TV, putting on music that would drown out the process of processing the meat. He bent and
pulled the white sheet off the first body and stared down at the Human in front of them. A middle aged man in a
suit, pale face and dark marks under his eyes.

He had chosen to die.


There was something strange about that that Uta couldn’t understand. He could understand the misery of this
life. The grief. The tragedy of it all— but to escape like this? Maybe that’s what madness looked like though; they’d
never know the reason behind it. Just as this Human couldn’t have known that his body would end up feeding Ghouls.

Now the ones who wanted to survive fed on the ones who didn’t . It was kind of poetic?

“Uta. You want that one?”

“Yeah. I’m hungry...I need to eat.” He glanced behind him, looking at the door to his bedroom where his mate lay
in the bed. Likely she only heard the music he played to drown out everything else.
He hoped she never heard anything else.

“I’ll eat the head now...it’s hard to hide in the fridge...unless you want to take it with you, Renji-kun?”

“It’s all yours. Touka. Take what you want from the second one.” Uta watched for a few moments as Touka
stepped closer and kneeling down to the other one's arms, pulling on them until the bones cracked and the muscle
and other tissues ripped.

He turned to his own task of dismantling the human in front of him. Uta grasped the man's head and twisted .
With it in his hands he pulled out one of the eyes and placed it in his mouth; relishing in the fresh taste of real
human meat .

It would take a while to feel normal again. He had to tell Ai-chan about that as well...


## Notes:

She having some sads. :(
Lets all appreciate Uta being a good fiance. :3




Chapter 76: Friendship is healing
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
## Chapter Text

Chapter 76: Friendship is healing



I sat quietly in the chair next to Uta’s desk, leaning on the end of it as I looked over paperwork for my family's
company.
My company. It was looking more and more like mine rather than something that my parents would have had.
However, it was difficult to concentrate on working on anything in the last few days...

A week had passed since the doctor had last visited. Which meant the casts might be able to come off soon. While
the physical pain of my body had worn away to absolutely nothing, once in a while I was crushed and frozen in
place. My heart would pound in my chest as I remembered that people I cared about were gone. Dead. I had felt
different when it was my parents, people I had felt very little for. But now—

My pet, my best friend, is gone .
Anteiku which had become a place of comfort and most of its people were gone .

I regret not spending more time with Bjron. I regret leaving the Cafe when I got upset with Uta. I could have spent
more time with them. Maybe I could have helped head off the attack? Convinced some investigators that nobody
there was a ghoul. Something had to have happened in the last month, right?

Regardless of what I may wish or regret; It was all gone and I had to keep going forward without them.

“Ai-chan...” A hand laid gently on my arm and I blinked, breathing in deeply and putting a hand over my rapidly
beating heart. “Mmm...I’m okay...”

Uta removed his hand and went back to his work, looking at me from the corner of his eye once in a while . After a
minute or two when I’d calmed down he spoke up again:

“I invited Tsukiyama.”


I blinked, looking at Uta with a raised eyebrow. Why?

“....He’s your friend.”

“He...” I hesitated then exhaled. “He is. He’s coming here...?” I glanced around the somewhat messy shop and
thought about how much of a mess upstairs also was; it wasn’t like I could clean or dust in the casts, but
Tsukiyama was very particular about being clean and neat .

“Yeah...He should be here soon.”

I need to get dressed in something else other than lounge clothing! I needed to clean up at least a little bit. I looked
like a crusty mess and Uta invited over my pretentious, uppity snobby friend over—

“Uta! I’m all—” I gestured at myself in general and scowled.

“I told him you weren’t feeling well. He said he’d take you out for coffee.”

“But—” Anteiku was gone.

Not that it was the only coffee shop in Tokyo. He must know of a different one. He had been banned enough to
be forced to go find a new place to drink at.

“—I still need to dress in something different to leave the house...it’s bad enough I’m in the shop with this on.”

Seconds later the door chime rang and in walked the man himself. Burgundy suit today. That was new.

“Ah. Princesse ...It’s good to see you. I heard you weren’t feeling well and rushed right over.”

He was smiling but something was wrong. I did a double take and studied him quickly: The flamboyant ghoul
didn’t seem so.... flamboyant or outgoing. Not so full of energy. He seemed sad . That wasn’t what I’d expected
from him.
Was it because of Anteiku or something else ?

“...Hey Shuu. I must look like a mess. Uta-kun didn’t give me much of a warning that you were going to be
coming....”

“Mmmm. You do look worse for wear, but it can’t be helped. You fragile Humans heal so slowly!~ You must tell
me that he is treating you gently .”


He crossed the shop floor and stood by, looking down at me. Uta barely looked up from his work as Shuu and I
spoke. My fiance seemed, outwardly at least , more relaxed than the last few times around Shuu.

I had to wonder if they’d come to some sort of truce, agreement or understanding since the Auction; perhaps
because of the auction.

“Uta-kun is taking good care of me...I’m healing fast. I—” I paused and glanced away from my childhood friend.
Uta paused his work and looked up. I hadn’t really ever told many people my risk factor of becoming a Ghoul.

“It’s a bit complicated. I’m healing pretty fast though. Nothing to worry about. But besides that I wanted to thank
you for what you did at the Auction...”

“You sent a letter already thanking me mon ami. It was nothing.” He was trying to act so casual about it, but there
was a slight tension in his jaw and he stared pretty darkly at Uta. “It was strange seeing you in such a place
though...Not something I’d have recommended.”

“Shuu...it’s okay. I’ve talked to Uta about all that—I'm not going again if I can help it. But you insulted a Ghoul
chef!” I raised a brow at him, watching how he turned his head to avoid looking at me. His own version of pouting
if I remembered correctly.

“He won’t cook for the Tsukiyamas again...but it’s no great loss. We have plenty of chefs.”

“Mmmm. I see. Did you get the other letter?” Shuu looked back at me with a slightly happier glint back in his eyes.
“I did! A beautiful letter—It’s been some time since I’ve received a letter with the Kaneshiro official seal on it. I
believe the last time was one from your parents, telling my parents to keep me away from their kid.”

“Wait—they sent a letter? ”

“They did!” Shuu laughed heartily. “They thought I was a bad influence! —” He continued to laugh. “What a
ridiculous notion! If anything I had a positive influence over you! After All, it’s not like I dragged you into
anything ghoulish , did I?” Another little stab at Uta . I glanced at Uta but he didn’t even flinch...continuing to sew
together a mask.

No. He hadn’t. Actually, it was impressive how much he avoided all the ghoulish things. He had quite effectively
kept me in the dark about not only himself and his family, but everything.

“No Shuu...you did a very effective job at keeping me in the dark. You were a good friend .”

“ Were ...? I’m offended mon ami!”

“.... Are. You are a good friend. And you are invited to our wedding. Thank you...but...I wouldn’t be a good
friend if I didn’t ask what’s bothering you.”


Shuu opened his mouth like he was about to deny it, but he paused and sagged.

“Kaneki...”
“Eyepatch? You mean—”

“Kaneki is gone... dead they say.”

“You were friends? After—” Shuu had definitely tried to eat the kid. “Uta are friends trying to eat each other part
of a normal Ghoul friendship, or what?”

Uta looked up with wide innocent eyes. His lips twitched a little. “...Sometimes. It’s not so uncommon for friends
to take swipes at each other. Renji and I when we were younger for example.”

I narrowed my eyes at him. “...you better not try anything with me Uta! I’ll bite back!”
“Oh, I hope you do .” Uta said, eyes lighting up a bit. Of course he would say that!

Having a friend here. Joking around a little. I felt better.

“Alright. Well Shuu...can you wait down here? And can I trust that the two of you won’t eat each other? I’ll
change clothing...we can go for some coffee? As long as...” I hesitated and nibbled my bottom lip.

“Shuu, you know that I’m not your pet...”

“...Princesse...” Shuu sighed softly.
“No Shuu...I am your friend . I am your friend or I’m not going to coffee with you.”

“It’s difficult being friends with a Human. It’s—”

“I’m sure it’s difficult for you to realize you actually care about someone you could eat. But Uta could eat me, you
could eat me...any really Human determined enough could try and eat me. But I could do the same to you. It
would be difficult...because you're stronger than me. But—I could certainly try! So that’s no excuse!”

Shuu covered his mouth with his hand as he began to giggle faintly, trying to stifle it. He apparently found my
outburst quite funny. Slowly his expression softened a little:
“Yes...Yes. I suppose that’s true.”

I pushed myself up onto my feet, balancing awkwardly on the cast that held my knee firmly in place. “Anyway, if
it helps. You could think of me as a very weak Ghoul?”

Shuu blinked, clearly confused as he watched me hobble across the shop to the staircase. The cast felt like it was in
the way more than holding me together. I was fairly sure it was healed but had been too nervous to take it off. It
would just be more proof that I was getting very close to not being Human.


With my dulled emotions slowly coming back in full force that sort of reminder was starting to terrify me once
more . There had been more than one nightmare in the last week that had me yelling and gripping onto sheets or
Uta as I woke. In at least one of them I’d dreamed of eating my own corpse; which had been terrifying to say the
least.

“Je suis confus mon ami. What do you mean?”

Honestly if Itori could be trusted with the information, then perhaps Shuu could as well. Between the two of
those Ghouls—Shuu might actually be more trustworthy with information.

“...Can I trust that you keep a bit of information to yourself? That means don’t tell anybody. Even your father...?”

“Of course, mon ami...”

“My family—” I took a couple struggling steps up the stairs, waving Uta away as he started to stand up. “My
family had a bit of a secret. Long story short: My family has a Ghoul relative in it. So there’s a good chance...”
Up another step.
“—That in the very near future.”
Another step.
“—My body will be overrun by RC cells...”
Another step, I grit my teeth together. It was annoying not being able to bend my knee. Or grip things with my
wrapped hand.
“—And I’d be a Ghoul. Unless I start taking suppressants. Which is why I can even get up the stairs now. Since my
knee was ‘snapped like a twig’ as my household doctor would say. Same with my fingers.”

“Mon ami...I never knew...”

“That’s kind of what ‘family secret’ means, Shuu. It’s not like the Kaneshiro’s would have shouted it from the
rooftops: ‘Look, we’ve got ghoul genetics and could possibly turn into Ghouls at any second .’” I laughed ruefully as I
dragged myself up the rest of the stairs.

“Just...wait right there. I’ll be back...”

## ♥

Uta listened until his fiance closed the door to the apartment above and moved away to get herself redressed into
some ‘better’ clothes to go out with Shuu.
He put down his work and eyed the Gourmet.

“...So she’ll be a Ghoul soon? Is that why she’s upset?”

“...No. Her dog died...”


“Oh that mutt—” Shuu stopped short and cleared his throat. “Right. She was rather fond of that animal, wasn’t
she? What was its name? Buck?”

“Bjorn...” Uta replied, listening to make sure Aika wasn’t falling or needing any help. “Also she was friends with
the Ghouls at Anteiku. She’s mourning because they died....she could use friends around her. You care about
her...or was I wrong?” Uta glanced his way, eyeing the Gourmet carefully.

“....Certainly your actions make me think I care more about her than you. How foolish could you be, bringing her
to that place?” The Gourmet hissed softly, sneering. “I would be surprised that she would ever forgive you after
that. But of course you have stumbled your way into finding the kindest, most forgiving woman in all of
Nihon...haven't you?”

“Kind enough to forgive you. She is mine. ” Uta stared at the Gourmet calmly. Staying calm on the outside even
though he was bristling under his skin. “---upset her again and I will eat you.”

“Mmmm. Very like your sort of rabble to threaten like that...”



## ♥

I opened the door to the apartment down to the shop again and sighed. Stairs. My greatest enemy as of late. Down
below the two men paused talking, hearing me coming. Whatever conversation seemed to end and then Uta called
up—

“Ai-chan...need help?”

“No I’m—” But he was already coming up the stairway. I relaxed when he plucked me up, spun me around and
walked back down the stairway to put me gently back on the ground. I’d come to learn that this was just how it was
going to be .

“I could have gotten down on my own...”

“Mmm. Perhaps, but you’d keep Tsukiyama waiting on you...” Uta glanced at the Gourmet and leaned down,
brushing his lips against my cheek lightly before pulling back. “...Don’t stay out too late. Come back if there’s too
many investigators...”

“Are you not coming...?” Uta’s eyes glanced at Shuu quickly and then he shook his head. “No, you’ll be okay with
him.”

“Of course she will. Come mon ami...I know of a fantastic little cafe. Sen Takatsuki sometimes frequents it!
Perhaps we might see her?” I froze at the name, staring forward with a small frown on my face.

“Princesse? Is something wrong...?”


“No...no it’s nothing. Just...Yoshimura liked her books...” I bit the inside of my cheek to keep from crying yet
again. Taking a shaking breath I hobbled towards the door, almost tripping on the cast for the millionth time.

“ Curses ... this god damned thing ...”

“How is your leg?”

“Fine! It’s this damned cast .” I paused and nibbled my bottom lip again. “...We could try taking it off if we get the
doctor to come back and look at it?”

“It’s only been another week...” Uta was looking at me blankly, but his tone had a hint of now familiar worry. He
had been so concerned for me now as my RC cell levels rose. It was nice to see he’d accepted that I was Human; and
wanted to stay that way.

“I know. But it feels fine...I—We can get another RC cell test done as well.” I swallowed nervously and shot Uta a
worried smile. “Just in case?”

“Okay. Do you want to send Kazuha a message..?”

“Since I’m going out, how about you do it? Since they seem to be answering to you, why not push him around a
bit?---Come’on, Shuu. You’ll have to deal with my hobbling...”

## ♥

Sitting down at the cafe table was both a relief to be off my feet and deeply painful. A cafe was a cafe; but that
didn’t make them all equal. This place still smelled like coffee and I knew there were ghouls around us, but it
didn’t have the same warmth.

“Is this where you went when you got banned?”

“It is. They are rather good—though nothing will beat Anteiku.”

I lifted a cup of coffee to my lips and took a sip. Not as good either. They didn't let it pour over the grinds nearly as
slowly as they should. “I think I’ve become a coffee snob...it’s not nearly as good...”

Shuu chuckled softly and took a sip for himself. He looked out the window as he slowly drank his cup.
Finally, after a few minutes he spoke up again. “So you are marrying him?”

“Mmm...I am.” I smiled faintly. The thought brought a real smile to my face. I gently pulled my shirt collar away
from my collar bone just long enough to show Shuu the scar dug into the flesh there. He looked surprised for half
a second before covering it with a smile.

“Well, you're practically already married then...I suppose all that’s left is the party! Do you need a planner?”


“....I—” I thought about it for a few seconds then nodded. The thought of having a planner hadn’t crossed my
mind before, but now that he offered I couldn’t help but think it was the best course of action. Get someone more
attuned with Ghoul culture to organize it.
“Actually yes...I don’t know what goes into that sort of wedding. Having someone help me plan would be
wonderful. Would you, Shuu?”

“Of course! Was there anything in particular you wanted?”

“Can it be done outside of Tokyo? I know a place with a big open field...? At...night?”
The gentleman leaned forward and chuckled. “Day, night. A wedding like this is an all day affair, mon ami! It’s a
rather big celebration! I will let you deal with invitations though, Princesse. Invite whomever you please...When
should we plan it for?”

When? Part of me wanted to push it back, wait what would be a standard engagement period of a year. The other
wanted it done tomorrow. I’d compromise.
“How about six months? It would be spring? I’ll double check with Uta if that’s okay; but does that give you
enough time to plan everything?”

“Six months? That should be enough time—the bead work can be quite complex. But I know some artists—”

“Bead-work?”

“Nothing to worry about, Princesse! You must come to the Tsukiyama residence at some point. Our tailor can
take your measurements while you are there! That can wait for a little while...On another topic Princesse, I hadn’t
realized you’d taken over your family's company until that big television event some months back...that actor you
had was a decent double. I doubt many people would realize it wasn’t you.”

## ♥


We spoke quietly, and made sure the topics were safe for outside ears. Not a word that suggested Ghouls . Shuu
had always been pleasant to talk to. A listening ear who wasn’t afraid to talk about his passions; though the fact
that most of them were food might be disconcerting. I settled on books and literature which had always been
another topic of interest. One that I knew he shared with Ken.

Halfway after discussing a newer book that had come out since the last time we had spoken, the door to the cafe
chimed. I turned in my seat, glancing to spot—

“Hey...is that...?”

“Oh! A treat! That’s Ms. Takatsuki . Didn’t you mention you liked her books?”


“No...I mean yes. I do...” But that wasn’t why I was drawn to go talk to her. I stood up and slowly walked over to
the table where the girl was settling down, hanging a bag off the back of her chair and getting ready to order.
I paused at the edge of her table awkwardly staring at her messy hair and slightly disheveled appearance.

She glanced up, eyes lighting up and smiling at me. “Oh, Hello! Are you a fan...?”

“I—sorry. Yes. I suppose so? I read a few of your books...and the movie adaptation wasn’t terrible...But I wanted
to tell you that someone I knew was more of a fan than me...”
The girl's eyes searched me quickly; I got the feeling I was being quickly studied before she smiled wide.

“Oh? A boyfriend? Is that him over there?”

She nodded at Shuu and I was torn between gagging and almost laughing. “No...god— no. Not him. Although I
think Uta does like your books too...I know this is weird. I don’t mean to interrupt you for long. It was just an old
man I knew. He just died recently. But he collected every single book you wrote...”

“...an old man?”

“Yeah. I’m coming across as strange; It’s just those books seemed important to him. So I thought you should
know. You know, it’s a shame you never visited Ant—” I hesitated and then smiled. “It’s a shame is all...he would
have loved to meet you I think. I apologize for bothering you, Ms. Takatsuki.”

“Hey, wait a second—what was his name?”

I paused and shook my head. “...I am sorry. I can’t say—that’s a secret.”

Turning away I ignored the feeling of eyes on my back and called out to Shuu— it was time to go.



## ♥

When we got back to the shop Uta was joined by the doctor and Kazuha who sat in my seat, arms crossed and
scowling about something. “Kazu, careful...your face might get stuck like that.”

“Madam! Your fiance told us you want your cast off...there is no way that you are healed enough for that to come
off! Your leg was broken . It’s only been two weeks.”

“And I have RC cells running rampant in my body. The leg feels fine. So does my hand.” To demonstrate I kicked
the chair he was sitting in without wincing. “Get out of my seat—the doc has to take this thing off.”

Kazuha stood up quickly, his eyes landing on Shuu and narrowing. “Wait a moment— you are that Ghoul boy that

the Madam ran around with as a child!”

The doctor was already kneeling by my leg holding a little saw. He guaranteed that it wouldn’t cut me when I
made a nervous whine when he brought it close to the cast.

“I am. Shuu Tsukiya—”

“I know who you and your family are. I was tasked with keeping the young madam in the house.”

“You were not very good at your job, were you?” I choked as Shuu spoke up, looking at Kazuha with a small scowl
and a raised eyebrow.
Kazuha blinked and scowled back. “You were a bad influence...not to mention she could have been killed . I am
sure you could understand why we didn’t want her running out into the world—”

“My god , would you two stop...” I sighed as Mr. Chikafuji began sawing into the heavy cast. The pressure on my
leg seemed to let up immediately, letting in fresh air that felt nice .


“Shuu, the cranky one is Kazuha...or Kazu for short. He’s my right hand man. He takes care of my company and
my estate. Kazu—this is Shuu Tsukiyama. He is a friend. Please try and be kinder.”

Kazuha took a breath and nodded, bowing over a hand on his chest. “Of course Madam...I am sorry I allowed any
old feelings interfere. I was merely remembering the 'old days'. The madam was quite a handful, it was easier to
blame someone else...”

“...honestly Shuu was a good influence. Without him I might have ended up dead. So you should be thanking
him...” Kazuha looked unsure but looked at the Gourmet ghoul and scowled.

“A thank you isn’t necessary!~”

The cast on my leg popped off and I stared at the pale skin. Not even a bruise remained...
Slowly I flexed it, feeling—

Nothing. It didn’t hurt.

Before the doctor could stop me I stood. Putting weight on it, I hopped on the limb that should by all rights still be
broken. The doctor was beside himself with amazement, reaching out to press his fingers into the joint and feel
around.

“Amazing! It’s completely healed!!!” The doctor's eyes sparkled with a warped child-like wonder.


“Sit sit!~ Madam, we'll free your fingers and then check your RC Cell level again...Just to be sure. That is, if you
do still want to avoid becoming a Ghoul?”

Sitting I nodded my head, dully staring at the entrapped limb as the doc began to peel away that encasement as
well. Upon being freed I wiggled my fingers and clenched them. Healed like my leg. Just like every other mark that
the investigator had put on me had vanished. Even the cuts hadn’t left a scar in their wake. The Ghoul may be used
to it, but seeing all the evidence disappear was strange.

“Just a little prick, Madam!~” The strange doctor smiled; holding the lancet and waiting for approval. I held out
my newly freed hand and winced when he pricked the skin.

“There we are—just give that a few minutes. In the meantime—This is yet another Ghoul friend?! How
interesting—Isn’t the Tsukiyama family rather well known? Very wealthy if I recall...”

Shuu glanced at the doctor and then myself. “This is—”

“Chikafuji! Resident doctor to the Kaneshiro’s—a pleasure.”

“You are a Human doctor, yet you seem happy to work with Ghouls?”

“Oh, yes! Quite happy! You are a fascinating lot, don’t you agree? Before I forget, Sir—” The doctor turned his
gaze to Uta and smiled wider. “You sent me your final measurements for weight. You are aware you lost weight,
aren’t you? Approximately ten pounds from the start of the Madam’s experiment to the end. Perhaps if you don’t
mind we could discuss how you are feeling? I can wait until you don’t have guests!~”

I looked up from my flexing hand and stared at Uta. Ten pounds? Wasn’t that kind of a lot...? He didn’t have much
‘fat’ to lose. So had he lost muscle?

The ghoul glanced at me quickly then back at the doctor. “...Yeah. You can wait upstairs. I’ll close up for the
night.”

“Well, I think that’s my sign to leave—Princesse! I will be in contact! We shall have to get you both measured!
Bonne nuit!” Shuu showed himself out, allowing me the peace of mind to stare at Uta.
He avoided my looks as he stacked some things to the side and turned off the light above his desk.

“Ai-chan...can you lock the door?”

I could put aside my supposition for the moment and help close up.
Still amazed that I could do it, I crossed the room. I marveled at how normal I felt. My leg was strong without any
wobble or pain and my hand gripped and turned the lock without any discomfort.

Kazu was watching carefully, a frown evident on his face as he watched me.

“Madam, how are you feeling...?” He glanced down at my ‘broken’ leg before looking back up. “I apologize...My
tone before was unprofessional—”

“Forget it, Kazu! It’s nice to see you be Human...rather than a robot. You had me fooled for a little while. Now
that I know you truly are Human I might consider giving you breaks!~”

The man scoffed and I chuckled shortly before glancing at Uta again.
“So...did you have something to tell us?”


## ♥

Uta waited until we saw my results on the RC cell test were the same and everyone was in the apartment.

He sat down on the couch and relaxed. His eyes were on me when he spoke up. “....Eating that food is possible.
But it’s not very good. It tastes bad. It also weakened me.”

“It...weakened you?” Wait—

“Mmmm. I didn’t feel hungry all month. Ghouls could survive on it like you’d like. However, they’d always be
weaker and slower than the ones that eat ‘real’ meat.”

So that day he had been weakened...? I stopped that thought and shook my head. No, I didn’t want to think about
it. I couldn’t deal with thinking about that.

“In the perfect world it wouldn’t matter if you can fight—because you wouldn’t need to. But right now it could
get Ghouls killed if they’re trying to eat it for an extended time. Are you feeling okay now? You’re eating normally
again...”

I caught Kazuha’s grimace but ignored it. “---so are you feeling better?”

“It's taking more food than I expected to start to feel normal again. I am hungry...”

“I see! So it keeps you filled but may be missing some nutrition!” The doctor piped up, scribbling notes down on a
pad of paper. “Tell me, do you hunt? How often do you eat? Do you eat more than one Human a month...? Or
less? Are you hungrier now after the experiment? Do you think eating more meat would help you return to your
normal equilibrium sooner?”

I glanced at the doctor and the Uta. When Uta gave me a glance I shrugged. The doctor was strange, him and his
strange questions. He had absolutely no survival instincts, or he really trusted Uta wouldn’t eat him.

After Kazuha and the doctor left I crawled onto the couch, curling beside Uta and snuggling up close. “How long

were you feeling like that...?”

“Since about a week in...it didn’t get worse so I thought it was okay. I hadn’t expected to have to fight so soon. I am
sorry, Ai-chan...”


“It’s okay. I’ll figure out a way to fix the meat so it will work. For everybody. In a perfect world it wouldn’t
matter...but we don’t live in a perfect world. So I have to make it better...” I knew he wasn’t apologizing for the
meat being bad, he was sorry Bjorn had died. I bit sharply on the inside of my cheek to try and fight back tears
again—

It was my fault. Not his. It wasn’t his idea to feed him—my love and my protector fake meat for a month. I hadn’t
once thought it would cause such a bad reaction.

“Don’t worry—just eat your normal food. Extra if you have to. Whatever it takes. Just try and feel better. I’ve got a
trip to take next week...Kazuha, Merlin and I are going to the labs where they made the meat. I haven't been there
in years so I’m taking a tour to see how things are running. One more step—”

I leaned forward and pressed my lips gently to Uta’s. He kissed back so softly and nodded his head. “I might have to
hunt again. I almost finished the ones from last week...”

I wouldn’t comment that meant he’d eaten a whole person in a week; I only nodded and snuggled closer to soak up
some warmth.
“Okay...we saw Sen Takatsuki when we went to the cafe.”



## Notes:

Friendship is healing (and we're healing friendships!) Aika doing a bit better; starting to feel
normal but with moments of **PAIN**. As grief is.
We all know Shuu can plan a banger ghoul wedding!~
Also lets not forget that he gets pretty upset when Ken goes missing. Aika isn't the only one
who's upset---everyone for different reasons.
Also I can't stop listening to the EPIC: Troy Saga and EPIC: CYCLOPS Saga musical tracks.
"You killed my sheep, my favorite sheep. What gives you the right to deal a pain so deep? Don't

you know that pain you sow is pain you reap?"
Gives me chills each time I hear it. :3




## Chapter 77:   Lab Visit
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 77:  Lab Visit

My phone woke me up early in the morning of the lab tour. It buzzed and shook on the side table until I struggled from Uta’s arms
enough to reach it. The ghoul pulled me back and growled softly; holding me close. “It’s too early...”

“It’s four am...I told you I’m going to be there by eight. I need to start getting around early. The lab is a bit further away and I want to get
an overview of everything before we walk through. Please Uta—I need to get a shower and some food.”

My stomach growled ferociously and I smiled sheepishly as Uta raised his head, giving me a stare. “You still want meat...”

“...Bacon or sausage sounds so good right now...I know I should eat something else...” My mouth watered and I felt my face fluster and
Uta continued to stare. “...The doctor said I might crave meat more...we’ve been testing every couple days. It’s not going up. I think the
side-effects are finally catching up to me though. The healing...the craving for steak.”

Mmmm. Steak might be nice for dinner.

“Come on Uta...let me up. Or maybe I’ll just—” I opened my mouth and bit him; lightly nibbling and gnawing on a part of his arm that I
could turn my head to nip at. The ghoul chuckled softly and finally relented after being bitten and ‘chewed’ on for a few seconds.

I wiggled out of bed, leaning back over the edge to kiss his cheek quickly before darting off to the bathroom to start getting ready for the
day. I got my shower quickly, shot Kazuha some messages confirming that I’d be ready soon and started a pot of coffee. When it came
time for breakfast I pulled out a pack of bacon and sausages and stared at the unused loaf of bread on the counter.

I forwent the bread: standing over the frying pan of meat—
While I stared down at it I felt an edge of panic starting to well up. I watched the grease bubble and pop. It looked delicious...
Not that bacon hadn’t before, but the cravings were more intense than normal want for bacon.

I was pushing it off though because I enjoyed my food. Because healing quickly on its own didn’t seem like such a bad thing. I wanted to
stay the same. But now there wasn’t a world where that could happen. Either I accepted being a ghoul and changed my diet. Or I accepted
the suppressants and my diet would taste terrible regardless of what I ate.

There was no more option to stay the same.

It might have been Roma’s fault, or maybe she just sped up something that would have happened eventually. It wasn’t like I’d been being
very careful about how much I was biting Uta.
Had licking his Kagune been a well thought out idea? No.
Should I have been more careful about some of our intimacy that might spread RC cells from him to myself? Of course.

But I’d blame that piece of human meat.
I’d blame Roma.

I took the heaping pile of meat out of the pan and onto my plate so I could bring it to the couch to eat it. As I took a bite I smiled and
moaned softly— So good. I ate quickly, shoveling the last few pieces into my mouth as Uta emerged from the bedroom. He was shirtless,
rubbing his eyes and looking around sleepily.

“There’s coffee in the pot...you look like you need it.”

“It’s early...” Uta almost never whined, but he did groan and complain once in a while. This time I couldn’t blame him, it was very early
for both of us. Especially with me staying up late to work on some paperwork that Kazuha had wanted to have done.


“I’ll make it up to you later. When we get home we can go...straight to bed.”

The ghoul blinked and smiled softly. “Mmmm. That’s not going to help me get more sleep.”

I laughed softly as he went to the kitchen. “Well that sounds like that might end up being your own fault. Try some coffee...it’ll help. I’ll
be back before you know it. It’s just a tour. I should be back by noon. I actually need to go grocery shopping, you can go with me. Since
you enjoy it—such a strange ghoul!~”

Uta poured himself some coffee, glancing over his shoulder. “Are you out of food?”

“Close to it....” Uta’s eyes landed on the unopened bread on the counter but he didn’t comment. He took out a container of his own
meat and began eating it, cold, with his back turned to me.

Sipping my coffee I stared at his back for a minute before speaking up. “Uta-kun...You know you can sit and eat. I know you're not going
to force me to eat it like someone. You eating it doesn't bother me...”

Uta paused and looked over his shoulder, swallowing down a large mouthful. “With how much meat you’ve been eating lately, you might
steal it.”

I scoffed loudly, recognizing the joke for what it was. Innocent.Teasing. Perhaps under the joke he was actually concerned. “I wouldn’t eat
that if it were the last thing on the planet. I am pretty sure you're eating their....spleen right now...? It’s been in the fridge for how long...?”

“Only a couple days...are you a picky-eater? I suppose Tsukiyama and you have something in common—”

“How dare you!~” I laughed aloud in mock offense.
Joking made the terrible and tragic things a little easier to deal with sometimes.



“When are you going to start taking the suppressants...?”

My smile fell a bit. The ghoul had leaned up and picked the pill bottle off the top shelf where I’d tossed them right after I’d been given
them. I hadn’t touched them since then. He turned the bottle about, sending the pills clattering from side to side in the case. I picked
myself up off the couch, walked past him and put the dish in the sink.

“...I was thinking about the end of the month. So...about a week from now? A week and a half? I’ll get a ton of ice cream, bacon and
donuts and—a bunch of stuff I like. We can have a movie night with some popcorn—” Once I started taking them, food would never
taste the same again. Might as well eat everything I liked first.

“---After that I guess I could see if the cooks remember anything that my father actually liked. I think Ms. Sato mentioned something
lemon flavored? Because it’s already kinda bitter...? So maybe I’ll grab some lemon cakes. Lemon candies?”

Uta nodded and then tilted his head, listening for a moment. “Someone’s at the door...”

“Probably Kazuha. I’ll go let him inside. The alley street isn’t exactly the safest place for a Human at this time of day...or night.” I turned
and hurried off, slipping on shoes to shuffle down the stairs and to the door. I left the chain lock on while I checked; but as soon as I saw
Kazuha’s slightly nervous figure standing by the door I popped it open.

“Hey. Come on, wait inside. I’ll be ready in a few minutes.”

He took a step inside and looked around, eyes scanning the masks. I closed the door behind him and followed his gaze. “You know, I
could get Uta to make you a mask I bet.”


“Why would I need a mask...? I thought it was my job to be front and center?”

“It is...but that doesn't mean you can’t look at them and decide you might want one. After all, all this is just because I bought a mask on a
whim. I wanted one...I didn't have a use for it until later.” I shrugged and looked at one of them that looked fairly simple, carved in wood.
One of Uta’s simpler masks, one that tried to imitate a blank human face.

“...Maybe I’ll see if any of the other staff want some masks too. I’ll have to ask the next time I stop by. Where’s Merlin? In the car still?”

Kazuha nodded his head: “Yes Madam. Do you intend on taking very long?”

“No, just a few minutes. I want to brush my teeth and do something with my hair. Then I’ll be ready.”

The man nodded again, folding his hands behind his back and stood by the case of masks. I smiled faintly and retreated quickly back up
to finish getting around.


## ♥


The car ride out to the labs was long. It was quite a bit further away from either home than I’d expected and took us through several areas
of high traffic which slowed us down quite a lot. I sighed, palm pressed up against my face as I stared out the window.

“So...this lab. What exactly haven't you told me about it...”

It wasn’t so much a question as a statement. I knew he’d kept things from me. Kazuha pursed his lips and scowled. “...there’s things there
I don’t think you’d like. I have put a pause on them until they get your approval though.”

“Things like what?”

“Things that I am sure will be uncomfortable to hear. I ask that you—”

“Ghoul things.” Merlin helpfully interrupted. “All sorts of ghoul genetics. Samples. Bit ‘an pieces. Gotten from the CCG over the years.
For a while they traded some things back and forth. Repressing drugs made by your company—research materials from the CCG. Not
to mention the live subjects—”

Research material. Live subjects?! Bile rose up in my throat and my teeth hurt as I clenched them tight; hissing through them. “Excuse me,
what did you just say?”

“Live subjects...well. Alive might be a bit o’ a stretch. Pretty much brain dead fell’ers.”

Kazuha’s brow twitched as he stared at the back of the older driver's head. “Would you like to explain everything, or perhaps you might
allow me to?”

“You're slow and ya’ don’t get to the point. Ya’ know what’s gonna bother her. Might s’well just come out and say it. An’t gonna make
her like it anymore...”

“Whatever the ‘live’ subjects are, you are going to stop that. Whatever is being done to them—is stopped.”

“Of course Madam. As I mentioned, I already had them halt those programs. The subjects in question are simply under medical care at

this point to keep them alive. You may wish for them to be removed from this care, however I will remind you that they will never wake
up and the care they are hooked up to is integral to them staying ‘alive’. By the time we got them they were brain-dead beyond the point
that even they could repair. I can not say what the CCG might have done to them beforehand. Your father did not hold the same concern
for them as you...”

“What...did you—what did the company do with them when they were on life support? Surely you didn’t piece them apart and use them
for experiments...?”

Kazuha frowned and looked away, eyes on the road ahead of us.
“...I did not. I did as your parents bid. Nothing less, nothing more.”

“That would have been your father lil’ lady...we might have respected him ‘cause he helped us. But that doesn't mean we always agree that
what he’d done was what you might consider: Humane. It's been a long time coming that you take a look at this place. You can decide
better once you know what you’ve got to work with. Right kiddo?”

I seethed, hating my parents for what they’d done; but nodded my head regardless. Right. It wasn’t Kazu’s fault. It wasn’t Merlin’s
either. They’d just done their jobs. That might have been one advantage of hiring people with sordid pasts; they’d do what they were told
no matter what it was. As long as they were kept out of the trouble they’d struggled to escape before.
At least I know. Knowing was one step closer to fixing it.

It might be less cruel to allow the ‘subjects’ to die.
Or maybe if they were kept in medical care for long enough they might start to regenerate...? I wasn’t the best judge on what a ghoul could
or couldn’t heal from. Despite what Kazu said they might one day wake up, return to some sort of life. I’d have to ask Uta or one of the
others...

The car pulled into a gate and then pulled down an underground tunnel, following LED lights and passing security checkpoints. They
saw Merlin’s car, the emblem on the front, and we were allowed to go through with no questions asked.

“Here we are...Madam. I urge you to keep your emotional reactions under control. These people are not like the ones from the manor
staff.”

I nodded my head. They couldn’t be expected to be as loyal. Not all of them were bound to agree with my idea of what was humane to do
to unconscious or even braindead ghouls. They probably didn’t even see it as an issue to be ‘humane’ about.

I had to be careful.

“We’re just here so I can see and learn about the place. I’m not marching in to change anything right away.” Kazuha’s face relaxed as I
appeased one of his fears he had evidently had. “If there’s anything I need done after, I’ll let you know...but I can already tell you,
something is going to be done about those ‘live’ test subjects.”

Kazuha inclined his head and then stepped out of the car, walking around quickly to open my door for me. I stepped out and looked
around as guards turned their eyes on me, staring. I made sure to walk with Kazuha and Merlin; the two of them flanked me as we
traveled.

## ♥


There were hours of lab to walk though. People to meet. They ranged from self ‘Important’ scientists who seemed determined to speak
down to me like I was just a little girl who was here for fun or a science project. The other half was made up of nervous but eager people
in lab coats. I grinned and bore it; but internally I wondered how many of them were really necessary.

Most of it looked like a fairly normal run of the mill lab. It wasn’t until we got to the deeper levels where we started having to scan a
keycard and have Kazuha’s eye scanned that things started to seem suspicious. Finally, I stood in front of a large glass panel and stared at

the bodies of two patients on the tables. They were hooked up to heart monitors, tubes ran down their throats, and IV’s seemed to be
feeding them a concoction or drugs or perhaps food. Aside from the medical apparatuses attached to them they were held down by a series
of straps; around their arms and legs and across their torso and foreheads.

“If they’re not conscious why are they strapped down...?”

“It’s a precaution. I can remove it if you’d like, however the workers might object to being near them in that condition.”

Even if the treatment is unfair, If they ever do wake up the last thing I want is for them to rampage through here. It wouldn't help
anyone; least of all them. “No...leave the restraints. Do you know their names?”

“Names...? No. I don’t believe we have names for them. They have been here for over ten years. The one on the left has been here for
twelve. I remember seeing them when I was younger after your father picked me up...we were never to speak of the things we saw down
here.”

I glanced at Kazuha’s face and saw his eyes were downcast, expression almost regretful. “You don’t like this anymore than me...do you?” I
asked softly, tilting my head at the patients in front of us. “All this bothers you...”

“I didn’t want him to throw me away...if I wasn’t good enough I thought I’d have to go back. I preferred it when my job was just keeping
you from running away into the city. At least I could justify it as keeping someone safe. You didn’t even know about the Ghouls...”

He cleared his throat and waved a hand towards a different hallway. “Down here there are samples. There’s a lot of staff that work down
here. Most of them are paper pushers and data analysts. They watch the little ticks and numbers that make up every new piece of
information this facility learns...”

I barely paid any mind to the people we passed in the hallways, listening to Kazuha or Merlin as they gave me new information here or
there. I looked on in fascination as they showed me the beginnings of cell division for a new organ being grown; all the while I wondered
how I might use it to help—

“Oi—the fuck you think you’re doing?”

That sentence was the first thing that told me that somethingwas going horribly wrong.

The second indication was that Merlin’s hand pulled from his pockets and he side stepped quickly forward, wrapping an arm around me
and shoving me backwards to the ground behind Kazuha who also stepped between me and whatever was happening.

I flinched at the sound of breaking glass and the stinging sensation of something burning my eyes. I blinked rapidly as tears gathered to rid
the irritant. Wincing through the pain and the tears I looked ahead. Squinting, I could see what looked a bit like a red mist in the air
before it quickly settled.

“Get back Madam—”

Merlin was coughing harshly after having charged forward despite his older age and tackled the culprit to the ground, pinning him face
down with his cheek pressed into the ground. “What the hell’ you think you’re doing Lad? You have any idea—”

“That bitch destroyed my life’s work! We were so close to making a weapon for them! They would have paid us all—We would have been
set!!! We could have finally gotten a leg up on those monsters! She ruined it! She ruined everything!”

I coughed and rubbed my eyes and Kazuha turned from the scene in front of us to face me; hovering and checking me over with a
worried expression.
“...Are you alright? Did the glass cut you at all?” I couldn’t help but notice the drop of ‘madam’ in favor of frantically checking if I was
okay. Things must be bad...


“Yeah...fine. What was that? What happened?”

“I...I don’t know. It seems that that young man threw a sample at us—or you.  We should get checked...” He looked up and down the
halls, clearly now much more on guard by the unexpected hostility in a place he thought had been safe.
“I think it’s best if we go back to the manor and have Chikafuji look over you. I don’t think I trust the doctors here.” He spoke more
quietly, leaning down to grip my arms. He pulled me up, helping to put me back on my feet.

“Security. Escort this man to holding. We will be leaving immediately. After we’ve found out what sort of substance that is I will deal
with him myself and decide if any charges should be held against him.” Kazuha gripped my shoulder, steering me away. Behind us Merlin
stood and left the attacker to the security guards who dragged him away—still screaming after us.

Merlin followed Kazuha and me—coughing as he walked.


## ♥


I felt fine, but I kept glancing at Merlin as he coughed. It was getting worse, wasn’t it? We made it back to my manor and I jumped out of
the car, rushing for the door.
“I’m getting the doctor. Merlin—you're not looking too good.” His face was a little red, perhaps from all the coughing— but what if it
was something else?

Behind me I heard complaints that I should be looked at first.
“Age before beauty, Merlin!” The reply was a laugh that ended in a harsh cough.

Hurtling down the hallways, I yelled for the doctor. His head popped out from a doorway and I jumped in surprise. “ Oh my, I thought I
heard someone screaming for me. I hadn’t expected the lady of the house. Weren't you and Kazuha going to be going to the labs? I really
wish I could have joined you. Oh, but were you looking for me?~”

“Quick...something happened. Merlin’s coughing a lot—some weird experiments at the labs. The glass shattered—I—” I stumbled over
my words as I did a very poor job of explaining. He did listen though, grasping that something was wrong and someone needed some sort
of medical care.
“Madam, calm yourself and bring him to my office. I shall be along in just a minute.”

I nodded, feeling frantic as I ran back down the hallways, following the sound of coughing as Kazuha led the older man towards the
doctors office. “He’ll be in the office in a few minutes...Are you feeling alright, Kazuha?”

“I am feeling fine. It seems like he took the brunt of whatever was in that capsule.” Kazuha furrowed his brows. “I’d like to find out what
it was though...do you want him charged with assault?”

“ Yes . What kind of question is that? He attacked us! He might have hurt Merlin! Of course I want him charged with assault!”

“Don’t worry ‘bout me kiddo. Probably just irritated the smoker's lungs. I told ya’, I’ve been smoking those things for years now...it acts
up a bit once in a while. It’s a bad habit. Don’t try it lil’ lady!” Even ill Merlin smiled and joked before he went into another round of
terrible coughing.

Chikafuji walked through the door and eyed Kazuha and then Merlin and then myself. “Well...all three of you here now. Perhaps Kazu-
san could explain what happened—I’m afraid the madam was quite tongue tied!~”

As Kazuha explained to the doctor I scooted closer to Merlin and watched him closely as he coughed and hacked. Despite his reassurances
I still worried . What sort of sample or drug had that man possibly have thrown at him? It could be anything. A poison? What if it causes

cancer? Or a lung disease? Even if it only gave him pneumonia, that could be deadly. Especially in someone who already had lung issues!

“That was crazy—tackling that guy like that. What if he’d had a weapon?! ”

“Worth it to keep you safe lil’ lady. It’s the least I could do...” Merlin smiled faintly and tried to clear his throat. “I participated in many of
the things I knew weren’t right...it’s good ta’ see them undone...the kid feels the same.”

“...Don’t worry about any of that. We’ll get you checked and you’ll get better. You're not dying of any lung cancer either. So you are
getting regular checks for that from now on. I’m almost debating demanding you don’t get those cigars anymore either!” He’d have the
best medical care possible; but that didn’t make him or anybody else immortal!

“Quit looking at me like that. It’s making me nervous! And don’t you take my cigars! I would be real cross with you.” Merlin chuckled —
and coughed. “Hey Doc, why don’t you look over the Madam first. Make sure she’s feeling alright. Then she can go back home safe and
sound with her gentle-lad. Pretty sure they had a date to go on later...”

“It’s grocery shopping, not a date?!”

“A ghoul going grocery shopping with you voluntarily. Surrounded by food they can't eat and they think is gross. Just to spend time with
you and ask you inane questions about the food. Sounds like a date ta’ me."

“I also agree with Merlin—”

“That it’s a date?”

“What—NO...” Kazuha pinched the bridge of his nose. “I agree that you should be a priority. We can get checked after. Besides I'm sure
that the sir is hoping to have you home soon."

I looked between them, seeing that they were not going to relent, I sighed and nodded.

"Fine...Make it fast, I feel fine . A little shaking up, definitely wide away...but good. " All things considered at least.

After a few tests, checks on my vitals and many many questions...I was free to go. More than simply free ; Merlin waved me off, urging me
to go home and not worry so much about an old man. Kazuha was a little more worried about long-term effects. But seeing as he didn't
seem to be feeling anything I've been further back—he was inclined to send me away.

"I'll bring you home myself...If we keep you too long your ghoul may come after us to take you back. I’d like to avoid explaining in person
that you were attacked. Again ..."

## ♥

Kazuha dropped me off near the shop. I only paused momentarily outside to take a deep breath in and collect myself. I was
shaken....though I had tried to hide it for the most part from my staff.


Based on what that man had said after he had thrown that—whatever it was —at us: he blamed me. I had done something, or given an
order that had caused him to blame me. It had ruined his ‘lifes work’. Something that could have hurt ghouls. Not that I was unhappy by
that notion. If anything I was glad that it had stopped something like a weapon—

But it was more proof towards what I already knew. Some people would be upset. Some people wouldn’t flex and bend with the world,
they’d break. They’d snap and they’d attack anyone they thought was to blame. This was the second time someone had attacked me
specifically because I favored helping the ghouls over killing them...



Now it has happened again. Only this time someone actually might have gotten hurt. I looked down at my phone; worried about Merlin.
They had my phone number and Kazuha had his orders to call me whenever they found out what was wrong.

Maybe it was just a smoker's lung...

I entered the shop and spotted Uta immediately, bent over his work.  He looked up and something on my face must have told him
something went askew . The ghoul put down his work and turned his chair, waiting for me to tell him what had happened.

He didn't need to ask , I simply dropped my body into my normal chair, rolled it closer and began to tell him...


## ♥


Kazuha called some time later saying that he was back at the manor, keeping an eye on the older driver and would keep giving me updates.
I raised my head and stared at the message solemnly. Still no answers?

“Ready to go to the grocery store, Ai-chan...?”

Looking up from my phone I frowned, confused for a few moments as I tried to think of what Uta was talking about. He had put away
his work for the night and was now placing aside completed masks to dry.

“Huh...oh yeah.” Oh. Right. I could get steak. I really wanted steak. Or pork chops. Bacon. Sausage. Roast beef. Chicken or—I swallowed
thickly and smiled weakly. I was concerned, but I didn’t want to bother or worry Uta. Or Kazuha. Or anybody. By the end of the month
I’d start the medicine and nobody would have to worry about me again; for this at least.

“Yeah...yeah. We should go shopping. I am kinda hungry—I was just hoping I’d hear more from Kazuha though...” I jumped up on my
feet and shuffled from foot to foot. “Are you ready to go now...?”

“Yeah.” The light above his desk clicked off and he stood up, brushing off scraps of his work from his pants.
“We can go now.” Scooping his keys off the counter he walked towards the door, pausing at my side to peer down at me curiously.

“Are you feeling alright?” He leaned in, tugging me close for a second and sniffing. “You smell strange.” He sniffed a few more times.

“On your clothes too...You don’t know what it was that got on you?”

“Hey—stop! Of course I am fine.” I shuffled from foot to foot, nibbling my bottom lip as he stared at me, studying me very closely. “We
don’t know what it was. Could have been anything. I’ll take a shower when I get home to get the smell off...I’m just worried about
Merlin. It didn’t really get on me much. I promise...I am feeling okay, Uta-kun. Completely fine. Can we please just go...?”

“Mmm. Okay.”

The walk there was quiet, and somber. There was an empty place next to me that normally Bjorn would have been occupying. Although I
knew that I had Uta with me, there was some piece of me that wanted to need my loyal protector...

At the grocery store I walked around, looking for food I felt like eating. I picked up a few things at random that I might eat. But in the end
I was drawn back to the meat department. Uta trailed behind me as I picked up a few packets, plucking up another...and another...
And another when it looked good.

“Ai-chan...”

“Hummm?”

“...” Uta’s eyes fell on the basket I was carrying; filled to the brim with all types of meat. I glanced down at it and balked. Somehow while I
picked out the food I hadn’t even realized how much I was picking up—actually another customer down the aisle was giving me an odd
look before vacating the area. Super. I was the strange meat lady at the grocery store now...

“This is...just...what I feel like eating...” I felt sheepish and embarrassed even though this was innocent enough; wasn’t it? I had a plan.
This was just for now—and then I wouldn’t want any of this. “Might as well enjoy what I want for a little while...right? Maybe I went a
little overboard on meat though...”

“Perhaps just a little.” The ghoul chuckled faintly, stepping beside me and reaching to hold the basket. A fiance carrying a heavy basket?
It was sweet and kind but I bristled automatically; gripping the handle tightly.
“I’ve got it.”

Uta’s hand paused next to mine and he raised his eyes. “...Are you su—?”

My phone went off and I blinked, broken out of the spell. I handed him the basket hesitantly. It wasn’t like he was going to take it, that
would be silly. I fumbled for the device in my pocket and pulled it out. A video call from Kazuha?

“It’s Kazu...” I said softly, staring at the button to answer. Was it Merlin? Did he get worse? Was he really sick—? Dying? I pressed the
button and squinted down at the screen, trying to get rid of the glare so I could see what was happening. “Kazu—where are you? Why is
it so dark? Is everything okay?”

The scene on the other end of the phone was shaky and dark. The sounds were confused and rustling. Whoever was holding the phone
had it away from their face. I could hear Kazuha in the background giving orders to people around him. “—Move the boy to another
room. Yes...bring his favorite things. We can set things up later for him. I—need this one. Make sure the staff from the labs are put in
containment. The one who threw it and the security who responded as well. Make sure they get medical attention—”

“—Hey! What’s happening?”

Chikafuji lifted the phone to show his face, grinning eerily in the dimmed hallway of the underground. “Ah, there you are ,Madam.
Where are you presently? I have some fairly urgent news.”

“The grocery store...? Me and Uta—”

“If you’d please, let me talk to him...give the phone to the Sir.” I stared at the phone for a few seconds before holding the phone out to

Uta. The ghoul took it, rotating it to look at the image curiously.

“Sir...get her home as quickly as possible. Have her take the meds immediately. A double dose. Crush it. Have her hold it in her mouth for
a minute and then swallow. She will get sick—and it will hurt her. However, it is better than the alternative. Or she probably will think so.”

I couldn’t see the image at this point but I heard Kazuha in the background, crying out wretched painfully. “She wasn’t close. But with
her cells already so high.”

Another painful retching and something falling to the ground and shattering.
“Merlin developed the start of ROS. He’s being medically treated—” I watched Uta’s face for a reaction since I couldn’t see the phone.
The ghoul’s eyes went wide and he tossed the bin of meat back into the cooler. Quickly he grasped my arm and was pulling me along, past
more confused patrons. I didn’t even want to know what they thought as Uta pulled me out the door by my wrist.

“Uta—wait. Why are we going? How did Merlin get ROS? Is he being treated—” There wasn’t a treatment for it, I knew that. But at least
he could be kept...alive? Until we found a cure.
I’d have to find a cure now too...

“Merlin started to grow a ROS protrusion. As Kazuha and yourself reported, he brunt of it when he ran through that mist. But some got
on your right-hand man and—” Now out in the street Uta hung up on the call.

I was scared. Shaking like a leaf as the ghoul pulled me along with him towards home. What about my plan? What happened to Kazuha?
What happened to Merlin? What was going to happen to me?

“Uta—”

The ghoul picked me up, forgoing having me ride on his back and simply throwing me over his shoulder and running. He kept his head
down and ignored people as they noted the odd scene that went sprinting by.
At the door to the shop he pushed it open and carried me all the way up to the apartment. Dropping me onto the couch he went to the
cabinet and pulled out the pills, looking at the label on it before pouring four pills out into his palm.

He pulled out a bowl from the cupboard and crushed the pills into a fine powder before bringing it to my side.

“Uta—?”

He leaned closer, hovering over me and reaching to grasp my chin. His fingers firmly pressed into my lips, urging me to crack my jaw
open for him. “Open—”
I did, opening my mouth and letting him pour the powder into my mouth. It was dry and I felt like coughing on it immediately. When it
was all in my mouth he pushed my jaw closed and stood still—watching my face as I grimaced.

It was disgusting. It hurt as it sat in my mouth mixing with saliva. It burnt as it slid against my gums. Uta let go of my face but sat
down beside me, reaching out to more gently hold my jaw closed as my body gagged on it. “Hold it Ai-chan...just hold it in your mouth
for a minute. I’ll have some water for you in a minute...”

I counted in my head, squeezing my eyes shut as I tried to think of anything but the foul tasting, burning powder in my mouth.

“Okay...Swallow Ai-chan...all of it.”

I did. Little by little mixing saliva in with the dry powder and struggling to get it all down. Already I could feel my body trying to reject it.
Once I had it all down Uta hopped up to grab some water, bringing it to me in a glass.


I drank it, relieved for a few moments as it washed away most of the taste and the feeling...but groaned and doubled over as the mixture of
powder and water tried to come back up.

“Keep it down...or you’ll have to take more.”
I whimpered softly . I didn’t want to do this anymore .

My phone rang again and Uta answered it.
“Did you—” Kazuha was on the other end this time, his voice and his breathing sounded ragged and unwell. “Did you get her home? Did
you give her the medicine in time...?”

“Kazuha-sama, we won’t know for at least a few hours if her medicine works...” Chickafuji’s voice sounded mechanical, as though it were
through a radio. My gut was burning but I still leaned over into Uta’s space, trying to look at the phone in his hands. The image on the
screen shifted and I could see Kazuha’s face. He looked...sweaty.

“I know—I know. Uta—keep an eye on her. There’s a fifty-fifty chance it doesn't work...if it’s too late...”

“Kazu...”

The man’s eyes glanced in my direction and stayed locked on my face. Despite his own obvious discomfort he still smiled faintly and
spoke in a manner that could only be meant to comfort someone, despite it being a ‘fifty-fifty chance’.

“It’ll be alright, Madam...You took a double dose...?” I nodded and he let out a relieved sigh.

“I am sorry, Madam...”

“No...it’s my fault, isn’t it...? That man was angry at me. Are you okay?”

“I’ll survive, Madam. I have a favor of you though...” The man closed his eyes and I could see he was visibly shaking. “...Do you think that
I could eat the synthetic—” He choked on his words and grimaced.

“The synthetic meat...Please Madam...I’m so hungry...”

I stared as he opened his eyes; red on black staring back through the phone.

## ♥
