## Chapter 84: Escape

Uta was far too weak to move far let alone fight and get us out of this. He was missing both arms and had both knees shattered. Even if he
had eaten and even if he’d be able to regenerate a little bit the investigator would just come back and do it all over again. Weakening Uta
again with more gas. Waiting until Uta got hungry again and possibly attacked me again.

Moreover, that monster would be bound to notice that I’d survived and if I started healing quickly—



I had to do it.
It was on me to protect us this time.

“He’s going to get us to the prison and release everything he knows about us. He might not even keep us both alive.” I eyed the stumps
where they’d taken off his arms. The two limbs were useless. One lay on a cold metal table where the man had placed it as some sort of
taunt and then the other dropped to the floor nearby.

“...please forgive me, Uta...”

I hated how my stomach growled. How I felt my mouth water as I concocted my half-baked plan. It was hard to ignore how good the
blood in the room smelled. I gathered my strength and crawled out from under him, shoving him off me and moving towards my target.
My thighs and arm burned painfully as I dragged my body away from him.

I couldn’t look at Uta, couldn’t bear to see what he might be thinking by any look he might have on his face right now.

This was the only way. I had to time it when that monster was away from the viewing window. Before he got back. Before he realized I
was still alive. He would remain unaware of what was going to happen until it was too late.

I closed my eyes and tried my best to imagine it wasn’t an arm.
## Uta’s—
The same hand that caressed me and cared for me. The same that carried me up a building to show me the view. The same that held mine
during Christmas. The same that I’d playfully bit his fingers when he fed me the pills to keep me human. The same that had protected me all
this time—

The smell though . It smelled like food . Already I was too far gone to be saved by suppressants. That much I could feel. I was craving
the meat and I was already healing to fast for a human. If it wasn’t for my ghoul genetics and high RC cell levels I have little doubt that
I’d be dead. I still couldn’t bear to look at my thigh but I knew I should have bled to death. It would be best to speed things up so that I
could protect us...catch the investigator off guard. He might have felt high and mighty about me being a ‘corrupted and brainwashed’
human, but he didn't know that I could turn ghoul any second.

After so long trying to stay human; now I'd throw myself full tilt off that cliff. Raise my RC cells as fast as possible.

I opened my mouth, drool pooling over my teeth as I closed them down on flesh.


‘Think of the rabbit.’

I recalled Uta telling me that one time I bit into his flesh—a love bite in comparison. But now it tasted better than the rabbit.


It was the first thing since I’d started the pills that tasted decent.
My teeth sank past skin and muscle, to the bone. Eyes closed and mind drifting I moaned as I tasted sweet meat on my tongue. My mouth
gripped the meat tightly in my hands and pulled my head back—ripping it and chewing.

I swallowed and went back for more.
## Bite.
## Rip.
## Bite.
Swallowed by hunger, the task of eating became easier and easier with each bite. I lost track of time. Eyes still closed and focus on food . The
empty pit in my stomach that needed to be filled before I could think straight again.
## Rip.
## Bite—
Before long I ran out of meat. My teeth struck bare bones. I tested it. It crushed under my jaws and I ground it down. It was like those candy
hearts on valentines!!! Especially when I started popping the smaller bits into my mouth; crunching them like candy in my mouth.

When I ran out of food I still wanted more . I could smell more and sniffed the air with my eyes still closed.

“Ai-chan...Ai...look at me.”

The voice brought me back a little. Uta...my fiance. My mate?  I opened my eyes, eyelashes fluttering as I adjusted to the light again and
stared at the man before me. He had moved slightly. He now was laid out on the ground on his back; Helpless. Weak from everything
they’d put him through during our time captured. Still captured. We weren’t free yet.

I moved towards him, shuffling across the floor. My wounds didn’t hurt nearly as much anymore but I still couldn’t look at them. Uta
was my priority right now. As I got closer he seemed focused on my eyes as I stared at him. “...Ai-chan...?” The uncertainty in his voice put
me on edge. Was I scary?

“I...I’m going to take care of us...It’ll be okay, Uta—” I breathed in and felt more saliva collect in my mouth. “... you smell so good .” I
realized what I’d said a moment later, staring down at him.

“I—I’m sorry that just—I didn’t...”

“It’s okay...”

“Uta...” He really did smell so good. I spotted his blank shoulder. I leaned over him, pinning him with very little effort and lowering
myself towards his shoulder. I wanted to bite. To put my mark on him. It would be only fair—-

His body twitched in protest, trying to move away. I stared down at him as he made an almost panicked noise— “Ai...?”

I raised one of my hands to hold his head still as I leaned in close; tempted to sink my teeth in deep. My thumb gently caressed his cheek.
His wide eyes were focused on mine. I pulled away though as I came back to my senses. Wrong time, wrong place. I tried to shake the
thought from my head and clear my mind.

There was too much in my head right now. The scent of this place. The sounds. The new emerging instincts? Uta sighed softly under me,
shivering and pulse going wild in his neck as he stared up at me.
“I could never eat you...” I said softly with a small frown.

“You just ate both of my arms, Ai-chan...”

“I...only ate one?” Plus I don’t think it’s fair to bring that up right now.

“...I just watched you.” I glanced around the room and tried to find the second one. It was... missing. Sitting in my stomach now

presumably. He had no reason to lie to me.

It was concerning that I only really could recall the one. And recalling it still brought saliva and drool to my mouth. It was also horrifying
to know that he watched me eat both his arms. Meat and bones; everything. I didn't want to think about it too hard. Not looking and
seeing what I was eating while I ate had saved me some trauma but I didn't want to imagine what it looked like when I consumed—

“...they weren’t attached...”

“They were not.”

“You ate some of me too, Uta-kun...”

“Mmm. We’ll call it even then.”

“You can regenerate, can’t you?”

The ghoul closed his eyes and hummed softly. He could .

“Are my eyes—?”


He opened his own, looking up at me and shook his head. “No Ai-chan...your eyes are back to normal.” Normal . Back from being
ghoulish. Because I am a—

“Ai-chan...what’s your plan.” Uta distracted my line of thinking and I turned my gaze back up to the empty observation box.

"...He thinks I'm human..."

“...He does.” Uta answered softly after a moment's pause.

“I...I am...not...”

“...no.” Uta confirmed softly. I felt my lip tremble but swallowed down my emotions for now. I couldn’t panic now. I couldn’t think about
anything further than a couple minutes ahead. We needed to get out of here. Then, and only then I could allow myself to think about
what I was now.

“...I’m going to get us out of here. He thinks you killed me—” I moved, finding it easier and easier by the minute as my body healed. I
could lift his body now laying his broken form over me just like he’d pinned me before. I'd Lay like I was dead.

“He’ll be back...and we both play our parts. Whatever you do, get him to come down here. Even if you feel better....let me take care of it.
## Okay?”

I closed my eyes and waited with Uta’s weight pressing down on me. Outside of recent memory, it was a comforting weight. Uta rested his
head back on my stomach. I wondered what he was thinking. My own mind felt numb. It was likely adrenaline having a calming clarity
effect for the moment. The trauma of having my husband eating me. The all consuming pain of being torn apart.

I heard the door above open and close and felt Uta raise his head to look at the investigator. I kept my breathing soft and shallow and
listened closely. “In the end she’s just another meal for you. I tried to tell her...she was so insistent that she stay by your side. Even if it got
her killed. She believed in you. It’s quite sad actually.”


The ghoul over me growled softly and I heard the investigator speak again, mocking Uta with his tone.  “Oh don’t worry...I won’t take
away the rest of your meal. You can eat the rest of the corpse if you’d like. Before you do, however; I would like to examine her body...”

I heard the voice move, footsteps moving down stairs and the door beeped and opened. Inside the room now.  I could smell him. Human
in all his glory. While Uta had tasted better than anything I’d eaten since the pills, the investigator smelled like a home cooked meal—or a
prized piece of wagyu. It was difficult to keep from drooling as the scent got closer and closer.

“—But after I have you may have it back. It will be the last real human flesh you taste so I’d enjoy it if I were you. Once you're done
healing, I’ll take out your kakuhou again. The last one wasn’t viable for a quinque. Once I have that then I’ll arrange for you to be sent to
## Cochlea.”

The investigator stopped as he stood over Uta. He scoffed softly and looked around. “You even ate your own arms...was it an attempt to
fill yourself so you might save her?”

“You stay right over here...” I felt Uta’s weight lifted off me and the investigator shove him off to the side. I cracked an eye when I heard
him rehooking Uta back to the table by the one restraint on Uta’s neck; leashing him like a dog. I closed my eyes again before he turned
back to me...

“Now— let's see the damage.” He was right over me, bent down to examine my ‘corpse’. He made a soft thoughtful ‘hum’ sound, likely
seeing my wounds from Uta’s teeth. “All the bites are on the meaty area’s...Deltoid, Bicep. Her thighs...were you trying to leave her alive?
This one doesn't seem so deep. Even through all that?”


“You did this...” I heard Uta’s contempt in his voice, distracting the investigator. I could hear how his voice turned away as he faced Uta. I
opened my eyes and saw the man, leaning over me but looking elsewhere. Summoning all my rage I flung my hands around his neck,
gripping tightly.

“It’s your fault...!!!” I hissed angrily. I wasn’t someone who hurt people. Not someone who killed. But this monster had hurt us for days.
Had tortured Uta. Had stolen life from my dog. I hated him.

The human’s eyes were wide with shock and fright as I grasped him and I shoved him back, sitting over him and gripping his airway to
stop his breath. His hands reached for my face and neck but a red tail of kagune wrapped around his wrists stopping him. Uta’s help.

I slammed the man's head back into the tile floor. His voice gurgled out from under my gripping hands. He must be so shocked to see me
looking down at him now, gripping his neck with a grip impossible for a human.

“YOU DID THIS TO ME.” The rage escaped me, slipping from my grip and rampaging. There wasn’t a single person that deserved it
more right now than this person.
I wanted him hurt.
I wanted him dead!


“I wanted to be human. I was doing so good. I was taking my medicine. I was eating disgusting food. I only complained a
little !—Even if it was terrible. Even if I hated every second! I was doing it! I was surviving that way so I wouldn’t have to
hurt anybody!”

I slammed him back down on the ground again and leaned down to continue screaming in his face.

“But you ruined it!!! You took away my best friend!!! You hurt my mate!!!! You tried to have me EATEN by him! And you
took away my HUMANITY!”


I kept slamming his head back into the floor, even after his eyes were rolled up in his head and his mouth gaped open. After there was
blood splattered across the now cracked white tile.



“Ai-chan...that’s enough...he’s dead.” I heard Uta but I still gripped the man's neck, grimacing down at him and shaking with rage and
fury. He was dead . I knew it; I could smell that. But I wanted him to get back up and say some more hateful words just so I could smack
him back down again.

“Ai-chan...please...we need to leave.” I hated how weak Uta sounded and I knew we had to leave. But I had things we had to do first.

“No—” I swallowed the saliva in my mouth. Think. Think. He knew who we were—but he was keeping it all to hand in later. Right? So
nobody else knew. But when he went missing there might be people who knew where to look!!!

“We...I need to look around and find any information he has on us. Then we need to torch the place.” I looked down to the investigator's
waist and found a keycard and a set of keys. I pulled them from his corpse with a sharp yank and stood up on wobbling legs.

My thighs were healed. Though there was a slightly lighter patch of skin and the left side had a divot that showed that I was missing some
flesh and muscle there...another scar that I’d carry for the rest of my life. When I took a step that side was slightly weaker. It would likely
take more time to build up the muscle again; if it ever was the same again.

Putting aside my physical condition, I searched his other pockets and grabbed his phone.
I shakily dialed a number I knew by heart and waited—

It rang once. Twice. Three times.
“Hello?” The voice at the other end sounded confused and on guard.

“Kazu...It’s me...”

“AIKA!? Where are you!?” I heard movement in the background, people rushing. Things were moving quickly, bursting into
movement the moment he said my name on the other end.
“We got captured by the same investigator that killed Bjorn...” I said softly, looking down at the man's corpse.

My voice shook a little as I tried to keep myself together. “He brought us somewhere private for his own...tests and observations...He’s
dead now. Can you find us with this phone?”

“Yes Madam. Give us a few hours. We can be there shortly. You’re far outside the city...”

“Just to be safe. And bring someone who’s good with computers. We need to make sure his personal data is wiped...”

“Yes Madam. Don’t worry. I’m sending people to help...just keep the phone on the line.”

“Sure...” I laid the phone down on a metal table and left it. I glanced at Uta and then the dead man. He needed to eat. More than just a few
chunks out of my thighs and arm.

I grasped the man's suit and dragged him towards Uta, dropping the corpse in front of my mate. I moved around the other side of the
table and put the code back in and heard the beep and release. “There...” Peeking around the other side. He was looking at the corpse but I
frowned a bit when Uta didn’t start eating.


“Uta-kun...you can eat him...You’ll need to regenerate more...”

The ghoul glanced down at the dead man and then back at me. “Do you want any...?”

My stomach clenched and had the audacity to growl and demand the food. Gritting my teeth I shook my head sharply from side to side.
“No...I don’t want any...”

“Ai...you’ll need to eat too.”

“...I ate already...” He cocked his head to the side and seemed to want to say something but held back. He struggled but with his
weakened Kagune managed to move himself and rip off the man's shirt. Unlike when he fed off me he went straight for the man's throat,
ripping it out and chewing it quickly before going back for more—

I turned away as my stomach protested. I did want the meat.
A terrible part of me argued that I’d hunted it. Killed it. It was mine. I should be eating it—

“I need to go find any information he had on us....” I spoke softly, aloud for myself as a reminder of what I was doing. Something to
distract me from going back.

I held my breath to stop from smelling the body behind me as I held the keycard up to the door. I was relieved when it opened up and we
were free. I walked up the stairway to the observation room. At the top of the stairs I finally let out a breath. I could still smell it, but it
was fainter up here. With my mind set upon my task I began picking up his journals and his documents. Collecting them up. Next the
computer up here would have to be gone through.

I could hear Uta ripping into the man but I tried to ignore it with all my might. It was distracting. “77...9....3.” Plugging the code into the
computer. I hoped that he was like many people; using the same code for almost everything.

A few seconds passed and it made a soft ding and then loaded up the desktop. I exhaled and went looking for his emails first. The main
question I needed to find out was did he tell anybody he had us here? I searched through a month's worth of emails looking for anything
that could be about us. He had a draft version of his findings but nothing that he’d already sent. I deleted the draft immediately. An hour
or more passed as I scoured the computer for anything even remotely ghoul related and deleted it.

I heard movement in the house above and tensed. I stood and moved myself into a corner so I wouldn’t be seen by whoever came in. I
might be able to catch them by surprise. The footsteps that came down the stairway were rushed and I tightened every muscle, prepared
to launch myself and prepared to fight.

“Madam!?” I froze. The voice was familiar even if the scent wasn’t.
“Kazu...?”

We froze, both shocked as we came face to face. He stared and I stared back; both of us were ghouls now. Both of us would be able to tell;
immediately.  He took it in stride, adjusting to stand up straight.
“Madam...are you okay? Why are you in such undress—?” He pulled off his jacket and threw it around my shoulders, tucking the front
closed in front of my chest to preserve some of my modesty.

Somehow I’d forgotten that my clothing had been taken from me. Modesty was the furthest thing from my mind at the moment. I
wanted to ask him how he had decided to leave his self-imprisonment—

Instead I scoffed. “What a stupid question. Where’s the computer expert I asked for...?”


“That—that would be me. I’m sorry—Hello M-madam! Oh gosh —” The driver boy from before ran down the stairway after Kazu.
Breathing hard and clearly sweating. He turned his face away, blushing when he saw what I was wearing. He smelled nice too—-

I shoved away the thought and grit my teeth as my eyes seemed to focus and sharpen.
“Easy, Madam...” Kazuha reached out and gently touched my shoulder, sliding himself between me and the young man. Ruka stared at
me with wide terrified eyes. “...Madam. We should get you home. There’s some of the synthetic organs there...”

“I am fine...” I shivered and shook my head. “...anyway we can only afford to feed one Ghoul...you said so yourself...” I ground my teeth,
trying not to think about what I’d eat next. Who I might eat next when everybody smelled at least somewhat appealing.

“...We’ll figure it out. I shall push for them to make more—it is to help humanity, isn’t it? Where is your husband...?”

“Down the stairs—” I reached out and grabbed Kazuha by his shirt before he could go far. “He’s eating ...leave him be for a bit. Take
care of these documents.” I shoved them into his hands with a grimace. “Perhaps Chikafuji would be interested in them...? I want these
computers wiped of all data. I want his email accounts deleted.  I want to know if he sent anything to anybody in the last two months
about us. I want to know what he knows...and I want to make sure nobody else does. Once you have all that; I want it all gone.”

## ♥


I wore stolen clothing from the investigators wardrobe as I carried Uta on my back. I hadn’t been able to find all our belongings and we
didn’t have time to keep looking. Kazuha had offered to carry Uta for me but I had found myself sneering at anybody who came near Uta
while he was so hurt. Despite his missing limbs he wasn’t much lighter now; thanks to his over-filled stomach.

When I went to pick him up it was really hard to ignore the half corpse left on the floor of the containment cell. Its eyes were plucked out
and his neck was gone , eaten down to the bone of his spine. Parts of his pecs and his stomach had been eaten or pulled out and picked
through. I really wish I hadn’t noticed that even his genitals hadn’t gone unmolested.

“Did you seriously eat his dick, Uta....?” The ghoul on my back chuckled and I shot him a scathing look.
“I did...besides the eyes, it’s one of my favorite parts...it tastes good...did you want it—?”

“Absolutely not!” I said sharply.

Uta laid his head down to rest it on my shoulder, laughing softly as I carried him out of the basement. We emerged in a fairly ordinary
looking home. Livingroom. Kitchen. Bathroom and bedroom. It was furnished just like a home should be. He had no pictures of family
but he had awards from the CCG.

He had certificates that told the world everything he’d achieved. Everything he’d killed. Everyone he murdered. Likely others that he’d
tortured just like us. Perhaps worse.

For everyone who didn’t make it because of him: “....Burn it.” I said softly, staring at the certificates.

Kazuha glanced around the room quickly and then nodded. “...of course Madam. There’s someone waiting for you. He was guarding the
front while we went in...”

Uta sniffed the air and spoke first. “Renji-kun.”

“That...is correct.” Kazuha glanced at me, looking worried before looking away. Hurrying away to check on the driver boy. I’d forgotten
his name. Koru? Roku?


Renji...? I sniffed and smelled—a scent. A Ghoul. I didn’t have a nose for who was who yet. Even Uta I could only recognise based on
what I remembered him smelling like. Even that was different, deeper or more complex now that my body was adjusting to being...this.

I reached for the door and it snapped open before I could grasp it. I raised my eyes and saw Renji, his eyes staring at me with concern. “I
smelled Uta...and...”

“...Me?”

“Imouto...are you okay? I can carry him...” Renji moved as though to take Uta from my back and I stepped backwards sharply. He was
mine. Mine to take care of. Mine to nurse back to health. My mate.

“Okay...alright. You’ve got him. You can hold him...” Renji took a cautious step back and glanced over my shoulder towards his friend.
“Uta...how are you feeling? What happened to your arms...? And your legs...?”

“We’re not talking about it now. Let's go. We’re torching the place. And we shouldn’t be anywhere near it when it goes up in
flames...Kazu. Come on. Get everybody out...” I carried Uta past Renji and out the front door. I spotted Renji’s beat up car and my
company car. It was a split second decision but I went to the beat up car and placed Uta gently in, crawling in after him.

“Madam...? Are you not going back to the manor...?” Kazuha exited the building while the boy and a few other humans prepared to light
the place up.

“...Renji. Can you follow Kazuha back to the manor...?”

“...Sure.” I felt watched as I sat quietly in the back of the car. I could smell Uta. I could smell Renji. I could even smell the human scent
lingering on him. It must be that human he was friends with. There were other scents too—female ghouls. Blood and alcohol. Itori
perhaps. Another I didn’t recognize and couldn’t begin to guess.

“Ai-chan...?” I knew Uta wanted to make sure I was okay. But I wasn’t. I couldn’t lie for much longer and pretend I was. I was hungry
and I wasn’t human anymore. My stomach growled again and I felt myself getting antsy. Just like I’d gotten at the supermarket; wanting
every piece of meat that appeared in front of my face. That would be concerning if I started to look at humans like that.
How many might I hurt just because I was hungry?


“Aika...” I winced, unaccustomed to Uta using my full first name. I glanced up at him and met his gaze with my own.
“I’m okay...” He was giving me a soft look but it turned frustrated when he couldn’t move his arms—or lack thereof. I hesitantly leaned
in close to him and he sighed softly, face relaxing when he got what he wanted.
“....it’s okay if you’re not...” I nuzzled my face into his neck, inhaling his scent. With all the blood on him he still made my mouth water.

“It’s okay if you're sad about changing into a Ghoul...”

I haven't decided if I was sad. That would require that I had thought terribly deep about it. Unlike my stomach; I definitely hadn’t
processed or accepted it yet.

“I was supposed to protect you so you didn’t have to worry about this...”
I squeezed my hands, clawing at his shoulder and growling softly.

“Don’t... don’t say that. It’s not your fault.”


“I should have fought harder or been more aware of our surroundings...”

“ Shut up! ”  I didn't mean to snap but I did, gripping him tight and trembling. “... Stop . Please. It’s not your fault. I don’t want to
yell...But I'm so hungry... I can’t think straight. My head hurts...” Renji stepped on the gas, spurring the car to go faster through traffic.

“...We should go back to my place.” Uta commented. “It’s faster to get there.”

“Uta...she needs food.”

“...and if she throws it up like you Renji? Then there’s nothing for her to eat. She’ll be hungrier than before.” I was listening to their
conversation. I knew that what he said was true but I didn’t want to eat what was in Uta’s fridge—and not just because it had been there
for well over a week.

The car suddenly turned, spinning around and taking off in another direction. Renji’s phone went off a few seconds later and he
answered it with one hand as he kept driving.
“... Where the hell are you going?!”  I recognized Kazuha’s voice over the line, likely calling because he noticed Renji’s sudden and rather
dangerous road activity.

“Back to Uta’s.”

“ What about the synthetic organs?! She needs to eat!”

“...have someone bring them.” Renji hung up and kept driving, back towards Uta’s shop and our home. My ghoulish husband lowered his
head, pressing his chin into the top of my head. Weak strings of his regenerating kagune wrapped around me to hold tight for a second
before evaporating.

“How long until your arms regenerate...?” I asked to distract myself. Thankfully the ghoul seemed to understand, chuckling softly at my
question.
“Oh this? It’s nothing...I’ve eaten now so...a day or so for the right one. It’s about halfway done. About two for the other...” Uta sighed
softly and groaned. “Reminds me of when me and Renji-kun got into fights. We used to wreck our bodies like this...Remember, Renji-
kun?”

“Yeah...I remember when you punched a hole through my stomach. I had to wait a day before I could eat anything...”

“Hahaha! I forgot about that one! I felt bad about that...”

“No you didn’t.” Renji said blandly, no doubt rolling his eyes as he sped us homeward bound.

“No, really. I did.” Uta said, trying to be earnest through his laughter.

Their conversation died a little when my stomach growled again and I bit my inner cheek until I tasted my own blood. I sat back,
deciding to finally push myself away from Uta and scooting myself across the car. All the way to the other window I sat there quietly with
shaking breaths.

“Almost home, Ai...”

“What do you have in the fridge, Uta...?” Renji questioned, glancing in the rear view mirror.

“...Some human. But...mostly some ghoul right now. They were acting like a punk on my street again. I warned them a few times before.
There’s eyes...if she wants to try some.” I felt Uta’s own eyes on me as I stared out the window.  I absolutely did NOT want to try
eyes.

“Uta...what happened while you were captured...?”


“....He asked a bunch of questions.“

“About any of us...? Or the Clowns?”

“No. He was a strange guy. Only asked about Aika and myself. How we lived together. If I thought about eating her. Our sex life...for
research.”

As we drove some fire trucks passed us at a high speed, rushing no doubt to put out the fire that was started in the investigators home.
The investigator whom I hadn’t even bothered to get a name for though I was sure it must have been somewhere in his paperwork...he
was someone who might forever be a nameless monster.

“...there’s blood-wine at the house.” Uta suddenly said. “Would you drink that, Ai?”

“Do you think alcohol is the best choice, Uta?”

“...it might hold her over until the synthetic stuff gets to the house.”

“...Blood-wine?” I murmured with a slight frown.

“Yeah...I meant to have it when we got back. But you can have it if you’d like.” I wanted to ask where the blood came from, but stopped
myself. I didn’t want to know. Not right now. I doubted that its origins were entirely innocent though.
“...I don’t think so Uta-kun...” I took a shaking breath and forced a weak smile. “I’ll...wait for the synthetic.”

I could feel him still watching me but I turned my gaze back to watching the world pass by. Distracting myself by counting the signs and
the roads we passed. We pulled into the usual spot where Renji stopped the car and hopped out. I ran around the car and got Uta out
quickly.

“My keys are in my pocket, Renji...can you grab them...?”

The silver haired ghoul gingerly reached into my pocket and picked out the keys. “...I couldn’t find your keys, Uta-kun. It’s possible he
put them somewhere I couldn’t find, or we dropped them when we were running...we should change the locks. Just in case...? Was there
anything else important on that keying?”

“Nah, not really. Nothing I can’t change...he also took our bracelets. Sorry I lost it...”

I looked at my own wrist and frowned. He was right, our matching set of bracelets were missing. As was his necklace he usually wore and
his piercings. For some reason the investigator had pulled them all out and they’d healed over. He looked a little strange without any of
them. His face looked naked.

“I liked them. But we don’t need them anymore. It does seem like you're going to have to re-pierce some stuff though.” I turned my head
and a smile tugged briefly at my lips.

Taking a step into the shop again felt strange—it smelled strange. It seemed like Uta and...myself? But not. My scent was human mixed
with RC Cell suppressants and underlying illness. The RC cell suppression was bitterly repugnant. And the illness was sour. I wasn’t sure
how else to describe it, save for viscerally unpleasant.

Was that what I’d smelled like for the last couple months?


I climbed the stairs and began to marvel at the lack of weakness. I could run up the stairs and did so springily bouncing up each stair until
I heard Uta’s soft grunt when it jostled him. “Careful Ai...feeling a little fragile here...”

“Sorry! Sorry—Uta...I just—”

“You feel better. I’m glad. You can jump around after you put me down, Okay?” The ghoul chuckled and then groaned a bit in pain. A
reminder that he was still rather grievously hurt. I was gentle when I off-loaded him onto the couch. Laying him down on his back and
grabbing a few pillows I stacked them behind so he could comfortably rest a little upright.

“...Yeah. Here....Let me take care of you...should I clean the wound with anything...? Maybe make sure there aren’t any shards of bone
anywhere?”

“I’m alright Ai.”

“You’ll need more food...” Renji said, the silver haired ghoul had slipped into the apartment when I hadn’t been paying any attention. He
was leaning down by the fridge and frowning at all the containers. “I’ll bring you something...I suppose I’ll also sort it for you...”

“I’m so lucky to have such a good friend.” Uta said softly with a cheeky little grin.

“I’m not doing it for you. It’s for Ai-chan...who else would get you food? I’m not  going to let her be the one to do it...”

“...of course not. I wouldn’t expect that...” Uta glanced up at me with a small frown on his face. His eyes lingered on me for a few
seconds, eyes searching for something and then looking away. The ghoul’s expression was looking lost and confused for a few seconds
before he covered it with a blank expression again. Masking again.

“...Where’d our phones go...?” He finally asked. “We should call Itori and let her know too. If she doesn't already know.”

I had forgotten to mention what I’d done with them. “I...broke them. When we were caught. I threw them and they cracked and broke
and fell into the drainage system...I didn’t want him to get our friends numbers or anything. We’ll need new ones...some of the data
might be in the cloud but—maybe not everything.”

“Oh...I guess that was after I passed out...” The ghoul frowned and laid his head back against the cushions. “...don’t think I’ve ever had
both my arms and legs messed up at the same time...”

“Well, you still have your legs. They’re just shattered from the looks of it. They should heal in about a day...” Renji commented, standing
up in the kitchen.

“Mmmm, yeah...then I can get around on my own at least.”

The two ghoul’s kept talking as Uta started to tell Renji everything that had happened. He glanced at me quickly before telling Renji
about my plan. My head-long leap out of humanity and into being a ghoul. To Renji’s credit, he didn’t even flinch when Uta told him
what happened to his arms.

“Excuse me...I just—one minute.” I stood up, softly murmured my excuses to go to the bathroom. I closed the door behind me and
clenched my fists tightly at my sides. Cautiously I went to the sink and slowly raised my eyes to stare at the reflection of myself.

I looked just like I always had...no ghoulish eyes. I was the same Aika I had always been.
Except. That’s not true, is it?

I closed my eyes and experimented. Purposefully thinking of the smell of meat. The taste of it in my mouth. My mouth watered and I
opened my eyes. I was staring back into the eyes of a ghoul, the veins of the active kakugan spreading down over my eyelids and onto my
upper cheekbones.


I’m a ghoul.

No contacts or special effects. I couldn’t rip these out and discard them like I could before.

My legs gave out and I clung to the sink, sliding down to the floor. I grasped my head tight in my hands, scratching my scalp and tugging
on my hair. I bit my tongue and squeezed my eyes tight until it hurt. Trying to cause enough pain to wake me up. Jolt me out of it!



I’m a ghoul.

I wanted to wake up now. Please!? Let it all be a terrible dream. Let it be a nightmare that I can wake from. Let it all fade away. Let me
wake up in bed in a cold sweat like all those times before.

Yet each time I blinked my eyes I was still looking at the tile floor. It grew blurry as tears slid from my eyes but it remained .


## ♥


Uta watched Aika leave him on the couch. He couldn’t follow, stuck in place and watching where she’d disappeared. After a few minutes
he could hear the sobbing and then the water from the shower head. The raven
ghoul stayed quiet, watching the door as well. Uta didn’t doubt that he was worried too. They had adopted each other as a found family.

“...What are you going to do if she can’t eat the fake meat, Uta?”

“...I’ll hunt for her of course.” The answer was as natural to him as breathing. Of course he would feed his mate.

“And if she won’t eat it...?”

“You know she will, Renji...” If she was hungry enough she would eat anything. She wasn’t his fragile little human anymore though. He
wasn’t sure how he felt about it. Excited perhaps? Yet, another part knew this wasn’t what she wanted. “...I’ll find food like you do when
it’s possible. She’d be happier with that...wouldn’t she?”

He remembered her screaming at the investigator as she slammed his head into the tile. She had survived through just a few months of the
pill to stay human. She had been miserable and suffered the whole time...would it be so horrible for him to hope she might eat something
that tasted good, would make her stronger and was happy? Regardless of its origins...?

He was conflicted.
She might be the same species now.
But she wasn’t like him at all. Perhaps that innocence was what he needed to protect now, more than ever before.

“I’ll figure it out. Can you make sure Kazuha can get in the building?”

## Chapter 85: Meat?

I could hear Kazuha as he entered the shop below and then as he followed Renji back up the stairs to the apartment. I could hear my 'big
brother' tell him that I was in the bathroom and I could hear them talking about me—asking if I’d be okay.

I wiped my eyes on my sleeve and sniffled.

I shouldn’t be so sad, should I? In the end I’d made the best choice out of a terrible lot of them. But it was still a choice .

We had survived. We survived and we’d even managed to destroy a lot of information on us that he’d collected. We would have to keep a
watchful eye on investigators who got too close and keep an ear out for anything that sounded like we’d been found out. The man’s
ordinary human pride and ambition had saved us from being outed right away like he should have done.

For now things could go back to normal. In a sense at least...

Except now I wasn’t Human.

There was a soft knock on the door and I looked up, sniffling and struggling to make my face presentable. My eyes and nose were a little
red from crying, and then rubbing them. But the reflection looking back was just...me.

The person at the door knocked softly again. This time speaking up: “Madam...? I brought you some food.”

Food. My personal goal would become a very personal hope for me. Even if it tasted terrible, at least I could continue to know that eating
wasn’t at the cost of someone else; right? Just more of the same last couple months. Me and Kazu could both eat—though we might need to
fudge some numbers and finagle things around to make it work. I reached up and turned off the shower head and cleared my throat
before answering.

“I’ll be right out...”

One last check in the mirror. I was still in the borrowed clothing and grimaced at the sight of its slightly too baggy form on me. As soon as
I ate; I was going to actually take a shower and get some clothing on that would make me feel—normal.

Deep Breath. And I opened the door, stepping out into the room only to have two sets of eyes on me. The third, Uta, was only missing
because from his placement on the couch he couldn’t see the bathroom.

“Madam. There you are. I came as quickly as I could. I hadn’t expected you to suddenly change direction.” Kazuha shot Renji a quick
look before returning back to me. “It’s...not good. As both myself and others have warned you. However, it should keep your hunger at
bay and Chikafuji has assured me I am perfectly healthy after eating it for this long.”

Kazu produced a styrofoam takeout container and I almost laughed. It was funny...wasn't it? He caught my quick slip in expression and
seemed to mistake it for something else. “Is something wrong...?”


“No.. Sorry. Everything is fine...It’s just...with you bringing it to me. In this box. It’s...dumb.” I laughed faintly. “It’s like a take-out
container. Should I tip you for delivery?”

Kazuha’s worried expression turned to a dull stare; one he usually gave me when I’d made a dumb or childish joke. The sort of expression
I always tried to drag from him while being a pain in the ass for him. He placed the container in my hands and exhaled. “It’s good to see
you still have your sense of humor...”

“Anything I can do to annoy you, Kazu!~” I glanced down at the box and walked around Kazuha, to the living room. Uta was on the
couch still, his eyes on me the moment I was in the room. He struggled to try and sit up. “Woah, Uta...don’t move. I’ll sit here.”

I knelt myself next to the base of the couch, placing the box of ‘food’ on the table. This way I could be close to him. With some hesitancy I
popped the lid on the box. The meat looked normal. It was a dark red color, freshly taken from growing and delivered to me. Renji and
Kazuha stood watching while Uta watched over my shoulder as I picked up the meat.

I hesitated. It would taste bad. It was the same as the last few months. I closed my eyes, opened my mouth and took a small bite. It was
smooth, dense, and slightly spongy in texture which were all normal for liver. The taste on the other hand, the taste was putrid. I almost
immediately gagged before managing to swallow it. I didn’t even bother trying to chew. Getting it down was the main goal right now and
nothing else mattered.

Renji and Uta were both saints for dealing with this taste and not complaining. Itori’s reaction was much, much more understandable
now. I wasn’t sure how they ever could have gotten it down without complaint. Uta even ate it for a whole month—

I opened my mouth and took bigger bites; hastily trying to swallow as much as I could before I gagged. Perhaps if I cooked it, it might be
better? Or if I did somehow mix donated blood with it in a blender...? Blood-Liver slushie—perhaps?

I had to stop after getting half of it down, pausing to take a breath and stick my tongue out. I shivered in disgust and glanced over my
shoulder. “...I am so sorry, Uta—for making you eat that.”

“It’s alright...How are you feeling...?”

“Um...Alright?” I shifted in my spot and waited a few seconds. It worked! I could eat! I wouldn’t have to—!!!


Just as I began to celebrate my stomach flipped and my thoughts crashed into a wall as it all tried to come back up in a violent torrent. I
grit my teeth and tried to keep it down; shoving a hand over my mouth as my body tried to retch and reject it.

“Shit—” Someone rushed by me and a few seconds later a bin was set in front of me. Yet still, I tried to keep it down, choking in the
attempt.

“...you can’t keep it down. Just like with human food. You’ll hurt yourself if you try, Imouto...” Renji knelt beside me, hand pressing on
top of my head in a comforting gesture. I gripped the edge of the bin and ejected the offending ‘food’. The parts came up in solids and
bile.

When it was all out I sat panting heavily and filled with a newly renewed hunger, as if it were back with a revenge.

“She can’t eat it then. If you’d allow, Renji-san....we could find out if there’s something similar between you and her that doesn't allow
either of you to eat the synthetic meat.”

I barely listened to them as Renji and Kazuha spoke, their words were distant compared to my disappointment and anger. Bitter tears fell
fresh from my face, falling into the bin with the rejected ‘food’ I couldn’t eat. Why couldn’t I eat the synthetic organs? It wasn’t fair—I
had them made! Of all the people to be affected so—I couldn’t even benefit from my own efforts to help Ghouls? I couldn’t even
help myself?!



I stumbled up to my feet, almost tipping the bin over in my haste to retreat away . Behind me someone shouted as I sprinted for the
bedroom, slamming the door behind me and shaking like a leaf. I slid down to sit against the door.

## ♥


It was sometime later and the apartment had long gone quiet when someone came back to the door. I pushed my back against it, fearful
that they might try to come in and I might not be able to resist. Kazuha might have had the right idea after all. I couldn’t trust myself...

“Aika...I got you something. Can you come out?” Renji’s voice was calm as he leaned on the doorframe.

“No...” I replied, squeezing my eyes shut and covering my head with my arms. “I don’t want whatever it is....”

“You need to eat...I didn’t expect you’d want what is in Uta’s fridge.” The raven ghoul sighed softly and leaned down so his voice was just
on the other side of the door as my head.
“Uta told me that you’ve cooked for him before. The meat was found the Anteiku way, nobody was killed....” He waited for a full minute
before speaking again. “If I need to, I will force you to eat—just as we did with Ken when he first needed to eat. I won’t let you starve
yourself. I know you won’t be happy if you end up hurting someone...especially Uta when he’s in this state.”

I raised my head and swallowed down a mouthful of saliva. If I was left here alone with this hunger, would I hurt Uta who couldn’t fight
back? Would I try to eat him just like he had taken chunks out of me...? Worse?

I didn’t want to hurt Uta. He had done everything he could to keep from letting me get hurt during our capture. Answered all the
questions. Endured having his kakuhou taken out. Even starving he had even tried his best not to kill me— I couldn’t let myself hurt him.

I slid away from the door and slid the lock undone. The door creaked open and Renji peered in, eyes soft as he looked down at me.
“...Come on Imouto. We need to get you something to eat...” The raven ghoul reached down and grasped my arm and helped haul me
up to my feet.

I followed him to the other room again, eyes kept low on the ground. As soon as I entered the living room I could smell the scent of fresh
human meat. It was dizzying how much I wanted it. I followed Renji to the kitchen, lured by the smell and the hunger. I lifted my eyes
and observed the stacks of butchered meat on the counter. In an instant the kitchen sharpened and focused, the color red seemed to leap
out at me a bit brighter making the meat even more enticing.

“I haven't sorted it into boxes yet. I’ll clean up after we sort what you’ll eat. The old man taught me how so for now I’ll cook for you if
you want to wait—” The ghoul cut off his words, watching as I reached for a piece of meat. It was cool to the touch but the blood was
fresh. Whoever they had once been had ended tonight. I opened my mouth and shoved the meat in.

Part of me had been terrified that it would taste as bad as the fake meat. That perhaps there would be something wrong  with me being
some sort of strange abomination of human turned ghoul—The worry was washed away with the first drops of blood on my tongue.

It was divine.

Sweet but also pleasantly tender and hearty. The fat in it seemed to melt in my mouth as I chewed it slowly. I reached for a second piece
and took a bite out of it. Renji didn’t stop me as I reached for a third piece, eating them like a kid might steal things off the counter. Just
as I had done as a kid with pieces of cut potatoes or grapes. I swiped cookies and fresh baked rolls while Ms. Sato and the rest of the cooks
rolled their eyes and smiled.


Renji didn’t stop me, though he did pick up a larger chunk and drop it into a hot frying pan. “Uta...you might be stuck eating all the old
stuff you got in the fridge.”

“That’s fine.” Uta called back from the other room. Then added: “...She’s eating?”

“She is...I’m still cooking in case she’d like to eat that as well.”

## ♥


Uta relaxed and let out a breath he’d been holding. She was eating ‘properly’ and he was happy about it. She, on the other hand, may not
be right now—but she was alive. That was something more than a small miracle after what he’d done to her.

He still remembered the taste of her flesh—the taste of perhaps the last vestiges of her humanity bleeding across his tongue. He had
struggled to not bite too deep. Not pull too much off one spot. Not to take from somewhere where he’d hit an artery. Everything he could
to keep her alive.

He only had some much control when he had been so badly hurt and starved. Yet if not for her one in a million—or—one in a billion
genetics: she might have perished regardless. He had almost lost her. He had almost been the one to kill her.
In a sense he had killed her. Her humanity was gone—striped from her by a careless night and a missed medicine.


He had cried —something he hadn’t done in...

....he wasn’t sure how long it had been to be perfectly honest. Perhaps not since the death of the parents he no longer remembered. He
didn’t know if she could forgive him for what he’d done—she’d said she did as he was doing it. He had said they were even after she’d
eaten his arms—an unexpectedly alarming sight that wasn’t soon going to be leaving his memory.

But even now—he wasn’t sure he could forgive himself. Her screams, her following whimpers and then silence would haunt him far
more than any of the ‘innocent’ people he killed and ate. Or even the people he had sold for a handful of yen.

Forgiveness aside: What was done was done.
There was no undoing her becoming a Ghoul, unless her company found a ‘cure’ to make her Human again. And she was presently
unable to eat her own fake meat, so that left her with little option but to eat the normal way.

Eat Human —or Ghoul should she prefer cannibalism over eating her former kind. She would eat and she would grow stronger. He had
plenty of time to try and make her happy, show her the benefits of being a Ghoul. Food would once again taste good. She could be
stronger than she ever had been before. She could go back to training which she had dearly missed. She could play with him? They might
make one hell of a team...

He wondered what sort of Kagune she’d have...he never did find out what her uncle had so it was all up in the air. He was very vague and
evasive about it when he brought it up talking around the fire.



Once his arms were back in working order there was a whole list of things he’d need to get done. His tattoos for one would need to be
redone. His piercings also had been messed up. He’d need to switch out some locks around the shop to make sure none of them were the
ones from the missing keying. What else?


Introducing Ai-chan to Itori and Nico all over again—this time she would be on more equal footing. He could try introducing Ai-chan
to eating human foods as snacks. Eyes perhaps? Though, judging how she’d popped his knuckle bones into her mouth like they were
candy...she might prefer something crunchier.

Uta closed his eyes and laid still on the couch, listening to the sound of cooking meat and the smaller subtler sounds of his wife eating in
the other room.

## ♥

BIG BROTHER. Yup.
