## Chapter 86: Day 1 Ghoul

## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 86:

I was done with my gruesome feast.

There was blood on my hands. Around my mouth. Smeared across my chin and cheeks. I could feel it sticky and drying as the silver
haired ghoul cooked more meat beside me. The scent filled the entire apartment and it was delectable.

Renji glanced down at me and then handed me a wet cloth, moving slowly as if not to startle me. As if I were a stray cat that might bite if
he moved too fast. I took it and mindlessly wiped away the evidence of my crime.

I'd eaten... someone .
Not just a bite or two. Not someone who could regenerate so they were still alive and would be well again. Just a whole lot of someone
who was dead and gone. And now my stomach felt...full . The last time I’d gorged on the meal to the point of being somewhat
uncomfortable I had still been a child. But now I slid down to sit on the floor of the kitchen and stared at the tile.

## Full.

When I'd started to eat it had been such a blur. I had wanted nothing but to eat and it was easy to rationalize that it was something I must
do. Once I started, it was so easy to keep going. Now that it was over—There wasn’t a lot of meat left on the counter.

“...Full, finally?” Renji questioned. He flipped the seared meat over in the pan and barely turned his head to glance down at me. I nodded
silently and bit harshly down on my bottom lip to keep it from trembling. “Alright, I’m going to put this in the fridge for you later. I
assume Uta ate a bit from the investigator since he’s got blood all down his front. But he should eat as much as he can. So I’ll give him the
rest of the raw stuff.”

I nodded again but didn’t say anything. Renji took the meat off the burner and put it aside before moving around me and picking up the
meat that was left over, putting it on a plate. Now that I was full, I didn't feel the same aggression that I had when someone took ‘my’
‘food’ from me. That feeling was all but gone now—back to normal .

From the other room I heard Uta messing with Renji.
“You gonna hand feed it to me, Renji-kun?!~”

“Eat it yourself...”

A few moments later Renji came back, rolled up his sleeves and began washing dishes. When everything was washed, rinsed and dried he
dried his hands and stood above me. I felt a hand gently touch the top of my head.


“Since you ate so much you won’t have to worry about food for at least a couple days if you don’t want to. It’s not always as bad as that.
Were you hurt...?”

I thought of the wounds caused by Uta and ducked my head a bit to avoid looking at Renji. “A...little bit.”

“Hum...Alright. That’s probably why you were so hungry. You should get changed and get some rest...”  The  ghoul slid his hand from
my head and walked away from me. “...I’m going to head home. Aika-chan...call me if you need anything. I’ll be back tomorrow to check
on you both.”

“Thanks Renji...”  I leaned my head on my knees and faintly smiled up at Renji before he left the apartment completely. Renji was right
of course. I should sleep. I should rest. But at the same time I felt disgusting. There was crusted blood of all origins on me along with
sweat from the last few days. Before I could rest in our bed I needed to get clean.

I got up to my feet and walked out to the doorway of the kitchen, peeking out to see what Uta was doing. He was laying on his back still,
eyes closed—

His eyes snapped open when I took a step into the room and I froze like I was caught someplace I wasn’t supposed to be.
“I...I’m going to get cleaned up.” I didn’t have a good reason why I felt so nervous; at least not one that I cared to analyze. Uta wasn’t
looking like he was in much better shape than before. He had blood from his mouth all the way down his chest. Dry now but cracked and
flaking onto the couch.

“I won’t be long.”

“Sure Ai-chan. I’ll make sure not to go far.” His face was blank but his eyes glimmered mischievously. I relaxed some, the nervousness
receding just a little. It’s just Uta. My Uta. There wasn’t any reason to be nervous.

“Better not.”

I sniffed as I entered the bedroom to get some fresh clothing. Now that I wasn’t hungry, Uta smelled good without being tempting. My
human scent though; it still smelled bad. Uta must smell this the entire time. Yet he didn’t even mention it or complain.

I rustled through our clean clothing and pulled out something that would be comfortable. The best comfort clothes were baggy pants
and a tank top that belonged to Uta. I picked out some underwear quickly. Then with them huddled close to my chest I hurriedly
shuffled to the bathroom. I tossed off the clothing I had on, into the corner for now. Perhaps later I might burn them when I get the
chance. I wanted them gone but they had also come from that place so it was evidence.

I turned my head and looked at myself in the mirror again, turning my body to look at the places on my body which were ‘injured’.
Wherever he had bitten there were pale scars on my body. I looked down at myself and ran my fingers over the scar on my left thigh. The
flesh was cratered deeper and the edges of the scars were clearly teeth shaped. It no longer hurt physically; though it was uncomfortable
touching the mark. He had done everything he could to not kill me, and he had succeeded. He had cried while he ate—but this was a
painful reminder that he hadn’t been able to resist. No matter how much he had wanted to. It was a reminder that I wasn’t so far above
food that he wouldn’t eat when given no other choice.

Maybe nobody was.

I turned on the water and climbed in. I flinched and shivered under the cold water at first until it warmed up and scorched my skin. The
blood and sweat washed off me in rivers and streams, darkening the water as it went down the drain.  I stood under the spray and stared at
my hands—

I’d eaten human flesh. I’d eaten a person. A human being, even if they’d killed themselves like Renji said—they’d have a family that
missed them wouldn’t they? Now they’re family wouldn’t even get a body to find.


They’d just be missing .

My hands shook and I bent over, crouching down to the bottom of the tub and letting my tears once again fall; mixing with the blood
and the water.


## ♥



One could only cry for so long before the tears finally ran dry. For now I had cried until a sort of numbness took over. There was nothing
I could do about what my diet was anymore. I had exhausted my options. This was just how it was.


There would be more later. Always more. Tears of self pity. Tears of regret. Tears for the ones that had to die. With a shaking breath I
uncurled myself from the bathtub floor and began to scrub myself hard; likely taking off a layer of skin as I went.

When I dried and dressed myself I left the bathroom. For a long while I stood at the edge of the living room, looking inwards at Uta. His
eyes glazed over my choice of outfit and he smiled faintly. "Ai-chan...stealing my clothing again. How are you feeling?"

"....cleaner?" I said after a few moments. I wasn’t sure if he meant physically. mentally...or if he was asking if I was still in pain? But I
wasn’t the one missing arms or having mutilated broken legs. All my pain was gone . I felt better now than I had in a long, long time.

“Are you in pain...?” I asked softly, lingering across the room from him.

“No. Not particularly.” The ghoul was still shirtless so I was able to get a good look at his bare chest and ‘arms’ as they regenerated. The
regrowing of them looked nearly as grizzly as they had looked being separated from his body. Perhaps after they were off and started
healing it was mostly just an inconvenience to not have the limbs rather than being terribly painful.

“You don’t look good....”

“It looks worse than it is. I’ll be walking around again by tomorrow.”

“And making masks by next week, I’m sure...I meant that you look like a mess. You’re getting blood flakes all over the couch.” I nibbled
on my bottom lip and turned away. I went back to the bathroom and looked around for something to clean with. Eventually I settled on
a few fluffy towels, a fresh bathing sponge and some wet wipes. Next, I was running down the stairs from the apartment so quickly that
Uta couldn’t even comment on where I was going. Peeking through his supply closet until I found a bucket which I rinsed out in the
industrial sink.

Bounding back up the stairs I set the supplies down on the coffee table, save for the bucket, which I went back to the bathroom to fill
with warm soapy water. Uta watched as I darted around the apartment, grabbing what I needed before returning to him. I placed the
bucket beside the couch and hesitantly asked:  “I’m...going to clean you up a bit...Is...that okay?”

The ghoul was staring at me, mouth turned down into a frown and his eyebrows slightly furrowed. “Ai-chan...are you afraid of me...?”


“...No. I’m not. I just—” I paused and really tried to consider if I was afraid of him. He must have noticed the way I stayed further away.
Gave him space. He had scared me when I thought he was going to eat me completely. When I thought he’d be the one to kill me. It

scared me that in the moment I’d accepted that would happen. I’d have to confront that later —but it wasn’t the root of how uncertain I
felt currently . Slowly I tried to put words to the feeling.

“I’m not sure....if you want me to be this close to you when you're so...after...um...” I couldn’t help but wince a little bit, adding quickly:
“I’m not hungry...I feel totally normal. Now. I ate so...I promise...?”

“I know you won’t eat me, Ai-chan.” The ghoul replied. His face relaxed and under the mask he had on a smile slipped out a little. He
leaned his head back to expose his throat. I couldn’t help but to stare at him when he did that. It was something he did so often with me,
but I’d never really noticed it the same way before.  My eyes latched onto the neck tattoo and lingered there for a second as he kept
speaking softly.

“I was worried you would be afraid and want to leave again like before...” He rolled his head to look at me, eyes glancing down to my leg
and then to my arm where the scars were visible. “...I am sorry, Aika.”

I swallowed and glanced at him quickly. He was sorry. He had been sorry even when he’d done it. Even as he took out chunks of skin and
muscle. It was easy to see from this side of being a ghoul how much control was taken away when you were starving .
But even seeing it from this side of the coin, it still hurt...

“I should be apologizing for...”

“...Eating my arms?” The ghoul supplied. I looked away. Yes. That.
“....They weren’t attached. You didn’t hurt me like I hurt you. I understand why you did. It was a good plan...it worked. You should
check with that Doctor to see where your numbers are. After cannibalizing part of me, they might be a bit higher than 1000.”

Would that matter? After I hit 1000, I was a ghoul. That was the end of it for me...nothing after that mattered. “Maybe I’ll have him do
another health check up...see a comparison. He’ll be over the moon to see me again.”



I smiled a little tearfully; liquid escaping around my eyes before I blinked it away quickly wiping them away with the back of my hand.
“Anyway. I’m not going anywhere...You can’t get rid of me now. And it would be really shitty if you wanted to get rid of me now that
I’m a Ghoul...”

“You’re stuck with me...until your Uncle finds out what happened.”

I frowned, not liking the until part of that sentence. “What...? Why until then?”

“Because he’s going to kill me.” I laughed softly, relieved that that was what Uta meant.

“He won’t. I’ll protect you.” Uta’s eyes went a little wide and he turned his head to stare at me with a little gleam in his eyes.
“You’ll protect me...?”

“From my uncle? Definitely. He’s not going to lay a finger on you, I swear it.” Even if Hiroshi was very upset with Uta, I was confident
that I could stop him. Probably just by giving him a pout. I sat myself on the edge of the couch and started mixing the soap into the hot
water.

“So how long is your Kakuhou going to take to heal? Are you feeling okay?” Uta grimaced as though the reminder actually caused him to
feel pain he’d simply forgotten about. Or perhaps the memory of having it ripped out was enough to cause him pain.

“...a day or two before I can use it like normal without it aching. A week before I’m back to full strength. How is yours...?”


How is mine?
I blinked and stared at him with the wet sponge dripping in hand,  not comprehending what he’d just said after he said it. “Mine...?”
Of course I knew I’d have one now. I was a Ghoul and Ghouls had a Kakuhou. Which means...logically I should have one.

“I don’t...know? I’m not sure what I should be feeling. I feel...normal? A bit more energized. I ran up and down the stairs without getting
out of breath...”

“Children don’t have theirs right away....” Uta seemed to ponder it before adding: “One day you’ll use it, and it’ll become second nature.
Like flexing your arm...Then you'll need practice.”

“More training with you then...?”

“...Or Renji. If you’d prefer.” Uta’s face was blank but I saw a slight twitch in his jaw. I think even after everything he would prefer if I’d
practiced or played with him. With my mate rather than Renji. He was jealous, and perhaps it wasn’t because he wanted to fight Renji for
himself. “You really would rather I trained with you...?”

“Yeah...of course.” Uta paused and studied me before adding: “...What if I started sparing and playing more with Itori...?”

He was mine, she couldn’t have him! I hated that idea.









## Oh...
## Shit.

Uta was watching my expression carefully as I realized and reacted. I looked away and grit my teeth. “You were the one to suggest Renji
train me to begin with...”

“He was a better option for keeping you safe, at the time. He trained Ken to begin with. That kid was soft. I thought it was better for my
fragile human to train with him.”

“...can I train with you and Renji? It might help if I can watch you two spar each other?”

“Both of us...?” Uta considered it, and his expression lightened up a bit. He grinned a little and he was likely thinking of sparing Renji
again. “Yeah. That’s fine. Two vs. One is a little unfair—but you and Renji could try.”

“So confident! But I could also practice on my own Uta-kun. What if I don’t need you to protect me now?”

Uta’s grin fell a little and a tiny frown formed on his face before he glanced away. Huh. He doesn't like that, does he? “...That is possible.”

Thinking about that I glanced at his pants with a slight frown. Moving so I’d be in a better spot to take them off I reached to unbutton
the ghoul from his bottoms. They were ruined, ripped and bloodied. The best bet might be to just get rid of them completely. Unless Uta
wanted to try and save them? He was good at sewing so—

“I know you wanted me restrained next time, but is this really the time for that?” I glanced up at Uta’s face, horrified for a second before I
saw his expression. He was back to joking.


“Shut up! You deviant! I’m getting these off so I can clean you up and get you into something more comfortable. Or you can lay around
in your boxers if you want. It’s not like anybody is gonna see you!” I scolded him with a blush on my face. He threw his head back and
laughed; his body shaking with it. I tugged down his pants before I got close to his knees. From there, I was extra careful with him as if he
were the fragile breakable one now. “---Anyway I’m not letting you into bed until you’re clean!”

When I got them off I could see the damage that had been done. Although his legs were still attached and mostly in the right direction—it
was clear they wouldn’t be bending tonight. Getting up from kneeling, I sat myself next to him on the edge of the couch.  I grabbed up
the sponge and soapy water. I soaked it up full and then squeezed most of it out again.

Gently I began to wipe down from his neck, shoulders and chest. When it came to the stumps of healing flesh I left them alone. I worked
down his legs, stripping the blood from his skin. I glanced up to his face as I got close to the wounded area.

“It doesn't hurt unless you try to bend them.” Uta answered my unvoiced question..

“I won’t try to bend you...” I was gentle with him, much more than I probably needed to be. He wasn’t made of china, but he was hurt. I
barely ghosted the sponge over his injuries to remove blood. When he was in better shape he could take a shower or soak in a bath.
We could soak in a bath perhaps...

Setting aside the sponge I leaned over him and wrapped my arms around him. I marveled at how easily I could pull him up to sit upright
much to the displeasure of the ghoul who made a pained groan. “...Sorry. I’m getting propped up so I can get your back. I’m trying to get
all the blood off. It might get itchy otherwise.”

I was quick about it, letting him lay back down as soon as I washed and dried his back with a towel. I threw a fresh one behind his back to
keep him from laying on the now slightly bloody couch. That was something to worry about later. Maybe I could convince him he needed a
new one. There was no telling how many times he’d gotten blood on it anyway.

An investigator with a UV light would have a field day...
....or a heart attack when the couch and room lit up like a Christmas light show.

“Now just your face...”  For this I used wet wipes; gently wiping away the blood, gore and the dried tears from his face. When I was done I
narrowed my eyes, frowned severely at him and leaned a bit closer to him. This earned me a look of wary confusion from the man in front
of me.

“...you look weird without your piercings.”

Uta’s expression relaxed and he chuckled. Briefly he licked his tongue out over the place where he normally had a lip ring. “Mmmm. I
know. I’m not used to not having any. It feels strange.”

“... I could try putting them back in. I’ve done one of your ears before.” I smiled faintly and hesitantly pressed a kiss against his cheek.
“Well...to be more precise I’ve messed up your ear piercings before. A few times .”

“You know where to find them if you want to try. Yours is missing as well, Ai-chan.”  I raised my hand to my ear and frowned, the hole
was gone too. My newly turned ghoul body healed it along with everything else.

“...mmm...Tomorrow.” It was tempting to do it tonight. To rightsomething that had been made wrong and put it back to normal. We
could always just take them back out and try again. We had done that before a few times until he had finally put them in himself. But I
wanted to sleep. Real sleep that didn't have me hooked to a cold metal table and restraining my wrists so tight that my hands felt numb.

I was dead on my feet, feeling the waves of exhaustion finally catching up with me.
I was full. I was clean. And now all that was left was to be warm in bed with Uta.


Grabbing the bucket of water I dumped it in the bathtub to drain and set it aside. Going back I looked over the ghoul, laying in his boxers
on the couch. Clean but certainly not entirely better.

“I’m going to have to lift you to get you to bed...”

“Ai-chan, I’ll stay here...go to bed.”

I was surprised by the instant hurt and worry that surged through me. So much so that I had to bite my tongue to keep from almost
raising my voice and saying ‘no’ aloud at him. I wanted to drag him to bed and keep him safe .

“You...want to sleep on the couch? It would be better for you to go to sleep in a bed. I think...after a few days away...wouldn’t that be
nice?”

“I’m comfortable here.”

“If you want to be in a different room...I can sleep on the couch and you can have the bed?” I offered, the worry that he’d avoid me now
reared its ugly head again.

“It’s not that. It’s just better to be propped up. This is comfortable...”

“Oh...okay...” I hesitantly took away the cleaning supplies, threw out the dirtied wet wipes and rinsed the sponge in the sink. On my way
back out I glanced at him again and swallowed down my worry.

“Goodnight Uta...shout if you need anything...”

“Night Ai.”
## ♥


The bedroom still smells like sick-me. A fact that was making me wrinkle my nose. Gathering all the dirty clothing I tossed them in the
basket; ready to be washed and get the stench out. The bed sheets were next; although I was reluctant to take his scent off as well. I
swapped them from fresh ones and then crawled up into bed. Grasping his pillow I pulled it close and shoved my face into the fabric.

## ♥

## Notes:
She's...upset. But also still a lil' numb.
Getting used to some stuff. New reactions that even surprise herself and understanding the 'other side'.






## Chapter 87:
Chapt er   Text

## Chapter 87:

Uta awoke from troubled sleep in the dark early morning hours of what he presumed to be the next day. He turned his head and could
see the hour on the TV cable box. 5:27 . In the AM judging by the amount of light in the room. He sat up, using what parts of his arms
had regenerated so far to push himself upwards. He turned his body and placed his feet on the ground. He bumped something warm and
breathing on the floor and paused—

Squinting in the dark his eyes slowly adjusted. Gradually he made out the outline of a body. Aika; her body curled up in a fetal position
beside the couch. From the looks of it she’d dragged herself out of bed and lay beside him with a pillow and a sheet for comfort.

He stayed still and just watched her breath softly without disturbing her as the sun began to rise. The light allowed him to notice the way
her face scrunched up as nightmares plagued her. And the way her hand would once in a while reach up and pat gently at him to make
sure that he was still there.

Even unconscious, she searched him out to make sure he remained—
It was cute. Odd and new for her since normally she slept more deeply; but cute.

Uta looked down at his arms and was satisfied to see that his healing had kicked into full gear as the suppressants worked out of his body
completely now. He’d already had the shop closed for...three days? His customers would start to wonder where he’d gone if he went
missing for too long; not to mention some other ghoul might think they could take his territory and he’d have to defend it again. He
wasn’t in any sort of condition to do that.

For now he had one hand at least, though it needed to finish healing to get full mobility and strength back. The other arm was regenerated
to the wrist. When Aika patted the couch again he hesitantly slid his better arm under her hand and felt her grasp it for a second or two
before relaxing. A moment later she released him and settled back into more restful sleep.

He stood up, wincing as he stepped over Aika. His knees bent and they held his weight, though they still felt sore and wobbly. He
stumbled his body towards the kitchen, grabbing the first container of meat he saw in the fridge and cracking it open using his one hand
and his teeth.

Uta tipped the container towards his mouth, drinking down the fluids and chewing on the small cut up chunks of meat that followed.
He ate quickly and gently put the container down in the sink to avoid making too much noise and waking Aika.

He glanced out at the woman on his floor. She was murmuring softly in her sleep, hand patting once again at the area where he’d laid. He
watched as she started to get restless now that he was missing.

Then she began to wake. Aika raised her head, eyes cracking and squinting as she searched the couch for him.

“Uta?!”
Her voice was tired, but so panicked when she didn’t see him right away.

“Right here.” He spoke up and her head spun, looking for him with wide eyes.
“Uta—you’re up!” Her eyes searched him up and down quickly. Her eyes landed on his arms and the single hand that he had back. He
watched as she struggled up out of her nest of blankets and rushed to him. It was difficult to resist taking an automatic step back—

“You’re up .” She repeated, reaching and hovering her hand over his chest and shoulders like she wasn’t sure if she was allowed to touch.
Then she looked down at his knees, examining the wounds he’d received.


Uta took a deliberate step forward into her upraised hands and drew her attention back to his face. He had to show her that everything
would be okay. Aika pressed them closer, flattening her warm palms over his chest and slipping them upwards until she caressed his neck
and up his jaw. Holding his face in her hands.


“I told you I would be. Did you sleep on the floor...?”

“...” Aika looked away and pulled her hands away; a slight flush on her face. “I couldn’t sleep...”

So that’s what it was. He knew how that felt. It had been worse for him when she’d left the house completely for those few days. He
hadn’t been able to sleep at all when she wasn’t in the same apartment.  Regardless he wasn’t going to tease her about it. He was the one
that separated them last night....though it hadn’t exactly worked though, had it...?

“I’ll be back in bed tonight.”

“Yeah?” Aika smiled faintly and glanced back down at his arms again, peering at the pale flesh and frowning. “...It’s strange seeing you
looking so ordinary. ”

Aika reached for his face again more confidently cupping a cheek in her palm. He leaned into it as she gazed at him. “Right before you
passed out your eyes were ordinary too...kind of human. It must have been the gas.”

He felt curious about that. He’d never seen himself with human looking eyes. The idea was about as strange as Aika having ghoul eyes—a
fact that even he was going to have to get used to seeing from time to time. “What color were they?”

“...Sort of...a grayish-purple. It was a soft color. Pretty—but...wrong on you. Like your eyes better like this.”


Speaking of eyes...

“Mmmm...Are you hungry, Ai-chan?”

She had to think about it. He watched her as her mind turned the question about. “No.” She finally spoke. “Renji said I won’t have to
worry about it for a couple days at least. I don’t think I want to eat as often as you do....”

“You’ll have to eat more in a sitting then.”

“I know that...” Her lip trembled and she dropped her hand again. “I just don’t want to hurt anybody...”

“I know. You won’t. Eating more often helps. It’s more...human.” He ate each day for the pleasure of it. Eating in one large meal and
going weeks without was boring. But for her, it would be better for her to keep a normal schedule. To be normal. To eat breakfast, lunch,
and dinner. Plus, she’d get used to eating it faster if she didn’t avoid the subject.

“I don’t want to find food—I can’t, I can’t chop it up—I...I can’t. ” She was beginning to panic. He expected that her upsets would come
and go but it was distressing seeing her so unhappy. Uta leaned forward, reached around her with his better arm and held her to his chest.
“I’ll take care of you. You don’t have to worry about a thing. You just eat whatever you want out of the fridge.”

“I don’t want to eat people! It’s wrong— ” She was crying now, he could feel the tears on his shoulder and smell the salt in them. He
leaned his head on her shoulder and held on a bit tighter.

“...is it wrong for me, Renji and Itori? Touka and Hinami?” He listed off people he knew she cared about. Who else did she know....?


“No, that’s not what I meant—”

“Nico? Nishiki...? That little ghoul girl you saved?”

“No—that’s not—I was Human—I—!”

“Ken? What about your uncle then?”

“No. It’s...it’s...not.” She was losing steam with her argument and her arms wrapped around him, holding on as though for dear life.

“Then how can it be wrong for you to live...? It’s just what we have to do to survive. It’s not wrong...”

“I’ll....I’ll still work towards making an alternative...” She swallowed and spoke softly, sniffling.

“...Good.” Even if it didn’t work in the end. If it all came to naught. That could occupy her mind and alleviate her guilt. She would be
able to look back later and say that she’d done everything that she could to try and help.

## ♥


I stepped out of Uta’s arms and wiped my eyes again and sniffled. I didn’t want to be a crybaby about it, but it just felt like my emotions
would burst from the seams and overflow. Yet, Uta was watching me with a patient expression.

“You think you can put some piercings back in me....?” He asked. A little grin tugged at my lips and I shrugged my shoulders.
“Sure...I think I can manage that. We’ll see how many times I need to try again before I get it right. Don’t ask about the tattoos though.”

He cracked a grin and leaned forward to press his lips to mine. I froze for a microsecond and hated that for a split second I panicked. I
pressed myself forward and kissed back hungrily to make up for that single second. He tasted good...like he had sweet syrup on his lips.

He froze for a second as I pressed closer; However it was short lived. He pulled back suddenly and broke the kiss. “...Why don’t you go
look through my drawer and grab some piercings for me. Anything you’d like. There should be some extra lip rings and curved barbells
for my lip and eyebrow.”

I pulled away, troubled but nodded. “Sure. Are you okay, Uta...?”

“Yeah I’ll wait for you here.”

## ♥

Uta cursed his reaction as she’d kissed him back like that. He’d felt her tongue and her teeth on him like they’d done a thousand times
before. Her tasting him just as he'd done to her just as often. Why was it so unsettling to him now?

He licked his lips as she walked away, getting the piercing kit from the desk below. It was likely she was tasting his breakfast on his lips;
not him. Still— He took a deep breath and forced himself to relax.

He was used to not  worrying about this. She was his fragile human before—weak and depending on him. And he trusted her because
she’d never given him a reason to doubt it.

She still hadn’t.
Not really.

He rubbed his face with his healed hand and groaned. She’d done what she’d done to save them both. He didn’t need her to explain it to
him. But the image of her eating parts of himself, especially his arms with the tattoos he was so very familiar with—the flesh and art
disappearing in between her lips. The way she had moaned around the meat. Then the bones crunching and popping in between her

teeth.

They weren’t really going to eat each other. Neither of them wanted that to happen and he’d do anything to avoid that sort of situation a
second time. But knowing that didn’t erase what HAD happened. He remembered how she screamed when he almost killed her. It
echoed in his ears like a ringing.


“Uta...?” The ghoul lowered his hand from his face and looked up at his human—no, his ghoul mate. She was giving him a concerned
look while she held the small black box in her hands. “Are you okay...?”

“Yeah. I’m still tired...”

She gave him a look that told him that she didn’t quite believe him, but instead of questioning it she moved to sit beside him on the
couch. Aika clicked open his box of quinque steel tools and piercings. “I grabbed a mirror too so you could see. I remember how you
showed me to put them in before...so I should be able to get these back in you. Just have to make sure to get the right angle.”

She was rummaging and finally picked out some for his ears. A good place to start. “Okay...let's see. Maybe this would work better if I
stand or—”

He patted his lap and waited. It would work better if she could sit over him, looking him straight on. She looked unsure for a moment
before crawling up into his lap, resting only a portion of her weight on his thighs. He would force himself and his instincts to trust her like
he knew he could until it became second nature once more.

He gently placed a hand on her back to make her ease down and she jumped ; startled by the touch she hadn’t seen coming.

“S-sorry...I— sorry .” Aika apologized immediately, as though she did something wrong. Both of them would have to learn to trust each
other more again...

“It’s okay...rest your weight on me. It’s not going to hurt me as long as you're not on my knees. You’re going to be sitting there for a
while.”

She did. Slowly. Aika put the box next to them and picked out a piercing. She held the tools delicately and leaned close. Eyeballing the
placement carefully to make it right and then pushing the tool through. The lobes of his ears were easy but she was hesitant to hurt him
so he could feel her pauses as she pushed the tools through. Inadvertently this actually made it hurt just a little more—not that he minded
terribly. Compared to what he was used to—it was just a small pinch.

He looked at each one as she put it in. The first one she missed was an orbital conch. She took it out and waited for the mark to heal
before trying twice more. The third time was the charm and she smiled so happily when he told her she’d gotten it right.

When it came to his eyebrow piercing she marked it with a black marker before putting any holes in his face. He looked it over and gave
his approval of the placement before she pushed the needle and then the jewelry through.

“Perfect. First try.” She beamed.

“Last one is the lip ring.” He licked his lip unconsciously and she stared as he tongue darted out of his mouth for those seconds. “I
promise not to bite, Ai-chan.” Something he’d normally say as a tease but now it was a little closer to home.

“Only if I ask you too, right?” He smiled before she moved his lip aside from his teeth, pinching it and lining up the tool to push it
through.

He liked when she touched him. Aika touched him gently. As though he were made of glass and he was precious. As though he were just

another human and he deserved that gentleness. He’d do anything to keep that all to himself.

Logically there was no need to fear her. No need to worry.

But she wasn’t his fragile little human anymore. She wasn’t Human at all.
She had been. He had just begun to truly accept that she was the one Human that loved him—despite being a Ghoul. Now that was gone
and he wondered why he’d wished for it to begin with.



Once she got her Kagune he’d have to deal with a ghoul who might just rival him one day.

She was still a patch of warmth in the world though. And all his...

‘Be Careful what you wish for....
....You never know what you have until you lose it.’

## ♥


I eyed Uta as he came from the kitchen with a bowl in his hand. His face and ears were all freshly pierced. I knew exactly what he’d gone
in there for but I didn’t want to look at what was in the bowl.

“Here.”

“I...told you. I’m not really hungry.”

“Try one.”

I whined softly, turning my head away as he sat next to me. He put the dish in his lap and picked up one offending ‘treat’ in between his
fingers. “Close your eyes. Try just one and I’ll never bother you about it again.”

“ Please.... Uta. No.” I could see him pouting from the corner of my eye. His reaction was so normal despite it being a very ghoulish topic.
The eyes he had were like...candy for him. He just wanted me to try his favorite kind. I understood that in a different context. Perhaps if it
were a warhead or some strange foreign candy I’d suck it up and try it.

But I still didn’t want any now.
And he was pouting just like a child.

He popped it in his own mouth and chewed it sullenly and I couldn’t help but smile. “...maybe...some other time. Okay? But if you keep
bothering me. Never. Got it?”

“...Okay.” He popped another into his mouth, sucking on it like it was actually candy.


There was a noise down the stairs and I turned my head and sniffed the air. Renji? A few seconds later the almost familiar scent knocked
and then opened the door to the apartment and entered. The silver haired ghoul looked us over quickly and spoke up.

“You're both still in one piece...that’s good. How are you feeling, Aika-chan?”


“Better. A lot better.”

“That’s good...I brought someone to visit you.” I stared at Renji with wide eyes. It was so soon. Too soon. I wasn’t ready to face anybody
else. I might never be. I couldn’t even think of who he might have thought to bring. Itori?

No. She would have barged right in too. (An idea that I have just now realized I hated. For some reason I couldn’t quite place.)

Then who?

“Come on—they’re fine.” Renji had turned his head and was speaking to someone else below him. I heard footsteps coming up the stairs
and tensed as someone much smaller than Renji poked her head out from behind the raven ghoul.

“Touka...” The strangely territorial feeling fell and died as I looked at her. I’d already decided that Renji was like a big brother. That made
her like a niece to me as well. In a way? Kind of?

“Hey.” Touka spoke up, almost sounding bored. Whatever reaction I’d expected from her wasn’t this. She was looking back at me; not
seeming surprised one bit by any changes she might see. Or smell. So Renji warned her and she was really good at hiding her reaction—or
maybe because of Ken the idea of humans turning ghoul just wasn’t so strange anymore.

With that in mind she was the best person to bring.
Perhaps it wasn’t by chance that Renji picked Touka to bring.

“Did...you get your books?” I managed to say through a clenching in my throat that threatened to choke the words from me completely.

“Yeah. Thanks again...I’ll pay you back after I’m done with school.”

“You don’t have to do that.” I had offered to pay for her schooling before as well—anything she needed. “Isn’t it a weekday? Don’t you
have school?”

The young woman scoffed and rolled her eyes. “It’s Sunday.”

“Really...? What’s the date?”

“...It’s the fourth.” Close to three days in that basement lab. Starved and tortured. I glanced at Uta with a small sad frown. We had been
imprisoned on his birthday. “We missed your birthday—we can throw a party again. A bit late though.”

“That’s fine...Itori will be happy to see you. She’ll probably be excited to see you...”

“Excited?”

“...She’s talked about how interesting it would be if you were a ghoul since your uncles.” Uta admitted and Renji sighed, shaking his head.

The young lady rolled her eyes and crossed her arms over her chest. Renji took a step in, taking off his shoes by the door and going to
stand  in front of the coffee table. Touka followed suit, only she sat cross legged on the ground.

“I told Touka what happened. I’m doing the same with the others that were at Anteiku. They’d only know the basics. And only the ones
that knew you. However, it would be best if everyone else didn’t find out...” My expression must have showed my confusion because he
sighed and added:

“After seeing the sorts of experiments that Dr. Kanou had...I think it would be best that nobody ever mention that you were ever

human.”

“The CCG might already know...unless our captor kept that from the CCG too. Or if they didn’t listen...”

“Someone handed in the wrong information and underestimated you.  It happens all the time. That is all they need to know. ” Renji said,
crossing his arms and turning his head to look at my mask that hung on a hook by the door.

“As far as they or anybody else needs to know, Wendigo was always a ghoul from the start. You’re not a one-eyed ghoul like Ken. You can
hide that you were ever human. It would be safer for you to do so unless you’d like to be an even higher priority for not just the
CCG...but other groups as well...”

I already was high on their hit list because of Uta’s wanted status. As for other groups... perhaps I didn’t want to know. “...Okay.”

“Who else knows?” Renji asked.

“Mmmm...Shuu. Tsukiyama...I told him exactly what was happening to me the last time he visited.”

“ That guy...?” I glanced up and gave Touka an apologetic smile.
“He was sweet to come visit me when I was upset. After Anteiku and everything...it’s complicated. Anyway, wasn't he part of Kaneki’s
group...?” If Ken trusted him enough to have him with him, then perhaps Touka might let go of her own grudge. Though, judging by her
expression it was unlikely.


“---Other than him...I’m not sure how much Nico knows. Itori might have told him everything she heard on the trip to see my uncle.”

“Roma...”

I turned my head and glanced at Uta with a frown. “Yeah...she knows too. But she hasn’t found out about this yet. I’m sure she’ll be
surprised. I still don’t want her anywhere near me...”

“She’ll find out sooner or later.” What a terrific day that will be when it comes. Perhaps I’ll get to see her face looking all shocked and
confused right before I claw it off. The room in front of me was sharpened as I glared at a coaster on the table— I could almost imagine
it.

“Ai....” Uta placed his good hand gently on my shoulder and squeezed. I jumped a little, turning to look at him with a raised brow. What?
His eyes were fixed upon mine.

“Your eyes.” Touka supplied. “You need to get in control of that. Otherwise you’ll have to walk around with sunglasses all the time like
## Uta-san.”

“That’s probably not a terrible idea until she’s gotten used to everything. Did you already eat the food in the fridge?” Renji asked. I
frowned and furrowed my eyebrows. I turned my head away, trying my best to avoid all eye contact with the other ghouls in the room.

“I’m not hungry yet...”

“You shouldn’t be, but your eyes—” Renji started and Uta cut him off.

“It’s not hunger.”


I took a deep breath and relaxed. Or tried to at least since I wasn’t sure how to trigger them or put them away save but thinking of ‘food’.
Apparently even a strong negative emotion like hate could also activate them.

I closed my eyes. Took a deep breath in. And out.
I opened my eyes again, glancing at Uta with a questioning gaze.

“You did it.”

“Thanks...sorry...I’ll get used to it. Or maybe I’ll steal your sunglasses too. The round ones...?”

Renji groaned and rolled his eyes. “Aika. No.” I cracked a small grin.
"What Big Brother, you don't want me to be safe?"

"Those glasses look ridiculous, it was bad enough when Uta wore them."

“So you’re trying to save me from a fashion crisis?” I couldn’t help but to tease him. It made me feel better to act normal . “You know,
while we’re helping each other. I’d suggest that you pick something other than a plain white shirt for a date when you finally ask that
woman out. Something purple or blue would look nice.”

His eyes went a bit wider and then he scowled as I brought up his human woman again. He didn’t argue this time though and I was
surprised. Touka glanced at her uncle and rolled her eyes.

“Right.....I’m heading home. I’ve got to study. Thanks again Aika-san...for the books.”

“No problem...if you need anything else for school you know where to reach me. Or you can ask your uncle. Right, big brother?” The
young woman looked flustered and stood up on her feet, shuffling over to the door and putting her shoes back on. After she was really
gone Renji glanced at me and then Uta.

“How are you two really doing...?”

“Fine.” Uta popped another eye into his mouth and chewed it slowly. Renji turned to me and I shrugged.
“...I’m still not sure it feels real yet...” I folded my hands in my lap and looked down at them. “...I knew your senses were stronger. Your
bodies were stronger. But feeling them myself, even just being able to lift Uta—.” I clenched my fist and relaxed it out again.

“...then there’s things that I can’t explain. Like why I had to leave the bedroom to go to sleep next to Uta.” Or how it felt to be hungry.
How hard it was to resist eating. Then there were the jealous or territorial feelings that reared their head and roared so suddenly that it
shocked me.

Worst then the startling moments when I pulled away from Uta was the fear and uncertainty...how much more would I change?
Would he still love me if I wasn’t the same? What if I became unfamiliar and too different from what he loved about me to begin with?

The ghoul next to me popped another eye in his mouth and swallowed it whole. “...It’s going to take some time to adjust...I think I’m
going to stay in for a few more days to finish regenerating. After that we can go running again...take your new strength out for a test
drive.”

I glanced up from my palms and faintly smiled. “Yeah...Sure.”







## Chapter 88: Ghoulish Birthday Party
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 88: Ghoul Birthday Party

Three days. Three whole days of weaving around each other. Laying on opposite sides of the couch while watching movies. Dodging each
other in the bathroom while we brush our teeth. Avoiding being too close for too long. Sleeping in the same bed but on either side rather
than curling together.

Uta was adjusting better I think. If he wasn’t comfortable then he was at least doing a decent job at hiding it. He was prepared whenever
we bumped into each other. He didn’t flinch away or hesitate nearly as much as I did when he reached into my space.

We would slowly relax, touching and watching something on tv or a movie. But then there were times when I seemed to create a chain
reaction. He’d move a little and I’d panic and freeze up. That would make him hesitate and pull away. He gave me extra space when that
happened but what little progress we’d made back towards normal would be swept away all over again.

We would be back to sitting further apart.

He had his hands back. Both of them bending and moving well enough that he went down to his shop to work on some masks. He had
even begun making one for my uncle as I’d asked for before. Among his work he gathered sketches of his tattoos. Apparently he didn’t do
his own tattoos on his arms which made sense since it would be rather hard to get all of it on when they crawled up both arms as they did.
But he had a copy drawn on paper in case this ever happened and he needed them redone. Not something one would normally need to
consider—but for a ghoul who could lose their arms I supposed it made sense.

In the meantime he liked to wear some long sleeves that covered the lack of pigmented flesh.

His legs also seemed to be back to normal. He now walked completely normally: but I still limped favoring the leg with just the surface
scarring. It was slight, hardly noticeable to an unfocused eye. It didn’t stop me from moving better than I had before becoming a ghoul
but the scarring and the muscle weakness on the one side remained even well after I should be completely healed. Perhaps it never would.

“I’m going tomorrow to get these redone.” Uta commented as I slowly walked down the stairs from the apartment. For the first time in a
few days I was dressed to go outside. A place that I’d avoided. A pair of black sunglasses perched upon the crown of my head waiting if I
ever needed to use them. If a human came into the shop for example.

I also hadn't eaten anything in the last few days which felt strange and inhuman. Even so, I avoided it when Uta would hold bits of meat
in front of me, offering to feed them to me as snacks. Each day he was being a little more pushy about it which I am certain was his own
way of being concerned. This morning I’d woken up peckish and had begun to feel panic welling up along with the hunger as I
continued, trudging through the day with a growing pit in my stomach.

Now with evening closing in I was going to have to admit that I was hungry. I know I shouldn’t go outside hungry and the meat Renji
had cooked still sat in the fridge. Available to me the moment I gave in and decided to eat. It would be better than the human meat that

Uta still had. Some of it smelled like ghoul when he pulled out the containers to eat.

“...Ai-chan. Are you hungry? You should eat before we go to the bar tonight.”

Uta held up a small bowl of meat and I turned my head away and winced as the room sharpened into focus. That had become a sure fire
way to tell that my eyes had changed to their ghoulish hue. I closed them, took a breath and tried to think of something calming.
Something other than meat.

“If there’s nothing you want to eat here I can go get you something.” He set down the dish on his desk top and took a bite out, dangled it
over his mouth and dropped it in.

I shook my head quickly: “No...no it’s fine. Don’t do that please...”

I didn’t want to eat at all. But going out of the shop and apartment on an empty stomach, possibly being near people? I couldn’t do that. It
wouldn’t be safe for me. Or Uta. Or the others.

Especially not for whatever poor soul we might run into.
What if I couldn’t control myself?
What if I hurt someone?
Killed someone?
What if I exposed myself or Uta as ghouls?

Too many ‘what ifs’.

We’d been lucky before with our capture. There wasn’t any more room for mistakes like that again; a fact that made me want to leave
home even less. It was safe here. However...Uta had convinced me to agree to leave because Itori would have another little birthday night
for him at the bar. Something I wouldn’t miss.

“I’ll...I’ll eat before we go...There’s that meat Renji cooked me before...” There wasn’t a lot but it might be enough for just tonight to tide
me over. Then I could worry about it more tomorrow. I trudged up the stairs back to the apartment and towards the fridge which
contained Uta’s—and my food.

I knelt down, popped the door open and stared inward. My vision re-sharpened as I glanced around the fridge; stomach clenching and
demanding it’s due. The meat Renji cooked was still wrapped nicely for me, waiting til the time when I would eat it. Picking the plate out
I pulled the plastic wrap off it and tossed it aside.

Even cold and a few days old it still smelled divine.

The door to the apartment opened and shut behind me and I jumped up surprised; as though I were caught doing something I shouldn’t
with the plate in my hands. Uta’s eyes caught on mine and then...he tilted his head to one side. “I’m going to get changed to go.”

“S-sure...” I hesitantly took my plate to the couch and sat down with it on my lap.

I wasn’t starving like last time. Which meant the desire I felt to eat it now was even more loathsome to admit. I didn’t feel forced to eat
yet, but I still wanted to and this time I couldn’t just blame instinct.

I stared down at it for a long time. Long enough that I knew Uta came back from getting around and was lingering nearby. Watching me
fail to eat.

A pale hand reached into my visual range and plucked up the meat from my plate.
“Hey!” I raised my voice in surprise and anger. My body leaped up, a snarl coming from my throat as someone took my food!


A hand collided into my shoulder and forced me back down; shoving me back down onto the couch and holding me there and I
struggled.

“It’s just me—I’m not taking it from you...” Uta’s calm voice didn’t match the otherwise aggressive act as he loomed over me.
“I thought you wanted me to eat it!” I barked, squirming.

“I do...but you’ve just been staring at it instead. Close your eyes.” I narrowed my eyes up at him and frowned dubiously.

“Do I need to get the silk scarf?” Uta threatened and I tried to wiggle out from under the pressure he was putting on my shoulder. He
gripped slightly harder, pushing down harder to keep me still. “Ai-chan?” He leaned close, whispering softly in my ear. “Do I need to force
you to eat?”

“N-no...if you just give it b-back...”

“Close your eyes.”

“Uta—”
“Eyes. Closed.” I shivered when I heard his tone shift a little bit into a growl; deeper and more serious. I was reminded that he was
stronger than me. I swallowed and felt my will power bending as he leaned over me, pushing me into the cushions of the couch and
pinning me there. I closed my eyes, trembling slightly.

“I’m not going to hurt you Ai...just open your mouth.”

“You don’t need to. I’ll eat it without—”

“Open.” His hand lifted off my shoulder but his shadow and presence still weighed heavily on me as he towered over me, breathing softly
by my ear. His fingers moved to grip my chin and pry my jaw open. “Good...now just eat, Ai.”

A small piece of cold meat was placed in my tongue and I closed my mouth around it. Slowly chewing. It tasted good; a fact that was both
a blessing and a curse. “Good...Now another. Open.”

This time I opened my mouth without complaint for the next piece to be placed on my tongue. My face flushed as he kept hand feeding
me, making sure that I ate each bite of food. One piece at a time.

"...I can’t let you starve yourself and I can’t let you leave the house hungry." Uta said gently after he'd placed the last bite in my mouth and
it had disappeared down my throat. His hand still lingered on my jaw, fingers brushing my lips. "You wouldn't be happy if you hurt
someone. So I won't let you...are you still hungry?"

“I don’t want to eat that stuff in the fridge...”

“Mmmm. Because it’s ghoul?”

“No? That doesn't matter...” I paused and frowned, realizing just a few moments after I said it that it was the truth. Ghouls. Humans.
People were people. I knew he killed other ghouls mostly when they stepped on his toes. And he didn’t waste the meat; simple as that.
But eating either one was just as terrible.

“Then it’s because it’s old...?” He brushed his fingers across my lips and peered down at me for a few moments. “Do you want something
fresh...You could take a bite of me.”

“ No!”  I flattered myself against the couch and looked up at him with panic. I wouldn’t lose control and hurt him! Never! I had to eat to

avoid that, no matter what. Uta in turn seemed far less concerned about what he’d just said, adding:  “It wouldn’t be that bad for you to
take a finger or two...they’re not tattooed yet.”

"I...I can't...I—don’t want to hurt you. Ever!"



## ♥


Uta watched her press herself back. Trying to pull away as he held her pinned with his presence. It took a few days to get used to the idea
that Aika was changed now. He’d watched her behavior, her ghoulish quirks she didn’t know how to hide mixed in with her very human
reluctance to the change that had happened to her. He watched her rebel against her new instincts and at times fail to even notice she had
them.

The first few days had felt, in a way, like there was an unfamiliar ghoul in his home and his territory. He didn’t like change; couldn’t
adjust to big changes often. But as the days passed he was able to relax more and she remained hesitant and jumpy. But she was still Aika
at the core. Nothing about that had changed. Ghoul’s were familiar to him.

He gave her space, waiting for her to come to him. When it came down to it he could handle a Kagune-less ghoul even if she had some
self-control issues. He hadn’t been leader of the ward for no reason; young ghouls out of control was a normal thing to deal with once in
a while. He could help her through the change and help her adjust. He just needed to make sure he did it in a way that didn’t break her.

A task easier said than done.

“Ai-chan...You need to trust me. I won’t let you hurt me.”

“I don’t want to eat any part of you...Never again.” Uta ran the pads of his fingers over her lips again, watching her lips part slightly as he
did so. He was sure she wasn’t only being dishonest with him; she was lying to herself as well. It was expected. The thought of biting down
would cross even his mind if she were to do the same to him. He had admitted as much during their interrogation. He just had more
experience with controlling his urges and making sure that thought didn’t become action.

She couldn’t resist hunger. She’d crave strangers' flesh more. Snap easier and would be more easily antagonized into fights; fights that she
might not even entirely understand why she started. He kept touching her lips and then pushed his luck. Putting his index and middle
finger into her mouth and pressed them down onto her tongue as saliva pooled around them.
She could bite down any second...


“U—ta...” She spoke, slurred around his fingers and desperately tried to keep control. And he was pushing it. He knew he was pushing
her restraint to a breaking point. He wouldn’t even blame her if or when she eventually bit him. Her hands were gripping the couch,
white knuckled and shaking from the strain. If anybody else's fingers were in her mouth right now—


“Ai-chan...trust me. You’re not going to hurt me.” He pulled his digits from her mouth slowly and bent down to kiss her now brightly
flushed cheek. He paused to gaze into her ghoulish black and red eyes before pulling away. “You didn’t bite. So you should be okay to go

out now...we’ll get you to try some blood wine too while we’re there. It’ll help with your hunger. And it’s tasty...”

Aika hadn’t ever been scared of him before their capture, nor their other ghoulish friends—but now that she was a ghoul, she was
terrified of herself.

“I...I don’t want to hurt anybody...what if someone else comes to the bar when—” She was breathing quickly, panicking. Their
apartment was a safe place for her. Home turf. Outside of that safety she was nervous. A nervous ghoul could be troublesome...but
tonight he was going to drag her out so she could get some fresh air. Fresh air, some drink and seeing their friends...perhaps those things
might get her to loosen up some. He had made extra sure that Roma wouldn’t be in the area so neither of them would start a fight that
Aika couldn’t win.

“It’s just Ghouls tonight, Ai-chan. Just Nico, Renji, Itori and myself. Nobody else.”

She seemed to think that through and nod. It only seemed to calm her down slightly though. “...Itori and Nico want to see you.” He
added softly.

Uta was fairly sure that Itori would be excited. The bartender woman was excited like he had once been. He still was. But it was muted a
bit with concern over her well being. Itori had sent him a myriad of text messages asking if Aika wanted to go out and have some fun.
Innocent fun; Itori had clarified. Roof hopping and climbing. Sightseeing. Maybe some shopping. That last bit Uta had noted wasn’t
ghoulish so much as girlish. Itori wanted a girlfriend to take out and have some normal woman fun.

Nico hadn’t messaged him past his confirmation that Roma would be busy somewhere else tonight. And Renji had already seen her as a
ghoul. Aika was comfortable with Renji.

“Come on. Relax and get your eyes under control again.”

“Then don’t stick your fingers in my mouth!” She snapped at him a little and he chuckled softly.


## ♥

My heart was still racing as I snapped at him. Everything in me wanted to bite down. Because of hunger; but also for teasing me. For
pushing me and testing me when he likely knew he shouldn’t .

A terrible part wanted to see his face when he realized he’d bet wrong. It was a part that reminded me of how Roma had said that I was
just as bad as them at the end of the auction last time. Maybe I was?

“I’m ready to go...just...” I closed my eyes and took a breath, trying to calm down. His test was just to make sure I was safe to go out.
Right?  But being shoved down and pinned—? I opened my eyes and glanced up at him; my face stays flushed as Uta waits for me.

Still sharp. Uta shook his head slightly and leaned patiently on the couch arm next to me.
“Here. Put some sunglasses on and you’ll be good.” He reached for me again and I froze up like a deer in the headlights. He hesitated and
started to pull back again. In that split second I reached out as quickly as I could and grabbed his hand.

“Please—It’s...fine. Sunglasses are fine...” I winced and cursed myself for always pushing him away. Physically I held onto the hand;
squeezing before letting go. “...Thank you Uta...I’m sorry. I’m giving you so much trouble. I’m trying to be normal .”


I was trying to be like my old self. The one he loved...was I doing a good enough job? It wasn’t fair for me to be upset with being a ghoul
when he never had a choice; known nothing else in his life. I didn't want to show my face while I couldn’t help but throw myself a pity
party.

“I love you.” He said, as if reading my troubled thoughts. He reached for the sunglasses perched on my head, moving just a bit slower as
he slipped them down onto the bridge of my nose. “...You don’t have to try to be ‘normal’, Ai-chan. Just come with us and have some
fun. Itori said she’s got me a present. I’m hoping that it’s a jar of eyes.”

He paused to peer down at my leg. I saw his eyes slide off it with an uncomfortable blank look masking over his expression. “Do you
think you can run on that leg?”

“Yeah.” I answered right away and patted it. “It’s still stronger than...before. When we ran. So even though I haven't in a while I’m sure I
could at least as well as before. I’m not sure how I’ll get on top of the roof though.” We hadn’t exactly practiced scaling the roofs
upwards, and I hadn’t been able to climb like him and Renji. So each time we needed to go up—someone carried me upwards.

“I’ll have to teach you.” He replied with a small smile, cracking his mask and glancing back at my face. He offered a hand to help me stand
up and I took it, letting him pull me to my feet.
“Not...tonight right?”

“Yeah. Tonight.” He had the audacity to smirk.

“Utaaaaaa.” I whined softly. “Please...”

“Hummm? Do you still want me to carry you?”

“No...” I pouted. He had only carried me because I couldn't keep up. “If we’re running there...I don’t need the sunglasses. We’ll be
wearing our masks. And...” I swallowed and shrugged, pulling off the glasses and fidgeting with them before setting them aside on the
coffee table.

“---If it’s just them then I don’t really need them there either.” There wasn’t much point in hiding my eyes from Itori and Nico. They
knew and they’d be able to tell right away. I took a small, deep breath and exhaled nice and slow. The room unfocused and I felt the
ghoulish eye color recede again; a feeling that I was becoming more accustomed to.

“The others can control their eyes better. Can’t they? Make them like this or normal...?”

“Your eyes are normal right now.” Uta tilted his head slightly. “The others can control theirs. Though everyone is affected by involuntary
reactions.”

Right. Others. Not Uta—he had the strange ghoul eyes that didn’t ever turn back. I smiled slightly and shook my head. “Right. Maybe I
should work on that. I suppose I can’t ask you for advice about that.”

His lips twitched slightly into a small smile. “No. I can’t help you with that. Itori told me once when we were younger that it was like
putting away your Kagune...but I never managed to do it. Practicing can’t hurt.”

Practice running and jumping with Uta. Practice activating my Kakugan. And eventually... a Kagune?

Baby steps. One thing at a time. I walked to the coat rack and pulled my deer mask down and petted the soft fur before putting it on,
fitting the familiar soft leather over my face. I leaned down and tied my shoes on tight before nodding towards the door.

“Alright. Ready to go...”

Ready as I’ll ever be...


## ♥


I stared up at the intimidating climb ahead of me and then glanced over at Uta who was watching and waiting. “You can climb it. You’re
stronger now. Just try it.”

“It’s a flat surface! How am I going to climb it?” I waved a hand at the wall incredulously.

“There’s hand holds.”

“Those are fingertip holds at best...” I grumbled, looking at where Uta was putting his hands. Despite the seemingly impossible climb; I
watched as he hoisted himself up. One grip spot to the next. Agile as always until he was far above me and climbed over the lip of the
building.

“Come on Wendy...We’re going to be late.”

“I’ll...catch up?”

I said uncertainty and watched how Uta’s masked face disappeared. Suddenly alone I looked up and down the street from behind my
mask. He wouldn’t go far. He wouldn’t leave me alone. He would—not when I was human. What about now?

‘Wait—’ I wanted to call out but my voice died in my throat as I started to panic. Wait, don’t go. I reached up with my hands and
followed Uta’s path; gripping to the wall like it was life and death. A few feet from the top I felt myself slip and yelped—

Only to be caught by a hand, gripping my wrist and pulling me up over the lip of the building. The masked ghoul let go and took a step
back. “You almost made it your first try. Later I’ll show you how to get up a bit faster by jumping.”

I heard him but I could only stare at him and then the ground as I tried to calm myself down. He hadn’t left me behind. I didn't know
what to say though.

I didn't want to admit that it was my bad leg that had slipped.

I settled for a: “Sure...” I watched as he ran and jumped to the next building, his head turning to see that I would follow and then
continuing to the next. And thus it started just like old times; Uta watching me make each jump across the gaps.

When I made the first large leap I put too much force into it, not expecting to send myself flying across the gap and then some. I
stumbled forwards and fell onto my face; saved only by my outstretched palms. Beside me on the roof Uta laughed.

I turned my head and watched as he did; holding his stomach with one hand and another held his mask where his mouth would be. His
shoulders shook with mirth and I slowly smiled. It wasn’t often he laughed like that.

“I think I pushed off too hard...”

Calming, Uta straightened up. His loud guffawing became his usual quiet chuckle. And just like that Uta moved on without another
word. He picked up the pace. I stood up and gave chase before he could get out of sight. “Hey wait—”


Each leap I made I felt the weakness on the one side and switched things up. Making sure to leap from and land primarily on the good leg.
Each time I caught up, Uta seemed to speed up. It happened a few times before I realized he was testing how fast I could go and upping
the ante each time I caught up to him.

“Hey—Come on! You’re not going to give the newbie a break and just stick with one speed? What if I fall?”

“You’ll be okay, Wendy. You’re keeping up.”

I looked backwards over my shoulder, looking over the parts of Shinjuku that we’d left behind us and then looked forward, leaping over
another gap and landing a bit more smoothly. I was! I laughed softly and smiled under my mask. “Yeah...Yeah I am! That’s cool.”

“Can you go faster?”

“If I run faster than you, how are you going to catch me if I fall?” I said, catching up to him once again. He turned his head. I couldn't see
his face but he reached out and gave me a playful shove before taking off in a new direction, leaping off the roof and taking a less
straightforward and bumpier route towards our destination.

“W-wait a second! Not fair—” I turned and went after him, leaping onto a narrow walkway and wobbling across it. I struggled to keep
up, tripping a few times and getting lost—ending up in an alleyway on the ground following Uta from the ground and looking upwards
as he leapt across the building tops and through alleyways.

I bumped into someone. An older gentleman who stared at me with wide eyes as I spun to face them—an apology already on my lips
when he grumbled. “Kids.” Under his breath. I inhaled and recognised his scent as a Ghoul instantly.
“S-sorry—”

“Wendy.” I heard my ‘name’ called and glanced upwards at Uta who stood over us at the rooftop, watching.
“S-sorry sorry! H-have a nice night!” I turned from the older man and took off again, running up a half wall and using it to climb
upwards back onto the roofs.

Uta had taken off by the time I got to the top but I chased after in the direction his scent led and where I knew we had to get to—Helter
## Skelter.

I jumped down, taking the metal emergency staircase down level by level and then leaping to the ground. I landed and looked around—
left right. No Uta? I waited another minute and paced before pushing the door to the bar in and stepping inside. Itori was grinning at the
bar and Nico glanced up from a glass of fermented blood-wine. “Hey! There she is!!!”

“Did Uta—?”

My question was cut off as arms wrapped around my waist. In a flash of panic I smacked the ‘attacker’ earning a pained groan and they
released me as I darted away from them, pressing myself back against the bar. I watched Uta bend over, holding his nose as he bled down
his face.

“S-shit! Sorry Uta! You surprised me! I was worried when you weren’t outside—I—are you okay?”

“Oop. Hey, nothing a bit of blood-wine can’t fix. Right, U-kun! Come on—Sit and have a drink!” Itori’s eyes barely even left me to look
at her friend, patting the bar top but completely unconcerned by Uta’s wound. Uta straightened and wiped his face with the back of his
hand before grabbing a rag from the counter and wiping away the blood he couldn’t lick up from his face.

“It’s okay Ai...That was my bad.” He threw the rag back on the counter much to Itori’s dismay and took a step closer to me. He took off
my mask first and put his hands on my hips. With a small tug he pulled us closer. “I just wanted to tell you; you did really well...”


I swallowed and held down a nervous twitch as he closed in. My face flushed after I recognised the praise and I slowly found myself
smiling. "Yeah?"

"Kept up with me."

"Here!!! A little welcome gift for a welcome party!!!" Itori pushed a glass of blood-wine in front of me and grinned. "You get a whole
bottle! So just ask if you want more!"

"Welcome party?" I glanced at Uta and he shrugged.
“She wouldn’t stop bothering me until I got you to come out.”


"...It’s a welcome party and also Uta's Birthday — speaking of which !"

Itori leaned under the counter and lifted a large jar, filled with a bunch of eyes, rolling and looking around the bar. Just as he had
suspected. "For you, U-kun!"

Uta reached across the counter and slid the jar towards himself with a small smile on his lips. "Thanks Itori-chan...I love it."

I glanced down at the glass offered to me and tried to hold back a grimace. It smelled good—However I should probably not ask where it
came from because I wouldn’t like the answer. For now I left it be.

Itori, however, seemed eager to discuss the elephant in the room.
"Sooo...?" She grinned and leaned across the bar on her elbows. "Renji said you'd turned Ghoul like your uncle...I never thought I'd see it
myself though. Has Uta been keeping you cooped up all to himself?"

"I...didn't really want to come actually..." I murmured slowly, glanced down at the bar top and my hands folded in my lap. "That...sounds
rude. It’s not that I don't...appreciate the welcome...I—thank you Itori."

“Hummm...it’s a lot to get used to, is it?”

“Mmm...” I hummed softly as confirmation. I glanced around the bar, searching for the familiar silver haired ghoul and found nobody
else.

“Renji-kun will be along shortly.” Itori said softly. I glanced at her and saw she wore a fairly gentle smile.

“You should relax. You deserve it. Renji mentioned it wasn’t good when they found you two. But he wouldn’t tell me everything. What
happened when you two got caught?” She nudged my drink closer to me and I nibbled my bottom lip. It smelled good—

A moment before the room sharpened I felt my eyes change and swallowed, dropping my gaze back down to my lap and closing my eyes.
Perhaps the sunglasses would have been a good idea after all.

“Hey—it’s fine. We’re all Ghouls here. Look—” I lifted my head, watching as Itori lifted her glass and took a sip. Her eyes went ghoulish
red on black as she swallowed her drink down. She smiled and her eyes went back to their usual color after a few seconds. “See? It’s a
normal reaction. Being around Uta all the time I’d think you would be used to it.”

“His are always like that... ” I managed a small smile and glanced at Uta who had taken a seat next to me. “I’m used to his like that all the
time. I’m not so used to...this.” I gestured at my own face and felt my face feel a little warm under all their gazes. “Or the staring...you’re
all staring.”

Uta turned his head away and looked down at the bottle of blood-wine near him, clearly debating drinking some of it himself.
“Ah! Sorry! Sorry! You’re right. It’s just— hey! That one’s not for you U-kun! That’s Aika-chan’s!!!” Itori stopped Uta when he reached
for the bottle of wine and a glass by smacking his hand away. I chuckled softly and reached for the bottle myself.

“If it’s mine then let him have some. It wouldn’t be good even if I wanted to drink all of it myself. Anyway...I know I smell different. I
know everything is different. I don’t want to complain...but it’s hard to adjust.”  I now could tell for sure that one of the female scents on
Renji had been Itori. Nico was a new scent all together.

I poured Uta a glass and slid it towards him. Inhaling deeply I reached for mine, gripped it tight and with a final push I tipped the glass
back into my open mouth and gulped down the contents quickly.

## Delicious.



"Hey!!! There we go!" Itori cheered for me just as human friends might cheer for their friend who finished a shot. I put the now empty
glass back on the bar top and licked my lips clean. All thoughts of where it came from were wiped from my mind as she poured a second
glass from the bottle.

With a wink Itori cautioned me: "A little slower on the next glass unless you want Renji and Uta carrying you home on their shoulders
and puking your guts out."
