## Chapter 89: Marked

I didn’t have an empty stomach per-say when I’d gone to the bar but the ‘alcohol’ hit me like I did. Renji arrived some time after it had
begun to affect me. I saw the flash of silver hair and felt a hand gently placed on my shoulder; my ‘big brothers’ scent was familiar and
comforting—Renji was the calm and level headed one.

“Hey!~” I slurred at him after I drank down my fourth glass of blood. It was taken from my hand before I could reach for the bottle
again. “That’s enough...”

“Hey!” I said in a very different tone, snappy and annoyed and just a touch whiny. I had turned to look at him but the world wobbled and
went fuzzy. And there were two...or three of him to be mad at for taking away the cup.

“...Imouto.” He sighed softly. “You’re going to vomit if you have any more.”

I said a close approximation of: “I’m fine. See?” And then stood up off my stool. When the ground began to rush at me two sets of hands
reached and pulled me back up to my feet.

“ Whoa there ! Alright, I hate to admit it, but Renji’s right. He’d going to have to carry you home at this rate. I’ll have to cut you off,
Aika-chan! You can take the rest home for later—if there’s any left.” The other female ghoul giggled and watched the men pull me back
up right and settle me back into the chair.
“...It seems she likes it! I’ll send you home with another bottle!” Itori said, leaning across the bar to ‘whisper’ to Uta.

Renji stepped behind the counter and started grabbing a few things. It took a minute or two for me to realize that he was making coffee
behind Itori’s bar. It smelled just like Anteiku’s coffee used to. He slid a hot cup in front of me and I smiled faintly and brought it in
front of my nose to smell. “...Thanks.”

I took a sip of it and leaned forward, arms crossed over the bar and laid down my head. Drinking away my sorrow and my stress wasn’t
healthy at all. But it was nice for just a minute to relax again—I felt fairly close to normal tonight. Nico and Itori had stopped staring, and
Uta chatted with the others about information she’d learned here or there. Nothing particularly important to me so it became a
comforting background noise. Hanging out with Uta and the others was familiar enough to my previous times here.

“...I should message my uncle.” I said softly; catching Uta’s attention. “He doesn't know yet...” I buried my head in my arms and groaned.
Truthfully, I was a little scared to tell him. I felt (and perhaps it was silly) that he might berate me for not being more careful. I was
supposed to have been forewarned and more prepared so I could stay human. And I’d failed...

“If you want to visit him then—” Renji started to say, perhaps misunderstanding what I was feeling.


“No!” I shot up from my seat, making myself dizzy. “... No ...I just—I’ll just...hold off on that for now. Okay? Anyway—” I glanced at
Uta and cracked a smile. “Wouldn’t want him trying to kill Uta. Right?”

Then there was the child to consider; how might he react to me being a ghoul now?

Uta paused, taking a sip of his drink and glanced at me. Eyes just a tiny bit wider as he considered what might happen if my uncle did
decide to try and attack him. “I really really don’t want you two fighting...so...maybe we can just put it off for a while. And he can never
know the details of our ‘stay’ there...”

“Speaking of details—!~”

“Itori—leave it.” Renji answered before either me or Uta could.
“But–!”
## “ Leave. It. ”

I was surprised by Renji’s tone. He had been cleaning some glasses behind the bar with Itori, but he stopped and was giving her a hard
stare down.
“Look at you Ren...acting all big brother! It’s cute! Alright, Alright ...I guess it was that bad, huh?” Itori glanced between Uta and I;
clearly wanting to ask more probing questions. But she let it go. For now.

“Let's get you two home...” Renji placed down the cup he had been drying and stepped out from behind the counter.

“I’ve got her, Renji...” Uta said, standing up and pushing aside the rest of his drink. Unlike myself he had paced himself, ready to make
sure we both got home alright.
“It’s fine. I am just making sure you two get home alright. There’s been a few patrols around. They probably don’t like how many people
they’ve been losing lately.”

Uta hummed softly and shrugged. “Alright Raven. Itori—I’ll get my tab later if that’s alright.”

“Sure, sure...don’t forget your gifts!~”

“I’ll get Aika, you carry your stuff—” Renji tried.

“I’ve got her.” Uta replied, stepping closer to me and already bending down so that I could hop on his back.

“Uta—”

Perhaps before when I was human I’d have agreed with Renji. He could have carried me because he hadn’t drunk a single thing. Uta
could carry his stuff and we’d all make it back safe and sound. But now, with an idea of how it would feel if someone wanted to take Uta
and carry him for me—I stepped closer to Uta instead; climbing onto his back before Renji could make his argument that it might be
safer or quicker.

I was going to go with Uta...and that was final.

Renji sighed and picked up Uta’s jar of eyes and my less than half full bottle of blood-wine. He pulled out his gas mask-like Raven mask
and then opened the door to the bar, letting in the night air. Uta pulled on his mask and plucked mine up from the counter. “Here Ai-
chan...”

“Can you go easy...I think I might throw up...”

## ♥


I did not throw up .

I was relieved, because it likely would have just been blood that came up, and aside from that being what I’d drank, just imagining that
made me uncomfortable.

Uta did go easy on the way back home. We mostly moved across the rooftops, but he made sure that he didn’t bump or jostle me; save for
one time when he almost lost his own balance. He had after all, had a drink or two.

I gripped tightly to him, breathing in his scent as I tucked my head against his shoulder. He smelled good—but in a sort of comforting
way rather than hunger. The meat earlier, and then the blood-wine I’d drank satiated me completely for the night.

Back at the apartment Renji stepped inside and looked around. The items he had carried for us were deposited on the table and he
glanced at me; still hugging tight to Uta's back as the goth ghoul kicked off his shoes by the door. “Do you need any food, Aika?”

## “I—”
“ I’ll get it for her.” Uta cut off my reply. Renji took a step back and lingered by the door; backing down and backing away.
“Yeah...just ask if you need anything.”

I felt Uta’s muscles relax a bit and he turned his head to look at me while I was clinging to him still.
“Itori’s just as nosy as usual...Thanks Renji...” Uta said more softly as the other man slowly turned and made his way back down the stairs
to leave.

Renji glanced back over his shoulder. “Don’t worry about it.”

I stayed quiet from Uta’s back, grip tightening on him when he tried to place me down on the ground. Instead I nuzzled closer. He stood
up straight again and slowly walked towards the table, trying to juggle me and the items. He slowly let go of me, testing that I was holding
on tightly enough without him holding onto my thighs. When he determined I was at no risk of falling off he put them away in the
refrigerator so they didn’t go bad and then turned us towards the bedroom.

“Time to sleep, Ai-chan? It’s getting late. You drank quite a bit more than I thought you would.”

“My head is clear again...I’m just sleepy.” More than anything I thought that if I let go, then the distance between us might grow again
into a gulf I couldn’t cross. We’d be sitting at opposite ends of the couch and pushing each other away forever until one of us decided
that it wasn’t working out.

Uta pushed the door to the bedroom open and walked us to the edge of the bed.
“Come on Ai-chan.” I let go of him enough to drop my legs to the ground, holding myself mostly upright. I still gripped onto him
though, holding tight as though he’d disappear if I let go.

“...Please stay?”

“I’ve got to shut off the light downstairs and make sure the doors are locked.” He didn’t pull away, but he made a good point that meant

I’d have to let him go. “I’ll be right back.” He promised as my hands slipped from him and I sat back on the bed.

“Okay...”

Uta paused at the doorway and then disappeared. I waited—seconds ticking by and making me think that he wasn’t going to come back.
My worst fear was that he’d say that he was sleeping on the couch again.

Yet—I could hear him when he came back into the apartment and closed the door behind him, locking it and tossing the keys onto the
coffee table. I listened as his footsteps came back to the bedroom. He poked his head in first and looked at me; exactly where he’d left me.

I felt my bottom lip wobble and he took a few careful steps forward; as though he didn’t know if he should. When he was close enough I
reached for him, grasping onto his shirt and pulling him closer so I could bury my head against his chest. “...did going out upset you, Ai-
chan...?”

I shook my head. Slowly, he raised his hands and placed them on my shoulders. His hands slid over my shoulders, down my sides and
then rested around my waist; holding me to him. I wanted it to be like it used to be. Raising my head I raised my hands, holding his face
in my palms and pulling myself up to press my lips against his.

He froze for a half second. A moment later he reciprocated. But a moment was long enough for fears to worm their way in and whisper in
my ears. Was it wariness? Was it because he didn’t want us anymore? Was it no longer allowed? He moved his hands down my sides and
grasped my hips, stepping forward and pushing me to sit on the edge of the bed. He slipped his hips between my thighs and moaned into
the kiss as he hungrily ‘replied’.

The fearful uncertain whispers were drowned out by my heartbeat drumming in my ears.
“I’ve got to be up early  in the morning, Ai-chan—” He pulled away, murmuring softly in the gap between us.

I pushed forward, cutting off his speech and biting his bottom lip. Shut up; I thought as I gripped onto his shirt and held him close. Shut
up and just stay close.

“Ai—”
“Uta. Please. Don’t leave me.”

The ghoul’s hands tightened down on my hips and he broke the kiss. He pulled me up onto his lap, turned us around and then pushed
me back. I bounced and found myself staring at my fiance looming over me. His eyes were unblinking as he focused. Leaning down he
nestled his head next to my shoulder and neck; speaking gently and full of certainty.

“I will never leave you, Aika.” He raised his head again, holding himself up on one hand and used the other to firmly hold my jaw; making
sure I didn’t look away. “You are mine. Understand...?”

Yes . He had put his mark ( so many marks now ) on me and I was his . "And you're mine..."

"Am I, Ai-chan?" He questioned almost playfully.


"You are." I said a bit more firmly. Though he wasn’t marked as such. A fact that nagged at me and him pointing it out was aggravating
now. I hadn’t been too concerned about it in the last few days, but there had been a gap between us since I’d turned ghoul. And I’d been
too afraid that I’d hurt him if I couldn’t control myself.

But he was walking around unmarked where the world could see. It had been one thing when I’d been human still—but now?
Patrons at the shop.
Other ghouls out-and-about.
Even our friends.

“ You are...” I repeated.
He smirked a little and let go of my chin. “That so?”

I grasped him and turned us over ; flipping him to the bottom and sitting up as I straddled him. Even without resistance I do not think I
could have done that so easily pre-ghoul . I grinned down at him and grasped his shirt; tugging it aside to expose the bare skin.  “Yes.”


He was watching me closely as I leaned down over him; his hands gripping my hips with fingers pressing hard indents into my flesh.
Nosing around his neck I inhaled and sighed softly at his scent; my Uta.
Not food.

It was a relief to not be hungry or tempted by someone I loved. I could see why Uta had always kept himself so well fed...eating each meal
and snacking in between to make sure he was full.

His pulse raced a little under my lips, his breath catching and shuttering when he inhaled. Kissing down his neck and over his collar bones
I moved to a spot on him that mirrored my own bite and opened my mouth. I didn’t think of the rabbit meat— Uta wasn’t food. Never
again.

This was an act of intimacy; not predation. Uta wasn’t a rabbit or a meal to bite into.

He was my Uta. My ghoul. My Love. My fiance. My husband. My mate. My person. Mine.
I cupped my jaws around his shoulder and bit down, slow but hard so that the skin gave under the pressure of teeth and they sank deep;
to the bone. The ghoul inhaled and made a soft choking sound that turned into a moan. One of his hands left my hips and moved up to
grip the back of my head; holding me close as I dug my teeth into him and held on. I could feel his skin trying to heal itself and run into
resistance as my teeth stayed put. I swallowed a mouthful of blood and couldn’t help but moan softly. I let go after some time and
swallowed the remainder.

His face was a sight to behold; flushed and panting—his shoulder ‘ruined’ with a fresh set of teeth marks.
“Like I said—mine .” He released my head, going back to gripping my hips. He pushed me down on him and I gasped softly.


“Uta...I’d almost think you’re a sadist if you liked that!” I meant it as a joke, but judging by the look on his face he really wouldn’t mind if I
bit him again.  “That mark is looking a little light—I could try again?”


He smiled at that, cheeks still flushed but eyes glimmering with delight. “My sweet Ai—”

## ♥


If only she could see her face now.  Eyes ghoulish, flushed face with blood running down her chin. It was beautiful. She would be
horrified—but  he couldn’t help but love the sight. He gripped her tightly to him and ground his hips up against her so of course she’d
know how he felt about getting bitten and marked.

They were married now. Truly linked both ways. The party wasn’t necessary. Plenty of ghoul couples never put together such a thing;
but it would be nice . He was looking forward to it now. Their friends, her family...likely some of her staff. All those curious fellows who
had begun to call him ‘Sir’. Perhaps even Kazuha would come and get to know some ghoul culture as well.

To think he would ever get married! Him! Not Renji—whom he had expected to find someone.
His younger self in those old photos would have laughed at the idea.

But here she was. A miracle.
A human fell in love with him . Had lived her life with him as closely as any couple. Her every breath and movement had been full of
trust that he wouldn’t harm her. She cared for and loved him; doing everything to protect him in her own Human ways.

He had broken her trust. Taking her to the auction had been a mistake—but she was so very forgiving. And he was so very grateful he
hadn’t completely ruined this one good thing in his life.

Then she’d turned into a Ghoul.
It was a new chapter; not a new start.

He shivered; feeling her lean her head back down to his shoulder and teasing him with her teeth lightly nibbling. A teasing threat to bite
again.

He was such a masochist sometimes.
Uta moaned a second time as she dug her teeth in and shifted her hips against him; a delightful combination.

## ♥


I ground down on him and he pressed back, hands roaming and then beginning to pull off articles of clothing one by one. Jackets and
tops first before his hands grasped at the hem of my pants. His own arguments that he had to wake early were already going out the
window as I nipped and mouthed over his skin.


I was relishing that I could still do this without thinking of eating him. I had been so afraid I’d feel too different about everything.
Including him.

Glancing at his bare arms still made me feel guilty . Though, I reminded myself that I hadn't been the one to separate Uta from them. I
jumped a bit when one of Uta's hands brushed my upper arm, feather light as it traced over the scarring. “Does that hurt?”

“No.” I answered, then tried to joke to make light of the more somber mood. “Just...well I think it’s more scarring that we really needed
to be married, yeah?”

“I am sorry, Aika...” He kept touching it, fingers tracing the edge and over the ruined skin. He hadn’t seen my legs yet, those I’d kept
hidden from him. Admittedly I didn’t like looking at them either.

“You didn’t want to. I know that. I...I’m sorry you had to see me eat—Uh...your arms.” I grimaced and broke eye contact, feeling way too
awkward to keep looking at him. The mood was kind of ruined, crashing and burning.

With the moment gone I settled on simply sitting back and just resting on him.”It was the fastest way to turn Ghoul...”

“I know...you could have asked for suppressants.” Uta’s hand moved from my arm to gently caress my face, wiping away a few tears that
started to fall from my lashes.

“Even if he gave them to me. Even if it didn’t make me into some sort of experiment. That wouldn’t have saved you...You already had
your Kakuhou ripped out. That...looked terrible. I couldn’t bear to watch him try again. I just... couldn’t. ” I whimpered softly.

“No...it wouldn't have. Thank you, Ai-chan...”

“...it was already going to happen. I was already healing from your bites...But at least this way it was a choice.” I slid off him and curled up
by his side; throwing an arm and leg over him to snuggle up close. “I was going to anyway...someday. I just had hoped it would be
peaceful then...but maybe it won’t ever be.”

The ghoul made a soft grumbling noise and turned, dislodging my grip and holding me so he could roll us over. We lay with him on top
again, settling his weight on me and nuzzling into my neck to speak softly. “Have you given up? Are you quitting trying to make that
meat, Ai-chan?”

“No...It’s just...” It seemed hopeless sometimes. Everything was against me. It seemed the harder I had tried to be normal, the harder I tried
to make things better, the harder I tried to live well—the world would just shove more trouble our way.

If I had a good day then an even worse day would follow and each new loss was greater than the last. My sense of safety and innocence. My
dog. My friends. My humanity.

“Don’t worry about anything else, Ai. I’ll take care of you while you try and change the world.” My bottom lip trembled. I bit my inner
cheek and squeezed my eyes shut, but try as I might I couldn’t hold back from sobbing fully. Letting go I wailed into his shoulder as I dug
my fingers into his back.

Uta was quiet. Letting me get it all out of my system. Holding me, being both protective and comforting. He was my rock to ground me.
Someone to cling to until I slowly ran out of tears and fell asleep.

## ♥


## Notes:
Oooop. The mood was ruined for sexy times. But recovery isn't done in a day. Lil' by little.

Also yes, Uta might be a little masochistic. (I think we all know he's sadistic at times



## Chapter 90: Gaslight. Gatekeep. Girlboss
## Notes:
(See the end of the chapter for  notes.)
Chapt er   Text
## Chapter 90: Gaslight. Gatekeep. Girlboss


When Uta woke Aika wasn’t at his side.
Her side of the bed—or rather the place nestled beside him had grown cold. He passed a hand over the place where she should be and
closed his eyes; listening. In the room next door he could hear the water running so it must be where she’d disappear too. He turned his
head and peeked out an eye to study the alarm clock. A soft groan escaped him. It was thirty minutes before he had to wake up, but not
enough time to go back to sleep. Not that he’d be able to go to sleep again without finding out what Aika was up to first anyway.

He pulled himself out of bed and ran a hand through his hair. He had forgotten to take the hairband out so now it was a mess. Half in the
band, and half pulled out and tangled. He tugged out the band the rest of the way and dragged his fingers through it until it was straight.
With his hair down he made his way out into the living room. The door to the bathroom was open and because of this he couldn't help
but let his curiosity win.

What was she up to?


He peeked in, watching Aika as she leaned over the sink and stared at the mirror. Her knuckles were gripping tight to the edge and her
face was screwed up in concentration. From his vantage point he could see the moment her eyes turned dark ghoulish red and black, and
the moment they turned back to her usual hue.

"Well done."

He didn't expect the bar of soap to be flung at him, but he caught it and laughed aloud. "Ai! You're so jumpy."

“Don’t sneak up on me like that!” She raised her voice indignantly at him, a flush gracing her face.

“You didn’t hear me coming?”

“I was concentrating!”

He could see that and it seemed to have paid off. Albeit, she made a funny face when she concentrated on her task.  “You can change
them. Now if you just relax when you do it.” Her cheeks flushed darker and she made another funny face, something like an embarrassed
pout.

“I can’t change them at will ...but I’m getting better? I thought I’d practice. So I can get them under better control.” He watched her lean
back over the sink and stare into the mirror. Her face scrunched up into that concentration again and he saw her eyes darken a bit.
However, it wasn’t all the way and they went straight back to normal. She let out a held breath and groaned in aggravation.

“You just need practice...” He advised with a faint smile. “There’s no rush Ai-chan...” He slowly moved to stand behind her, giving her
plenty of time to realize he was there. She didn’t jump when he wrapped his arms around her waist and rested his chin on her shoulder.
“...The rest of your life in fact. Plenty of time . You’ll learn to change your eyes at will. Use your Kagune...”

Aika made an unsatisfied ‘hum’ sound and he watched her face in the mirror. Perhaps a different approach? A reminder that she could
keep doing anything she had wanted as a Human?
“You’ll push your company to do some good. You’ll get better at your art if you’d like. Play music. Sing... You have a beautiful singing
voice Ai. We still haven't gone out for karaoke. I bet I could find a stage for you someplace. There’s some ghoul nights at some clubs...”

Aika seemed uncertain, though her eyes were on his reflection. He had her attention. “...Really? It wouldn’t be like an auction right?”

“I promise. Just blood-wine, singing and dancing.”

“---And nothing like what happened after that one night...?”

Right. The chase through the streets. The night he’d had to murder quite a few investigators in front of her. Then she saw his kakuja . “I
don’t plan on it.” He leaned his head a bit to the side and turned to press his lips against her cheek and down her neck. “How are you
feeling...? Hungry?”

Even before she answered he saw the way her eyes slid away from the reflection, right before she tried to lie. “...It’s not really bad right
now.”

“Then you should eat. Before it gets worse.”

“You’re not going to force me to eat again!”
She tried to shrug him off and he gripped tighter to her. Was that a challenge? With a smirk he chuckled: “ Are you going to eat on your
own then?”


“Yes....I can eat.”

“So...what are you going to eat, Ai-chan...?”

She ran into a problem here, because the only thing left in the fridge was the meat that was nearly a month old at this point. Which, it
seemed, Aika had a sort of limit on how old the meat should be before it was eaten. He had seen her throw away human food that was
only a week or two old in the fridge. Perhaps, there was a difference in standards for the two of them.

He’d have to keep fresher food for her.

“I...don’t...”

He wasn’t going to be cruel to her. He’d only tease her so much. “I’ll get you something.”

“Uta... please...” Don’t kill . He knew she didn’t want something that he’d killed himself. Instead she would rather have meat that decided
to leave this earth. He knew of some places that Renji-kun had shown him before. He would look and he would hopefully find
something fresh for her. He wasn’t sure he could do that consistently though.

Although Renji may not have told her; but even the Raven sometimes had to hunt for his food.

So did all Ghouls.

“Stay here and keep practicing with your eyes. I’ll bring something back and prepare it...” He leaned back, pulling her with him as he tried
to get eyes on a clock. “---I have time before my appointment.” Leaning down to her ear he spoke softly. “ And you’ll eat it. Won’t you,
## Ai-chan? ”

“Y-yeah. I’ll eat.”

## ♥



He prowled the streets, passing by others looking for their marks or other means to get food. Many of them either greeted him or skirted
out of his way. He found an unfortunate victim that had likely jumped from the bridge above...however. Here he ran into a small
problem. There was already another leering over the body and pulling chunks from it.

Normally this wouldn’t be such a problem; someone eating the scraps while he hunted in his territory never bothered him much before.
## However...

The ghoul turned, scrambling up and stumbling back a few paces as he approached. Uta glanced down at the body and scowled behind
his mask. The other ghoul had already done a number on it. If anything older than a few weeks was out of the question; so was anything
‘half-eaten’ by some stranger he imagined.

He might call her a picky eater.
Tsukiyama and Aika actually did have something in common.

The ghoul that had been eating the corpse was very young. Fifteen? Sixteen? Probably newly out on his own since he was eating scraps
from something he just found under a bridge. Although he could easily take care of this; Aika would be angry if he killed the boy over the

meat. “Don’t hunt here again.”

“Y-You’re No-Face...I thought. S-someone said you wouldn’t care about these sorts...?”
Uta did not want to explain that it wasn’t for him; but for his mate. Thankfully, all he had to do was stand still and be quiet and the
younger ghoul got nervous and backed off a few more paces.

“...Take that with you.” Uta finally pointed at the corpse before turning and walking away.

....what now?
She would be actually pissed if he shoved food she actually didn’t want into her mouth. So forcing her to eat the older meat was out of the
question. He’d finish that later today after his tattoo appointment and make room for what he brought back today.

But he couldn’t go back empty handed. She needed food.
And he did not want to ask Renji who was more experienced with this sort of ‘hunt’.

Would she actually know if he hunted and killed something...?






He brushed away the thought as soon as it occurred to him. Uta knew it would be a terrible thing to do to her. If, or when she ever did
find out she’d never trust him again with food—with anything perhaps. He’d already broken her trust once before and he wasn’t eager to
do it again.

Uta took out his phone and frowned down at a familiar number.
## ♥


I looked up at the doorway as Uta walked back into the apartment. Renji followed close on his heels. They both carried bodies over their
shoulders, wrapped in sheets.

“Renji...?” I glanced at Uta and watched as he dropped the bundle to the ground with a loud thump.

“...I was having some trouble finding something for you. Renji helped...”

Oh. Oh...Uta didn’t seem happy that he hadn’t been able to find something on his own. I glanced at Renji who seemed to feel the tension
and placed down the second bundle near the first. They both looked a little scuffed . They’d gotten into some kind of altercation? I could
smell blood on one of the bodies—and one of them was a ghoul. “You two get into a fight?”

“Nothing I couldn’t handle.” I wasn’t going to question him further; he’d likely be the one eating the ghoul he’d killed.


Renji on the other hand cleared his throat and spoke: “I just showed you another spot since someone took the first. But...I’ve got
something else to get back to.” He nodded towards me and took his leave.

“Wait—” Renji did, glancing over his shoulder and re-opening the apartment door a bit to see what I’d called him for.
“Do you think—we could start training again next week?” Uta stood still, mask not slipping an inch but listening close to what I said. I
continued, adding: “ But ...Uta comes with me. Both of you could train me now that I should be able to keep up.”

Renji glanced at Uta first. I watched Uta and waited. His posture was more relaxed after I mentioned him going to the training. I had
remembered what he’d said about going and playing with Itori for sparing— absolutely not. It wasn’t her fault, but even Uta mentioning
an imaginary situation had made me want to claw her face off.

I was not used to being this possessive. I was going to have to get a handle on it...I couldn’t even imagine what Uta had gone through.

If he were weaker than me? If I were responsible for protecting him? I’d be out of my mind anytime he was out of my sight.

“Yeah. Next week sounds good to me. You pick the days, Renji-kun...we’re flexible.” Uta mentioned, looking down at the two wrapped
bundles on the floor. “Ai...do you want to go to the bedroom?”

“I’m...going to—” I hesitated. “I’m going to go out...”

“Out...?” Uta watched me carefully as I thought it over. It would be the first time I’d be going out of the house by myself, and only the
second time since going ghoul.
“...Yeah. I’m going to the craft store. And maybe some other places.” I tried to think of some things that would keep me out for a little
while. “I never realized how strong that one soap I have is...and we’re almost out of toothpaste...I should probably buy some groceries.”

I faintly smiled at Uta’s inquisitive expression. “I still have to buy food Uta...it would look strange if I suddenly wasn’t. If anybody goes
through my finances It would be important that it looks as normal as possible...and being an owner of a company—that could happen.
I’ll keep some here for aesthetics so we’d pass inspection. Stuff that won’t go bad soon—then if there’s any homeless in the area I could
always hand it out.”

Uta’s expression relaxed and he nodded with a simple: “Ah. Yeah. That’s true. Are you going to be okay alone?”

“....I—-Yeah. Yeah I’ll be fine. I’ve got to pick up some materials for a mask too. Something that’s smaller and pocket-able? I’ll have my
phone on me. So if you get worried....” He might worry the moment I was out the front door—but...

I gave him a thumbs up and smiled. “I’ll be fine.”

“Right. I’ll take care of this quickly.”

“I could go with you.” Renji mentioned, glancing at Uta and then myself.

“I’m not a kid, Big Brother. I’ve got shopping handled. Go back to your kitten.” I walked to the door, stopping to slip on shoes and lean
in close to the silver haired ghoul. He stared at me when I inspected him. Leaning closer and closer...I finally plucked a stray piece of fur
off his coat.

“Cat!~”

I smirked when I saw a faint coloring cross his cheeks. I stepped around him and trodded down the stairs. “I’ll be back, Uta-kun!~”


## ♥


At the start I was nervous being out on my own. But I was curious as well. Now as I passed people in the street it seemed I could better
pinpoint who was Human and who was Ghoul. At first I was careful, giving people space and walking around without breathing in their
scents. But as I walked and I got used to being out in the sunlight again I took a breath in. Slow and careful.

I could smell how everybody’s scent mixed and mashed, human foods, gasoline and a million other unnameable things crushed into each
other to make one overwhelming sense. My eyes watered a little but the good thing was that no particular human stood out as tempting
to me. The hunger hadn’t gotten that bad yet and I was in control.

The craft store was first.

I wandered the store aisles and slowly began to sink into normalcy. Picking through canvases I picked up a few that I could try to put
something new on when I had some free time. Between working on paperwork. Which...I really should get back to working on. I’d
already been having my pity party for a little while. Kazuha hadn’t been pushing me—But the world wasn’t going to change itself. And if
it did, it wasn’t necessarily in a better direction.

As I looked through fabrics, leathers, furs and many, many other materials: I found myself humming softly. I picked out some leather,
some fabric, some clay, some foam and a few other items and piled them all onto the checkout counter.

The woman behind the counter looked over the mountain and smiled cheekily. “Uh...big project?”

“ Yeah ...kind of? I guess a few projects. I’m not sure what I want to do yet. Time got away from me and I kind of grabbed anything I
liked.” I smiled sheepishly and paid for my items. With a large bag in one hand I walked towards the grocery store. I wouldn’t need
much—just enough for appearances.

Walking through the store felt familiar and foreign. I looked at the food and couldn’t feel the same hunger that might have drawn me to
buy the colorful apples or steaming pies.

The smell of the items was off putting and only the colors seemed to stand out to me—like art. I could kind of see what Uta had said
about my human food.

The grocery store had a small selection of soaps, but all of them smelled strong and made my nose crinkle up and made me want to sneeze.
Toothpaste was toothpaste—and I grabbed a tube of it for both Uta and myself.

All in all; I didn’t linger long in the grocery store.

Which meant I was headed home— early. When I entered the shop I started putting away some of the art supplies. There was shuffling
above and I glanced up at the doorway when it cracked open and ghoulish eyes stared down.

“Got home early...I thought it would take me longer but I just picked up some basic stuff from the grocery store. Some cans and stuff.”

“I’m not done, Ai-chan.”

“That’s fine.” I went back to putting away some of the items I’d bought.
“I’ll stay down here for a bit. I’ve got some things to work on. I think I might try to plan out my own mask? You can help me later with
it...?” He’d let me work on enough over all this time, that I really thought I might be able to pull off my own. Something small and basic.

“Okay. I’ll tell you when I’m done.”


Sure. I didn’t get to say that, the door was already closed when I opened my mouth. Seconds later, music played from the upstairs,
drowning out any noise that dismembering bodies might make. “Okay...maybe. The best bet would be to start with drawing?”

## ♥


When Uta finally climbed down the stairway I was leaned over the desk; drawing abandoned and working on what I felt would be best.
On the desk in front of me was a leather mask base for just my upper face. In my hands I was kneading small lumps of clay into shapes
that would serve as my horns once they dried and I could fit them into their final home on the leather mask.
Horns I decided were a staple of my masks.

My antlers on my first and the curled ram horns on the next. Even this new mask would have small little horns—

I tried not to jump when Uta’s hands touched my shoulder and he leaned over to watch what I was doing. He silently watched for a
minute and I glanced up. “You’re doing good...I’ll be back in a little bit. Do you want to watch the shop for a while, or do you want me to
close...?”

“I can watch it. If anybody needs something I know I quickly measure them and have them fill out an order form. If they need something
fixed I’ll take the mask, fill out a contact sheet and tell them a week if it’s minor. For major fixes, it could take longer and you’ll give them
a call back when you're in the shop.”

Uta’s mouth curled into a soft smile and he leaned close to brush his lips and nose against my throat. “Good...It might be a little while.
You can close up if you get tired.”

“Don’t be out too late...”

I watched him leave but quickly bent back over my work.

The hours passed quickly as I crafted my mask. A few times someone walked in and looked around. I put down my work and greeted
them cheerfully; offering help if they needed it. Two humans. Three ghouls. One ghoul needed a quick fix—I took in the mask and took
down their information before they were on their way again.

Finally, when I was close to closing time the doorbell rang and I turned the chair around to greet the person— only for my words to close
up in my throat.

“Hey Man—Oh...Hey! Is Uta-san in? He wasn’t a week or so ago. The place looked closed down when I tried to bring him his usual
delivery.”

I wracked my brain for his name and then slowly said: “You are Umi-san...correct? Uta introduced you last time. You’ve got eyes for Uta-
kun again?” The man seemed to hesitate, staring at me real hard as if he were confused or uncertain.

“Yeah...you're his cute chick he had around last time...aren’t you?”

I swallowed nervously, remembering that in the not so distant past Uta hadn’t been so shy about letting some of his customers and locals
know I was his . That I was Human and I belonged to him. “The same...something wrong?”

“Uh...no. I just thought—” I sympathize with him a little; it must be quite the mindfuck. I lifted an eyebrow and reached a hand out for
the brown paper bag he had in his hand.
“Thought what—? Here let me have that. I’ll put it away for him later.”

“...uh—sure. Sure.” Umi seemed to still be caught up on me smelling different. I frowned and shot a short glare at him.

“Problem?”

“No...sorry. Was there anything you’d be interested in ordering? I guess I never asked before...” Probably because I was Human and he
had known it. Now the poor man was confused and re-thinking what he thought he knew.

## Gaslight. Gatekeep. Girlboss
I had to go with what Renji said. I had to play it cool. As far as he needed to know he had just been stupid to not notice I was a ghoul
before. I had always been a Ghoul.

“No thanks.”

“You sure!?~ I can get you anything special you might want!” He seemed to have gotten over most of his own confusion and was now
playing salesman . Perhaps to make up for his ‘mistake’ in our earlier interactions.
“No—I think Uta wouldn’t be happy if I let someone else bring me food!~” I watched the man’s grin drop and he nodded.

“Yeah. Sure-sure. No problem. I get’cha. Let him know I was by with those and have him gimmi’ a call when he wants more.” The man
waved over his shoulder as he left the shop. I wanted a minute and then let out a long sigh as my muscles all relaxed.

That...was close.

## ♥


When Uta returned home to his shop and pushed open the door he found Ai-chan at his desk. She was sleeping, her head resting on her
arms folded in front of her.
Nearby was a nearly finished mask. He picked it up and turned it about to examine it. It was decent and he could see she’d used
everything he’d taught her and a few things she must have noticed him doing with the masks while she watched him work. Her stitches
were small and neat. The cuts were concise without wavering. Better than his very first masks when his hand had been unsteady. It was
small and flexible; she could put it in a pocket even with the small horns poking out of the leather as if they grew from it. From the smell
of it she’d fallen to sleep waiting for the glue to dry. It needed some finishing stitches.

He was tempted to finish it for her—but he set it back down and reached to pull her from the chair and carry her up the stairs.

She’d want to finish it for herself.
Her very first mask made completely with her own hands.

He seated them on the couch and laid back, letting her shift in her sleep and nuzzle close as he put something on the TV to watch. His
newly tattooed arms were already healing the ink in and setting. They itched a bit but he resisted scratching. His artist had done
this...three times now? For different reasons in the past. Sometimes it was simply a touch up—other times he had lost a limb or a chunk
out of his arm. However, it had never been both at the same time until now.

He turned his arms around...double checking that everything was accurate to how they had been. The shapes were burned into his
memory by now. The familiar art was comforting to have back.
The woman in his arms shifted and he wrapped his arms back around her and watched her mouth twist into a small smile.
## ♥

## DOGS & GIRLS & GHOULS
## MASTER INTEGRATED CANON REFERENCE — EDITABLE WRITING FOLD

Includes Rules, Character Continuity, Relationship Development, Worldbuilding & Writing Directives
## —

## MASTER FILE PURPOSE
This is the working canon document for Dogs & Girls & Ghouls. It is not intended to function as simple
chapter summaries.
It should preserve:
●  chronological events
●  scene-level continuity
●  character knowledge
●  relationship progression
●  emotional consequences
●  callbacks
●  objects and symbols
●  injuries and physical changes
●  Ghoul biology
●  CCG knowledge

●  unresolved mysteries
●  future setup
●  dialogue/voice consistency
●  changes in character behavior
●  consequences that carry between chapters.
Canon hierarchy
## PART I — CORE STORY PREMISE
Aika Kaneshiro is a Human woman who escaped her wealthy and controlling family and eventually became
part of the world surrounding Anteiku and Uta.
Her relationship with Uta begins with curiosity and familiarity and gradually becomes deep romantic
attachment.
The story does not reduce their relationship to:

●  Human saves Ghoul
●  Ghoul fixes Human
●  Human becomes a Ghoul
●  Ghoul becomes more Human
●  one partner abandoning their identity for the other.
Instead, the central relationship remains:
Two people from fundamentally different worlds choosing to understand one another without requiring the
other to become something else.
Aika retains her humanity. Uta retains his Ghoul nature.
Their differences remain meaningful.
Their relationship develops through trust, proximity, ordinary routines, danger, humor, physical affection
(sexual and emotional), artistic exchange, and increasingly honest knowledge of one another.
## —
## PART II — FOUNDATIONAL CHAPTER CONTINUITY CHAPTERS 1–20 — RELATIONSHIP
## FOUNDATION
## Chapters 1–4 — First Encounters
Aika encounters Uta through his mask shop, HySy ArtMask Studio. The initial relationship is:
Customer → strange artist → recurring acquaintance.
Aika requested for her mask in bone, the animals she hunted in the mountains with her uncle she kept the
display bone collection that she hunted.
After that two days later Aika begins repeatedly visiting the shop and bringing Uta coffee and donuts not to
hurry the mask but because she wants to and plus shes excited for it and also to apologize for her dog .
Uta becomes interested in her because she is unusual, observant, and willing to interact with him without
immediately trying to understand or categorize him.
The Wendigo/deer-wolf mask develops from their artistic connection.
Aika’s dog Bjorn is established early.
Aika eventually becomes connected to Anteiku.
## —
## Early Aika / Uta Dynamic

Uta initially views Aika primarily through curiosity.
Aika sees Uta as strange, unsettling, talented, and increasingly interesting. Their relationship grows through
ordinary repetition:
●  coffee
●  mask work
●  conversations
●  visits
●  artistic exchanges
●  proximity.
Uta’s attachment develops gradually.
He does not suddenly become emotionally conventional. His affection remains expressed through:
●  proximity
●  observation
●  remembered details
●  physical contact
●  protection
●  teasing
●  artistic gestures
●  allowing Aika closer into his private world.

““Oh, don’t worry. I’ll be with you so nobody will think to do anything. I promise!” He took a step forward
to reach for an arm until I took a step backwards and Bjorn growled louder at the ghoul. The purple haired
Gourmet ghoul paused seeing that I moved backwards away from him.
For half a moment I thought I’d made a horrible mistake. For a split second Shuu’s facial expression flashed
to a grimace as I moved away from him.
“Shuu.” I said firmly. “Sorry. Someone’s waiting for me.”
“Oh?” I froze when I could see he leaned forward and down to take a few sniffs in my direction.
“Ah. I see. The mask maker. You two are rather close.” His friendly tone dropped off a little and his nose
wrinkled as he looked down at me, no smile on his face now. “His scent is all over you. I heard some
rumors...but I hadn’t really thought...”
I took another step backwards and stared up at my old friend. “I always wondered where you went, Aika!
For those years where you hung out with me and we played games; you were mine. And then you
disappeared. Completely stopped coming back to see me. Can you imagine how that made me feel?”
“I realized afterwards when I met another girl why I never felt like eating you back then. You see, you were
a cute little pet! You Humans keep pets and don’t have any desire to consume them. Even if they are
animals other people might eat...”
“Shuu...you’re scaring me.”
“...and now you’re still alive. My long lost pet!” “Tsukiyama.”
I flinched back further as I heard someone’s angry tone fill the air. My goth ‘hero’ appeared - phone in hand
and a scowl on his face.
“She’s mine.”
I reached for Bjorn’s collar and pulled him with me despite his resistance; getting further away from Shuu
and back towards Uta.
They’d been right all along about Shuu even when I’d wanted to not believe them. Shuu and I had had fun
back then; that much was absolutely true. But the ghoul didn’t look at me as anything but a pet that he lost
track of...he’d made that perfectly clear a few moments ago. “Ah, Princess. You didn’t need to call for
help...I told you I never felt like eating you. I still
don’t.” Regardless he looked on guard now that Uta showed up and let me move away from him towards
Uta’s side without any attempts to stop me.
“You okay?” Without removing his eyes from Tsukiyama; Uta asked as I got to his side and put myself
slightly behind him. Protected.

“Yeah...I’m fine.” I said softly. I felt emotionally hurt and a little bit like crying; however I was physically
unharmed. I wasn’t even sure Shuu had actually been a physical threat to me at that moment.
But I hadn’t trusted him enough to find out.
Uta had probably heard everything since I pushed ‘call’ through my phone. He’d found me pretty damn
quickly too.
“Je suis désolé.” The gourmet held up his hands in a cheery submission I found peculiar. It was like he
didn’t want to show he was on guard or nervous; but didn’t want a fight. “I’m sorry. I’m not here to steal
your property Uta-san!~I guess my lost pet has found a new home. Take care of her for me, would you?”
“...get lost.”” ,

Aika brought it up to Uta after that moment when at her apartment outside the door.
“Can I come in then?”
I did a quick mental check to try to remember how messy my apartment was. I remembered that it was actually a huge mess. I needed to
do laundry and clean up a bit. “Actually...no. I’ve been so busy I haven't had time to clean up any...”
“Oh. Alright.” He replied, he still cocked his head to one side to try and peek around me though as I let in Bjorn.
“I’ll see you tomorrow, Uta?”
“Yeah. The store will be closed tomorrow...I’ll leave the door open for you. Just come in.”

“Alright...” I almost left the conversation there and retreated back into my safe and cozy apartment.
But there was that nagging question I’d had since I’d run into Shuu.

“Uta?” He stopped and looked back at me; eyebrows raised as I called out to him. I was afraid of the answer I might get, but I also
couldn't let the question fester like a wound in my mind.

“...do you think I’m a pet? Or property?”

## Chapter 19:

“A pet?”
I dropped my gaze away from my friend. A person whom I had grown close to, cared for and hoped they thought of me the same. At the
very least, not like Shuu.

“Shuu said I had been his ‘pet’ in the past. Then you said: ‘she’s mine’’ a few minutes ago. Other Ghouls referred to me as ‘yours’. Even
that friend at the bar implied both that I was a pet and that he was surprised I was still around because he assumed you would have killed
and a-ate me by now...Even when people don’t really say what they mean. That doesn't mean I can't hear it behind the coding...I'm not
stupid and it's not going over my head. I understand perfectly what they mean to say.”
“--I’m not property. A toy. Or a pet...” I muttered softly. The butterflies in my stomach had to be put to a stop if that were the case. If
that was how he actually thought of me then I’d have to catch and stomp out the life from each and every one of them.
Or I’d be completely doomed; hopeless.
“You're...”
“...a friend.” Uta said in a quiet tone after a moment of hesitation. The pause confused me a little bit and I looked up from the ground.
He’d walked back towards me; but stopped a comfortable distance to give me space. The distance gave me the option to retreat into my
‘safe’ house. “You’re MY friend. You know perfectly well what I am Ai-chan, and you live in my territory. If other Ghouls know you are
‘‘mine’ then you're safer from them...”
“So saying I’m “yours”; it’s just...ghoul politics?”

“Something like that...”
I chewed my lip; watching him while he calculated my own responses.
“Ai-chan...If you want to talk more about this, can we go inside?” Uta said, looking up and down the road. It was quiet but that didn’t
mean that there weren't any extra unwanted pairs of ears listening in.
I nodded my head in agreement since I understood his worry. Our conversation wasn’t over though.
“My house is a mess...”

“Then come back with me.” He nodded towards his shop and home.
It wasn't like I didn’t feel comfortable going with him. Uta harming me wasn’t a fear that I had much in my mind recently. But if I went:
"I'd have to walk back in the dark, Uta..."


“Stay overnight. My couch is yours when you want it. Bjorn can come too if you want. I don’t mind.”
I looked back into my apartment at Bjorn who watched me expectantly. I had to feed him. I debated it internally and then nodded.
“Alright, can you wait here while I get him some food?” The dog behind me wiggled more vigorously when hearing ‘food’ and knew I
meant for him. Despite the tension seeing him wiggle like that made me smile a little bit.
“Yeah. I’ll wait.”
I ducked into my house, closed the door and leaned back against it, letting out a long tired sigh. I’d asked him. I’d actually just blurted out
that question! His response hadn't entirely answered any of my questions entirely. However, he HAD called me a friend. That was
enough to soothe me just the smallest bit. I got Bjorn’s food from the fridge and dropped it into the doggie bowl. I took my time to wait
around as my heart calmed down back to a normal rate.
So it was ghoul politics and he was being...territorial and possessive. That was all. Ghouls could be like that. He'd told me as much before;
hadn't he? Experimentally I sniffed my shirt’s shoulder. Was it really that obvious to other Ghouls? I didn’t smell a thing but Shuu had
looked downright offended when he smelled Uta on my person.
So was Shuu’s claim that I belonged to him all that different from Uta’s? Then there was the way that Shuu had backed off instantly after
the goth appeared on scene. What made the other ghoul back down? It seemed submissive in a way that was so completely unlike the
Tsukiyama I knew. If I could even still say I knew him. Obviously I’d missed the mark when it came to that particular man.
I just didn’t want this to repeat with Uta. I did not want to sit here thinking we were close, to care for him or worse; let feelings develop
only to find out he thought of me as just something interesting to play with and got bored

I’ll give you the direct convo since it’s a long chapter.
He picked up the dish and brought it into his kitchen where I heard the fridge door open, he placed his ‘snacks’ away and closed it again.
The ghoul came back empty handed. "Thanks."
"No problem..."
For a few moments he stood there silently, staring at me as I fidgeted. How should I start?
"Ask your questions. And then I'll ask you some of my own. Fair?" He said, breaking the quiet moment. He sat down on one end of his
couch and lounged out comfortably while I stayed standing and fidgeting. He patted the couch with a hand, trying to get me to move to
sit down and get comfortable. But I remained where I was and shuffled my feet about.
"What does being my 'friend' mean to you? Shuu...I thought he was a friend. At times he said I was. I never realized he only ever saw me as
a pet or plaything..."
“...and the only reason he didn’t want to eat me was because he thought of me like that. I guess I’m the stupid one because you warned
me about that...”

I wasn’t brave enough to lift my eyes to look at the artist. Friendships between Ghouls and Humans. How was that supposed to work
exactly? I thought we had been doing a good job. But there were so many worries that still plagued me at times. It was getting worse for
me now when I didn’t know how to feel. I’d feel myself getting closer, leaning in and letting him get very near whenever he wanted. That
sort of thing was getting familiar and sometimes I completely forgot that he was technically from a totally different species.
For a Human I thought being close to a Ghoul meant acceptance that they couldn’t change. They had no power over what they were
anymore than I did. Humans and Ghouls both were assigned a role when they were born. I accepted that we were both living, breathing
and thinking creatures. They had some more...primal instincts; But that didn’t mean they were monsters.

In most respects, from what I could see - they were not much different from Humans.
But more than just acceptance of his nature, being around him in the ‘Ghoul’ side of the world meant I would be in danger. Other
Ghouls might look at me like I was a pet or plaything, because to them being FRIENDS with a ‘meal’ would be unacceptable.
And the line between ‘meal’ and ‘human friend’ might be a little thin.
“You still smell delicious...There are some moments I’ve looked at you and wondered; What would you taste like?”
Uta hesitated when I flinched under his gaze. This wasn't where I thought this conversation would go at all. I hadn't quite gotten over
being teased - or told the brutal honest truth - that he could eat me. "But I'd miss you if I did that. Or if I let someone else take you
away..."
"As for Nico....You can ignore him. He always calls people ‘pets’ or ‘darling’. He means it a bit...differently...”

“He was surprised you didn’t kill me.” I frowned, trying to root out all my concerns. I finally looked up at the male. He looked vastly
uncomfortable and I almost felt bad for giving him the 3rd degree.
“Everyone is surprised actually. With my past as the ward leader being so bloody and I don’t have very many human friends. The Ghouls
at Anteiku even spoke to me about bringing you there at first. This isn’t...typical. I enjoy getting human customers, my pulse races and I
get excited. It’s enjoyable....but they never get closer than that." He exhaled and raised a hand to feel his pulse.
"I can not blame my friends for being surprised. I’m surprised...” I took a few hesitant steps towards the couch and then finally sat myself
down. “In any other case I’d have killed you as soon as you figured out what I was. But I enjoyed your visits and I kept letting you leave
even after I thought you might suspect. When I took you out on that building I told you; I want you to stay close...” He exhaled and
leaned back, staring up at his ceiling. “But...I may still scare you off...”
I took the moment to look over the man; leaned back, throat exposed as he stared up at his blank ceiling. While I worried about whether
he thought of us as friends - his worry was that I would leave.
“Something other than eating people, killing my muggers getting chased by CCG officers through the streets?”
“Something else...” He agreed, his eyes still fixed on the ceiling. I didn’t have a clue what could be ‘worse’ than the rest. He seemed
concerned that whatever it was could actually scare me off. Which was absurd to me; All the other things I'd mentioned already happened
and here I still was.

“Are you going to tell me at some point...?” I questioned.
“Yeah...” Uta said. “But not yet.”

“My turn: Ai-chan...do you think ghouls are monsters?”
“...no.” I answered right away. That was an easy one.
“Evil?”
“No. Not anymore than anybody else. How could I think they were after meeting people like Touka, Yoshimura and the others...”
"Are you afraid of ghouls?"
"...You've asked that before. I told you I was a little. I'm actually a little less afraid now. I suppose after meeting you that changed a bit. If I
hadn't met you like I had...I probably would still be. There are ghouls that still scare me though..."
“Are you afraid of me?”
“...no. You make me nervous sometimes. But not afraid. I’m still getting used to some of your quirks. But most of the time I completely
forget that you’re a ghoul. I forget that the people at Anteiku are ghouls too. They’re just people. Recently though they’ve been keeping
me a bit in the dark and that’s making me a bit on edge...”

“Hum?” Uta dropped his eyes down from the ceiling and shot me a curious look. “What was it you wanted to know?” This past week I
hadn’t seen much of Uta at all. It hadn’t even occurred to me that he might be more willing to talk with me about the things the other
ghouls were keeping from me! I'd spent so much energy pestering the people at work when I could have just come over and bothered my
goth friend! Excited, I sat up and started speaking rather quickly. “Well! Recently they’ve been talking about a group of ghouls who are
getting ready to maybe attack other wards...and then with all the doves around...”
“Aogiri tree.” Uta said, filling in the information I had been missing. I shot him a blank look. “Eh?”
“The ghoul group is called “Aogiri tree". They’ve been causing some issues in other wards. Attacking the CCG and drawing attention to
themselves for years...But recently they've been more active. Itori and Nico have looked into them a little bit.”
“Oh! Well they've been trying to keep me in the dark for the most part but Yoshimura has been having someone walk me home everyday
because I guess it’s dangerous. But that is not making me feel safer. It just makes me more concerned...they’re my friends you know? I like
the people I work with! I want to know what’s up with them. If something is bothering a friend I don’t want to be kept out of the loop. I
know I'm 'just a human' and Touka says it's none of my business but I want to be included.”
Uta chuckled softly. “Really? You’d rather know? Even if it’s horrible?”
“Yes!” I said emphatically. My eyes turned to look at the ghoul in the eye. He may keep his secret to himself for now. I could respect that.
But when he did want to tell me then at least he’d know I was here to listen. I wasn’t going anywhere!
“What about after you learned about Tsukiyama and the Ghoul Restaurant. Don’t you think that’s horrible? It’s a black market human
trafficking ring. They kill and torture humans for fun...”
“It’s...not nice.” I said in a dull tone; eyes dropping to the ground. It wasn’t nice at all. If asked before I’d probably have preferred to not
know about that in particular. However now I did know. As I learned more about the world the darker and more gloomy it appeared.
“It's certainly not my favorite thing. But I still don’t hate him for it. I don’t even hate him for thinking of me as a pet. It just
hurts...because I cared-- No. I still care about him.”
“Even after today?”
“Of course. I thought of him as a friend. I don’t just stop caring about someone because they didn't care as much as I thought. Or because
he does something I don’t like. I can’t just dismiss all the fun we had. He never did anything to hurt me. I mean, I don’t blame you for
being chased down by Ghoul investigators...and that was horrible and I'd prefer if that hadn't happened.” A tremor shook up my spine as
I remembered that encounter.
“Sorry. That...outing didn’t go quite like I’d planned. I was going to take you someplace else after...” Uta muttered; clearly disappointed
by the turn of events. "They kind of ruined it."
“It’s not your fault. It was just shit luck to end up landing right next to them. The view off the building was really nice though. Maybe we
can do that again and not repeat the second part. Because...I really don’t enjoy being hunted down with a tentacle sword.” He laughed
again as our tense conversation led back into one that was more relaxed. Normal for us.

“Quinque. I told you about them.”
“Yeah...those are the weapons the CCG make out of ghouls...right?” As funny as my name for it had been it was painful to remember
that it had once been a kagune attached to a ghoul. Just like Uta.
“Yeah. That's them.”
“So...a Kagune. I never really asked. Those are like...”
“Tentacles?” He smirked, raising a thin eyebrow at me. I puffed out my cheeks indignantly. “Poking fun at me again I see. What I meant
was; All ghouls have that sort of thing?” Looking him over you’d never have guessed. Ghoul looked human; But I also didn’t know how
ghoul anatomy really worked.
“Yup. They’re not all ‘tentacles” though. That Dove had a bikaku type weapon.”
Clearly this meant nothing to me. A lot of the things Uta told me weren't known to the public. Only the CCG and ghoul’s themselves

would know things like this. Seeing the dead-ass stare of incomprehension on my face Uta continued; “There’s different types of Kagune.
It’s at least partly genetic. It depends on where the organ is in a ghouls body. Ukaku; around the shoulders. Koukaku; behind the shoulder
blades. Rinkaku; the waist. And Bikaku are around the tailbone. Those ones often look like tails like you saw. Or...a tentacle. But every
kagune varies from ghoul to ghoul.”
I leaned forward in my seat towards the ghoul and stared at my friend with a fevered interest. “So...how is that...” I struggled to find a
good way to say it. “How is something like that in your body...” That ‘sword’ had been at least twenty feet in length. There was no way
with his structure that it was simply bunched up inside like a slinky or something. “You don’t...mind explaining this to me. Do you?”
His shoulders rose and fell; a shrug. “I don’t mind. RC cells in our kakuhou burst out through the skin and form the Kagune which is like
a liquid muscle. The whole thing isn’t stored inside.” He chuckled, seeing my confusion give way to understanding.
“That makes a lot more sense than what I was trying to imagine...”
The next ‘obvious’ question was on the tip of my tongue. I wanted to know more about Uta, not just theoretical ghouls biology. What
sort of Kagune did he have? What did it look like? Was it like that one I'd seen the other night?
“...would it be terribly rude of me to ask about yours?” I asked, trying to be more polite about it than just blasting the ghoul with a
million questions that were all possibly very invasive. It was a struggle...
“Mine?” He studied me then seemed to contemplate it. I thought that I’d overstepped some code of conduct for ghouls and was about to
apologize; but instead he simply gave me a condition. "If I tell you then you'll keep it to yourself?" At first I didn't totally understand why
it would be a secret, even between other ghouls. However if knowing the type of kagune told you where it was in the body I suppose that
would give someone a leg up in a fight. Only after I nodded my head in agreement did he lean forward and touch a spot on his lower
back; near his waist. “Mine's here."
“A Rinkaku?” I said, parroting the information he’d given me a minute ago.
“Yeah.”
“...can I see it?”
The ghoul looked at me with open surprise and I stared back; mortified at the words that slipped out of my mouth. “S-sorry...that was so
rude! I shouldn’t have asked!" I pulled my feet up onto the couch and tucked my beet red face down to my knees to hide. I sat, muttering
into my joints. "I just want to see without one without it trying to kill me...” I was unable to look up and meet his eyes as he started to
laugh like it was the funniest joke he’d heard in years.
“I think Bjorn may not like me doing that unfortunately.” He said, still chuckling. “Maybe some other time.” I peeked up to look at my
dog. Bjorn was staring at us as he always did when we were in a room together. “Oh...yeah that might freak him out.”
## ♥

Uta got up and got me some blankets for the couch. When he came back with them they were tossed gently over my head and I had to
fight my way out from under them. Just as promised it was mine for the night. The goth nodded at the bathroom when I poked my head
out from under covers. “I saved the toothbrush I gave you last time for you. It’s in the cabinet above the sink in there. If you’d like...” He
kept my toothbrush here in case I visited overnight again? I wanted to be able to say that was silly but I was almost out of fingers on the
one hand to count the amount of times I’d accidentally fallen asleep here. Maybe keeping one here wasn’t a terrible idea.

“Thanks. I end up sleeping here more than I thought I would. Uta-kun....Do you want to watch a movie?”I said, experimentally putting
‘kun’ on his name. His lips twitched and he reached to move my legs out of the way to sit. I scrunched my body up out of the way to let
him take the other side of the couch again.
“Not sleepy?” Picking up a remote he started to flick through TV options.
“Not yet...too much on my mind.”
“Care to share?”
I shook my head as a definite no; but I was smiling all the same. “Just some stuff I need to think on my own...”
“About our conversation?”

“No. Well kind of...but no.” I could feel the butterflies squirm around in my stomach again and I wasn’t quite sure what to do about it.
Or if I should do anything at all...

What he picked out was a horror movie. I didn’t mind too much but I was extremely prone to jump at all the jump-scares. The ghoul
laughed at me each time until I lightly shoved his arm. “Quit it...”
“A good scare if good for you Ai-chan. Gets your blood pumping! Don’t you like getting your pulse up a little bit?”
“You do that to me enough as it is!”
I snuggled myself under the blankets Uta provided me with and tried to get comfortable again during a quiet time in the movie. During
the movie I’d glanced over towards the ghoul. Looking over to Uta I could see he was relaxed, manspreading and arms looped over the
back of the couch to stretch out as much as possible. His red eyes were fixed on the flatscreen. Uta had no reservations about getting very
close and personal to me...What harm would it be if I...?
I turned my body around and scooted closer while my mind sang: ‘You’re being a stupiiiid bitch!!! This will never work! ♫’
Still, I got close enough to very slowly lean my head gently on his shoulder. I stayed very still, tense and a little uncomfortable in this
position for a few minutes. And....
He didn’t react. Nothing. Nada. Nothing whatsoever. I argued with myself internally that this wasn’t the worst reaction. He could have
asked me to move. But this felt like an exercise in futility and it had actually been a total waste of time and energy. Afterall, I’d just been
worried he thought of me as a pet and now I was trying to get closer? Was this even allowed? I finally sat up; pulling away...only to have
an arm drop down from the couch behind me and encircle my shoulder; holding me closer and blocking my ‘escape’.

When I looked up at Uta’s face I could see his eyes had turned from the screen to look at me from the corner of his eyes. “Cold?”
I was completely bundled up in the blankets and leaning gently on his side. So no. I was not cold. In fact I was completely burning up at
this point! “N-no. Just trying to get comfortable...”
His eyes turned back to the screen but his arm didn’t move off my shoulders or let me retreat back to 'my' side of the couch. I laid my
head back down and leaned very gently on his side. As minutes passed I let my muscles relax little by little and started paying more
attention to the movie again. The butterflies kept messing up my stomach but for now I wasn't minding too terribly...
I don’t know how the movie ended. For all I knew all the humans had died to the ghosts or whatever had been in the house because three
quarters of the way through I started to drift off to sleep. The last thing I remembered before drifting off was that I’d completely
forgotten to give him the gift.
Tomorrow I’d give it to him..definitely tomorrow.



From the continuity Somanoko the author established, Tsukiyama upset Aika because his way of talking
about her crossed the line from friendship into objectification/possession.
The important part wasn’t simply that Shuu is a Ghoul or that he has unusual tastes. Aika was hurt by the
implication that he saw her as something rare and interesting to possess rather than simply as his friend.
That is why it connects so strongly to Chapter 19. When Shuu referred to Aika in a way that treated her like
a “pet” or something belonging to him, it hit one of her deepest sensitivities: she had escaped a family that
tried to control her, so being treated as somebody’s property is especially upsetting.
So the continuity point should be:

Tsukiyama’s comments made Aika question whether their friendship had ever been entirely genuine,
because his language suggested that he viewed her as a fascinating possession rather than an equal friend.
And that becomes one of the reasons Aika later reacts so strongly when other Ghouls describe her as Uta’s.
She isn’t necessarily accusing Uta of doing what Shuu did; she’s reacting to the same kind of language
because of what it represents to her.
Yes. Chapter 76 makes the reconciliation much clearer, and it establishes a few important things about Aika
and Shuu that build directly on their earlier conflict.
What Shuu had done that upset Aika
The earlier problem was Shuu treating Aika like something he could possess rather than recognizing her as
his friend. His language and behavior had crossed the exact boundary Aika was especially sensitive about:
being claimed, controlled, or reduced to someone’s property.
That hurt because Shuu wasn’t just some random Ghoul. He was her childhood friend. She expected him to
understand that their relationship was based on friendship and mutual choice, not ownership.
So when Aika confronts him again in Chapter 76, she deliberately makes the distinction explicit:
“Shuu, you know that I’m not your pet...”
And then even more importantly:
“No Shuu...I am your friend. I am your friend or I’m not going to coffee with you.”
That is essentially Aika telling him: You can care about me. You can be protective. You can even struggle
with the fact that I’m Human and you’re a Ghoul. But you don’t get to own me.
How they make up in Chapter 76
The reconciliation isn’t really one huge dramatic apology. It’s much more them.
Shuu initially struggles with the idea:
“It’s difficult being friends with a Human.”
Aika refuses to let him use that as an excuse. Her response is basically, Yes, I understand the danger. But
I’m still your friend.
She points out that Uta could eat her, Shuu could eat her, and any determined Human could potentially hurt
Shuu too. The difference in species doesn’t erase their ability to choose how they treat each other.
And Shuu accepts the argument.
“Yes...Yes. I suppose that’s true.”
That little change matters. He’s no longer arguing that the Human/Ghoul difference makes ordinary
friendship impossible.

Then Aika reinforces it by calling him a good friend. She initially says:
“You were a good friend.”
Then immediately corrects herself:
“Were...? I’m offended mon ami!”
“.... Are. You are a good friend. And you are invited to our wedding.”
That’s effectively her extending the friendship back across the broken boundary.
What Aika tells Shuu about herself
A major part of their reconciliation is that Aika trusts Shuu with something extremely important.
She tells him about the Kaneshiro family’s Ghoul genetics.
She explains that she has a Ghoul relative in her family and that there is a possibility that her body could
eventually be overwhelmed by RC cells and that she could become a Ghoul.
And she explicitly asks him to keep it secret, even from his father.
That is a huge demonstration of trust.
She’s essentially saying:
I am trusting you with information that could completely change how people see me. Please don’t betray
that trust.
Shuu’s response is immediate:
“Of course, mon ami...”
And from there, he knows something about Aika that very few people do.
There’s also a lovely bit of irony in Aika saying:
“That’s kind of what ‘family secret’ means, Shuu.”
Because she’s treating him like the old childhood friend he is again instead of treating him as someone she
has to fear.
## —
And then Shuu proves the friendship is real
The coffee date is important because they don’t spend the entire time talking about their conflict. They
just... spend time together.
They talk about books. They talk about literature. They talk about Kaneki.

They talk about Aika’s company.
They talk about her wedding. They joke.
That’s what makes the reconciliation feel genuine. Their relationship isn’t repaired because they made a
solemn declaration; it’s repaired because they’re able to fall back into being friends.
And Shuu immediately starts helping with the wedding. Which brings us to June.
What was established Shuu would do in June?
The important established point is that Shuu is going to help plan Aika and Uta’s wedding.
Aika asks him directly:
“Actually yes...I don’t know what goes into that sort of wedding. Having someone help me plan would be
wonderful. Would you, Shuu?”
And Shuu enthusiastically accepts.
He specifically offers to handle the parts of the wedding involving Ghoul customs and preparation,
including:
●  wedding planning
●  finding people/artists who understand the necessary beadwork
●  arranging the appropriate wedding clothing
●  having Aika measured by the Tsukiyama family’s tailor
●  helping organize the larger celebration
●  coordinating the Ghoul-cultural aspects Aika doesn’t understand yet
Aika proposes six months, putting the wedding around spring. And Shuu says that should be enough time.
So the continuity going forward is essentially:
Shuu has gone from someone Aika was hurt by because he treated her possessively → to someone she
consciously chooses to trust again → to one of the people helping prepare her and Uta’s wedding.
And there’s an especially nice emotional symmetry there. Aika’s biggest boundary with Shuu was:
“I am your friend, not your possession.”
By Chapter 76, Shuu demonstrates that he understands it.
He doesn’t need to possess Aika to have a place in her life.
He gets invited to her wedding because she’s choosing him as her friend.

And then, rather hilariously, he gets put in charge of helping make the wedding spectacular. This connects
to her history of having other people make decisions about her life.
The conflict establishes a permanent relationship rule:
Uta’s possessive language must not become literal ownership.
Ghoul culture may attach different meanings to claiming language than Humans do.
Uta’s instincts can remain possessive. Aika’s autonomy remains non-negotiable.
The Chapter 19 conflict establishes an important distinction between possessive language and ownership
rather than establishing that Aika dislikes being called “mine” or “his.”
Aika’s initial reaction is rooted in her history of having other people decide what her life, future,
relationships, and choices should be. When Uta uses possessive language before she fully understands its
Ghoul cultural meaning, she momentarily hears the possibility of being claimed without having chosen it
herself.
The conflict is therefore about choice and meaning, not the word “mine” itself.
Uta explains that among Ghouls, possessive language can carry meanings of protection, association,
bonding, warning, attachment, or recognition. It can be instinctive and emotionally significant without
necessarily meaning literal ownership.
Aika gradually comes to understand this distinction.
As their relationship develops, Aika becomes comfortable with — and eventually genuinely enjoys — Uta
calling her his. She uses possessive language toward him as well. Their possessiveness is mutual,
affectionate, culturally informed, and rooted in an already-established choice to belong together.
Their eventual Ghoul marriage and mutual scarring make this even more significant: they have chosen one
another and marked that bond mutually. “His” and “hers” become natural expressions of their relationship
rather than threats to either person’s independence.
## Permanent Relationship Rule
Uta’s possessiveness is real and should not be softened into neutrality.
He is intensely attached to Aika. He can be territorial, protective, jealous, worried about losing her, and
openly possessive in both language and behavior. He calls her “Ai-chan” and may casually refer to her as
his, particularly in intimate, playful, protective, or dangerous contexts.
Aika does not automatically recoil from this. She likes being wanted by him.
She likes being recognized as his partner.
She can tease him about his possessiveness, encourage it, return it, or deliberately provoke his reactions.
The distinction is that Uta does not get to decide her choices for her. Autonomy and possessiveness coexist.

Uta will not physically or psychologically force Aika to remain with him, but he is absolutely not passive
about abandonment. If Aika attempts to leave him, he will follow her, seek her out, confront the situation,
explain what she means to him, admit that he does not want her to leave, and ask her to stay.
He can be intense. He can be frightened.
He can be emotionally vulnerable. He can say plainly that he wants her.
He can make it very clear that losing her is unacceptable to him emotionally. But the final decision remains
something Aika must make willingly.
The important distinction is not “Uta cannot claim Aika.” It is “Uta cannot make her stay against her will.”
Their relationship therefore contains both:
●  mutual possessiveness
●  chosen belonging
●  Ghoul bonding customs
●  marriage/scarring
●  territorial instincts
●  jealousy
●  intense attachment
●  fear of abandonment
●  physical and emotional closeness
●  respect for each other’s ability to choose
Aika can sincerely think of herself as Uta’s, and Uta can sincerely think of her as his, without either belief
turning the other person into property.
Their bond is strongest precisely because both of them chose it.
Aika’s sensitivity is not to possessive language itself, but to the possibility that possessiveness could
become control. Because her bond with Uta is mutual and chosen, she eventually embraces his possessive
language and returns it naturally.

## PART IV — AIKA’S TWO-WOLVES PHILOSOPHY
Hiroshi’s lesson:
One wolf represents:
●  joy
●  peace
●  love
●  hope
●  serenity
●  humility
●  kindness
●  benevolence
●  empathy
●  generosity
●  truth
●  compassion.
The other represents:
●  anger
●  hatred
●  envy
●  sorrow
●  regret
●  greed

●  arrogance
●  self-pity
●  guilt
●  resentment
●  lies
●  false pride
●  ego.
The familiar answer is:
“The one you feed.”
But Hiroshi’s deeper lesson is that neither wolf should simply be starved or destroyed.
The darker wolf also carries:
●  courage
●  tenacity
●  fearlessness
●  strategic thinking
●  strong will
●  survival instinct.
The gentler wolf cannot always make every difficult decision. The darker side cannot be allowed to
dominate either.
Core philosophy
Balance means acknowledging both sides without allowing either to consume the other.
This philosophy increasingly informs Aika’s adult choices.
