## That Has Happened
Aika mentally reconstructs the progression of her life. She remembers:
●  Her old boss attacking her.
●  The moment she struck him with the pipe.
●  Running to Uta with blood on her hands.
●  Uta welcoming her rather than rejecting her.
●  Discovering that Uta was a Ghoul.
●  Feeding Uta while he was injured.
●  Gradually becoming comfortable with his Ghoul nature.
●  The attack on Anteiku.
●  Surviving while a friend was kidnapped, tortured, and never returned.
●  Uta killing people who threatened her.
●  The mugger.
●  The Ghoul in the street.
●  Their bodies becoming part of Uta’s world and feeding habits.
●  The Doves chasing them.
●  Opposition from some of Uta’s friends when their relationship became serious.
●  Roma repeatedly tormenting her and trying to drive her away.
●  More encounters with the Doves.

●  Training with Renji and worrying every time she accidentally injured him.
●  Discovering that Hiroshi is a Ghoul.
●  Learning that Ghoul genetics exist in her family.
●  Learning that she herself may potentially become a Ghoul.
This is a major continuity consolidation.
Aika’s reaction to Uta cannot be understood solely through Chapter 56. She has spent months surrounded by
violence, death, Ghoul culture, CCG danger, and moral contradictions.
Yet she keeps coming back to the same realization:
She was not most frightened by Uta’s Ghoul nature.
She was frightened because, for a few moments during the training fight, she didn’t recognize him as Uta.
Her protector became an unknown threat. That distinction matters enormously.
## Aika Realizes She Needs Space, Not Distance
Aika concludes that she needs a different kind of training. She has only just received Crystal Lily.
She needs time to learn:
●  its weight,
●  its movement,
●  its range,
●  its flexibility,
●  how the RC extension behaves,
●  how to swing it naturally,
●  how to control it without panicking.
She does not need to immediately fight someone overwhelmingly stronger than her.
She specifically recognizes that Uta and the other Ghouls are far more physically capable than she is.
Her solution is practical:
Train regularly, but gradually.
She also recognizes that she needs someone to talk to. Renji is too personally involved.

Itori isn’t the right person for this conversation.
Touka would probably listen, but Aika doesn’t want to burden her while she’s dealing with school and her
own life.
Eventually Aika decides there is one person she can trust with this. Yoshimura.

## 14. Aika’s Real Fear
Aika explains that sometimes what frightens her isn’t necessarily what happened.
It is how she reacted.
She believes a “normal” Human should have:
●  screamed,
●  cried,
●  become angry,
●  run away,
●  been terrified.
Instead, she often felt:
●  welcomed,
●  relieved,
●  protected,
●  safe.
She remembers being able to go to Uta with blood on her hands. She remembers Nico helping keep her
hidden.
She remembers being grateful rather than horrified. And she admits something that has been troubling her:
Why does the Ghoul world feel so natural to her?
That question becomes tangled with her hereditary Ghoul possibility.
She wonders whether becoming a Ghoul might actually be the easiest answer. But then she immediately
questions that conclusion.
If she chooses to remain Human, what would that mean to her Ghoul friends? Would they see it as
rejection?
Would she somehow be choosing to stand outside the world they never had a choice about?
This is one of the chapter’s central identity questions.

## 15. Yoshimura Tells Aika About Ukina

Yoshimura responds by sharing part of his own history with Ukina. He tells Aika about being a Ghoul with

Yoshimura explains that love can make people bend far beyond what they ever expected. Ukina accepted
him and his world.
She eventually went as far as changing her own behavior dramatically to preserve their unborn child.
But Yoshimura ultimately had to kill her. The loss never stopped hurting.
That pain became part of him.
Yoshimura asks Aika to keep what he told her private. Aika promises to do so.

And her possible future transformation is not something she has to decide simply because other people

## —
-       Why Wendigo gets a B Itori explains the logic.
Normally, without evidence of a kagune, Wendigo might have received a lower classification. But the CCG
has observed enough to establish that she is dangerous.
The investigator she killed is included in the report. The bridge incident is also connected to her.
Her association with No-Face and the Clowns raises her perceived threat level further. Therefore the CCG
essentially says:
They don’t know what Wendigo is capable of, so they are treating her as potentially stronger than the
evidence currently proves.
This uncertainty is valuable continuity.
The CCG still believes Wendigo is a Ghoul. They do not know she is Human.

- Wendigo and No-Face officially linked
This is arguably the most consequential piece of the wanted-list update. The CCG now publicly interprets
Wendigo and No-Face as likely mates.
That means Aika’s association with Uta is no longer merely something the Clowns know. It is becoming
part of the CCG’s intelligence picture.

## Consequence
If investigators encounter Wendigo, they now have reason to expect: No-Face may be nearby.
Likewise, encountering No-Face may make them look for Wendigo. This gives the two identities a
dangerous new level of association.

CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE TRACKER and of chapter 66 return home. Aika

- Aika Gives Uta the Tour
Aika shows Uta around the manor. Uta remains unusually quiet.

Her bedroom remains the childhood room she was confined to.
Although she owns the estate, she has not emotionally escaped that room.

Yet she still sleeps in the room where she once lacked freedom.
She has control over the building, but some part of her has not yet accepted that she is free inside it.

## 23. Final Emotional Beat
Aika eventually lies face-down on her bed. She is miserable.
She hates:
●  the emotional distance,
●  her own anger,
●  pushing Uta away,
●  being unable to read him,
●  wanting him closer while simultaneously needing him to change something.
She had hoped showing him the manor would make him ask questions or reveal what he was thinking.
Instead, Uta remains difficult to read. Her frustration reaches its simplest form:
If only he would express something. Anything. And that is where the chapter ends.
- Aika finds Uta
Aika nearly walks into Uta while heading toward his room.
Despite still being angry with him, she consciously recognizes that Uta has come to her home and that
repairing their relationship requires allowing him to remain part of her life.
Uta has been exploring the manor and comments on the family’s art collection, recognizing works
associated with artists such as Hokusai, Yokoyama Taikan, and Kuniyoshi.
Aika notices that his face is difficult to read again. Her frustration builds.
Rather than have another verbal argument, she proposes fighting. But she establishes strict rules:

●  No weapons
●  No kagune
●  No biting
●  Fists only
This is crucial because it deliberately contrasts with Chapter 56.
In Chapter 56, Uta’s training became frightening because he pushed Aika beyond what she emotionally
expected.
Here, Aika defines the boundaries herself.
- The manor gym
Aika and Uta go to the manor’s gym.
It contains:
●  a boxing ring
●  weights
●  punching bags
●  martial-arts mats
●  enough open space for serious training
Aika notes that Renji can train her there as well. She and Uta begin sparring.
Uta repeatedly dodges and gently puts her onto the mat.
Instead of being reassured by his restraint, Aika becomes angrier. She wants an outlet for everything she has
been holding inside.
Eventually she lands a punch on Uta.
He catches her wrists and immediately identifies what is actually happening: Aika is angry.
-         Aika finally says what she has been unable to say This becomes the emotional heart of the chapter.
Aika tells Uta that she isn’t angry because he’s a Ghoul.
She is angry because he chose to bring her to the Auction while knowing she would hate it. She feels that he
deliberately ignored the warnings of people such as Renji.
More painfully, she tells him she is angry because she doesn’t believe he understands that she genuinely
loves him.

Aika lists everything she has already accepted:
●  Uta killing Humans for survival
●  hiding him from investigators
●  lying to protect him
●  helping conceal his identity
●  preparing his food
●  enduring the dangers associated with being around him
●               accepting the darker parts of his nature Her frustration is essentially:
“I have already chosen you repeatedly. Why do you still act as though I might leave the moment I see the
worst of you?”
She also explains how painful his silence after she left was. She cannot read him.
She expected him to reach out.
Instead, when she returned, he was quiet.
She interpreted that silence as possible rejection.
This directly resolves the misunderstanding established in Chapters 64–67.
-         Uta finally breaks through his emotional restraint Uta holds Aika.
She initially resists. Then he quietly says:
“Please don’t leave.”
This is one of the most important Uta moments in the entire arc.
Rather than his usual detached manner, he openly admits that he needs her to stay.
He apologizes for taking her to the Auction despite knowing the danger.
Aika recognizes how upset he actually is from tiny changes in his voice and breathing rather than a dramatic
emotional display.
She finally understands:
Uta’s silence was never indifference.
He was devastated.
- Aika establishes a new boundary

Aika tells him that things have to change. She cannot keep bending indefinitely.
Her position regarding the Auction becomes explicit:
She can accept Uta’s need to survive. She cannot accept treating Humans as commodities.
She tells him the Auction is cruel regardless of whether the victim is Human or Ghoul. Uta explains that the
Clowns will not stop.
Aika therefore makes a compromise:
She will not demand that Uta abandon the Clowns entirely. Instead, she asks him to go less often.
Uta agrees.
She also asks him to keep Roma away from her.
Uta’s immediate reaction shows that he shares her hostility toward Roma.
This is a significant new relationship boundary:
Aika is no longer simply adapting herself to Uta’s world. She is asking Uta to make reciprocal changes.
Chapter 70: “Human Tofu”
This chapter is a huge milestone for Aika’s long-term goal.
First synthetic-organ feeding
Kazuha obtains a batch of synthesized human organs. The first available organ is liver.
Uta eats it. His reaction:
## ●  Bland.
●  Almost tasteless.
●  No immediate nausea.
●  No vomiting.
●  His body appears capable of keeping it down.
●  Most importantly, he continues eating it voluntarily despite the poor taste.
That makes the experiment an initial success.
It isn’t delicious.
It isn’t satisfying in the culinary sense.

But it is edible to a Ghoul without immediately causing obvious rejection. That distinction matters
enormously.
“Human Tofu”
Kazuha jokes that Aika is essentially making:
“Tofu for Ghouls.”
Aika embraces the concept.
Her immediate goal becomes improving the taste rather than simply proving that the organs can be
consumed.
She even starts theorizing whether synthesized organs could be biologically conditioned through artificial
blood filtration to acquire something closer to the characteristics of Human-derived organs.
Kazuha points out the enormous complexity of that process.
Aika doesn’t abandon the idea.
This establishes her research philosophy:
Making an ethical alternative technically possible is not enough. She wants it to be practical enough that
Ghouls would actually choose it.
That becomes one of her most important ideological distinctions.
## —
Aika’s philosophy becomes explicit
Aika acknowledges something crucial:
Some Ghouls might gladly accept bland food if it means nobody has to die. But others might prefer killing
because:
●  They want the taste.
●  They don’t care about Human lives.
●  They actively hate Humans.
●  Or killing itself is part of their worldview.
Roma becomes the obvious example.
Aika therefore recognizes that creating Human-Tofu won’t magically reform every Ghoul.
Her goal is instead to eliminate the excuse:

“There was no other choice.”
She wants to create an alternative good enough that choosing not to kill becomes genuinely viable.
That distinction is central to Aika’s future ideology.
## —
Aika and Uta: marriage development
Chapter 70 contains a major relationship milestone.
Aika tells Uta that she wants to remain with him even if his future remains fundamentally Ghoul rather than
becoming something more Human.
Uta asks whether she would remain part of his future if his world doesn’t become better.
Aika says yes.
The conversation naturally reaches marriage.
Uta confirms that his earlier suggestion that she could marry him was genuine. Engagement status
Aika explicitly accepts Uta’s marriage proposal.
She refers to him as her fiancé afterward.
The existing Ghoul scar/bonding mark becomes symbolically important here:
●  Aika already carries the permanent mark associated with their relationship.
●  Uta does not yet have the reciprocal mark from her.
●  They discuss making the marriage formally recognized within Ghoul tradition later.
They also discuss:
●  A Ghoul wedding.
●  Friends and family attending.
●  Food and drinks.
●  Traditional clothing and jewelry.
●  Aika’s dislike of a stereotypical white wedding dress.
●  What surname they might use.
Surname discussion

Uta reveals that he doesn’t remember his family surname.
He remembers being eight when his parents were killed, but doesn’t remember the name they had.
Aika offers:
## ●  Kaneshiro
●  Uta’s forgotten family name if he discovers it
●  Or creating an entirely new surname.
Aika specifically says that if she had a choice, she would rather not be called Kaneshiro. This is a major
identity point.
The Kaneshiro name represents:
●  Her parents.
●  The restrictive upbringing.
●  Their corporate legacy.
●  The weapons research.
●  The household’s old power structure.
So choosing another surname could eventually become another way of saying: I am still Aika, but I am not
their daughter in the way they wanted me to be.
Uta is invited to choose a completely new shared family name.
He hasn’t chosen one yet.
Current marital status after Chapter 70: engaged, not yet formally married.
## —
The manor security incident
After the successful Human-Tofu test, Uta and Aika are privately affectionate in the hallway. A security
officer suddenly approaches with a weapon drawn toward Uta.
Aika immediately steps between them.
This is extremely important because it reverses the territorial dynamic established earlier.
Uta’s territory:
Aika is protected there.

Now Aika’s territory:
Uta is protected here.
She explicitly tells the security officer to lower the weapon and reports the incident to Kazuha. She calls an
emergency staff meeting.
## —
Aika establishes the Kaneshiro Manor’s new rules Aika addresses the entire household.
Her position is unequivocal:
●  Ghouls are not to be treated as monsters.
●  Uta is her fiancé.
●  Her guests are to be treated with respect.
●  Threats against Ghouls are unacceptable.
●  Threats against Humans are equally unacceptable.
●  Staff uncomfortable working alongside Ghouls may resign.
●  Nobody is permitted to threaten or attack Uta.
●  Her household is no longer governed by her parents’ attitudes toward Ghouls.
One especially funny line becomes a major domestic callback:
Aika tells everyone she will not tolerate someone pointing a weapon at her fiancé while he is simply trying
to kiss her in the hallway.
This completely detonates the room’s professional atmosphere.
The Doctor finds it hilarious.
Merlin had apparently bet on the engagement. Kazuha is visibly caught off guard.
## —
The staff’s true history is revealed
This chapter dramatically expands the Kaneshiro household lore. The manor staff are not ordinary domestic
employees.
Nearly the entire household staff has a criminal or otherwise highly questionable past. Examples:
## Ms. Sato

●  Former poisoner.
●  Poisoned her first and second husbands.
●  Now head cook.
●  No longer poisoning people.
●  Known for excellent pies.
## Merlin
●  Former US Navy.
●  Got into serious trouble after arriving in Japan.
●  Was accused of killing someone while drunk.
●  Aika’s father made the legal problem disappear.
●  Merlin became fiercely loyal in return.
●  Quit drinking that same night.
●  Has remained sober since.
●  Served as the family’s fixer.
●  Has handled dangerous situations and Ghoul-related matters.
●  Now serves Aika as driver/fixer.
## Kazuha
●  Former Fourth Ward street child/pickpocket.
●  Attempted to pickpocket Aika’s father.
●  Instead of punishing him, Aika’s father took him in.
●  Gave him food, education and a future.
●  Eventually Kazuha became the household’s highly educated lawyer/fixer.
●  His loyalty to the Kaneshiro family therefore isn’t simply employment.
●  He owes Aika’s father his life trajectory.
## Dr. Chikafuji
●  Former smuggler.

●  Previously involved in trafficking unusual biological materials.
●  This included Human and Ghoul remains.
●  Explains both his medical fascination and his comfort with disturbing biological questions.
Other household workers
Merlin identifies backgrounds involving things such as:
## ●  Burglary
## ●  Embezzlement
●  Organized crime
●  Various other criminal histories
The important distinction is that these are primarily household staff. Kazuha clarifies that ordinary
employees at:
●  Kogane no Shiro’s laboratories
●  Corporate headquarters
are not necessarily criminals and do not know the family’s deeper secrets.
## —
The Kaneshiro household’s original social contract
This is one of the most important worldbuilding revelations in Chapters 69–70.
Aika’s father didn’t simply hire criminals.
He created a reciprocal system:
He protected them from the consequences of their pasts. In exchange they:
●  Kept the family’s secrets.
●  Protected the household.
●  Performed unpleasant jobs.
●  Remained loyal.
●  Followed orders.
For many of them, the Kaneshiro household was genuinely better than the outside world. That explains why
their loyalty survived for so long.

It also explains Merlin’s earlier statement:
“Nobody leaves the company.”
The deeper implication is that the household operates almost like a protective criminal ecosystem.
Merlin describes it as a hive protecting its nest.
## —
Aika’s moral shock
Aika is shaken by the revelation.
Not because she suddenly hates the staff. Quite the opposite.
She realizes she never bothered to ask where they came from. She knew:
●  Sato as a kind cook from childhood.
●  Kazuha as her Warden/butler/lawyer.
●  Merlin as her rough driver.
●  The others as familiar household figures.
But she never understood the machinery beneath the manor. This produces an important self-criticism:
She has been calling the manor “her territory” without actually understanding how her territory functions.
That becomes a direct challenge to her new role as head of the Kaneshiro household.
## —
The dead security officer
The officer who threatened Uta is killed by the household almost immediately after being dragged away.
Aika is horrified by how casually it happens. She did not order his death.
This distinction matters.
The household’s old machinery operates automatically.
They have been trained to protect the Kaneshiro family through ruthless means.
Aika’s attempted intervention comes too late.
The officer’s body is subsequently treated as something that can be sent to the laboratory for research unless
Uta wants to consume it.

Aika is deeply disturbed by this.
It forces another confrontation with the reality that:
Changing the household’s values will not happen merely because Aika declares new rules.
The old system has momentum.
## —
Uta’s reaction
Uta understands something Aika is only beginning to grasp. The manor is not simply a rich Human
household.
It is another dangerous ecosystem. And Aika has inherited it.
He notices that she is shaken by discovering:
●  Kazuha’s past.
●  Merlin’s past.
●  Chikafuji’s past.
●  The staff’s criminal backgrounds.
●  The household’s willingness to kill for her.
Yet he also recognizes something about Aika:
She isn’t horrified by their histories simply because they are criminals. She is horrified because she didn’t
understand the world she now controls. Uta reassures her that the staff still listen to her.
Aika points out that much of their obedience actually flows through Kazuha. Uta jokes that if Kazuha ever
betrays her, he can eat him.
Aika after a beat recognized the joke and I think she also saw the seriousness underneath it too Aika
immediately establishes the boundary:
Kazuha is off limits unless he genuinely betrays her.
This is another important example of Aika adapting Ghoul-style territorial language while maintaining her
own ethical boundaries.
## Chapter 71: Vacation  ‘ˇ‹<-<],
Added to the Dogs & Girls & Ghouls Master Integrated Canon as canonical.

This chapter is particularly important because it develops three threads at once: Aika and Uta learning what
“relaxing together” actually means, Uta’s first real interaction with Yuto, and the beginnings of Uta
becoming part of the household rather than merely staying there.
## Master Chapter Record
- The vacation begins
Aika decides that, after the succession of increasingly serious events, she and Uta need to relax
immediately.
Her reasoning is essentially that if disasters keep arriving one after another, there needs to be deliberate
space for comfort before everyone goes insane.
Aika takes Uta through the manor looking for a better room than the modest room currently assigned to him.
She eventually finds a luxurious bedroom with a large indoor jacuzzi.
She begins imagining the two of them actually sharing a room:
●  Uta could have his desk and mask-making materials.
●  Aika could have her own desk for Kogane no Shiro paperwork.
●  They could work separately while remaining together.
●               Aika realizes she may finally be ready to leave her childhood bedroom, which she still associates
with being imprisoned and controlled.
This is an important psychological development.
The manor had once been another version of her family’s control. Now she is beginning to choose which
parts of it become her home.
Uta points out that she does not need to buy things to convince him to stay. They are supposed to be on
vacation.
- Aika and Uta redefine intimacy
Aika deliberately asks Uta to postpone anything more heated and instead simply relax. She massages his
shoulders, neck, scalp, and hair. Uta visibly relaxes under her touch. The chapter explicitly establishes an

Intimacy is not synonymous with sex. For Aika, physical closeness can mean:
●  affection
●  trust
●  comfort
●  touching without an ulterior motive

●  quiet companionship
●  simply being together
Uta reciprocates with gentle affection and massage.
They eventually share the jacuzzi, music, warmth, and quiet conversation.

physicality itself: they are learning how to be peaceful together.

Renji explains that the woman he knows is doing somewhat better than when they first met. However, she

## —
- A DIFFERENT KIND OF GHoul/HUMAN COEXISTENCE
The conversation naturally turns toward how Renji obtains food. Aika points out that Renji has an
advantage Uta does not.
Renji explains that Anteiku-style feeding is not a perfect solution either. They still hunt when necessary.
Aika acknowledges this. Her philosophy is not:
“My friends must all make the same choices.”
Instead, it is:

That distinction is becoming increasingly important to Aika’s worldview.
She accepts that Uta may continue making choices she personally would not make. She does not want to

At the same time, she recognizes that Renji’s method of surviving may be psychologically easier for another
Human to accept.
This reinforces one of the central relationship principles of the story:
Aika’s coexistence philosophy is based on choice rather than forced moral uniformity.
## —
## 4. AIKA’S VIEW OF UTA
Aika describes Uta as fundamentally nihilistic rather than merely gloomy or brooding. She understands that
his worldview comes from the world he has lived in.
Importantly, she does not condemn him for it.
She also acknowledges that Uta does not truly believe her Human-Tofu project will transform society.
Yet he continues eating it. That contradiction matters.
Uta’s behavior demonstrates that he can support Aika’s hopes even when he does not share her optimism.
Aika recognizes this.
## —
## 5. AIKA’S SELF-ANALYSIS: OPTIMIST OR NOT?
Renji calls Aika an optimist because she wants to change society. Aika rejects the label.
Her distinction is:
She is trying to be optimistic, but she is not naturally an optimist.
She actively thinks about the consequences of societal change. Her concerns include:
● What if people don’t want change?
● What if people actively resist it?
● What happens to people who don’t fit the new system?
● Could a new society simply create another group oppressed by a different “boot”?
●           What happens to the thousands of CCG employees whose livelihoods depend on the existing
system?

●           What happens to their families if the CCG ceases to exist? Aika admits something particularly
important:
She cannot bring herself to care very much about the suffering of the CCG’s institutional structure if
dismantling that structure means improving life for the people she loves.
She recognizes this as potentially selfish.
She is not pretending that her desired future is morally perfect. Her reasoning is essentially:
Every social order harms someone. She wants to create the one she believes will harm fewer people and
protect the people she cares about.
This makes her vision of coexistence more complicated than simple idealism.

Later, Aika sits at the dining table with:

## 8. THE RESULTS ARE DIFFERENT
This is one of the most important discoveries in the chapter. Uta
● Has been eating the synthesized liver for approximately two weeks.
● Can keep it down.
● Has not been experiencing hunger.
●           Has been secretly pretending it tastes better than it does. Itori
● Immediately dislikes the taste.
● Swallows it.
● Does not vomit.
●           Finds the lingering taste unpleasant. Nico
● Eats it relatively stoically.
● Does not vomit.
●           Appears physically capable of tolerating it. Renji
● Initially eats it normally.
● Then develops a strong adverse reaction.
● Rushes to the rubbish bin.
● Vomits the synthesized organ back up.

This produces the first clear evidence that not all Ghouls necessarily react to Human-Tofu in the same way.
## —
## 9. UTA IS CAUGHT LYING ABOUT THE FOOD
Aika immediately realizes something.
Uta had previously described the Human-Tofu as being essentially tolerable. The other Ghouls make it
obvious that this was not entirely true.
Uta has been eating something he finds genuinely unpleasant.
He simply didn’t tell Aika because he didn’t want to discourage her.
Aika is amused and touched rather than genuinely angry. She tells him that he does not have to pretend to
like it.
She does, however, establish that she needs honest information for the experiment. Their exchange
reinforces an important piece of their relationship:
Uta will sometimes conceal discomfort when he thinks honesty might hurt Aika emotionally. Aika responds
by asking him to be truthful about the experiment.
She still appreciates why he lied.
This chapter is a major aftermath chapter rather than an action chapter. Its core movement is Aika slowly
returning from shock and grief into speech, while Uta quietly takes over the role of caregiver. At the same
time, the destruction of Anteiku forces the surviving Ghouls back toward hunting, making Aika confront the
consequences of the CCG’s “victory.”
## —
## 1. MASTER CHAPTER RECORD
## Chapter 75: Silence
Time: Approximately one week after the Owl Suppression Operation, late August. Location: Uta’s
apartment/shop in the 4th Ward, with Kaneshiro Manor also referenced. Primary POV: Aika, followed by
## Uta.
Aika’s physical condition
Aika is recovering from the injuries sustained during the previous chapter. She is:
● seriously injured and largely bedridden
● wearing a cast on her leg
● wearing a brace on her hand

● dealing with injuries to her back and face
● taking pain medication
● sleeping frequently
● physically healing considerably faster than an ordinary Human would be expected to
Dr. Chikafuji examines her and confirms that her healing is unusually rapid despite her still-Human RC
levels.
After approximately one week, her injuries appear much farther along in the healing process than expected.
Her RC count has only increased by a small number of points, meaning there is still no indication that she
has crossed into Ghoul transformation.
This is important because her accelerated healing appears connected to her unusually high RC level without
yet making her a Ghoul.
## —
## 2. THE SILENCE
Aika has not spoken since Bjorn’s death and the confrontation with the investigator.
Not because her throat is damaged. She simply cannot make herself speak.
Her silence functions as psychological withdrawal. Speaking would make everything feel real. She spends
much of the week:
● sleeping
● remaining heavily medicated
● staring blankly
● barely eating
● barely drinking
● avoiding consciousness when possible
Physical pain actually gives her something concrete to focus on. Her injuries become a way of grounding
herself when her thoughts become unbearable.
Her mind repeatedly returns to:
## Yoshimura. Koma.
## Irimi. Bjorn.

The loss of Anteiku compounds the grief.
She also hears that Koutarou Amon is missing in action, with the CCG announcing him among the
deceased. Even though Aika wasn’t particularly close to him, the news hurts because the entire event has
become an enormous pile of people disappearing from her life.
## —
## 3. BJORN’S BURIAL
Kazuha has Bjorn buried in the garden at Kaneshiro Manor. Aika knows this but cannot bring herself to
move his bed or toys. Bjorn’s absence is physically visible throughout the apartment.
His bed remains near the heating vent he loved. His toys remain scattered across the floor.
These objects become silent reminders that he is gone.
This is an important continuation of Chapter 74: Bjorn’s death is not treated as something Aika simply
recovers from after one chapter.
His absence becomes part of the environment.
## —
## 4. UTA AS CAREGIVER
Uta becomes remarkably attentive during Aika’s recovery.
## He:
● stays close to her
● moves her between the couch and bed
● brings her food and drinks
● helps her manage her injuries
● tolerates her crying
● works from the apartment rather than leaving her alone
● communicates with Yuto so the child knows Aika is being cared for
● brings her favorite Human foods
● continues watching her condition
● contacts the doctor
●           tries to get her outside once she is physically capable He brings her things such as:

● ice cream
● brownies
● waffles
But Aika cannot taste or enjoy them.
The emotional numbness has spread into ordinary pleasures.
This makes Uta’s role particularly important: he doesn’t try to force her into being cheerful or “move on.”
He simply stays.
## —
- Aika EATS TO AVOID AN IV
Aika’s lack of eating and drinking becomes medically concerning.
Kazuha warns that if she continues refusing food and water, the doctor may have to use an IV. Aika dislikes
needles enough that this motivates her to eat and drink.
But she is essentially eating as a survival task rather than because she wants food. This reinforces how
emotionally withdrawn she has become.

## 6. KAZUHA’S CHANGE IN RELATIONSHIP WITH UTA
A subtle but significant household development occurs here.
Kazuha calls Uta “Sir.”
The doctor also calls him “Sir.”
This appears to reflect Uta’s new status within the Kaneshiro household following Aika’s marriage
announcement and engagement.
Uta is no longer merely Aika’s strange Ghoul boyfriend/visitor.
He is becoming recognized as part of the household hierarchy.
Kazuha still remains Aika’s primary administrator and protector, but Uta is now being treated as someone
with authority as her fiancé.
Aika notices this immediately.
## —
## 7. KAZUHA AND UTA ARGUE OVER AIKA’S CARE

Kazuha worries that Aika is deteriorating emotionally and physically. He argues that she needs:
● fresh air
● activity
● social contact
● closer medical observation
● potentially additional medication
Uta refuses to move her back to the manor immediately. His position is simple:
He is taking care of her.
He intends to bring her outside once her leg is strong enough and believes seeing friends may help.
Kazuha ultimately backs down.
The conflict shows something important about Uta and Kazuha: They are not necessarily enemies.
Both are fiercely protective of Aika, but they approach that protection differently.
Kazuha thinks in terms of logistics, medical supervision, security and household structure. Uta thinks in
terms of immediate emotional presence and simply being there with her.
## —
## 8. DR. CHIKAFUJI’S MEDICAL UPDATE
Dr. Chikafuji provides an important update on Aika’s biology. Despite remaining Human, her injuries are
healing unusually quickly. Her:
● leg
● hand
● back
are all healing at an accelerated rate.
The doctor attributes this to her unusually high RC levels.
This is another confirmation that Aika’s biology is becoming increasingly abnormal even though she
remains Human.
He also confirms that there is nothing physically preventing her from speaking. Her silence is psychological.
The doctor therefore understands that she is choosing not to speak, whether consciously or instinctively.

## —
## 9. ASAHI HAYASHI
Uta asks Kazuha to investigate the investigator who attacked Aika. Kazuha identifies him as:
Asahi Hayashi He was:
● a First Class Investigator
● taken into the CCG when young
● promoted quickly
● regarded as naturally talented
● without known family according to available records
Kazuha warns that obtaining too much information could attract attention. Uta accepts the limitation.
He tells Kazuha that if Hayashi appears anywhere looking for Aika, he will kill him.
Kazuha responds that Uta might have to get in line, because several people would like revenge against
anyone who hurt Aika.
This is another subtle sign that Aika’s household is becoming a frighteningly protective network around her.
## —
## 10. A MONUMENTAL REVELATION: AMON
Kazuha also gives Uta information concerning the Owl Suppression Operation.
Koutarou Amon is officially presumed dead by the CCG, but his body was never recovered. Likewise, the
body of the Owl was never recovered.
## Therefore:
Amon’s actual fate is unresolved. The Owl’s actual fate is unresolved.
This should be preserved as an active continuity mystery rather than treating either character as definitively
dead.
## —
## 11. AIKA SPEAKS AGAIN
The emotional turning point arrives when Uta is sitting beside her, reading through the reports. Aika finally
tries to speak.
Her voice is extremely weak and damaged from disuse. She cannot immediately form normal words.

But she reaches for Uta’s sleeve.
That gesture communicates what she cannot say:
She is afraid of losing him too.
She watches the CCG’s victory coverage and realizes the danger isn’t over.
Her fear is not simply about herself. She is thinking about:
## ● Uta
## ● Renji
## ● Touka
## ● Itori
## ● Nico
● the surviving Anteiku Ghouls
She cannot bear to lose anyone else.
Uta understands without requiring her to explain.
He tells her he will bring Renji along and make sure the others have food. He will also tell Itori and Nico.
Aika relaxes slightly.
This is her first meaningful communication since Bjorn’s death.
## —
## 12. THE CONSEQUENCE OF ANTEIKU’S DESTRUCTION
Aika realizes something bitter:
The destruction of Anteiku has not made the world safer. It has made surviving Ghouls more desperate.
The Ghouls who once had relatively peaceful access to food through Anteiku must now find food
elsewhere.
Aika’s interpretation is deeply cynical:
The CCG calls its operation an attempt to create peace, yet destroying a relatively peaceful Ghoul
community forces survivors into more dangerous circumstances.
Therefore the operation may actually result in more deaths, not fewer.
This connects directly to Aika’s Human-Tofu philosophy.

Her goal has never been merely to say that Ghouls are misunderstood. She wants to create practical
alternatives that remove the argument:
there was no other choice.
Anteiku’s destruction demonstrates exactly why she thinks alternatives matter.
## —
## 13. TOUKA ARRIVES
Later, Touka arrives with Renji.
Uta initially warns Aika that there is “food” downstairs.
Aika understands what that means and agrees to go down. Because she cannot walk properly, Uta carries
her downstairs.
This is a quiet but important domestic continuation of their relationship after the disaster. Aika sees Touka.
Touka immediately notices how badly Aika was hurt.
Aika cannot speak properly yet, but eventually manages to greet her.
## —
## 14. TOUKA AND AIKA
Touka tells Aika:
Kaneki is gone.
The CCG has claimed that he is dead. Aika comforts Touka as best she can.
Rather than allowing the conversation to remain centered on death, Aika asks about school. She tells Touka
to make sure she passes her classes.
She offers to help buy her books.
When Touka asks why she would do that, Aika responds with her belief that: kids are the future.
She tells Touka that she cares about her and Yoshimura.
This scene is extremely important because Aika’s first real conversation after Bjorn’s death is not about
herself.
It is about making sure Touka keeps living. Touka is visibly moved.
## —
## 15. TOUKA’S RESPONSE

Touka tells Aika that she is glad Aika survived. She also apologizes for what happened.
She doesn’t finish the sentence because both of them understand what she means.
Aika responds with hope:
She believes Kaneki will appear somewhere. She reminds Touka that Kaneki is strong.
This is not certainty.
It is Aika deliberately choosing hope when she has very little left.
## —
## 16. UTA TAKES AIKA BACK UPSTAIRS
After the conversation, Uta carries Aika back upstairs. Aika asks whether the others were safe.
Uta confirms they were.
She asks him to wake her if she falls asleep. Then she apologizes for being silent.
Uta doesn’t treat her silence as something she needs to apologize for.
Their relationship remains built around the idea that she doesn’t have to perform emotional recovery for
him.
## —
## 17. UTA’S POV
The chapter shifts into Uta’s perspective.
His thoughts reveal how he has interpreted Aika’s silence. He understands that people respond to trauma
differently. Some rage.
Some work.
Some become reckless. Some withdraw.
He has seen people disappear into silence before. His position is essentially:
If Aika is alive, he can wait. He will keep caring for her.
He will keep making sure she eats.
He will let her recover at her own pace.
This is an important expression of Uta’s attachment.
He does not try to force her back into normality.

## —
## 18. UTA’S PRIVATE FEAR
Uta is nevertheless deeply worried about Aika. He notices:
● her blank expression
● her silence
● her grief
● her physical deterioration
● her accelerated healing
● her weight loss
● her lack of appetite
He repeatedly asks Chikafuji whether she should start suppressants. The doctor reassures him that she is
currently stable.
But the situation remains uncomfortable because Aika’s biology is increasingly unusual.
Uta is therefore dealing with two different threats simultaneously:
- Aika’s psychological collapse after Bjorn’s death.
- Aika’s increasingly Ghoul-like biology.
## —
- THE GHOUls NEED FOOD
Renji returns carrying two bodies. Touka follows him.
The implication is clear:
The destruction of Anteiku means the survivors have returned to hunting. Uta prepares food for them.
The chapter deliberately contrasts this with the earlier Human-Tofu experiment.
Aika wanted a world where Ghouls didn’t have to kill.
Now Anteiku’s destruction has removed the relatively peaceful infrastructure around which that experiment
was developing.
The irony is brutal:

The CCG destroyed a community that was already trying to coexist, while the survivors are now forced
back into the exact behavior the CCG claims to be preventing.
## —
## 20. THE TWO BODIES
The chapter establishes that Renji has obtained food for the group. One of the Humans is described as
having chosen death.
Uta reflects on this strangely.
He understands suffering and despair, but doesn’t understand the Human’s decision.
Thematically, this creates a dark mirror:
Aika is desperately fighting to keep living. Uta is desperately keeping Aika alive.
Meanwhile, someone else has given up their life, and their body has become food for those who are still
trying to survive.
The chapter uses this contradiction to deepen Tokyo Ghoul’s moral ambiguity.
## MASTER CHAPTER RECORD
## Chapter: 76
Title: Friendship is healing
Time: Approximately two weeks after the Owl Suppression Operation
Primary locations: Uta’s mask shop/apartment, outside café
Primary POV: Aika, with an extended Uta POV section
## —
## 2. AIKA BEGINS RETURNING TO NORMAL
Aika is now physically capable of sitting at Uta’s desk and doing company paperwork.
She thinks of Kogane no Shiro increasingly as her company, rather than something inherited from her
parents.
That distinction matters.
The company is becoming part of the life she has chosen rather than another piece of her parents’ legacy
imposed upon her.
Emotionally, however, she remains unstable. The physical pain has essentially disappeared. The emotional
pain has not.

She can be sitting quietly and suddenly become overwhelmed by memories of:
## ● Bjorn
## ● Anteiku
● the people she lost
● the CCG operation
●           the possibility that she could have prevented some of it She begins thinking about regrets.
She wishes she had spent more time with Bjorn.
She regrets leaving Anteiku after her argument with Uta.
She wonders whether she could have done something to stop the CCG attack.
But she ultimately recognizes that none of those possibilities can change what happened. She has to
continue forward.
## —
## 3. UTA INVITES SHUU
Uta tells Aika that he invited Tsukiyama over. Aika is surprised.
Uta’s reasoning is simple: Shuu is Aika’s friend.
This is significant because Uta is not merely tolerating Shuu. He recognizes that Aika needs her friends
around her.
Shuu arrives wearing a burgundy suit, but Aika immediately notices something unusual. He is subdued.
The flamboyant Gourmet is still recognizable, but his usual energy is muted. Aika realizes he is grieving
too.
## —
## 4. SHUU’S GRIEF OVER KANEKI
Shuu’s emotional state becomes clear when Aika asks what is bothering him.
His answer:
## Kaneki.
He has heard that Kaneki is dead.
This reinforces that Kaneki’s disappearance affects several characters differently:

● Touka is grieving him.
● Shuu is grieving him.
● Aika is grieving the people around her while hoping Kaneki is actually alive.
● The CCG officially considers him dead.
Shuu’s grief also complicates their relationship because Kaneki was someone Shuu once viewed through
both friendship and predatory Ghoul instincts.
## —
## 5. AIKA TEASES UTA AND SHUU
Aika asks whether Ghouls trying to eat their friends is apparently a normal part of Ghoul friendship.
Uta jokingly says that sometimes friends take swipes at one another.
He gives his relationship with Renji as an example.
Aika immediately threatens to bite Uta back if he tries anything. Uta enthusiastically says he hopes she
does.
The exchange is intentionally playful rather than threatening, and Aika realizes something important:
Having a friend around is helping.
The joking makes her feel a little more like herself.
## —
## 6. AIKA REASSERTS HER BOUNDARY WITH SHUU
Shuu calls Aika Princesse, as usual. Aika directly reminds him:
She is not his pet. She is his friend.
She tells him that if he cannot treat her as a friend, she will not go for coffee with him. Shuu admits that
friendship with a Human is difficult.
Aika counters that being physically vulnerable does not mean she is powerless.
She reminds him that while a Ghoul could potentially eat her, she could also attempt to fight back.
Her argument ultimately gets Shuu laughing.
The conversation restores some of their old rhythm.
## —

## 7. AIKA REVEALS HER FAMILY SECRET TO SHUU
Before leaving, Aika decides Shuu can be trusted with one of the Kaneshiro family’s biggest secrets.
She explains that:
● the Kaneshiro family has Ghoul genetics
● Hiroshi is a Ghoul relative
● her own RC levels are unusually high
● she may eventually become a Ghoul
● suppressants could delay or prevent that transformation
●           her accelerated healing is connected to those genetics This is a major expansion of Shuu’s
knowledge.
Shuu now knows Aika’s Human/Ghoul transformation risk.
Aika deliberately chooses him as someone trustworthy enough to keep this information secret. She
specifically asks him not to tell anyone, including his father.
Shuu agrees.
This makes him part of a relatively small circle aware of Aika’s biological secret.
## —
## 8. UTA AND SHUU’S PRIVATE CONVERSATION
While Aika changes upstairs, Uta and Shuu speak privately.
Uta asks whether Aika’s potential transformation is why she is upset.
Shuu corrects him:
## No.
Bjorn’s death is the immediate source of her grief.
Uta also explains that Aika is mourning the Anteiku people she lost. He tells Shuu that she needs friends
around her.
Then Uta directly tests Shuu’s attachment to Aika.
Shuu responds by criticizing Uta’s decision to bring Aika to the Auction.
He believes Uta’s choices put Aika in danger.

This is one of the clearest examples of Shuu’s affection for Aika overriding his usual rivalry with Uta.
Uta responds possessively, making it clear that Aika is his partner and warning Shuu not to hurt her again.
Their tension remains, but it is controlled.
They are essentially operating under an uneasy understanding:
They both care about Aika.

## 9. AIKA AND SHUU GO FOR COFFEE
Uta stays behind.
Aika and Shuu visit the café that Shuu had used after being banned from Anteiku. The experience

The coffee is acceptable.
It isn’t Anteiku.

● an outdoor wedding

● a large open field
● a nighttime component

● Ghoul cultural traditions
● invitations to the people she cares about
Shuu explains that a Ghoul wedding is a major celebration that can occupy an entire day.

Aika considers how long they should remain engaged. Part of her wants to wait a conventional amount of

Approximately six months.
That would place the wedding around spring. She still needs to confirm the timing with Uta.
This establishes the first concrete proposed wedding timeline.
Wedding: approximately six months from Chapter 76, pending Uta’s agreement.

Shuu therefore knows Aika has taken control of her family’s company and understands at least some of the

## 13. AIKA MEETS SEN TAKATSUKI
While at the café, Aika notices Sen Takatsuki. Shuu recognizes that Aika likes her books.
Aika approaches her.

She nearly reveals that this person had been connected to Anteiku, but stops herself. Instead she says that it
is a shame Takatsuki never visited the café.
Takatsuki immediately becomes interested. She asks who the man was.
Aika refuses to say.
She calls it a secret.
This is a very important encounter because Aika has just unknowingly given Takatsuki a personal clue
connecting her writing to someone at Anteiku.
## —
## 14. THE YOSHIMURA CONNECTION
Aika’s interaction with Takatsuki is emotionally loaded.
She isn’t simply telling an author that someone liked her books.
She is trying to preserve something about Yoshimura. His physical world has been destroyed.
Anteiku is gone.
But his affection for books remains something Aika can still pass forward.
She protects his identity while still allowing Takatsuki to know that her work mattered deeply to him.
## —
## 15. AIKA RETURNS AND GETS HER CAST REMOVED
When Aika returns to the shop, Kazuha, Uta and Dr. Chikafuji are waiting. Kazuha is furious that Aika
wants her cast removed.
Aika insists that the leg feels completely normal. The doctor examines her.
The cast comes off.
Her leg is completely healed.
There is no remaining visible injury. Her hand is also freed from its brace. Her fingers work normally.
Even the injuries from Asahi Hayashi have healed without lasting visible marks.
This becomes another startling biological confirmation that Aika’s RC levels are affecting her healing.
## —

## 16. AIKA’S FEAR OF HEALING
The healing is medically miraculous. Emotionally, it frightens Aika.
Every healed injury is evidence that her body is becoming less conventionally Human. She knows her RC
levels are unusually high.
She knows Chikafuji believes continued progression could eventually lead to Ghoul transformation.
Therefore, her healing is simultaneously:
a gift and a warning.
She is beginning to experience the physical benefits of her abnormal biology while becoming increasingly
afraid of what those benefits might mean.
## —
## 17. KAZUHA MEETS SHUU PROPERLY
Kazuha recognizes Shuu from Aika’s childhood.
He was once responsible for keeping the young Aika inside the Kaneshiro estate. Shuu immediately teases
him about having failed.
Kazuha responds that Shuu was a bad influence and that Aika could have been killed. Aika stops the
argument.
She explains that Shuu was actually a good influence and may have helped keep her alive. Kazuha
reluctantly accepts this.
Aika introduces Shuu formally: Kazuha is her right-hand man. Shuu is her friend.
She asks Kazuha to treat him accordingly.
Kazuha apologizes and acknowledges that he allowed old resentment to influence his behavior. This is
another small friendship repair.
## —
## 18. UTA’S TEN-POUND WEIGHT LOSS IS REVEALED
The doctor casually reveals something extremely important:
Uta has lost approximately ten pounds during the Human-Tofu experiment. Aika immediately notices.
Uta had previously admitted that Human-Tofu weakened him. Now the scale of the problem becomes
concrete.
This confirms that the experimental diet wasn’t merely unpleasant.

It had a measurable physical cost.
Uta had been concealing the severity of the problem from Aika.
## —
## 19. THE COMPLETE HUMAN-TOFU RESULT
Uta finally explains the truth. Human-Tofu:
● can be eaten by some Ghouls
● suppresses hunger
● is capable of sustaining them for a period
● is unpleasant in taste
● does not provide everything a Ghoul needs
● causes reduced strength and speed when eaten exclusively for an extended period
Uta explains that he did not feel hungry during the month. But he became progressively weaker.
He had noticed the weakness roughly a week into the experiment.
He simply didn’t tell Aika because he didn’t want to derail her research or worry her.
This finally resolves the apparent contradiction from Chapters 73–74. Human-Tofu was not a failure.
But it was not yet a complete nutritional replacement either.
## —
## 20. AIKA’S RESPONSE
Aika does not blame Uta.
Instead, she immediately thinks about how to fix the problem. Her conclusion:
She needs to improve the formula.
She understands that a substitute that merely fills the stomach isn’t enough.
If Ghouls become weaker while eating it, the food could actually make survival more dangerous.
This is especially important after Anteiku’s destruction.
The real-world conditions now make nutritional completeness essential.
## —

## 21. AIKA’S NEXT RESEARCH TRIP
Aika explains that she will soon visit the laboratories where the synthetic organs were produced. She plans
to travel with:
## ● Kazuha
## ● Merlin
The purpose is to inspect how the organs are made and understand the process better. She sees this as
another step toward making the Human-Tofu genuinely viable.
## —
## 22. UTA MAY NEED TO HUNT AGAIN
Because Human-Tofu isn’t nutritionally complete, Uta has returned to normal food.
He says he may need to hunt again soon. Aika accepts this.
She understands that until her alternative is actually sufficient, she cannot ask him to endanger himself by
relying on an incomplete food source.
This is one of the more mature developments in Aika’s philosophy.
She still wants to eliminate unnecessary killing.
But she now recognizes that good intentions aren’t enough if the alternative doesn’t actually keep people
alive.

Chapter 79: “Yuto’s Vacation”
## Canon Archive Entry
This chapter is deceptively quiet. It is largely a transition chapter, but it locks in several important pieces of
the family structure, Aika’s worsening condition under suppressants, Uta’s evolving relationship with Yuto,
and Hiroshi’s acceptance of Uta as family.
- Bjorn’s memorial and Yuto’s first lesson in the complicated world
Aika begins at Bjorn’s grave in the Kaneshiro Manor garden, surrounded by forget-me-nots. The gravestone
bears Bjorn’s name and a paw print.
Aika is still openly grieving. Even after wiping away her tears, seeing the grave remains painful.
Yuto runs up happily because he is finally being allowed outside after spending so much time confined for
his safety. Aika ruffles his hair and notices that Uta has clipped Yuto’s hair again, maintaining the hairstyle
Yuto wanted.
Yuto notices Bjorn’s grave and asks who he was.
Aika explains that Bjorn was her best friend and her dog, and that an investigator killed him. This becomes
an important lesson for Yuto because he still carries the simplistic belief that: Investigators = good guys
Ghouls = bad guys
Aika challenges that directly.
She explains that investigators would kill her and Uta if they caught them, despite the fact that Yuto
considers both of them good people. Yuto begins to understand that the categories he learned from his
parents do not cleanly describe reality.
He specifically says he likes Uta and Kazu, which is significant because both are Ghouls.
Aika explains that the fact that her friends are Ghouls is a secret because the outside world does not accept
them.
Yuto then understands that he himself is also a secret because his survival and connection to Aika’s Ghoul-
associated household would attract CCG attention.
This establishes Yuto’s developing understanding of the Human/Ghoul divide as something political and
social rather than simply moral.
## —
-         Yuto wants to go back to school On the way to meet Renji, Yuto asks:
“Can I go back to school again?”
Aika immediately wants to give him that possibility, but she explains that he may need schooling
somewhere other than his old school.

The reason is not punishment. It is safety.
If Yuto suddenly returned to his old school, investigators could discover that he survived, question him
about his parents, ask who is caring for him, and potentially trace him back to Aika, Uta, Kazuha, or the
wider Ghoul network.
Aika promises that she will make sure he receives the best education possible, even if it has to be arranged
differently.
Yuto admits that he misses his friends.
This is an important reminder that, despite everything that has happened to him, Yuto is still a child who
wants ordinary things: school, friends, toys, hobbies, and eventually a normal life.
## —
- The piercing conversation
Yuto asks Aika whether he can get piercings like Uta.
Aika freezes because she realizes she is increasingly occupying a parental role without actually being
Yuto’s parent.
She completely panics and redirects the question to Uta. Uta also panics.
Renji ultimately provides the sensible adult answer:
No, Yuto is too young. Ask again after his birthday. Aika immediately backs Renji up.
This becomes another little glimpse of the strange accidental family developing around Yuto.
Yuto wants to imitate Uta’s appearance, just as he already copied his hairstyle.
And Uta is beginning to occupy a role that Yuto associates with someone older and important enough to
imitate.
## —
- Renji becomes “Uncle Renji”
Aika casually calls Renji “Uncle Renji.”
Renji is genuinely surprised.
When he questions how she figures that, Aika explains that she sees him as an older brother and part of her
found family.
She openly contrasts him with her biological family, which largely failed her emotionally and restricted her
autonomy.
Aika tells him that she cares about him.

Renji initially seems caught off guard, but then takes her hand and reassures her that he was only surprised.
This effectively establishes a reciprocal familial bond:
Renji = Aika’s chosen older brother / big brother figure.
Uta immediately turns the concept into a joke by wondering whether this makes Itori an aunt.
Aika’s mental image of Itori as the stereotypical wine-loving party aunt provides some much-needed humor.
Family structure expanding
By this point, Aika’s “family” is no longer primarily defined by blood:
● Hiroshi: uncle
● Renji: chosen older brother
● Kazuha: annoying older-brother figure
● Merlin: rough-and-tumble uncle
● Uta: fiancé and future husband
● Yuto: child she is responsible for, although his permanent placement remains unresolved
● Itori: potentially the chaotic aunt
● Shuu: close friend and now wedding planner
This is a major thematic continuation of Aika’s earlier rejection of the Kaneshiro family’s definition of
family.
## —
- The trip to Hiroshi’s cabin
Renji drives Aika, Uta, and Yuto into the countryside.
Aika takes her Gibson guitar, while Yuto carries two bags, one containing clothes and the other activities.
Uta automatically takes the heavier bag.
This is another small domestic moment showing how naturally the three are beginning to function together.
Aika takes her suppressant during the drive.
The medicine is now having a significant impact on her physical abilities.
She becomes exhausted during the walk to Hiroshi’s cabin, unable to keep up with Yuto, Uta, and Renji.

Eventually Renji carries her on his back.
He calls her “imouto”, reinforcing the sibling relationship they have just established.
Wedding discussion with Hiroshi
Aika tells Hiroshi that she wants to hold the wedding at the countryside location.
She wants him there.
She also wants him to meet her friends.
Aika trusts the people attending because they are either Ghouls or people already deeply connected to her,
and therefore unlikely to expose Hiroshi.
Hiroshi considers the plan carefully. He then notices something important:
Aika, Uta, and Yuto already look like a family.
Yet Aika intends to eventually find Yuto another home.
This is the beginning of Hiroshi questioning whether Yuto is really temporary.
## —
- Aika and Uta’s private conversation
Later, Aika pulls Uta away from the campfire. She admits how exhausted she is.
Uta reassures her again that he does not want her to become a Ghoul simply because it would make things

He says he will protect her so she can remain Human if that is what she wants. This reinforces one of the
central relationship rules established earlier:
Uta loves Aika as the person she chooses to be, not as a version of her that resembles him.
Aika also worries about losing the ordinary forms of closeness she shares with him because of the
suppressant.
Uta notices that he can taste the medicine when they kiss. He says he will be careful.
This chapter therefore continues the established non-explicit intimacy between them, but the important
continuity point is the physical consequence of the suppressant:
Aika’s medication is now detectable to Uta through his heightened senses.
## —
- Uta’s possessiveness is explicitly explained

One of the more psychologically important conversations occurs here. Aika asks about Uta’s tendency to
mark her and his possessive behavior. Uta explains it through an analogy to the incident at the grocery store.
Aika had reacted strongly when he tried to take something she had chosen for herself. To Uta, the feeling is
comparable:
He does not want other people touching her. Aika points out that Renji carried her earlier. Uta admits he
noticed Renji’s scent on her.
However, his jealousy has softened because he understands that Renji is family. This distinction matters.
Uta’s possessiveness is still present, but Aika’s chosen-family relationships are becoming incorporated into
his understanding of her boundaries.
He specifically identifies:
## ● Renji
## ● Merlin
## ● Kazuha
as people Aika considers family. Aika explains each relationship:
Renji: big brother
Merlin: rough-and-tumble uncle
Kazuha: annoying older brother whom she enjoys irritating
Uta is learning that loving Aika means accepting that her life contains other deep attachments.
## —
- Aika worries about Kazuha
Aika remains deeply concerned about Kazuha’s voluntary isolation.
She understands why he locked himself away, but she does not think he can remain there forever.

of hurting Uta or someone else.
Uta tells her that she could not hurt him.

This reinforces his role as someone Aika trusts to keep her safe even if her biology changes.

## —
- Aika falls asleep beside Uta
Aika and Uta lie together beneath a blanket outside.
The country air, stars, and quiet environment provide a rare moment of peace. Aika eventually falls asleep

Uta later carries her to the hammock so she will be more comfortable. He tucks her in and moves her hair
away from her face.
This is one of the chapter’s clearest domestic-care moments.
It also mirrors his increasingly protective behavior throughout Chapters 74–79.
## —
- Hiroshi accepts Uta
The second half shifts into Uta’s POV.
Hiroshi talks to him privately.
He tells Uta that Aika called him during the suppressant emergency and described Uta running through the

Hiroshi admits that he had been wrong about him.
He had assumed Uta would prefer Aika to become a Ghoul and might deliberately allow her transformation.
Instead, Uta did everything he could to ensure she received the medicine in time. Hiroshi therefore
recognizes something fundamental:
Uta genuinely respects Aika’s choice to remain Human.
He gives Uta food and essentially welcomes him into the family. Hiroshi explicitly frames the relationship:
Aika loves Uta.
Aika is marrying Uta.
Therefore Uta is now Hiroshi’s nephew.
There is still a warning attached:
If Uta ever hurts Aika, Hiroshi’s earlier warning remains.
But the tone has changed from suspicion to familial acceptance. Major relationship lock
Hiroshi → Uta: accepted as nephew/family, while retaining protective boundaries toward Aika.

## —
- Hiroshi questions whether Uta wants Yuto
This is arguably the chapter’s most important quiet development.
Hiroshi asks Uta whether he and Aika are actually going to give Yuto away.
Uta says that is Aika’s plan.
But he also recognizes that Aika is attached to the boy.
Uta himself has begun becoming attached.
He admits that he never considered having children before.
He and Aika both believed the world was too dangerous and broken to bring a child into. But Yuto has
already begun affecting him.
Uta notices:

● Yuto imitates his hairstyle.
● Yuto asks about his piercings.

● Yuto has accepted his presence despite his Ghoul nature.

When Yuto begins sliding off the log in his sleep, Uta gets up and moves him back into a safe position.
His thought process is characteristically Uta: Watching Yuto fall on his face would be funny. But Aika
would scowl at him.
So he fixes it.
That tiny action is more revealing than a declaration.
He is already behaving like someone responsible for the child.

Aika’s preference: find a safe family/home eventually Uta’s preference: uncertain, increasingly attached
